statement: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) reported, as an example, that from 12 to 15 January in several localities of Rutshuru territory, North Kivu, at least 10 children, nine women and eight men suspected of collaborating with Wazalendo groups were killed by AFC/M23 combatants.

BCNUDH reported that on 2 January 2026 the FARDC used armed drones in Masisi territory, North Kivu, against AFC/M23 positions, and that several strikes hit densely populated areas in Masisi-centre, injuring 42 people and killing seven others, including two women, a girl and a boy, and destroying houses.

place: Goma (Himbi quarter per UN Group of Experts), North Kivu
statement: UN News, citing a MONUSCO press release, reported that a French UNICEF employee was killed on Wednesday 11 March 2026 in a drone attack on a building housing humanitarian workers in Goma, and that the attack also killed two civilians and damaged civilian homes.

Beto.cd, in an article credited to AFP summarising the UN Group of Experts report S/2026/466, reported that the experts reconstructed the strike that killed UNICEF worker Karine Buisset in Goma on 11 March as an aerial fragmentation munition fired by a drone coming from Lake Kivu, and that attribution remains contested.

7sur7.cd reported that AFC/M23 military spokesperson Willy Ngoma was killed on Tuesday in a drone strike attributed to the FARDC near Rubaya, Masisi territory, according to concordant sources and movement officials.

Radio Okapi reported on Monday 25 May that aerial strikes attributed to military drones, whose origin remained undetermined and which no party had claimed, hit Rubaya (Masisi) and Rumangabo (Rutshuru) the day before; a strike on Sunday around 07:30 hit a training centre for the women and widows of ICCN rangers in the Virunga National Park compound at Rumangabo, with no loss of life confirmed, and an earlier strike around 00:15 targeted a guest house in Rubaya.

place: Ihula, Katobo, Mukohwa (Kisimba groupement), Walikale territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the villages of Ihula, Katobo and Mukohwa in Kisimba groupement, Walikale territory, were retaken by AFC/M23 rebels on Tuesday 26 May after intense fighting against the FARDC and allied Wazalendo; according to its sources, the rebels used drones to bomb loyalist positions.

Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that fighting between Wazalendo armed groups and AFC/M23 rebels was reported on Wednesday 10 June in Masisi territory, notably at Kishanja and Kasenyi, with heavy and light weapons heard.

place: Kiseguru, Bwito chiefdom, near Virunga National Park, Rutshuru territory
statement: 7sur7.cd reported that the FARDC announced in a communiqué that 10 civilians were summarily killed by the M23 in the locality of Kiseguru, near Virunga National Park, Bwito chiefdom, North Kivu, on Tuesday 02 June 2026, and that the FARDC condemned this as a new violation of international humanitarian law; the same communiqué said several other citizens were arrested and transferred to Kanyangambi central prison in Rutshuru on the pretext that they were FDLR.

place: Baswagha chiefdom and Bapere sector, Lubero territory
statement: The Kivu Morning Post reported that at least 54 people were killed in attacks by ADF-MTM since January 2026 in the Baswagha chiefdom and the Bapere sector of Lubero territory, according to a provisional toll compiled on Thursday by the Comité local de protection communautaire (CLPC), whose president Vianney Kitsamba cited 33 deaths in Baswagha and 21 civilians in the Bapere sector.

Radio Okapi reported that in a statement published on Tuesday 3 February 2026, the provincial coordination of North Kivu civil society said at least 62 civilians had been killed since the start of the year by suspected ADF rebels in Beni and Lubero territories, 52 of them in Lubero and 10 in Beni.

place: Beni and Lubero territories (health post not located by the source)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the North Kivu civil society tally of violence by suspected ADF rebels in Beni and Lubero since January 2026 included one health post burned, 67 shops and 10 houses burned, 23 motorcycles burned and the destruction of a local chief's 'barza' meeting place.

Actualite.cd reported, citing health sources, that the health centres of Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya and Musenge and the reference health centre (CSR) of Masoy had ceased activities in the Mwenye groupement of Lubero territory, along with several health posts, following persistent insecurity marked by killings of civilians attributed to suspected ADF rebels; the reference health centre of Masoya, chief town of the groupement, had closed about a week earlier.

Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, an ADF incursion in the night of 21 to 22 July 2026 in the Bapere sector of Lubero territory cost the lives of at least seven civilians and several homes were burned, forcing many households to flee.

place: Mavwe-Mavwe, Mandelya locality, Mwenye groupement, Lubero territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that five civilians were killed and about ten houses burned in a new attack attributed to ADF combatants in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 21 January at the village of Mavwe-Mavwe, in the Mandelya locality, and that four women were among the victims.

place: Kasika and Mabanga Nord quarters, Goma
statement: MediaCongo, carrying a report credited 'Gloire Kamandi/Butembo, Actu30 / MCP', reported that the Karisimbi communal youth council alerted on Wednesday 8 July 2026 to the abduction of more than 50 young people by armed men in the Kasika and Mabanga Nord quarters of Goma, and that the council fears their possible forced enrolment into the March 23 movement (M23/AFC).

Umuryango.rw reported that the AFC/M23 announced six members of one family, a woman and her five children, were killed in an attack it said was carried out by the FDLR in Rutshuru territory, and that, according to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, the attack took place in the night of 2 July 2026 in the Kabizo/Butare area of Bwito chiefdom.

Actualite.cd, relaying Reporters sans frontières (RSF), reported that Espoir Mbata, director of the community radio Top Buzi FM, was held in a container at the North Kivu Provincial Assembly in Goma by the AFC/M23, forced to film an interview of the M23 spokesperson and then released, according to RSF on Friday 24 April.

place: M23-controlled artisanal mines incl. Rubaya and Lomera (North and South Kivu)
statement: Amnesty International reported in a September 2026 briefing that it documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners by M23 or their collaborators in mines in North and South Kivu, at least nine of whom were beaten brutally and died at health centres or before they reached the hospital.
Amnesty International reported that more than 20 miners from Rubaya were kept in a pit and beaten three times a day by M23 fighters.

place: M23-controlled areas of eastern DRC (North and South Kivu; place not specified in the excerpt)
statement: Health Policy Watch reported that UN experts, in a statement the previous week, called for an end to what they described as a 'reign of terror' by the Rwanda-backed M23, citing a growing volume of civilian testimony, and said rapes, gang rapes, violent assaults and killings of civilians are a common feature of M23's modus operandi, adding that 'while these crimes are not exclusive to M23, the number of individuals affected is staggering and must end'.

place: Minembwe and Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Witnesses and relatives told Human Rights Watch that drone attacks in the highlands killed at least two Banyamulenge people in March 2026: an 86-year-old man near Minembwe on 23 March and a 14-year-old boy near his village in Fizi territory on 30 March. HRW said it was unclear if the attacks intended to target military objectives.

place: Madegu and Ilundu, near Minembwe, South Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch reported that a community radio station in Madegu, near Minembwe, was damaged in an apparent drone attack on 9 March 2026, and that an apparent drone attack was carried out on a church in Ilundu village at night, also in March. Human Rights Watch said it could not establish responsibility with certainty but that the targets suggest the Congolese army or allied fighters controlled the drones; Human Rights Watch said it had asked the Congolese army's regional commander for information on the strikes and had not received a response.

Human Rights Watch reported that, according to Minembwe residents and UN and diplomatic sources, the Twirwaneho had forced families to provide a fighter or financially compensate the armed group and retaliated if they refused, and that, according to the same sources, the Twirwaneho had also blocked civilians from leaving Minembwe.

place: Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch reported, citing security sources, that the Burundian army had about 4,000 troops deployed to Fizi and Mwenga territories to fight alongside Congolese armed forces.

place: Rugezi, Mulima, Point Zéro, Kazaroho, Bilalo Mbili, Mikenge, Fizi, South Kivu
statement: Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga reported that Rwandan air force fighter jets had once again bombed Rugezi, Mulima, Point Zéro, Kazaroho, Bilalo Mbili and Mikenge on Wednesday 8 July 2026, causing enormous material and human damage; the territorial authority said several civilians were wounded in these bombings.

Radio Okapi reported that, according to the 'nouvelle dynamique de la société civile', Fizi branch, about 16 civilians were killed and 12 others wounded in a bombing reported at Mulima the previous weekend, and that the victims included women and children.

place: Mulima, Point Zéro, Rugezi (Fizi); Kipupu, Mikenge, Kiseke (Mwenga), South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that residents of several villages in Fizi and Mwenga had fled into the bush; according to local sources the displacement was caused by bombings attributed to kamikaze drones from Rwanda. Fizi's elected national deputy, Nyamangyoku Ishibwela, raised the alert and said that even civilians wounded in these strikes struggle to receive medical care.

place: Mikenge, Itombwe sector, Mwenga, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Mikenge, in the Itombwe sector of Mwenga territory, was retaken on Sunday by the FARDC, supported by the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB) and the Wazalendo militia, after remaining for over a year under the control of Twirwaneho fighters and allied rebels.
SOS Médias Burundi reported, according to local sources, that the FARDC, the FDNB and the Wazalendo militia now controlled strategic points in the centre of Mikenge, including the general hospital.

place: Kasika and Kalambi, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing concordant sources, that after AFC/M23-Wazalendo clashes the previous Sunday, Kasika in Lwindi chiefdom (Mwenga territory) remained under AFC/M23 control while the Wazalendo were positioned at Kalambi, about 20 km away.

Rwandan outlet Umuryango reported that AFC/M23 spokesman Kanyuka said in a post on X on 21 August 2026 that civilians, including women and children, were killed in attacks at Luntukulu on the Nzibira road in South Kivu.

Umuryango reported that Kanyuka, the rebel coalition's spokesman, also said the armed forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo were continuing to launch bomb attacks in the Minembwe area, and that kamikaze drones and TK-6 weapons were being used in these operations.

place: AFC/M23-controlled areas of North Kivu and South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to independent UN experts, the AFC/M23 had reportedly set up a system of control based on fear in the areas it administers, and that the experts' statement reported arbitrary arrests and detentions, acts of torture including sexual violence, and cases of forced labour and forced recruitment of civilians.

MSF reported that between January and April 2026 its support to Baraka general referral hospital (Fizi territory, South Kivu), through medical and logistical supplies and staff training, helped treat 426 war-wounded patients arriving in the influx of violence-related injuries.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, in the days preceding the signature of the Washington Agreement between the DRC and Rwanda, the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and AFC/M23 launched a coordinated military offensive in South Kivu, taking control of Uvira on 10 December 2025.

The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 after sustained international diplomatic pressure, and that the withdrawal, presented as a goodwill gesture, was followed by consolidation of AFC/M23 and RDF positions as they redeployed to adjacent areas.

place: Bukavu-Uvira (RN5) corridor, Ruzizi Plain, South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that at the end of November 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF launched a major offensive along the Bukavu-Uvira (RN5) corridor and adjacent axes, aiming to seize the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira, to compel Burundi's disengagement from the conflict.

The Group of Experts reported that the offensive on Uvira was conducted under the direct command of Mr. Makenga and Mr. Byamungu, and that AFC/M23 and RDF sources had signaled since early October the intent of taking Uvira, pointing at a carefully planned operation by AFC/M23 and Rwanda.

place: Ruzizi Plain; Kamanyola, South Kivu; Cibitoke, Burundi
statement: The Group of Experts reported that Rwanda deployed over 8,000 RDF troops, including special forces, and heavy equipment to the Ruzizi Plain frontlines, and that BM21 rockets were fired from Kamanyola on 4 and 5 December, with cross-border shelling on 5 December causing civilian casualties in Cibitoke, Burundi.

place: Uvira (city) and Ruzizi Plain, South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that heavy artillery fire and shelling in the Uvira offensive caused civilian casualties and displacement from the Ruzizi Plain towards Burundi, and that after AFC/M23 and RDF consolidated control of Uvira in early December they conducted cordon-and-search operations that led to the killing of those suspected of affiliation with FARDC or Wazalendo.

The Group of Experts reported that before their January 2026 withdrawal AFC/M23 instructed the Banyamulenge community to leave Uvira, claiming returning Wazalendo and FARDC forces would target them, and that some members of the Banyamulenge community alleged this movement was coerced to justify claims of a genocidal threat.

The Group of Experts reported that when Wazalendo groups re-entered Uvira on 18 January they triggered widespread disorder, including looting, destruction of civilian, humanitarian and State properties and the killing of individuals accused of collaborating with AFC/M23, and that Banyamulenge churches and homes were looted or destroyed in several neighbourhoods; it did not document any targeted killings of Banyamulenge civilians.

The Group of Experts reported that, according to multiple sources, government authorities including DRC President Félix Tshisekedi instructed Wazalendo elements not to target civilians, particularly the Banyamulenge, and that FARDC placed 31 Banyamulenge families remaining in Uvira under its protection.

The Group of Experts reported that after the Wazalendo return to Uvira in January 2026 the South Kivu Governor convened all Wazalendo leaders, banned unauthorized armed elements, roadblocks and any substitution for government functions, and arrested recalcitrant combatants, and that provincial authorities began a registration process with payment of $325 to each registered combatant.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (AFC/M23-held areas)
statement: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23-occupied territories were divided into three 'defense zones': a first zone covering Nyiragongo, Rutshuru and Lubero territories led by 'General' Baudoin Ngaruye, a second covering Masisi and Walikale led by 'Brigadier-General' Justin Gacheri Musanga, and a third covering South Kivu led by 'General' Byamungu.

place: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that overall military command of AFC/M23 remained with 'General' Makenga, although his position was increasingly contested within the movement and by Rwanda, and that Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa remained the political leaders, all receiving instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services.

place: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that the estimated combat strength of AFC/M23 was around 30,000 elements, and that the figure included thousands of recently graduated FARDC, Congolese national police and Wazalendo elements who were either captured or volunteered following the fall of Goma.

The Group of Experts reported that the RDF 3rd Division, under Major General Eugene Nkubito, operated predominantly in North Kivu, and the 4th Division was mainly deployed in South Kivu under Brigadier General Vincent Gatama until his redeployment to Mozambique in late 2025; special forces units under Brigadier-General Stanislas Gashugi supported both, and the RDF Army Chief of Staff, General Vincent Nyakarundi, oversaw operations.

The Group of Experts reported that in December 2025 RDF deployment in eastern DRC was conservatively estimated at 8,000 to 10,000 elements in South Kivu and 6,000 to 8,000 in North Kivu, with no evidence of significant withdrawals thereafter.

The Group of Experts reported that President Kagame appointed retired General James Kaberebe as Senior Defence and Security Advisor on 1 December 2025 and Brigadier-General Jean-Paul Nyirabutama as his deputy on 29 January 2026, and that Mr. Nyirabutama was directly involved in operational matters in eastern DRC including communication channels with AFC/M23.

place: Lubero, Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that withdrawals by RDF and AFC/M23 from frontlines in North Kivu began on 23 March 2026 but fell short of agreed terms, barely exceeding 15 to 20 km, and amounted to tactical repositioning; RDF personnel and equipment were redeployed from Lubero to the Masisi-Walikale axis.

The Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing RDF and AFC/M23 retained control over most withdrawal-designated localities and kept their operational focus on Pinga and Walikale, with intense clashes persisting in April 2026 along the Walikale-Masisi border against FARDC, VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR.

The Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 FARDC, with Wazalendo, FDNB and private military contractors, launched an offensive from Uvira towards Minembwe against MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23, and that on 31 March FARDC launched a major offensive on Minembwe to which RDF responded with drone strikes and aerial resupply for MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23.

The Group of Experts reported that Minembwe had effectively been encircled by FARDC and allied forces since mid-2025, with severe obstacles to population movements and entry of essential goods and humanitarian assistance, and that since February 2026 access was limited to air supply only.

The Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho prevented civilians from leaving Minembwe through coercion and threats of violence, and that, as previously reported, all boys between 10 and 12 years of age and all able-bodied men were compelled to join Twirwaneho and participate in combat.

The Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments; the Group stated it did not substantiate intentional targeting and that Banyamulenge community members reported three civilian deaths.

The Group of Experts reported that on 14 January 2026 a FARDC drone strike targeted the 'Blue Cat' bar-restaurant in the Kalundu district of Uvira during a meeting of senior AFC/M23 and RDF officers, causing significant casualties.

place: Rubaya and Mushaki, Masisi, North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that on 24 February 2026 a FARDC drone strike in Rubaya killed sanctioned individual 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Willy Ngoma, the military spokesperson of AFC/M23, and that on 7 March 2026 a strike in Mushaki targeted a house associated with a high-ranking AFC/M23 commander.

place: Masisi centre, Shoa and Nyabiondo hills, North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that several FARDC drone operations affected civilian objects and populations: strikes in late October 2025 in Shoa and the Nyabiondo hills (Masisi) killed at least three civilians and caused displacement, and a drone strike on 2 January 2026 in Masisi centre damaged civilian and administrative buildings and the sub-base of War Child, causing at least seven fatalities.

The Group of Experts reported that on 11 March 2026 two successive detonations were reported near a residential compound in the Himbi neighbourhood of Goma, the second causing the death of a UNICEF staff member; M23 military personnel deployed to the scene shortly after the strike and removed all ballistic remnants; AFC/M23 attributed the strike to FARDC while Congolese authorities announced an investigation, and the Group's investigations continue.

The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 continued to forcibly or voluntarily recruit adults and minors, and that former recruits denounced systematic torture and executions in training camps, notably in Rumangabo.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (eastern DRC)
statement: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 was the leading perpetrator of conflict-related sexual violence according to cases documented and verified by the United Nations, and that humanitarian actors recorded a dramatic increase in cases of such violence since 2024, disproportionately affecting women and girls.

The Group of Experts reported that in January 2026 the UN in the DRC verified at least 46 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 61 victims in conflict-affected provinces of eastern DRC, with North Kivu the most affected province (33 victims: 22 women and 11 girls), followed by South Kivu (22 victims: 13 women and nine girls) and Ituri (six victims).

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (and Ituri)
statement: The Group of Experts reported, citing a UN source, that for the January 2026 verified cases armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 52 per cent of victims (M23 most, with 21 victims, then Nyatura four, Raïa Mutomboki three and ADF two), while State agents were responsible for 46 per cent of the cases, with FARDC soldiers ranking first, followed by the PNC and one official from the Ministry of Mines and Energy.

The Group of Experts reported that IPS inspectors of the AFC/M23-run Provincial Health Inspection Department inspected the premises of humanitarian actors after an 11 February 2026 AFC/M23 'Note Explicative', requested aggregate data on sexual violence incidents and access to confidential patient files containing names of victims, and that some humanitarian actors were ordered to cease distributing dignity kits to curb what AFC/M23 alleged were 'fake' victims.

The Group of Experts reported that at a joint meeting in late March 2026 AFC/M23 officials reprimanded humanitarian actors and accused them of inventing data about sexual violence, affirmed that AFC/M23 did not tolerate sexual violence, and criticised the lack of perpetrator data in patient files; the officials present included Colonel John Imani Nzenze and Ms. Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete.

place: Byambwe (Biambwe), Manzya groupement, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that on 15 November 2025 ADF elements entered the village of Byambwe, Lubero territory, killing 23 civilians including women admitted to the maternity ward inside a Catholic Church-run health center, setting four hospital pavilions housing patients on fire, and looting and burning the medical facility, from which equipment and medicines were taken.

place: Centre de santé de Byambwe, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant local sources, that ADF fighters targeted the health centre in Byambwe (night of Friday to Saturday 15 November), where they killed people, looted medicines and set neighbouring houses on fire; the provisional toll, not yet confirmed by official sources, was 20 civilians killed, including 18 patients receiving care in the facility.

place: Ntuyo / Nturo village, Manguredjipa, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported in an annex that an attack attributed to Abwakasi's elements on the night of 8 to 9 September 2025 on civilians attending a funeral in Ntuyo village, east of Manguredjipa in Lubero territory, killed 71 civilians, including men, women and children, and that at least 36 houses were looted and set on fire; the main text of the same report dates the massacre of 71 civilians at a funeral in 'Nturo village' to November 2025.

The Group of Experts reported that between January and December 2025 the UN in the DRC verified at least 887 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 1,534 victims in conflict-affected provinces of eastern DRC, a 59 per cent increase on 2024 (364 cases); North Kivu was the most affected province (676 victims), followed by South Kivu (537) and Ituri (300).

The Group of Experts reported, for the 2025 cases verified by the UN, that DRC armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 75 per cent of victims (M23 ranked first, followed by CODECO, Wazalendo and Mai-Mai factions) and State agents for 19 per cent (FARDC soldiers first, followed by the PNC), and that the UPDF, the FNDB and RED-Tabara were also responsible for CRSV cases.

The Group of Experts reported, citing its earlier report (S/2025/858, para. 82, annex 38), that it had verified a sharp escalation of conflict-related sexual violence cases in South Kivu in areas under the control of the DRC Government and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups.

The Group of Experts reported that mining activity at AFC/M23-controlled Rubaya increased substantially compared with a year earlier according to its March 2026 satellite imagery model, with production assessed to exceed 2024 estimates of approximately 120 tons monthly, and that AFC/M23 taxed all actors, with a per-kilogram tax at commercialization of $4 for coltan and $2 for cassiterite.

The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 issued per-kilogram tax invoices in Rubaya and Mubambiro, and that once shipments were delivered in Rwanda the transporter settled AFC/M23 tax payments by depositing the amounts in an Equity Bank account held by Patient Haba, the AFC/M23 provincial financial coordinator.

place: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that in early December 2025 AFC/M23 introduced a codified list of taxes mirroring Congolese State tax structures, and that the national water and electricity companies (SNEL and REGIDESO) were placed under the administrative authority of the AFC/M23-appointed governor and the financial oversight of the AFC/M23 finance department.

place: Lubero, Beni, Rutshuru, Nyiragongo, Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that VDP/Wazalendo groups established new geographically organized coalitions called 'synergies': the 'Synergie Front Grand Nord' (24 armed groups in Lubero and Beni, commanded by UPLC leader 'General' Mayani), the 'Synergie Petit Nord' (14 groups in Rutshuru and Nyiragongo, commanded by Jonas Bigabo), and the 'Synergie Masisi-Walikale' (17 groups, led by APCLS leader Janvier Karahiri and sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwisa).

The Group of Experts reported that between 80 and 150 Wazalendo groups were reported active across South Kivu, with at least 70 self-proclaimed Wazalendo 'Generals' operating in Uvira and its surroundings, and that by December 2025 Uvira had become the epicentre of tensions and clashes between FARDC and Wazalendo and among Wazalendo fighting over revenue from illegal taxation.

The Group of Experts reported that at the time of drafting Wazalendo factions in South Kivu remained divided into at least three coordinations, one led by Yakutumba, another by Alexis Mwamba Dunya (the RAD-appointed coordinator in South Kivu) and a third by Ngomanzito, and that renewed efforts to establish a unified command had failed.

place: Kiliba, Songe, Luvungi, Lubarika, Walungu, South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that on 22 August 2025 Brigadier-General Mwehu Lumbu Evariste, Commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector in South Kivu, met the main Wazalendo groups to define a counteroffensive strategy against AFC/M23 and RDF, and that FARDC subsequently transferred truckloads of weapons and ammunition to Wazalendo at several front lines, including Kiliba, Songe, Luvungi, Lubarika and Walungu.

place: Uvira axis, Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that several Wazalendo factions carried out joint operations with the FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain: FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover, and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux.

The Group of Experts reported that the Coalition nationale du peuple pour la souveraineté du Congo (CNPSC), led by Yakutumba, maintained a parallel administration in areas it controlled, particularly in Fizi territory, that in January 2026 its 'finance bureau' published a list of taxes across multiple sectors, and that since 2023 it had operated a parallel judicial system with detention facilities, former detainees reporting release conditioned on payment of fines of 2,000,000 to 5,000,000 Congolese francs.

place: North Kivu (Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru, Walikale) and South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that FDLR was fragmented into three principal factions (FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-FPP), that 'Major-General' Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and 'General' Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) remained FDLR-FOCA's military commander and political leader, and that UN and intelligence sources estimated total FDLR strength at between 3,500 and 4,500 combatants.

The Group of Experts reported that in late March 2026 a FARDC helicopter landed in Pinga to deliver weapons to FDLR-FOCA units led by 'Major-General' Uzabakiriho Cyprien that had been fighting AFC/M23 and RDF in Masisi territory, and that on 7 April a confidential encounter between a Kinshasa delegation including FARDC generals and the FDLR-FOCA high command in Pinga decided that FDLR-FARDC cooperation would continue.

The Group of Experts reported that on 29 March 2026 FARDC announced the launch of an operation to neutralize FDLR around Pinga-Walikale and deployed additional troops from Kisangani to Walikale, but that at the time of writing no anti-FDLR operations had taken place.

place: Uvira, Minembwe and Point Zero, South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that private military contractors accompanied FARDC when they entered Uvira in January 2026, that multiple drone strikes conducted with their support targeted AFC/M23 positions around Minembwe on 1 February 2026, and that between 2 and 8 February 2026 they airdropped FARDC 'Hiboux' special forces units at Point Zero.

place: Washington, D.C.; areas of interest in Lubero, Masisi and Walikale (North Kivu) and South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that a meeting in Washington, D.C. on 17 and 18 March 2026 between representatives of the Governments of the DRC, Rwanda and the United States resulted in an 'initial steps plan' that foresaw withdrawal of RDF and AFC/M23 'personnel and equipment', Rwanda's disengagement from defined areas, efforts by the DRC to neutralize the FDLR, and restrictions on drone strikes.
The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 representatives announced that no withdrawal was taking place, describing movements as routine troop rotations.
The Group of Experts reported public statements by the President of Rwanda, Paul Kagame, that 'defensive measures' also included troop deployment in the DRC.

place: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 conducted armed night raids on hospitals in Goma, targeting Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals on 1 and 3 March respectively as part of operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants who had not surrendered, that male caregivers were briefly detained and released, and that a total of 164 patients were abducted (48 from Heal Africa and 116 from CBCA Ndosho), some undergoing treatment and others who had refused to leave for fear of forced recruitment. It reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and 'General' Makenga issued public denials of responsibility, saying they acted in full compliance with international humanitarian law to secure the hospitals from 'infiltrated rogue combatants' who were 'endangering' patients and staff, and that, contrary to those assertions, witnesses confirmed no weapons were found in the hospitals and the arrested individuals had not endangered patients or staff.

place: CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported in an annex that on 3 March 2025 Fikiri Mwishuko, the Chef de groupement of Shanga, was abducted by AFC/M23 from the CBCA Ndosho hospital amongst other sick and wounded patients, and that he subsequently died, reportedly after having been tortured by AFC/M23.

The Group of Experts reported that on the night of 4 to 5 April 2025 armed AFC/M23 elements entered the MSF-supported Kyeshero Hospital compound in Goma in search of FARDC elements who had completed treatment but stayed for fear of being recruited, opened fire within the grounds, killing one person, injuring three and assaulting two staff members; the soldiers did not enter the ward but bullets struck treatment areas.

The Group of Experts reported that an official AFC/M23 communiqué of 5 March 2025, signed by Lawrence Kanyuka, denied responsibility for the raids on Goma hospitals and accused MONUSCO officials of erroneous interpretation of the facts; the communiqué acknowledged that 130 FARDC elements were taken but claimed the operation was peaceful and in full compliance with international humanitarian law because the elements had 'infiltrated' the medical facilities.

place: Heal Africa hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that in an interview excerpt published on X on 13 March 2025, 'General' Sultani Makenga, asked about the raid on the Heal Africa hospital, repeated that the men arrested were former FARDC pretending to be patients or hospital staff.

place: Masisi town and Goma (city), North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that between 19 January and 14 February 2025 multiple incidents harmed medical facilities and personnel: on 20 January bullets and several rockets landed near the MSF-supported hospital in Masisi town, killing one MSF worker and injuring another; on 27 January firing and shelling affected two Goma hospitals, injuring a medical practitioner and a newborn at Goma Provincial Hospital; and humanitarian actors reported at least 27 health structures in and around Goma were impacted between 25 January and 14 February.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (Goma and surrounding areas)
statement: The Group of Experts reported that human rights defenders said survivors of sexual violence faced significant barriers in accessing medical care, primarily due to fear of reprisals by AFC/M23 elements, and that a further alarming surge in sexual violence cases had been reported across North and South Kivu, attributed to all armed actors party to the conflict.
sources: United Nations Security Council; Global Protection Cluster

statement: The Group of Experts reported that reports on the mass escape of prisoners from Muzenze prison in Goma on 27 January 2025 indicated that over 160 women perished in a fire, with a significant number of women reportedly raped by escaping male prisoners, and that it had not been able to independently verify the figures.

place: between Kalehe and Kavumu, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that between 6 and 8 February 2025, in South Kivu between Kalehe and Kavumu, retreating FARDC forces looted civilian property and a health centre, forcibly enlisted civilians to transport stolen goods, deliberately killed at least 15 civilians and engaged in widespread sexual violence; in the same paragraph it reported that MONUSCO documented the rape of three girls aged 13 to 17 by FARDC soldiers between 31 January and 2 February, without stating where, and that FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported the arrest of alleged perpetrators.

The Group of Experts reported that on 15 February 2025 the withdrawal of FARDC forces from Bukavu led to the escape of over 2,800 detainees and widespread looting, and that on 27 February two explosions at a public meeting hosted by Nangaa in Bukavu killed 17 civilians and wounded 68.

place: Rusayo 1 and 2 IDP camps, Goma outskirts, North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that on 26 January 2025 several bombs launched from positions on the Bulenga peninsula, controlled by RDF, struck the Rusayo 1 and 2 internally displaced persons camps on the outskirts of Goma, killing at least 12 people including children and injuring many others.

The Group of Experts reported that between 28 January and 9 April 2025 it recorded at least 70 distinct incidents of targeted killings in Goma attributable to AFC/M23, resulting in over 200 fatalities, with adult men the majority of victims but also women and children.

The Group of Experts reported that musician and activist Delcat Idengo (real name Delphin Katembo Vinywasiki) was shot and killed by AFC/M23 elements on 13 February 2025 in Goma shortly after publicly criticizing AFC/M23, and that eyewitnesses identified AFC/M23 fighters as responsible. The Group also reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka publicly denied any involvement the same evening, calling the killing a 'score-settling between different factions of the Wazalendo and the FARDC', and reiterated the denial on 12 March 2025.

The Group of Experts reported that Bertrand Bisimwa publicly denied civilian deaths in the fighting for Goma, claiming that all fatalities were combatants, and that the Group stated these claims were contradicted by consistent reports of civilian casualties from residents, humanitarian and medical actors, UN sources, public reporting and photographic and video evidence.

The Group of Experts reported that after the expiration of a seven-day ultimatum issued by AFC/M23 on 11 February 2025, demanding the surrender of members of the FARDC, PNC, Wazalendo and FDLR and urging civilians to denounce them, AFC/M23 intensified house-to-house searches and targeted operations against individuals suspected of affiliation with Wazalendo, FDLR or FARDC.

place: IDP camps west of Goma (city), North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that after taking control of Goma, AFC/M23 forcibly displaced internally displaced persons camps west of the city, ordering civilians to vacate within 72 hours, without ensuring that returns were safe, and that tens of thousands were displaced again.

place: Masisi centre (North Kivu) and Minova (Kalehe, South Kivu)
statement: The Group of Experts reported that on 4 January 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF took control of Masisi centre in North Kivu and retained control despite repeated attempts by Wazalendo, FDLR, the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and FARDC to retake it, and that two weeks later they captured Minova town in Kalehe territory, South Kivu.

place: Sake, Mubambiro and Goma (city), North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that between 21 and 27 January 2025 several columns of RDF troops, each comprising hundreds of well-equipped soldiers, advanced into and seized control of Sake, Mubambiro and Goma town following a coordinated encirclement of each locality, and that Goma was fully conquered on 27 January.

The Group of Experts reported that on 24 January 2025 the Military Governor of North Kivu, Major-General Peter Cirimwami, known for his long-standing ties with FDLR-FOCA, was shot dead in Sake; in its annex 6 the Group says he was shot on 24 January while visiting FARDC and Wazalendo forces in Sake and succumbed to his injuries the following day.

place: Nyabibwe, Kavumu airport and Bukavu (city), South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF broke through the joint FARDC-FDNB positions in Nyabibwe on 6 February 2025, seized the strategic airport of Kavumu on 14 February, and that Bukavu, the provincial capital of South Kivu, was taken on 16 February without combat.

The Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF forces withdrew from Walikale following sustained FARDC airstrikes targeting critical infrastructure including the Kigoma airstrip and mounting international pressure, and that, according to corroborated information, the withdrawal followed a direct instruction from the Government of Rwanda.

place: North Kivu and northern South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that in January and February 2025 a conservative estimate of 6,000 RDF troops, including special forces, were active in North Kivu and northern territories of South Kivu, with a footnote citing former RDF and Rwandan intelligence reporting at least 10,000 RDF troops deployed in eastern DRC, and that by the time of writing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 RDF troops remained active in AFC/M23-controlled territories.

The Group of Experts reported that since 17 February 2025 Uvira experienced a severe breakdown in law and order as the AFC/M23 advance loomed and security forces retreated or lost control, with criminal elements and undisciplined FARDC and Wazalendo engaging in widespread killings, looting and attacks on civilian and humanitarian infrastructure, and that residents reported bodies strewn all over the city.

The Group of Experts reported that from February 2025, as DRC authorities and security actors largely withdrew from Uvira, Wazalendo armed groups de facto controlled Uvira town and surroundings, using disproportionate force and committing widespread abuses, in particular targeting Banyamulenge communities, and that FARDC headquarters and the South Kivu Governorate were reinstalled in Uvira in early March.

The Group of Experts reported (S/2025/446, in its section on Uvira) that a key Wazalendo leader, 'General' Ebuela Mtetezi, was killed by rival Mai Mai groups on 16 March (no year printed; the surrounding paragraph concerns early 2025), reportedly because of his clandestine support to AFC/M23; the sentence cites the Group's earlier report S/2024/432, annex 105.

The Group of Experts reported that Twirwaneho's sanctioned military leader, 'General' Michel Rukunda, was killed by a FARDC CH-4 drone strike on 15 February 2025, and that the following day, after heavy clashes with FARDC, Twirwaneho took control of the Minembwe airstrip, effectively cutting off FARDC resupply in the Hauts Plateaux.

The Group of Experts reported (S/2025/446, paras. 176 and 178) that Charles Sematama assumed the military command of Twirwaneho and on 23 February (no year printed; the sentence cites S/2024/969, para. 106) announced its alliance with AFC/M23, and that in late March AFC/M23 'Colonel' Japhet Gakufe and Charles Sematama arrived in Minembwe with an estimated 200 AFC/M23 combatants.

place: Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux (Minembwe), South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 the majority of 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops were positioned in South Kivu, notably the Ruzizi Plain along the tri-border area and the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that heavy clashes between FDNB supported by FARDC and Wazalendo, and AFC/M23 supported by RDF, resulted in several hundreds of FDNB casualties.

The Group of Experts reported that in February 2025 the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced the readiness of Burundi to fight back, and that Rwanda in turn signalled a commitment to regime change in both Burundi and the DRC.

The Group of Experts reported that in Lubero town on 20 February 2025, after AFC/M23 advances led to heavy clashes and FARDC withdrawals, FARDC elements engaged in systematic looting of civilian homes and shops, and that the next day FARDC issued a public apology, attributing the acts to fleeing, undisciplined soldiers acting in violation of orders and assuring they would face justice.

place: Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that, during operations by RDF and AFC/M23 in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, targeting FDLR and associated armed groups and civilians accused of collaborating with them, RDF and AFC/M23 forces carried out summary executions, arbitrary arrests and detentions, and the deliberate destruction and burning of civilian infrastructure, including homes and villages; and that since operations began in April 2025 UN and humanitarian sources reported over 300 civilians killed in Bwito chiefdom alone, both as collateral casualties and through targeted executions.

place: Binza, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that between 9 and 27 July 2025 over 300 civilian casualties were reported across Binza, notably in Nyamilima, Kisharo, Burambo, Kiseguro, Katwiguro, Musinga and Kigarigari, and that witness accounts, confirmed by photographic and video evidence, indicated civilians were summarily executed following arbitrary accusations of collaboration with FDLR or other Wazalendo armed groups, bodies were frequently disposed of in rivers, and burials were prohibited by local AFC/M23 authorities.

place: Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that in Bwito chiefdom AFC/M23 deployed its newly constituted 'Fourth Brigade', reportedly composed of recent recruits including former Wazalendo and FARDC elements, under the command of Mapenzi, the former leader of NDC-R/M who joined AFC/M23 in March 2025, replacing RDF forces partially redeployed from the area since September.

place: Bibwe (Masisi, North Kivu) and Nzibira (Walungu, South Kivu)
statement: The Group of Experts reported that in mid-September 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF launched operations across northern Masisi, seizing Bibwe and several surrounding localities (an estimated 100 km²) while advancing towards Lukweti, and that on 21 September AFC/M23 captured Nzibira in Walungu territory, South Kivu, a strategic mineral trading hub.

place: Minembwe and Mikenge, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 reinforcements led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, and that a second reinforcement led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Oscar Ndabagaza was blocked while crossing hostile areas before reaching Mikenge at the end of August.

The Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force', named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer, and deployed primarily in Goma and Bukavu.

place: Rumangabo and Tchanzu, North Kivu; AFC/M23-held areas
statement: The Group of Experts reported that systematic forced recruitment intensified in all areas under AFC/M23 occupation, with men and underage boys rounded up, often under the pretext of identity verification or security operations, and that attempted desertion or refusal of orders at training sites such as Rumangabo and Tchanzu led to inhumane punishments and summary executions.

place: Goma and Sake, North Kivu; Rwanda
statement: The Group of Experts reported that on 12 May 2025 AFC/M23 rounded up over 2,000 civilians, mostly Hutu, from collective shelters around Goma and Sake and transferred them under coercive conditions to the UNHCR transit centre in Goma, that 1,798 were subsequently transferred to Rwanda between 17 and 22 May, and that the AFC/M23 focal point for humanitarian affairs, Chantal Murekatete Kayitaba, threatened UNHCR staff to abort screenings. The Group reports that, despite AFC/M23's framing of the operation as a 'voluntary return' of Rwandan nationals, the conditions for voluntary returns were not met.

The Group of Experts reported, in an annex, that in areas under the control of Mai-Mai Yakutumba and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups in Uvira and Fizi territories 'the recent months' were marked by a sharp escalation in human rights violations including conflict-related sexual violence, extortion and summary executions of civilians accused of collaborating with AFC/M23; separately, citing verified reports from field inquiries by UN-supported national NGOs, it said that between January and June 2025 at least 325 cases of sexual violence affecting over 400 victims were documented in South Kivu province alone, exceeding the total recorded in all other provinces combined, with incidents peaking in March.

place: Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
statement: The Group of Experts reported that Wazalendo armed groups in South Kivu entrenched systems of control through an expanding network of roadblocks across Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, where civilians were compelled to pay fees and were subjected to extortion, abuse, sexual violence and summary execution, with at least 12 roadblocks on a 60-kilometre stretch of the RN5 between Uvira and Luvungi.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (eastern DRC)
statement: The Group of Experts reproduced statistics from a UN source on conflict-related sexual violence for July and August 2025 that list M23 as the main perpetrator, surpassing the FARDC and Wazalendo, with a significant number of minor girls among the victims; it also reported that, according to United Nations human rights monitoring statistics, between April and October 2025 AFC/M23 was listed as the main perpetrator of summary executions, responsible for approximately 45 per cent of all summary executions reported across the country.

place: Goma (CBCA Ndosho and Heal Africa hospitals), North Kivu
statement: Reuters (via VOA) reported that U.N. Human Rights Office spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani said in a statement that M23 fighters raided CBCA Ndosho Hospital and Heal Africa Hospital in Goma during the night of 28 February, taking 116 and 15 patients respectively (at least 130 sick and wounded men); the abducted men were suspected of being Democratic Republic of Congo soldiers or members of a pro-government militia known as Wazalendo. Reuters said M23 spokespersons Willy Ngoma and Lawrence Kanyuka Kingston did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Lawrence Kanyuka, political spokesperson of AFC/M23, said the UN statement was false because those arrested in the hospitals were FARDC soldiers who had gone there to hide.

Amnesty International reported that Sultani Makenga, M23's military chief, said in an interview that Congolese army members in hospitals posed as patients or carers, that M23 found 14 weapons in hospitals and that hospital staff alerted them.

Amnesty International said on 18 March 2025 that, since taking Goma in January, the Rwanda-backed M23 had raided hospitals, abducted patients from their beds (civilians and hospitalised Congolese soldiers) and subjected them to torture.

place: Goma and surroundings, North Kivu; South Kivu hospitals
statement: The WHO reported that, since 26 January, 3082 injured and 843 dead had been reported from 31 health facilities in and around Goma, and 65 injuries from 3 hospitals in South Kivu.

Dr Sidibe Abdurahman, emergency physician at CBCA Ndosho hospital, said, as quoted by DW, that since January the hospital had received more than 1,000 patients against a capacity of 146 beds and was totally overwhelmed.
The ICRC reported, from a study of health facilities in the Kivus, that three fifths of the facilities surveyed had experienced looting since the intensification of the conflicts.

The ICRC reported that the majority of medical facilities noted a halving of consultations of children under five in the first quarter of 2025 compared with the same period in 2024, and quoted an observed increase of more than 4 times in the number of stillbirths in the facilities covered by the assessment, particularly in North Kivu.

Louvain Coopération reported that on 9 March 2025 the general hospital of Walungu, South Kivu, one of its partners, was hit by numerous rounds of bullet and rocket fire; five people, patients and health staff, were injured, one seriously; it said the causes of the attack remained uncertain.
UN News reported, in a passage it quoted without naming the speaker, that in South Kivu the number of wounded exceeded the capacity of the hospitals and health centres of Kalehe and Minova.
Human Rights Watch reported that it documented eight cases of rape by M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers against women in and around Uvira during the occupation that began in December 2025.

Human Rights Watch reported that survivors of sexual violence in Uvira spoke of a near-total lack of accessible health services during the M23 and Rwandan occupation, in particular the absence of timely HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and of adequate care for injuries and infections resulting from sexual violence.

Human Rights Watch reported that it documented the summary execution of 53 civilians by the M23 and Rwandan forces in Uvira, most on December 10, 2025, and that the forces went door-to-door seeking men and boys accused of ties to the Wazalendo.
Human Rights Watch reported that the M23 abducted civilians into their forces during the Uvira occupation and that, in at least 12 documented cases, their whereabouts remain unknown.

place: Uvira and Fizi territories (health zones Lemera, Ruzizi, Nundu), South Kivu
statement: AFPDE reported in a humanitarian alert, citing reports from partner structures, that the territories of Uvira and Fizi faced a wave of violence marked by the systematic looting of health infrastructure from 5 December 2025. It said that more than 8 health centres, including KATOGOTA, LUBERIZI, NAZARENO, KILIBA CBCA, I’AMBA/MAKOBOLA, KABIMBA, MUNENE and ABEKA, and 1 hospital (Centre hospitalier d’ABEKA) were vandalised by unknown persons, depriving about 145003 people of all access to care. Elsewhere the same alert gives a total of 7 health structures neutralised, and it dates the Kabimba incident '15/01' with no year.

Opinion-info.cd reported on 30 January 2026 that, according to AFPDE, more than 145 000 people in Uvira and Fizi territories were deprived of access to care following the systematic looting of 'eleven' health structures in the region; the list it prints names twelve (Katogota, Luberizi, Nazareno, Kiliba CBCA, Kigoma, Mutarule, Nyakabere, Iamba/Makobola, Kabimba, Munene, Abeka and the Abeka hospital centre). The article does not name the looters; it says the situation worsened from early December 2025, after military positions at Katogota and Lubarika broke, and that health centres were looted as residents were fleeing.

LeJour reported that the military hospital of Uvira began refurbishment after damage and equipment losses suffered during the occupation and withdrawal of the M23-RDF coalition, and that, according to hospital officials, looting affected beds, mattresses, pharmaceutical cabinets and consumables as well as water and electricity networks.

place: Bitale, Kalehe territory (Bunyakiri health zone), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) announced it had treated about twenty patients wounded in clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo militiamen at the Bitale hospital centre, Kalehe territory, South Kivu.

place: Masisi rural commune, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight reported, citing Actualite, that on 23-24 July 2026 in Masisi rural commune, Masisi territory, North Kivu, pharmacies were forced to close due to clashes between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo fighters, and reopened on 25 July 2026 after security conditions improved.

place: Buleusa, Ikobo groupment, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight reported, citing Actualite, that on 02 August 2026 in Buleusa, Ikobo groupment, Walikale territory, North Kivu, an unspecified number of pharmacies were looted of medicines by Wazalendo fighters during a raid at around 2300hrs.

place: Bulengera commune, Butembo city, North Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight reported that on 27 July 2026 in Bulengera commune, Butembo city, North Kivu, Zawadi Mapendo Health Post was set on fire by unidentified men following rumours that a health worker was deliberately infecting patients or falsely diagnosing them with Ebola.
sources: Insecurity Insight; Le Potentiel; Beto.cd; Actualite.cd

place: Kavikene locality, Congo ya Sika district, Butembo city, North Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight reported that on 28-29 July 2026 in Kavikene locality, Butembo city, North Kivu, Crinovic Hospital Centre was set on fire and destroyed by unidentified perpetrators overnight after its director was accused by local residents of killing patients under the pretext of Ebola.
sources: Insecurity Insight; Le Potentiel; Journal de Kinshasa; Beto.cd

place: Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu (combined figure)
statement: Physicians for Human Rights, citing a Mercy Corps analysis, reported that 68 security incidents targeting the Ebola response were recorded in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu between May 15 and June 30, 2026, including 51 attacks on personnel, health facilities, vehicles or equipment.
sources: Physicians for Human Rights; Crisis Analysis Team; UNICEF

place: Kalinga quarter, Kamituga, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that a 32-year-old woman was raped and then killed by armed men on a date it gives as 'mardi le 13 juillet' in Kamituga, South Kivu, and that, according to civil-society sources, her body was found in the morning in the Kalinga quarter. The Association des femmes journalistes engagées pour la paix (AFJEP) said the rape was committed by unidentified persons and called for an investigation. Actualite.cd described Kamituga as controlled by Wazalendo militiamen allied to the national army ('alliés à l’armée congolaise').

Human Rights Watch reported that in North Kivu M23 armed group fighters raped a 42-year-old woman who reached a hospital within 72 hours, but the hospital had no kits; HRW wrote that the Rwanda-backed M23 controls the area.

place: Masisi Centre, Masisi hospital (HGR), North Kivu
statement: MSF reported that on Sunday 19 January two MSF employees were slightly injured when a rocket hit the MSF garage next to the Masisi general referral hospital (HGR) in North Kivu, that another rocket hit a latrine close to the hospital, and that the hospital and the MSF staff living base were also hit by bullets.
sources: MSF; Human Rights Watch; Voice of America

place: MSF base, Masisi Centre, North Kivu
statement: MSF reported that on a Thursday an MSF employee was very gravely wounded by gunfire that again hit the MSF base at Masisi Centre, and that a child sheltering with his family in the base was also wounded. MSF said fighting between VDP/Wazalendo and M23/AFC fighters had occurred in and around Masisi Centre almost daily since early January.

place: Masisi Centre, near Masisi general referral hospital, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that MSF announced on Saturday 22 February the death of one of its employees, who had been shot the previous Thursday during violent clashes between M23/AFC rebels and VDP/Wazalendo near the Masisi general referral hospital; a statement by MSF quoted by Radio Okapi named him as Jerry Muhindo Kavali, and Radio Okapi said he died aged 49 after more than ten years with MSF. In a later release MSF said a radio operator at its Masisi Centre base was mortally hit on 20 February by gunfire between VDP/Wazalendo and M23/AFC fighters close to the MSF building.

MSF reported that on the evening of 18 April an MSF employee, a nurse at the Masisi general referral hospital, was shot dead at his home in Masisi centre by an armed man in uniform, the second MSF employee shot dead in Masisi centre in two months. MSF said two men in military uniform armed with assault rifles assaulted and extorted civilians in Masisi town before bursting into the MSF employee's home, and reminded all weapon carriers, whom it named, that protecting civilians in conflict is an obligation.
MSF said that since January about fifteen incidents had directly affected teams, ambulances, offices and structures run or supported by MSF.

place: Walikale town and Walikale general hospital, North Kivu
statement: MSF reported that fighting between the FARDC and the M23/AFC and their respective allies reached Walikale town on 19 March, trapping MSF staff at its base and at the hospital, and that violence severely affected access to health care as 80% of the population fled the town and more than 700 displaced people took refuge in Walikale general hospital. MSF's North Kivu programme manager said MSF teams must suspend medical activities when fighting breaks out and cannot move safely.

place: Kibua health zone (Kibua general referral hospital; Mungazi and Kishanga health centres), Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Walikale civil society denounced the systematic looting of several hospitals and health centres by alleged M23 elements between 3 and 4 April 2025, particularly in the Kibua health zone, where the general referral hospital and the Mungazi health centre were stripped of biomedical, administrative and medical equipment, and that Fiston Misona, president of the territorial civil-society coordination, said the rebels dismantled solar panels, took essential medicines and destroyed administrative documents.

place: Walikale health zone, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that 9 of 18 health structures in the Walikale health zone had already been ransacked between 17 and 23 March, during the initial M23 advance.

place: Referral hospitals of Walikale, Itebero, Pinga and Kibua health zones, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the four referral hospitals of the Walikale, Itebero, Pinga and Kibua health zones in North Kivu had suffered 'un pillage massif en janvier dernier' during fighting between the FARDC and the M23 rebels, paralysing many services and causing the loss of essential medical equipment.

place: Binza and Bambo health zones; Kiseguru village; Rutshuru general referral hospital, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: MSF reported that patients from Binza treated at Rutshuru hospital described massacres and summary executions of civilians in the fields east of Virunga National Park, and that 124 intentionally wounded people were treated at Rutshuru general referral hospital in July and August, mostly from the Binza and Bambo health zones. MSF said all survivors name armed men as the perpetrators, some citing the M23 armed group, and that it could not verify the exact number of victims.

place: Muliki health centre, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory) and Bahunde chiefdom (Masisi territory), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to civil society, fighting between AFC-M23 rebels and the FARDC in the Bwito and Bahunde chiefdoms (Rutshuru and Masisi territories) between 28 September and 8 October 2025 caused at least 4 deaths, 13 disappearances and the rape of 8 women; Radio Okapi also reported that the Muliki health centre was looted, along with the theft of about twenty cattle. The source does not say who carried out the rapes or the looting.

place: Biambwe/Byambwe health centre, Lubero territory (Biena health zone), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the toll of the ADF attack in Byambwe/Biambwe, Lubero territory, on the night of Friday 14 November was revised from 20 to 28 killed, including 17 patients executed at the reference health centre, per Lubero territory administrator colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain, who called the figures provisional. A caregiver quoted by Actualite.cd said the maternity ward and operating theatre were burned and medicines looted, and that 17 people including four breastfeeding women were executed in their hospital beds.

place: Byambwe health centre; Mabiango, Tunarudi, Sambalysa; Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: UN News reported that, according to information gathered by MONUSCO, at Byambwe 17 people were shot dead in a health centre, including women patients who had come to give birth, and that in other localities (Mabiango, Tunarudi, Sambalysa) homes were burned, civilians abducted and medical supplies looted, in a wave of ADF attacks that killed at least 89 civilians in Lubero territory between 13 and 19 November.

place: North Kivu (statement issued at UN headquarters)
statement: UN News reported that UN Secretary-General António Guterres, in a press release, 'fermement condamné' (strongly condemned) the attacks attributed to the ADF in North Kivu and expressed his condolences to bereaved families, and that the UN Security Council, in a statement, reaffirmed its 'détermination' to support the peace process and demanded humanitarian access that is 'total, sûr et sans entrave'.

place: Byambwe diocesan health centre (Diocese of Butembo-Beni), Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Vatican News reported that at around 10:00 PM on Friday ADF militants entered the town of Byambwe and attacked a diocesan health centre run by the Sisters of the Presentation, massacred patients and set the facility ablaze, killing several women in the maternity ward. Italian missionary Fr Giovanni Piumatti, who confirmed the attack to Vatican News, was quoted as saying fifteen people were killed in the clinic and another five in the surrounding area, that the attackers set fire to the facility and twenty-seven nearby homes, and that they looted all the medical supplies.

place: Goma and surroundings; MONUSCO camp in Goma, North Kivu
statement: UN News reported, citing OCHA's health cluster, a worsening cholera outbreak in and around Goma, with at least 420 cases and 1 death over two consecutive weeks (3 to 15 February), more than a third of the 1,280 cholera cases recorded in North Kivu since the start of the year, and suspected cholera cases in the MONUSCO camp in Goma where disarmed FARDC members had taken refuge, with one death and 24 suspected cases under treatment.

place: Kalehe, Minova and Miti Murhesa (Kalehe territory), South Kivu
statement: UN News reported that the health cluster said three mpox treatment centres had been destroyed at Kalehe, Minova and Miti Murhesa as a result of bombings.

UN News quoted Dr Boureima Hama Sambo, WHO Representative in DRC, as saying that WHO aid teams 'cannot move freely to support the hospitals, even ambulances cannot run', calling it a public-health nightmare, and he warned that mpox patients had fled at least one camp's treatment centre and were living in host communities.

place: North Kivu; Virunga General Hospital, Goma
statement: Insecurity Insight reported, in an attacks-on-health-care news brief, that since late January reports had increased in North Kivu as M23 rebels expanded control, attacking ambulances and looting vital medical supplies, and that in one incident a baby in an incubator at Virunga General Hospital in Goma was injured by an M23-fired bullet that pierced the ceiling of the neonatal unit during clashes between M23 and the Congolese army.

place: Goma, North Kivu (CBCA Ndosho and Heal Africa hospitals)
statement: The EastAfrican reported that the AFC (Congo River Alliance) 'strongly denies' the UN human rights office's allegations of attacks on hospitals, saying it never targeted civilian establishments, that the UN mission MONUSCO had manipulated the details, and that its raid was aimed at securing medical infrastructure it said had been infiltrated by fighters; the AFC claimed the heads of the hospitals corroborated in the operation.

place: Centre hospitalier La Providence, Vukonderya cell, Bulengera commune, Butembo, North Kivu
statement: Radio Télévision Communautaire la Référence (RTCR) reported that in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 25 June 2025 presumed armed bandits visited several homes and the Centre hospitalier La Providence in the Kamesimbonzo quarter, Bulengera commune, Butembo, and that, according to John Kameta, president of the Bulengera communal civil-society core, two of the bandits came into the hospital around midnight and took one hundred thousand Congolese francs belonging to patients, as well as telephones.

place: Ludaha village, Cirunga group, Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight, citing Radio Maendeleo, reported that on 10-11 August 2025 the Ludaha Health Centre in Ludaha village, Cirunga group, Kabare territory, South Kivu, was looted overnight by armed men who took medical equipment including a microscope, a printer, telephones and money; nurses and other health workers were also attacked while treating patients.

place: Katana village, Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight, citing Radio Maendeleo and RTR, reported that on 11 August 2025 in Katana village, Kabare territory, South Kivu, a hospital under construction was destroyed by the local population, who also looted the residence of the vice-president of the Senate, and that AFC/M23 rebels had reportedly asked residents to attack his properties because, according to them, he was serving his individual interests.

place: Panzi General Hospital, Panzi district, Ibanda commune, Bukavu, South Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight, citing La Prunelle and Radio Okapi, reported that on 14 August 2025, around 7pm, the water tank at Panzi General Hospital in Panzi district, Ibanda commune, Bukavu, was damaged amid heavy gunfire by unidentified gunmen; the leak flooded a large part of the hospital grounds and disrupted medical activities. It added that a fruit vendor was shot and killed by a stray bullet.

place: Kasheke village, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight reported that on 6 November 2025 in Kasheke village, Kalehe territory, South Kivu, three health workers from the General Reference Hospital were attacked and seriously injured by M23 rebels on accusations of treating Wazalendo fighters and their families, and the medical director was evacuated to Bukavu for intensive care treatment.

place: Chahoboka Health Centre, Katana town, Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight, citing only unnamed personal communications, reported that on 22 November 2025 in Katana town, Kabare territory, South Kivu, the Chahoboka Health Centre was attacked by M23 members when they raided the town, and four people, including two health workers and a patient, were taken outside and shot and killed.

place: Baraka port, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight, citing OCHA DRC, reported that as of 17 November 2025 a shipment of medicines belonging to an international organisation was blocked at Baraka port, Fizi territory, South Kivu, delaying operations and causing a shortage of medicines and supplies in the health facilities the organisation supported.

place: South Kivu (provincial authorities in Uvira intervened); exact place not given
statement: Insecurity Insight reported that Forces de défense nationales du Burundi (FDNB) soldiers stopped a truck of a local NGO transporting materials to support medical facilities in the fight against cholera in South Kivu and forced it to turn back, despite an intervention by provincial authorities in Uvira.

place: a hospital in South Kivu (not named by the source)
statement: Insecurity Insight reported that in March 2025 M23 fighters occupied a hospital in South Kivu and installed artillery to defend themselves against attacks from local armed groups.

place: a general hospital in South Kivu (not named by the source)
statement: Insecurity Insight reported that in South Kivu five health workers and four patients, including one child, were killed when a hospital was hit by shelling of an unidentified origin.

place: Walungu Hospital, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: The UN Fact-Finding Mission on North and South Kivu reported that on 9 March a shell reportedly hit the pediatric ward of Walungu Hospital, killing five people including two children.

place: Eastern DRC; half of incidents in South Kivu, mostly Kalehe and Shabunda territories
statement: Insecurity Insight reported that between February and November 2025, 41 health workers were kidnapped in 20 incidents in eastern DRC, and that half of the recorded kidnapping incidents occurred in South Kivu, most of them in the Kalehe and Shabunda territories.

place: Eastern DRC (place not given by the source)
statement: Insecurity Insight reported that, among health workers kidnapped in eastern DRC in 2025, a nurse was raped then kidnapped by men armed with guns and taken away to an undisclosed location.

place: Mulima (45 km north of Fizi centre), serving the Minembwe and Itombwe health zones, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, in an article on an OCHA bulletin, wrote that in June 2025 consignments of medicines intended for health structures in the Minembwe and Itombwe health zones in South Kivu were blocked at Mulima (45 km north of Fizi centre) for about two months.

place: Minembwe General Reference Hospital, Minembwe, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post, relaying an OCHA communiqué, reported that the health system in the Minembwe area was on the verge of collapse with a prolonged shortage of medicines, and that at Minembwe General Reference Hospital between July and September 2025 more than 60% of deaths concerned children.

place: Uvira General Hospital, Uvira, South Kivu
statement: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) reported that heavy violence and clashes broke out in Uvira in February 2025 between the Congolese army (FARDC) and their presumed allies, the Wazalendo fighters, and quoted a mother who said they heard gunshots inside the hospital where her 10-month-old son was admitted at the mpox treatment centre of Uvira General Hospital.

MSF reported that persistent insecurity on the road linking Bukavu, Kamanyola and Uvira made it practically impossible for humanitarian organisations to move between the two sides of the front line, and that humanitarian aid now had to transit through several countries to reach the populations on each side.

place: Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, South Kivu (Muku, Mulambi)
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing a nurse it contacted, that in the Kamisimbi grouping (Walungu territory, South Kivu), where AFC/M23 troops and Wazalendo fought repeatedly, only Kamisimbi hospital remained functional while Muku hospital, Mulambi health centre and several other structures had closed.

place: Lubero centre (Lubero), Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the NGO EADEV, based in Lubero, in a report, noted about twenty cases of rape of displaced women in Lubero centre recorded over two weeks, and said the perpetrators were men in uniform who abuse the women in the fields where they go to look for food; an EADEV focal point was quoted as saying 18 cases of rape were recorded in the last week of December 2024 and the first week of January 2025.

place: Vuhato, Kayna health zone, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: OCHA reported, citing local sources, that in the night of 5 to 6 April armed elements allegedly raped at least 32 women and abducted nine young men during an attack on the village of Vuhato in the Kayna health zone.

place: Kipese and Katondi, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that M23 rebels took control on Thursday 20 February of the agglomeration of Kipese and Katondi in Lubero territory, and that, according to local sources, M23 fighters were visible in the area the previous evening.

place: Kitsumbiro; Lubero centre, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the capture of Kipese and Katondi followed the fall of Kitsumbiro, also controlled by the M23, and that the Congolese army and Wazalendo were visible in Lubero centre, about twenty kilometres from the front lines.

place: Lubero centre, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that scenes of looting were recorded in the area of Lubero centre, and that traders accused some alleged FARDC soldiers of being the perpetrators of the looting of shops and stores.

place: Beni (presentation); captured south of Lubero, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the army presented a soldier, described as Rwandan, captured south of Lubero during fighting against the M23 rebels, which the source describes as backed by Rwanda.

Radio Okapi reported that Colonel Mak Hazukay, spokesperson for the Front Nord operations, assured that all persons captured or who surrendered would be treated in accordance with the principles of international humanitarian law.

Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC presented in Beni two VDP (Wazalendo) of the Maï-Maï group Force des patriotes pour la paix/Armée du peuple (FPP/AP), led by the self-proclaimed general Kabido, who surrendered to the FARDC following their leader's rallying to the M23.

Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a public declaration from Mbwavinywa, three armed groups announced their break with Kinshasa to join the M23/AFC: the FPP/AP of the self-proclaimed general Kabido, the NDC-R/M and Maï-Maï Kifuafua.

BETO reported that the self-proclaimed general Kabido, head of the FPP/AP armed group, was arrested on Thursday 12 June in Butembo, as confirmed by the coordinator of the VDP Wazalendo/Front Nord, loyal to the FARDC.

place: Muhangi (also Mapanga), Bulengya grouping, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local civil society, about thirty civilians were killed on Wednesday 15 January by ADF rebels at Muhangi, about a hundred kilometres from Lubero Centre, a provisional toll; local sources said the ADF attacked Muhangi at around 4 pm and killed thirty-two civilians with machetes, among them the head of the Bulengya grouping, who was killed at Mapanga, a neighbouring village.

place: Lumba, Mwenye grouping, Lubero territory, 35 km north-west of Butembo, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the toll of the attack attributed to ADF rebels on Wednesday at Lumba, 35 km north-west of Butembo, rose from six to twelve civilians killed according to civil society, which said several others were missing.

place: Bambuba-Kisiki grouping (Mbau), Beni territory, North Kivu
