statement: Radio Okapi reported that at least 16 people died in ADF rebel attacks during January in the Bambuba-Kisiki grouping, Beni territory, and that, according to local sources, the assailants also burned dozens of houses; the local sector chief welcomed the presence of MONUSCO peacekeepers installed for a week at Mbau to protect civilians.

place: Beni (handover); several localities of Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on Friday 11 April the FARDC handed to Beni civil society about forty civilians, former ADF hostages, including 13 women and 8 children, who it said were freed in clashes between the ADF and joint FARDC-UPDF forces in several localities of Lubero territory.

place: Beni and Butembo; withdrawal from Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that in Beni and Butembo social groups rose up to protest the withdrawal from Lubero of the Ugandan soldiers deployed in the DRC under the joint FARDC-UPDF operations.

place: Kanune, Luhanga and Mbwavinywa, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: OCHA reported that on 9 and 10 April armed violence broke out in the localities of Kanune and Luhanga, then Mbwavinywa, where two civilians died, displacing about 4,000 people towards Bunyatenge and Masika.

place: Kanyabayonga, Kayna and Lubero health zones, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, relaying an OCHA report, reported that on 13 April one person was killed at Kanyabayonga after stepping on an unexploded device, and that, according to humanitarian partners, the Kayna and Lubero health zones recorded four explosive-remnant incidents with at least 10 civilians killed since January.

Actualite.cd reported that the Butembo-Lubero garrison military tribunal convicted 25 people, including 24 soldiers and one civilian, after mobile hearings held from 26 June to 8 July 2025 in Lubero-centre: two soldiers were sentenced to death and, per MONUSCO, the others to 5 to 20 years; the defendants were prosecuted for serious human rights violations including sexual violence, notably 14 cases of rape of minors, and murders of civilians.

place: Muhola hill, Baswagha chiefdom (Lubero), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC and the Ugandan army (UPDF) retook control of Muhola hill in Baswagha chiefdom on Friday 4 July, described as a stronghold of a Maï-Maï group led by a commander nicknamed « Le Blanc », a week after intense fighting.

place: Mabambi, Kalundu, Kivugha and Maboya (Lubero), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, a week after the launch of the joint offensive, regular forces retook control of several localities south of Lubero, including Mabambi, Kalundu, Kivugha and Maboya, that the fighting caused major displacement of local populations, and that the targeted Maï-Maï group is accused by local authorities of multiple abuses against civilians.

place: Bandulu (Lubero) and the Bapere sector, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, quoting an OCHA monthly report, reported that on 18 July suspected ADF abducted 14 people in the locality of Bandulu, of whom seven hostages have since escaped, and that three days earlier 15 people had been abducted in the Bapere sector.

place: Senga and Katanga villages (Lubero), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, quoting an OCHA monthly report, reported that on 11 July, in the villages of Senga and Katanga, 11 people were killed and six others wounded by bladed weapons.

place: Oicha-Eringeti axis and Mangina (Beni), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, citing OCHA, reported that suspected ADF killed at least seven civilians in the village of Kinyamuseghe, Beni territory, on the night of 11 to 12 July, that more than 20 people were killed the same week in localities bordering Ituri, and that these incidents displaced more than 55,000 people (8,389 households) towards the Oicha-Eringeti axis and Mangina.

place: several localities of Beni and Lubero territories, North Kivu
statement: MONUSCO said in a press release that attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) between 9 and 16 August 2025 in several localities of Beni and Lubero territories killed at least 52 civilians, including eight women and two children, one of whom was a young girl, and that the death toll may rise; it said the violence was accompanied by abductions, looting and the burning of homes, vehicles and motorcycles.

place: Mayi-Moya, North Kivu (territory not stated by the source)
statement: MONUSCO said that on 13 and 14 August, during incidents in Mayi-Moya (North Kivu), it provided physical protection to 206 civilians, including 70 women and 93 children, who sought refuge at its military base.

place: Ntoyo village, near Manguredjipa (Lubero), North Kivu
statement: The UN Humanitarian Coordinator in the DRC, Bruno Lemarquis, said he strongly condemned two armed attacks by the ADF during the night of 8 to 9 September 2025 against civilians in North Kivu, the first in the village of Ntoyo, Lubero territory, which he said claimed the lives of at least 71 people; an OCHA advocacy note of 9 December said attacks attributed to suspected ADF elements killed at least 70 civilians at Ntoyo while they were holding a funeral wake.

place: Ntoyo, less than seven km from Manguredjipa, Bapere sector (Lubero), North Kivu
statement: DW reported that ADF rebels surprised residents gathered for a funeral wake at Ntoyo, and quoted Alain Kiwewa, military administrator of Lubero, as saying that 71 bodies had been found on site with their throats cut, 14 houses had been burned and there were about fifteen wounded.
DW reported that the Congolese army confirmed the ADF attack at Ntoyo and that military authorities in charge of operations against the ADF went to the site to reassure the population.

An Amnesty International researcher wrote that she travelled to Butembo to speak with survivors of the 8 September massacre in Ntoyo village, where, in her account, fighters killed more than 60 people, many of whom were attending a funeral wake, and witnesses told her ADF members had mingled among mourners for hours before striking people's heads with hammers.

place: North Kivu (and Ituri); ADF camps, location not stated
statement: An Amnesty International researcher wrote (December 2025) that the ADF are abducting and killing civilians and abusing women and girls as sexual slaves in North Kivu and Ituri provinces, and that she spoke to six survivors among the girls and women abducted by the group and forced into "marriages" with ADF fighters, who said they had been told the "choice" was to accept or be killed, and most of whom escaped after FARDC and UPDF operations that targeted their camps; the piece does not say when or where these survivors were abducted.

An Amnesty International researcher wrote that witnesses told her ADF fighters arrived at Byambwe as a nondescript group including women and children, asking for directions to the local hospital, after which gunshots rang out at the medical facility, and that in total the fighters killed more than 30 people, including 17 at the health facility.
sources: Amnesty International; UN News; AP; Radio Okapi

place: Biambwe, Biena, Kaumo, Masengi and Masoyi (Lubero), North Kivu
statement: 7sur7.cd reported, citing local civil society, that five reference health centres in Lubero territory, in the Manzia and Mwenye groupements, had stopped operating because of repeated ADF attacks; the head of Biambwe civil society, Nzanzu Achille, said that since the Biambwe attack the health centres of Biambwe, Biena, Kaumo, Masengi and Masoyi were closed.

place: Biena and Manguredjipa health zones (Butembo-Manguredjipa axis, Lubero), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that after the ADF attack on the Biambwe hospital, health services in the Biena and Manguredjipa health zones were slowed, and an anonymous health worker of the Biena health zone said colleagues were hesitant to resume work for fear for their safety.

Radio Okapi reported that fighting broke out on Sunday 26 October at Kalangira, in Baswagha chiefdom, between armed youths identified as Wazalendo and AFC/M23 rebels; according to the North Kivu governor the FARDC were not involved, and the incident was reportedly linked to an attempt to free three notables abducted five days earlier by an AFC/M23 official.

Radio Okapi reported that the North Kivu governor denounced the installation of new AFC/M23 positions at Vuvatama and Kanyamitala, warned of the risk of a resumption of hostilities and reaffirmed the FARDC's determination to defend their positions in case of attack.

place: Buffer zone south of Lubero-Centre (Lubero), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Kalangira clashes took place near the buffer zone controlled by the Ugandan army, deployed for eight months to contain the rebels' advance towards Lubero-Centre.

place: Mbingi and Bunyatenge (Batangi chiefdom), Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that large AFC/M23 reinforcements had been reported since Sunday 15 March in the south-west of Lubero territory, where the rebels had occupied many villages for several months; that, according to its sources, vehicle shuttles carrying men and materiel had been observed for about two weeks at Mbingi and at Bunyatenge; and that security sources confirmed the arrival of the reinforcements and said it could be preparation for offensives against FARDC and Maï-Maï positions in the Kanyabayonga groupement.

place: Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi, Kipese; Alimbongo, Kirumba, Kanyabayonga; Lubero territory
statement: Anadolu Agency, relaying Radio Okapi citing security sources, reported that AFC/M23 rebels began moving out on Monday from several villages in Lubero territory that they had occupied for more than a year, and that after leaving Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese they were said to have set up camps in the Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga areas.

Anadolu Agency reported that North Kivu Governor Evariste Kakule Somo told local media in Lubero on Thursday that he had observed an 'effective withdrawal' from several areas, called on the population to stay calm and said the rebel movement was part of 'the implementation of the peace agreements, notably those negotiated under US auspices'.

place: Musenge village, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that at least fourteen houses, a health centre and part of the Catholic church of Musenge, Baswagha chiefdom, south Lubero territory, were burned on Monday 26 January at around 20 heures (as printed) in an attack attributed to the ADF, and that two soldiers died during the army's counter-attack; Lubero territory administrator Colonel Alain Kiwewa was quoted as saying that no civilian death had been recorded so far and that the village had been emptied of its population.

place: Musenge village, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the village of Musenge, Baswagha chiefdom, was attacked in the night of Saturday to Sunday 25 January 2026, in attacks it attributed to ADF fighters, and that according to local 'forces vives' at least 25 civilians were killed, 63 houses burned, two motorbikes burned and one person seriously wounded.

place: Musenge village, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Lubero territory administrator Colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain said that since the night of 24 January 2026 the ADF had carried out a deadly attack on Musenge village, burning almost the whole village, a health centre and a Catholic church, and that two soldiers were found burned.

place: Mambimbi-Isigo, Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the president of Bapere civil society Kakule Kagheni Samuel, six more bodies were found on Monday, bringing to 21 the number of civilian victims of the attack attributed to the ADF at Mambimbi-Isigo (Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector), carried out in the night of Friday 6 to Saturday 7 February 2026; several people remained missing.

place: Malibo, Oicha-Mamove axis, Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, in a passage saying that ADF violence had also intensified in neighbouring Beni territory, reported that six civilians were killed in an ambush at Malibo on the Oicha–Mamove road in the evening of 'mardi 4 février 2026' (as printed; that weekday and date do not match), a few hours after another ambush on the same stretch that killed four others, making at least ten civilians killed in a single day on that road, where several motorbikes were also burned.

place: Ntoyo, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Ntoyo health centre, Lubero territory, had reopened and resumed its activities five days earlier, six months after a deadly attack attributed to the ADF; that it had been forced to close after the attack of 8 September 2025, which local authorities said killed more than 100 civilians; that a large part of its medical equipment and medicines had been looted or destroyed in that incursion; and that consultations remained limited by shortages of medicines and equipment, which deputy head nurse Joseph Lungabo said complicated care for residents who had returned.

place: ADF camps and affected areas, eastern DRC (report covers North Kivu and Ituri)
statement: Amnesty International reported that it interviewed five women and two girls who were abducted by the ADF and forced into 'marriages', and that interviewees mentioned incidents of sexual violence by ADF fighters towards women and girls outside of 'marriage'.

place: Byambwe village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Amnesty International reported that the ADF has repeatedly attacked health facilities and raided supplies, and that in November 2025 a health centre in the village of Byambwe was targeted, with at least 17 civilians killed and four wards set on fire.

place: Wayene, Bulengera commune; Kafekit compound; trial at Kitulu roundabout, Mususa commune, Butembo
statement: Radio Moto Butembo (RMBB) reported that the flagrante-delicto hearing of the Butembo garrison military tribunal against four people, two of them Wazalendo, continued on Wednesday 24 June 2026 at the Kitulu roundabout, Mususa commune, Butembo; that the defendants were being prosecuted for criminal association, abduction and extortion; and that they were accused of having arrested Egyptian itinerant traders and 9 other Congolese citizens, including 6 girls, on Monday 22 June at Wayene and taking them, some tied up, to the Kafekit compound, where some were subjected to torture.

place: Vuhakatwa, Wayene quarter, Bulengera commune, Butembo city
statement: Radio Elimu UOR (Butembo) reported that the Butembo garrison military tribunal sentenced to death on Thursday 25 June 2026 four defendants (named in the source and listed in entities_named), whom the prosecution had pursued, two of them as Wazalendo, for criminal association, abductions followed by torture, and extortion, in the case of the abduction of 3 Egyptians and 9 Congolese; the defence said it would appeal.

Radio Moto Butembo reported that the World Food Programme launched a food distribution at Lubero-centre on Tuesday 26 May for displaced people and host families affected by the M23 advance in the south of the territory and by massacres attributed to alleged ADF, and that Lubero-centre had for months received displaced people from Kanyabayonga, Kirumba, Mathembe, Vutsorovya, Hutwe and Alimbongo.

place: Bashu chiefdom (Kitovo, Misugho, Rwamiso) and north of Butembo, North Kivu
statement: Grands Lacs News reported that between 1 and 4 January 2026, armed clashes broke out between Wazalendo factions in the Bashu chiefdom and north of Butembo city, pitting the group of self-proclaimed general Tango Fort against the Maï-maï Wazalendo RNL led by Baraka Lolwako, with a certain Fiston Nzoli reportedly involved, and that according to local sources several Tango Fort camps at Kitovo, Misugho and Rwamiso were burned.

place: Lwamiso camp, Bashu chiefdom, North Kivu
statement: Grands Lacs News reported that the Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord claimed the January 2026 operations against Tango Fort, saying it wanted to neutralise him and his supporters, accused of illegal detentions, torture, killings and arbitrary taxation, and that it welcomed the release of at least 11 illegally detained people, including minors, during the attack on the Lwamiso camp.

place: Kanyabayonga, Kayina, Kirumba (Lubero territory), North Kivu
statement: Agence congolaise de presse (ACP) reported, in a dispatch from Lubero, that three large agglomerations of Lubero territory (Kanyabayonga, Kayina and Kirumba) are occupied by M23 rebels supported by Rwanda.

Bwiza reported that, in Lubero where the AFC/M23 permanent secretary was visiting development projects, he told residents of Kanyabayonga that they would not be abandoned and said: 'we are still here, we are going nowhere', rejecting social-media claims that the group would leave.

place: Beni city and surroundings, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the local rights organisation Le Cri des victimes du Congo (CVC), in a statement on Sunday 19 July, expressed concern at a resurgence of armed attacks, killings of civilians and incursions attributed notably to ADF rebels in and around Beni city, and called for an independent investigation; Radio Okapi had not obtained a reaction from FARDC.

place: Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that local civil society said on Tuesday 18 August that more than 2 400 people had been killed in two years in the Bapere sector, Lubero territory, attributing the killings to the ADF.

place: Vyanze (Kirivu hill), Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that Wazalendo/VDP and AFC/M23 fighters clashed at Vyanze, Lubero territory, on Wednesday 30 September 2026 from 4 am to about 10 am; according to concordant sources, Wazalendo temporarily dislodged M23 from the Kirivu hill position before advancing to the centre of Vyanze, then withdrew for lack of ammunition after M23 returned. No casualty figure was communicated.

place: Musundi and Hutwe groupements (Kandole, Kirivu, Vyanze), Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that fighting between Wazalendu and M23-AFC continued on Thursday 1 October 2026 in the groupements of Musundi and Hutwe (Batangi and Bamate chiefdoms, Lubero territory); sources said Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie had reportedly recovered Kandole and Kirivu, and that a large rebel reinforcement had reportedly come from Kitsombiro via Kasusa and Luvererya towards Vyanze.

place: Kalimba, Kiribata, Vusesa, Vungulo (Lubero territory), North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that, according to sources contacted on the spot, residents moved towards Kalimba, Kiribata, Vusesa and Vungulo, and that more than a thousand households had already been recorded in these reception areas since Wednesday 30 September.

place: Majengo-Musigha / Kasugho, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that five presumed M23 fighters surrendered to Wazalendu (VDP) in Lubero territory during the week and were handed on 1 October to security services at Kasugho, after reaching a Wazalendo position at Majengo-Musigha; the VDP Front Grand-Nord synergy spokesperson John Mahangaiko made the announcement.

place: Majengo-Musigha / Muhungama-Mitoto, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that the five presumed M23 fighters who surrendered in Lubero territory said, in their testimony, that they were former soldiers captured and forcibly enrolled during the fall of Goma to the M23.

place: Kasenye-Lima, Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that the 'kapita' Kombi Lwayivweka, 38, was arrested by presumed Wazalendu of the MDPC group of general Kaganga for not bringing food to the fighters, taken to their camp, tortured and whipped, and released on Tuesday 22 September after local authorities intervened; according to the radio's sources his release was obtained for payment of USD 50 and a hen.

place: Vulamba commune, Butembo city, North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that the coordinator of DYFEGOU said community alerts had reported human rights violations by Wazalendu, including the enrolment of minors into the VDP and rapes of women and girls; that DYFEGOU had registered five cases since the beginning of August, taking Vulamba commune (Butembo) as a sample, one of them almost in the town centre; and that police authorities told the organisation the armed perpetrators were said to be Wazalendo.

Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that Rose Kahambu Tuombeane, coordinator of DYFEGOU, said her organisation had received community alerts denouncing human rights violations by the Wazalendu, and cited among them the enrolment of minors into the ranks of the VDP; DYFEGOU said it remained available to help reintegrate the children enrolled in the VDP.

place: Kimemi and Vulamba communes, Butembo city, North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that Maître Muhindo Wasivinywa, coordinator of the REDHO human rights network in Butembo, said in an interview on Saturday 24 October 2026 that there are incursions into the city, notably in Kimemi and Vulamba communes, now accompanied by sexual violence, that his group had recorded more than nine rape cases, and that incursions were previously not accompanied by rape.

place: Butembo city, North Kivu (complaint filed in Beni)
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that the North Kivu Bar lodged a complaint on Tuesday 20 October 2026 at the Auditorat militaire supérieur in Beni against chief superintendent Georges Ngonzila, commander of the PNC in Butembo city, over alleged arbitrary arrests, torture, and blows and injuries against lawyer Me Papy Wakilongo on Saturday 17 October 2026; the officer's hierarchy was said to have taken up the case.

Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that Me Wivine Kavira Burutere, a member of the North Kivu Bar council, said that in the same circumstances another person, a woman, was also assaulted ('violentée') by the same officer, who according to her allegedly touched the woman's intimate parts; she said: « Les éléments de preuve sont réunis pour qualifier l’infraction de viol ».

place: Kyambya and Bulengera cells, Bulengera commune, Butembo city, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that local civil society (Société Civile Forces Vives de Bulengera) said armed bandits in civilian clothes raided households in Kyambya and Bulengera cells, Bulengera commune (Butembo), around 1 am in the night of 26-27 September, wounding three people by bullets and machete, beating and tying up others, and taking more than USD 1 400 and valuables, without intervention by law enforcement.

place: Butembo city (Kyaghala quarter / Bulengera commune), North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué released on a Monday, the Butembo civil society organisation SOCICO denounced 'violent resistance' by a group of people against health workers of the Ebola response, saying a team member was seriously wounded on the hand and knee by machete, the response vehicle was stoned, and sampling and body-securing activities were interrupted.

Radio Okapi reported that its reporter observed on Wednesday 8 July 2026 that, more than a year after violent fighting in Alimbongo (Lubero territory), the Alimbongo health centre still showed roofs torn off and walls pierced by shell fragments from past bombardments, and the Bureau central de la zone de santé had been heavily hit by strikes and relocated to makeshift premises; the outlet does not date the fighting or say who fired.

place: Muhila, near Butuhe, Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported, citing civil-society sources in that part of Beni territory, that a person identified in the headline as an ANR chief at Butuhe was killed on Tuesday 27 October 2026 around 17 heures at Muhila, near the Butembo Saibu industrial soap factory, while returning from a work mission at Kivira village.

place: Makumo, Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that gunfire was heard at Makumo, a mining village in Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, on the evening of Tuesday 27 October 2026, and that sources on the spot said presumed ADF fighters led by their rebel chief Abou Wakas tried to attack the village but were repelled by the FARDC-Wazalendu coalition; no toll was available.

Kivu Morning Post reported that a 'ville morte' (general stay-at-home strike) was observed on Tuesday 11 August in Butembo after a call by youth of citizen movements and pressure groups, who denounced insecurity and the desecration of the tomb of the artist Delcat Idinco and demanded the release of activist Clovis Mutsuva, detained in Beni; the page adds that the call was launched by youths claiming to be of LUCHA to denounce killings of civilians attributed to the ADF.

AFP reported, citing several UN and security sources, that M23 fighters and more than 3,500 Rwandan soldiers (according to the UN) entered Goma on Sunday, which they had been besieging for several days.
Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said on Monday in a statement posted on X that the government continued to work to avoid carnage and loss of life, as reported by AFP.

BBC News Afrique reported that the Minister of Rural Development, Muhindo Nzangi, said the DRC army controlled 80% of the city of Goma on Monday evening while M23 had taken only a few areas on the outskirts.

Congolese newspaper L'Avenir reported that President Félix Tshisekedi, in a live address on RTNC on Wednesday 29 January 2025, called on Congolese to show resistance and resilience in the face of an unprecedented worsening of the security situation in the east, which it said he attributed to Rwandan defence forces supporting the M23.

place: North Kivu (place not stated in these excerpts; Kasengezi per M23 and Sake per Rwanda in other claims)
statement: DW reported that the military governor of North Kivu, général major Peter Cirimwami, was shot during a field visit on Thursday, and that different sources disagreed on whether he was dead or alive; Jeune Afrique reported that the army spokesperson confirmed his death on 24 January.

DW reported that, according to the M23, military governor Peter Cirimwami had been seriously wounded at Kasengezi while on his way to the front line, which DW said was difficult to verify; DW added that the Congolese government had still not communicated on the matter.

The Rwandan foreign ministry said in a statement dated 26 January 2025 that the recent heavy fighting around Goma was triggered by constant ceasefire violations by the FARDC in coalition with the FDLR, European mercenaries, Wazalendo, Burundian armed forces, SAMIDRC forces and MONUSCO troops.

The Rwandan foreign ministry said in a statement that the late Maj Gen Peter Cirimwami, Military Governor of North Kivu, who it said was killed during fighting around Sake, served as liaison with the FDLR, citing UN reports.

place: Goma, North Kivu (context: SADC summit statement)
statement: Rwanda's foreign ministry said on 2 February 2025 that it rejected the accusations against the Rwanda Defence Force made in the statement of the SADC extraordinary summit of 31 January 2025, and said the RDF does not attack civilians.

UN News (Swahili) reported that Mr Lacroix, speaking to journalists, confirmed the deaths of three MONUSCO peacekeepers (one from Uruguay, two from South Africa) and wished a quick recovery to 12 other peacekeepers wounded during clashes with M23 rebels.
BBC News Gahuza reported that at least 19 soldiers from South Africa, Malawi and Tanzania were killed when the M23 took the city of Goma in January.

Studio Hirondelle reported that Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, at a briefing in Kinshasa on 3 February, speaking of the massacre and carnage committed in Goma, said that his colleague the Health Minister had been told by his services that morning that there were more than 2,000 bodies to bury.
BBC News Afrique reported that the UN said at least 2,900 people were killed in the fighting, that 2,000 bodies had been buried and that 900 others were still in the city's morgues.

BBC News reported that at least 700 people in Goma were killed and close to 3,000 injured as the rebels clashed with the DR Congo army and its allies, according to the UN and the Congolese government.

place: Munzenze central prison, Goma (city), North Kivu
statement: BBC News Afrique reported that, according to an internal UN document it consulted, between 165 and 167 women were assaulted by male detainees during the escape from Munzenze prison in Goma, and that most of the women were killed after detainees set fire to the prison; the BBC said it could not verify the information.

place: Munzenze central prison, Goma (city), North Kivu
statement: Belga, in La Libre, reported that a local official told the German news agency DPA that at least 160 female detainees were raped during an escape from the Goma prison; Belga added that it was not yet known whether the rapists were escaped prisoners, M23 rebels or members of other local militias.

place: Goma (city), North Kivu; Bukavu and Kabare, South Kivu
statement: UN News reported that the destruction of prisons caused by the offensive led to the escape of many prisoners from the central prisons of Goma and Bukavu, and also in Kabare in South Kivu; Patrice Vahard, director of the BCNUDH, said in an interview with UN News on Wednesday evening that escapees may include people imprisoned for atrocities, notably rape and gender-based violence.

MSF's emergency coordinator in Goma said that on Wednesday 29 January, the first day the fighting had eased, the team received nearly 140 wounded at the hospital triage, many of whom were hospitalised, and that wounded people who had stayed at home had been unable to access care until then.

The Guardian reported that Chadrack Kabumba, 20, was treated at Virunga hospital for bullet wounds to his knee and shoulders after being shot four times on his way to check whether his property had been vandalised, the day after M23 entered Goma.

place: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
statement: Amnesty International said on 18 March 2025 that armed M23 fighters stormed the Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals in Goma on the night of 28 February and the morning of 3 March and abducted more than 130 people, including Congolese soldiers (some wounded) and health workers, who were taken to a stadium where some were tortured. Amnesty also reported that M23 military chief Sultani Makenga had said in an interview that Congolese army members in the hospitals were posing as patients or carers, that M23 had found 14 weapons in hospitals and that hospital staff had alerted them, and that M23 had arrested those who were not part of the hospital.

place: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, relaying Amnesty International, reported that armed M23 fighters burst into the Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals in Goma on the night of 28 February and the morning of 3 March, abducting more than 130 people including wounded Congolese soldiers and health workers who, according to Amnesty, were taken by force to a stadium where some were tortured. Actualite.cd also reported that M23 military chief Sultani Makenga said some of the abducted soldiers had posed as patients or carers, that his group had found 14 weapons in the hospitals, and justified the abductions by saying medical staff had reported the presence of Congolese soldiers.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (places of individual cases not stated in the excerpts)
statement: Amnesty International said humanitarian organisations had reported a sharp rise in rape and sexual violence in North Kivu and South Kivu, and that victims told it they were raped by M23 fighters and threatened with death; in one account, a woman said M23 fighters suspected her of being a spy and five armed fighters in military uniforms raped her collectively; in another case, two men in Congolese military uniform raped a pregnant woman and abducted her husband.

UN News reported that UNFPA's country representative Mady Biaye said that the 895 rape cases reported by UNHCR for the first half of February concerned only survivors who received medical care at the 23 UNFPA-supported sites in Goma.

place: Eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu; places not itemised in the excerpt)
statement: UN News reported looting of contraceptives, damaged health centres and depleted aid stocks as sexual violence proliferated in eastern DRC, with tens of thousands of women and girls struggling to access emergency care; UNFPA's DRC representative Mady Biaye said UNFPA health infrastructure in Goma had been damaged by the fighting and its Goma warehouse looted (no perpetrator named). The article set the US decision in January to suspend almost all foreign aid programmes for three months against these difficulties; Biaye said the US had been due to contribute 10 million dollars in 2025 for contraceptives in the DRC, 'Mais tout ça c'est arrêté', and the article notes that contraceptive stock-outs were already being felt.

Studio Hirondelle reported that on 3 February 2025 the rebels unilaterally declared a ceasefire 'because of the humanitarian crisis caused by the Kinshasa regime', to take effect on 4 February, and said in a communiqué circulated notably on X that they had 'no intention of taking control of Bukavu or other localities'.

place: Eastern DRC (reaction to ceasefire declared 3 February)
statement: Studio Hirondelle, citing AFP, reported that Patrick Muyaya told AFP that this was proof that the unilateral ceasefire decreed was, as usual, a decoy.

place: Rumangabo military camp, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Imvaho Nshya, a Rwandan outlet, reported that M23 deputy spokesperson Dr Oscar Balinda said the group issued a communiqué calling on FARDC soldiers hiding in houses to gather at the Goma unity stadium, and that Balinda said more than 1,500 were then taken to the military camp at Rumangabo; the outlet said the soldiers were taken there on Thursday 30 January 2025.

place: Grande Barrière border crossing, Goma, North Kivu / Rubavu, Rwanda
statement: Umuseke, a Rwandan outlet, reported that FARDC soldiers began fleeing to Rubavu via the Grande Barrière border crossing on Monday 27 January 2025.

place: Kishishe and Bambo, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that M23 rebels retook the localities of Kishishe and Bambo in Rutshuru territory from Wednesday 14 May 2025 after fighting Wazalendo fighters, whom they dislodged from the area.

Radio Okapi reported that a notable of the region said two people were wounded the day before at Kishishe and that several shops were looted at Bambo; it said a large part of the population stayed confined at home during the heavy-weapon fighting.

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said it treated about twenty wounded people, including six serious cases and one death, after violent clashes on Thursday 15 May in and around Bambo, Rutshuru territory, between M23/AFC and Wazalendo fighters of the CMC group.

Actualite.cd reported that MSF condemned the holding of clashes in populated areas close to care centres, regretting that gunfire hit a hospital service; the outlet said the fighting at Bambo took place close to the MSF-supported hospital and that the use of heavy weapons forced medical teams to take temporary shelter, limiting their capacity to provide emergency care.

Actualite.cd reported, in an article on an MSF appeal, that since 15 May Bambo had been the scene of intense clashes between AFC/AFC rebels (as printed) and Wazalendo militiamen of the CMC group, which had caused more than 900 families from Bwito chiefdom to flee to the town.

place: Kirumba, Lukarara, Rukano, Kagando, Runzenze (Tongo and Bambo groupings), Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that at least 29 civilians, described as collateral victims of clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo over the previous six days, were buried on Tuesday 27 May in Kirumba, Lukarara, Rukano and Kagando villages in Rutshuru territory; six more bodies were buried at Runzenze the same day.

place: Tongo and Bambo groupings, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that several dozen villagers' houses were burned and that goats and other goods were reportedly looted, while young villagers were reportedly taken hostage by M23 rebels to carry these goods, in villages of the Tongo and Bambo groupings in Rutshuru territory.

place: Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo and Mutanda groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that since Thursday 22 May AFC/M23 elements had been conducting an operation to hunt presumed Rwandan FDLR rebels in several villages of the Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo and Mutanda groupings in Bwito chiefdom, in particular at the edge of Virunga National Park.

place: Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo, Mutanda groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that since Thursday 22 May near-daily clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo groups had occurred in Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo and Mutanda groupings of Bwito, and that sources reported at least 14 civilians killed, dozens wounded and several houses burned up to Sunday 25 May.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that after violent clashes between Wazalendo and M23 on the previous day, at Nyamilima in Rutshuru territory a girl of about 10 years was killed and houses were burned at Mulema (Walikale), as of Tuesday 10 June.

place: Bukombo, Tongo and Bambo groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to sources in the region, between 18 May and 10 June more than 600 houses were burned, at least 75 people killed and 42 wounded, with more than 26 villages affected in the Bukombo, Tongo and Bambo groupings.

place: Rutshuru territory (place of the arrests not specified in the excerpt)
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that in fighting in Rutshuru territory about ten houses were hit by bomb fragments and several civilians were arrested ('interpellés') by M23/AFC rebels after the Wazalendo withdrawal.

place: Lushebere, between Kishishe and Kirima, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to several concurring sources, M23 elements attacked FARDC positions supported by the Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDP, commonly called Wazalendo) at Lushebere in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory; a local youth parliament president quoted by the outlet placed Lushebere between Kishishe and Kirima and said M23 had just progressed on the Lushebere-Kishishe-Bambo axis.

Radio Okapi reported that, according to a communiqué of the DRC Interior Ministry published on Saturday 12 April 2025, at least 52 people were killed in an attack described as 'organised and simulated' and attributed to AFC/M23 rebels supported by the Rwandan army.

Radio Okapi reported that local sources spoke of an attempted incursion by Wazalendo to retake Goma, while the government rejected that thesis and instead accused M23 of having orchestrated a premeditated attack against civilians.

place: Goma area (not specified in this sentence)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the official document (the Interior Ministry communiqué) listed 297 assassinations and summary executions, 72 rapes, hundreds of disappearances, more than 146 cases of bodily torture and the looting of more than 2 000 head of cattle and vehicles between 6 and 11 April 2025.

place: Goma and surrounding areas (not specified in excerpt)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the Congolese government, by an official communiqué of 8 May, denounced violence perpetrated by the AFC/M23 supported by the Rwandan army, citing more than 308 assassinations, 124 cases of rape, 315 cases of torture and hundreds of forced recruitments between April and May 2025.

Radio Okapi reported that MSF said, in a communiqué published Friday 11 April, that about twenty armed men affiliated with M23/AFC entered the compound of the Kyeshero hospital in Goma looking for people who had taken refuge there; one person died, three were injured and two hospital staff were violently assaulted.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (MSF-supported hospitals)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that MSF warned of an alarming increase in violence targeting medical facilities and staff in eastern DRC since the start of 2025, saying it had faced about fifteen violent incidents directly affecting hospitals it supports in North and South Kivu.

place: Mutaho, Mujoga, Karungu (Nyiragongo territory) and Goma
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing OCHA, that violent clashes took place on 9 April in the localities of Mutaho, Mujoga and Karungu in Nyiragongo territory and reached Goma two days later; OCHA also reported a clear rise in crime around Goma and Nyiragongo since the advance of the AFC/M23.

place: Mutanda grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Bwiza.com, a Kigali-based Kinyarwanda-language outlet treated here as Rwanda-aligned, reported, without citing a source for the figure, that about 38 people, including women and children, were killed between 26 and 31 May 2025 in Mutanda grouping, Rutshuru territory, an area it described as controlled by the AFC/M23 rebels.

place: Kashalira market, Kirima village, Mutanda grouping, Rutshuru territory
statement: Bwiza.com reported, citing local residents, that Muhindo Sabuni Philémon, head of Kirima village, was killed at Kashalira market on Friday 30 May by unidentified armed men; the outlet said he had reportedly been recently appointed by the M23 administration.

place: Marangara, Runzenze, Butare and other hamlets, Mutanda/Bwito, Rutshuru territory
statement: Bwiza.com, a Kigali-based Kinyarwanda-language outlet treated here as Rwanda-aligned, reported that 'other information' it did not source confirmed about 543 houses were burned, notably in Marangara, Runzenze, Butare, Kanyangiri, Kasali, Kanyatsi, Mashango, Kibwe, Nyenyeri and Buhambi hamlets in North Kivu, and that at the end of May Wazalendo fighters burned about ten houses in Butare village where they suspected the owners of working with M23.

place: Eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu prisons escapes)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the NGO TRIAL International, in a communiqué, said that several escaped prisoners, convicted or prosecuted for international crimes, had quickly joined armed groups including M23 and Wazalendo militias and were taking part in the fighting, and that it denounced killings, death threats, torture, rapes and extortion targeting those who contributed to their indictment or conviction.

Radio Okapi reported that, at a meeting of North Kivu civil-society coordinations, participant Pepin Kavota said that between January and May 2025 more than 200 civilians were killed by the M23/AFC/RDF in Rutshuru, 76 in Masisi, and '9600 à Goma' (figure as printed), alongside 3500 people wounded by weapons in Nyiragongo territory and Goma city.
Radio Okapi reported that Pepin Kavota, a participant in the North Kivu civil-society meeting, also mentioned kidnappings and forced recruitment within the rebel armed groups.

Jeune Afrique reported that AFC/M23 was multiplying sweeping operations in the North Kivu capital to flush out soldiers and militiamen who refused to surrender, and that, amid arbitrary arrests, forced disappearances and sometimes killings, Goma residents were bearing the full brunt of an explosion of insecurity denounced by NGOs and citizen movements.

place: Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch said that between 10 and 30 July 2025 M23 fighters summarily executed local residents and farmers, including women and children, in villages, fields and near the Rutshuru River across the Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory, and that witness accounts, the UN and military sources indicate the Rwanda Defence Force were also involved in the M23 operations.

Human Rights Watch said its research indicates the M23 military operations in Binza in July 2025 were carried out by the 1st Battalion of the 1st Brigade, commanded by Col. Samuel Mushagara and Brig. Gen. Baudoin Ngaruye, respectively, and noted General Ngaruye is under UN sanctions.

UN News reported that the UN human rights office (OHCHR) said it had received first-hand accounts indicating that at least 319 civilians were killed by M23 fighters, aided by members of the Rwanda Defence Force, between 9 and 21 July in North Kivu province, and that Rwanda has repeatedly denied its forces support the M23.

place: Goma, North Kivu (press conference); Rutshuru territory (subject)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that AFC deputy coordinator Bertrand Bisimwa, at a press conference in Goma on 7 August 2025, called the UN report on the alleged massacre of more than 300 civilians in Rutshuru in July 'non factuel'; according to Bisimwa, the villages named as massacre sites would lie in the protected zone of Virunga National Park and therefore be uninhabited, and he said there is no family in mourning in Rutshuru and that the figure of 300 dead is implausible.

The Government of Rwanda (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) said in a statement that it rejects the false accusations in the recent OHCHR statement, that OHCHR alleges 'without any evidence' that the Rwanda Defence Force 'aided' in the killing of '319 civilians' in farms in eastern DRC, and that the gratuitous inclusion of the RDF in these allegations is 'unacceptable'.

The Government of Rwanda (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) said in a statement that it firmly rejects the findings of Human Rights Watch, OHCHR and UNJHRO alleging mass killing of civilians in Binza, that 'Human Rights Watch itself admits that it did not independently verify the alleged killings', and that only an independent investigation will shed light on these allegations.

place: Kihito fields and Nyamilima, Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that eight bodies were buried over the weekend after deadly attacks on 8 August in the fields of Kihito and at Nyamilima (Binza, Rutshuru); it said seven victims, five wood-sawyers and two farmers from one family, were killed by gunfire or bladed weapon and, according to local sources, were reportedly targeted during an operation by AFC-M23 rebels to hunt alleged FDLR; the eighth victim, a local official of Kiheka neighbourhood, was found dead at home after a night incursion by unidentified armed men.

place: Binza groupement; Nyabanira, Kasave; Kiwanja–Nyamilima–Ishasha axis, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that a fragile calm prevailed on Wednesday 16 July in Binza groupement (Rutshuru) after several days of intense fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and various local armed groups along the Kiwanja–Nyamilima–Ishasha axis, and that, according to local sources, the most recent clashes took place on Tuesday in Nyabanira and Kasave.

place: Kongo-paysannat, west of Nyamilima, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, the disappearance of about a hundred farmers, notably in the Kongo-paysannat area west of Nyamilima, and said about twenty farmers had been missing since Monday 21 July; it linked the loss of access to farmland to fighting between AFC/M23 and alleged FDLR fighters near Virunga park.

place: Katwiguru to Nyamilima axis, Binza, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that after three months of prohibition the M23 again allowed residents of the Katwiguru–Nyamilima axis (Bwisha chiefdom, Binza, Rutshuru) to access their fields from Monday 25 August, for an expected two weeks according to local sources, and that the restriction had been imposed by the M23 to avoid confusion between civilians and alleged FDLR rebels.

place: Kahumiro, near Kibirizi, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Kahumiro, near Kibirizi in Rutshuru territory within the Virunga park zone, had been the scene of violent clashes since 20 August 2025 between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters and alleged FDLR elements.

Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that M23 rebels 'under the command of Makenga' launched an operation to hunt alleged FDLR rebels at Kahumiro, while community leaders said there was no longer an active FDLR presence in the area.

Radio Okapi reported that local sources spoke of about ten deaths among residents, mainly Hutu and other local ethnic groups of Bwito chiefdom, in the Kahumiro clashes, and that hundreds of households fled to Kibirizi and neighbouring villages.

place: Sake, Masisi territory (about 20 km north-west of Goma), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the chief of Kimoka locality (Kamuronza groupement), named as Kibihira Bauma, was shot dead at his home in Sake in the night of Saturday to Sunday 3 August 2025, in a zone it described as totally under M23 control according to testimonies; the authors were not identified and no official report had been issued.

place: Goma city, Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that a report by the North Kivu provincial youth council documented 47 deaths, 75 cases of sexual violence, 14 abductions, 66 armed robberies and 63 cases of arson between 7 June and 3 July 2025 in Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories and Goma city.

place: Kasika and Katoyi quarters, Karisimbi commune, Goma; Nyiragongo territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that two people were killed by armed bandits on the evening of Wednesday 9 July 2025 in Goma; according to local sources, the first was a motorcycle taxi driver killed in Kasika quarter and the second a woman killed in Katoyi quarter, Karisimbi commune; it described Goma and Nyiragongo territory as under AFC/M23 control since late January 2025.
Actualite.cd reported that, to secure Goma, the AFC/M23 administration installed infrared surveillance cameras in some quarters of Goma on Wednesday 9 July 2025.

Actualite.cd, citing an OCHA report on June 2025, reported that since 5 June more than 3,600 people (about 720 households) fled Bukombo, south of Rutshuru, after intensified fighting between armed groups, and that most of the displaced found refuge at Birambizo General Reference Hospital, the local Catholic parish and host families.

Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC accused armed men likened to M23 fighters of abducting at least 42 women in Bukombo centre grouping, Rutshuru territory; according to the communication officer of the 34th military region, Dieudonné Kasereka, the events took place on Sunday 28 December in Bwito chiefdom, and the 42 victims reportedly underwent torture before being abducted, according to the army citing testimony from inhabitants.

place: Mashango and Karambi, Bukombo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported on 15 October 2025 that civilian sources gave a toll of at least seven people killed, including two women, in the tenth day of fighting between AFC/M23 and CMC-Nyatura Wazalendo in Bwito chiefdom, with nearly ten other women reportedly raped and more than a quarter of the houses of Mashango village burned.

place: Chirumba (Tongo grouping) and Kagango (Bambo grouping), Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported on 15 October 2025 that at least 39 people were killed more than a week earlier in the villages of Chirumba (Tongo) and Kagango (Bambo); according to civilian sources in the area, the killings and abuses were reportedly committed during reprisal operations by AFC/M23 rebels.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources on 7 November 2025, that at least four people were killed and seven wounded in successive incursions by armed men over the previous two nights in Katsiru, Bwito chiefdom; per local notables, unidentified armed men attacked local defence units set up by AFC-M23, which occupies the area.

place: Muko, Karambi and Mashango, Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, after clashes on Tuesday and Wednesday between AFC/M23 rebels and wazalendo in the villages of Muko, Karambi and Mashango (Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory), one person was killed, several others wounded and about ten houses burned, according to its sources; several local sources said AFC/M23 rebels searching for CMC-FDP wazalendo initiated the fighting, causing displacement, and burned houses in the three villages.

place: Rumangabo, Goma-Rutshuru road (Virunga National Park), Rutshuru territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that an AFC/M23 unit on patrol on the Goma-Rutshuru road inside Virunga National Park fell into an ambush set by Wazalendo near Rumangabo on Wednesday 24 December; several sources said a vehicle of the rebels was burned, and one anonymous source spoke of rebel casualties.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, a series of robberies attributed to armed groups in Rutshuru and Masisi over two days; in Rutshuru, three women fish sellers returning from Vitshumbi by motorbike were attacked on Friday 19 December on the Rwindi-Kibirizi road in Virunga park and lost their goods, money and phones.

Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC, in a communiqué issued on Saturday, accused the rebel coalition, which it said is backed by Rwanda, of intensifying attacks in the east of the country in violation of commitments made in the Washington and Doha peace processes; according to the text signed by army spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekeng Bomusa Efomi, the rebels attacked several military positions in South Kivu and North Kivu over the previous 72 hours.

place: Kirumba, Lubero territory (from PENA centre, Rutshuru)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that on Monday 15 December 2025 vehicles carrying support troops were seen crossing Kirumba towards the north of Lubero territory, coming from the PENA centre in Rutshuru territory; the article attributes the positions in Lubero to AFC/M23 and cites Lubero civil society.

place: Health centres in Masisi and Rutshuru territories (not named by the source)
statement: MSF reported that in October two health centres supported by MSF were hit by stray bullets in Masisi and Rutshuru territories in the same week, and that in total three MSF staff have been killed in North Kivu in 2025.

place: Bukombo grouping, around Mweso (Bumbasha, Mubirubiru), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters, allies of the FARDC, continued on Thursday 15 January in the Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory, around the town of Mweso, and that according to local sources the fighting involved Wazalendo of the Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC).

place: Bumbasha, Kivuma, Kanyangohe, Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that several civilians, including displaced people, were wounded in the villages of Bumbasha, Kivuma and Kanyangohe during fighting in Rutshuru territory, and that a local customary source said a precise toll was hard to establish.

place: Kiyeye, Kihondo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory; Nyanzale health centre
statement: Radio Okapi reported that several dozen civilians mobilised by AFC/M23 fighters for community work were targeted by CMC militiamen ambushed in the locality of Kiyeye, in the Kihondo grouping; separately, according to MSF as relayed by Radio Okapi, at least 32 wounded, mostly civilians, victims of shell fragments and direct fire, were evacuated and treated at the Nyanzale health centre (the source does not say all were wounded in the Kiyeye ambush).

Radio Okapi reported that the humanitarian organisation MSF, in a communiqué, also reported that several civilian houses were burned in the area after the attack in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory.

place: Bukombo, Kihondo, Mutanda, Bambo and Tongo groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Actualite.cd, summarising an OCHA report for January, reported that between 12 and 16 January fighting occurred in more than ten villages of the Bukombo, Kihondo and Mutanda groupings, as well as Bambo and Tongo, in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, where about fifty civilians were killed, and that the report noted the displacement of several hundred people.

place: Kivuma and Kanyangohe, Bukombo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (about 5 km from Mweso)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that fighting pitted AFC/M23 rebels against wazalendo early on the morning of Tuesday 3 February at Kivuma and Kanyangohe, two localities of Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory), and that after several hours of violent clashes the AFC/M23 rebels were forced to fall back to Mweso, their starting base; Radio Okapi also reported that AFC/M23 rebels launched an attack on Wazalendo positions in Kivuma and Kanyangohe, in the Bukombo grouping.

place: Rwindi-Kanyabayonga road, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing concordant local sources, that a convoy of travellers from Rutshuru territory heading to Butembo was ambushed by unidentified armed men on Sunday 1 February on the Rwindi-Kanyabayonga stretch, in an area under AFC/M23 control, with several wounded and no deaths, and that travellers' valuables were looted.

place: Kabanda, near Kibirizi, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that in the village of Kabanda, near Kibirizi (Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory), an incursion by unidentified armed men was reported between 3 and 4 a.m.; the attackers looted the population's belongings, a young boy known by the name Jade was killed, and three civilians were wounded and admitted to the Kibirizi reference health centre.

place: Bambo and Kibirizi, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local sources, the instability in Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory) is notably linked to a hunt operation led by the AFC/M23 against the Rwandan Hutu FDLR rebels and their local allies, including fighters of the Collectif des Mouvements pour le Changement (CMC/Nyatura).

place: Masisi and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu (Mitimingi, Kaunda, Mbiso named for Masisi; no Rutshuru places named)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that despite a ceasefire announced for 18 February at noon, fighting continued between the FARDC and AFC/M23; it said that since early Friday 20 February AFC/M23 had been fighting Wazalendo of PARECO at Mitimingi, Kaunda and Mbiso in Masisi territory, and that other clashes were reported in some areas of Rutshuru territory.

place: JTN agro-pastoral concession, Bwito chiefdom, near Mweso
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources reached from Mweso, that two civilians (a young girl and a cattle guard) were killed by stray bullets on Thursday 26 February in an exchange of fire between AFC/M23 elements on patrol and an unidentified armed group in the JTN concession, Bwito chiefdom, near Mweso; twelve cows were also shot dead, and no official toll was communicated by the parties.

place: Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja road, Virunga park, Rutshuru territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that on Wednesday 18 March armed men fired on and stopped a vehicle on the Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja road inside Virunga park, Rutshuru territory, wounding two passengers, a woman and her son, who were evacuated to the Kanyabayonga reference health centre; the assailants' identity remained unknown, though several security sources said this part of the territory is under AFC/M23 influence.

place: Kalembe, Mweso health zone, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, the head nurse of the Kalembe health centre (Mweso health zone, Masisi territory), identified as Kapita Lucien, was shot in the hand after being violently beaten, and that the local Red Cross coordinator, Byamungu Mauwa Samson, also suffered physical abuse on the same occasion; the outlet attributed the incident to armed elements of the AFC/M23 and reported that the two men were reportedly accused, without formal proof, of links with the wazalendo and were taken away by motorbike by their abductors to an unknown destination. The article said AFC/M23 officials had not yet reacted.

place: Goma (city), Sake and Nyiragongo territory visited
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Bruno Lemarquis, Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in the DRC, on a mission in Goma since Monday 16 March, called on the leaders of the AFC/M23 rebellion to guarantee absolute respect for humanitarian space, in a statement made during a meeting with the de facto authorities of Goma and its surroundings, led by Corneille Nangaa.

Actualite.cd reported that Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, in an exchange with the diplomatic corps accredited in Kinshasa on Wednesday 25 March 2026, called the situation 'préoccupante', said the reopening of Goma airport for humanitarian flights had not happened, and accused the AFC/M23 of lacking political will.

Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 maintains that the humanitarian situation is improving in the zones it controls and alarming in the zones controlled by Kinshasa, in the context of the dispute over reopening Goma airport.

place: Tongo, Butare, Kabizo, Bambo (Kishishe), Nyanzale, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the North Kivu governor under AFC/M23 administration, Bahati Musanga Erasto, began a tour of Bwito collectivity, Rutshuru territory, on 12 February 2026, visiting Tongo, Butare, Kabizo, Bambo (Kishishe) and Nyanzale, and that at the end of the tour more than twenty young people were recruited into the ARC.

place: Kisangani (Bangoka) airport, Tshopo (statement concerns attacks on Masisi, Walikale, Rutshuru, Minembwe)
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that the AFC/M23 confirmed it carried out a drone attack on Kisangani airport (Tshopo) as a 'warning' to Kinshasa, as its leader said, and that the movement said its drones destroyed a military drone base at the airport 'where attacks killing civilians were prepared' in Masisi, Walikale, Rutshuru, Minembwe and elsewhere; BBC said it could not independently verify either side's claims.

BBC News Gahuza reported that the Tshopo provincial government said eight bomb-carrying drones tried to attack Bangoka airport at Kisangani on Sunday but were all shot down before reaching their target, and that the government side condemned the attack on a civilian airport and blamed the M23 and Rwandan forces.

place: Rwankuba, Kiringa and Bwuma (Bwito chiefdom), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that clashes between wazalendo and AFC/M23 were reported from the morning of Friday 10 April 2026 in the locality of Rwankuba (Kihondo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory), with heavy gunfire heard in the villages of Kiringa and Bwuma.

place: Bushenge, Gisigari groupement, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that six civilians were killed on 23 April 2026 in their fields at Bushenge, Gisigari groupement (Rutshuru territory), and that, according to several local sources, the killings were attributed to the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) operating through the AFC/M23 rebels. The outlet said the circumstances were not clearly established and the motive was unknown.

place: Rumangabo and Tshanzu training camps, North Kivu (Rutshuru territory per Actualite.cd's account of the report)
statement: Human Rights Watch said, in a report, that Rwandan military forces and the M23 armed group carried out a campaign of forced recruitment and abusive detention of thousands of captured combatants and civilians in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo; the report documents large-scale roundups and arrests in North and South Kivu and grave abuses against detainees at the Rumangabo and Tshanzu training camps in North Kivu between mid-2024 and December 2025. HRW said its researchers found that M23 fighters, backed by Rwandan military personnel, committed murder, torture and corporal punishment and used forced labor and child soldiers.

place: Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi territories (North Kivu), and Kalehe (South Kivu)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that a communiqué published on Thursday 4 June 2026 by the spokesperson of the 34th military region, Major Dieudonné Kasereka, said that 204 AFC-M23 rebels had surrendered to the FARDC and their allies in Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi (North Kivu) in waves during April and May.

place: North Kivu (Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi) and Kalehe, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on Wednesday 8 April 2026 the command of the 34th military region of North Kivu confirmed the voluntary surrender of 263 elements from the ranks of the AFC/M23 between February and March 2026.

place: Rumangabo (ICCN headquarters, Virunga National Park), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that a kamikaze drone hit the headquarters of the Congolese Institute for Nature Conservation (ICCN) at Rumangabo, Rutshuru territory, on the morning of Sunday 24 May 2026; Virunga National Park public-relations officer Méthode Uhoze confirmed the facts to the outlet and said the attack came around 8 a.m. The outlet reported that the building was burned and the frame destroyed, that no toll was yet available and that the author of the attack had not been identified.

Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a statement on X, accused government forces of 'un bombardement criminel et indiscriminé' on Rumangabo; he said it took place on Sunday 24 May 2026 at 07h35 against the densely populated area of Rumangabo and the eco-guards camp of Virunga National Park, using CH-4 combat drones.

place: Goma–Butembo road (Goma city; Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories on the route), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that from Saturday 23 May 2026 the North Kivu governorate under AFC/M23 administration suspended passenger transport between Goma and Butembo until further notice, announced in a communiqué of Friday 22 May 2026 as a preventive measure against Ebola (Bundibugyo strain). Kivu Morning Post reported the same communiqué.

place: Goma (the 11 March 2026 strike alleged); statement made from Rwanda
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that Rwanda's foreign minister (printed 'Oliver Nduhungirehe'), in a statement the day after the Mushaki drone attack, deplored the silence of the international community and of the UN mission in the DRC regarding 'crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo'; he said that on 11 March 2026 FARDC attack drones struck Goma, killing UNICEF humanitarian Karine Buisset and two other civilians.

place: Kabanda and Kabuye, Bambo centre, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said FDLR fighters infiltrated the Kabuye and Kabanda areas in the night of 18 May 2026 (time given as 'saa Saba z’igicuku'), killing a 77-year-old named Nzirorera Nsekuye at Kabanda and abducting Munenge Samuel and Karuhije Innocent at Kabuye; the outlet placed the incident in Bambo centre, Rutshuru territory.

place: Hohé, near Rushege, Tongo groupement, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that local sources, including notables, said at least nine civilians were killed on Thursday 17 July in the village of Hohé, Tongo groupement, Rutshuru territory, and attributed the attack to AFC/M23 fighters on patrol.

place: Kibirizi, Kasesero, Kilambo; Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that at least five people were killed, one wounded and two missing in the last six days in the north of Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory. It said these incidents came a few days after the killing of five people on 28 July in the same area; among the victims were Justin Kahiti, chief of the village of Kirima recently appointed by the AFC/M23, his motorcycle driver and two of his bodyguards, who were killed in an ambush at Kasesero.

place: Kilambo (Kanyabayonga groupement) and Kibirizi (Mutanda groupement), Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, the day before Sunday 2 August, two people were abducted in their fields around the village of Kilambo, Kanyabayonga groupement, and that their families said they were still without news; on the evening of Sunday 2 August unidentified armed men burst into a civilian's home in Kibirizi, Mutanda groupement, and shot him.

place: Avenues Salongo 3 and Katoyi 1 (per the article), near Katindo camp, Goma
statement: Actualite.cd reported that at least about fifty young people were arrested on Tuesday 7 July during an operation by AFC/M23 police elements near the disused Katindo military camp in Goma, and that no official information was given on their place of detention or the reasons for their arrest.

The outlet reported that a teacher died in detention in Goma after his arrest by AFC/M23 elements, according to several sources close to his family, who accused elements of the movement and their allies of responsibility for his death. According to these sources, he had been arrested after demanding the return of his plot, which he believed had been occupied since the AFC/M23 took control of the city, and was reportedly taken to a place of detention known as 'Chien méchant', where, the family sources said, he reportedly suffered violence before succumbing to his injuries.

place: Nyirubara (Radio Okapi) / Gikoro (Actualite.cd), Jomba groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Radio Okapi and Actualite.cd reported an explosive-device explosion on Saturday in Jomba groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, with differing accounts. Radio Okapi, citing concordant sources, placed it at Nyirubara village, said it happened while children were handling an explosive device they had just picked up, and gave seven dead (five children and two women) and about ten seriously injured taken to health facilities. Actualite.cd placed it at Gikoro, gave at least seven dead and more than ten seriously injured, said according to several sources that the device had reportedly been abandoned by persons not yet identified, and that the victims were reportedly mainly farmers; it called the toll provisional.

Radio Okapi reported that on Tuesday 28 July a so-called peaceful march organised by a platform presenting itself as the Société civile plurielle et Forces vives du Nord-Kivu paralysed several sectors in Goma between 7 and 11 a.m. and ended at the MONUSCO headquarters, where the organisers handed a memorandum to the mission's representatives. The call had been widely relayed the day before by neighbourhood authorities, who said the initiative was part of a decision taken by the de facto AFC/M23 authorities in the zones under their control; some residents interviewed by Radio Okapi said the mobilisation was coercive.

place: Goma (ISTM, ISTA, ISP, ISC); also Bukavu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that on Monday 10 August 2026 the deputy permanent secretary of the AFC-M23, Delion Kimbulungu, accompanied by the deputy governor of North Kivu Bahati Shadrack, toured higher-education institutions in Goma, including the ISTM, ISTA, ISP and ISC, where he chaired handover ceremonies between the old and new management teams. It said the decision designating the new management committees concerns ten institutions in Goma and Bukavu, and was signed by Bertrand Bisimwa and submitted for approval to Corneille Nangaa.

place: Territories under AFC-M23 control (entry from Beni, Butembo, Oïcha)
statement: La Prunelle Verte reported that the AFC-M23 administration announced stricter movement restrictions: people coming from Beni, Butembo and Oïcha were no longer allowed to enter the territories under AFC-M23 control until further notice, and vehicles from those areas must be checked, as a measure it presented as preventive against Ebola.

place: Kayna health zone (Itsu health area; Kirumba quarantine site)
statement: Enquête.cd reported that the health crisis cell set up by the rebel administration announced on Thursday 3 September a new confirmed Ebola case in the Kayna health zone, a 21-year-old man from Butembo identified at a health checkpoint in the Itsu health area and transferred to the Kirumba quarantine site; it said Reuters also reported on 4 September a new case in an AFC/M23-controlled zone after the epidemic had been declared over in the territories under its control.

place: Mulala, about 20 km from Vitshumbi, Rutshuru territory
statement: Bwiza (Kigali) reported that the AFC/M23, through its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, said FDLR fighters attacked civilians at Mulala in Rutshuru territory on the night of Monday 31 August, killing four and wounding ten, and that two women going to their fields were abducted; the movement accused Kinshasa of failing to stop FDLR activities.

Radio Okapi reported that, in a declaration on Tuesday 21 July in Mangina, Beni territory, the coordination of North Kivu civil society implicated the ADF in the north and the AFC/M23 coalition in the south in the worsening security situation; its coordinator John Banyene said: 'Le M23 continue de massacrer, torturer, violer, piller les ressources naturelles et les biens de la population'. Radio Okapi, summarising the declaration, said the rebels were deploying recently trained troops at Tchanzu with logistical support from the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF).

Congovirtuel reported, citing Africa Intelligence, that Théo Binamungu, described as a close political adviser to Nangaa, was arrested at the end of August by loyalists of Makenga, interrogated by the military intelligence of the Armée de la révolution congolaise (ARC) and then by the Direction pour la sécurité et les renseignements (DSR), and transferred to Munzenze central prison on 8 September.

place: Kiseguro (Binza groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that fighting was reported on the morning of Tuesday 13 October around Kiseguro, Rutshuru territory, between presumed Wazalendo fighters and those of the AFC/M23, described as recently renamed the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN). Local sources said the attack on an AFC/M23 (FRN) position began around 5 a.m. and no toll was available.

place: Kiseguro (Binza groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the Wazalendo launched the attack on a Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) position at Kiseguro on Tuesday morning and, after several hours of fighting, withdrew from the area, leaving the positions in the hands of the FRN rebels.

place: Kiseguro (Binza groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Les Volcans News reported, citing local sources, that clashes broke out on Tuesday 13 October 2026 at about 5 a.m. at Kiseguro, and that control of Kiseguro by either side was not clearly established when the article was written.

place: Kalengera (Kisigari groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that around 22:00 the night before the 13 October clashes, explosions were heard at Kalengera, Kisigari groupement, Rutshuru territory, and that a military drone strike was said to have targeted a rebel position there; no toll was communicated.

FNTV reported, citing a family source quoted by the Agence congolaise de presse (ACP), that Martin Dushime, 27, a final-year medical student said to have been forcibly enrolled in the AFC/M23, surrendered to the FARDC; the article states he had been abducted in Goma on 6 July 2025. The accusation of abduction and forced recruitment comes from the family source and the outlet and is not confirmed by AFC/M23 in the article.

Actualite.cd reported that Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) provided care to more than 10 300 survivors of sexual violence at Sake, Masisi territory, over 13 months of intervention, and announced the transfer of its medical activities at Sake to Première Urgence Internationale (PUI).

place: Lubero, Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu
statement: Enquete.cd reported that the 33rd Military Region spokesperson, Captain Dieudonné Kasereka, as cited by several Congolese media, confirmed on Sunday 4 October that twenty-nine fighters presented as belonging to the AFC-M23 laid down arms and surrendered to the FARDC and Wazalendo groups between 1 and 4 October 2026 in Lubero, Masisi and Walikale territories; according to the military authorities, several of them were reportedly young recruits enrolled by force.

Top Africa News reported that African Union facilitators held closed-door talks with AFC/M23 leaders in Goma on Monday, meeting political coordinator Corneille Nangaa and his deputies Bertrand Bisimwa and Freddy Kaniki; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the movement received the mission in the framework of efforts toward a political, durable and African-led resolution of the conflict, and no joint communiqué or concrete agreements were announced.

place: Goma, North Kivu (Grande Barrière, Goma-Rubavu crossing)
statement: Tic-Tac Hebdo reported that AFC/M23 North Kivu governor Bahati Musanga Erasto signed communiqué n°01/007/CAB/GP-NK/2026 of 2 October, setting the Grande Barrière border post at Goma to open daily from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. the following day; the document was circulated by Lawrence Kanyuka.

place: Katoyi and Kasake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing several military sources, that the FARDC-Wazalendo coalition was said to have retaken the centre of Katoyi on Tuesday, but was said still to be struggling to retake Kasake, which was reportedly still occupied by AFC/M23 rebels.

place: Ngungu (Ufamandu 1er groupement), Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Les Volcans News reported, according to local sources, that families displaced by armed clashes had taken refuge in Ngungu, Masisi territory, and that they said they had received no food aid since arrival and lacked sufficient means for medical care of their family members.

place: Rutshuru territory, North Kivu (exact place not stated)
statement: Enquete.cd reported, citing journalist Daniel Michombero who cited the group's spokesperson, that three fighters of the 'FRN-M23-RDF coalition' were killed in an attack attributed to the Wazalendo of the CMC/FDP movement in Rutshuru territory (the article goes on to quote Me Héritier Gashegu); two bodyguards of the new commander were also killed and another fighter wounded; according to the same sources, a woman presented as the presumed wife of the commander, and her infant, reportedly also died, hit by gunfire during the attack.

place: Ruza, about six km from Kabizo, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
