statement: Enquete.cd, relaying journalist Daniel Michombero citing the group's spokesperson, reported that three fighters of the FRN-M23-RDF coalition were killed in an attack attributed to the Wazalendo of the CMC/FDP movement; according to Me Héritier Gashegu, quoted in the article, one of the fighters killed had just been deployed to replace Nshimiye Kabo, described as head of the coalition's operations in that part of Rutshuru territory, who had been killed on 16 October at Ruza, about six kilometres from Kabizo.

place: Abala, Nyaruhinga and Kabanja, Fizi territory, South Kivu (abduction in Goma, North Kivu)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC announced the surrender of seventeen fighters of the AFC-M23/Twirwaneho coalition in Fizi territory, South Kivu, and that operation Sokola 2 Sud-Kivu spokesperson Sub-Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi said one of them was a young civilian who had been kidnapped and forcibly recruited in Goma, North Kivu, by the M23; the army also said several children aged 14 to 16 were among the 17.

The news site reported that FARDC-Wazalendo coalition elements recovered Masisi-Centre from the M23/RDF rebels on Wednesday 8 January 2025 after a counter-offensive; the president of the Masisi territory civil society confirmed this to the outlet and said fighting continued around the town.

place: North Kivu (Masisi territory localities, not named)
statement: The news site reported that Guillaume Ndjike Kaiko, spokesperson of the military governor of North Kivu, announced on his X account on Tuesday evening that the Tuesday counter-offensive had allowed FARDC-Wazalendo to recover several localities from the enemy, which suffered heavy losses, without naming the localities.

The news site reported that, according to first accounts, a bomb reportedly came from the rebel zone during fighting in the heights of Sake, where FARDC and presumed rebels had been clashing since the morning, and that its sources on the spot said the explosion killed three civilians; the local civil society said the bomb struck them in their house.

BBC News Afrique reported that the M23 rebellion took control of Masisi, about 80 km north of Goma, on Saturday, and, citing Radio Okapi, that the army and its Wazalendo allies had retaken the town of Ngungu in Masisi territory.
Human Rights Watch reported that, after it captured Masisi in January, the M23 ordered two displacement sites dismantled, according to a humanitarian source.

Radio Okapi reported, citing witnesses, that Walikale's general hospital and an NGO logistics base were damaged during the fighting, causing deaths and injuries, after the Walikale area passed under rebel occupation.

place: Mubi and Ndjingala mining centres, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on the same Thursday scenes of looting were reported in the mining centres of Mubi and Ndjingala, while gunfire continued to be heard.
Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that FARDC soldiers and their Wazalendo allies were reported to have fallen back toward Mubi-Lubutu on the road to Kisangani.

place: Mubi, Ndjingala, Logu, Biruwe, Makana, Kangama, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the population, armed men in military uniform carried out systematic looting in several villages, including Mubi, Ndjingala, Logu, Biruwe, Makana and Kangama in Walikale territory.

place: Walikale chef-lieu, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that six days after its announced withdrawal, the AFC/M23 was still present in Walikale's chef-lieu.

place: Walikale general referral hospital, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the compound of Walikale general referral hospital, which already held more than 600 displaced households, recorded an influx of new households, and that hospital sources said the assistance of MSF Holland could not cover needs.

place: Walikale, North Kivu (statement issued from Kigali)
statement: A statement from the office of the government spokesperson of Rwanda said Rwanda welcomed M23's announcement on the repositioning of its forces from Walikale in support of peace initiatives underway, as well as the DRC's announcement that all offensive operations by FARDC and Wazalendo would be halted.

Xinhua reported that, in response to the AFC announcement, the Congolese military urged Congolese self-defence forces to de-escalate the same day, stressing the need to prioritise peace talks and advance the Luanda and Nairobi dialogue processes.

place: Kanii and Masisi-centre, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that violent clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters in villages around the Masisi chef-lieu, near Kanii on Thursday, left residents hiding; some sources said Wazalendo launched an offensive to dislodge the M23, others a M23 counter-offensive against Wazalendo coming from the Nyabiondo axis.

place: Kilambo, Buabo grouping, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that M23 rebels took Kilambo (Buabo grouping, south of Masisi chef-lieu) at the end of the previous week and were attacked by Wazalendo on Tuesday 15 April, and reported that on the morning of Wednesday 16 April the rebels were counter-attacking to reoccupy the whole area.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Wazalendo fighters of the Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC) attacked M23 positions at Buleusa, Walikale territory, around 6 a.m. on Thursday 17 April, a locality occupied by the M23 for several months.

place: Bibatama, Luke, Mungote, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the villages of Bibatama, Luke and Mungote in Masisi territory were the scene of violent clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters for almost all of Sunday, and that hundreds of residents fled.

Radio Okapi reported that local sources denounced extortion of residents of Ufamandu 2 by fighters of the group Union des patriotes et démocrates pour la défense du Congo, 'd'un certain Noah Maachano', who were said to be imposing since the previous week a parallel tax of 10 000 Congolese francs (3.5 USD) per household.

place: Kinyumba, Burubi, Kibanda, Kikomo, Kasopo (Osso Banyungu sector), Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that fighting broke out on Friday 25 April between M23 rebels and APCLS Wazalendo fighters in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory despite the truce declared at Doha; sources at Nyabiondo-Centre said the rebels reportedly launched simultaneous attacks on Wazalendo positions around 5 a.m., while other sources said APCLS fighters were the first to open fire on M23 positions.

place: Kibati, Walikale territory, and Nyabiondo, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to other sources, the rebels were also said to have repositioned at Kibati, Walikale territory, where they set up forward positions after withdrawing from Walikale, and that a local notable said their objective would be to conquer all of Masisi and retake control of the chef-lieu of Walikale territory.

place: Kasopo, Lushali, Burubi, Kinyumba (Masisi); Kibati, Kashebere (Walikale)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Wazalendo fighters of the Alliance des patriotes pour un Congo libre et souverain (APCLS) retook the villages of Kasopo, Lushali and Burubi in Masisi territory after violent clashes with the M23 on Friday 25 April; that, according to local sources at Nyabiondo, Kinyumba remained under rebel occupation; and that the same sources said M23 withdrew from its forward position at Kibati (Walikale territory) on the night of Friday 25 April, falling back toward Kashebere, 15 km away.

place: Walikale town, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that on 19 March 2025 the M23 took control of Walikale town and withdrew from it shortly afterwards, while peace-negotiation initiatives were under way in Qatar and Washington.

place: Northern Walikale territory and Lubero, North Kivu
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that on 2 May 2025 the M23 clashed with the FARDC as it expanded west into Lubero, toward the shores of Lake Edward, and that in mid-May the group resumed its expansion in the northern part of Walikale territory.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil sources, that between 200 and 400 young people, including some secondary pupils, were seized by the AFC-M23 rebels in a cordon operation on Wednesday 5 November and taken to the Materdei parish compound in Masisi; the local sources described it as forced recruitment, while the report said there had been no communication about the operation on the movement's digital platforms.

Actualite.cd reported that on Wednesday the wazalendo, withdrawing from Ihula and Ibuga (Kisimba grouping, Walikale) after clashes with AFC/M23, took away five people they accuse of collaborating with the AFC/M23 rebels; the fate of these hostages remained unknown.

place: Mpombi, Banakindi, Kisimba grouping (Walikale); Mpety; Pinga
statement: Actualite.cd reported that on Tuesday the rebels and wazalendo clashed at Mpombi (Banakindi locality, Kisimba grouping, Walikale); after a tense day the wazalendo pushed the rebels back towards Mpety, their main stronghold around Pinga, and Mpombi and its surroundings remained in wazalendo hands.

place: Mulema and Karere, near Kazinga, Osso-Banyungu (Masisi)
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that during fighting in Nyamaboko (Osso-Banyungu, Masisi), in which Ngululu and Kataandwa were particularly affected, the Wazalendo occupied the village of Mulema while AFC/M23 took control of the village of Karere, about 3 km from the centre of Kazinga.

Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that at Mwesso, during an agitated night before Wednesday morning, AFC/M23 rebels fired in the air after learning of the death of one of their officers, killed in an ambush set by the Wazalendo on the Mokoto–Kibarizo axis, and that during this firing a civilian was wounded by a stray bullet at Mbuhi.

place: Ngululu and Mikeno, Osso Banyungu / Mufuni-Shanga (Masisi)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that clashes broke out early on Monday between the rebels and Wazalendo in Masisi, beginning around 5:30 at Ngululu (Osso Banyungu sector, Nyamaboko grouping); according to local sources the rebels allegedly attacked positions of Wazalendo elements, notably the APCLS led by Janvier Karairi, and fighting spread to Mikeno (Mufuni-Shanga grouping), with residents fleeing towards Walikale territory. No official toll was communicated.

place: Kahunda and Mitimingi, Ufamandu 2, Katoyi sector (Masisi)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to concordant sources, AFC-M23 rebels, described as supported by Rwanda, were fighting the VDP/Wazalendo of the group PARECO/FF in Ufamandu 2 (Katoyi sector, Masisi) on Saturday; the fighting began around 07 hours local time when M23 rebels attacked Wazalendo positions at Kahunda and Mitimingi, and residents fled towards Walikale territory or into the forest.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Kasopo locality (Osso Banyungu sector, Masisi) was deserted after two days of fighting from Wednesday 10 September between M23 rebels and a coalition of Wazalendo groups made up of elements of the MAC, the APCLS and Uhuru.

Actualite.cd reported that on Friday AFC/M23 rebels, according to several local sources, initiated fighting by attacking positions of the wazalendo of the APCLS armed group of Janvier Karairi on Changara hill and at Showa near Bukombo (Osso Banyungu, Masisi), and that the wazalendo pushed the attack back to Bukombo, disrupting traffic between Masisi centre and Nyabiondo.

Actualite.cd reported that, according to its sources, at around 17 hours local time a FARDC Sukhoi aircraft dropped bombs on rebel positions at Kibanda, near Kasopo (Osso Banyungu, Masisi), in support of FARDC soldiers and wazalendo fighting the rebels on the ground since the morning, and that the bombing let them repel the rebels who had attacked wazalendo positions at Kibanda.

place: Mpeti and Malemo, Walikale and Masisi
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, in an official communiqué dated Saturday 20 September, the spokesperson of the 3rd defence zone, Major Nestor Mavudisa, denounced 'attaques et provocations intolérables' attributed to the rebels since Thursday 18 September; the army said it reserved the 'droit de riposter avec rigueur'.

Radio Okapi reported that AFC-M23 accused the FARDC on Friday 19 September of bombing the villages of Bibwe, Nyange and Hembe (Bashali Mokoto grouping, Masisi) with drones and Sukhoi-25 fighter jets; the same day, sources close to the FARDC accused the rebellion of killing about twenty civilians in the village of Chanjikiro, Kisimba grouping, Walikale.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the Wazalendo, in a communiqué denouncing attacks against them, stated that on 15 November 2025 the positions of the ANCDH/AFDP at Kashanje (Masisi), of the UPLC/EPLC at Mikenge (Mwenga) and of the CMC/FDP at Kitunda (Rutshuru) were attacked.

Actualite.cd reported that on Friday 17 October 18 AFC/M23 fighters surrendered with their weapons to government forces at Munsanga (Kisimba grouping, Walikale), coming from Rusamambu in Ikobo grouping according to the grouping's administrative secretary, and were later escorted by wazalendo to Pinga and handed to FARDC military authorities there; military sources confirmed the surrender.

place: Kiseya–Kilambo axis, near Kimua, Bafuna groupement, Walikale
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources and confirmed by a source in the North Kivu 3 education sector, that three schoolgirls were allegedly victims of sexual violence when about thirty final-year pupils were intercepted by unidentified armed men on Friday 19 June on the Kiseya-Kilambo road in Bafuna groupement, Walikale territory; the pupils were robbed of their belongings and then released.

Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that Wazalendo attacked AFC/M23 positions in Kalembe, Masisi territory, on the night of Sunday 24 to Monday 25 May 2026; residents said a provisional toll was five people killed and nine injured, all civilians, and that houses and shops were also pillaged. The outlet said no official communication had been made, and that Kalembe remained under AFC/M23 control.

Radio Okapi reported that dozens of residents of Kihuma village, Buabo groupement, Masisi territory, were victims of pillaging during an incursion by armed men on the night of Sunday to Monday 27 April; local notable sources also reported the abduction of two young boys, whose whereabouts were unknown.

Radio Okapi reported that local civil society of Buabo said at least fifteen civilians had been shot dead in one month in attacks by armed men in several localities of the Buabo entity, Masisi territory, an area it described as under AFC/M23 occupation where several other armed groups also operate; it said an attack on Friday 25 April in Ndete and Mashaki killed five civilians, including a teacher, an infant and its mother.

place: Kinyumba and Nyabiondo (Isiro quarter), Osso-Banyungu sector, Masisi
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that violent fighting had opposed AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo militiamen since early Friday 27 February on the Kinyumba axis, about ten kilometres north of Nyabiondo (Osso-Banyungu sector, Masisi); according to the same sources it was reportedly an attack launched by AFC/M23 against positions held by Wazalendo. The sources also said at least three civilians were wounded on the Thursday evening when a military device exploded in the Isiro quarter, in the centre of Nyabiondo.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that after violent fighting on Sunday 5 April between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo at Lukweti, about ten kilometres east of Nyabiondo (Masisi), the M23 assailants were repelled and fell back to Nyabiondo, their starting position; the locality, described as a Wazalendo stronghold, remained under Wazalendo control with an uneasy calm from Monday afternoon. No toll had been communicated.

place: Nyabiondo; Bahunde chiefdom villages around Rubaya, Masisi
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the Wazalendo briefly retook control of Nyabiondo (Osso-Banyungu sector, Masisi) on Wednesday before being dislodged again; it also reported that clashes had continued for several days in the Bahunde chiefdom, affecting the localities of Kasenyi, Kinigi, Runigi, Kanyaru, Nyakigano, Nyamyamba and Kasaki, around Rubaya.

place: Ngungu–Ufamandu axis, Nyabiondo, Katoyi, Bahunde chiefdom, Masisi
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that amid the fighting around Nyabiondo, Katoyi and the Bahunde chiefdom (Masisi), health structures faced a shortage of medicines, the Ngungu–Ufamandu road had been cut for more than ten days and prices of basic goods were rising.

place: Walikale and Masisi territories (Yaki, Kasopo, Ndete, Mulema, Luke, Kasenyi, Mbizo)
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, mass displacement and villages nearly emptied of inhabitants since Sunday 31 May in Walikale and Masisi territories after new clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo groups allied to the FARDC; it named villages affected in Masisi (Ndete, Mulema, Luke, Kasenyi, Mbizo).

place: Yaki, between Kashebere and Miba, Luberike groupement, Walikale
statement: Radio Okapi reported that violent clashes on Sunday 31 May at Yaki, between Kashebere and Miba in Luberike groupement (Walikale), opposed AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters of the NDC-Rénové group led by Guidon Shimiray.

place: Kibati, Luberike groupement, Mungazi–Kashebere axis, Walikale
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that after fighting on Sunday 1 March the two sides were said to share control of Kibati (Luberike groupement, Walikale): FARDC and allied Wazalendo reportedly held the centre of Kibati and two former rebel positions, while AFC/M23 still held two positions on the axis to Kashebere; fighting resumed on Monday 2 March, the third consecutive day, after rebel reinforcements arrived from Kashebere.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that after two days of intense fighting begun Sunday 31 May with an offensive by regular forces against rebel positions, a precarious calm held on Tuesday 2 June at Kibati (Walikale), where FARDC and Wazalendo occupied the centre and the rebels the surrounding hills; traffic between Mungazi and Kashebere was suspended.

place: Buhimba, Waloa Yungu groupement, Walikale/Masisi boundary
statement: Actualite.cd reported that fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo began on Saturday 13 June 2026 at Buhimba (Waloa Yungu groupement, Walikale), after Wazalendo positions there were bombed around 15:00 local time; the outlet said Buhimba had been under Wazalendo control for a week after they dislodged AFC/M23 following intense fighting.

place: Buhimba, Waloa Yungu groupement, Walikale (rebels from Kasopo, Masisi)
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing customary sources in Waloa Yungu groupement, that on Thursday 1 January AFC/M23 rebels coming from Kasopo (Masisi) tried to retake Buhimba, on the Walikale-Masisi boundary, which they had lost about two months earlier, and that, according to its sources, the FARDC supported by Wazalendo repelled them back to Kasopo and about ten AFC/M23 fighters were captured by the army. The outlet added that FARDC officials in Walikale had promised to comment within hours.

place: Kashuga–Kalembe road, Bashali Mokoto groupement, Masisi
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing a witness, that on the morning of Tuesday 27 January 2026 six armed men in military uniform intercepted a motorcycle taxi rider and two passengers about two kilometres from Kashuga on the Kashuga-Kalembe road (Bashali Mokoto groupement, Masisi); the outlet reported the victims were beaten and tortured and taken to an unknown destination, and that one escaped.

place: North Kivu / eastern DRC front lines (statement)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, whom it described as president of the movement and its deputy coordinator, said on Wednesday that the Kinshasa regime had 'once again trampled the ceasefire' by launching a 'generalised offensive on all front lines and beyond', and that there had been 'no public reprimand, no condemnation' of it; the outlet also reported that spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a separate communiqué, reported attacks that day in Minembwe and Kalehe.

place: Kibanda, near Kasopo, Nyamaboko 1 groupement, Masisi
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that on Wednesday 25 February fighting resumed at Kibanda, about two kilometres from Kasopo (Nyamaboko 1 groupement, Osso Banyungu sector, Masisi), where Congolese soldiers and Wazalendo coming from Buhimba (Walikale) launched an offensive against AFC/M23 positions; the outlet said AFC/M23 had occupied the locality for several months.

place: Masisi-Centre, Masisi (HGR Masisi and MSF logistics base)
statement: Congoprofond.net reported that a violent fire broke out on Monday 19 January 2026 around 23:00 at the logistics base of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) and spread to much of the Masisi General Reference Hospital (HGR) in Masisi-Centre; at publication the fire was still burning, no official source had given a cause and no casualty toll had been communicated.

place: Bumbasha, Karambi, Chahemba (Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru) and Mweso, Masisi
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that violent clashes on Monday 12 January between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo of the CMC group, starting at Bumbasha a few kilometres from Mweso, caused hundreds of residents to flee toward neighbouring villages and to Mweso centre in Masisi, where they took refuge in churches and schools; no toll was communicated.

Actualite.cd reported, citing customary and local security sources, that the town of Katoy, seat of Katoy sector in Masisi territory, returned to Wazalendo control on Sunday 12 July after fighting with AFC/M23; the Wazalendo offensive was said to have been launched by fighters from Waloa Loanda groupement in Walikale, and AFC/M23 were said to have withdrawn towards the Ngungu axis.

place: Walikale territory (groupements Waloa Uroba and Bakano)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the NGO Groupe d'action pour la protection de l'enfance (GAPE) said, in an interview on Wednesday 15 July 2026, that at least fifty-six children had been recruited by local armed militias, notably Wazalendo factions, in Walikale territory during the first two weeks of the school holidays; according to testimonies cited by GAPE's coordinator, the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily to join the groups.

place: Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements, Walikale
statement: Radio Okapi reported that GAPE's inquiries covered several localities of the Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements (Walikale), notably in the ranks of the armed groups 'Uhuru' of 'général Machite' and 'Kalomendo'; GAPE's coordinator, Bayomba Mishiki Bam’s, said that according to testimonies the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily.

Actualite.cd reported on 1 August 2026 that violent fighting between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo self-defence groups began in the early hours of Saturday 1 August at Shango village, Butsike locality, Nyamaboko 1 groupement, Masisi territory; per local sources AFC/M23 attacked Wazalendo positions and gunfire was heard in neighbouring Shoa and Mahanga, with no casualty or damage figures available.

place: Buleusa, Rusamambu, Kalonge, Kasopo, Kateku (Ikobo and Kisimba groupements), Walikale
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local sources, clashes on Monday 3 August in the Ikobo and Kisimba groupements (Walikale) between AFC/M23 and a coalition of Wazalendo groups were accompanied by looting; notables reported important looting at Buleusa, seat of Ikobo groupement, and nearby Rusamambu, where kiosks and shops were entirely emptied. Local sources said Wazalendo fighters led by self-proclaimed general Jonas Bigabo launched simultaneous attacks on AFC/M23 positions between midnight and 4 a.m.

Kivu Morning Post reported, citing concordant and administrative sources, that AFC-M23 fighters retook Remeka, seat of Ufamando groupement in Masisi territory, on Thursday 20 August 2026 after intense fighting against FARDC allied with Wazalendo; Kashukano, Kamuobe, Miano and Buuli were also said to have fallen to AFC-M23.

place: Luntukulu, Nzibira axis (location as printed by the source)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23, in a communiqué, accused government coalition forces of summarily executing several civilians at Luntukulu, on the Nzibira axis; according to AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka the victims allegedly included women and children.

place: Buruso (Masisi); Biriko, Kilambo, Busurungi (Walikale); Nyamaboko I
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing a notable contacted on the spot, that fighting on Saturday around Buruso (Ufamandu I groupement, Masisi) and Biriko (Waloa Loanda groupement, Walikale) between AFC/M23 and a Wazalendo coalition allied to the FARDC caused new displacement toward Walikale-Centre, Hombo and elsewhere; Radio Okapi described the Ufamandu I and II groupements as almost entirely emptied of residents, and military sources said they shot down on Saturday in Nyamaboko I a kamikaze drone attributed to AFC/M23.

Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that on Tuesday 8 September wazalendo dislodged AFC/M23 from Rutoboko and then retook Kibahemula in Nyamaboko 1er groupement, Masisi; the Humura commercial centre was said to remain under AFC/M23 control.

place: Kazinga, Humura, Ngomashi, Mwima, Burinda (Nyamaboko 1), Masisi
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing concordant sources, that AFC/M23 took control of the villages of Kazinga and Humura in Nyamaboko 1 groupement, Masisi, dislodging the Congolese army and Wazalendo militias who had retaken the area; an anonymous health source quoted said AFC/M23 had also retaken Ngomashi, Mwima, Humura and Burinda.

Mediacongo, carrying a report credited 'DMK, La Tempête des Tropiques / MCP', reported that, according to certain sources, the army allegedly used air strikes on Tuesday 8 September at around 5 p.m. against rebel positions at Malemo (Bahali Mokoto groupement, Masisi) and Luola (Walikale); local sources said they heard loud detonations.

Kivu Morning Post reported, citing anonymous local sources, that violent fighting began at about 5 a.m. on Thursday 10 September 2026 at Kibati, Luberike groupement, Walikale, when a Wazalendo-FARDC coalition launched an offensive on AFC-M23 positions; it described Kibati as having been under AFC-M23 control for several months, and a resident said no inhabitants remained in Kibati.

Actualite.cd reported on 18 September that the centre of Kibati, in Luberike groupement (Walikale), had returned under AFC/M23 control after the withdrawal of the FARDC and wazalendo, who had briefly occupied Kibati and advanced to Milonge, about five kilometres along the Kibati-Kashebere axis.

7sur7.cd reported that the FARDC, in a communiqué signed by Lieutenant Marc Elongo, spokesperson of operational sector Sokola 1 Grand-Nord and Front Nord, said on 20 September they observe the ceasefire on all North Kivu front lines while denouncing attacks they attribute to AFC/M23-RDF on the Walikale-Masisi axis, which they said violate the Doha and Washington accords and cause displacement toward Walikale, with villages burned and fields destroyed.

place: Masisi, Walikale and Rutshuru territories; Miko hill and Remeka centre (Masisi)
statement: 7sur7.cd reported a communiqué from major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region, in which the FARDC, supported by VDP, said they neutralised 14 AFC/M23 elements over three days of fighting in Masisi, Walikale and Rutshuru, with thirteen other fighters wounded, three captured and two VDP fighters killed; the FARDC said they retook the Miko hill and Remeka centre (Masisi) on Tuesday 15 September 2026.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting resumed early on Friday 25 September between AFC/M23 and the FARDC supported by wazalendo at Remeka, Ufamandu 1er groupement (Masisi), about a week after the FARDC and wazalendo retook the centre of Remeka in a counter-offensive; AFC/M23 reportedly attacked with reinforcements from Ngungu.

Actualite.cd reported that Médecins Sans Frontières was transferring its medical activities at Sake, Masisi territory, to Première Urgence Internationale after 13 months; in that period MSF teams treated more than 10 300 survivors of sexual violence, and MSF said it was redirecting resources to other areas including Katoyi in Masisi.

Radio Okapi reported that the Club des Filles Reporters RDC (CFR RDC), after a mission from 25 to 27 September 2026, said nearly 2 350 displaced families lived in precarious conditions at Lukaraba (Walikale) and Hombo Sud (Kalehe, South Kivu); at Lukaraba the families had fled Ziralo, Ufamandu, Remeka, Lurere and Biriko, and at Hombo Sud the hospital was said to be under strain from sick or war-wounded displaced people.

place: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (call on North and South Kivu conflict)
statement: Jeune Afrique reported that the leaders of SADC and EAC, meeting in a summit in Tanzania, urged an end to fighting between the Congolese army and the M23 and its Rwandan allies, and that the defence chiefs of the two blocs were tasked to meet within five days and give technical guidance on an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, a spokesperson said.

place: Luanda, Angola (mediation on eastern DRC conflict)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Angola's earlier mediation ended after two diplomatic setbacks: it had announced the end of its mediation and said it wanted to concentrate on African Union priorities.
Actualite.cd reported that a joint summit of SADC and EAC heads of state had resulted on Monday in the merger of the Luanda and Nairobi processes.

place: Washington, D.C. (sanctions relating to North and South Kivu conflict)
statement: Al Jazeera reported that the US Treasury Department said on Thursday that Rwanda's Minister of State for Regional Integration James Kabarebe was being targeted because he is "central to Rwanda's support" for the M23 armed group.
BBC News reported that, responding to the US sanctions, Rwanda's foreign ministry said the sanctions would not resolve the conflict.

place: Washington, D.C. (agreement concerning the conflict in North and South Kivu)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the signing ceremony of the DRC-Rwanda peace agreement in Washington was presided over by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in the presence of Congolese Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner and her Rwandan counterpart Olivier Nduhungirehe.

The DRC foreign ministry said in a press release that the comprehensive peace accord with Rwanda was signed in Washington in the presence of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and described it as a decisive step towards ending the conflict.

place: Doha, Qatar (DRC government and AFC/M23; North and South Kivu conflict)
statement: UN News reported that, in a statement released on 19 July, MONUSCO said the Declaration of Principles signed in Doha under Qatari mediation between the DRC government and AFC/M23 "reflects the parties’ resolve to prioritise peaceful means, establish a ceasefire, and set up a joint mechanism to define its practical implementation."

The Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Minister of State Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulaziz bin Saleh Al Khulaifi affirmed that the signing of the Doha Framework Agreement for Peace between the DRC government and the Congo River Alliance (March 23 Movement), which took place Saturday, represents an important step.

The Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the parties' progress included the signing of the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism on October 14, 2025, and the detainee release mechanism on September 14, 2025.

BBC News Afrique reported that the verdict of the Haute Cour militaire in the trial of Joseph Kabila was delivered on a Tuesday after several postponements: the former Congolese president was sentenced to death by the court, which also ordered his immediate arrest.

place: Goma airport, North Kivu (statement made in Kigali/Rwanda)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe told the press on Thursday 30 October 2025 that any decision on reopening Goma airport must be taken within the Doha negotiations, and that Paris could not reopen an airport while those concerned were not present.

place: Goma airport, North Kivu (statement in Kinshasa)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya recalled that the reopening of Goma airport would take place only with the authorisation of the Congolese authorities and exclusively for daytime humanitarian flights.

place: Walikale, Masisi (North Kivu); Fizi, Walungu, Mwenga (South Kivu)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa asked on X how the reopening of Goma airport for humanitarian reasons could be discussed while Walikale and Masisi in North Kivu and Fizi, Walungu and Mwenga in South Kivu were, in his words, subjected daily to bombardments by the Kinshasa regime targeting civilian sites, factories, bridges, airfields and humanitarian aircraft.

Jeune Afrique reported that, after several days of pressure from the US administration, the Kigali-backed rebel group announced in the night of 15 to 16 December its intention to withdraw from the city of Uvira, which it had taken the previous week.

BBC News Afrique reported that, in a press release published Tuesday, AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa said the unilateral withdrawal followed a request from the American mediators. Anadolu Agency quoted a communiqué signed by Corneille Nangaa: "The AFC/M23 will unilaterally withdraw its forces from the city of Uvira, as requested by the American mediation".

The US State Department said, in a release on the signing of the Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity between the DRC and Rwanda, that the DRC and Rwanda signed the Regional Economic Integration Framework, that President Felix Tshisekedi signed on behalf of the Government of the DRC and President Paul Kagame on behalf of the Government of Rwanda, and that the signing ceremony was attended by, among others, Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye.

The US Department of the Treasury announced on 2 March 2026 that its Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) had imposed sanctions on the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and four of its senior officials, stating that the RDF is actively supporting, training, and fighting alongside the M23.

The US Treasury said that, days after the Washington Accords signing, M23 captured Uvira, a strategic city on the border with Burundi, in an offensive that resulted in civilian deaths and forced thousands of residents to flee their homes; it said that despite M23's subsequent exit from Uvira, its continued presence near the border with Burundi, and the RDF's continued support for M23, carried the risk of escalating the conflict into a broader regional war.

Radio Okapi reported that representatives of the Congolese government and the AFC/M23, meeting from 17 to 21 August 2026 in Switzerland, agreed new steps for the Doha peace process, including a roadmap for continuing negotiations and strengthened follow-up of their commitments.

BBC News Afrique reported that the creation of the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), with Joseph Kabila as president, was announced by FRN adviser Claude Ibalanky at a joint press conference at the former president's residence in Goma, a city controlled by the M23; BBC described the FRN as replacing the AFC-M23, and reported that Kabila would have as deputies the rebel leaders Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa, Freddy Kaniki and Sultani Makenga.

Sosoyamboka.net reported that, in a declaration published on Sunday 18 October, Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya denounced the creation of the FRN as a new label masking the actors in the crisis, and said: "Quelle que soit sa dénomination, ce groupe armé relooké est appelé à disparaître au terme du processus de Doha".

Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa said in Goma, in front of EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib and then the press, that the 'premiers demandeurs' for reopening the Goma international airport were the authorities in Goma, i.e. his movement, and that the AFC/M23 now said it accepted 'the principle' of discussions on the reopening process, 'taking into account the constraints' of the area it controls.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the AFC/M23 made public on 6 June 2026 in Goma decision N°033/COORDO-PR/AFC-M23/2026 appointing new political-administrative authorities in South Kivu, including Kyalangalilwa Mulondani Nicolas as mayor of Bukavu.

Radio Okapi reported that the Congolese Ministry of Higher Education (ESU-RSI) firmly condemned on Monday 10 August the AFC/M23's appointments at several public higher-education institutions in Goma and Bukavu, calling the appointments publicised on 7 August 2026 by the de facto authorities a 'grave and unacceptable interference'.
Actualite.cd reported that the AFC-M23 confirmed that a case of Ebola virus disease had been reported in Goma, an announcement made on Sunday 17 May 2026 by its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka.

A joint statement by the representatives of the Government of the DRC and of the AFC/M23, published by the African Union Peace and Security Department, said the Parties agreed on the critical importance of ensuring life-saving humanitarian assistance for the people of eastern DRC and made substantial progress toward a protocol on Humanitarian Access and Judicial Protection, agreed to refrain from attacks on objects indispensable to the survival of the civilian population, including hospital and school facilities, and agreed to respect and protect humanitarian actors.
sources: African Union Peace and Security Department

place: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Amnesty International said on 25 June 2026 that the Wazalendo member group CMC-FDP, backed by the Congolese army, has killed and tortured civilians, looted property, and abducted women as sexual slaves in Rutshuru territory; Amnesty interviewed 16 victims, survivors and family members about abuses between June and December 2025.

place: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Amnesty International reported that CMC-FDP spokesperson Héritier Donald Gashegu responded in writing on 16 June 2026 and denied responsibility for the abuses Amnesty documented, asserting that CMC-FDP remains committed to respecting human rights.

place: Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces
statement: Human Rights Watch and the Congolese organization SOFEPADI said that conflict-related sexual violence in eastern DRC had escalated, and that HRW had documented sexual violence by members of at least five non-state armed groups and the Congolese army.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (and Ituri)
statement: Human Rights Watch and SOFEPADI said that expanded fighting in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu, funding cuts and limited access to health services made it harder for survivors of sexual violence to get support, and that many clinics offering health care and other support had been forced to close.

Beto.cd reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye said on France 24 on 23 September 2026, on the margins of the UN General Assembly, that he saw no sign of disengagement of Rwandan forces from eastern DRC and judged that the FDLR were only a pretext.

Al Jazeera, citing AFP and Reuters, reported that on Monday the UN and government sources said a ceasefire monitoring team had arrived to track the Qatari-mediated truce, and that the UN said the mission had deployed to Minembwe in South Kivu, where intense fighting had persisted in recent months.
Actualite.cd reported that the villages of Muzinzi and Bwahungu in Walungu territory were the scene of fighting between the FARDC supported by the Wazalendo and the M23.

place: Bilalombili village near Mikenge, Itombwe, Mwenga territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to several local sources, fighting resumed early on 1 March 2025 in Bilalombili village near Mikenge, Mwenga territory, where the Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and Android elements allied to the M23 attacked Wazalendo positions.
Actualite.cd reported that local civil-society groups denounced the burning of houses in Bilalombili village, which had hosted people displaced from Mikenge and elsewhere, without giving a number.

place: Kilungutwe, Mwenga territory (from Walungu across the Kadubo river)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, after fighting with Wazalendo militiamen, the AFC/M23 rebels entered Mwenga territory late on Monday 3 March 2025 via the locality of Kilungutwe.

place: Walungu, Kaniola, Burhale, Bwahungu and Kamisisi, Walungu territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that on the Monday (3 March 2025) on which the M23 entered Mwenga, fighting was reported in Walungu, Kaniola, Burhale, Bwahungu and Kamisisi in Walungu territory, and that it counted the AFC/M23 as already present in six South Kivu territories (Mwenga, Kalehe, Kabare, Walungu, Uvira and Fizi), the count resting in part on the Twirweneho group's allegiance to the rebellion, with only Shabunda and Idjwi not yet affected by the war.

place: Kaziba Centre, Kaziba chefferie, Walungu territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels seized Kaziba Centre late at night on 10 March 2025 after a full day of fighting against the FARDC supported by Wazalendo militiamen.

place: Kaziba, Walungu territory; Kigarama and Rurambo, Uvira highlands
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that Kaziba in Walungu territory and the localities of Kigarama and Rurambo in the Uvira highlands had been occupied by Wazalendo since Saturday 15 March 2025, and that residents saw no AFC/M23 rebels in Kaziba.
Radio Okapi reported that two people died and many others were wounded in violent clashes on Tuesday 18 March between Wazalendo and the M23 in the Burhale groupement, Walungu territory.

Radio Okapi reported that the chef-lieu of Walungu territory was encircled, with the Wazalendo on one side and the M23 on the other, that the local administration was paralysed with its officials forced to live in hiding, and that the police and intelligence services were absent.

place: Butondo village, Ihanga groupement, Luindi chefferie, Mwenga territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that on Sunday 13 April M23 rebels and various Wazalendo groups opened a new front in Butondo village (Luindi chefferie, Ihanga groupement, Mwenga territory), and quoted a local source denouncing the looting of cows, saying the M23 left with 16 cows the first time.

Radio Okapi reported that clashes on Thursday 17 April between Wazalendo fighters and the AFC-M23 rebels in the Kamanyola groupement, launched by Wazalendo from the hills above Kamanyola against M23 positions in Kamanyola-Centre, began at 8:30 in Kalunga and lasted five hours, with wounded taken to a local medical institution according to sources on the spot.

place: Nyangezi, Walungu-Centre, Muzinzi and other positions around Bukavu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that M23 troop reinforcement was also seen on its positions in the rural areas under its control, a list that included Nyangezi, Walungu-Centre and Muzinzi.

place: Kaziba chefferie (Mushenyi, Cibanda, Nyanfunze), Walungu territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that several residents of Kaziba, Walungu territory, left their homes on Wednesday 23 April because of clashes between the AFC/M23 rebels and various Wazalendo groups.

Radio Okapi reported that Kaziba chefferie had been the scene of violent clashes since the evening of Saturday 26 April, that the AFC-M23 was trying to dislodge Wazalendo to reach the Minembwe highlands where its allies Twirwaneho, Androïd and Gumino are based, and that residents said five truckloads of soldiers arrived at Tchofi and Kasheke.

Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels retook control of Kaziba, Walungu territory, on Sunday 27 April after clashes with the Wazalendo, who were forced to pull back, and that several residents who fled Kaziba took refuge in neighbouring villages and chefferies, notably Luhwinja.

place: General Reference Hospital, Walungu Centre, Walungu territory
statement: Amnesty International reported that, after a security incident in Walungu Centre on 9 March, M23 fighters fired heavy weapons in the direction of the General Reference Hospital in Walungu, damaging the main hospital and injuring patients.

place: Walungu and Kabare territories, South Kivu
statement: The OHCHR-mandated fact-finding mission reported that in June and July M23 summarily executed dozens of individuals following confrontations with Government forces in Walungu and Kabare territories, South Kivu, as apparent collective punishment.

Radio Okapi reported that an official FARDC communiqué signed on Monday 23 June by army spokesperson General Sylvain Ekenge denounced a massacre by the RDF/AFC/M23 coalition that cost the lives of 17 civilians on Sunday 22 June around 18:30 at Munzinzi village, Walungu territory.

Ouragan.cd reported, citing the FARDC communiqué signed by spokesperson Sylvain Ekenge, that seventeen civilians were executed on the evening of Sunday 22 June at Munzinzi and that the army said the assailants acted in reprisal for military failures, accusing residents of collaborating with the regular army.

place: Kaziba chiefdom and Kamanyola (Walungu territory), South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that after fighting continued late on Tuesday in Kaziba chiefdom and at Kamanyola (Walungu territory), about ten civilians were killed by shells at Kaziba and three children in central Kamanyola.

place: Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on Tuesday 2 December violent clashes broke out from 3am in Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu territory, between the FARDC and the AFC rebels linked to M23, with heavy weapons fire heard into the morning.

place: Kamanyola and Katogota, Walungu and Uvira territories, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Kamanyola (Walungu territory) was divided: the FARDC controlled the southern part while the AFC-M23 rebels occupied the northern part up to the Rwandan border, after an AFC-M23 assault on FARDC advance positions at Katogota around 3am.

Radio Okapi reported that accounts of control of Kamanyola differed: some sources spoke of shared control between the belligerents, others of total control by the FARDC-Wazalendo coalition and the Burundian army, while all confirmed heavy-weapons detonations from surrounding mountains.

Radio Okapi reported that, according to civil society, at least seven dead and six wounded admitted to local health structures at Kamanyola within 48 hours, with civilians fleeing towards Bugarama in Rwanda and schools and markets closed.

place: Kamanyola and Lwanguku (Mwera hill), Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that bombs fell in the Rugenge neighbourhood in the centre of Kamanyola, destroying two houses and wounding several people including two children; it also reported, per a local human rights defender, that at least five people were reportedly killed, including a village chief, by a bomb near Lwanguku.

place: Katogota and Kamanyola, Uvira/Walungu territories, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that exchanges of fire concentrated around Katogota, facing Kamanyola, where Burundian, Congolese and Wazalendo positions faced M23 fighters, with a provisional toll of five civilians wounded including three children hit at home by shell fragments.

place: Walungu territory (Kaniola, Mulamba, Tubimbi, Kamisimbi, Nyangezi groupements), South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the collective of human rights organisations in Walungu territory published a report on Saturday 22 November 2025 stating at least 112 civilians, including women and children, had been killed since March 2025 in fighting involving AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo.

place: Kaniola, Mulamba, Tubimbi, Kamisimbi, Nyangezi, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Walungu human rights collective said the violence documented in the groupements of Kaniola, Mulamba, Tubimbi, Kamisimbi and Nyangezi was accompanied by rapes of women and large-scale pillage.

place: Kaniola groupement, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Walungu human rights collective's report cited two members of one family arrested in Kaniola groupement on 20 November during clashes between Wazalendo fighters and M23 rebels, with their families without news since, and called for their release.

place: Kirungutwe (Burhinyi) and Kasika (Wamuzimu), Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant local sources, that violent fighting broke out from Tuesday 25 November 2025 at Kirungutwe (Burhinyi chiefdom) and Kasika (Wamuzimu chiefdom), Mwenga territory, between AFC-M23 rebels and the FARDC supported by Wazalendo, killing at least ten civilians.

place: Kirungutwe-Kasika-Mwenga-Centre-Kamituga axis, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that accusations of pillage were made against the FARDC and the Wazalendo on the Kirungutwe, Kasika, Mwenga-Centre and Kamituga axis.

place: Maimingi, Kimbili, Nyalubemba, Shabunda territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the M23 occupied the villages of Kimbili and Nyalubemba in Shabunda territory on 20 November, after an offensive against FARDC and Wazalendo forward positions, and had taken the village of Maimingi on 16 November, described as the rebellion's first incursion into Shabunda territory.

place: Kibandamangobo forest, Shabunda territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that on Monday 6 October FARDC supported by Wazalendo were resisting AFC/M23 rebels, said to be backed by the Rwandan army, in the Kibandamangobo forest, Shabunda territory, preventing them reaching the territory's main town.
Radio Okapi reported, citing witnesses, that the fighting in Shabunda territory caused mass displacement of the population accompanied by scenes of pillage of civilian property.

Radio Okapi reported that violent clashes broke out on Tuesday 21 October 2025 between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo self-defence groups in the Nyangezi area, Walungu territory, and continued on 22 October.
Radio Okapi reported that on Monday 29 September FARDC supported by Wazalendo launched a counter-offensive to retake Nzibira, Walungu territory, a week after its occupation by AFC-M23 rebels.
Actualite.cd reported that fighting resumed on the morning of Sunday 10 August 2025 between AFC/M23 rebels and wazalendo militiamen at Mulamba, Walungu territory, according to its sources.

place: Mulamba and Kaniola, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that a few hours before the fighting resumed on 10 August, Didier Kabi, spokesperson of the South Kivu provincial government, said FARDC and wazalendo had withdrawn from Mulamba and Kaniola to avoid bloodshed and that these zones were controlled by the AFC/M23 rebels.

place: Mugogo, Walungu Centre, Cagala, Kaniola road, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that a precarious calm had prevailed since the afternoon of Wednesday 19 November in several Walungu territory villages after clashes between wazalendo factions and AFC/M23, notably at Mugogo, Walungu Centre and Cagala on the Kaniola road, where heavy and light weapons were heard on Tuesday.

place: Kalimbi, Kasika, Lwindi bridge, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, per independent sources, the rebels were reportedly at Kalimbi, 5 km from Mwenga-centre, while the army and its allies were reportedly at the Lwindi bridge; per local civil society the AFC-M23 was still at Kasika and its surroundings and only patrolling Kalimbi-centre, while on Sunday 30 November 2025 displaced families moved towards Kitutu and Kamituga.

place: Kilungu-Kasika axis, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga territory; Nyamibungu aerodrome, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that Burundian soldiers positioned on the Kilungu-Kasika axis in Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga territory, reportedly left their positions for Kamituga, with videos on social media on Sunday 19 October 2025 showing hundreds of Burundian soldiers, and local sources and civil society confirmed it.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil society, that two people were killed and several wounded in clashes between the FARDC and Wazalendo combatants in Kamituga on Thursday 9 October 2025, triggered by the killing of a FARDC captain attributed to armed men assimilated to Wazalendo, with combat lasting about four hours.

Radio Okapi reported that young people of Kamituga demonstrated on Friday 10 October to demand that Wazalendo leave, accusing them of abuses including theft and murder, and that the president of the Espace Lega council, Crispin Mpombo, called on the government to protect civilians.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that a mixed unit of police and FARDC soldiers dispersed a peaceful march in Kamituga on Tuesday 22 July against electricity overbilling by the company CRE SEKO, with live fire and tear gas reported and several arrests; organiser Lucky Mutiki said the movement would continue.

place: Kamituga (Bitanga) and Lupupu mining site, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that a young man named as NDINO DONATIEN, accused of having raped, killed and buried a 13-year-old girl on Thursday 31 July, was arrested on Friday 1 August 2025 near the Lupupu mining site; the Mwenga civil society president Hilaire ISOMBYA named the victim as Bitondo Byamungu.

place: Kalimoto near Kalambi, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that a Médecins Sans Frontières convoy was attacked by Wazalendo militiamen on "vendredi 3 mai" (as printed; 3 May 2026 was a Sunday) at the former hot spot called Kalimoto, a few kilometres from Kalambi in Lwindi chiefdom (Mwenga territory), while heading to Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu to assess humanitarian needs; it reported that the agents were looted and that MSF staff came out unharmed.

place: Kisenya village, Bamunguba-Sud groupement, Bakisi chiefdom, Shabunda territory
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least six people were killed and seven others wounded in fighting between two Wazalendo factions on Friday 20 February 2026 in Kisenya village, Shabunda territory, which caused the displacement of more than 1073 households; quoting Shabunda territory civil society, it said Wazalendo elements of the Kiseketi dit Solide group (known as Katabilalo) and of Mukamba Lukabya dit Karuleta clashed with Wazalendo elements of the Ngandu Lundimu group, and that the provisional toll would be six dead, including three men, a woman and two children aged 14 and 17, with seven seriously wounded and about 1073 households displaced into the bush.

place: Bubala village, Bamunguba-Sud groupement, Bakisi chiefdom, Shabunda territory (about 65 km north-east of Shabunda-centre)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing Shabunda civil society, that in the night of 20 to 21 February 2026 Wazalendo elements of the armed group of a self-proclaimed general "BASILA", coming from Lulingu, made incursions at Bubala village, fired shots and looted livestock and valuables, and that Bubala institute teacher Munembwe Samitamba was wounded by bullets in the back.

place: Kalole-Masanganjia axis to Mukoloka, Shabunda territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that national deputy Placide Wenda, in an alert launched on Tuesday 3 March in Kinshasa, denounced serious crimes including torture and human mutilations by armed men in Shabunda territory, and noted that inhabitants reportedly had ears cut off or eyes gouged out; Radio Okapi said two people died in one week in clashes between two Wazalendo factions on the Kalole-Masanganjia axis to Mukoloka.

place: Wakabango chiefdom and Bamuguba-Sud groupement, Shabunda territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Wazalendo groups had been officially declared undesirable by the different social strata in Shabunda territory, accused of atrocities against civilians including widespread looting, extortion and mutilations; local sources said on Thursday 5 March that the social climate had become deleterious in Wakabango chiefdom and Bamuguba-Sud groupement; and it reported that the provincial infrastructure minister publicly asked the Wazalendo to withdraw without delay from the territory capital.

Radio Okapi reported, citing the army, that FARDC captured warlord Amisi Sisawa alias "Muswahili", leader of an armed group claiming to be Wazalendo, in an operation on Sunday in the locality of Kitete, Shabunda-Centre, with fire exchanged in the early hours of Sunday 29 March; according to the army the operation ended with the arrest of Amisi Sisawa and thirteen of his fighters, and the toll also reported two dead and two seriously wounded.

Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Nord-Sud Kivu operational sector, Meya Jérémie, said the group led by "Muswahili" was involved in several serious human rights violations, the alleged acts including looting, extortion, torture and forced labour, notably in mining areas.

Radio Okapi reported that the administrator of Shabunda territory, Justin Balegamire Byenda, detained in Maniema for more than nine months, was acquitted by military justice and reinstated on Thursday by provincial justice minister Faustin Mayani Shindano, amid an open conflict with his deputy Konga Konga, each reportedly relying on Wazalendo militiamen to assert power.

Radio Okapi reported that Mwenga territory civil society accused some FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo (VDP) of involvement in torture, killings and looting, in an area it described as under central government control.

Radio Okapi reported that Mwenga territory administrator Ishikitilo Mao said that on receiving the civil society's letter about some undisciplined soldiers "we convened a meeting with the military authorities", and that the FARDC commander in charge of the Mwenga sector admitted the presence of "brebis galeuses" (black sheep) within his troops and said he had already sanctioned three elements, including one Muzalendo volunteer, transferred to the general staff in Kisangani.

place: Ilinda; Kibumba [as printed "Kibumb a"], Mwenga territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Lungele Itebo, president of the Mwenga civil society coordination framework, cited an incident on 12 March in which Dodos Ngama, a young man of 30, was "fusillé" (shot) by a "VDP -RAD Wazalendo" element at Ilinda, and said that on 13 March Mukaba Masilia Ndebo, aged 56, was also "fusillé" at "Kibumb a" (spelling as printed).

Radio Okapi reported that Lungele Itebo, president of the Mwenga civil society coordination framework and part of a team documenting abuses attributed to groups presented as "pseudo Wazalendo", listed among recent cases that nurse Bwato Mulungula was stripped of all his belongings at Musika on 03 March 2026.

place: Mwenga centre, Buziba, Kitutu, Lugushwa, Kakemenge, Kibe, Mwenga territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that on Tuesday 24 March residents of Mwenga observed a "ville morte" (stay-at-home day) to denounce multiple harassments by some FARDC and Wazalendo elements; Samuel Itebo, president of the Mwenga civil society forces vives, said some FARDC and Wazalendo elements extort the population and threaten to kill those who resist, and denounced the reappearance of paying barriers, the seizure and use of civilians' motorcycles by soldiers without compensation, and the occupation of hotels and civilians' houses without compensation.

Actualite.cd reported, quoting the association AFJEP, that on the night of 27 January around 21h a man of about 45, a state agent assigned to the mining service, sexually raped a 3-year-old girl, and that the victim was taken to Kamituga General Referral Hospital (Hôpital Général de Référence de Kamituga) for medical care; according to women's rights defenders the act took place in Sawasa neighbourhood, and the alleged perpetrator was in the hands of law enforcement. The source does not link the incident to the armed conflict.

place: Ilundu village, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that deaths were reported in Ilundu village, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, on Sunday 7 June, and that according to local sources bombardments in the area killed at least two people; local civil society sources said one of the two dead was a young person aged 19. The outlet said the wounded included two children, one of them aged 7 (its headline gives six wounded in all), and said two classrooms of Ilundu primary school were damaged. The article does not say who carried out the bombardments; its headline refers to drone bombardments.

Kivu Morning Post reported that Twirwaneho fighters, allies of AFC-M23, retook the locality of Mikenge in the highlands of Mwenga territory after fighting against FARDC supported by Wazalendo and the Burundian army; according to local sources Mikenge fell after Congolese army drone strikes followed by ground fighting on Monday 8 June 2026.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the Congolese army retook the city of Mikenge, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, on Wednesday 10 June 2026; according to local sources the army counter-attacked with attack drones, pushing Twirwaneho fighters to withdraw during the night, and a security source of the Congolese army said it had retaken Kalingi and Mikenge that morning. The same article quoted an administrative source in the area saying violent fighting was still under way at Mikenge and elsewhere that morning.

place: Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi (Mwenga and Fizi territories)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC announced they had retaken, on the morning of Wednesday 10 June, control of Mikenge, Kakenge and Kalingi in the highlands of Fizi and Mwenga territories; according to an army communiqué these localities had been occupied the previous Monday by a coalition of Twirwaneho and M23, whose assailants reportedly used military drones, and the FARDC said the recapture followed a counter-offensive of about 48 hours with Wazalendo support. Fizi territory administrator Samy Kalonji Badibanga confirmed the recapture and gave an earlier date than the communiqué for the return of Mikenge to FARDC control (see note), and said the attack of Monday 8 June was reportedly facilitated by drones attributed to AFC/M23 and by allied armed groups, notably Red Tabara and Twirwaneho.

place: Gakenke and surroundings, Minembwe highlands, Lulenge sector, Fizi territory
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that on Wednesday 10 June 2026 the "coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime", notably the FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo and elements of the Burundian national force, launched attacks against the densely populated areas of Gakenke and surroundings in the Minembwe highlands (Lulenge sector, Fizi territory); on X he said the attacks, carried out with kamikaze-type and KT-6 combat drones and heavy artillery, caused heavy loss of life, destroyed many homes and forced civilians to flee. Kivu Morning Post said no communication was possible in the zone, telephone lines and the internet being cut.

Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to "independent sources" it did not name, at least some thirty ("au moins une trentaine") soldiers of the Burundian army reportedly lost their lives on Tuesday 9 June 2026 in fighting on the Minembwe axis, which continued the next day.

place: Mikenge, Bukunji, Bichumbe near Point Zéro, Mwenga and Fizi territories
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least 21 people, including 15 soldiers of the DRC armed forces, were killed in clashes on Wednesday 20 May 2026 between the Twirwaneho allied to AFC-M23 and the Congolese army, supported by Wazalendo militias and the Burundian army, in Fizi and Mwenga territories; according to concordant sources and civil society, the toll was recorded at FARDC positions in Mikenge (9 dead), Bukunji village (three dead) and Bichumbe village near Point Zéro (three dead). The outlet said the toll remained provisional because the zone was inaccessible to the press, and that a security source disputed it.

place: Mikenge, Bukunji, Bichumbe, Mwenga and Fizi territories
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that a security source contacted in the region refuted the outlet's toll for the clashes (see the related claim) and instead gave a figure of 4 dead and six wounded.

place: Mwenga health zone (Iganda, Sungwe, Kalole, Tuseswa), Kamituga and Kitutu health zones, Mwenga territory
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that Lungele Itebo Samuel, president of the Mwenga territory civil society, said that in January 2026 the Kamituga and "Kititu" (as printed) health zones were hit by a measles epidemic causing deaths, especially among children, with no response so far, and that since February 2026 the population of Mwenga health zone had been hit by cholera, with 13 deaths and 34 cases under inappropriate treatment to date in health facilities of Iganda, Sungwe, Kalole, Tuseswa and the Mwenga general referral hospital; the civil society said these facilities lacked pharmaceutical products to eradicate the epidemic.

Radio Okapi reported that Kaniola civil society said three civilians returning from a Léopards match were summarily executed on 24 September at Kaniola, naming them as Birhalugirakulimushi Jules, Kashokwire Kulimushi Isaac and Bizimana Ciraza.

place: Kaniola groupement, Ngweshe chiefdom, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Opinion-info reported that the South Kivu civil society's provincial coordination bureau said three civilians were killed at about 20:30 on the evening of Thursday 24 September after being violently beaten, identifying them as Birhalugurha Kulimushi Jules (55), Bashokwire Kulimushi Isaac (35) and Bizimana Ciragiza (36), and saying they were returning from the DRC-Guinea match.

place: Luntukulu, Mulamba groupement, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Opinion-info reported that South Kivu civil society said it had received alerts of several murders of civilians at Luntukulu (Mulamba groupement), more than ten cases in September, which the article says were given without documentation allowing independent verification; the article adds that cases of beatings, rapes and forced recruitment of young people are also reported.

place: Nzibira-Luntukulu and Kashanja, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Kaniola civil society said that on 21 September at Nzibira-Luntukulu two teachers were tortured and subjected to an attempted assassination, and that on 23 September at Kashanja a taxi driver from Kalengera, Zigashane Mashali, was extorted of 30 000 Congolese francs (13 USD) before being killed by beating.

place: Kange, Luciga groupement, Luhwinja chiefdom, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Opinion-info reported that, according to the civil society, men presented as AFC/M23 police positioned at Munanira allegedly attacked with sticks and a knife a civilian identified as Bisasi Cinigi at Kange, Luciga groupement, Luhwinja chiefdom, on Thursday 24 September.

place: Nzibira-Shabunda road, Nzibira (Walungu) to Shabunda, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Kaniola civil society ('forces vives') said on Friday 16 October that the Nzibira-Shabunda road had been blocked for nearly four weeks, that it accuses AFC/M23 fighters (now Front pour la refondation de la nation) of demanding the recruitment of 10 young people from Nzibira in their ranks as the price of reopening it, and that the blockage greatly disturbs economic activity and access to health care.

place: Nzibira and Kaniola, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, according to information provided by civil society, that the localities of Nzibira and Kaniola (Walungu territory) remained under the influence of the rebellion, and that attempts by Wazalendo fighters to retake these areas were said to meet resistance.

Radio Okapi reported that the citizens' movement OBAPG said the latest reported attack on the Bukavu-Walungu-Mwenga road occurred at Kankinda, where several traders were robbed of their goods and women were reportedly victims of sexual violence.

place: Lugushwa, Wamuzimu chiefdom, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local civil society, a young man known as Safa was killed in the night from Tuesday to Wednesday 21 October at Lugushwa, Mwenga territory, hit by two bullets said to have been fired by a female Wazalendo fighter as he returned from a Champions League match screening; activities were paralysed in Lugushwa the next day and the exact circumstances remained to be established.

Radio Okapi reported that the civil society of Kitutu village, Mwenga territory, alerted to the continued presence of soldiers and Wazalendo fighters in mining sites of the area, one month after President Félix Tshisekedi's order for the immediate and definitive withdrawal of forces illegally present in the mines.

Radio Okapi reported that Félicien Myaka, president of the Kitutu civil society, said any dissenting voice is immediately silenced, sometimes by violence, and urged local authorities to apply the head of state's order on forces in mining sites.

place: Kashongo, Magunda, Msongyo and Maheta, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that massive population displacements had been recorded for several days in the villages of Kashongo, Magunda, Msongyo and Maheta following clashes of 24 to 27 September 2026 between the AFC/M23 coalition, which it described as backed by Red Tabara and Twirwaheno, and the FARDC/Wazalendo; the local Itombwe youth council said the incidents caused large population movements.

place: Itombwe sector (Kashongo, Magunda, Msongyo, Maheta), Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the Itombwe local youth council said a significant proportion of displaced households lacked adequate shelter and had difficulty accessing food and drinking water, and that several schools and health structures were reportedly closed, damaged or difficult to reach.

place: Point Zéro Centre, Itombwe sector, South Kivu (the article says Mwenga territory)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, violent clashes had been under way since the morning of 28 August between AFC/M23 rebels and their allies and the FARDC backed by Wazalendo groups in the Point Zéro area, which the article places in Mwenga territory, with fighting beginning around 4 a.m. in the Itombwe highlands at Point Zéro Centre.

place: Mwenga territory (Kamituga, Kitutu, Kibe, Lugushwa, Kibumba, Ngenga), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that videos had circulated online a few days earlier showing elements assimilated to the Wazalendo vandalising trucks during construction work at Mwenga; civil society called for legal action against the authors of the vandalism 'à balles réelles' on 31 July 2026 at Ngenga, and demanded the opening of a secured humanitarian corridor for humanitarian NGOs wishing to intervene in the government-held part.

place: Cirimiro, boundary of Kaziba and Luhwindja chiefdoms, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: KazibaOnline reported that the Cirimiro commercial centre, at the boundary of the Kaziba and Luhwindja chiefdoms, was targeted by an armed looting on the evening of Sunday 11 October 2026, in which, per information reported to it, a trader was shot, a motorbike was burned and goods were taken; it named the wounded trader as Mugisho Eraston Gadi Nakahakwa and said the attackers' identity remained to be established.

place: Mitimbili hills, Ntagereka groupement, eastern Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: KazibaOnline reported, citing a local source, that a resumption of clashes was reported on Monday 12 October 2026 on the Mitimbili hills, Ntagereka groupement, starting about 6 a.m., and that the source said the fighting opposed M23 elements to the FARDC and Wazalendo fighters; no human or material toll could yet be established.

Actualite.cd reported that M23 rebels conquered the cité of Minova (Kalehe territory) in South Kivu on Monday 20 January, after intense fighting on the last hills of Masisi territory in neighbouring North Kivu.

Actualite.cd reported, quoting a journalist who attended a meeting held by M23 in Minova, that the rebels said schools could reopen within 48 hours and promised that the RN2 Minova-Bweremana-Sake-Goma road would be reopened.

place: Kavumu and Katana, Kabare, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that two people died and two others were wounded after shooting by FARDC soldiers in Kabare territory, 25 km north of Bukavu, on the evening of Monday 20 January; local sources said the victims were hit by bullets fired by a group of FARDC soldiers heading to the front. The deputy commander of the military region in charge of intelligence and operations confirmed the shooting without giving its motive, and did not confirm the toll.

place: Miti and Kavumu, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the citizen movement LUCHA denounced killings in Miti and Kavumu (Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory) during the night of Friday to Saturday 8 February; in a statement signed in Bukavu LUCHA reported that 9 people were killed by what it called undisciplined soldiers of the Congolese armed forces.
Radio Okapi reported that the Kavumu airport in South Kivu passed under the control of M23 rebels, supported by Rwanda, on the afternoon of Friday 14 February.

place: Kabamba (Irhambi Katana) to Kabare, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the rebels and their allies, the Rwandan armed forces, entered Kabare territory from the cité of Kabamba in the Irhambi Katana grouping on the morning of Friday 14 February.
Radio Okapi reported that M23 fighters, supported by the Rwandan army, appeared in the streets of Bukavu, chef-lieu of South Kivu, on Sunday 16 February.

place: Nyabibwe, Kalehe, Kavumu airport, Bukavu, South Kivu
statement: Afrikarabia reported a sequence of M23 captures in South Kivu: Nyabibwe on 5 February, Kalehe on 12 and the Kavumu airport on 14, before entering Bukavu on 15 February.

UN News (Swahili) reported that the UN Humanitarian Coordinator, Lemarquis, said in a video interview with UN News that Kalehe, which he described as a large town in the province, had fallen that afternoon.
BBC Gahuza reported that M23 fighters entered the small town of Kamanyola, on the border of DR Congo, Burundi and Rwanda, on Tuesday night, according to residents.

BBC Gahuza reported that Radio RFI said there was fighting on Tuesday between M23 and Burundian troops who were camped at Kamanyola, before those troops fled; it also reported that the FARDC did not respond to BBC's request about the capture of Kamanyola.

CAJ News Africa reported that the Panzi Foundation, whose headquarters are in Bukavu and which runs a hospital, was wary of the safety of its staff after rebel forces took control of Bukavu, and quoted Panzi as saying its team was unharmed, Panzi Hospital remained open with an on-call staff, and its surgeons were treating an influx of patients with gunshot wounds and severe injuries from explosives.

place: Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2, Nyawaronga, Kalehe highlands
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on Wednesday 9 April, on the Kalehe highlands, Wazalendo of COPACO and MCDPN, commanded by self-proclaimed generals Kirikicho, Maike and Bahige, recovered Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2 and Nyawaronga after fighting with M23 backed by Rwanda.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local activists, that after fighting on Sunday 6 and Monday 7 April on the hills above Bushushu, Lemera and Ihusi, local sources said most of the population of the Kalehe highlands had displaced toward Bushushu, Mabuka and Ihusi.

Radio Okapi reported that M23, supported by Rwandan forces, retook four localities of Kalehe and Kabare territories on Tuesday 15 April after fighting with Wazalendo allied to the FARDC, including Lemera, Bushaku 1 and Bushaku 2 (Kalehe) and Kabamba (Kabare).
Radio Okapi reported that the localities retaken included Kabamba (Kabare), where three civilians were killed in the Irhambi Katana groupement; the source does not say who killed them.
Kivu Morning Post reported that M23 also controlled the Kavumu airport (Kabare territory) after attack attempts on the town the previous weekend.

Radio Okapi reported that, according to concordant testimonies, M23/AFC reinforcements arrived by Lake Kivu from North Kivu and by road from Bukavu and Kavumu, a redeployment that sources in the region said followed the Wazalendo's temporary recapture of Kavumu airport on 13 April.

Radio Okapi reported that M23 rebels were accused of looting on Sunday 20 April during their withdrawal from the Kalehe highlands, and that witnesses said they systematically ransacked kiosks and shops in the Kasheke commercial centre.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that during the same M23 movement from the Kalehe highlands passers-by had phones and money stolen and others, in particular young people, were forced to carry the rebels' luggage.

Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that Wazalendo fought M23 for at least an hour at Irambo, and that a man of about thirty was shot dead inside the grounds of the Catholic parish of Irambo Kalehe as a result of the violence.

place: Kasheke-Lemera axis; Tchofi, Kasheke (Kalehe); Kabamba, Mabingu (Kabare)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on Wednesday 14 May tension remained high at Tchofi and Kasheke (Kalehe) and Kabamba and Mabingu (Kabare), that M23 was pushed back on Tuesday evening from Katasomwa to the Kasheke and Tchofi ports, and that sources on site said it resumed fighting on Wednesday morning with troops from Bukavu and Goma.

Congo Rassure reported that on the morning of Monday 12 May shots caused panic at Mugote market, in the south of Idjwi island, as the population tried to oppose taxes imposed by M23 rebels, which it said now control that part of the territory.

place: Chofi and Fizi, Mbinga-Sud groupement, Kalehe
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing human rights defenders in Kalehe, that about 18 young people suspected of belonging to the Wazalendo were taken to an unknown destination by the rebels during a 'youth hunt' that began on Friday at Chofi.
