Radio Okapi reported that the same rights defenders said one of the abducted young people was reportedly killed, and that a couple accused of being close to M23 was abducted by Wazalendo at Kamunyerere.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that on the evening of Thursday 5 June Wazalendo attacked M23 positions at Mabingu, on the Kabare-Kalehe boundary, which M23 had held for about ten days, and succeeded in dislodging the rebels.

place: Edge of Kahuzi-Biega National Park near Mabingu; Kasheke axis, Kalehe
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, while losing ground at Mabingu, M23 rebels carried out round-ups targeting men whom they equate with Wazalendo fighters, and that these arbitrary arrests took place at the edge of Kahuzi-Biega National Park, according to witnesses.

Radio Okapi reported, citing human rights activists, that the Mabingu fighting caused the death of one civilian and seriously wounded two people, a woman and an 11-year-old girl, and that residents of Mbinga Sud (Tchofi, Kasheke, Luzira) fled toward Idjwi island, Kajuchu and the Ihoka and Ishovu islets.

Radio Okapi reported that on Saturday 7 June AFC/M23 rebels ransacked all the equipment needed to run the Lemera tea factory in Kalehe territory, and that local sources said ploughing machinery was taken to an unknown destination.

place: Cirunga, Mumosho, Katana (Kabare); Kalehe; Nyangezi, Lurhala (Walungu)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that fighting between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo intensified on Wednesday 18 June in Kabare (Cirunga, Mumosho, Katana), Kalehe and Walungu (Nyangezi, Lurhala), and that at Cirunga a resident said two people died when Wazalendo tried to dislodge AFC/M23.

7sur7.cd reported violent clashes between Wazalendo and AFC/M23 on several front lines in South Kivu since Tuesday 17 June 2025, and that on 18 June residents of Cirunga said they saw bodies on the ground, causing general panic in the Bagira commune of Bukavu where schools sent pupils home.

place: FOMULAC general hospital, Katana health zone, Kabare
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that Dr Yolande Nshombo, head doctor of the Katana health zone (Kabare), told Governor Emmanuel Birato, AFC-M23 representative, on Sunday 25 May that the FOMULAC general hospital was caring for many war wounded and managing a cholera epidemic, and that it lacked medical supplies.

Radio Maendeleo reported that health care providers said that since the capture of Bukavu, health structures in the Baraka area (Fizi territory) were no longer supplied and pharmacies struggled to find appropriate medicines.

place: ANR main office and military camp, Bagira, Bukavu
statement: Amnesty International reported that M23 detention sites in Bukavu were the main ANR office and a military camp in the Bagira district; it said that at the time of publication it had received no response from representatives of the M23 (or from Rwanda's justice ministry and prosecutor general).
Amnesty International reported that M23 fighters beat a man, later held at the ANR office in Bukavu for three weeks, giving him 100 blows with wooden sticks.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that five civilians were shot dead between 11 and 12 July at Karambi (Kabare territory) by armed men identified as M23-AFC-RDF rebels, in reprisal for the alleged killing of one of their members by the population; it named the victims, and said two of them were teachers returning from an exam centre at EP Chanya.

Radio Okapi reported, in an article on a night of terror at Bukavu and Nyantende, that at around 19 heures armed men burst into the local hospital at Nyantende, first neutralising the security guards and then turning on patients; according to local sources the assailants looted goods, extorted phones from patients and violently assaulted an on-duty doctor, then withdrew unhindered to an area reputed to be under rebel control.

Radio Okapi reported, in an article on a night of insecurity in Bukavu and Nyantende, that those events came only a few days after a cordon operation carried out by the M23 rebels in the Nyamugo neighbourhood of Kadutu commune, which it said led to the seizure of four AK-47 weapons and the arrest of about thirty young people suspected of criminal activity.

place: Kamakombe and Mbayo, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting broke out on Wednesday 30 July in Kamakombe village (Kabare territory) between M23-AFC rebels, described as allied to the RDF, and a Wazalendo group; it said the clashes had begun on the Tuesday in Mbayo village (Bugorhe groupement) following a reinforcement of M23 troops coming from Kavumu airport, and, according to several local sources, these troops launched an offensive against the Mouvement décisif de la libération du Congo (MDLC/RRADRDC), a Wazalendo branch present in the area.

place: Kamakombe, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, under a headline on fighting between M23 and Wazalendo resuming despite the accord, that at dawn M23-AFC-RDF insurgents launched an offensive in Bugorhe groupement against positions of the Wazalendo of the Mouvement décisif de la Libération du Congo (MDLC) at Kamakombe village (Kabare territory); after a brief M23 occupation of half the village, the Wazalendo pushed the attackers back towards the heights of Kavumu; the same day another attack attributed to the M23 targeted the Muzinzi subgroupement in neighbouring Walungu territory.

place: Kasheke (and Kamakombe), border of Kabare and Kalehe territories, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that four civilians were killed on Thursday 7 August in fighting between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo of the MDLC group at Kasheke village, on the border of Kabare and Kalehe territories; according to local sources, the M23 attacked MDLC positions at Kamakombe and opened a second front against the MDLC headquarters at Kasheke, headed by the self-proclaimed general Imani Shabani, and the toll was described as provisional.

place: Kasheke, Buzunga, Lemera (Mbinga Sud groupement), Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that violent clashes between Wazalendo and M23 since the afternoon of jeudi 10 juillet in the villages of Kasheke and Buzunga (Kalehe territory) caused a mass displacement of civilians; Radio Maendeleo likewise reported that fighting on 10 July caused a mass displacement of the population in the villages of Kasheke, Buzunga and Lemera in Mbinga Sud groupement, Kalehe territory.
Radio Okapi reported, in an article on fighting at Kasheke and Buzunga, that witnesses spoke of generalised panic, looted goods, houses visited and even cases of abduction, notably at Buhama.

Kivu Morning Post reported that a communiqué of the FARDC Third Defence Zone, signed by Major Nestor Mavudisa Kamba Mayoyo, spokesperson of 'cette zone militaire', said that 'ces ennemis de la paix' attacked FARDC positions at Kamatembe and Kalao (Mubuku groupement, Kalehe territory) on the morning of 12 July 2025, and that, according to the FARDC, another position was attacked at Batanga, Irambi Katana groupement, Kabare territory.

place: Kabulungu, Bughore, Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: 7sur7.cd reported that fighting between Wazalendo and AFC/M23 broke out again on Wednesday 16 July 2025 on the hills above Kabulungu village (Bughore, Kabare territory), according to local civil society, and quoted a resident saying 'Des civils ont même été tués'; socio-economic activity had been paralysed there since the previous Monday.

place: Katana (Kabare territory) and Kalehe health zones, South Kivu
statement: MSF said that an assessment it carried out in March, following violent clashes in the area in early 2025, found that of 24 health facilities evaluated in the Katana and Kalehe health zones, 15 had had to close, 10 had been damaged and 16 had been looted; Radio Okapi, reporting the same assessment, gave about 15 closed, 10 damaged and 'une quinzaine' looted.

place: Katana and Kalehe health zones, and Bukavu airport, South Kivu
statement: MSF said that, besides the damage to health facilities, patients faced barriers to care such as economic difficulties and insecurity, and that insecurity and the closure of the Bukavu and Goma airports continued to limit humanitarian access.

Radio Okapi reported that pastor Kelly Bahati Kazibaziba was shot dead on Monday 11 August by armed men on Michombero avenue in Kadutu commune (Bukavu); according to several local sources it was a premeditated murder, with suspicion of a link to the stance of his brother Joseph Kazibaziba, a businessman and president of the South Kivu Chamber of Mines, known for denouncing abuses attributed to the M23 rebellion.

Radio Okapi reported that gunfire spread panic in the Panzi neighbourhood (Ibanda commune, Bukavu); according to the neighbourhood chief, armed individuals appear at nightfall and fire in the air, and on jeudi at around 19 h a fruit seller was fatally hit by a stray bullet as she was walking home; the outlet said rumours placed members of the Wazalendo group in the area but that no proof had been provided.

CongoRassure, in an article summarising OCHA-RDC's latest report, reported that OCHA-RDC said a relative calm was observed across Bukavu during August, but that local sources reported several cases of burglaries, killings and arbitrary arrests attributed to armed men.

CongoRassure, in an article on OCHA-RDC's latest report, reported that persistent clashes that broke out on 17 July in Kabare territory continued throughout August, and that on 13 August at least four civilians were killed by armed men at M'bayo, a locality where about 43 000 people were displaced following armed violence between 17 and 26 July.

place: Schools in Kabare territory (and Kamisimbi, Walungu), South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that school activities had been paralysed since Tuesday 9 September in several schools of Kabare territory and at Kamisimbi (Walungu); according to local sources, armed men presenting themselves as Wazalendo burst into schools to send pupils home, arrested teachers and forced them to join the armed struggle against the M23 rebels, which the Nouvelle Dynamique de la société civile condemned.

place: Lomera mining site, Luhihi, Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that M23 officials suspended all mining activities at the Lomera site in Luhihi (Kabare territory) from 'lundi 9 septembre' (as printed), for security reasons according to them, and demanded prior identification of all operators; it said thousands of people were affected by the measure of the M23, which it said occupies the region, and that the reopening date was unknown.

place: Highlands (hauts plateaux) of Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that continuing clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters in the highlands of Kalehe territory were preventing parents from preparing their children's 2025-2026 school year and, according to several local sources, were causing massive displacement of the population.

place: Chulwe and Cishadu, Luhago grouping, Kabare territory
statement: OCHA reported that on 4 October violent fighting in the localities of Chulwe and Cishadu, Luhago grouping (Kabare territory), caused the mass displacement of families to safer areas, that figures for the recently displaced were being verified, and that several victims, including dead and wounded among civilians, were reported.

place: Civanga and Kasirusiru, Kabare territory; refuge at Miti and Murhesa
statement: OCHA DRC reported that on 12 October 2025 about 450 households, close to 2,700 people, fled new fighting between armed groups in the localities of Civanga and Kasirusiru (Kabare territory) and took refuge at Miti and Murhesa, and that humanitarian access remained strongly limited by persistent insecurity.

place: Mountains above Katasomwa, Mbesho, Kashihe, Katoki, Mweya, Bwangala, Kilijiwe, Kasasa, Kaitoleya, Bushushu 1 and 2, Kalehe territory; refuge in Kalehe centre, Kasheke, Tchoki, Luzira and others
statement: OCHA reported that between 12 and 15 October about 27,700 people fled fighting between armed groups in the mountains overlooking Katasomwa, Mbesho, Kashihe, Katoki, Mweya and other localities of Kalehe territory, and that the living conditions of the displaced and of host communities were critical, including a rupture of medical inputs and an increased risk of sexual violence.

place: Kasheke and Luzira health areas, Kalehe health zone
statement: Caritasdev.cd, summarising a Caritas Bukavu report on the humanitarian crisis in Kalehe, reported that the fighting of 12 October displaced more than 7,700 people to the areas of Kasheke, Luzira, Bushaku and Kabamba.

place: Luzira and Kasheke health areas, Kalehe health zone
statement: Caritasdev.cd, summarising a Caritas Bukavu assessment report on Kalehe, listed under protection and abuse 7 cases of sexual violence documented in October, and reported child enlistment, extortion and cruel treatment.

place: Minova health zone and Chabombo health area, Kalehe territory
statement: Actualite.cd, quoting an OCHA DRC report, reported that between 6 and 12 November two international organisations had to temporarily suspend their movements for monitoring nutrition and health activities in the Chabombo health area because of intensified fighting in Katasomwa, Lumbishi and Chambombo, and that, in addition, four humanitarian workers were arrested by armed actors in the Minova health zone.

Actualite.cd reported that MSF has supported, since September, the Bunyakiri general referral hospital, the Bitale hospital centre and several surrounding health centres, and that in eleven weeks of intervention MSF teams recorded 13,300 medical consultations and cared for 98 cases of sexual violence.

place: Tushunguti centre, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the situation remained confused on Tuesday in Tushunguti centre village, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, and that, according to local sources, the tension followed the killing of a resident by an armed element assimilated to the Wazalendo Kirikicho fighters; a civil-society actor said the victim, killed on Monday evening, was an agent guarding a CICR depot in the area, and that the population then pursued the alleged perpetrator, who was also killed.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that Honneur David Safari, editor-in-chief and founder of the outlet La Prunelle RDC, had been missing since the evening of 'samedi' (Saturday) 28 December 2025 in Bukavu; that a source close to him said he had confided that people were behind him and had noticed he was being followed; and that representatives of South Kivu journalists went on Monday to the AFC/M23 intelligence office to ask for its involvement in the search.

Top Africa News reported that AFC/M23 denied losing control of Kavumu airport: reliable sources who spoke to UMUSEKE maintained that the airport remained firmly under the control of AFC/M23 fighters, and in a statement the alliance dismissed the claims as deliberate misinformation, its spokesperson saying 'Wazalendo and FARDC have no such capability'.

place: South Kivu (Kabare, Uvira, Kalehe, Idjwi, Walungu named)
statement: The outlet reported that in territories such as Kabare, Uvira, Kalehe, Idjwi and Walungu agricultural and school activities were regularly disrupted by clashes, that the war had pushed some health structures to close while others had lost staff, and that those still operating faced medicine stock-outs; it said, citing an ICRC study, that these factors were contributing to many civilian deaths.

place: South Kivu: Uvira, Walungu, Mwenga, Shabunda, Kabare, Fizi, Kalehe territories
statement: OCHA reported in a flash update that since 2 December 2025 the security situation in South Kivu had deteriorated following an escalation of armed clashes in the territories of Uvira, Walungu, Mwenga, Shabunda, Kabare, Fizi and Kalehe, and that, according to estimates from local authorities, civil society and partners on the ground, more than 500,000 people were on the move across the province.

La Croix reported that nine months after M23 took Bukavu in February 2025 a relative calm reigned in the city, but that behind this facade lay a climate of fear fed by executions, sexual violence and the persistent presence of armed groups.

place: Kalehe highlands (Lumbishi, Chambombo, Katasomwa, Kitendebwa, Zilaro), Kalehe, South Kivu
statement: Soleil du Graben reported that the humanitarian situation of more than 10.000 people who had fled fighting since 05 February 2026 in Lumbishi, Chambombo, Katasomwa, Kitendebwa, Zilaro and other places in the Kalehe highlands was very worrying; citing concordant sources, it said displaced families were sheltering with host families or sleeping in the open at Numbi, Nyabibwe and Kalungu, and that a local notable appealed for humanitarian aid. The outlet attributed the displacement to clashes between armed groups without naming them.

place: Katasomwa, Kitendebwa, Kashihe, Mweya, Kiduveri, Kalehe, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that fighting between the Congolese army, backed by Wazalendo, and AFC-M23 fighters was reported on Tuesday 24 February 2026 in several villages of Kalehe territory, causing mass displacement; an anonymous resident named Katasomwa, Kitendebwa, Kashihe, Mweya and Kiduveri.

place: Kitendebwa, Kashihe, Kiduveri, Kalehe, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the Kinshasa regime had once again trampled the ceasefire and that on Tuesday 24 February 2026 at 07h00 its 'forces coalisées' (coalition forces) launched deliberate attacks on densely populated areas of Kitendebwa, Kashihe and Kiduveri in Kalehe territory. The outlet, in its own narration, refers to the ceasefire signed in Doha.

place: Kavumu and Katana-Kavumu axis, Kabare, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that on 21 February 2026 AFC/M23 and Wazalendo clashed at Kavumu and along the Katana-Kavumu stretch in Kabare territory, with fighting resuming in the evening around 18h30, disrupting the Bukavu-Kavumu road and confining residents; one local source quoted said the clashes began after a Wazalendo element was evacuated from a health structure. The article does not name the structure, who evacuated him or why, and describes no attack on health care.

Actualite.cd reported that traffic had timidly resumed on the Kalonge-Bunyakiri axis in Kalehe territory after three months of interruption, which it attributed to persistent clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo militiamen; a civil society actor at Kalonge said motorbikes and buses were already travelling and that the situation had been catastrophic at Kalonge and Bunyakiri.

Mediacongo reported that daily life in Bunyakiri, Kalehe territory, remained profoundly disrupted by the prolonged blockage of Route nationale 3 (RN3), which it attributed to AFC-M23/Wazalendo clashes lasting more than three months; the president of a local civil society group said the movement of goods was almost nil for lack of authorisation from the AFC-M23 authorities.

Actualite.cd reported, relaying the MSF annual report on its 2025 activities, that the MSF emergency team helped populations displaced at Katana, Kalehe and Bunyakiri by clashes between the Congolese army, its Wazalendo allies and the armed group AFC/M23; MSF said its medical teams supported health facilities whose activities had been disrupted by the conflict and, in hospitals and health centres, cared for survivors of sexual violence among other services.

place: Mugeri, Mwanda, Irhambi-Katana, Kabare, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that an incident occurred around 12h, at midday, in a part of the province under AFC-M23 control, at Mugeri sub-village (Mwanda village, Irhambi-Katana groupement, Kabare territory): armed men entered the home of a man known as Huit MUCIGA and shot him and his wife at the same time. The article's body says a child beside them died on the spot and that the man, taken to Mugeri health centre and then to FOMULAC Katana hospital, died later the same day, while the woman remained in very critical condition; its lead gives a toll of one dead and two wounded, inconsistent with the body. The headline attributes the incursion to Wazalendo; the body does not name the attackers. Sources close to the family said the man had reportedly been accused of collaborating with AFC-M23.

Kivu Morning Post reported that at least seven civilians were killed and fifteen wounded during an incursion by Wazalendo, militiamen allied to the Congolese army, at Shanje, Kalehe territory, on the night of Sunday to Monday 30 March 2026; citing local sources and an anonymous resident, it said the militiamen fired on civilians in the market around 18h30 and looted the population's property.

Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that on 29 March 2026 at 18h30 'la coalition de Kinshasa' infiltrated the densely populated centre of Shanje, Kalehe territory, where it 'executed 7 innocent civilians', whom he named; the outlet reported that he also said more than twenty people were wounded, and he alleged that the Kinshasa regime continues to ally itself with FDLR elements and deploy them on various fronts.

The outlet reported that at least 9 people were killed and 20 wounded in the night of Sunday to Monday 30 March 2026 at Shanje village, Kalehe territory, during an incursion of armed men; it cited a local church official, speaking anonymously on Radio Maendeleo, who said the bandits arrived and fired, and said wounded were taken to a medical facility and that the real identity of the armed men was not yet known.

BETO reported that AFC fighters left the localities of Pitakongo and Bunyatenge on Saturday 28 March 2026, after having already withdrawn on Thursday and Friday from at least twelve localities of Lubero territory and from the strategic town of Minova; it said the disengagement did not seem to result from a military rout but rather from a planned manoeuvre, citing information relayed by other media and local sources that the move would fit within the ongoing peace processes, and it reported that the rebel mayor of a city under AFC administration described the moves as tactical repositionings.

Actualite.cd reported that Espoir Mbata, director of the community radio Top Buzi FM, was arrested on Sunday 29 March at Minova, Kalehe territory; according to local sources and colleagues at the station he was reportedly detained by AFC/M23 elements, and a journalist close to the radio, speaking anonymously, said the arrest was reportedly linked to an on-air comment by Espoir Mbata about a possible withdrawal of AFC/M23 elements from Minova. The outlet said some journalists had left Minova that morning fearing arrest.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that around 16:00 on Monday 6 April 2026 several places in the Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory (Kaziba, Katale, Kafufula, Katanga, Mpanama, Braza, Bushege and Lulamba) had already passed under AFC/M23 control after fighting with wazalendo.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that on 6 April 2026 in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe) the AFC/M23 fought wazalendo from several local armed groups, including the COPACO led by Kirikicho Mirimba Mwanamayi, the MCDPIN of Grevisse Nsimparingira and the group of Haguma Kanyengwenye.

Actualite.cd reported that the town of Tushunguti, chef-lieu of Ziralo groupement in Kalehe territory, fell under AFC/M23 control on Tuesday 7 April 2026 after fighting with wazalendo, according to its sources; it said no official toll had been communicated.

Actualite.cd reported that Tushunguti (Kalehe) was again under FARDC control, supported by wazalendo fighters, after a brief AFC/M23 occupation that began on 7 April 2026; it said the counter-offensive was launched from the Biriko and Busurungi axes in Walikale.

Actualite.cd reported, citing several of its sources, that Tushunguti again passed under AFC/M23 control on Sunday 3 May 2026 after two days of fighting against wazalendo, who withdrew towards Biriko in Walikale.

Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that on 12 April 2026 AFC/M23 elements carried out a cordon-and-search operation in Minova under a curfew, and that several men aged 18 to 40 were arrested and held for several hours at the 'Mille arbres' stadium.

Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said nearly 48 000 displaced people were in an alarming humanitarian situation after fleeing fighting between AFC/M23 and wazalendo in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe), and that all schools in the groupement remained closed.

place: Bunje and Nyalugusha villages, Ziralo, Kalehe territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that several houses were burned along the Bunje-Katale axis, notably in the villages of Bunje and Nyalugusha, during fighting between the belligerents; it did not say who burned them or on which day.

Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to local civil society, more than 38 500 people fled their villages following fighting in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe), most of them towards Lulambo and Biriko in Walikale territory.

place: Chambombo, Nyalugusha village, Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that Kalehe civil society said SEBUTAGWIRA HARERIMANA JACQUES, director of the EP Chambombo, was shot dead during fighting between Wazalendo and AFC-M23 at Chambombo on Wednesday 29 April 2026.

place: Mbayo village, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that five people were shot dead and one seriously wounded in a shooting attributed to presumed AFC/M23 rebels on Thursday 21 May 2026 at Mbayo village, Kabare territory; according to a civil society official of Bugorhe groupement, the assailants gathered their victims and executed them one by one.

Actualite.cd reported that on 9 June 2026 school and commercial activities were disrupted in Mbayo and Kamakombe villages (Kabare) by fighting between AFC/M23 elements and wazalendo militiamen from morning until late evening; it said this followed fighting a week earlier at Kafurumaye, near Kahuzi-Biega National Park.

place: Businde, Bugorhe groupement, near Kavumu airport, Kabare territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that an explosive device killed one child and seriously wounded three others on Tuesday 28 April 2026 near Kavumu airport (Kabare); the victims, all minors, were scavenging scrap metal when they found an abandoned crate of explosives, and the three wounded were transferred to the Bukavu general referral hospital.

The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) reported that on 5 April 2026 at Cirunga, Kabare territory, eight men and two women were arrested by AFC/M23 elements for demonstrating spontaneously after learning they were to be removed from posts in that village.

Soleil du Graben reported that an AFC/M23 delegation led by the vice-governor in charge of political, administrative and judicial matters, Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge Doux, relaunched customary administration of the Ntambuka chiefdom on Idjwi island and installed a seven-member peace committee, in the presence of Idjwi territory administrator Pascal Ntambuka.

DW reported on 22 May 2026 that the first positive Ebola case in South Kivu was recorded in the Miti-Murhesa health zone, Kabare territory, in the area held by the AFC-M23; it said the alert was confirmed by the AFC-M23 governor Patrick Busu Bwa Ngwi and by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka.

Radio Okapi reported that, according to the South Kivu provincial health division chief Dr Aimé Alengo, the focus of the Ebola outbreak in South Kivu was in the Miti-Murhesa health zone of Kabare; Radio Okapi said the zone lies in a region affected by insecurity linked to armed groups, notably the AFC/M23 rebellion, which further complicates the response, and that Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba announced diplomatic initiatives aimed at guaranteeing secure humanitarian and health access to areas under armed-group control.

Kivu Morning Post reported that on Tuesday 26 May 2026 North Kivu health authorities, at a briefing in Goma, announced that Bukavu city had three new positive Ebola cases, according to Dr Biya Kizinkinko, health division head and member of the AFC-M23 Ebola response task team.

place: Chambombo, Lumbishi, Kaziba de Rumbishi, Kwisimbi, Gafufura, Kazinga (Kalehe), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that heavy-artillery fighting resumed early on Tuesday 11 August 2026 in several localities of Kalehe territory, South Kivu, between AFC/M23 rebels and the FARDC, supported in some sectors by Wazalendo; first shots were heard around 5 a.m. in Chambombo, Lumbishi, Kaziba de Rumbishi, Kwisimbi, Gafufura and Kazinga.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its own sources, that the bombardments in Kalehe territory on 11 August 2026 caused deaths and injuries among civilians and that several houses and other property were reportedly damaged; it added that the intensity of the fighting forced several families to leave their homes for safer areas.

Enquete.cd reported, citing several local sources contacted on the ground, that after several hours of fighting on 11 August the Wazalendo retook control of the localities of Chambombo and Kazinga from AFC-M23-RDF elements in Kalehe territory; it said that according to local civil society Lumbishi was reportedly shared between the two sides, each occupying some positions.

Enquete.cd reported, citing medical sources, that several AFC-M23-RDF fighters wounded in the Kalehe fighting were reportedly admitted to the hospital of Numbi, among them a Rwandan officer presented as a colonel who was reportedly gravely wounded; the outlet said this information could not be independently verified.

place: Lumbishi, Chambombo (Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe), South Kivu
statement: La Presse Africaine reported that during fighting between the FARDC (supported by Wazalendo) and AFC/M23 from 11 to 14 August 2026 in Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe, the spokesperson of the 34th military region, Major Dieudonné Kaseraka, reported five civilians killed and four FARDC soldiers wounded at Chambombo and Lumbishi, while local sources put the toll higher, at least six civilians killed, among them a woman and her two children.

place: Hauts Plateaux of Kalehe, South Kivu
statement: La Presse Africaine reported that local civil society said population movements towards Walikale were noted, that cattle pillage and losses of property were reported, and that several health structures remained difficult to operate, following the 11-14 August 2026 fighting in Kalehe's Buhavu chiefdom.

place: Lumbishi (Kalehe), South Kivu; Kasake (Masisi), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that a relative calm was observed on Monday 13 July in Kasake (Masisi, North Kivu) and Lumbishi (Kalehe, South Kivu) after three days of fighting between Wazalendo and AFC-M23 rebels, and that according to several local sources both localities were reportedly now under Wazalendo control.

place: Shangi, Katahandwa, Shoa (near Lumbishi), Kalehe/Masisi border
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local sources, Wazalendo fighters led by Noah Maachano, of the Maï-Maï Lamuka group, had reportedly also deployed in several neighbouring villages, notably Shangi, Katahandwa and Shoa.

place: Lumbishi centre, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe, South Kivu
statement: La Prunelle RDC reported that at least five people were killed and several wounded on Friday 7 August 2026 in the explosion of an explosive device in the centre of Lumbishi (Ziralo grouping, Kalehe highlands), and that the wounded were evacuated to the Numbi hospital centre.

place: Bunje, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe, South Kivu
statement: La Prunelle RDC reported that in a communication published on Friday 7 August the FARDC operational sector Sukola 2 Nord–Sud-Kivu said RDF-AFC-M23 coalition fighters had tried an incursion into Bunje (Ziralo grouping) before firing several 82 mm mortar rounds towards inhabited areas, which according to the army killed three people, including a woman and her two children, and seriously wounded several; the sector's spokesperson, Second Lieutenant Meya Gbé Jérémie, said the coalition had fired 'à l’aveuglette' into densely populated areas.

La Prunelle RDC reported that Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson of the armed movement, in a communication on X accused the coalition forces of the Kinshasa government of having bombed the Lumbishi market, the movement first reporting five civilians dead and several wounded and then, in an update, 9 dead.

Actualite.cd reported that the South Kivu provincial government, which depends on the central government in Kinshasa, denounced the pressure and predation to which it said the population of Bukavu is subjected under the administration of AFC/M23, citing levies including so-called sanitation taxes and taxes on commercial activity and, according to several testimonies, acts of intimidation, violence and flogging.

Actualite.cd reported that the DRC higher-education ministry (ESURSI), headed by Marie-Thérèse Sombo, issued a ministerial order, announced on Tuesday 25 August 2026, suspending academic activities for academic year 2026-2027 at several institutions in Goma and Bukavu, including the Université Officielle de Bukavu, ISC-Bukavu, ISTM-Bukavu, ISP-Bukavu, ISDR-Bukavu and ISAM-Bukavu.

RFI (carried by Yahoo Actualités) reported that, alongside Kinshasa's suspension of academic activities, a separate decision suspended the salaries of 48 agents accused of having joined AFC/M23, pledged allegiance to it or accepted positions under its authority, and that in response AFC/M23 deputy coordinator Bertrand Bisimwa announced a substitute mechanism; RFI added that UN experts' December 2025 report had said AFC/M23 ordered universities to cut their links with the Congolese higher-education ministry.

La Presse Africaine reported, citing local sources, that clashes involving M23 fighters had reportedly caused population displacement in several areas of Kalehe, Masisi and Walikale; Olivier Kaskoti, a Tembo notable and honorary president of Buuma bwe Batembo (Beni section), said localities in Ziralo grouping and parts of Ufamandu grouping (Masisi) and Walowa-Lwanda (Walikale) faced a deteriorating security situation for several days, and alleged that M23 used drones and artillery fire, allegations the outlet said could not be independently verified.
La Presse Africaine reported that an appeal on the Ziralo situation demanded the release of 'le patriote' Kirikocho Mirimba Mwana Mayi, who the appeal said had been in detention for several weeks.

place: Nkola village, Rubenga chiefdom, Idjwi, South Kivu
statement: La Presse Africaine reported that the body of a woman bearing traces of violence and of bladed weapons was found in Nkola village, Rubenga chiefdom, Idjwi, on a Sunday in early August 2026 (the article gives two different dates for that Sunday); a source on the spot said she was reportedly killed during the night by unidentified individuals who used knives and machetes, her body found with a serious neck wound, and village chief Doris Habiragi confirmed the information and said investigations were under way.

Mediacongo reported that the ultimatum set by the United States for Rwanda to withdraw its troops from eastern DRC expired on Wednesday 15 July 2026, and that, according to security and local sources, the rebel movement, after consolidating its positions in the Hauts Plateaux and other strategic areas, would now be seeking to extend its influence towards Baraka, an important town in Fizi territory.

place: Kafufula, Katale, Katoke, Chambombo, Bishaka (Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom), Kalehe territory
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that after intense fighting since 3h on Monday 5 October 2026, Wazalendo fighters were said to have retaken control of Kafufula, Katale, Katoke, Bikari/Kuma Dépôts, Chambombo and Bishaka in the Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory, from AFC-M23 troops.
Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local leaders, that at about 11h on Monday a presence of Wazalendo fighters was reported in the town of Lumbishi, about 8 km from Numbi, Kalehe territory.

Radio Maendeleo reported, citing an occasional correspondent, that in the morning of Monday 05 October an unusual presence of fighters claiming to be Wazalendo was seen on the hills of Mabingu village, Irhambi-Katana grouping, Kabare territory, and that several school heads sent pupils home fearing clashes.

place: Kavumu primary school near Numbi, Kalehe territory
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that at the Kavumu primary school, about 4 km from Numbi, parents rushed to collect their children because of the deteriorating security situation and the approach of the battlefield.

Enquete.cd reported, according to local sources, that the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo fighters, had retaken control of the centre of Numbi, Kalehe territory, and that clashes had reportedly preceded the retaking.

Radio Maendeleo reported on 20 October that after the Wazalendo offensive that led to their entry into Shanje, Lumbishi and Numbi between 5 and 6 October, a counter-offensive had allowed troops of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) to retake control of them.

place: Shanje area (Kirwa, Bunyata, Igali axis) and Bogamanda-Nyamutwe, Kalehe territory
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported a still-provisional toll of at least 8 dead, including civilians, and several wounded in new clashes that had pitted AFC-M23 troops against Wazalendo fighters for nearly three days in several villages around Shanje, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe highlands; the same article quoted a source in a medical structure receiving some cases as reporting several wounded civilians in addition to about ten deaths near Shanje and in the Bogamanda-Nyamutwe area.

Radio Maendeleo reported, citing witnesses, that returnees found homes destroyed or burned, goods looted and fields devastated in Kalehe highlands, and that at Shanje almost all shops were burned in the night of 6 to 7 October. Actualite.cd reported separately that a large fire broke out around 4 a.m. on Wednesday 7 October in Shanje, affecting homes and the local market.

place: Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa and Lumbishi health areas, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing a local civil-society source, that in the health areas of Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa and Lumbishi (Kalehe highlands) health facilities had difficulty caring for the sick because they too had been looted, and schools struggled to resume.

place: Bunyakiri health zone (Tushunguti, Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa health centres), Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory
statement: Kivutimes (project Habari za Mahali) reported on 21 October that MSF Spain gave PEP kits for survivors of sexual violence to four health structures (Tushunguti, Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa) in the Bunyakiri health zone, Ziralo grouping, and that, according to Katabana Monde, head nurse at Matutira, the structures record cases of sexual violence among their populations, notably in the context of displacement caused by the fighting; providers had had difficulty obtaining PEP kits in time.

Actualite.cd reported that journalist Laurent Vainqueur Muliro of community radio Walikale Amka (RTCWA) was shot dead on the evening of Wednesday 21 October in an ambush attributed to presumed Wazalendo militiamen near Bitale, Kalehe territory; the page says two other people were also killed and two seriously wounded, with the travellers' property looted.

place: Kabulungu and Mulangala, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that the local youth council of the villages of Kabulungu and Mulangala, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory, denounced insecurity attributed to unidentified armed persons: intimidation of farmers, theft of livestock and extortion of money, and 'inhuman treatment' of people who resist.

place: Kabulungu and Mulangala, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that the same Kabulungu and Mulangala (Kabare territory) youth council also reported cases of arrests followed by detention in unknown places, the victims reportedly being released only after payment of a sum of money.

Radio Maendeleo reported on 3 October that, according to civil society, more than 1,900 households from Kalehe highlands (mainly Ziralo and Numbi groupings) and Ufamandu grouping in Masisi had taken refuge in the Buzi grouping of Minova, having fled fighting between the AFC/M23 and the government coalition over the previous two weeks.

Actualite.cd reported that thousands of families who fled clashes between the FRN and the FARDC supported by Wazalendo in the Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, were living in difficult conditions at Nyabibwe, lacking food, shelter and basic necessities, mostly women and children.

place: Hombo Sud, Kalehe territory (and Lukaraba, Walikale, North Kivu)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Hombo civil society, after an assessment mission of 25 to 27 September 2026, said the local hospital centre at Hombo Sud (Kalehe territory) was receiving a large number of displaced people needing care, as well as people wounded by violence, with limited capacity.

place: Ruzizi 1er border post, Bukavu; Grande Barrière, Goma
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the South Kivu provincial government (Kinshasa-appointed), in a communiqué of Monday 5 October signed by its spokesperson Didier Kabi, expressed concern at the extension of the closing hours of two border posts controlled by the AFC/M23, Ruzizi 1er in Bukavu and Grande Barrière in Goma, saying it could facilitate the entry of new populations and their settlement in AFC/M23-controlled zones.

Kivu Morning Post reported that FRN vice-president Bertrand Bisimwa, in a speech at Bukavu on Thursday, defended continued teaching in FRN-held zones despite measures by the Congolese government, and that the FRN promised to support teachers whose pay had been suspended by Kinshasa.

place: Kongo Central (statement); applies to Goma and Bukavu institutions
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Higher Education minister Marie-Thérèse Sombo, launching the 2026-2027 academic year in Kongo Central on Monday 26 October 2026, said the provisional suspension of academic activities at Goma and Bukavu institutions aims to protect students and staff, preserve the legality of university governance and prevent irregular academic acts from compromising the value of diplomas.

Kivu Morning Post reported, citing a video from the South Kivu governor's communication unit, that FRN vice-presidents Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo and Bertrand Bisimwa met FRN cadres from across South Kivu in Bukavu on Thursday 22 October 2026 to discuss the movement's political vision and organisation.

place: Minembwe (Fizi) and Mikenge, Itombwe sector (Mwenga), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Twirwaneho said Minembwe and surroundings were 'liberated', that a regional source confirmed to it that all of Minembwe was controlled by Twirwaneho, and that, according to several sources, Mikenge in the Itombwe sector (Mwenga territory), 28 km from Minembwe, had also come under Twirwaneho control after fighting with the Congolese armed forces on Tuesday.

place: Luvungi and Sange (Ruzizi plain), Uvira territory
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that after being sighted at Kamanyola and then Luvungi, M23 rebels were now visible at Sange in Uvira territory, South Kivu, and that residents confirmed their presence although the rebels had not yet made a public statement.

Kivu Morning Post quoted Paul Byamungu, a member of Uvira civil society, as saying that after the meeting at Kamanyola, M23 was now with them, that they had communicated nothing, and that there had been no public meeting so far.

URN (via The Observer, Uganda) reported that M23 president Bertrand Bisimwa released a statement on Monday accusing FARDC soldiers and their allies of deploying Sukhoi fighter jets and attack drones to bomb several villages in Minembwe, and that, according to Bisimwa, the strikes were aimed at areas populated by Banyamulenge civilians, as well as Minembwe airfield.

URN (via The Observer, Uganda) reported that, on Tuesday night, South Kivu vice-governor Jean Jacques Elakano announced that the operation by the army and coalition forces had destroyed all aircraft transporting M23 rebels from Bukavu city, resulting in the deaths of over 10 fighters.

The New Times (Kigali), a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that, according to AFC/M23's Bertrand Bisimwa on X, no Munyamulenge could travel to Baraka, Fizi, Uvira or Mwenga, that the Minembwe airstrip was the only means of evacuation for the sick and of delivery of medicine and essential supplies, and that it had been damaged by a government plane.

OCHA reported in its South Kivu situation report that at least 127 women and minor girls were victims of rape in Uvira city during the forced confinement caused by the violent clashes of 15 to 22 February 2025, of whom 54 (43 percent) received medical care within 72 hours.
OCHA reported that many sexual-violence cases in Uvira city went without medical care because of a shortage of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) kits in several health structures.

place: Sange (Ruzizi health zone) and Uvira health zones
statement: OCHA reported that a cholera epidemic was affecting the Uvira and Ruzizi health zones, that 242 cases and ten deaths had been recorded in the two zones as of 10 March 2025, and that the Ruzizi cholera treatment centre, located in Sange, faced a stock-out of medical supplies while case numbers kept rising.

place: Uvira Hauts Plateaux: Kahololo, Kageregere, Kitembe, Bijombo, Mugete, Mitamba, Magunda, Muranvya
statement: OCHA reported that between 1 and 14 March 2025 clashes between the FARDC and the M23 continued in the Uvira Hauts Plateaux, affecting the localities of Kahololo, Kageregere, Kitembe, Bijombo, Mugete, Mitamba, Magunda and Muranvya.

OCHA reported that humanitarian actors estimated more than 554 000 people were affected by the crisis in Uvira city, including 270 000 internally displaced people, of whom more than 126 000 fled to the Ruzizi plain in February 2025.

Kivutimes reported that Twirwaneho and Wazalendo (led, it said, by Ebuela Seba alias Mtetezi) fought at Mikenge, Itombwe sector, from the morning of Monday 3 March 2025; according to local sources Wazalendo dislodged Twirwaneho, which had held the centre for more than two weeks, and Twirwaneho fighters fled toward Kalingi; around 18 heures men of Sematama counter-attacked with heavy weapons and reoccupied Mikenge.

place: Mikenge IDP camp, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory
statement: Kivutimes reported that after occupying Mikenge the Wazalendo set fire at midday to the camp of internally displaced people that housed mostly members of the Banyamulenge community, and that no source had confirmed a precise human toll although there were victims on both sides.

place: Mikenge IDP camp, Itombwe, Mwenga territory
statement: Kivutimes reported that the NGO New Hope Réconciliation Centre called on humanitarian organisations to help victims of the attacks that targeted the Mikenge displaced camp, which the article described as a devastating attack carried out by Mai Mai armed groups called Wazalendo, and that the camp, which housed about 310 households mainly of Banyamulenge families, was reduced to a heap of ashes.

place: Hauts Plateaux de Minembwe to Fizi centre, Fizi territory
statement: Radio Okapi reported that fighting between the armed groups Red Tabara and Wazalendo was reported on Thursday 20 March in Fizi territory, South Kivu, that people of the Minembwe Hauts Plateaux were fleeing toward Fizi centre, and that the territory administrator confirmed this, appealed to the belligerents to end hostilities and invited humanitarian organisations to assist thousands of displaced people.

place: Minembwe Hauts Plateaux: Mukoko toward Kakenge; earlier Gahwera and Kivumu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that fighting resumed in the Minembwe Hauts Plateaux between the FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters and the coalition of the armed groups Twirwaneho and Gumino, and, according to the Fizi territory administrator, that the FARDC supported by Wazalendo militiamen launched an assault on the coalition's positions.

place: Kamanyola, Walungu territory (Ruzizi plain border with Rwanda and Burundi)
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing several concordant sources, that the rural town of Kamanyola, in Walungu territory, had been under occupation by the M23 and their Rwandan allies since Tuesday 18 February, late in the evening.

Agence France-Presse reported that military and official sources said Burundian troops were being discreetly withdrawn despite official denials; a senior officer told AFP 'Nous avions érigé une ligne de défense à Kamanyola' to try to stop the advance of the M23 and Rwandan soldiers but had to make a tactical retreat under enemy attack on Tuesday, adding that part of 'our troops' deployed in eastern DRC were returning home on foot, which a senior Burundian official confirmed to AFP.

MediaCongo, relaying nouveaumedia.cd / MCP, reported that, after the capture of Kamanyola, the M23 and allies of the Rwandan army were said to have taken the villages of Luvungi and Sange, a few kilometres from Uvira, causing panic in Uvira where shops closed and some people crossed the border into Burundi, and that clashes between uncontrolled elements of the army and Wazalendo were said to have killed civilians.

place: Mukoko toward Kakenge, Minembwe Hauts Plateaux, Fizi/Mwenga
statement: Radio Okapi reported that honorary senator Moïse Nyarugabo, in a tweet on Friday 21 March, said that since 6h that morning the FARDC and Wazalendo, coming from Fizi via Mukela and Mulima, had resumed their attack at Mukoko toward Kakenge, and that the inhabitants of the Fizi and Mwenga Hauts Plateaux, especially Minembwe, were again waking up under bombs.

place: Rugezi, Basimukuma Sud, Mutambala sector, Fizi
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that intense fighting had been reported since the morning of Friday 9 May 2025 in Fizi territory, between AFC-M23 rebels allied to Twirwaneho and Wazalendo at Rugezi, sector of Mutambala; Wazalendo spokesperson Aimable Nabulizi said Wazalendo of the Biloze Bishambuke self-defence force of General Ngomanzo were attacking Rugezi.

BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 fighters were said to have taken Katogota on Thursday, 80 km north of Uvira city; Uvira resident Elias Muhasha told the BBC that M23 fighters took Katogota after heavy fighting that began on Wednesday; the M23 side neither confirmed nor denied reaching Katogota, but social-media video posted on Thursday showed some M23 fighters indicating they were in Katogota.

BBC News Gahuza reported that from the morning of Friday heavy fighting was reported at Lugezi/Rugezi, Basimukuma-Sud grouping, Fizi, between Wazalendo and Twirwaneho fighters, and that many civilians fled; a Fizi resident who did not wish to be named told the BBC when the fighting began; some people were said to have been killed, but their number and the number of displaced civilians were hard to establish; local journalists said Wazalendo of the Biloze Bishambuke group were the ones fighting Twirwaneho fighters.

Kivu Morning Post quoted a communiqué of the Twirwaneho (MRDP-Twirwaneho) saying that the Rurambo region had been violently attacked by government forces in coalition with Burundian troops and Wazalendo elements, that these acts deliberately targeted Banyamulenge civilians, and that it would take all necessary defensive and offensive measures; in the same article Wazalendo spokesperson Aimable Nabulizi said intense fighting had been reported at Rugezi since the morning of Monday 19 May 2025, where the Wazalendo of General NGOMANZITO faced AFC Twirwaneho M23 rebels.

Kivu Morning Post reported that Wazalendo fighters allied to the Congolese army claimed to have taken control of Rugezi, Basimukuma grouping, Fizi, on Tuesday 20 May 2025 after night fighting with Twirwaneho allied to AFC-M23; the claim came from Wazalendo spokesperson Aimable Nabulizi, who said the enemy had been dispersed.

place: Rugezi, Hauts et Moyens Plateaux de Fizi; route to Uvira
statement: Radio Okapi reported that recent clashes between the FARDC and a Twirwaneho-Red Tabara-M23 coalition at Rugezi in the hauts et moyens plateaux of Fizi, 'five days ago', caused mass population displacement; the Fizi territory administrator Samy Kalonji Badibanga said some households were heading to Uvira, and unconfirmed information said Wazalendo had singled out displaced people heading to Uvira as belonging to rebel movements.

place: Lulenge, Mutambala and Tanganyika sectors, Fizi
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on Wednesday 11 June the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Kalonji Badibanga, said more than 600 000 internally displaced people lived in precarious conditions in the sectors of Lulenge, Mutambala and Tanganyika, and that their number had grown in the Hauts et Moyens Plateaux of Fizi since the taking of Rugezi village by Twirwaneho and Red Tabara militiamen allied to AFC/M23; he said children no longer attended school, which led to their forced enrolment in armed groups.

place: Sange and Kabunambo; origin Kamanyola, Katogota, Luvungi, Bwegera, Luberizi (Ruzizi plain), Uvira
statement: Radio Okapi reported that nearly 4,000 displaced households were registered in the Ruzizi plain, in the cité of Sange and the Kabunambo grouping, caught between FARDC positions to the south and AFC/M23 to the north, having fled Kamanyola, Katogota, Luvungi, Bwegera and Luberizi, hosted since 20 February; Uvira territory administrator Jean de Dieu Masibwa, who visited on Saturday 28 June, called for humanitarian assistance.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that intense fighting took place on Saturday 12 April at Rugezi and Kabanju, Fizi territory, between Burundian forces allied to the FARDC and the Mai-Mai Biloze Bishambuke and fighters of the Twirwaneho armed group; according to a Twirwaneho fighter contacted by the outlet, who spoke on condition of anonymity, at least 17 Burundian soldiers were killed and the Twirwaneho captured one of them with radios and rifles.

place: Mboko port, Bijombo, Swima, Uvira and Fizi territories
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that since Wednesday new Burundian troops had crossed Lake Tanganyika into the territories of Uvira and Fizi; that on Thursday 22 May several Burundian soldiers stationed at the port of Mboko, in the Tanganyika sector, told residents they were heading to Bijombo to confront the rebels; and that these movements followed a strategic meeting held on 14 May in Uvira between the Congolese and Burundian military high commands.

place: Mulongwe and Lusenda refugee camps; Baraka, Fizi
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported on 4 June 2025, citing several local and humanitarian sources, that more than 3,000 people in the Burundian refugee camps of Mulongwe and Lusenda in Fizi territory had reportedly joined Wazalendo militias; a refugee quoted said he earned up to 10,000 Congolese francs a day at a Wazalendo checkpoint in Baraka, and refugees said some returned to the camps armed and in uniform.

Kivu Morning Post reported that Congolese army drones reportedly bombed on Thursday 15 May 2025 the positions of Twirwaneho fighters allied to AFC-M23 at NDAKE/Mikenge, Itombwe sector, Basimukindji 1 grouping, Mwenga; an anonymous security source claimed dozens of officers were eliminated, a figure the page does not corroborate.

place: Hôpital général de référence d'Itombwe, Mikenge, Itombwe sector, Mwenga
statement: Kivutimes reported on 1 May 2025 that the Hôpital général de référence d'Itombwe at Mikenge, in the Hauts-Plateaux of Mwenga territory, was the victim of systematic looting of its medical equipment during violent clashes between the Twirwaneho armed group, allied to AFC/M23, and Wazalendo groups in March 2025; Nakiele hospital centre donated a binocular microscope and caesarean, delivery and hernia kits.

place: Luhwinja chefferie; Luchiga, Kabalole, Luduha, Idudwe groupements; Mwenga
statement: Radio Okapi reported that AFC/M23 rebels took the chefferie of Luhwinja, Mwenga territory, without fighting on the evening of Tuesday 6 May 2025, and that the groupements of Luchiga, Kabalole, Luduha and Idudwe also passed under rebel control from 6 May; according to local sources Luhwinja was the first entity of Mwenga to fall under rebel occupation since the fall of Bukavu.

place: Kaziba (Walungu) toward Minembwe (Hauts Plateaux de Fizi) and Luhwinja (Mwenga)
statement: Radio Okapi reported on 29 April 2025, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 rebels who had come from Nyangezi via Mushenyi were attacking FARDC and Wazalendo positions in the Kaziba chefferie (Walungu), and that from Kaziba the rebels were progressing toward Minembwe in the Hauts Plateaux of Fizi while another group advanced toward Luhwinja.

Kivu Morning Post reported clashes between Wazalendo fighters allied to the Congolese army and AFC-M23 rebels allied to Twirwaneho; according to security sources, the fighting was taking place in several villages of Balala Nord groupement, Fizi territory, and the same sources said it was a Wazalendo offensive.

place: Bijabo, Namara, Kamombo (Balala Nord groupement), Fizi
statement: A Wazalendo spokesperson told Kivu Morning Post that Wazalendo of the FDCC, led by General Kakobanya, attacked AFC Twirwaneho M23 strongholds at Bijabo, Namara and Kamombo in Balala Nord groupement, Fizi territory, from Tuesday 1 July 2025.

place: Natulonge, Luhemba, Kawela, chez Sekaganda (Bashimunyaka Sud groupement, Lulenge sector), Fizi
statement: Kivu Times reported, citing local sources, that fighting broke out on 25 July 2025 between Wazalendo of Bilozebishambuke, led by Delphin Ngomanzito, and Twigwaneho/M23 elements in several localities of Bashimunyaka Sud groupement, Lulenge sector, Fizi territory (Natulonge, Luhemba, Kawela and chez Sekaganda). It said no human or material toll was yet known and that no security or administrative authority had yet communicated.

SOS Médias Burundi reported on 6 August 2025 that violent fighting had opposed, since Wednesday, Wazalendo and the Twirwaneho group in Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, concentrated around Mikenge, Marunde and Bukunji, where the Wazalendo, backed by the FDLR according to the outlet, launched a coordinated offensive against Twirwaneho positions. The outlet reported that no official toll had been communicated.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that, in a communiqué sent to it, Aimable Nabulizi, spokesperson of the Wazalendo in South Kivu, accused Twirwaneho fighters of having attacked their positions, without acknowledging the support attributed to the FDLR or the Burundian and Congolese armies.

place: Kipupu, Bilalo Mbili, Lulenge (Minembwe region), Fizi/Mwenga
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a communiqué published on 6 August the MRDP-Twirwaneho denounced attacks by the FARDC, with the support of the FDLR and the Burundian army, targeting the villages of Kipupu, Bilalo Mbili and Lulenge in the Minembwe region, and said these offensives specifically targeted Banyamulenge civilians. The communiqué said several villages, including in the Mikenge locality, had been hit by heavy-weapon attacks causing many deaths and forcing hundreds of families to flee again, and that the victims were deprived of all emergency aid.

Kivu Morning Post reported that fighting broke out that morning at Mikenge between Wazalendo of the FDCC, led by General Kakobanya and allied to the Congolese army, and Twirwaneho forces allied to AFC-M23; according to local sources heavy and light weapon fire was heard. The outlet said the Wazalendo had claimed the capture of Mikenge the day before and that the morning attack was seen as a Twirwaneho counter-offensive.

place: Maheta, between Maheta and Mikungubwe (Itombwe sector, Basilukidji 1), Mwenga
statement: Actualite.cd reported that two police officers were killed at Maheta village, Mwenga territory, after a clash with elements of the Twirwaneho, Ngumino and Red Tabara coalition, according to civil society sources. Kelvin Bwija, coordinator of Congolese civil society for the Uvira - Fizi axis, named among the victims the commander of the Itombwe commissariat, Kapinga Lwesso, and a police officer, Kabambi Lulenda, and said several other bodies had not yet been found; another source said one more person had been carried away into the bush.

Radio Okapi reported that FARDC, supported by Wazalendo militias, and a rebel coalition of Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and M23/AFC had been fighting since Tuesday 26 August in the high and middle plateaux of Fizi territory, concentrated in Mutambala sector around Rugezi village in Basimukuma-Sud groupement; Fizi territory administrator Samy Kalonji Badibanga said the rebels sought to seize the Misisi and Salamabila mining sites.

place: Rugezi (Fizi); Mwite, Kangovu, Mikenge, Bilalo Mbili (Mwenga/Minembwe)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported on 28 August 2025 that fighting between the FARDC, backed by Wazalendo militias kept up by Kinshasa and the Burundian army (in the outlet's words), and the Twirwaneho and M23 groups began on Wednesday 27 August in Rugezi (Fizi), Mwite and Kangovu (Mwenga), then spread on Thursday to Mikenge and Bilalo Mbili. It quoted a resident saying there were no more medicines at Minembwe.

Kivu Morning Post reported that fighting broke out on 27 August 2025 at Rugezi (Mutambala sector, Fizi) between AFC-M23 rebels allied to Twirwaneho and Wazalendo backed by the FARDC. It said the Wazalendo units were led by Lt General Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito of the Force d'auto-défense Wazalendo Biloze Bishambuke (FABB), who said he had repelled attacks by AFC-M23 and Red Tabara at Rugezi.

Radio Okapi reported that fighting broke out on the morning of Thursday 18 September 2025 between two Wazalendo factions in Mwenga territory, linked to a provincial decision to remove illegal barriers, notably those of the self-proclaimed general Yakaliba; according to local sources, fighters loyal to 'general' Malaika, backed by former provincial interior minister Foka Mike and the FARDC, dismantled checkpoints on Route nationale 2. A provisional toll of several dead and wounded was given.

Actualite.cd reported that a man and his wife were killed in the night of 28 to 29 September 2025 in Baraka town, South Kivu; local civil society said they were shot at home by armed men 'not otherwise identified'.

place: Sange, Kabunambo, Luberizi, Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the Uvira territory administrator, Jean de Dieu Selemani Mabiswa, said more than 4017 households from Kamanyola, Katogota, Luvungi, Kigoma and Kabunambo had taken refuge in Sange town and Kabunambo groupement, and that cholera was affecting the Lemera and Ruzizi plain health zones, with malnutrition cases at Luberizi.

Radio Okapi reported that at least 100 000 people had been displaced in recent months following violence by Twirwaneho militiamen and their allies, the Red Tabara group, mainly on the high and middle plateaux of Fizi, and that these armed groups illegally exploit gold and coltan in the Mitumba range. The Fizi territory administrator, Sammy Badibanga, warned of a grave humanitarian crisis, denounced the persistent illicit exploitation of natural resources, and called for an urgent strengthening of emergency interventions by provincial and national authorities and NGOs.

Radio Okapi reported that on 16 July 2025 the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Kalonji Badibanga, said the humanitarian situation of displaced people from the high and middle plateaux of Fizi was critical, deprived of food, drinking water, medical care and shelter.

In its July 2025 protection highlights, the DRC Protection Cluster reported, for Mwenga territory, where armed groups were committing extortion and other abuses notably in Itombwe sector, that at least 05 cases of rape and several acts of extortion, beatings and abductions had reportedly been alleged at the start of the period, in a context of retreat of government forces and extension of armed groups' hold over localities of the territory.

The DRC Protection Cluster July 2025 highlights reported, for Fizi territory, abductions of civilians, extortion and rape of women by armed groups, in a context where security forces seemed to be gradually losing control of some localities, and that on 19 July 13 civilians were reportedly taken hostage in the bush of villages in Babungwe-Nord groupement.

place: Kagurube/Runingu (RN512, north of Uvira) to Sange, Mwaba, Biriba, Kabunambo, Kiliba
statement: The DRC Protection Cluster July 2025 highlights reported that on 23 July several gunshots were heard in Kagurube/Runingu village on the RN512 north of Uvira, and that, fearing clashes, about 202 households (1,010 people) of Runingu reportedly moved preventively to Sange, Mwaba, Biriba, Kabunambo and Kiliba.

Actualite.cd reported that in a communiqué of 12 August 2025 signed by FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge, the FARDC denounced what they called an intentional and manifest violation of the Washington peace agreement and the Doha declaration of principles by the AFC/M23, citing near-daily attacks on their positions in North and South Kivu, and reserved the right to respond appropriately to provocations.

Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 alerted to major FARDC troop and equipment movements at Nzimbira, Mwenga, Bunyakiri, Kibuwa, Pinga and Uvira, and said two military ships carrying 1,125 fighters of the Kinshasa-regime coalition forces docked on Kalemie-Uvira axis on Sunday 10 August 2025.

place: High plateaux of Fizi and Uvira; presented in Kinshasa
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on Saturday 6 September the FARDC presented to the press six people arrested on the high plateaux of Fizi and Uvira, whom the army accused of collaborating with the AFC/M23. As presented by the FARDC, they included a man identified as Nuyomugabo Sagel, described as a serving soldier of the Rwanda Defence Forces; FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge said the arrest was tangible proof of Rwanda's direct involvement in the conflict. The army described the others as Byishimuse Dieudonné, a Rwandan national trained for the M23; Biringiro Bironi Tesane and Sadiki Elisa, AFC/M23 fighters; Ngaianga Ramazani, affiliated with Twirwaneho; and Muhingirrwa Sangwa Vincent, a state agent and alleged M23 collaborator arrested in Uvira but living in Bujumbura. All were transferred to Kinshasa for interrogation. The identities and affiliations are as presented by the FARDC.

Kivu Morning Post reported that Wazalendo, in a communiqué, denied collusion with the FDLR and accused Twirwaneho of using civilians as human shields and of violence in areas under their influence, citing cases of rape, arson, property destruction and illegal land occupation.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the MRDP-Twirwaneho said Sukhoi fighter jets and drones were mobilised to support ground forces, that these air assets would strike MRDP-Twirwaneho positions and civilian villages, and that the plan was coordinated by General Pacifique Masunzu from Kisangani. The outlet added that a military aircraft had been overflying Minembwe, and that the Congolese government and the FARDC had not reacted.

place: Bangwi, near Makobola (Fizi / Uvira border), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting broke out on Sunday after an attack on AFC/M23 rebels in the village of Bangwi (Makobola area, Fizi/Uvira border), with intense clashes lasting all day and causing mass displacement of the population towards Swima and Mboko.

place: Makobola, Bangwi, Kasekezi, Ngalula, Pemba (Fizi territory), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd quoted M'massa Etùba, president of civil society of the Babungwe sud grouping, as saying that since the taking of Makobola the last AFC/M23 position was at Bangwi near the Iàmba health centre (Nundu health zone), the Wazalendo were in the Pemba escarpments and the FARDC at Kasekezi and Ngalula.
Actualite.cd reported that, despite FARDC reinforcements to the Wazalendo from Kalemie, the town of Mboko, 55 km north of Baraka, remained under the control of AFC-M23 fighters.

place: Lake Tanganyika off Makobola / Swima, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the AFC/M23 had deployed a marine unit on Lake Tanganyika that took part in the fighting, and that after a Wazalendo attack on Monday the 'marins' of the AFC/M23 fired from the lake.

place: Baraka (Baraka-centre and Katanga commune), Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that disturbances hit Baraka-centre (Madjengo II, Malala and Macampagne districts) and Katanga commune, and that at least thirty houses were looted in the night from Friday to Saturday and four young girls ('jeunes filles') were raped.

place: Baraka (Baraka-centre and Katanga commune), Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that at least thirty houses were looted in Baraka in the night from Friday to Saturday, and that schools had been closed for three days and the market paralysed.

place: Katanga commune, Baraka, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that on Saturday morning at about 10:00 local time an exchange of fire broke out in Katanga commune of Baraka, in which a soldier was killed by Wazalendo elements and a civilian was wounded; it added that FARDC units and Wazalendo factions were visible in the town.

place: Makobola, Fizi / Uvira border, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, from its first information, that the FARDC and Wazalendo groups had set up a position at Makobola, about 80 km from Baraka, where the Wazalendo chief William Yakutumba was said to be based, and that the AFC/M23, already in Uvira, would first have to cross that position to advance on Baraka.

FiziMedia reported, citing an alert by the coordinator of the youth group CJIOP, Orphée ‘Yamone’a Kamengele, and several concordant local sources, that the population of Baraka faced serious human rights violations attributed to FARDC elements who had fled the recent fighting in Uvira, denouncing systematic looting, cases of rape, physical violence and repeated uncontrolled gunfire at night, and that voices were demanding the immediate transfer of these FARDC elements to Kalemie.

place: Baraka, Fizi health zone, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said in a press release that, because of the intensification of fighting between the AFC/M23 and the Congolese army and its Wazalendo allies in South Kivu, it had no choice but to interrupt prematurely its medical activities in Baraka (Fizi health zone) for security reasons, that it had evacuated its teams from the town, and that medical activities at Baraka general hospital and in three health centres had ended.

place: Mi’enge, Itombwe grouping, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: FiziMedia reported, according to concordant local sources, that the general referral hospital of Mi’enge, in the Itombwe grouping (Mwenga territory), was vandalised and largely destroyed in the night of Tuesday 30 December 2025 by elements of the Twirwaneho rebellion, allied to the M23-AFC, and that medicines, medical equipment and other essential material were looted.

place: Itombwe highlands, Tuwetuwe, Mwenga territory (and parts of Fizi), South Kivu
statement: Factuel.cd reported that on Thursday 6 November 2025 fighting continued for the third consecutive day in the Itombwe highlands (Mwenga territory), opposing Wazalendo of the Front de Défense du Congo (FDCC), led by General Kakobanya Nakalambi Justin, to a rebel coalition of AFC-M23, RDF, Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and FNL/Zabampema; per local sources the fighting was particularly violent around Tuwetuwe, where the coalition tried to take a FARDC-held position and FARDC supported by FDCC Wazalendo repelled the attack.

place: Mikenge and Bilalombili, Hauts Plateaux (Itombwe), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post quoted a Wazalendo spokesperson in the area as saying that on the morning of Tuesday 4 November 2025 intense fighting broke out around Mikenge between Wazalendo of the FDCC of General Kakobanya Nakalambi Justin and 'the enemies of the AFC Twitwaneho M23, Red Tabara FNL ZABAMPEMA', and that the Wazalendo had already occupied a large part of Mikenge, including its stadium, and all of Bilalombili had fallen.

place: Minembwe and Banyamulenge villages, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the fighting around Mikenge followed an alert by Twirwaneho and by former senator Moïse Nyarugabo about the encirclement and humanitarian blockade of Minembwe and several Banyamulenge villages by the Burundian and Congolese armies.

place: Katogota, Uvira territory (Ruzizi plain), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that in the Ruzizi plain at Uvira, a precarious calm was reported at Katogota, an area under the control of AFC/M23 troops.

place: Luberizi, Luvungi, Lubarika, Uvira territory (Ruzizi plain), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that AFC/M23 troops 'would have advanced' to Luberizi and 'would have taken' control of a good part of Luvungi and Lubarika, according to residents who spoke of a notable absence of FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundian army elements since the evening of Saturday 6 December.

place: Sange, Uvira territory (Ruzizi plain), South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that more than thirty people were killed on Sunday evening in the town of Sange after a bomb exploded in the middle of an inhabited area; according to several testimonies, the blast followed internal clashes between FARDC soldiers, a group of Congolese soldiers returning from the front and trying to flee towards Uvira having reportedly been stopped at the Sange bridge by another FARDC detachment; the provisional toll was at least 7 Burundian soldiers and 7 civilians, plus an undetermined number of Congolese soldiers and Wazalendo.

place: Rusizi (Ruzizi) plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: Congovirtuel reported that the Burundian lieutenant-colonel killed in the Rusizi plain was identified as Lt-Col Athanase Minani, a former FAB officer who commanded the 8th battalion of the Burundian contingent in the DRC; it said the incident, around 4 December 2025, also killed three of his guards and at least 20 Burundian soldiers during fighting intensified that week. SOS Médias Burundi likewise named Lt-Col Athanase Minani as the first senior officer the Burundian army had lost since its official intervention in eastern Congo in March 2023.

place: Mboko, Tanganyika sector, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources in the region, that the fear of population in the Tanganyika sector of Fizi was precipitated and aggravated by the movements of FARDC, Burundian and Wazalendo soldiers fleeing the Uvira front to take refuge in Fizi; it quoted Sammy Amimo, vice-president of civil society in Fizi territory, as saying Mboko town was overwhelmed by displaced people, with more than 18 000 families having arrived although the rebels had not yet reached the Tanganyika sector.

place: Mwandiga, Balala-Sud grouping, Mutambala sector, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: FiziMedia reported, according to several concordant local sources, an attempted assassination on Tuesday 23 December 2025 at about 7 a.m. at Mwandiga against Mwami Ngena Milingita, chief of the Balala-Sud grouping (Mutambala sector, Fizi territory); the alleged author was said to be an individual claiming to belong to the Wazalendo CNPSC movement led by William Amuri Yakutumba, named Efaro and acting under a commander known as Asumani; no victim was recorded.

place: Minembwe, Itombwe and Hauts Plateaux health zones; Fizi–Lusuku–Point Zéro–Mikenge–Minembwe axis, South Kivu
statement: SOSOYAMBOKA.NET, relaying an OCHA communiqué, reported that OCHA recalled that since January 2025 the Minembwe, Itombwe and Hauts Plateaux area had seen a resurgence of armed clashes with serious incidents, including attacks on civilians and the pillaging of health structures, that since May 2025 the Fizi–Lusuku–Point Zéro–Mikenge–Minembwe axis had been completely closed, controlled or blocked by armed groups, and that in August 2025 armed actors at Point Zéro reaffirmed their refusal of any humanitarian access; it added that, according to South Kivu's Commission Mouvement de Population (October 2025), close to 172 000 displaced and returnees were enclaved without access to essential goods or aid.

place: High and middle plateaux of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
statement: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani stated in its civic barometer that Burundi, whose troops fight alongside the FARDC, had deployed more than 10 000 soldiers in the high and middle plateaux of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga. The figure carries a footnote (6) to a Koaci.com article whose URL is dated 7 February 2025 and refers to 10 000 additional Burundian soldiers deployed. The same barometer says that after the clashes in the Ruzizi plain and the capture of Uvira by the AFC-M23 many Burundian soldiers fled the fighting to return to their country, and 'quelques milliers' (a few thousand) remained in the high and middle plateaux of Mwenga, Fizi and Uvira.

place: Eastern DRC (Burundian forces in Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga plateaux)
statement: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani reported that the AFC-M23 rebels had issued a communiqué asking Burundi to withdraw its forces and proposing the opening of a humanitarian corridor to facilitate their return.

The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani reported that Burundi had affirmed its will to keep its troops on Congolese soil and to continue operations alongside the FARDC, in line with the bilateral partnership, according to its foreign minister, Édouard BIZIMANA.

place: Zones officially under government administration (places not specified by the source), South Kivu
statement: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani said in its barometer no. 9 (November-15 December 2025) that in zones officially under government administration the massive presence of Wazalendo militias was causing growing concern among the population, and that women were not spared the violence of these militias: some were publicly whipped and stripped, others were victims of rape and of mass sexual violence in front of their relatives.

place: Minembwe, Mikenge, Ndondo, Kahololo and surroundings (Fizi and Mwenga plateaux), South Kivu
statement: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani listed among the situation's consequences that populations of the middle and high plateaux of Fizi and Mwenga were besieged and deprived of any humanitarian assistance, notably in the villages of Minembwe, Mikenge, Ndondo and Kahololo and surroundings.
