Actualite.cd reported that the village of Point zéro, on the boundary between Fizi and Mwenga territories on the Mitumba range, in the high plateaux, passed under the control of Twirwaneho fighters, allies of the AFC/M23 rebels, from the morning of Friday 16 January 2026; according to its sources in the area, the fighters attacked the FARDC position that morning, forcing the army to withdraw.

place: Point Zéro to Mulima and Mutambala (Fizi)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, that after Twirwaneho took Point Zéro on Friday 16 January, elements of FARDC, of the Burundian national defence force (printed 'FNDB') and Wazalendo groups withdrew to the localities of Mulima and Mutambala.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that FARDC, supported by the Burundian defence force (FDNB) and Wazalendo militiamen, retook the locality of Point Zéro in Fizi territory on 'Friday', from Twirwaneho fighters.
SOS Médias Burundi reported that residents said a Congolese army drone had reportedly bombed the commercial centre of Madegu, wounding three civilians.

place: Bidegu and Minembwe villages (Hauts Plateaux, Fizi)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that Moïse Nyarugabo, an honorary Congolese senator, said that on Thursday 12 February 2026 the FARDC coalition, supported by drones and mortars aimed at the villages of Minembwe, killed a 101-year-old woman named Mukuzakabano Elisabeth; the outlet's next sentence says two other women were wounded in this attack, during which the hospital of Bidegu was bombed.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the Angolan Presidency announced in a communiqué on Thursday a ceasefire between Kinshasa and AFC/M23 from 18 February 2026, an announcement it said came as the FARDC had launched an offensive on several villages of Minembwe.

Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 accused the FARDC of multiple ceasefire violations despite the negotiation process under way in Doha, and said it was open to any peace and de-escalation initiative.

Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola Sud operations in South Kivu, Sub-Lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan, said on Monday 2 February that the army had been fighting for five days to retake Minembwe, regarded as the stronghold of Twirwaneho and its allies.

Radio Okapi reported that Sub-Lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan, FARDC spokesperson, said the enemy was dropping bombs blindly in populated areas where civilians were, while the regular army 'does not fight in agglomerations' and protects the population.

Radio Okapi reported that the administrator of Fizi territory, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, said the number of internally displaced people was approaching one million across Fizi territory, and that fighting on Thursday 5 February at 'Point Zéro' caused a new mass displacement.

place: Lake Tanganyika shore, Makobola-Mboko, Fizi-centre, Point Zéro Kwa Mulima (Fizi)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Kalonji Badibanga, said displaced people in Fizi territory were sheltering in schools and churches, and that the Tanganyika lakeshore, a focus of cholera and measles, exposed children to major epidemic risks.

Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that FARDC supported by Wazalendo have recovered Mikenge since Sunday 1 March, according to Pacifique Kararuka, president of the Nouvelle société civile congolaise at Kipupu.

Actualite.cd reported that FARDC spokesperson in the region, Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said villages including Mikenge, Kakenge, Bilalombili and Bidegu 1 had been retaken, and that five elements were captured, 17 surrendered and 11 bodies left on the ground, among them a brigade commander of AFC/M23 and a logistics officer of Twirwaneho.

SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported, citing local sources, that FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo now control strategic areas in the centre of Mikenge, including the main hospital, while Twirwaneho actors were reportedly still in the surrounding area.

place: Bidegu, Ilundu, Rugezi, Kalingi, Kalongi, Kakenge (Minembwe, Fizi)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that on Sunday fighting was also reported in several villages of Minembwe including Bidegu, Ilundu, Rugezi, Kalingi, Kalongi and Kakenge.

place: Kabambare and Pangi territories, Maniema (displaced from Fizi highlands)
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing a Mercy Corps humanitarian report for February, that 15 200 households from the highlands were recorded in Maniema province, in Kabambare and Pangi territories, and said clashes between FARDC with Wazalendo and Ngumino-Twirwaneho allied to AFC/M23 in the Fizi highlands caused the movements, while the report also attributes part of the Kabambare displacement to heavy rains.

place: Kabunango, Runingu, Kabunambo, Sange, Biriba, Kasambura (Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that intense fighting opposed the FARDC/Wazalendo coalition and AFC/M23 rebels from the morning of Tuesday 17 March in the villages of Kabunango and Runingu in the Uvira grouping, South Kivu, and that traffic was cut on the RN5 linking Bukavu and Uvira; Martin Mafikiri of the Nouvelle société civile congolaise said both sides had reinforced in the Ruzizi plain.
Actualite.cd reported that, according to the rebellion (AFC/M23), the 17 March fighting in the Ruzizi plain was a 'guerre généralisée' (generalised war) waged by the government army and its allies.

place: Runingu, Kashatu market; Uvira city entrance
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, that Wazalendo militiamen operating at Runingu announced on Sunday the prohibition of entry into Uvira city for anyone coming from areas controlled by M23, citing suspected spying on FARDC positions; Ruzizi plain residents of Kamanyola, Luvungi, Luberizi and Sange said they were turned away from the Kashatu market at Runingu.

MSF said that on 1 May 2026 its team travelling between Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu in South Kivu for a needs assessment was stopped at a checkpoint controlled by Wazalendo elements, and that armed men then fired among themselves while the team was caught in the middle. MSF said all staff later returned safely to Bukavu.

place: Minembwe centre, Gitavi, Bidegu, Kalingi, Ilundu, Kakenge (Hauts Plateaux), Fizi/Mwenga
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local sources, that on 17 June 2026 FARDC (supported by the Burundian army and Wazalendo) and Twirwaneho allied to AFC-M23 fought on three axes around Minembwe centre: axis 1 (Mikenge to Gitavi) led by the army and Wazalendo; axis 2 (Bidegu-Kalingi) led by the special forces Hiboux and Serpent noir using combat drones; axis 3 (Kakenge) led exclusively by the Burundian army and FDLR units, according to local and security sources.

Kivu Morning Post reported, in an account of the 17 June 2026 fighting around Minembwe whose opening it attributes to local sources, that on axis 1 (Mikenge towards Gitavi) several houses of Banyamulenge civilians were burned by the army and Wazalendo militiamen in the first village of Gitavi. The article gives no specific source for this incident and carries no FARDC response.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the humanitarian blockage at Minembwe was intensifying, with no exit and no resupply of food and medicines, and that humanitarian access was blocked. It said the Mahoro Peace association, which groups Congolese nationals living in the United States, had indicated that 32 civilians were wounded between 8 and 11 June.

place: Kitavi, Irundu, Madegu (Ugeafi school), Minembwe centre airfield, Fizi
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the spokesperson of operation Sukola 2 Sud-Kivu, Lieutenant Reagan Kalonji, said FARDC had since the evening of Tuesday 16 June retaken total control of Kitavi village, the Irundu agglomeration and positions at the Ugeafi school at Madegu near Minembwe centre, and that on 17 June the army was trying to retake the Minembwe-centre airfield. The Fizi territory administrator Sammy Badibanga said the clashes created a catastrophic humanitarian situation.

DW (Swahili) reported that the Congolese army claimed to have controlled Minembwe since Wednesday evening and that Twirwaneho had fled, but that residents denied it. Human rights defender Maniragaba Byashonyi said no FARDC soldiers were in the centre of Minembwe and that the centre was controlled by MRDP/Twirwaneho.

place: Minembwe periphery, Lwiko, Mutunda, Miko, Ilundu, Bidegu, Fizi/Mwenga
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, after fighting around Minembwe, the FARDC, the FDNB and their allies had reportedly withdrawn to the localities of Lwiko, Mutunda and Miko, leaving several peripheral positions of Minembwe under the control of Twirwaneho/M23 fighters. It said the FARDC had not published a detailed communiqué at the time of writing, while local military sources confirmed a strategic repositioning after particularly violent clashes in the Ilundu and Bidegu areas.

SOS Médias Burundi quoted former national deputy Moïse Nyarugabo as saying 'La menace sur Minembwe est écartée', that despite Sukhoi bombardments, drones and heavy artillery the forces engaged had been pushed back beyond the Lwiko river; it reported he accused the coalition of bombardments causing civilian losses and mass displacement.

place: Bijombo (Muramvya, Masata, Nyakirango, Irango, Kajembwe), Uvira territory
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing residents' testimonies, that clashes had intensified since Friday 3 April 2026 in the Bijombo area of Uvira territory between FARDC supported by FDNB elements, Wazalendo and Gumino fighters on one side and Twirwaneho fighters affiliated with the M23 on the other, displacing thousands of civilians; Muramvya, Masata, Nyakirango, Irango and Kajembwe were among the most affected localities.

SOS Médias Burundi quoted a resident of Muramvya village (Bijombo area), 'Yohana', as saying residents were fleeing because 'the Wazalendo are threatening civilians and stealing our livestock', and that some residents were hiding in the bush, others had fled to the forests and many had taken refuge in churches in Masoro and Gahuna.

place: not stated by the source (article on Bijombo, Uvira territory, and Minembwe)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Burundian army spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged on the BBC that Banyamulenge are trapped in areas 'where the enemy is', saying 'It’s understandable that those who go to buy food for the enemy are trapped.'

place: Minembwe, Mikenge (Hauts Plateaux de Fizi, Itombwe, Uvira)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a communiqué MRDP-Twirwaneho denounced ongoing attacks on civilians in Minembwe and Mikenge, rejected FARDC accusations that Minembwe served as a sanctuary for Burundian RED-Tabara rebels, demanded the immediate withdrawal of Burundian forces from Congolese territory and called for an independent international investigation into human rights violations in the region. The outlet quoted Colonel Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, in the communiqué, as calling those accusations false.

place: Minembwe, Kakenge, Kalonge, Bidegu, Kalingi, Mikenge, Fizi/Mwenga
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from 08:00 on Friday 15 May 2026 Kinshasa had ordered the deployment of heavily armed combat helicopters from Kalemie to join strikes on Minembwe and surroundings, in addition to combat drones, heavy artillery and Sukhoi-25 jets. Fighting was reported at Kakenge, Kalonge, Bidegu and Kalingi (Fizi) and at Mikenge (Mwenga).

Actualite.cd reported (9 June) that Mikenge village (Mwenga) was hit by bombardments on the night of Sunday to Monday '7 juin', leaving at least two dead and 6 wounded including two children; it said the army attributed the bombardments to the AFC/M23-Twirweneho rebel coalition and, according to an army communiqué, the air attacks hit FARDC positions at Mikenge and its surroundings, causing heavy material damage.

place: Mikenge general hospital, Mikenge (Mwenga territory); the page places the attacks in the Minembwe highlands, Fizi territory
statement: Mediacongo, carrying a piece credited 'Patrick Kitoko, Opinion Info / MCP', reported that, according to a FARDC communiqué of 20 May 2026, the Mikenge general hospital was reportedly 'intentionally targeted' and 'completely destroyed' during drone strikes that hit localities including Kalingi and Mikenge in the early morning, with a provisional toll of several civilian victims that reportedly included hospital staff members. FARDC also accused Rwanda and its 'proxies' of being behind the offensive. The communiqué was signed by FARDC acting spokesperson Lieutenant-Colonel Mongba Hazukay Mak. Africa-Infos.cd (21 May) reported the same communiqué, no. 13.

Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X that at 14:00 on Wednesday 24 June 2026 'les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa ont bombardé, à l’aide de drones de combat, l’hôpital général de Minembwe, y compris le pavillon pédiatrique'. The outlet also quoted AFC/M23 deputy coordinator Bertrand Bisimwa: « Le bombardement d’un hôpital en temps de guerre est un crime de guerre ». This is an AFC/M23 allegation; the article gives no casualty figure for the hospital and carries no FARDC response.
sources: Kivu Morning Post; The New Times; Habari Express

statement: Mediacongo, carrying a report credited 'Radio Okapi / MCP', reported, citing local sources, that clashes took place on Wednesday 24 June in the villages of Ilundu and Alengei between FARDC and the fighters of the Twirwaneho armed coalition and their allies; the militia accused FARDC of drone bombardments on its positions, while local actors called this a 'fuite en avant'. It also reported that at the sixth meeting of the Joint Oversight Committee (Comité mixte de surveillance, CMS) on the security situation in the DRC, held on 24 June 2026 in London, Kinshasa and Kigali reaffirmed their commitment to defuse tensions over Minembwe.

Mediacongo (Radio Okapi / MCP credit) reported that, according to local civil society, repeated Twirwaneho attacks on positions retaken by FARDC were causing new displacement, and that Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga said victims and vulnerable people were estimated at several thousand.

place: Point Zéro, Kasika, Nyaruhinga, Mukoko (Fizi / Mwenga territories, Minembwe area), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that forces his movement calls the 'coalisées du régime de Kinshasa' intensified their ground attacks on the Point Zéro area at around 04:45 in the early hours of the morning; he also said these forces attacked Kasika (Mwenga territory) early that morning, and that government forces attacked Nyaruhinga and Mukoko in the Minembwe area. This is the AFC/M23 account.

Radio Okapi reported that, according to the Fizi territory administrator, at least eighteen people were killed and many others wounded in drone bombings 'du M23 et de ses alliés' on the morning of Friday 3 July in the village of Mulima; the administrator said there were many victims among women, men and children, as well as livestock losses. The attribution to the M23 and its allies is the administrator's.

place: Mulima, Kangouli, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Badibanga, said: 'Les infrastructures sanitaires et scolaires ont été détruites, et plusieurs élèves ont vu leurs écoles anéanties dans les villages de Mulima, Kangouli et leurs environs' (health and school infrastructure destroyed; several pupils' schools wiped out in Mulima, Kangouli and surroundings). The source does not name or number the health facilities.

place: Sange and Luvungi (Ruzizi plain), Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi's press review reported that the Agence congolaise de presse (ACP) reports the discovery of eleven mass graves in South Kivu, seven months after massacres attributed (attribués) to the M23 in the towns of Sange and Luvungi, Uvira territory; according to ACP the announcement was made on Monday 27 July by the Auditorat militaire supérieur du Sud-Kivu after an investigation conducted jointly with the 33rd military region.

place: Point Zéro (Mwenga/Fizi highlands, Itombwe), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo recalled, in a later article on fighting at Point Zéro, that on 4 July Twirwaneho elements, allies of the AFC/M23, had taken control of Point Zéro after dislodging the FARDC.

place: Point Zéro-Centre, Itombwe highlands, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that violent clashes had pitted AFC/M23 elements and their allies against the FARDC, backed by Wazalendo groups, since Friday morning at Point Zéro, Itombwe highlands, Mwenga territory. It also reported that tension remained high in the belt between Luntukulu (Walungu territory), Tchulwe and Lubimbe (Shabunda territory), where a reinforcement of AFC-M23 troops was announced.

place: Point Zéro, Kakenge, Rubemba, Mikenge, Kalongi, Rugezi, Mukera (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing testimonies and local sources, that the FARDC, the FDNB and Wazalendo militiamen had lost several localities, notably Point Zéro, Kakenge, Rubemba, Mikenge and Kalongi, a loss these sources attributed to Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC/M23, and that FARDC and FDNB soldiers had reportedly withdrawn from the Rugezi, Kakenge and Point Zéro sectors towards Mukera, while others had reportedly headed towards Misisi.

SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing local sources in Fizi territory, that three vehicles carrying ammunition and Burundian soldiers had reportedly been targeted by drones at Mulima during the past week, and that according to these sources several soldiers had reportedly been killed, among them a colonel and a major of the Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB); it said no official toll was available at the time of publication and that the information could not be independently confirmed.

place: Lwindi chiefdom (Kasika, Kalambi, road to Kigogo), Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that new clashes between Wazalendo fighters and AFC-M23 troops broke out on Tuesday 1 September 2026 in the Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga territory, on the road to Kigogo; the sources said the Wazalendo launched the assault first, that heavy artillery was used, and that civilians were reportedly hit by bullets.

place: Ruyengo, Fizi territory (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC said they shot down a kamikaze drone at Ruyengo, Fizi territory, on Thursday 20 August 2026 around 8 a.m.; the report attributed the device to RDF/M23 elements and their allies Twirwaneho/Red-Tabara. The spokesperson of the Sukola 2 operations (south sector, South Kivu), sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, said this came a few hours after the FARDC foiled several rebel attacks on their positions in the Fizi highlands.

place: Maheta, Magunda, Nabuhera, Kakuku, Musonjo (Basimukindji 2 / Bijombo), Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that violent clashes broke out from the evening of 26 September 2026 in several villages of the Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, which several local sources placed notably in the Basimukindji 2 groupement at Maheta, Magunda, Nabuhera, Kakuku and Musonjo; a local leader said AFC/M23 fighters sought to advance to Masango before being pushed back, and the article said the clashes caused a massive displacement of the population.

place: Rugezi, Gipimo, Kuwihene (Basimunyaka Sud, Lulenge sector, Minembwe area), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said that on 27 September 2026 the government coalition (FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundian forces) intensified attacks at Rugezi, Gipimo and Kuwihene (Basimunyaka Sud groupement, Lulenge sector); it added that sources close to the FARDC said they shot down a drone at Rugezi, while AFC/M23 'Twirwaheno' sources said they repelled an attack in the area.

place: Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories, South Kivu
statement: MediaCongo reported that UN Secretary-General's spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric on Monday condemned drone attacks reported in Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories, South Kivu, without identifying their authors, and that according to the UN violent clashes since 4 July, including reported drone attacks, had reportedly left at least five dead and dozens wounded among civilians.

place: Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories; Kipupu and Malanda (Mwenga), South Kivu
statement: MediaCongo reported that Stéphane Dujarric said fighting had disrupted supply routes, causing critical shortages of medical supplies needed to treat the wounded, and that at least 6,000 people had fled to Kipupu and Malanda in Mwenga territory.

place: Hauts-Plateaux of Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, at a press briefing, said of the Hauts-Plateaux that 'le Rwanda excelle avec des tirs de drones à partir de son territoire', calling this once again proof of bad faith in not advancing the peace process, and added that the armed forces were well mobilised. This is the Kinshasa government's accusation.

place: Hauts plateaux, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga, that sixteen fighters of the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) and their allies surrendered to the FARDC on Tuesday 27 October in the highlands of Fizi territory, South Kivu, and that they had reportedly decided to lay down their arms; the outlet said this information, reported by the administrator, could not be confirmed by independent local sources at the time of publication.

Radio Okapi reported that Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga said the surrenders concerned the zones of Mikenge-Minembwe, Mulima, Rugezi, Bikarakara and Kabandja, and that FRN fighters and their allies kept surrendering to the FARDC for protection, citing Twiraneho, AFC-M23, Red Tabara and FNL Zabampema among the allies.

place: South of Minembwe, Fizi highlands, South Kivu
statement: Kinpressactu.cd reported, citing local sources, violent clashes on Sunday in several villages south of Minembwe in the Fizi highlands between the FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters and a coalition of Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and AFC/M23.

place: South of Minembwe, Fizi highlands, South Kivu
statement: Kinpressactu.cd reported, citing local sources, that the Sunday clashes south of Minembwe took place amid recurrent use of drones said to strike government-force positions and inhabited areas; it added that accusations of drones attributed to Rwandan forces and of bombardments hitting civilians could not be independently verified for these clashes.

place: Rubarati and Ruhuha, Bijombo highlands, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Twirwaneho spokesperson Fidèle Rugabo confirmed that AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho fighters had retaken control of Rubarati and Ruhuha (Bijombo highlands, Uvira territory); the outlet said this had not been independently confirmed when written.

place: Bijombo highlands (Magunda, Rubarati, Masango, Ruhuha), Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Congolese government coalition would have lost several positions in the Bijombo highlands of Uvira territory after drone attacks attributed to the AFC/M23.

place: Magunda and Malimba, Masango area, Bijombo highlands, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the troop movements it described came a few days after the retaking of positions at Magunda and Malimba by Burundian soldiers, the FARDC and Wazalendo militiamen, positions it said had reportedly been occupied earlier by RED-Tabara fighters; it said these operations followed clashes reported in the Masango area that reportedly cost the lives of seven Burundian soldiers, according to the information reported.

place: Uvira and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that new clashes between AFC/M23-Twirwaneho troops and the government coalition were reported throughout the weekend of Saturday 10 to Sunday 11 October 2026 in several localities of Uvira and Mwenga territories, with civilian losses and renewed displacement reported.

place: Masango, Magunda (Bijombo), Uvira territory; Basimukinji 2 (Itombwe), Mwenga territory
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that the weekend's fighting was reported at Masango and Magunda (Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory) and at Basimukinji 2 (Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory), and that AFC/M23-Twirwaneho troops were said to have launched the first attacks from their Magunda positions after learning that Burundian troops and Wazalendo fighters were reorganising for a counter-offensive.

place: Bumba, Basimukinji 1 grouping, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that civil-society actors continue to document alleged human rights violations attributed to armed men claiming to be Wazalendo in this part of South Kivu, and that over the weekend a misunderstanding reportedly degenerated into the burning of several houses in the village of Bumba, Basimukinji 1 grouping.

place: Kuwihene and Rugezi axis, Fizi territory (near Minembwe), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, new offensives in Fizi territory in the entities of Kuwihene and on the Rugezi axis, adding that the situation remained volatile although the positions of the parties reportedly remained unchanged.

place: Point Zéro and Nyaruhinga, near Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that calm returned at Point Zéro and Nyaruhinga in Fizi territory after clashes of 30 September between the AFC/M23 coalition, supported by Red Tabara and Twirhaneho, and the FARDC/Wazalendo/FNDB forces; according to local civil society, the FARDC/Wazalendo coalition repelled an AFC/M23 offensive in the surroundings.

place: North-west of Katogota (Muhungu, Birayi, Ndagereka, Matale), Itara-Luvungi grouping, Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: The outlet reported that violent clashes opposed FRN rebels and fighters of the FARDC-Wazalendo coalition early on the morning of Tuesday 20 October 2026 in the Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, and that, according to local sources, the fighting was concentrated on the mountain axis north-west of Katogota, in the villages of Muhungu, Birayi, Ndagereka and Matale in the Itara-Luvungi grouping; it said several hundred families fled their villages and that no official toll had been communicated.

place: Magunda, Kitembe, Kitoga, Kigoma grouping, Hauts Plateaux d'Uvira, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local civil society, that at least 155 houses were damaged by torrential rain and strong winds in the villages of Magunda, Kitembe and Kitoga (Kigoma grouping, Bafuliiru chiefdom, Uvira highlands), with the weather reported to have struck since 20 October 2026.

place: Rubuga and northern Hauts Plateaux d'Uvira health zone, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing the same local civil society, that the Rubuga health centre lost its entire roof to the winds, complicating access to care, and that Byamungu Shamamba Paul, president of the Nouvelle Société civile congolaise in Uvira territory, said about eight health centres in the northern part of the Hauts Plateaux d'Uvira health zone had attendance difficulties and insufficient humanitarian support.

Iwacu reported that the FDNB, in a note responding to a 25 July 2025 press release by the MRDP-Twirwaneho spokesperson accusing Burundi of training the FDLR and providing it logistical support in weapons in Luvungi, Lubarika, Rurambo and Minembwe, said Burundi cannot in any way support aggressors of a neighbouring country.

Iwacu reported that the FDNB communiqué, signed by its spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, said Burundian soldiers in the DRC carry out their mission of fighting Burundian and/or foreign negative forces in collaboration with the FARDC under bilateral accords, with strict respect for human rights and international humanitarian law.

Anadolu Agency reported that FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza said in a message on X that no Burundian soldier was deployed in the city of Bukavu, rejecting the M23's accusation after the double explosion at an M23 rally; Anadolu quoted M23 president Bertrand Bisimwa as saying preliminary investigations indicated the explosives were those used by the FDNB.

BBC Gahuza reported that, asked about a Reuters report of Burundian troops returning home from the DRC, FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza replied by text message "Fake News" and said on X that FDNB soldiers sent to the DRC were continuing their activities in their assigned areas.

place: Minembwe area, Fizi / Mwenga, South Kivu
statement: BBC Gahuza reported that the Burundian army (FDNB) said its troops in South Kivu had blocked the roads of people leaving the Minembwe area in order to "protect Uvira and the Burundian border", and asked residents of Minembwe to "separate from the enemies" there; FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza was quoted saying the route had to be blocked because it was one they had to use to reach Uvira.

BBC Gahuza reported that protesters in Minembwe accused Burundian troops and those working with them of blocking roads (at Mu Mikarati, Point-zero and elsewhere) that bring in necessities mainly from Uvira, and that residents of the area said they struggled to obtain necessities such as food, medicines, oil and soap; Baratuza told the BBC there was no Burundian soldier in Minembwe.

Burundi Forum reported that the FDNB published a communiqué, also relayed on its X account, in which spokesperson Brigadier General Baratuza Gaspard said that no FDNB soldier was currently in the locality of Minembwe and that comments relayed on social media questioning the conduct of Burundian soldiers deployed in the DRC were "sans fondement" (unfounded).

place: Burundian territory (place not stated); Burundian positions in the DRC
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, in Gitega on Monday, Burundi's foreign minister Edouard Bizimana told diplomats that Rwanda had targeted Burundian territory and dropped three bombs, wounding two civilians, a child and a woman, and that Burundian positions in the DRC had been attacked by Rwanda since 2 December, including with drones.

Actualite.cd reported that, in a communiqué, the Rwandan government accused the DRC and Burundi of violating the ceasefire, said the FARDC, Burundian troops (FDNB), the FDLR, Wazalendo militias and foreign mercenaries had carried out bombings near the Rwandan border, and claimed Burundi had deployed nearly 20 000 soldiers in South Kivu and besieged Banyamulenge villages at Minembwe.

Africa Insight reported that Burundian foreign minister Edouard Bizimana told diplomats on 8 December 2025 that the AFC/M23 coalition had sought to capture Uvira before the 4 December Washington peace accord but Burundian troops had intervened.

Iwacu reported that, in an RFI interview, Burundian foreign minister Edouard Bizimana said the rebels used heavy weapons, artillery and Turkish-made kamikaze drones and "launched bombs on civilian populations, forcing people to flee".
Iwacu reported that Bizimana said in an RFI interview that if the rebels and their Rwandan allies entered Uvira "all options are on the table", adding "What threatens Uvira also threatens Bujumbura".

Actualite.cd reported that Burundian foreign minister Édouard Bizimana wrote on X that the rebels' announced withdrawal from Uvira was "a pure lie" meant to mislead international opinion, saying the Rwandan forces and the rebels had not withdrawn from Uvira.

place: Commune of Tshibitoke (as printed; Cibitoke, Burundi)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Burundi's ambassador to the UN, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, told a special session on the crisis in the east that bombardments from Rwanda hit the commune of Tshibitoke on 4 December, wounding a woman and a child, and warned that Burundi's restraint "has limits" and that it reserved the right to self-defence under the UN Charter in case of new attacks.

place: Bugabira (northern Burundi, on the Rwandan border)
statement: AFP reported that President Ndayishimiye again warned Rwanda during a visit to the shared border, telling residents of Bugabira, a commune on the border with Rwanda, "Celui qui va nous attaquer, nous allons l'attaquer" (whoever attacks us, we will attack them), in a speech broadcast on Wednesday by local media.

BBC News Afrique reported that President Ndayishimiye told the BBC he had "credible intelligence" that Rwanda was planning to attack Burundi; the BBC said Rwanda had responded by calling the statements surprising.

Iwacu reported that, at his press conference, President Ndayishimiye spoke again about his decision to send troops to eastern DRC to support the FARDC and curb incursions by certain Burundian rebel groups based in South Kivu; Iwacu noted he gave no further details.

Iwacu reported that President Ndayishimiye said at his press conference that he had asked the AFC-M23 rebels whether they were really Congolese, that they admitted they were, and that he had proposed they accept being cantoned at Rumangabo so that a negotiation, disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration process could follow, "mais la guerre a repris de plus belle" (but the war resumed all the more).

Actualite.cd reported that, at the new-year exchange of wishes with the diplomatic and consular corps, President Évariste Ndayishimiye called on Rwanda to repatriate the leaders of the Red Tabara movement exiled in Kigali, whom he considers a threat to Burundi's security, and said Burundi had not broken off relations.

Antoine Kaburahe's site reported that, in a press interview, President Ndayishimiye defended keeping several thousand Burundian soldiers in eastern DRC, saying they operate in support of the FARDC under regional accords, and rejected accusations of collaboration with the FDLR; Rwandan foreign minister Olivier Nduhungirehe, interviewed by Kaburahe, rejected the president's accusations and said the FDLR collaborate openly with the army of the DRC and the Burundian army.

BBC News Gahuza reported that FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza confirmed that two Burundian soldiers, Major Jérémie Nitunga and Captain Félicien Kanjori, were arrested in the DRC, but denied they were held in Kinshasa.

place: Mikenge, Itombwe sector, Mwenga, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the centre of Mikenge (Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory), held for more than a year by Twirwaneho combatants and rebels, was retaken on Sunday by the FARDC supported by the FDNB and Wazalendo militiamen, who according to local sources now control strategic points of the centre, including the general hospital.

place: Not stated in the first caption; blockade of Minembwe (Fizi / Mwenga, South Kivu) per the second caption
statement: SOS Médias Burundi published a photo captioned as showing Banyamulenge women demonstrating, placards in hand, against the blockade imposed by the Burundian army, on 4 November 2025 (place not stated in the caption); a second caption said members of the Banyamulenge community demonstrated in Indiana (USA) in December 2025, at the call of the Mahoro Peace Association, to denounce the military blockade that deprives civilians of Minembwe of food and care.

The FARDC, through spokesperson Maj Gen Sylvain Ekenge, called the AFC/M23 announcement of its withdrawal from Uvira a 'simple manoeuvre of diversion' meant to ease international pressure on Rwanda and its proxies; BBC Gahuza reported that Ekenge, in a video statement read on RTNC on Saturday, said claims of withdrawal bore no relation to the reality on the ground.

Radio Okapi's press review, citing Africa News, reported that Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya, on his X account, questioned what credibility to give to the M23's unilateral manoeuvre and said the government expected an effective withdrawal of Rwandan troops from all occupied zones.

Al Jazeera reported that the DRC government described M23's pledge to withdraw from Uvira as a 'nonevent, a diversion, a distraction', and that Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya told Reuters the intention was to distract the American mediation team, which he said was preparing to take measures against Rwanda.

place: Kinshasa (statement concerning the conflict in the east)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that an official FARDC communique signed by chief of general staff Lt Gen Jules Mbanza Mwilambwe announced the suspension of Maj Gen Sylvain Ekenge, until then FARDC spokesperson.

BBC News Gahuza reported that the office of President Félix Tshisekedi said on X that, at a restricted ministers' meeting on Thursday, Tshisekedi described the attack as a 'flagrant violation' of Rwanda's commitments under the peace agreements signed in Washington the previous week; the article ties this to the rebels' capture of Uvira, which it presents as a military attack by Rwanda.

place: Kinshasa; concerning Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: DW reported that President Félix Tshisekedi, in a speech to Congolese parliamentarians on Monday, said that as long as a single village, neighbourhood or hill remained under the threat of illegal arms, he would consider his task unfinished; DW added that the speech did not reassure residents of Uvira territory.

place: Brussels (statement on the North and South Kivu conflict)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that President Félix Tshisekedi, speaking at a forum, offered his hand to Paul Kagame to 'make the peace of the brave' and asked him to order the M23 troops supported by Rwanda to stop the escalation.

Radio Okapi reported that at the Council of Ministers of Friday 10 October 2025, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa described President Tshisekedi's outstretched hand to Paul Kagame as a 'sincere quest' for peace.

place: Geneva (statement on Goma and Bukavu situation)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka, opening the 58th session of the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva on Monday 24 February, called for 'dissuasive sanctions against Rwanda'.

place: Kinshasa (statement on the M23 and Rwanda)
statement: In an interview with NotreAfrik published by Wakat Séra, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka said the M23 and Rwanda are 'intrinsically linked' and that any serious negotiation should be held directly with Rwanda.

place: Addis Ababa (statement on the conflict in eastern DRC)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the Prime Minister's office said Judith Suminwa was preparing to speak at the African Union Peace and Security Council on behalf of the Head of State with force and determination, putting forward her country's precise expectations.

place: Munich (statement on North and South Kivu conflict)
statement: DW reported that President Félix Tshisekedi intensified his accusations against Rwanda, criticising decades of what he described as 'predatory aggression' against the DRC, at the Munich Security Conference.

The UN General Assembly's summary of President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi's address said he stated that the withdrawal of Rwandan troops and an end to support for M23 are non-negotiable conditions for real peace.

place: Kinshasa; Doha (declaration concerning North and South Kivu)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya welcomed the 19 July signature in Doha, under Qatari facilitation, of a declaration of principles between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23, which he said contains clear commitments on civilian protection, national sovereignty and peace consolidation.

place: Kalangira, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Beto.cd reported that the military governor of North Kivu, Maj Gen Evariste Somo Kakule, said armed youths unidentified clashed with AFC/M23 fighters at Kalangira, Baswagha chiefdom (Lubero), and, in a communique, that the incident did not involve the FARDC, which remain faithful to the ceasefire.

place: Kisanga, Masereka; Kipese, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Beto.cd reported that, according to the spokesperson of the North Kivu military governor, Lt Marc Elongo, three notables had been arrested and abducted five days earlier by the AFC/M23 official in the locality of Kisanga, near Masereka, and had allegedly then been transferred to Kipese, where they were allegedly detained and tortured; the page says the army reported this was confirmed after an emergency provincial security council meeting, and names the three detained persons, with a hedge ('seraient'), as Mumbere Charles, Kakule Mulokya Block and Solo Manzu Bungwe.

Forum des As reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya wrote in a post on X on Thursday 23 July that demanding the participation of the 'son', M23/AFC, in the dialogue between Congolese was directly demanding that of the 'father', Rwanda; the outlet added that the government considers the links between the rebel movement and Kigali established.

Forum des As reported that Muyaya said the dialogue announced by President Tshisekedi is intended for national actors who have not taken up arms and must remain complementary to the diplomatic processes in Washington and Doha.

Actualite.cd reported that the South Kivu provincial government, led by Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi from Uvira, denounced the 'insufficiency, even inaction' of the AFC/M23 rebels administering Bukavu after a fire, and the pressure and 'predation' of the population under their administration.

Actualite.cd reported that a fire on Thursday 10 September ravaged two schools in Kadutu commune, Bukavu, killing pupils, with about twenty others wounded, provisional figures it said were confirmed by medical sources and the AFC/M23 authorities; Radio Okapi reported a provisional toll of 29 children dead from hospital sources.

Actualite.cd reported that the United States, via Massad Boulos on X, acknowledged the first transport and transfer of 15 detainees from DRC authorities to AFC/M23 under the Doha prisoner-exchange mechanism.

Actualite.cd reported that the transfer of fifteen detainees took place on 6 and 7 August, facilitated by the ICRC; the detainees left Beni, transited through Uganda and were handed to AFC/M23 in Rutshuru territory.

Actualite.cd reported that the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), led by Joseph Kabila, announced in a political declaration dated 12 October in Goma that it ended the existence of the Alliance Fleuve Congo, which it 'succeeds by right', and aims to fight Kinshasa 'by all means including force'.

Actualite.cd reported that FARDC spokesperson Major-General Sylvain Ekenge said that at the meeting chaired by President Tshisekedi the army chief of staff presented the operational situation and the commander-in-chief gave instructions to the defence and security forces.

place: Rugezi zone, Minembwe region, South Kivu (territory not stated by the source)
statement: The Kivu Morning Post reported that the FRN accused Kinshasa's forces on Thursday 22 October 2026 of preparing generalised attacks, saying the army bombarded the Rugezi zone in the Minembwe region, South Kivu, with kamikaze drones and heavy artillery in the night of 21 to 22 October.

place: Luvungi, Lubarika, Ruzizi plain, South Kivu
statement: The Kivu Morning Post reported that the FRN communiqué also reported reinforcement of troops and military equipment at Luvungi and Lubarika and movements of Burundian troops crossing the Ruzizi river towards the Ruzizi plain, where, according to the communiqué, they would join other military elements.

place: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that in a communiqué published on Monday 24 August 2026 the DRC government accused the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) and their AFC/M23 auxiliaries of summary executions, sexual violence, torture and abductions, citing consolidated data of more than 300 people killed in June and July 2026.

Radio Okapi reported that the same government communiqué asserted that more than 100 families of Rwandan origin crossed the border via the Kabuhanga track in Nyiragongo territory on 10 August 2026 and were reportedly then settled at Rwibiranga (Buhumba groupement), and that Kinshasa denounced the imposition of taxes in areas controlled by the AFC/M23, including fees in schools and taxes reportedly imposed on health structures.

Radio Okapi reported that local civil society and notables of Kaniola, Walungu territory, denounced rapes, which they presented as a means of terrorising communities, after the AFC/M23 incursion, per testimonies collected on the spot.

Radio Okapi reported that the South Kivu provincial government spokesperson, Me Luganywa-Bashizi Didier, condemned the abuses reported at Kaniola and called for those responsible to be brought to justice.

place: Birambizo general referral hospital, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Birambizo general referral hospital was again the target of looting on Wednesday 19 August; in the same report it said, citing local sources, that unidentified armed men took medicines, medical equipment and office supplies in the night of Monday to Tuesday. The two dates on the page do not agree.

Radio Okapi reported that since 13 August several health workers at Birambizo general referral hospital (Rutshuru) had been arrested by persons presented as AFC/M23 military cadres, in circumstances still to be clarified, among them the director of nursing care; according to a hospital agent, fearing further arrests several officials of the hospital had left the area, which contributed to disrupting the hospital's functioning and access to care for several days.

MediaCongo reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame reminded the African Union facilitators on Wednesday that Rwanda would maintain its posture as long as the root causes of the conflict are not resolved; the outlet wrote that by root causes he mainly alluded to the 'continuing presence' of the FDLR in eastern DRC, and that according to Kagame the FDLR represent a direct and existential security threat.
Imvaho Nshya, a Rwandan outlet, reported that AFC/M23 announced it had closed the airspace of Goma in order to stop DRC forces from continuing to use Goma airport to drop bombs on the population.
Al Jazeera reported that M23 announced the capture of Goma on Monday, which the DRC government described as a "declaration of war" by Rwanda.

BBC News reported that Corneille Nangaa, who heads an alliance of rebel groups that includes the M23, said their ultimate aim was to topple President Félix Tshisekedi's government and vowed to continue the offensive to Kinshasa.
BBC News reported that on Thursday Nangaa presented the rebels as the new administrators of Goma, telling journalists they were there to stay and would get services up and running again.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that the M23 installed a new North Kivu provincial administration with Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto, until then adviser to the M23 military coordinator, as governor, assisted by vice-governors Minani Ngarambe Willy and Amani Bahati Shadrack, and that the Alliance Fleuve Congo also announced other appointments including Julien Katembo as mayor of Goma.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that the new governor, speaking in Kinyarwanda, said he had identified three main threats to security: former prisoners released by the Congolese authorities as M23 fighters were about to enter Goma, the local militias known as the Wazalendo, and the Hutu FDLR.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that Corneille Nangaa, head of the Alliance Fleuve Congo, promised "une administration responsable qui doit rendre des comptes" (a responsible administration that must be accountable).

Al Jazeera reported that the AFC/M23 said in a statement posted on X that, in response to the humanitarian crisis it attributed to the regime in Kinshasa, it declared a ceasefire starting 4 February 2025 for humanitarian reasons; Al Jazeera added that there was no immediate comment from the DRC government.

Al Jazeera reported that a rebel alliance that includes M23 said, in a statement read on local radio on Monday, that it would assist the population of Bukavu who were "abandoned" by the army and allied combatants, and that its forces had been working to restore security.

place: Bukavu and Goma, North and South Kivu
statement: Al Jazeera reported that Erasto Bahati Musanga, the rebel-appointed governor of North Kivu, announced that ports in Bukavu and Goma would reopen on Tuesday.

DW reported that, after two explosions at an M23 rally in Bukavu, M23 accused the Congolese authorities of being behind the attack and said in a statement that it condemned "the criminal regime of Kinshasa, which just implemented its plan of exterminating civilian populations".
DW reported that Congo's president, Felix Tshisekedi, called the Bukavu rally attack "a heinous terrorist act".

The New Times (Rwanda) reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, president of M23, pointed an accusing finger at Burundi after the Bukavu rally explosions and said preliminary investigations indicated that the explosives belonged to the Burundian army.
The New Times reported that, according to the group's leader, the explosives at the AFC/M23 rally in Bukavu on 27 February killed at least 11 people and injured 65, six of them in critical condition.

place: Luanda (Angola); statement concerns North and South Kivu conflict
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, in a communiqué published on Monday, AFC/M23 announced it would not take part in the Luanda talks planned for Tuesday 18 March under Angolan mediation, denouncing individual European Union sanctions on several of its leaders.

Anadolu reported that the Alliance Fleuve Congo, a rebel alliance that includes M23, announced on Saturday that it was withdrawing from the town of Walikale and its surroundings, a few days after taking control of the area; Anadolu said residents saw rebel elements still in the town that afternoon.

Kivu Morning Post reported that Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson of AFC-M23, said on X that, contrary to the communiqué of Sunday 23 March 2025, the FARDC and their coalition forces had not withdrawn their attack drones from Walikale, delaying the repositioning of AFC/M23 forces.
Kivu Morning Post reported that the FARDC took note of the announced M23 withdrawal from Walikale and committed to avoiding any offensive action, calling on the Wazalendo to do the same.

Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 announced the break of its agreement with the SADC after violent clashes in Goma, accusing SAMIDRC regional forces, in coordination with the FARDC, of military operations including attacks on the night of 11 April 2025.

place: Doha (Qatar); concerns North and South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the DRC government delegates and the AFC/M23 rebellion, after talks in Doha under Qatari auspices, agreed to work towards a truce in view of an effective ceasefire, in a joint declaration made public on Wednesday 23 April 2025 and read on RTNC.

place: Place of statement not stated (concerns North and South Kivu)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23, led by Corneille Nangaa, said on Monday it took note of the agreement signed in Washington on 27 June between the DRC and Rwanda while expressing strong reservations and reaffirming demands for a more inclusive peace process.

KT Press (Rwanda) reported that Corneille Nangaa, political coordinator of AFC-M23, announced that the movement regretted the widespread violation of the ceasefire on all front lines by what he called the regime in Kinshasa, which he said trampled point II of the Declaration of Principles signed in Doha on 19 July 2025.

KT Press reported that, in a formal statement before the Q&A at a Goma media briefing, Nangaa accused Tshisekedi of tearing up the Doha peace agreement signed in July 2025 and of choosing war over dialogue, and said Kinshasa's coalition forces had launched fresh offensives across eastern Congo in violation of the ceasefire.

place: Doha (Qatar); applies to North Kivu and South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Congolese government and the AFC-M23 rebels signed on Tuesday 14 October 2025 in Doha, under Qatari mediation, a mechanism to monitor and verify the ceasefire in the provinces of North and South Kivu.

KT Press reported that AFC/M23 rejected French President Emmanuel Macron's announcement of the planned reopening of Goma International Airport, calling it "premature, disconnected from reality, and made without consultation", in a statement issued by Corneille Nangaa.

Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 announced in a communiqué that it would unilaterally withdraw its forces from the city of Uvira, presenting the decision as a confidence-building measure to support the Doha peace process; it said the withdrawal was conditional on security guarantees including demilitarisation, protection of civilians and deployment of a neutral force. BBC Gahuza reported Nangaa said M23 would withdraw at the request of United States mediation.

TRT Afrika, relaying Reuters, reported that M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma told Reuters on Wednesday that "we are ready to leave (Uvira), but our conditions have to be reviewed", adding that the citizens of Uvira needed protecting and that the city should be occupied by a neutral force; residents told Reuters the rebels had not withdrawn.

BBC News reported that M23 leader Bertrand Bisimwa said on Wednesday that the withdrawal from Uvira was "under way", with spokesman Willy Ngoma adding that this was "for the sake of peace", and that Bisimwa in a post on X urged mediators and international partners to ensure the city was protected from "reprisals, violence and remilitarisation".

TRT Afrika, relaying Reuters, reported that DRC Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya dismissed the announced M23 withdrawal from Uvira as a "diversion", alleging it was an attempt to relieve pressure on Rwanda; the page also says Rwanda's government spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

BBC News reported that Muyaya described the M23's decision to leave Uvira as a "positive sign" but said the government needed to confirm the situation on the ground, having earlier called for "vigilance" in response to the "alleged withdrawal".

Radio Elle FM Goma reported that the de facto governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto, launched a large reforestation operation in Goma on a Salongo day, saying "Nous avons trouvé une ville et un parc dévastés"; in the same report the outlet wrote that disorderly felling of trees by armed groups such as the FDLR and Mai-Mai militias had profoundly affected biodiversity.

Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa said in a recent statement that 'À ce jour, pas un seul prisonnier n’a été libéré, en violation flagrante des accords signés', accusing the Kinshasa government of blocking implementation of the Doha commitments.

place: AFC/M23-controlled areas, North and South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that Corneille Nangaa said that in the zones controlled by the AFC/M23 'la population vit désormais dans la paix, la dignité et la sécurité retrouvées', and accused the central government of promoting hate speech, saying 'Le discours de haine est désormais devenu une doctrine d’État'.

place: Kisangani, Tshopo (claimed target); statement on Minembwe and Hauts-Plateaux, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a statement posted on X on 3 February, Corneille Nangaa presented as a response to what he called an indiscriminate military campaign by the central government the AFC/M23's claimed operation against what it described as the Congolese army's drone command centre in Kisangani (Tshopo).

Kivu Morning Post reported that the Tshopo provincial authorities and the FARDC announced they had neutralised eight explosive-laden kamikaze drones in the night of 31 January to 1 February 2026, and that the Tshopo authorities accused the AFC/M23 of trying to target Bangoka airport.

place: Minembwe, Hauts-Plateaux, South Kivu and other localities named
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué reacting to an African Union Commission statement, the AFC/M23 said that since 22 January 2026 localities including Minembwe, Twangiza, Rwitsankuku, Katogota, Sange, Kalundu port, Masisi, Walikale, Rutshuru, Lubero, Mwenga and Kalehe had been targeted by 'huit à douze drones d’attaque pilotés par des mercenaires étrangers', that these strikes allegedly hit civilian targets including hospitals, schools and churches, and that its own drone-neutralisation operation caused no civilian loss.

place: Mikenge, Kakenge, Point Zero, Minembwe highlands, Fizi, South Kivu
statement: Anadolu reported that on Sunday the Congolese army said in a statement that AFC/M23 and its coalition had launched drone attacks on Saturday evening on its positions at Mikenge and Kakenge in South Kivu and on civilian areas at Point Zero, with a provisional toll of four civilians killed and eight injured, mostly women and children, while Anadolu noted there was no immediate reaction from Rwanda.

place: Point Zéro, Hauts Plateaux de Minembwe, Fizi, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC announced in a communiqué on Sunday 26 April that they had shot down on Saturday 25 April 2026 a UAV belonging to the Rwandan army, intercepted at Point Zéro in the Minembwe highlands, Fizi territory.

Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from Saturday 25 April to Sunday the Kinshasa regime's coalition forces carried out simultaneous, sustained bombardments at Gakenke, Mikenke and their surroundings in the Minembwe region, using kamikaze combat drones and KT-6 type drones, which the movement called a flagrant violation of the ceasefire.

place: Mushaki market, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, in a communiqué, the rebel movement's spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka gave a provisional toll of at least 21 civilians killed and more than 67 wounded, among them women and children, in drone strikes the rebellion blamed on government forces against the public market of Mushaki, and that the movement called the attack a serious violation of international humanitarian law.

Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to AFCM23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa, the Congolese army's drone attack on Mushaki, forty kilometres from Goma, killed 20 people and wounded about sixty civilians.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the Rwandan Minister of Foreign Affairs, Oliver Nduhungirehe, deplored in a statement the weekend before the silence of the international community and the UN mission in the DRC in the face of the 'crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo', speaking the day after the Congolese army drone attack on Mushaki.

BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka told Reuters he knew of no mass graves during the group's time in Uvira, and accused the DRC government of spreading propaganda aimed at damaging its image.

place: Kilomoni and Kavimvira, Uvira, South Kivu
statement: BBC Gahuza reported, citing Reuters, that two mass graves had been found in Uvira, and that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told reporters in Uvira that the graves were in the Kilomoni and Kavimvira areas, one holding 31 bodies and the other 141; BBC said it could not independently verify how the people died.

place: Minembwe commune: Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu, Rwitsankuku; Fizi/Mwenga highlands, South Kivu
statement: Umuryango reported that the AFC/M23 announced that fighting in the Minembwe commune, South Kivu, had ended after it said it had taken areas held by the FARDC and their allies, and said it had captured Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu and Rwitsankuku; the message was given by AFC/M23 deputy leader Bisimwa during a visit to the area.

Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa called on Burundian President and African Union chair Évariste Ndayishimiye to guarantee humanitarian access to the Minembwe highlands, denouncing what he called a 'blocus humanitaire' affecting the mostly Banyamulenge Tutsi zone.

place: Minembwe, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu (subject); statement in Goma
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that at a press conference in Goma on Wednesday 7 October 2026 the AFC/M23 accused the Congolese authorities of imposing a blockade on the people of Minembwe; Corneille Nangaa said they faced shortages of food, medicines and basic necessities and attributed the blockade to the Kinshasa regime and a coalition of FARDC, Burundian forces, FDLR, Wazalendo and mercenaries.

place: Mulima, on the route to Minembwe, Fizi, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that at the same press conference Corneille Nangaa said that in the night of 23 to 24 September a humanitarian convoy of UN and NGO organisations had been blocked at Mulima on its way to Minembwe, and that the convoy, headed by OCHA, ACTED and Médecins du Monde, was according to the AFC/M23 deliberately attacked by the Kinshasa coalition forces.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the vice-presidents of the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), Corneille Nangaa and Bertrand Bisimwa, presented the FRN's organisation in Goma on Wednesday 21 October, and that Nangaa set out an institutional architecture of four organs including a Collège des fondateurs of 20 members and a Conseil de la révolution of five members.

Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa condemned on Wednesday 19 August 2026 remarks by opposition politician Martin Fayulu about the Banyamulenge community, calling them 'irresponsables' and 'incendiaires', in a statement on X.

place: eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu)
statement: UN News reported that the UN Security Council unanimously adopted a resolution in which it demanded that the M23 immediately cease hostilities, withdraw from all areas it controls and fully reverse the establishment of illegitimate parallel administrations in DRC territory, and in which its 15 members called on the Rwanda Defence Forces to stop supporting the armed group and immediately withdraw from Congolese territory without preconditions.

UN News reported that in the same resolution the Security Council strongly condemned all attacks directed against civilians and infrastructure, including UN, humanitarian and medical personnel, and condemned summary executions and maiming, sexual and gender-based violence, human trafficking and the recruitment and use of children.

The Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs published a joint statement between Qatar, the DRC and Rwanda in which the Heads of State reaffirmed the commitment of all parties to an immediate and unconditional ceasefire as agreed at the EAC-SADC summit.
The African Union Peace and Security Council adopted a communiqué that unequivocally condemned the activities of M23 and its supporters, ADF, FDLR and other armed groups.
sources: African Union Peace and Security Council

statement: The African Union Peace and Security Council communiqué commended Angola's President João Manuel Lourenço, Chair of the ICGLR and AU Champion for Peace and Reconciliation, for mediating between the DRC and Rwanda and called on the two parties to return urgently to the Luanda Process.
sources: African Union Peace and Security Council

place: SADC (decision on the deployment in eastern DRC)
statement: The SADC communiqué of its Extraordinary Summit stated that the Summit terminated the mandate of SAMIDRC and directed the commencement of a phased withdrawal of SAMIDRC troops from the DRC.
SADC said in a press release that it had officially commenced the withdrawal of SAMIDRC from eastern DRC as of 29 April 2025, by road through Rwanda to the troop-contributing countries.

US Senior Advisor Massad Boulos said at a State Department digital press briefing that the US position was that Rwanda should cease all military support of M23 and withdraw all Rwandan troops from DRC territory.

UN News reported that Secretary-General António Guterres welcomed the peace agreement between the DRC and Rwanda signed on Friday in Washington, DC, and said in a statement that evening that the accord was a significant step towards de-escalation, peace and stability in the eastern DRC and the Great Lakes region.

UN News reported that MONUSCO head Bintou Keita told the Security Council that armed groups were not only seizing territory but attempting to install a parallel administration, recently appointing a governor and two vice-governors in Bukavu and financial and mining officials in North Kivu.

UN News reported that, at the Security Council meeting that renewed the MONUSCO mandate, the United States said negotiations were "yet again disrupted" by M23 advances "supported by the Rwanda Defence Forces", and Ambassador Jennifer Locetta said M23 must immediately withdraw at least 75km from Uvira and return to compliance with its obligations under the Framework Agreement.

UN News (French) reported that in its resolution renewing the MONUSCO mandate the Security Council strongly condemned the M23 offensive in South Kivu, carried out with the support of the Rwandan Defence Force, and demanded their immediate withdrawal from Congolese territory.

Actualite.cd reported, citing the final communiqué it received, that the African Union Peace and Security Council asked the group of facilitators to propose urgent measures to defuse the situation in eastern DRC and to report to the AU Mediator.

The Qatari foreign ministry said on 2 February 2026 that the DRC government and AFC/M23 had signed in Doha the terms of reference stemming from the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region, and that the two parties renewed their commitment to the ceasefire and the Doha Framework Agreement for Peace signed between them on November 15, 2025.

Actualite.cd reported that the DRC responded favourably to the Angolan proposal and officially accepted the principle of a ceasefire in the east, and that, according to the Presidency of the Republic, this acceptance of the ceasefire from 18 February was made "in a spirit of responsibility, appeasement and search for a peaceful solution to the conflict".

Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23, while not joining the Angolan scheme, which it says it does not recognise, also reaffirmed its commitment to implement, without delay and in good faith, the ceasefire mechanism agreed under the Doha process.

Actualite.cd reported that the senior US adviser for Africa, whom it called "Monsieur Afrique de l'administration Trump", wrote on X that, encouraged by the DRC's acceptance of Angola's ceasefire proposal, all parties must immediately cease hostilities, including drone attacks that continue to cost innocent civilians their lives, and that the priority is now to make the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism agreed in Doha operational.

Actualite.cd reported that the East African Community summit of heads of state held on Saturday 7 March 2026 in Arusha urged the African Union, in its final communiqué, to provide the financial and logistical resources needed for the AU-led mediation process on eastern DRC.

UN News reported that on Thursday Vivian van de Perre, MONUSCO Deputy Special Representative for protection and operations, told the Security Council that recent hostilities between the government and AFC/M23 were marked by growing use of offensive drones and continued GPS jamming and spoofing, and that a recent 'joint exploratory mission' to Uvira found that security guarantees and freedom of movement are indispensable before peacekeepers can be deployed.

A joint statement by the Government of the DRC and the AFC, together with the United States, Qatar, Togo as African Union mediator, the AU Commission and Switzerland, on talks in Montreux, Switzerland, said the Parties agreed to facilitate rapid, unimpeded, safe and sustained humanitarian access and freedom of movement for humanitarian personnel, goods and services, and agreed to refrain from any attack, destruction or removal of objects indispensable to the survival of the civilian population, including hospital and school facilities.

UN News reported that MONUSCO head James Swan told the Security Council that the security situation in the east remained highly unstable, with heavy fighting between AFC/M23, supported by Rwandan forces (as UN News wrote), and the FARDC allied with Wazalendo, and that clashes were mainly in Rubaya and around Rutshuru in North Kivu and in the high plains of South Kivu.

UN News reported that Swan said the use of offensive drones, artillery and heavy weapons had sharply increased risks to civilians and infrastructure, that AFC/M23 had partially withdrawn from some areas but continued to consolidate parallel administrative structures, and called for swift deployment of the ceasefire monitoring mechanism under the Doha process.

A joint statement by the governments taking part in the Sixth Joint Oversight Committee for the Peace Agreement between the DRC and Rwanda, published by the US State Department, said that the DRC updated on its work to neutralize the FDLR and Rwanda updated on the process of its disengagement of forces/lifting of defensive measures.

A joint statement by the representatives of the DRC Government and of the AFC, published by the US State Department after meetings in Switzerland, said the Parties developed a roadmap setting out sequenced steps and timelines for negotiations under the Doha Framework Agreement and agreed on the importance of a standardized method for reporting allegations of ceasefire violations.

A joint statement by the governments taking part in the sixth Joint Security Coordination Mechanism meeting in Geneva (DRC, Rwanda, US, Qatar, Togo as AU mediator, AU Commission), published by the US State Department, said the DRC and Rwanda agreed to advance two initiatives to strengthen monitoring and verification of Washington Accords implementation on the ground.

UN News reported, in its own account around a Security Council meeting, that fighting continued in the highlands of Mwenga, Fizi and Uvira in South Kivu, causing new displacement and hindering aid delivery, and that the first two missions of the ceasefire verification mechanism had gone to Minembwe (South Kivu) and then Masisi (North Kivu).

UN News reported that Néné Bintu Iragi, president of South Kivu civil society, told the Security Council that in territories controlled by AFC/M23 there were killings, arson, arbitrary detentions and 'collective punishments' and a parallel administration imposing taxes on the population.

UN News reported, in its account of an address by Deputy High Commissioner for Human Rights Awa Dabo to the UN Human Rights Council, that OHCHR documented at least 1.080 victims of conflict-related sexual violence across the country (a national figure) between June 2025 and May 2026, mainly women and children, that the real figures are probably much higher, and that armed groups were reportedly responsible for 74% of the victims recorded.

Actualite.cd reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, according to the outlet, said that a momentum had been interrupted because of Rwanda's expansionist aims expressed through the AFC/M23 rebellion in South Kivu, and the outlet added that he alluded to the rebels' occupation of Uvira and their announced withdrawal under US pressure, a withdrawal the outlet said Kinshasa disputed.

place: Masisi and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, despite the ceasefire announced for 18 February at noon, clashes continued in eastern DRC between the FARDC and AFC/M23; it said the truce had been proposed on 11 February by Angola after a meeting in Luanda, and that the DRC officially adhered to it while AFC/M23 had committed to an immediate halt to hostilities under the Doha process.

Reuters reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame said he agreed with the U.S. government on the need for a ceasefire in eastern Congo but gave no indication of bowing to calls for Rwandan troops and M23 rebels to withdraw from Goma.
CNN reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame, asked in an interview whether there were Rwandan troops inside the DRC, answered 'I don't know' and said Rwanda would do anything to protect itself.

Al Jazeera reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame, at a news conference in Kigali, said that the FDLR's presence in the DRC is Rwanda's main concern and that 'if this problem is not resolved, it is natural for Rwanda to remain involved' in the conflict; Al Jazeera added that Rwanda denies Kinshasa's allegations against it.
Al Jazeera reported that Kagame said Rwanda has information that Congolese authorities 'are arming the FDLR and integrating its members into their own forces'.

place: South Kivu, near the Rwandan border
statement: The Government of Rwanda said in a statement that responsibility for ceasefire violations, ongoing attacks and fighting in South Kivu cannot be placed on Rwanda, and condemned the FARDC and the Burundian army (FDNB), together with the FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries, which it said have been systematically bombing civilian villages close to the Rwandan border using fighter jets and attack drones.

place: Kamanyola, Walungu/Uvira area; Bugarama and Nyarushishi, Rwanda
statement: The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that, as a result of the past week's bombing of Kamanyola from Burundi, over 1000 Congolese citizens had fled across the border to Bugarama in western Rwanda, where they were accommodated at the Nyarushishi Transit Camp.

The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that the Burundian Army had amassed close to 20,000 troops in South Kivu in the service of the Government of DRC and had laid siege to Banyamulenge villages in Minembwe in a deliberate attempt to starve the residents.

The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that the DRC had openly stated it would not observe any ceasefire and was fighting to recapture territories lost to AFC/M23 even as the peace process unfolded, and that the DRC's failure to neutralize the FDLR as stipulated in the June 2025 Peace Agreement continued to delay the resolution of the conflict in eastern DRC.

The Government of Rwanda welcomed, in a statement carried on its foreign ministry's news listing, 'today's signing' of the Doha Framework for a Comprehensive Peace Agreement between the DRC Government and the AFC/M23.

Jeune Afrique published an interview with Rwandan President Paul Kagame under the headline quote 'N’attendez pas de moi que je lève nos mesures de défense alors que vous laissez Félix Tshisekedi faire ce qu’il veut' (Do not expect me to lift our defence measures while you let Félix Tshisekedi do what he wants).
DW reported that Rwandan army spokesperson Ronald Rwivanga said that five civilians were killed and 25 were wounded on the outskirts of the border town of Gisenyi.

Kigali Today (Rwandan outlet) reported that Minister Nduhungirehe, answering an RFI journalist, said 'Nta munsi n’umwe utambuka hatabayeho ibitero byo mu kirere bigabwe na Guverinoma ya Congo, ku birindiro bya AFC/M23' (not a day passes without air attacks by the Congolese Government on AFC/M23 positions), which he called a violation of the ceasefire agreements.

Taarifa (Rwandan outlet), in an article on remarks by Nduhungirehe, wrote that following the capture of Uvira by the M23 on 10 December 2025 (Taarifa's date), Rwandan and Burundian security officials held meetings at the shared border on 14 and 28 December to discuss confidence-building measures and de-escalation mechanisms; Taarifa narrates this sentence itself and attributes the surrounding remarks to Nduhungirehe.
The New Times (Rwandan state-aligned outlet) reported that President Kagame told EAC and SADC leaders that the ongoing war in eastern DR Congo was started by the Congolese government.

place: M23-held areas of North and South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that accusations of Rwandan involvement in the conflict in eastern DRC, supported by several international reports including those of the UN Group of Experts, are ones that Kigali continues to reject.

place: Munzenze Central Prison, Goma (gereza ya Munzenze), North Kivu
statement: The BBC reported, citing an internal UN document it had seen, that between 165 and 167 women were assaulted by male inmates during the jailbreak at Munzenze prison in Goma, and that the report states most of the women were killed after inmates set fire to the prison; the BBC said it could not verify the reports.

place: Munzenze Central Prison, Goma (gereza ya Munzenze), North Kivu
statement: The Guardian quoted Van de Perre, deputy head of the UN peacekeeping force based in Goma, as saying that there was a major prison breakout of 4,000 escaped prisoners, that a few hundred women were also in the prison, and that 'they were all raped and then they set fire to the women's wing'; the quoted passage does not say who 'they' were.

place: Munzenze Central Prison, Goma (gereza ya Munzenze), North Kivu
statement: UN News reported that the UN human rights chief said that according to judicial authorities at least 165 women prisoners were raped during the mass escape from Muzenze prison in Goma on 27 January, and that most of them were reportedly killed afterwards in a fire whose circumstances remain unclear.

place: Munzenze Central Prison, Goma (gereza ya Munzenze), North Kivu
statement: The OHCHR summary report of the fact-finding mission on North and South Kivu included satellite imagery of Munzenze Central Prison, Goma, captioned as showing its condition after a prison break and fire which killed the majority of the prison's 160 female inmates on 27 January 2025.

place: Munzenze Central Prison, Goma (gereza ya Munzenze), North Kivu
statement: BBC Gahuza reported that Délion Kimbulungu, secretary of AFC/M23, presenting a report of AFC/M23, said the events at Munzenze prison happened in the morning while M23 arrived in the evening, and that their investigation found the prison escape had begun a few days before M23 arrived; the BBC said it could not independently verify the claims of M23.
BBC Gahuza reported that the Kinshasa side said the M23 group had a role in what it called the 'amahano kuri gereza ya Munzenze' (the horror at Munzenze prison).

OHCHR's Fact-Finding Mission reported a pattern of widespread rape and other sexual violence, primarily against women and girls but also men, boys and LGBT individuals, by M23 during cordon-and-search operations, house-to-house searches and in detention, and by FARDC and Wazalendo during their retreat from the frontlines in January and February.
