The report of the OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission on North and South Kivu (A/HRC/60/80, submitted to the UN Human Rights Council) stated that a victim recounted M23 conducting house-to-house searches for FARDC soldiers in Katindo neighbourhood, Goma, and that she was gang-raped by three M23 members, together with her mother.

place: Residences and hotels occupied by M23, Goma area, North Kivu
statement: The report of the OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission on North and South Kivu (A/HRC/60/80, submitted to the UN Human Rights Council) stated that others, including girls, were abducted and held, sometimes for weeks, in residences and hotels occupied by M23 members, where they were subjected to repeated rape and other abuses.

place: M23 improvised detention facilities and private residences, North and South Kivu
statement: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that cases of sexual violence were also documented in detention: women, men, boys and LGBT individuals were subjected to gang rapes while detained in M23 improvised detention facilities or private residences.
The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that in North Kivu women and adolescent girls were subjected to gang rapes by retreating FARDC and Wazalendo.

The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that sources specifically identified members of the 'Guépard' and 'Satan II' FARDC units, deployed along the South Kivu frontline, as responsible for multiple incidents of sexual violence and looting.

The report of the OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission submitted to the UN Human Rights Council (A/HRC/60/80) stated that in mid-February violent clashes between retreating FARDC and local Wazalendo groups in Kamanyola and Uvira resulted in civilian casualties and facilitated the escape of a reported 770 inmates from Uvira prison on 19 February, including some the report describes as sentenced for 'war crimes and crimes against humanity'.

FIDH and other signatory organisations stated that reports indicate mass prison escapes at Muzenze prison in Goma, and also in Bukavu, Uvira and Kalehe in South Kivu and in Kalemie in Tanganyika province.

Amnesty International reported that, of 14 survivors of sexual violence from North and South Kivu it interviewed, eight said they were gang raped by M23 fighters, five said they were gang raped by Wazalendo fighters and one said she was gang raped by FARDC soldiers.

Amnesty International reported that all survivors of gang rape by M23 fighters said the perpetrators wore uniforms resembling M23's and spoke Kinyarwanda, and that these gang rapes took place between March and May 2025 when the fighters controlled Goma and Bukavu.

Amnesty International reported that in Rutshuru and Masisi territories in North Kivu, and in Kalehe territory in South Kivu, Wazalendo groups raped women and girls, including one woman gang raped in late March 2025.

place: Remeka, Katoyi sector, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing various sources in Katoyi sector, that a group of Wazalendo militiamen raped at least 11 women and a 13-year-old girl on Sunday 31 August in the locality of Remeka, Masisi territory, and that some victims were also publicly humiliated, stripped and forced to walk naked in the market.

place: Masisi territory, North Kivu (article concerns Ufamandu 1er area; exact locality of these two cases not given)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that a monitoring report shared among local leaders recorded two further cases of rape of minors on 2 September, in an article on abuses attributed to Wazalendo in Masisi territory.

place: Bukuba/Remeka health centre, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Bukuba/Remeka health centre in Masisi territory was among places looted, according to reports it cited, in an area where Wazalendo groups were said to dominate.

UN News reported that OHCHR identified a pattern of widespread sexual violence by members of the DRC armed forces and their Wazalendo allies as they withdrew from the front lines, and that the M23 armed group committed torture and ill-treatment, including sexual violence, against detainees.

The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) documented 39 cases of conflict-related sexual violence in April 2025 in North Kivu (21 cases), Ituri (16) and South Kivu (two), affecting 64 victims in total, 20 of them minors.
UN News reported that the UN human rights chief, M. Turk, said that in Goma on 27 January two hospitals were bombed, killing and wounding several patients, including women and children.

MSF International President Dr Javid Abdelmoneim told the UN Security Council on 12 December 2025 that in the first six months of 2025 nearly 28,000 survivors of sexual violence sought care in MSF-supported facilities in eastern DRC, an average of 155 a day, and that three out of four attacks were committed by armed individuals.

place: Kazinga health centre, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: MSF told the UN Security Council that in Masisi, two weeks earlier, the Kazinga health centre, clearly marked with MSF insignia, was looted and destroyed by a Wazalendo militia, and that three MSF colleagues had been killed that year.
MSF told the UN Security Council that ambulances had been stopped at gunpoint and armed actors had stormed medical facilities, threatening patients and staff.

Human Rights Watch said that the humanitarian situation in Uvira and its vicinity was dire and that hospitals and health centers had been overwhelmed at a time when humanitarian assistance had dropped because of lack of access and funding shortfalls.

Human Rights Watch said that on 8 September Congolese military forces opened fire on protesters in Uvira, killing an 8-year-old boy and wounding at least nine civilians, including an 11-year-old girl.

place: Outskirts of Uvira (périphérie d’Uvira), Uvira, South Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch reported that a woman told it she was assaulted on 3 January 2026 while collecting food in her fields on the outskirts of Uvira, and that she met an M23 fighter and a Rwandan soldier; HRW also reported that after the rape she suffered severe bleeding and was ill.

Human Rights Watch reported that a woman who said she was raped on the outskirts of Uvira explained that, during the M23 occupation of Uvira, hospitals did not provide treatment for sexual violence, and that she could not obtain a PEP kit during the critical 72 hours following a rape.

Human Rights Watch reported that on 1 January 2026, during New Year celebrations, the M23 detained seven men and a woman, and also took away a 16-year-old boy who was with two friends near the "Parking" military base in Kavimvira quarter.

place: M23-controlled areas of North and South Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch said that the M23's control over much of North and South Kivu has significantly hampered the delivery of humanitarian aid, with the major airports in both provincial capitals closed since early 2025 and other restrictions on access and movement.

Ouragan.cd reported that in a communiqué made public on Thursday 22 January the Congolese government denounced a "partial and truncated" interpretation of events by Human Rights Watch, and that Muyaya said no death or injury had been recorded within the Banyamulenge community since the withdrawal of the Rwandan troops.

Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23, in a clarification of Friday 15 May by its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, questioned the credibility, impartiality and objectivity of the Human Rights Watch report on Uvira, said its withdrawal from Uvira took place in broad daylight and calmly, and attributed the abuses in Uvira to a government coalition of FARDC, FNDB, FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries.

Actualite.cd reported, citing a Human Rights Watch communiqué of 22 May, that HRW said it had asked in April for a meeting with Rwandan President Paul Kagame to discuss abuses by the Rwandan army and the M23 in eastern Congo and had received no response.

The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) reported that during the first half of 2026 it documented 267 cases of sexual violence in the conflict provinces, affecting 401 victims (282 women, 113 children, 5 men and one person of unknown sex and age).

BCNUDH reported that in the first half of 2026 armed groups were attributed 148 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 259 victims (M23 133 victims, Wazalendo 66, ADF 15, APCLS 11) and state agents 116 cases affecting 130 victims (FARDC 130 victims, PNC 6; as printed, the FARDC and PNC figures together exceed the State-agent total).

BCNUDH reported that on 11 June 2026, at night, Wazalendo burst into a home in Mudaka, Kabare territory, South Kivu, where a woman and her daughter were; both were abducted and taken into the bush, where they were raped in turn by their captors.

place: Nyalu- gushwa (as printed; Nyalugushwa), Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: BCNUDH reported that on 10 June 2026 a 12-year-old girl was raped by a Wazalendo element at Nyalugushwa, Kalehe territory, and that after the rape the alleged perpetrator killed her by strangulation and threw her body into the Nyabarongo river.

BCNUDH reported that in the first half of 2026 it documented 31 violations of international humanitarian law, including one attack on a school, 10 attacks on hospitals, 17 attacks on protected persons and three attacks on protected sites, with State agents responsible for five and armed groups for 26.

place: Mikenge (Minembwe hauts plateaux), Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: BCNUDH reported that on 20 May 2026, during armed clashes between AFC/M23 elements and loyalist forces, the hospital of Mikenge was hit by a bombardment attributed to AFC/M23 elements, and that according to sources several wounded and sick FARDC soldiers who were there were reportedly killed.

place: Kalingi and Mikenge, Minembwe hauts plateaux, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Africa-Infos.cd reported that in its press communiqué n°13 of 20 May 2026 the FARDC denounced attacks attributed to a coalition of the RDF and the AFC/M23 in several localities of Minembwe, said that several drone strikes targeted Kalingi and Mikenge in the Minembwe highlands from the first hours of the morning, and said that the Mikenge General Hospital was reportedly "intentionally targeted" and then completely destroyed.

place: Masisi-centre (Mont Ngaliema quarter), Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: BCNUDH reported that on 2 January 2026 three women, two men, a girl and a boy were killed and 42 others wounded in Masisi-centre, North Kivu, by shells presumed to have been dropped by drone by the FARDC, exploding in a residential quarter; Actualite.cd reported that, according to available information, a Congolese army drone targeted AFC/M23 positions in the Mont Ngaliema quarter of Masisi-centre, and that a provisional toll gave four civilians dead and seven wounded.

Actualite.cd reported that the Bitale agglomeration came under the control of AFC/M23 rebels on the morning of Monday 15 June 2026, after two days of intense fighting against the FARDC and Wazalendo militiamen.

place: Mwenga–Kamituga axis, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that Wazalendo militiamen targeted a convoy of agents on a mission on the Mwenga – Kamituga axis in South Kivu; it quoted MSF as saying that on 1 May an MSF team travelling to Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu to assess humanitarian needs faced a security incident, and that all its staff were safe and continuing their planned activities in Mwenga.

BCNUDH reported that in January 2026 it documented at least 46 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 61 victims (39 women, 21 girls and one man), 59 per cent fewer than the 147 victims documented in December 2025, which it explained mainly by intensified fighting and insecurity that limited humanitarian access to victims and led to under-documentation.

place: Eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu concentrate about 80% of documented victims)
statement: ReliefWeb, republishing a MONUSCO item, reported that BCNUDH said in a press release that 887 cases of conflict-related sexual violence were documented last year, affecting 1 534 victims (854 women and 672 girls), that North and South Kivu concentrate nearly 80 per cent of documented victims, that armed groups are responsible for 75 per cent of victims, with M23 first with 439 victims, and that FARDC, PNC and ANR members were involved in 19 per cent of documented cases.

place: Eastern DRC (North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri)
statement: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC reported in its final report that AFC/M23 was the leading perpetrator of conflict-related sexual violence according to cases documented and verified by the United Nations, and that humanitarian actors recorded a dramatic increase in such cases since 2024, disproportionately affecting women and girls.

place: North Kivu (AFC/M23-run provincial health department, Goma)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that it reviewed a document dated 11 February 2026, entitled "Note Explicative", that AFC/M23 distributed to multiple humanitarian actors involved in health care; that following its distribution the AFC/M23-run Provincial Health Inspection Department (IPS) initiated a series of inspections of humanitarian actors' premises; that IPS inspectors requested aggregate data on sexual violence incidents, access to confidential patient files containing names of victims, and consumption records for supplies such as PEP kits and dignity kits; and that some humanitarian actors were ordered to cease distributing dignity kits.

place: North Kivu (meeting between AFC/M23 and humanitarian actors, late March 2026)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that at a joint meeting in late March 2026 between humanitarian actors and AFC/M23, attended by AFC/M23 officials including Colonel John Imani Nzenze, AFC/M23 Director of Intelligence and liaison with humanitarian actors, and Ms. Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete, Special Adviser on Gender, Family and Children, Education, and Social and Humanitarian Affairs, AFC/M23 reprimanded humanitarian actors and accused them of inventing data, affirmed that it did not tolerate sexual violence and criticised the lack of perpetrator data in patient files; further meetings in late March and April 2026 resulted in an agreement that only aggregate data on sexual violence would be shared.

place: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu (Mudugudu base)
statement: Amnesty International said that the two sexual violence survivors it interviewed about abuses by CMC-FDP fighters in Rutshuru territory were held in conditions that amount to sexual slavery.

place: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Amnesty International reported that CMC-FDP said it "categorically rejects" the allegations that its fighters raped, sexually enslaved or forced women to "marry" its commanders, and that no complaints, official reports or referrals had been brought to the attention of its internal disciplinary or judicial bodies regarding the incidents.

place: Rubaya coltan mine area (Masisi, North Kivu) and Lomera gold mine (Kabare, South Kivu)
statement: Amnesty International reported that, in research into M23 abuses at the Rubaya and Lomera mines, it documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners by M23 or their collaborators, at least nine of whom were beaten brutally and died at health centres or before they reached the hospital; Amnesty said it wrote to the M23 spokesperson and an M23 mining representative on 11 August 2026 and had received no response at the time of publication.

Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23, in a clarification dated 22 September signed by Bertrand Bisimwa, "formally and in their entirety" rejected the accusations in Amnesty International's report on abuses at mining sites in areas under its control, calling them "not established and insufficiently substantiated".

place: AFC/M23-controlled areas of North Kivu and South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that UN independent experts, in a communiqué published on 21 July in Geneva, denounced serious and systematic violations against civilians; according to Radio Okapi, the experts said AFC/M23 had reportedly set up a system of control based on fear in the areas it administers, and the communiqué reported arbitrary arrests and detentions, acts of torture including sexual violence, and cases of forced labour and forced recruitment of civilians.

place: Rumangabo and Tshanzu, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu; Goma; Bukavu
statement: Human Rights Watch reported, based on interviews with 102 former detainees and dozens of other sources, that the M23 detained thousands of captured fighters and civilians, some as young as 12, and that the M23's apparent aim of taking security measures to locate soldiers, militiamen and officials opposed to it gradually turned into a vast, systematic campaign of mass arrests and incommunicado detention targeting civilians with real or perceived links to the army, in particular young men and adolescents.

Human Rights Watch reported that, according to several witnesses, M23 captain Gaston executed a certain colonel Amurabi at Rumangabo around June 2025, and that Amurabi was a defence lawyer in the military justice system in Goma according to a former detainee and Congolese judicial and military intelligence sources.

BCNUDH reported that of the 2 607 violations and abuses documented in the first half of 2026, 78 per cent (2,068) were committed by armed groups, 20 per cent (536) by State agents and 25 by foreign armed forces, and that AFC/M23 remained the main perpetrator among armed groups, followed by the Wazalendo groups.

Radio Okapi reported that the NGO "Rien sans les femmes" raised the alarm over rising rape cases against women and girls in Lubero-centre, Lubero territory, North Kivu, and that more than 250 rape cases had been documented in local hospitals since the start of 2025, according to Bernadette Kurabe, the organisation's focal point. Radio Okapi's report gave 253 cases between January and April 2025; the source does not attribute the cases to a perpetrator.

place: Njingala, Mafombi, Mubi, Logu and Makana villages (Walikale-Kisangani axis), Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that a local human rights NGO based in Walikale-centre said at least about thirty cases of sexual violence were recorded among displaced people in the villages of Njingala, Mafombi, Mubi, Logu and Makana between 17 and 23 March, and that in Makana two young girls who allegedly resisted attempted rape were shot dead at point-blank range by their armed attackers. Radio Okapi said the displaced had fled Walikale-centre since its occupation by rebel forces on 17 March. According to the head of the NGO, rape victims were referred to the health centres of Ndjingala and Bisie, which are struggling to meet needs for lack of medicines and because of the massive influx of displaced people.

place: Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru) and Bahunde chiefdom (Masisi), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting between AFC-M23 rebels and the FARDC took place in the Bwito (Rutshuru territory) and Bahunde (Masisi territory) chiefdoms of North Kivu between 28 September and 8 October 2025, and that, according to civil society, the fighting caused at least 4 deaths, 13 disappearances and the rape of 8 women.

place: Muliki health centre, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the fighting between AFC-M23 and the FARDC in the Bwito and Bahunde chiefdoms between 28 September and 8 October 2025 also caused heavy material damage: several dozen houses were burned, including the Nyabiteja primary school in the Kihondo grouping, and the health centre of Muliki was also looted, along with the theft of about twenty cattle. The source does not say who looted the health centre.

place: Masisi, Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
statement: CSDF, a Congolese women's health and rights organisation, said that June 2025 marked a notable deterioration in the security and human rights situation in Masisi, Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories; that, according to protection monitoring data covering 22 health zones, 842 violations were documented; that serious incidents rose by more than 35 per cent compared with May, with Masisi alone accounting for 50 per cent of the cases, followed by Nyiragongo (21 per cent) and Rutshuru (12 per cent); and that June 2025 was the annual peak of gender-based violence, with 247 documented cases (17 per cent of all violations of the month), of which 93 per cent were rapes.

UNFPA said in a statement in February 2025 that nearly 500 cases of sexual violence were reported within a single week in the Goma area, including more than 150 involving children, and that this number likely represents only a fraction of the actual survivors, namely those who managed to reach care.

place: Goma and displacement camps around Goma, North Kivu
statement: UNFPA said in a statement in February 2025 that its eight UNFPA-supported mobile clinics, safe spaces and listening centers were only partially functional, that the other facilities providing treatment and counselling to survivors in displacement camps had been looted, that medical supplies and equipment worth millions of dollars had been looted from storage facilities in Goma, and that Goma, with more than 2 million inhabitants, had only three functioning hospitals able to provide clinical care to survivors of sexual assault.

place: Goma and Saké (Masisi territory), North Kivu
statement: MSF said that between January and April 2025 more than 7,400 victims and survivors of sexual violence received treatment at Ministry of Health facilities supported by MSF in Goma, and that an additional 2,400 were treated in Saké during the same period.

place: Goma area (Rusayo displaced persons camp and a school courtyard), North Kivu
statement: MSF said that in February 2025 the M23/AFC armed group ordered the dismantling of displacement camps, effectively forcing their residents to leave, and quoted a patient it called Nasha (MSF says patients' names have been changed), who said that after the Rusayo displaced persons camp was destroyed she moved to the courtyard of a school, where armed men broke in one evening at 10:30 pm, attacked her and shot her husband dead when he tried to protect her.

The BBC reported that a 22-year-old woman, Pascaline, said she was raped by two men at Munzenze prison in Goma in the early hours of 27 January, and that her attackers came over the wall from the men's block right next door called "Safina"; a second woman, Nadine, 22, said she was also raped by two men. The BBC said it could not verify how many women were raped that night, out of a total of 167 who, sources say, were being held, and reported that 132 female prisoners and at least 25 children burned to death, according to two sources.

The BBC reported that a survivor who does not want to be identified, whom the BBC calls Florence (a name the BBC gave her), said that in this case the attackers at Munzenze prison were fellow inmates, who were not armed or in uniform; the BBC noted that the fire and the rapes are "shrouded in confusion, with all sides eager to blame someone else".

Actualite.cd reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), in its report on the main trends of human rights violations in the DRC for the month of January, recorded in North Kivu eight victims of conflict-related sexual violence, of whom three were attributed to M23 members, three to the FDLR and two to the FARDC.

place: Goma and a nearby camp, North Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch reported, from a survivor account, that in February, after the M23 took control of Goma, four M23 fighters forced their way into the house of a 22-year-old woman called Patience (a pseudonym, per HRW), tied her to her bed and two of them raped her; HRW said the fighters then forced her out of the house and took her to a nearby camp, where for three days multiple fighters raped her and three other women who had been taken there.

place: Goma and an M23 camp near the city, North Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch reported that M23 fighters abducted a woman it called Justine (a pseudonym, per HRW) from her home in Goma in March 2025 during an apparent forced recruitment operation, beat her and her 20-year-old son and forced her to walk to their camp near the city, where two men took her to a secluded area, beat her and raped her; HRW said she arrived at the hospital within 72 hours but the hospital had no PEP kits.

Human Rights Watch reported that, according to UNFPA, in May 2025 only 7 of 34 health zones in North Kivu had a minimal supply of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) kits, and that by September only 895 complete kits were available for the entire province, where hundreds of cases occur each week; HRW also said IMA World Health had ordered 116,000 kits in early 2025 but the funding was withdrawn so the kits never made it to health centres in eastern Congo.

place: Kalungu, Buzi grouping, Kalehe territory (South of Minova), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing humanitarian sources, that five young girls of the same family were raped by armed men in the locality of Kalungu, 15 km south of Minova in Buzi grouping, and were treated at a local hospital centre.

place: Bihovu, Shanje, Lowa-Numbi village, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that at Bihovu, in Lowa-Numbi village (Shanje), two women were also victims of rape on 14 January.

place: Bukavu (verdict); offences in Kalehe, Kabare and Walungu territories, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that a court in Bukavu, which it calls the 'tribunal de grande instance' (a civil-party lawyer quoted in the article thanks the Bukavu 'tribunal militaire de garnison'), sentenced to death on Friday 14 February 2025 212 soldiers accused of murder, attempted murder, rape and fleeing the enemy, for acts committed during the M23 advance in localities and villages of Kalehe, Kabare and Walungu territories.

place: Katana, Kabamba, Miti, Kasheke to Kamanyola, Kabare and Walungu territories, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that from 6 to 8 February 2025, acts of vandalism and killings were committed by soldiers deployed in the villages of Katana, Kabamba, Miti and Kasheke as far as Kamanyola.

The UN fact-finding mission report said that civil-society organisations reported more than 1 000 victims of sexual violence in South Kivu between January and June, mainly women and adolescent girls, while official sources reported 127 cases of sexual violence in South Kivu in the first two weeks of February alone.

The UN fact-finding mission report said that in South Kivu a man was stripped completely naked, beaten until he lost consciousness, and raped by several members of the FARDC and Wazalendo who were going from house to house looting.

place: Goma, Bukavu and Kabare prisons (North and South Kivu)
statement: The UN fact-finding mission report said that, according to the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), 199 people convicted of sexual and gender-based crimes escaped from the prisons of Goma, Bukavu and Kabare.

place: Bukavu central prison and Kabare prison, South Kivu
statement: The UN fact-finding mission report said that on 14 February two further prison escapes, in Bukavu and in Kabare, allowed detainees to flee, some of them convicted of crimes under international law; a footnote cites BCNUDH figures of 2 285 detainees escaping from Bukavu central prison and 221 from Kabare prison.

The UN fact-finding mission report said that from 15 to 17 February 2025 soldiers of the FARDC units Guépard and Satan II summarily executed at least 20 civilians in Kamanyola after hundreds of their soldiers died in clashes with the Wazalendo; it said most victims were men and adolescents suspected of being Wazalendo members or supporters, and that according to credible sources the number of victims would be much higher, although further investigation would be needed to confirm it.

place: South Kivu (locality not given in the sentence)
statement: The UN fact-finding mission report said girls were victims of sexual violence and were used for sexual purposes by commanders and other members of armed groups, and as cooks or messengers; the sentence sits in its section on the recruitment and use of children (which opens on Wazalendo groups), in a paragraph (para. 61) that otherwise describes boys apparently under 18 at Wazalendo checkpoints in South Kivu, patrolling in Uvira and carrying weapons in Fizi territory. The sentence itself names no group.

place: Walungu hospital, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: The UN fact-finding mission report said that on 9 March a shell reportedly hit the paediatric ward of Walungu hospital, killing five people, including two children.

place: FSKI hospital, Walungu centre, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that at least five people hospitalised at the Fonds social du Kivu (FSKI) hospital in Walungu died on Sunday, a day the article prints as '9 janvier' (9 January) although it was published in March, after a shell hit the roof of the paediatric ward; it said several sources in Walungu said the shell was fired by the M23 rebels, who it said were occupying the administrative centre of Walungu territory.

The Congolese National Human Rights Commission (CNDH-RDC) reported that on 19 April 2025 Pascaline NGWASI, coordinator of the Association des Mères Célibataires pour le Bien-être des Enfants Abandonnés, was arrested, beaten and raped by M23/AFC members in the Mabenga neighbourhood of Bukavu.
sources: Commission nationale des droits de l'homme

place: Mushenyi hospital, South Kivu (the CNDH files the case under the heading 'KALEHE'; territory otherwise not stated)
statement: The CNDH-RDC reported, in a section on violations of the right to health, that on Friday 2 May 2025 five decomposing bodies of Wazalendo members were found who had been abducted on 24 April 2025 by M23/AFC-RDF rebels from the hospital of Mushenyi, where they were being treated for gunshot wounds after the fighting at Nyanfunze, towards Kaziba; it named the five.
sources: Commission nationale des droits de l'homme

place: Kakaba-Bushwege village, Mushenyi sector, South Kivu
statement: The CNDH-RDC reported that on 23 April 2025 AFC/M23 elements perpetrated what it calls a 'massacre' in the village of Kakaba-Bushwege (Mushenyi sector), summarily executing five civilians and wounding several others after, it said, mistaking villagers wearing traditional boots called 'GODIO' for Wazalendo; it named three victims and two young boys of the Chibwana family.
sources: Commission nationale des droits de l'homme

place: Muku, Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: The CNDH-RDC reported that on Monday 30 June 2025 M23 soldiers entered the locality of Muku, Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, and killed 6 civilians in reprisal for the alleged presence of Wazalendo in the area under their control; a caption names one victim, Francis, from Kalebero.
sources: Commission nationale des droits de l'homme

statement: The CNDH-RDC reported that on Sunday 29 June 2025 M23 soldiers killed 4 civilians in the locality of Kaniola (Walungu territory) and set fire to several civilians' houses.
sources: Commission nationale des droits de l'homme

place: Kavimvira neighbourhood, avenue Nyagaa, Uvira, South Kivu
statement: The CNDH-RDC reported that on 23 May 2025 the lifeless body of Pascal KILOZO was found in the Kavimvira neighbourhood of Uvira, on the shore of Lake Tanganyika; it said the circumstances of death were unknown but raised concern about a possible extrajudicial execution or murder.
sources: Commission nationale des droits de l'homme

statement: The CNDH-RDC reported that during the night of 4 to 5 April 2025 a child musician was killed in Bukavu by elements identified as belonging to M23-AFC; it said several consistent testimonies suggested the child had recently performed a song about freedom.
sources: Commission nationale des droits de l'homme

statement: The CNDH-RDC report said that the Council of Ministers of 28 February 2025, in its record, established for South Kivu that up to 27 February 2025 the city of Bukavu had recorded more than 1.130 wounded, more than 29 deaths in care establishments and 16 people who died at the rally.
sources: Commission nationale des droits de l'homme

place: Irambo Health Center, Bukavu, South Kivu
statement: UM News reported that during an attack by armed men on the night of March 18 on the United Methodist Irambo Health Center in Bukavu, a nurse was sexually assaulted and another beaten, according to the centre's medical director Dr Jimmy Kasongo; medicine and money were also stolen.

place: Irambo Health Center, Bukavu, South Kivu
statement: UM News reported that gunmen looted the medicine supplies of the United Methodist Irambo Health Center in Bukavu during an attack on the night of March 18, with more than $4,500 dollars and 789,200 Congolese francs also stolen, and that pharmacist Sandra Bontamba said the attack came 24 hours after the hospital had received essential medicines.

place: Bukavu (general hospital) and near Katana, South Kivu
statement: The Guardian reported that patients at hospitals in Bukavu described sustaining serious injuries during the chaotic withdrawal of the Congolese army and its allies in the days before M23 rebels marched in: Priscilla Nabintu, 22, said a bullet hit her [in the shin] as she lay on her bed at home near Katana; Ghislaine Ntakwinja, 41, said unidentified gunmen shot her in her right hand in her house; and Mugisho Shalukoma, 20, was recovering from a leg amputation, the result of gunshot wounds. Esperance Mwamini Birindwa, an ICRC nurse, said 162 people had been admitted with injuries related to the M23 takeover between 14 and 24 February.

place: Eastern DRC (ICRC operations; place not stated)
statement: The Guardian quoted ICRC project manager Emmanuel Konin as saying that, despite all efforts, evacuations sometimes take longer than expected because of access difficulties and that some patients whose lives could have been saved had died of their injuries.

place: Kavumu village, about 30 km north of Bukavu, South Kivu
statement: DW reported that a woman it called Riziki (not her real name) said that three soldiers broke into her house to loot and that one of them came into her bedroom to rape her but she resisted; DW said the crime took place in February in Kavumu village, about 30 km north of Bukavu.

place: Kalehe and Uvira regions, South Kivu
statement: DW reported that in South Kivu MSF had assisted almost 700 people in the Kalehe and Uvira regions since the start of 2025, and that according to MSF's report the vast majority of attacks reported by victims in 2025 were committed at gunpoint, with perpetrators remaining unaccountable.

Christianity Today reported that on a recent visit to Panzi Hospital in Bukavu, 185 of its 450 patients were receiving treatment for sexual violence, and that after the rebels captured Bukavu in February the hospital remained operational in the following weeks, treating injuries and gunshot wounds and delivering 110 babies.

place: Bukavu, Kabare and Uvira prisons, South Kivu
statement: The Global Protection Cluster's March 2025 protection update said that further mass prison escapes from Bukavu, Kabare and Uvira followed during the offensive towards the South Kivu capital, and that some escapees had been convicted or were suspected of serious human rights violations, including sexual and gender-based crimes.

The UNFPA situation report covering April 2025 said that in Minova, South Kivu, activities were still paused due to limited access, though implementing partners were prepared to resume operations as soon as the situation improved.

The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing (its letter of 5 June 2026) the FDLR was fragmented into three principal factions, FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-Force de protection du peuple (FPP), and that all three had recently adopted alternative designations to obscure their FDLR affiliation.

The UN Group of Experts reported that "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and "General" Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) remained FDLR-FOCA military commander and political leader respectively; it named "Brigadier-General" Emmanuel Nsengiyumva as overall FDLR-RUD leader and "Colonel" Dan Hategekimana as FDLR-FPP leader.

place: Bwisha and Bwito chefferies; Jomba, Binza, Busanza, Bukoma, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that the traditional FDLR-RUD area of operations was in the Bwisha and Bwito chefferies, Rutshuru territory, and that at the time of drafting FDLR-RUD units were particularly active in Jomba, Binza, Busanza and Bukoma, overlapping with the FDLR-FPP area in Rutshuru territory.

place: Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru, Walikale (North Kivu); outskirts of Goma
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR-FOCA, the largest FDLR faction, remained active on several major front lines in North Kivu, notably in Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale territories, and that its special unit, the Commando de recherche et d'action en profondeur (CRAP), was reported to have active units on the outskirts of Goma and infiltrated in Goma town.

The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR sources claimed the group's overall strength exceeded 10,000 combatants, while United Nations and intelligence sources estimated total FDLR strength at between 3,500 and 4,500 combatants.

The UN Group of Experts reported that since April 2025 RDF units had led joint operations with AFC/M23 aimed at neutralizing the FDLR, and that RDF and AFC/M23 systematically destroyed and burned civilian settlements inhabited by members of FDLR, their families or alleged supporters.

place: Burambo, Kiyeye, Mayi ya Chumvi, Ngeri, Kiganda (Rutshuru territory per the report context)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported, citing United Nations sources, that on 30 May 2025 AFC/M23 ordered the evacuation of over 240 households from five villages (Burambo, Kiyeye, Mayi ya Chumvi, Ngeri and Kiganda), leading to mass displacement of civilians.

place: Masisi, Rutshuru, Nyiragongo, Walikale territories and outskirts of Goma (North Kivu)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that since June 2025 VDP/Wazalendo units, often operating jointly with FDLR, had conducted incursions and ambushes against AFC/M23 and RDF, either to recapture strategic positions or to disrupt their advances and supply lines.

place: Bibwe, Mpeti, Minjenje (northern Masisi / Walikale, North Kivu)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that between mid- to late September and October 2025 FARDC increased air strikes, notably in Bibwe, Mpeti and Minjenje between 19 and 21 September, relying on VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR elements to conduct asymmetric ground operations.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the DRC expressed its commitment to neutralizing the FDLR, publicly stated that it did not support the FDLR and called on FDLR combatants to disarm and surrender.

place: AFC/M23- and RDF-controlled areas of North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that the bulk of FDLR forces operated in areas controlled by AFC/M23 and RDF, beyond the operational reach of the FARDC, affecting the latter's ability to neutralize FDLR elements that refused to surrender.

Congolese media reported that on Friday 10 October 2025 the FARDC issued a communiqué, signed by army spokesperson Major General Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, calling on all FDLR factions to lay down their arms and warning that in case of refusal the FARDC would proceed to disarmament by constraint or by force; the UN Group of Experts likewise reported that FARDC issued a communiqué on 10 October 2025 calling on FDLR to disarm and surrender, warning of forced disarmament.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the FARDC announcement triggered tensions between FARDC and FDLR and between FARDC and certain Wazalendo factions, and that subsequently some FARDC officers and government actors sought to reassure FDLR of their continued cooperation, given the essential role of FDLR in ongoing operations on the ground.

Actualite.cd reported that DRC Minister of Regional Integration Floribert Anzuluni confirmed at a press briefing in Kinshasa on Tuesday 28 July that the FDLR had signed a protocol of demilitarisation, demobilisation and cantonment.

Afrikarabia reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe considered the DRC's announcement of an FDLR surrender protocol a 'grossière manipulation' that is in no way consistent with the Washington accords.

Afrikarabia reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo, on X, rejected a 'protocole négocié avec une milice génocidaire que le gouvernement de la RDC continue d'armer et de soutenir' and said the FDLR remain integrated in the Congolese army and active on the front lines.

place: Nyiragongo volcano area and Virunga National Park (North Kivu)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that key FDLR commanders and combatants were compelled to relocate to localities in Rutshuru, Masisi and Nyiragongo territories, and that FDLR military commander and sanctioned individual "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawunguka (alias Omega) and other key leaders, fearing RDF attacks, withdrew to the vicinity of the Nyiragongo volcano and inside Virunga National Park.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 1 March 2025 AFC/M23 transferred several FDLR captives to the Government of Rwanda, including 'Brigadier-General' Ezechiel Gakwerere; according to AFC/M23 they had been arrested during their raid on Goma, while the Group itself reported that most, including Gakwerere, were arrested during armed operations targeting hospitals, and it records 'controversies around his arrest and transfer' in an annex.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 4 January 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF took control of Masisi centre and retained it despite repeated attempts by Wazalendo, FDLR, the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and FARDC to retake it.

The UN Group of Experts reported that about two weeks later AFC/M23 and RDF captured Minova town in Kalehe Territory, South Kivu, and that the 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops based in Minova retreated before their arrival, leaving behind significant quantities of military equipment.

place: Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 the majority of 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops were positioned in South Kivu, notably in the Ruzizi Plain along the tri-border area and in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that heavy clashes between FDNB (supported by FARDC and Wazalendo) and AFC/M23 (supported by RDF) resulted in several hundreds of FDNB casualties.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in February 2025 the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced Burundi's readiness to fight back; it also reported that in mid-March the two countries agreed on verbal and military de-escalation, reportedly concluding a non-aggression agreement.

The UN Group of Experts reported that during more than a month of controlling Uvira, AFC/M23 forced the withdrawal of FDNB, captured large FARDC bases and dominated the entire Ruzizi plain along the Burundian border, and that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 following sustained international diplomatic pressure.

place: From Uvira towards Minembwe, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 FARDC, with support from Wazalendo, FDNB and private military contractors, launched an offensive from Uvira towards Minembwe against MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23, who had reinforced MRDP/Twirwaneho in August 2025 and February 2026.

place: Point Zero, Kanguli, Tuwe-Tuwe, Mwenga-Fizi road, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 the AFC/M23 coalition, including Twirwaneho combatants, temporarily seized Point Zero, Kanguli and Tuwe-Tuwe along the Mwenga-Fizi road, and that FARDC-FDNB forces regained these positions on 29 January.

place: Uvira axis, Ruzizi Plain, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that several Wazalendo factions carried out joint operations with FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain; for example FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux.

The UN Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments; the Group stated it did not substantiate intentional targeting of the civilian population.

The UN Group of Experts reported that additional AFC/M23 public justifications for the offensive on Uvira cited the presence of FDLR-FOCA elements operating alongside FARDC and FDNB, and said it did not identify evidence that such elements posed a direct threat to Rwanda justifying military intervention in the DRC.

The UN Group of Experts reported that security concerns led Burundi to close border posts with the DRC and designate several frontier areas as 'military zones' on 9 December 2025, and that on 25 February 2026 Burundi reopened a number of crossings.

place: Ruzizi Plain, Katogota, RN5, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts assessed that control of Katogota and surrounding heights strengthens the influence of AFC/M23 over the northern 'gate' of the Ruzizi Plain and offers options of advancing toward Uvira by bypassing strong FDNB and FARDC/Wazalendo blocking positions along RN5.

place: Mikalati (Mu Mikarati), Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, an attack on Saturday by Burundian soldiers in the town of Mikalati, Fizi territory, against residents returning from the weekly market in Bijombo (Uvira territory); its headline section gives four civilians killed, mass abductions and over 100 missing.
SOS Médias Burundi reported that a survivor, now a refugee in Mikenge, described meeting Burundian soldiers at Mikalati who attacked, looted and abducted many people, especially women.

place: Mikalati military site, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the survivor said the military commander ordered the soldiers 'to kill the men and collect their belongings', that the Wazalendo community claims 45 people, mostly women, are being held at the Mikalati military site, and that no official statement had been issued by the Burundian or Congolese governments as of Sunday morning.

place: Minembwe, Fizi/Mwenga Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that OCHA had already warned of difficulties accessing food and healthcare in Minembwe, due, according to local sources, to a blockade imposed for a month by the Burundian army.
sources: SOS Médias Burundi; Kivu Morning Post

statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged on the BBC that some Banyamulenge are trapped in areas 'where the enemy is' and said it is understandable that those who go to buy food for the enemy are blocked.

BBC News Gahuza reported that the Burundian army stated that its troops in South Kivu had blocked the roads of people leaving the Minembwe area in order to 'protect Uvira and the Burundi border', and that FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza told BBC Gahuzamiryango that in Minembwe there was not one Burundian soldier.

place: Minembwe; Mu Mikarati; Point-zero, South Kivu
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that demonstrators in Minembwe (an area controlled by the Twirwaneho group together with AFC/M23) accused Burundian troops and those working with them of blocking the roads that bring supplies, mainly from Uvira, at Mu Mikarati, Point-zero and elsewhere, and asked that the Burundian troops return home.

BBC News Gahuza reported that Burundi accuses Rwanda of continuing to attack the positions of its soldiers sent to eastern DRC; that Burundi's Minister of Foreign Affairs Edouard Bizimana, speaking on Monday before representatives of countries in Burundi, said without giving proof that the aim of the attacks was for Rwanda and M23 to capture Uvira before 25 December 2025; and that the Rwandan government had not yet responded.

place: Burundi (Murembwe Central Prison); related to deployment in DRC
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that at least 272 Burundian soldiers are serving sentences of up to life imprisonment in Murembwe Central Prison in southwestern Burundi after refusing to be sent to fight in the DRC.

place: Nyakakoma, Binza grouping, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that an incursion followed by systematic looting by armed men assimilated to former FDLR fighters was reported on the night of Sunday 14 September 2025 in the lakeside village of Nyakakoma, Binza grouping, Rutshuru territory, according to an anonymous local source; the page says no human incident was reported.

place: Gatumba border (Burundi side) / Uvira, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that long lines of Burundian soldiers were seen on Wednesday 10 December at the Gatumba border returning to their country, according to local sources in Uvira and Bujumbura; it added that Burundi's ambassador to the DRC denied this departure of part of the Burundian soldiers.
Radio Okapi reported that the departure of part of the Burundian soldiers from Uvira was denied by Burundi's ambassador to the DRC.

Actualite.cd reported, citing an April 2026 report by the Congo Research Group (CRG) and the Center on International Cooperation (CIC), that the capture of Uvira on 10 December 2025 by the M23 and the Rwandan Defence Forces put the Burundian contingent deployed alongside the Congolese army out of action; the article also states that between 12 000 and 15 000 FDNB soldiers were deployed on the eastern Congolese front against the M23/Rwanda alliance.

Radio Okapi reported that the DRC Ministry of Defence announced on 29 January 2025 that, by presidential order of Tuesday 28 January, general-major Evariste Somo Kakule was appointed military governor of North Kivu province under the state of siege.
Radio Okapi reported that the new military governor of North Kivu had been commander of the 31st rapid reaction brigade of the FARDC based at Kindu in Maniema province.

Cocorico.cd reported that brigade general Muhondosi Muyusa Constantin was named commander of the 34th military region in North Kivu, whose headquarters had been relocated from Goma to Walikale because of the occupation of Goma by AFC/M23 forces.

Cocorico.cd reported that the situation at Walikale remained under FARDC control despite the departure of part of the population, and that the army had slowed the rebels' advance, pushing them back to Mpofi as they advanced toward Walikale-centre.

7sur7.cd reported on 22 October 2025 that newly appointed FARDC commanders had arrived in Uvira, among them brigade general Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques as new commander of the 33rd military region and general AMULI CIVIRI as commander of operational sector Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu.

7sur7.cd reported that the army spokesperson of operational sector Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu, sub-lieutenant Mbuyi Kalonji Reagan, said the new 33rd military region commander replaces the late brigade general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel, who died after feeling unwell while on duty, and that general Civiri replaces general Mwehu Lumbu Evariste.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that general Olivier Gasita, in charge of intelligence and operations in the 33rd military region, was not affected by the October 2025 reshuffle and remained in post despite demonstrations in Uvira in September; the same report said that, according to several local sources, he had left Uvira on 8 October 2025 and was staying in Kinshasa.

Congorassure.cd reported on 26 January 2026 that brigade general Dunia Kashindi Fabien had been designated provisional commander of the 33rd military region, covering South Kivu and Maniema, according to an official note from the FARDC chief of general staff that the outlet said it had seen.

Congorassure.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi returned to Uvira on Friday 23 January after several weeks of absence, to the applause of the population, having left the city shortly before 10 December 2025.

BBC Gahuza reported that Uvira residents confirmed that Wazalendo fighters entered the city on the morning of Sunday and FARDC soldiers entered in the evening, after AFC/M23 announced on Saturday that it had left the city 'fully'.

BBC Gahuza reported that the South Kivu governor on the government-controlled side, then in Bujumbura where he had taken refuge, said the government had information that some M23 fighters remained in Uvira, urged great caution and asked the population to avoid ethnic violence.
BBC Gahuza reported that other videos circulating on social media showed looting that took place after the M23 fighters left Uvira; the passage does not attribute the looting.

Mediacongo reported that the High Military Court opened debate in Kinshasa on Friday 25 September (2026) in the case of two general-majors prosecuted for their alleged role in the loss of Bukavu during the AFC/M23 offensive in South Kivu in 2025: Robert Anvul Yav, who then commanded the South Kivu military region, and André Ehonza Uketi, former head of operations Sukola 2 Nord.
Mediacongo reported that, according to the public prosecution, Robert Anvul Yav allegedly left Bukavu before the arrival of AFC/M23 and did not organise a counter-offensive.

Mediacongo reported that the case file includes allegations about handing arms and ammunition to Wazalendo fighters at Lumbishi in Kalehe territory, and that, according to prosecution elements reported in the file, some equipment handed over was defective and some ammunition out of date.
Mediacongo reported that, in earlier hearings, the two accused generals contested the prosecution's reading of events, explaining that AFC/M23 forces had a significant advantage in men and equipment.

Radio Okapi, citing ACP, reported that the High Military Court handed prison sentences of under five years to four general officers of the army and police accused of fleeing before the enemy in the east, and that its first president, lieutenant general magistrate Joseph Mutombo, announced that divisional commissioner Jean Romuald Ekuka, former vice-governor of North Kivu, was sentenced to 36 months in prison (the page prints the offence as 'libertété').

Radio Okapi, citing ACP, reported that the High Military Court president said deputy divisional commissioner Eddy Léonard Mukuna was sentenced to 24 months for cowardice, brigade general Papy Lupembe to 12 months for cowardice before the enemy, and Danny Yangba Tene to 12 months in prison for the same charge.

Actualite.cd reported that about ten Wazalendo groups active in Mwenga and Shabunda territories wrote to the President and the FARDC chief of general staff demanding the replacement of commander Tshihutu Vela of the 3306 regiment based in Mwenga, accusing him in a joint memorandum, among other grievances, of appropriating arms and ammunition at the expense of the other groups.

Actualite.cd reported that commander Tshihutu is also accused, in collaboration with former provincial interior minister Albert Foka Maik, of appropriating the retrocession of 48.000 USD (as the page prints it) given by the province each month to the Wazalendo of Mwenga-Shabunda.

La Presse Africaine reported that brigade general Dunia Kashindi Fabien, 33rd military region commander, said at the funeral of self-proclaimed Wazalendo general Rukumeta Biriho Pierre in Uvira on Thursday 26 June 2025 that the Wazalendo were giving everything for the defence of South Kivu and had sworn never to betray Congo or Uvira.

Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March 2025 Wazalendo fighters attacked several Banyamulenge villages within a 10-kilometre radius of Bibokoboko, Fizi territory, and quoted a community leader saying they killed seven people and destroyed houses, health centers and schools.

Human Rights Watch quoted a Banyamulenge community leader as saying that Wazalendo fighters who attacked villages around Bibokoboko, Fizi territory, in the 3 March 2025 attack destroyed health centers, among other buildings.

Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March in Sange, Uvira territory, a Wazalendo commander detained and whipped a 48-year-old man accused of stealing a television, and that a relative and a neighbour said the man died of his injuries.

Human Rights Watch reported that on 14 February Wazalendo fighters killed a 25-year-old Munyamulenge man in Mulongwe, Uvira, after accusing him of being Rwandan, shooting him twice in the hip; he died from his injuries according to two sources.

Human Rights Watch reported that, following the M23's capture of Bukavu, Wazalendo fighters entered over 20 Banyamulenge households in Uvira, stealing goods and threatening residents, and in one case shot a woman in the head and beat at least three people.

Human Rights Watch reported that the interim governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, told the media on April 23 that the province was unable to collect taxes because of the Wazalendo fighters, who should 'not take the place of the state'.

Human Rights Watch reported that on April 4 an armed group commander wrote to President Félix Tshisekedi complaining that Justin Bitakwira Bihona Hayi, a National Assembly member who coordinates support for the Wazalendo coalition in South Kivu, was not fully distributing government funding to all Wazalendo armed groups.

Human Rights Watch reported that military and other sources estimate about 20,000 Wazalendo fighters, although the exact figure is unknown, and that in September 2023 some members of the coalition formed the Patriotic Defense Volunteers (VDP), an 'official' auxiliary force.

Human Rights Watch reported that military, humanitarian and other sources expressed concern about the Congolese army's lack of command and control over the Wazalendo, who in some instances have reportedly disarmed or attacked Congolese soldiers.

Umunota, a Rwandan outlet, reported, citing information from Uvira, that heavy gunfire heard overnight in Uvira city was fired at FARDC soldiers who had gone to steal in Murugenge, Kavimvira, and that local Wazalendo then intervened and exchanged fire with them for about an hour and a half.

place: Uvira and the Bukavu-Uvira corridor, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, summarising a UN Group of Experts report transmitted to the Security Council, reported that the experts wrote that the offensive on Uvira was carried out under the direct command of Makenga and Byamungu, and that James Kabarebe, a retired RDF general, was established to have played a key role in coordinating it.

Actualite.cd, relaying a UN Group of Experts report, reported that the experts recalled that Uvira was taken on 10 December 2025 and that AFC/M23 and RDF forces advanced rapidly south as far as Makobola, about twenty kilometres from Uvira.
Actualite.cd, relaying a UN Group of Experts report, reported that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 after sustained international diplomatic pressure.

place: North and South Kivu (M23 area of operations)
statement: The U.S. Treasury (OFAC), announcing sanctions on him, said that John Imani Nzenze is an M23 commander and M23's chief of intelligence, regarded as one of the closest collaborators and confidants of Sultani Makenga, whom it described as the U.S.- and UN-sanctioned overall military commander of M23.

The U.S. Department of the Treasury stated that, following the 15 November 2025 signing in Qatar of a peace framework agreement between the DRC government and M23, M23 seized Uvira and later withdrew, while still controlling Goma and Bukavu.

The U.S. Treasury (OFAC), announcing sanctions on him, said that Lawrence Kanyuka Kingston is M23's civilian spokesperson and a public relations officer for the Congo River Alliance, which it described as a U.S.-sanctioned coalition of rebel groups that seeks to overthrow the DRC government.

The U.S. Treasury (OFAC), announcing sanctions on him, said that James Kabarebe, a former RDF general and Rwanda's Minister of State for Regional Integration, is a Rwandan government liaison to M23 and orchestrates RDF support for the armed group.

place: North Kivu (M23-appointed governorate) and M23 structures
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the European Union announced sanctions on M23 figures including Bertrand Bisimwa (head of the political wing, already under UN sanctions), 'Jean Bahati Musanga' [as printed by Radio Okapi] (North Kivu governor appointed by the rebels), Désiré Rukomera (in charge of M23 recruitment and propaganda) and Jean-Bosco Nzabonimpa (deputy head of finance).

Actualite.cd, citing an April 2026 report by the Congo Research Group and NYU's Center on International Cooperation, reported that M23 chief of staff General Sultani Makenga has been under UN, US and EU sanctions since November and December 2012, and that General Baudouin Ngaruye, commander of the first operational sector, and Innocent Kaina are under the same three regimes since the same period.

Afrikarabia reported that Willy Ngoma, military spokesperson of the AFC/M23, was killed by a drone strike and that, according to first indications, the drone attack was launched by the Congolese army at Rubaya, Masisi territory; Actualite.cd, in an article on a CRG/CIC report, described him as former spokesperson and military commander of M23 and wrote that he was killed on 24 February 2026 in a drone strike near the Rubaya mining site, North Kivu.
The UN Group of Experts reported that the overall military command of AFC/M23 remained under 'General' Sultani Makenga, with political leadership held by Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the Rwandan-Congolese national Fred Ngenzi Kagorora and Brigadier General Patrick Karuretwa remained in frequent contact with Makenga, Bisimwa and 'Colonel' Imani Nzenze, and that the military and political leadership of AFC/M23 continued to receive instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 5 February 2025 AFC/M23 announced new administrative appointments, designating Bahati Musanga Joseph (also known as Bahati Erasto) as governor of North Kivu, with Manzi Ngarambe Willy and Amani Bahati Shaddrak as deputy governors.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 28 February AFC/M23 announced new administrative appointments in South Kivu, naming Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba as governor with Dunia Musumbuko Bwenge and Gishinge Gasinzira Juvénal as deputy governors.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 maintained two principal intelligence entities: the Directorate of Security and Intelligence, headed by Basile Gasigwa (a.k.a. 'Gas'), and a military intelligence unit led by 'Colonel' Imani Nzenze.

place: AFC/M23 training centres (locations not given in excerpt)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 sources confirmed 'Colonel' Léon Kanyamibwa was in command of all training centres, with the support of AFC/M23 and Rwandan trainers.

place: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force' under the movement's internal security structure, named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 14 September AFC/M23 publicized the 'pass-out' of 7,437 'commandos' who had finished their training in Rumangabo; that the graduation ceremony was presided over by 'General' Sultani Makenga and AFC Political Coordinator Corneille Nangaa, who said the cohort would form four brigades of 'commando' units; and that the Group could not independently confirm the number of 7,437 announced by AFC/M23.

place: Tchanzu training centre, Rutshuru, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 1 October AFC/M23 announced the graduation of an additional 9,350 'commandos' at the Tchanzu training centre, a number the Group could not independently confirm, and that 'General' Sultani Makenga presided over the ceremony, attended also by 'Colonel' Léon Kanyamibwa, AFC/M23 commander in charge of trainings.

place: Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals, Goma, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 conducted armed night raids on hospitals in Goma, targeting Heal Africa on 1 March and CBCA Ndosho on 3 March (2025) in operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants who had not surrendered, and that a total of 164 patients were abducted, 48 from Heal Africa and 116 from CBCA Ndosho; it reported that AFC/M23 leaders Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and 'General' Makenga publicly denied responsibility.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on the night of 4 to 5 April 2025 armed AFC/M23 elements entered the MSF-supported Kyeshero Hospital compound in Goma in search of FARDC elements and opened fire within the grounds, killing one person, injuring three and assaulting two staff members.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, following the March 2025 hospital incidents, Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and 'General' Makenga issued public denials of responsibility, claiming compliance with international humanitarian law and an aim of securing hospitals from 'infiltrated rogue combatants'; the Group wrote that witnesses confirmed no weapons were found in the hospitals.

The UN Group of Experts reported a further alarming surge in cases of sexual violence across North and South Kivu, attributed to all armed actors party to the conflict, both in the immediate aftermath of the fighting and during the subsequent consolidation of AFC/M23 control.

According to Radio Okapi, a communiqué published on Friday 7 March 2025 by the DRC Ministry of Justice announced a reward of 5.000.000 USD for anyone enabling the arrest of the 'convicts' (condamnés) Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa and Sultani Makenga.

place: M23 military high command (North and South Kivu)
statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, General Sultani Makenga as M23 chief of staff and General Byamungu Bernard (“Taiga/Tiger One”) as deputy chief of staff.
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

place: Nyiragongo to Lubero, headquarters Rutshuru town, North Kivu
statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Brigadier General Baudouin Ngaruye as commander of the 1st Operational Sector (Nyiragongo to Lubero, headquarters in Rutshuru town).
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

place: Masisi-Walikale and South Kivu, headquarters Mushaki, North Kivu
statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Brigadier General Gacheri Eraston as commander of the 2nd Operational Sector (Masisi-Walikale and South Kivu, headquarters in Mushaki).
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, the M23 Headquarters Regiment as now deployed to South Kivu, with its 1st battalion deployed in the Uvira operation and its 2nd battalion deployed to Minembwe.
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Corneille Nangaa as AFC coordinator, Bernard Bisimwa (president of M23) as deputy coordinator, Freddy Kanyiki as deputy coordinator and Benjamin Mbonimpa as secretary general.
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) reported that a commander who later reconciled with Makenga and joined the reconstituted M23 in 2022 was reassigned from commander of operations in Goma to lead the northern sector based in Rutshuru, and that the two had more recently clashed again over revenue collection; the report identifies him as Baudouin (Baudouin Ngaruye).
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: BBC News reported that former president Joseph Kabila was named leader of a new rebel coalition, announced at a press conference at his residence in Goma by the coalition's adviser Claude Ibalanky, with M23 leader Sultani Makenga as one of Kabila's four deputies and the other three also from the AFC-M23 alliance; BBC said the Congolese government had not commented.

place: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of writing, multiple AFC/M23 and intelligence sources said a comprehensive reshuffle of AFC/M23 leadership and structure was forthcoming, including a change of the movement's name, and that Joseph Kabila was expected to assume a prominent position.

place: UN Security Council, New York (listing); targets are AFC/M23 leaders
statement: Citing a UN communiqué, the news site reported that the Security Council's 1533 sanctions committee approved on 14 July the listing of six individuals and two entities, among them Corneille Nangaa, presented as head of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23), and Colonel John Imani Nzenze, M23 intelligence chief, sanctioned for alleged involvement in planning and supporting the rebel movement's activities.
Radio Okapi reported that the two entities added to the UN sanctions list were the Alliance Fleuve Congo and the armed group Twirwaneho.

7sur7.cd reported that the UN sanctions listing included Colonel Charles Sematama, military chief of the Twirwaneho group, active in the Hauts Plateaux of South Kivu and accused of abuses against civilians.

place: North Kivu and northern South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that in January and February 2025 a conservative estimate of 6,000 RDF troops, including RDF special forces, were active in North Kivu and northern territories of South Kivu.

place: AFC/M23 controlled territories, North and South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 RDF troops remained active in AFC/M23 controlled territories, including in urban centres.

The UN Group of Experts, citing its previous reports, reported in July 2025 that Major-General Ruki Karusisi (described as RDF Special Force Commander), Major-General Eugène Nkubito (RDF 3rd Division Commander) and Lieutenant-General Mubarakh Mugunga (RDF Army Chief of Staff) played key roles in planning and commanding military operations in North Kivu and South Kivu.

The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF operations were conceived and coordinated, among others, by General James Kabarebe, Army Chief of Staff Major-General Vincent Nyakarundi and Brigadier General Patrick Karuretwa, and that RDF established forward headquarters in Gisenyi, Rwanda, bordering Goma town.

The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF soldiers were briefed by 'Colonel' Espoir Rukinisha about their tasks, and that according to RDF sources interviewed by the Group, Rukinisha was the commander of the third bataillion in Bigogwe, Rwanda, before joining M23 in 2023.

place: Goma area (Kitchanga, Kibumba, Kanyamahoro), North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 25, 26 and 27 January 2025 RDF troop reinforcements, including RDF Special Forces, arrived from Kitchanga, Kibumba and Kanyamahoro in the DRC, as well as from Gisenyi, Rwanda.

The UN Group of Experts reported that it documented the presence of soldiers of the following RDF brigades and battalions in North Kivu in February and March 2025: 107 Brigade (55th, 79th, 87th, 85th, 57th, 15th, 03rd, 06th and 04th Battalions), 135 Brigade (27th and 29th Battalions) and 109 Brigade (69th, 85th, '72rd' [as printed] and 75th Battalions).

The UN Group of Experts reported that elements of the RDF 3rd Division, under Major General Eugene Nkubito, operated predominantly in North Kivu, and the 4th Division was mainly deployed in South Kivu under Brigadier General Vincent Gatama until his redeployment to Mozambique in late 2025, both supported by special forces under Brigadier-General Stanislas Gashugi.

place: Rwanda (decisions concerning operations in eastern DRC)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 1 December 2025 President Kagame appointed retired General James Kaberebe as his Senior Defence and Security Advisor, and on 29 January 2026 appointed Brigadier-General Jean-Paul Nyirabutama as his deputy.

The UN Group of Experts reported that Rwanda deployed over 8,000 RDF troops, including special forces, and transferred heavy, advanced military equipment to the frontlines on the Ruzizi Plain, including jamming systems, BM21-type multi-barrel rocket launchers, GPS-guided 120 mm mortars, kamikaze and first-person-view drones, aiming for a rapid victory.
The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 following sustained international diplomatic pressure, after controlling the city for over a month.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 2 February 2026 approximately 25 trucks carrying RDF troops departed from Bugarama and Nyangezi in Rwanda, arriving in Kamanyola before continuing toward Luvungi and Sange along the RN5.

place: South Kivu (Ruzizi Plain, Moyens and Hauts Plateaux, Ngweshe-Mwenga, Fizi)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that as of mid-February 2026 RDF deployments in South Kivu were approximately 1,800 troops along the Ruzizi Plain-Moyens Plateaux axis, 800 in the Hauts Plateaux, 1,800 along the Ngweshe-Mwenga axis and an undetermined number elsewhere, including towards Fizi.

place: Ruzizi Plain, Lemera, Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Mwenga
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that new RDF troop and materiel reinforcements were documented in April passing through Nyangezi-Kamanyola towards the Ruzizi Plain, Lemera in the Moyens Plateaux and the Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Mwenga, and that RDF positioned anti-aerial defence systems (MANPADS) and conducted attacks with kamikaze and armed drones, notably between 10 and 19 April.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the US designated Vincent Nyakarundi (Chief of Staff of the RDF), Major-General Ruki Karusisi (commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former Special Operations Force Commander), General Mubarakh Muganga (Chief of Defence Staff) and Stanislas Gashugi (Special Operations Force Commander since 15 March 2025) for their leadership roles within the RDF.

Human Rights Watch reported that the US sanctioned the Rwandan army and four commanders (Maj. Gen. Vincent Nyakarundi, Maj. Gen. Ruki Karusisi, Gen. Mubarakh Muganga and Brig. Gen. Stanislas Gashugi), and that military and UN sources told HRW several thousand Rwandan soldiers, including special forces, crossed into the DRC in the weeks before the December Uvira offensive.

AP and Reuters (as published by Al Jazeera) reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said in a statement that the US sanctions 'unjustly' target Rwanda and 'misrepresent the reality and distort the facts of the conflict' in eastern DRC, and accused the DRC of violating the peace agreement.

AP and Reuters (as published by Al Jazeera) reported that the Congolese government said it welcomed the US sanctions on the Rwandan military, describing them as 'a strong signal in support of respect' for its territorial integrity and sovereignty.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in an interview with Jeune Afrique on 26 March 2026 President Paul Kagame rejected Rwanda's responsibility in the DRC conflict, portraying it as a Congolese internal issue.

place: Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps, North Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch reported that former detainees identified Rwandan soldiers during roundups and among instructors and commanders in the Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps (North Kivu), based on uniforms, equipment, accents and inability to speak French or Kiswahili, and that military, intelligence and UN sources confirmed Rwandan forces' involvement.
Human Rights Watch said the Rwandan government and M23 leaders have long rejected allegations of abuses but have not conducted investigations.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the Mouvement des Patriotes pour la Défense de la Patrie (MPDP), a Wazalendo armed group, announced its creation on Saturday 11 October 2025 in the city of Uvira, South Kivu.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the MPDP is led by Pascal Biriho, alias Makanika, as commander of the forces, and by A. Byadunia Meschak Alexis as president of the political branch, and that both are former close collaborators of the warlord and former PNC officer Nyerere Bunana.

Kivu Morning Post reported that at the MPDP launch the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Dunia Mwamba, congratulated the MPDP commander while insisting on discipline and respect for the laws of the Republic, and symbolically handed a weapon to commander Pascal Biriho as a sign of support.

place: Misisi and Lulimba, Fizi territory (Ngandja sector), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that at least four people were killed and valuables destroyed in clashes at Misisi and Lulimba, Fizi territory, between two Wazalendo factions: the CNCCP of commander Yakutumba and the FABB of Ngoma Nzito.

place: Misisi and Lulimba, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Sammy Kalonji Badibanga, confirmed the fighting and gave as its main cause the decision of Yakutumba's men to remove illegal barriers set up in the area.

Kivu Morning Post reported that for more than a week fighting had opposed the Wazalendo of the Coalition nationale du peuple pour la souveraineté du Congo (CNPSC) of William Amuri Yakutumba to certain elements of the Biloze Bishambuke self-defence forces of Kalembe Ngoma Nzito, and quoted an elected official from Uvira, president of the defence and security commission of the provincial assembly, as saying the clashes began on 25 October 2025 and caused loss of life.

Kivu Morning Post reported, citing an administrative official at Mwenga Centre, a provisional toll of at least eight dead and five wounded in clashes on Thursday 18 September 2025 between two Wazalendo groups in Mwenga territory.
