Kivu Morning Post reported that the Mwenga clashes opposed fighters loyal to self-proclaimed general Malaika and those of general Nyakiliba, and that the pro-Malaika Wazalendo were supported by elements of the Foka Maïk group and of the army.
Kivu Morning Post reported that the root of the Mwenga clashes was the removal, by the fighters of Malaika and of Foka Maïk, of barriers that Nyakiliba had set up on the RN2.

place: Beni, North Kivu (Sokola 1 Grand Nord and Front Nord)
statement: 7sur7.cd reported that the new commander of the Sokola 1 Grand Nord and Front Nord operational sector took up his functions on Wednesday 23 July 2025 in Beni, North Kivu, and that general Mugisa Muleka replaced major-general Nyembo Abdallah, who had led the sector.

place: Kisangani, Tshopo (outside the Kivus; rotation of the former Sokola 1 commander)
statement: 7sur7.cd reported, citing the recent national defence telegram, that general Nyembo Abdallah was sent to Kisangani to lead the 31st military region based in Tshopo province.

place: Beni, North Kivu (Sokola 1); previous post Mambasa, Ituri
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the appointment of general Mugisa Muleka Joseph as the new head of Sokola 1 operations was communicated in a general staff telegram made public on Tuesday 15 July, and that he was previously commander of the 31st Principal Defence Brigade at Mambasa since 17 July 2020.

place: North Kivu (Sukola 1 Grand Nord and Front Nord)
statement: Congo-Press (MediaCongo Press) reported that major-general Nyembo Abdallah was named commander of the Sukola 1 Grand Nord operational sector and the Front Nord in North Kivu, an official designation announced on 22 May 2025 by the FARDC chief of general staff.

place: Uvira city, South Kivu (33rd military region)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC supported brigadier general Olivier Gasita, contested by the Wazalendo and struggling to take up his functions as deputy commander of the 33rd military region in charge of military operations and intelligence at Uvira, South Kivu.

Actualite.cd reported that, at a press conference in Kinshasa on Saturday 06 September 2025, FARDC spokesperson major-general Sylvain Ekenge said that an officer no longer belongs to his community but to the whole nation.

Actualite.cd reported that Sylvain Ekenge said on 6 September 2025 that no other presidential ordinance had relieved Gasita of his function and that he remained deputy commander of the 33rd military region, in charge of military operations and intelligence.

Actualite.cd reported that, reacting to Wazalendo allegations that Gasita was close to Rwanda and to the AFC/M23 rebellion, Sylvain Ekenge said Gasita would have another superior in charge of the whole region.

Radio Okapi reported that brigadier generals Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques and Amuli Civiri, named respectively commander of the 33rd military region and commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector in South Kivu, arrived in Uvira on Wednesday 22 October 2025 via the Kavimvira border post with Burundi.

place: Uvira, South Kivu (33rd military region; Sokola 2)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the appointments of brigadier generals Ilunga Kabamba and Amuli Civiri as commander of the 33rd military region and commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector followed the death in August of brigade general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel, former commander of the 33rd military region, and the replacement of general Mwehu Lumbu Evariste as commander of the operational sector.

Radio Okapi reported that general Olivier Gasita, sent to fill the vacant post of operational sector commander, had been violently contested by the population in demonstrations that resulted in deaths, many wounded and significant material damage.

place: Iamba health centre, Makobola, Nundu health zone, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Iamba health centre at Makobola, in the Nundu health zone, Tanganyika sector, Fizi territory, was pillaged on 30 December, and that, according to concordant sources, the FARDC and Wazalendo militiamen were allegedly responsible.

Kivu Morning Post reported that structures pillaged at Makobola included the Makobola health centre and a recently built hospital, and quoted another local source as saying that all the equipment of the new building of this large hospital, built but not yet operational, was pillaged.

Kivu Morning Post reported that, besides the pillage at Makobola, cases of rape were reported, as lamented by civil society actors who asked to remain anonymous; the same passage says that, according to concordant sources, the FARDC and Wazalendo militiamen were allegedly responsible for the pillage.
sources: Kivu Morning Post; Actualite.cd; Kivu Times

statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Mwenga territory civil society forces vives, meeting on Monday 16 March 2026, denounced the harassment committed by FARDC and Wazalendo elements.

place: Musika, Ilinda and Kibumba, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing the Mwenga civil society, that at the start of March at Musika a nurse was robbed of 200 000 FC, his android phone and his boots, and that on 12 March a young boy was shot ('fusillé par balle') at Ilinda and on the 13th another was shot ('fusillé') at Kibumba; the civil society gave these as examples ('À titre d'exemple') after denouncing harassment by FARDC and Wazalendo elements, but the passage does not name the perpetrator of each incident.

Kivu Morning Post reported that Shabunda civil society, which denounced several recent deadly incidents, said a citizen was beaten to death by Wazalendo elements and that three children aged 10 to 15 were hit by bullets as they left school, one of whom died on the spot.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the president of Shabunda civil society, Maître Isaac Kibunda, said that the armed Wazalendo, supposed to support the FARDC on the front lines, were committing serious abuses against the civilian population.

Kivu Morning Post reported strong tension on the morning of Friday 10 October 2025 in Kamituga, Mwenga territory, caused by a demonstration of residents demanding the immediate departure of Wazalendo fighters accused of multiple abuses in the region.

Kivu Morning Post quoted the Mwenga territory civil society as giving, for the unrest in Kamituga, a provisional toll of several victims, including PNC elements and a FARDC soldier, as well as wounded civilians and the pillage of shops and phone shops.

Enquete.cd reported, citing several local sources, that Wazalendo movement leader James Fyeka Adui, arrested in Uvira on 5 September, had been transferred to Kinshasa some days earlier, and that he is accused, according to concordant sources, of involvement in the murder of a civilian in Uvira in May 2026; the outlet added that these accusations had not yet been publicly confirmed in detail by judicial authorities.

La Prunelle RDC reported that James « Fyeka Adui » was arrested on 5 September 2026 by the security services in Uvira, and that on 6 September contradictory information had circulated about his release, some sources saying he had been released after his hearing and others that he remained detained.

La Prunelle RDC reported that a voice message attributed to James « Fyeka Adui » was circulated on social networks, in which the author accused the commander of the 33rd military region of withholding funds meant for local Wazalendo armed groups; that he was summoned by the military intelligence services of the 33rd military region a few days after the message circulated; and that the Unité spéciale des Wazalendo pour les opérations au Sud-Kivu later announced his suspension as spokesperson.

Enquete.cd reported that Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito, head of the Wazalendo special unit, issued a firm call on Monday 5 May 2026 in Uvira for Wazalendo fighters to withdraw from urban areas and join the front lines, after meeting Jacques Kongolo, adviser to the President of the Republic.

Enquete.cd reported that a three-day moratorium was granted to Wazalendo fighters in Uvira to leave the city and return to combat positions, with only commanders allowed to circulate in the urban area in strictly limited numbers, and that any breach would expose offenders to the sanctions of military regulations.

place: Nyakigano, Nkokwe and Kashovu near Kasake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing several concordant local sources, that Wazalendo allied to the FARDC, under the command of Jams Mutayomba and Noah Maachano, had reportedly also retaken on Monday morning several positions previously held by the AFC/M23, with Nyakigano, Nkokwe and Kashovu, around Kasake, notably cited.

place: Katale, Shanje and Chambombo, Ziralo grouping, near Lumbishi, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, after fighting reported on Sunday in Kalehe territory, South Kivu, that sources close to the Congolese army claimed the Wazalendo had retaken several villages in the Ziralo grouping, notably Katale, Shanje and Chambombo, near Lumbishi.

Radio Okapi reported that two people died in an exchange of fire in the night of Sunday 24 May in the town of Runingu, Uvira territory, between two Wazalendo groups, each led by its own commander, said to disagree over a question not yet elucidated.

Kivu Morning Post reported that in two decisions made public on 6 April 2025 the AFC announced appointments of territory administrators, bourgmestres, cité heads and their deputies in North and South Kivu; in North Kivu it named Kulu Musubao Jean-Louis administrator of Lubero territory with Radjabu Kwizera Elie as deputy, Munyandekwe Innocent as bourgmestre of Kirumba assisted by Kavugho Jeanine, and Kahinda Jean-Baptiste as bourgmestre of Kayna with Mumbere Siméon as deputy.

place: Kalehe, Kabare, Bukavu (Ibanda, Kadutu, Bagira) and Minova (South Kivu)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that in the same two decisions Buseyi Jean-Bosco was named administrator of Kalehe territory with Ndaye Faustine as deputy, Elie Rubabura Espoir named for Kabare assisted by Cikuru Barakaziga, and three new bourgmestres were named for the Bukavu communes of Ibanda, Kadutu and Bagira; Balyahamwabo Paulin became head of the Minova cité.

Kivu Morning Post reported that in a decision made public on 11 June 2025 the Conseil de l'Alliance Fleuve Congo reorganised the South Kivu administration, naming Patrick Busu Bwa Ngwi Nshombo governor and Mukiza Nzabinesha Gadi vice-governor in charge of the economy, finance and development, and that Busu succeeded Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba, recalled to new functions within the AFC/M23 coordination.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the AFC decision named Mukiza Nzabinesha Gadi as South Kivu Vice-Governor to fill the vacancy left by the death of Juvénal Gishinge Gasinzira, and that the decisions were signed by Bertrand Bisimwa, president of the M23 and deputy coordinator of the AFC, and approved by Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, coordinator of the Alliance.

A text published by Soleil du Graben (which styles itself 'the news portal of eastern DRC') and signed 'Celcom' said that at the first security council meeting of the year, chaired on 6 January 2026 by Governor Patrick BUSU BWA NGWI Nshombo, the vice-governor in charge of financial and development matters, MUKIZA GADI NZABINESHA, who it said had long been blocked in Minembwe, was officially presented to the participants.

A text published by Soleil du Graben and signed by a communication cell said that Nicolas Kyalangalilwa took over as head of the Bukavu city hall from Ladys Muganza Wakandwa, in a decision it attributes to the 'mouvement révolutionnaire AFC-M23', at a handover ceremony on Friday 13 March 2026 under Vice-Governor Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge Doux; it said the outgoing mayor had taken the reins of Bukavu in February 2025.

place: Bukavu (Bagira, Ibanda, Kadutu communes), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that in Bukavu Nicolas Kyalangalilwa was confirmed as mayor of Bukavu with Nyota Luandja Celine named deputy mayor, Shaka Muhoza, who had been acting, was confirmed bourgmestre of Bagira with Léon Bahaya as deputy, and that Mweze Prisca and Ruremesha Tého were named bourgmestres of Ibanda and Kadutu.

place: Idjwi, Kabare, Kalehe territories and Minova (South Kivu)
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that Pascal Ntambuka was named administrator of Idjwi territory, Elie Rubabura Espoir was reappointed administrator of Kabare with former national deputy Kasindi Kingombe Benjamin as assistant, Buseyi Jean Bosco was named administrator of Kalehe, and Sengimana Ruhungande Augustin was named head of the Minova cité.

Kivu Morning Post reported that Désiré Kisuba Ngabo, until then deputy mayor, became mayor of Goma replacing Julienne Katembo Ndalieni, who was named administrator of Lubero territory, in a reshuffle of administrative cadres signed on 8 April 2026 by the governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto.

place: Goma (Goma and Karisimbi communes), Lubero (North Kivu)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that in the same April 2026 reshuffle Juvénal Nshimimana became deputy mayor of Goma and Katembo Isevisya became deputy bourgmestre of Goma commune, Radjabu Kwizera Elie head of Karisimbi commune, Innocent Munyandekwe Fizi assistant administrator of Lubero territory and Jeannine Kavugho bourgmestre of Kirumba commune.

Kivu Morning Post reported on 24 November 2025 that the spokesperson of the North Kivu governor confirmed that Goma mayor Katembo Julien Dalieni, appointed by the AFC/M23, had been suspended for 15 days, the decision citing a 'manquement grave aux valeurs de la révolution' without further detail.

place: Goma (Goma and Karisimbi communes), North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that North Kivu governor Bahati Musanga Erasto signed on 1 April 2026 a provincial order designating new neighbourhood chiefs and deputies in the city of Goma, aimed at strengthening local governance.

Kivu Morning Post reported that North Kivu vice-governor Amani Bahati Chadrack published a circular (n° 01-009-CAB-GP-NK-2025, dated 18 August 2025) banning unjustified price rises for cement in Goma and its surroundings and officially fixing sale prices.

Kivu Morning Post reported that by an order signed on Monday 8 September 2025 North Kivu governor Bahati Musanga Erasto named seven members of a Commission Provinciale de Pacification et Résolution des Conflits (CPRC), created by an order of 22 August 2025 and presented as a body for pacification in the 'liberated' zones, and that the governor's director of cabinet, Nsanzamahoro Tengera Vincent, was charged with executing the orders.

Actu26 reported that Ephrem Kabasha, described as the new administrator of Rutshuru territory recently appointed by the AFC/M23, sought to reassure transport operators and the population about the security situation in the Busendo area and announced he would hold discussions with the high military hierarchy to strengthen security arrangements on that axis.

place: Rumangabo and Goma-Rutshuru road (Rutshuru, North Kivu)
statement: Actu26 reported that on the Monday before its report violence at Rumangabo was marked by reported looting of property, and that people were wounded by gunfire on the Goma-Rutshuru road; the page does not name the perpetrators.

Kivu Morning Post reported that an order designated Maître Jean-Philippe Chubaka Mashamba head of the Department of Justice and Human Rights, with Maître Shyaka Jean-Paul in charge of judicial reforms and Maître Mugisa Tibasima Emmanuel in charge of human rights as deputy heads of department.

Actualité.cd reported that the death toll of at least 226 in the collapse at the Rubaya coltan mine in Masisi territory was confirmed to it by Kambere Muyisa Lumumba, whom it described as spokesperson of the North Kivu governor appointed by the AFC/M23 rebellion.

Radio Okapi reported that President Félix Tshisekedi appointed commissioner Louis Segond Karawa vice-governor of North Kivu on Friday 7 March 2025, in the context of the occupation of Goma by the M23, and that he had been South Kivu provincial police commissioner from 2015.

Actualité.cd reported that Uvira city mayor Kifara Kapenda Kiki, who had returned to Uvira on Thursday, said that those who had occupied the city had left Uvira but 'ils ne sont pas loin', and acknowledged abuses ('dérives') both within the FARDC and among the wazalendo self-defence groups during the fighting.

The US State Department said on 2 June 2026 that it was designating John Imani Nzenze, chief of intelligence for the Rwanda-backed M23, 'an armed group that has committed killings, serious human rights abuses, and attacks on civilians in eastern DRC', and Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, saying the FDLR had 'committed sexual violence'.

place: Nyongera (HQ of 1st Brigade), Rutshuru, North Kivu
statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Emmanuel Kabundi as commander of the 1st Brigade (HQ in Nyongera) and Colonel Rigobert Manga as its deputy commander, within the 1st Operational Sector (Nyiragongo to Lubero, headquarters in Rutshuru town).
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Mapenzi Lihue as commander of the 2nd Brigade (HQ in Bambu) and Colonel Gakufe Jafet as its deputy commander, and said the brigade was formed largely out of a wing of the Nduma Defence for Congo (NDC) faction led by Colonel Mapenzi.
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

place: Nyiragongo to Lubero (HQ Rutshuru town), North Kivu
statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, the staff of the 1st Operational Sector as: T1 Administration Colonel Seraphin Mirindi, T2 Intelligence Colonel Ndagije, T3 Operations Colonel Bisamaza Richard, T4 Logistics Lt Col Bahati Gahizi, and T5 Political-Military Relations Lt Col Rugabisha Clément.
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

place: Masisi-Walikale and South Kivu (HQ Mushaki), North Kivu
statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, the staff of the 2nd Operational Sector (Masisi-Walikale and South Kivu, headquarters in Mushaki) as: T1 Administration Colonel Gilbert Bwira, T2 Intelligence Lt Col Muhire, T3 Operations Col Jimmy Nzamuye, T4 Logistics Major Kalengay, and T5 Political-Military Relations Lt Col Damascène.
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Samuel Nsabimana as commander of the 1st Brigade of the 2nd Operational Sector (Masisi-Walikale and South Kivu, headquarters in Mushaki).
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Justin (“Zero Three”) as commander of the 2nd Brigade of the 2nd Operational Sector, noting that he had 'now gone as a liaison to Minembwe'.
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Josué Biyoyo (“Buffle”) as G1 (Administration) in the M23 military high command.
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Jeff Kabayiza (“Sauce Tomate”) as G4 (Logistics) and Colonel Ernest Sebagenzi as G5 (Political-Military Relations) in the M23 military high command.
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Kamanzi Rubens (“Romeo Kilo”) as commander of the Headquarters Regiment (now deployed to South Kivu), Lt Col “Romeo Delta” as commander of its 1st battalion (deployed in the Uvira operation) and Lt Col Badege as commander of its 2nd battalion (deployed to Minembwe).
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

statement: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Antoine Manzi as responsible for 'military prisons', with the note that he was in CNDP and M23 I and was close to Laurent Nkunda.
sources: Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation

place: Kaniola and Kashanja (Kaniola groupement), Walungu, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the civil society group Forces vives of the Kaniola groupement (Walungu, South Kivu), in a letter to BCNUDH, MONUSCO and the ICRC, accused AFC/M23 officer Charles Kagigi of establishing a regime of terror, and said that over four days it documented several crimes, including a taxi driver from Kalengera (Zigashane Mashali) extorted of 30 000 Congolese francs (13 USD) and beaten to death on 23 September at Kashanja, and three civilians returning from a Leopards match (Birhalugirakulimushi Jules, Kashokwire Kulimushi Isaac and Bizimana Ciraza) summarily executed on 24 September at Kaniola. The group also said that 'colonel Kagigi' publicly swore to 'raze the Kaniola groupement' and demanded his departure.

place: M23 headquarters (Rubare, Rutshuru per CRG table), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, citing an April 2026 report by the Congo Research Group and NYU's Center on International Cooperation, reported that Colonel Innocent Zimurinda is commander of the headquarters (quartier général), sanctioned by the UN since December 2010, by the European Union since the same date and by the United States since January 2013.

place: Ngululu and Humura, Masisi-Walikale axis, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, since Saturday, AFC/M23 elements had taken control of Ngululu before seizing the commercial centre of Humura on Sunday, amid intensifying fighting between AFC/M23, the FARDC and the wazalendo in Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu.

place: Nyiragongo, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, Walikale and South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23-occupied territories were divided into three 'defense zones', led respectively by 'General' Baudoin Ngaruye (first zone: Nyiragongo, Rutshuru and Lubero territories), 'Brigadier-General' Justin Gacheri Musanga (second zone: Masisi and Walikale) and 'General' Byamungu (third zone: South Kivu).

place: Nyiragongo, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, Walikale and South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, relaying the UN Group of Experts report, reported that 'brigadier general' Justin Gacheri Musanga led the second zone (Masisi and Walikale) and a 'general' it named as Innocent Byamungu the third zone (South Kivu) of the movement's 'defence zones'.

place: Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms, Rutshuru territory
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that the AFC/M23 'First Defence Zone' command, covering Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms, was led by 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 September 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye, commander of AFC/M23's 'First Defense Zone' covering the Goma-Rutshuru-Kanyabayonga-Kirumba axis, declared in Kirumba that AFC/M23 intended to resume hostilities aimed at capturing Butembo and Kisangani.

place: Goma, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, Walikale, Walungu, Mwenga, Minembwe
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that one RDF brigade operated within AFC/M23's 'first defence zone' (Goma, Nyiragongo, Binza, Bwito, Rutshuru, and Kanyabayonga, Kirumba and Kipese in Lubero), and another RDF brigade in the 'second defence zone' (Masisi, Walikale, Bibwe, Kalembe, and South Kivu areas including Walungu, Mwenga and Minembwe).
The UN Group of Experts reported that in late March AFC/M23 'Colonel' Japhet Gakufe and Charles Sematama arrived in Minembwe with an estimated 200 AFC/M23 combatants.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, after AFC/M23 reinforcements led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, a second reinforcement led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Oscar Ndabagaza was blocked as it attempted to cross hostile areas before finally reaching Mikenge at the end of August.

The UN Group of Experts reported that 'Colonel' Gafishi Semikobe Simon was officially appointed AFC/M23 'Officer for Mobilisation and Recruitment' on 11 February 2025 and also carried out responsibilities relating to the 'security files'.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 confiscated identification documents, including voter cards and land titles of the refugees, and publicly burned them in the presence of AFC/M23 officials, including AFC/M23 spokesperson Oscar Balinda, military spokesperson Willy Ngoma and Goma's military commander, 'Colonel' Nsanze Nzamuye Jimmy, and in the presence of local media.

place: AFC/M23 territory, North and South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that 'General' Makenga held overall military command of AFC/M23, although his position had become increasingly contested within the movement and by Rwanda.

place: Kalundu district, Uvira (Blue Cat bar-restaurant); Mushaki (Masisi) on 2026-03-07
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that FARDC drone operations also targeted AFC/M23 leadership: on 14 January 2026 a drone strike targeted the 'Blue Cat' bar-restaurant in the Kalundu district of Uvira during a meeting of senior AFC/M23 and RDF officers, causing significant casualties, and on 7 March 2026 a strike in Mushaki targeted a house associated with a high-ranking AFC/M23 commander.

BBC Gahuza, relaying Reuters, reported that the drone strike that killed AFC/M23 military spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma at dawn on Tuesday near Rubaya killed at least nine people but narrowly missed AFC/M23 military chief Gen Sultani Makenga, who escaped unharmed according to four people who told Reuters.

place: Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps, Rutshuru territory
statement: Human Rights Watch reported that its research and the United Nations indicate that the M23's Léon Kanyamibwa and Bertin Masozera directed military training with support from other M23 officers, and that Rwandan military trainers operated in both Rumangabo and Tshanzu.

Human Rights Watch reported, in its section 'Summary Executions and Beatings' on former detainees from Rumangabo, that one M23 commander, 'Captain Gaston', was named by a dozen former detainees as having been particularly brutal in his treatment of recruits, and that detainees often referred to him by the nickname Longangi.

place: Rumangabo and Tshanzu training centers, Rutshuru territory
statement: Human Rights Watch reported that senior AFC/M23 leaders including Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, Maj. Gen. Sultani Makenga and Bertrand Bisimwa, and commanders such as Gen. Baudoin Ngaruye, Bertrand Byamungu, John Imani Nzenze and Willy Ngoma, were all reported to have been seen at the Rumangabo and Tshanzu training centers in 2025.

Kivu Morning Post reported that in early December 2025 more than 100 Mai-Mai fighters surrendered to AFC/M23 in Uvira in the presence of General Byamungu Maheshe, described as deputy commander of the AFC/M23.

Actualite.cd reported that the day after attacks on Wazalendo positions on 25 September in the groupements of Kaniola and Kamisimibi, General Bernard Byamungu, described as the movement's number two, held a public meeting at Nzibira in Walungu territory.

Kivu Morning Post reported that on Monday 29 December, at an exchange of wishes of senior AFC/M23 cadres in Goma, the military coordinator of the AFC/M23 and ARC chief of staff, General-Major Sultani Makenga, told participants: 'Soyez en état de guerre, cette guerre nous allons la gagner'.

place: Goma (dateline); strike location not stated in the excerpt
statement: Enquete.cd reported from Goma on 24 May 2026, according to sources close to the rebellion, that Bernard Maheshe Byamungu, alias 'Tiger One', described as one of the main military chiefs of the AFC/M23-RDF coalition, had died after being wounded in a drone strike.

FNTV reported on 23 May 2026 that, after checking with several local sources and Wazalendo movements, it could give a clear denial that General Bernard Byamungu of the AFC/M23 had died: the man killed in the drone attack was a Wazalendo commander with the same name, colonel Byamungu Ruduga Abdallah, active in the Uvira high plateaux.

Kivu Morning Post reported that FARDC brigadier general François Kamanzi, commander of operations of the 12th military region in Kongo-Central, had joined the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) led by Joseph Kabila; FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said he joined the ranks of the 'Lions de Sarambwe' within the Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC).

Actualite.cd reported that the staff of the 34th military region announced it had detained at Walikale two Wazalendo commanders accused of indiscipline and of violence that seriously affected civilians: self-proclaimed generals Kirikicho Mirimba, alias Mwana Mayi, of the COPACO movement (Coalition des Patriotes au Congo), and Musubao Kalimba, alias Kasilasi.

place: Tushunguti and Zirhalo groupements, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe (South Kivu)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the military authorities, the two Wazalendo commanders had been engaged in fratricidal clashes for nearly 17 months, the most recent being the fighting of 15 to 18 February 2026 in the groupements of Tushunguti and Zirhalo, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory (South Kivu); according to the army, these clashes caused 14 civilian deaths, 7 seriously wounded and 7 women victims of rape.

Radio Okapi reported that fifty-four soldiers of the 3415th regiment of the FARDC had been appearing since Monday 26 October before the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit hearing at Walikale, North Kivu, prosecuted notably for murder, abandoning post, dissipation of war munitions and refusal to obey.

place: Ntoto, Waloa Loanda groupement, Walikale (territory), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, according to major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region, the defendants were arrested on 20 October following incidents at Ntoto, Waloa Loanda groupement, on the border with Masisi territory, which left two dead, a soldier and a civilian; the page says the facts allegedly occurred during an altercation between the soldiers and Military Police elements trying to stop them from leaving the combat zone without authorisation.

Radio Okapi reported that another group of ten soldiers of the same regiment had been convicted on 1 September to sentences ranging from ten months of prison to principal penal servitude for opening fire on their company commander.

place: Kimbulu village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that three FARDC soldiers, all from the 21st principal defence brigade, were sentenced to twenty years in prison each for collective rape in Lubero: the court found them guilty of sexually assaulting a 28-year-old woman in the village of Kimbulu during the night from Sunday to the previous Monday, and ordered them to pay jointly 10,000 US dollars to the victim in reparation.

place: Kaviseghe village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that a FARDC soldier was sentenced to seven years of penal servitude for the rape of a 15-year-old girl; according to the court, the facts took place in the village of Kaviseghe, and the soldier allegedly had sexual relations with the adolescent several times in his room.

place: Katundu village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that a FARDC soldier was found guilty of the murder of three people (his partner, their child and another soldier) in facts dating back to 12 August at the village of Katundu; according to the elements retained by the court, he had opened fire point-blank on his partner in a context of jealousy.

Radio Okapi reported that the Beni garrison military tribunal (North Kivu) sentenced three FARDC officers (two lieutenants and a captain) to death for desertion and breach of orders, after they had been recruited, according to the court, by a man presenting himself as coordinator of the Comité national des patriotes (CONAP); two men presenting themselves as Wazalendo commanders got twenty years in prison for, notably, illegally recruiting soldiers and spreading false information, having set up, according to military justice, a clandestine recruitment network in the Malepe quarter of Beni using without mandate the name of the Réserve armée de la défense (RAD); the verdict came on the evening of Friday 10 July.

Radio Okapi reported that a member of the Wazalendo movement called « Far West » was sentenced to death on Wednesday 6 May, the Butembo garrison military tribunal having found him guilty of the murder of a motorcyclist and of the rape followed by murder of his female customer, facts which occurred the previous week at Kimbulu, Lubero territory; Lubero civil society also demanded the outright abolition of the « Far West » movement, which it accuses of being involved in serious human rights violations.

place: Kibati, Luberike groupement, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that fighting between the rebels of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) and the FARDC, supported by the Wazalendo, continued for the third consecutive day on Sunday 18 October 2026 at Kibati, Luberike groupement, Walikale territory, North Kivu, the FARDC and Wazalendo having launched an offensive against FRN positions there to dislodge the rebels; the outlet says Kibati has for about two years been one of the main foci of confrontation between the FRN and government forces supported by the Wazalendo in that part of Walikale.

place: between Kirumburumbu and Muuli villages, near Misinga, Ikobo groupement, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that two AFC/M23 commanders deployed at Misinga, Ikobo groupement, Walikale territory, were kidnapped by Wazalendo in the night of Sunday to Monday 30 June, the sources not giving their identities; on the Monday the AFC/M23 searched the forest of Kirumburumbu and Muuli in vain and forced farmers to leave their fields to continue the search.

place: Shengesha, Bashali chiefdom, Masisi; Mudugugudu, Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing several local sources, that two Wazalendo factions, the ACNDH group led by self-proclaimed general Jean-Marie and another group led by Ignace Sauli, clashed at Shengesha, Masisi territory, fighting with heavy and light weapons throughout the day and driving residents to flee; the outlet also reported clashes the same day involving CMC-FDP Wazalendo in Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, concentrated in Mudugugudu village.

place: Biramba and Luhonga, Bashali Mokoto groupement, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to first reports, Wazalendo led by self-proclaimed general Ignace Dunia Sauli attacked M23 positions at Biramba, Masisi territory, causing exchanges of heavy-weapon fire, after fighting at Luhonga on Sunday 29 June.

place: Bishusha groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least nine civilians were killed and several others seriously wounded, among them three children including a five-year-old girl, in an armed incursion by presumed CMC-FDP Wazalendo militiamen into Bishusha groupement, Rutshuru territory, in the night of Monday to Tuesday 28 October 2025; according to anonymous health sources at Bishusha Centre, the armed men came in around 19 h, largely targeting local traders, and goods and shops were looted.

place: Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the administrator of Rutshuru territory under the FRN, Euphrem Kabasha, accused the Wazalendo of the CMC of being behind an attack that killed civilians at Kabizo, saying that in the night of 25 to 26 October, at about 1:30, Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, was attacked by the FDLR together with the Nyatura CMC FDP of Gashegu Héritier and Mbitezi, and that five people were killed.

place: Kabizo-Katovu road, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, the Wazalendo ambushed a convoy of FRN rebels heading to Kabizo to install a new commander, near Kabizo and Katovu, Rutshuru, with a provisional toll of three rebel fighters killed, per sources in the area.

place: Munzambaye hill, Congo Ya Sika quarter, Vulamba commune, Butembo, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that self-proclaimed general Kakule Kaputu, alias « Tango Fort », was shot dead during fighting between his Wazalendo group and that of his rival Fiston Njoli at Butembo, according to Paluku Jean-Baptiste Muyisa, president of the communal civil society; the fighting began on a Sunday morning on Munzambaye hill, Vulamba commune, and lasted until Monday 5 January, and the body was reportedly displayed publicly at Furu.

place: Butembo and Burondo, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the spokesperson of the Wazalendo synergy Front Nord, John Mangaiko, had declared on 6 January 2026 at Butembo that Kakule Kaputu (« Tango Fort ») was killed in an armed operation and not in a targeted assassination, describing Tango Fort as an armed fighter involved in attacks on other Wazalendo and in acts of insecurity against the population; the outlet added that in a video published on 4 March 2026 at Burondo, Lubero territory, the political-military movement Bana Bateseka, a member of the Wazalendo Front Grand-Nord, announced the dissolution of the armed group Tango Fort, and that according to the video its deputy commander, colonel Thembo, announced his rallying to Bana Bateseka with all his fighters.

place: Luke, Katoyi sector, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing an administrative and security source in Masisi, that the self-proclaimed general Mutayomba, a Wazalendo commander on the Katoyi axis, was wounded in fighting against the AFC-M23 at Luke, Masisi territory, on 'Friday 21 May 2026'; the administrative source said he was lightly wounded and evacuated by helicopter to Beni, while a FARDC military source confirmed the injury but described it as serious.
Brigadier general Muhondosi Muyuwa Constantin, commander of the 34th military region, reiterated his appeal for the surrender of the M23 members still active, the outlet reported.

Actualite.cd reported that major-general Nyembo Abdallah, interim commander of the 3rd defence zone, had been staying in Walikale since Friday 21 November, a visit which major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region, said was part of an inspection of the troops and of command; the delegation was received by the commander of the 34th region.

place: Minembwe and Mikenge, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 reinforcements led by "Lieutenant-Colonel" Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, and that a second reinforcement, led by "Lieutenant -Colonel" Oscar Ndabagaza, was blocked while crossing hostile areas before reaching Mikenge at the end of August 2025; it described these as support to MRDP-Twirwaneho enclaves in the Hauts Plateaux.

place: Uvira and Fizi territories, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that in areas under the control of Mai-Mai Yakutumba and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups in Uvira and Fizi territories there was a sharp escalation in human rights violations, including conflict-related sexual violence, extortion and summary executions of civilians accused of collaborating with AFC/M23; it also said that Raia Mutomboki and other factions aligned with Yakutumba had expanded their operations and perpetrated abuses, and that at least 325 cases of sexual violence affecting over 400 victims were documented in South Kivu between January and June 2025.
The UN Group of Experts reported in its final report that the strength of MRDP/Twirwaneho was estimated at 2,500 to 3,000 combatants, led by Charles Sematama.

The UN Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho prevented civilians from leaving Minembwe, including through coercion and threats of violence, fearing defections and information leaks, and that, as previously reported, all boys between 10 and 12 years of age and all able-bodied men were compelled to join Twirwaneho and participate in combat.

place: Masango, Magunda, Kipupu, Nyaburunda forest, Sange, Kamombo sector; Uvira, Mwenga and Fizi territories, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that RED Tabara had long-standing camps in Masango (Uvira territory), Magunda (Mwenga territory) and Kipupu (Mwenga territory), and that, although the RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23, RED Tabara combatants took part in hostilities alongside AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and RDF across several axes; that FNL elements were present in the Nyaburunda forest (Uvira territory), in mountainous areas near Sange and in Magunda, where they co-locate with RED Tabara units; and that by mid-February 2026 RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundi accuses Rwanda of supporting RED-Tabara, that Burundian authorities identify Alexis Sinduhije, a former journalist and president of the opposition party MSD, currently in exile in Belgium, as the group's leader, and that Kigali rejects these accusations.

The UN Group of Experts reported that two ADF units, led by "Mzee" Meya Sebagala in Ituri Province and by sanctioned commander Ahmad Mahmood Hassan, alias Abwakasi (CDi.040), in Lubero territory, were responsible for most ADF mass casualty attacks, and that supply rendezvous sites were overseen by senior ADF figures including Mzee Meya, Abwakasi and Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender.

The UN Group of Experts reported that throughout 2025, attacks perpetrated under the command of Abwakasi (Ahmad Mahmood Hassan), whose ADF unit it places in Lubero territory, led to the killing of over 600 civilians, making it the deadliest ADF unit, with an estimated 25,000 people displaced and at least 26 villages and 9 mining sites destroyed; it reported that the group of 'Mzee' Meya Sebagala, which it places in Ituri Province (Mambasa territory), was responsible for the killing of over 230 civilians.

place: Lindi River, Asangwa, Bapere sector (Lubero/Tshopo border), North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that ADF commander Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender, reportedly died from injuries sustained during clashes with Shujaa forces on 14 March 2026 along the Lindi River (in Asangwa, Bapere sector), which divides Lubero territory from Tshopo Province; the Group said it could not independently confirm his death.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, with FARDC counter-offensive operations affected by troop shortages, FARDC relied increasingly on Wazalendo armed groups against ADF, including the UPLC led by "General" Germain Kambale Mayani, elements of the NDC-R of sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwissa, and a local APCLS detachment led by "General" Fimbo.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the FDLR-FOCA military commander was "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and its political leader "General" Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro); that the overall FDLR-RUD leader was "Brigadier-General" Emmanuel Nsengiyumva (alias Faida/Fayida Hakimu); and that the FDLR-FPP leader was "Colonel" Dan Hategekimana (alias Dan Simplice).

The UN Group of Experts reported a divide among Wazalendo between "old" warlords actively engaged on the frontlines, including sanctioned individual William Yakutumba (CDi.043), Makanaki Kasimbira John, Delphin Ngomanzito, René Itongwa and Ilunga, and "new" Wazalendo leaders perceived as opportunistic entrants.

place: Walikale, Masisi and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, reporting on a UN Group of Experts report, said the experts wrote that Guidon Shimiray Mwissa, head of the NDC-R and VDP commander, moved his headquarters from Pinga to Kibati in Walikale territory, that APCLS leader Janvier Karairi Boingo and troops were based at Lukweti in Masisi territory, and that the CMC-FDP led by Dominique Ndaruhutse was in Virunga National Park taking part in fighting in areas of Rutshuru territory.

Kivu Morning Post reported that Colonel Mustapha of Twirwaneho, an ally of AFC-M23, was reportedly killed in a CH-4 drone strike by the Congolese army at Rugezi in Fizi territory on Thursday 28 August 2025, according to a Wazalendo spokesperson in South Kivu, who said eleven Twirwaneho fighters died with him; it also reported that AFC-M23 and Twirwaneho fighters accused the Congolese army and its allies of launching several drone attacks in Fizi territory in violation of the ceasefire.

Actualite.cd reported that Twirwaneho was structured and militarised by Michel Rukunda, alias Makanika, a FARDC deserter who had been deputy commander at Walikale, and that he was killed in a Congolese army drone strike in Fizi in February 2025; it also reported that the group was active in the Hauts Plateaux of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga.

place: Minembwe, Hauts Plateaux, Fizi, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, quoting a Human Rights Watch report, reported that residents of Minembwe and UN and diplomatic sources said Twirwaneho had forced families to provide one fighter or pay financial compensation to the armed group, and that it carried out reprisals in case of refusal.

place: Byambwe, Bapere sector / Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: 7sur7.cd reported that MONUSCO, in a press release of 21 November 2025, condemned ADF attacks between 13 and 19 November 2025 in Lubero territory, saying at least 17 civilians, including women admitted to the maternity ward, were killed in a Catholic Church health centre at Byambwe, 60 km west of Lubero, and four pavilions housing patients were set on fire; MONUSCO also cited abductions and looting of medicines in other localities.

The US State Department spokesperson said that the United States was designating Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, and said the FDLR has carried out ethnic violence against civilians, used child soldiers, committed sexual violence and launched cross-border attacks.

place: Bukavu, Kalehe, Kamanyola, Kavumu; Hauts et Moyens-Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira, South Kivu
statement: CongoRassure reported that a new battalion, the '22ᵉ Task Force (TAFOK)', was being mobilised in the border town of Gatumba before deployment to Bukavu, bringing the total of Burundian battalions in the DRC to sixteen, five of them positioned in the Hauts et Moyens-Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira to hunt Burundian rebels; that the Burundian regiment was under the command of 'général Pontien Hakizimana, alias Mingi' and structured in four brigades of three battalions each; and that the FDNB had deployed nearly 10 000 soldiers, a strength currently fluctuating between 8 000 and 12 000.

place: Rumonge (Burundi) to Fizi territory (Bibokoboko, Point Zéro, Milimba) and Kalemie
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several concordant security sources, a new redeployment of Burundian soldiers to the DRC observed between 29 December 2025 and 4 January 2026, toward Fizi territory (Bibokoboko, Point Zéro, Milimba) and Tanganyika province, in particular Kalemie, carried out from the Burundian navy position near the Rumonge fishing port, with about ten military vehicles mobilised according to police and military sources; a soldier contacted said the main objective would be to reinforce two Burundian battalions left isolated in mountainous areas of eastern DRC.

SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several security sources, that a large part of the Burundian soldiers withdrew in December 2025 following M23 advances in South Kivu and losses suffered by the FDNB; it reported that the secretary general of the CNDD-FDD had spoken of a 'strategic withdrawal' ('retrait stratégique'), saying Burundi remained master of its military decisions, and quoted Révérien Ndikuriyo as having declared: 'it is like at home, we go there when we want'.

place: eastern DRC (parts not specified by the source)
statement: Anadolu Agency reported that the Burundian army spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, said on X that, contrary to what Reuters and social networks reported, FDNB soldiers deployed in the DRC continued to carry out their missions in their sectors of responsibility.

Iwacu reported that at a press conference on Thursday 16 January the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, rejected allegations that Burundian soldiers had been captured or killed by M23 in eastern DRC, saying those captured were not Burundians, while neither confirming nor denying casualties, which he called a military secret.

place: Kamenge military hospital, Bujumbura; North Kivu fighting
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Thursday, January 23, 2025, according to its sources, the Kamenge military hospital in Bujumbura counted 81 injured and 19 dead Burundian soldiers from fighting with M23 in Congolese territory, and that the army buried Lieutenant Patience Gapara, killed in the fighting with M23 in North Kivu; by its own estimate, 7,500 to 9,000 Burundian soldiers were on Congolese soil.

place: Kalundu port (Uvira), Bijombo (Uvira territory), Itombwe (Mwenga territory)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on 15 May 2026 several boats carrying Burundian soldiers landed in Ruzizi near the port of Kalundu in Uvira, before troops deployed to Bijombo (Uvira territory) and Itombwe (Mwenga territory), a deployment the article said was estimated (without saying by whom) at approximately two battalions, in addition to operations in April 2026 at Point Zero, Mulima, Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi and Bidegu with the FARDC and Wazalendo.

SOS Médias Burundi reported in May 2026 that the FDNB is accused by several local and international organisations of human rights violations in the Minembwe area, including road blockades, destruction of property and looting targeting civilians, and that the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged that movement restrictions could be imposed on individuals considered 'collaborators with the enemy'.

place: Kitoga, Muhuzi, Itombwe, Minembwe, Mikalati, Kipupu, Point Zero; Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories
statement: Umuryango.rw (Rwandan outlet) reported, citing SOS Medias, that vehicles carrying Burundian soldiers were seen at Kitoga, Muhuzi and in the Itombwe forest and that Burundian soldiers were reinforced in other areas including Minembwe, Mikalati, Kipupu and Point Zero in Fizi; it said, without giving a source, that there were now about 20 thousand Burundian troops in South Kivu, mostly in Uvira and Fizi.

place: eastern DRC (RDF deployment); sanctions announced in Brussels
statement: ACP (Agence Congolaise de Presse) reported that EU foreign ministers adopted sanctions including three Rwandan generals, Eugène Nkubito, Pascal Muhizi and Ruki Karusisi, describing Karusisi as commander of the special forces deployed in the DRC, and listing Nkubito as commander of the RDF 3rd Division and Muhizi as commander of the RDF 2nd Division. TRT Afrika reported that those sanctioned by the EU included special forces commander Ruki Karusisi and two army division commanders, Eugene Nkubito and Pascal Muhizi.

SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition, dateline Goma, 3 March 2026) reported that the United States announced sanctions on Monday against the RDF and four of its senior officers, whom Washington accuses of actively supporting the M23 rebellion, and that OFAC designated General Mubarakh Muganga, Major General Vincent Nyakarundi, Major General Ruki Karusisi (commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former special forces commander) and Brigadier General Stanislas Gashugi (current commander of Rwandan special forces); Kigali immediately denounced the sanctions as 'unjust' and 'unilateral'.

RFI's Invité Afrique Midi episode on the state visit of the Burundian president to Kinshasa, with Jean-Jacques Wondo, a strategy and security analyst at Afridesk, as guest, was headlined: '«On peut estimer à 10 000 le nombre de soldats burundais toujours présents au Congo»'.

place: Goma and surrounding areas, North Kivu (place not specified in the excerpt)
statement: UN News reported that OHCHR spokesperson Jeremy Laurence said OHCHR has documented summary executions of at least 12 people by the M23 between 26 and 28 January.

UN News reported, in the section of its article on the OHCHR briefing, that in other areas under M23 control in South Kivu, such as Minova, fighters have occupied schools and hospitals, forced IDPs out of camps and subjected the civilian population to forced conscription and forced labour.

UN News reported that OHCHR has documented cases of conflict-related sexual violence by the army and allied Wazalendo fighters in Kalehe territory, South Kivu, and is verifying reports that 52 women were raped by Congolese troops in South Kivu, including alleged reports of gangrape.
UN News reported that DRC officials report at least 165 women were raped by male inmates during the mass prison break from Goma's Muzenze prison on 27 January, as M23 began its assault on the town.

UN News reported that OHCHR spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani said OHCHR had confirmed cases of summary execution of children by M23 after they entered the city of Bukavu, and that OHCHR was also aware that children were in possession of weapons.

UN News reported that the OHCHR spokesperson condemned attacks on hospitals and humanitarian warehouses as well as threats against the judiciary, directly linked to the rapid advance of the M23 fighters across North Kivu and South Kivu.

place: Kabare and Bukavu central prisons, South Kivu
statement: UN News reported that OHCHR spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani noted break-outs from Kabare and Bukavu central prisons on 14 February.

UN News reported that UNHCR spokesperson Eujin Byun said that in South Kivu more than half of the aid groups providing critical support to survivors of sexual violence report being unable to reach those in need due to insecurity and continuous displacement.

UN News reported that UNHCR spokesperson Eujin Byun said that in North Kivu the destruction of health facilities, including mortuaries, and overcrowded hospitals increase the risk of spreading infectious diseases, including cholera, malaria, and measles.

UN News reported, in a passage on humanitarian assessments in Goma, that WHO and partners, after an assessment with the Government over the past five days, reported that 700 people had been killed and 2,800 injured were receiving treatment in health facilities, with numbers expected to rise.

place: DRC-wide (conflict provinces include North and South Kivu)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) said in a communiqué that it documented 2.767 human rights violations and abuses and IHL violations across the whole territory of the DRC in the first half of 2025.

Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report on the first half of 2025 accuses State agents of responsibility for sexual violence against 70 victims, including the FARDC (69 victims) and PNC agents (one victim).

place: DRC; North Kivu and South Kivu account for close to 80% of victims
statement: ONU Info reported that, according to BCNUDH data, 887 cases of conflict-related sexual violence were documented the previous year, affecting 1,534 victims, including 854 women and 672 girls, and that North and South Kivu account for close to 80 per cent of documented victims.

ONU Info reported that, per the BCNUDH report, armed groups are responsible for 75 per cent of conflict-related sexual violence victims the previous year, with the M23 first at 439 victims, followed by Wazalendo groups, and that State actors including FARDC, the Police nationale congolaise and the Agence nationale de renseignement were involved in 19 per cent of documented cases.

ONU Info reported that, per the BCNUDH report, 70 per cent of conflict-related sexual violence victims have access to emergency medical care but fewer than 2 per cent receive holistic care including legal, psychological and social support.
Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH recorded 61 victims of conflict-related sexual violence in January 2026, a 59 per cent drop from December 2025.
Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report notes that 42 political actors were still detained in January 2026, amid arrests judged arbitrary.

place: North Kivu (52 victims), South Kivu (12), Ituri (8)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH documented 46 cases of conflict-related sexual violence in June 2026, against 40 in May, affecting 73 victims (56 women, 15 girls and 2 men), of whom North Kivu accounts for 52 and South Kivu 12, and that the AFC/M23 is cited for 34 victims.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (109 health centres studied)
statement: The ICRC reported that violence and fighting in North and South Kivu hinder the movement of sick people, limit the transport of the wounded and make medical supplies hard to deliver, and have led to health-care workers leaving and medical facilities being looted or destroyed.

Radio Okapi reported on 17 February 2025 that calm had returned to the city of Uvira after clashes that caused the death of 12 people, civilians and soldiers, and that the violence broke out the day before after an altercation between FARDC soldiers and a group of Wazalendo fighters. It cited Serge Kigwati, president of the Société civile des nationalistes congolais, as saying the altercation began when the Wazalendo tried to disarm soldiers returning from the northern front and heading south, and the FARDC refused to hand over their weapons.

place: Kalundu port, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: MediaCongo reported that live-fire exchanges shook the city of Uvira on Sunday 16 February 2025 at the Kalundu port, where it said the FARDC and the Wazalendo clashed, the Wazalendo trying to prevent the FARDC from boarding a boat bound for Kalemie.

Actualite.cd reported that at least 17 people were killed on Tuesday and Wednesday in the city of Uvira in spontaneous clashes between Congolese soldiers and Wazalendo militiamen (its headline says about ten dead; the local source it quotes gives a toll of more than 17 civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo combined), and quoted an unnamed local source who said the Wazalendo refused to let soldiers leave for Kalemie with weapons and ammunition, and that soldiers seized phones, money and other goods, broke down doors and shot civilians who resisted.

place: Uvira central prison, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that all detainees of the Uvira prison (named 'prison Mulunge d’Uvira' in the article) escaped that morning, and that the mass escape from the central prison of Uvira was confirmed notably by sources of the local Catholic church. A local activist told Actualite.cd that the prison doors were broken by fleeing soldiers who wanted to free their detained comrades and that other civilians also left.

Agenzia Fides reported that the state authorities had even decided to release the prisoners before the rebels' arrival in Uvira, and that the withdrawal of Burundian soldiers a few days after the fall of Bukavu would have favoured the rebels' advance towards Uvira.

Radio Okapi reported that after taking Bukavu and Kamanyola, the rebels conquered the cité of Sange, about 30 kilometres from Uvira, on Wednesday 19 February, and described the M23 as supported by the Rwandan army.

Radio Okapi reported that acts of pillage and violence were reported in Uvira, that armed persons were looting and ransacking shops and homes, and that the office of the Uvira bishopric was vandalised and priests and the bishop were assaulted and robbed of their belongings. It said local sources attributed these acts to FARDC soldiers and to undisciplined Wazalendo fighters.

place: Episcopal seat, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: Vatican News reported that on Thursday 20 February three FARDC soldiers entered the episcopal seat of Uvira, forcing Mgr Muyengo Mulombe and two priests to hand over their phones and cash, and that the priests named in the article are Ricardo Mukuninwa and Bernard Kalolero.

place: Uvira city quarters (Kimanga, Nyamianda, Kabindula, Kilibula, Songo, Mulongwe) and Kalundu port, South Kivu
statement: Kivutimes reported that night attacks by 'uncontrolled soldiers' were wreaking havoc in Uvira, notably in the Kimanga, Nyamianda, Kabindula, Kilibula, Songo and Mulongwe quarters, despite measures taken by the military authorities of the Sokola 2 Sud operational sector. It added, citing sources close to the institutions, that on Thursday 20 February these soldiers looted the CENI warehouse in Uvira and a Bralima depot at the Kalundu port.

Actualite.cd, in an article built on a message by the Bishop of Uvira, reported that banks, pharmacies, markets and health centres had closed in Uvira, and quoted Mgr Sébastien-Joseph Muyengo Mulombe describing systematic looting with violence and killings, including in family homes and convents.

place: Hôpital Général de Référence, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: MSF said that the Hôpital Général de Référence in Uvira had repeatedly been caught in crossfire, endangering patients and staff, that medical activities had to be interrupted again the previous week with patients sheltering, and that armed men entered the hospital premises, moving and firing inside.

MSF said that it had been forced to reduce its teams in Uvira, where they had supported the Ministry of Health in diagnosing and treating mpox patients for several months, and that it redirected part of its activity to supporting the care of war wounded by delivering medical supplies to several health structures in the Uvira health zone.
MSF stated that Burundian authorities now estimated at 35'000 the number of people who would have been displaced since the start of February.

OCHA said it was alarmed by the escalation of violence and insecurity in Uvira, and that clashes and rising crime were putting local communities and humanitarian workers in extreme danger, with humanitarian partners reporting multiple incidents of looting and sexual violence.

place: Uvira city and the Ruzizi plain, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu operation, Jérémie Meya (lieutenant Jérémie Meya Gbe), said the FARDC had begun an operation to track down fleeing soldiers and alleged perpetrators of various harassments in Uvira, with the stated aim of 'cleaning' Uvira and the localities of the Ruzizi plain so the population could go about its business safely.

Actualite.cd reported that over the previous few days at least 20 dead and more than 60 people wounded by bullets had been taken in charge in the Uvira health zone, and that humanitarian organisations had recorded a toll of about a hundred wounded; it did not say whether the dead and wounded were civilians or combatants, or who caused the casualties.

place: Uvira city (Kavimvira border post), South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that political-administrative authorities, FARDC soldiers and police settled in the city of Uvira on Monday 24 February, and that governor Jean-Jacques Pulusi, his deputy and about 600 uniformed men, including police and soldiers, who had left Bukavu some days earlier for Burundi, arrived in Uvira through the Kavimvira border.

Radio Okapi reported, citing the communication cell of the South Kivu governor, that the provincial executive head and his deputy were now staying in Uvira and would continue to administer South Kivu from there because Bukavu, the capital, was under rebel occupation.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources on Saturday 29 March, that cohabitation between the FARDC and the Wazalendo was becoming difficult, notably in Uvira, and that the two parties had set up two parallel commands, which made operational coordination difficult.

place: Songo, Kabindula and Nyamianda quarters, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several witnesses, that Wazalendo-affiliated fighters under the command of 'generals Mayele and Makanaki' had multiplied acts of pillage in the Songo, Kabindula and Nyamianda quarters of Uvira, targeting the Banyamulenge community, and that some Wazalendo justified the attacks by accusing the Banyamulenge of complicity with the M23; a community leader it quoted rejected that accusation as false.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Friday 21 March 2025 Wazalendo fighters attacked the premises of the organisation Ebenezer International Ministry in Uvira, taking several electronic devices, including computers and Motorola phones.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that the vice-governor of South Kivu, Jean Jacques Elekano, condemned the violence against the Banyamulenge in Uvira and called for respect for all communities, saying in a communiqué that surveillance had been reinforced and calling on law enforcement to act firmly against these abuses.

Human Rights Watch reported that on 14 February Wazalendo fighters killed a 25-year-old Munyamulenge man in Mulongwe, Uvira territory, after accusing him of being Rwandan; he was shot twice in the hip and died of his wounds, according to two sources.

Human Rights Watch reported that after the M23 took Bukavu, Wazalendo fighters entered more than 20 Banyamulenge homes in Uvira, stealing property and threatening residents, and that in one case they shot a woman in the head and beat at least three people.

Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March in Sange, Uvira territory, a Wazalendo commander arrested and whipped a 48-year-old man accused of stealing a television, and that a relative and a neighbour said the man died of his injuries.

place: Bibokoboko area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March Wazalendo fighters attacked several Banyamulenge villages within 10 km of Bibokoboko, Fizi territory, and that a military source and residents said there was no known presence of opposing armed groups near Bibokoboko at the time.

place: Bibokoboko area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch quoted a community leader as saying, of the 3 March Wazalendo attack around Bibokoboko in Fizi territory, that the fighters said they had come to 'clean' the Banyamulenge, killed seven people and destroyed homes, medical centres and schools.

place: Uvira general hospital, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing hospital sources, that the Uvira health zone faced an outbreak of cholera among soldiers, with at least 40 cases hospitalised in the cholera treatment unit of the Uvira general hospital, and a medical official quoted as saying the unit was completely overwhelmed with patients lying on the floor.

place: Military garrison tribunal, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that at least 90 soldiers from the North and South Kivu fronts had been appearing since Wednesday 12 February before the military garrison tribunal of Uvira on various counts, notably fleeing before the M23 and extortion.

place: Rurambo and Kigarama, Bafuliro chiefdom, Uvira territory (highlands), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels took control of the villages Rurambo and Kigarama, in the Bafuliro chiefdom in the Uvira highlands, following the allegiance of the Rushaba wazalendo group to the AFC/M23.

place: Kashama, Kigarama and Uvira highlands, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said Rushaba had been with Nyamusaraba in the 'Task force' together with the Burundian forces before deserting it, starting clashes at Kashama and allying with the M23. The article describes the Task force as composed of Congolese soldiers, Burundian soldiers and wazalendo, and quotes another source on site as saying there was a coalition of Banyamulenge based in Kahololo/Marungu, Rushaba wazalendo and M23 elements from Kaziba.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Minembwe group of villages in Fizi territory fell on Friday into the hands of fighters of the armed group Twirwaneho, two days after the death of Colonel Makanika, the group's military chief, killed in a drone attack. Citing witnesses, it said Twirwaneho fighters occupied all FARDC positions in several named localities, and a Twirwaneho fighter told the outlet that the soldiers had abandoned several weapons and ammunition.

SOS Médias Burundi quoted residents of Minembwe, who came out to celebrate Twirwaneho's capture of the area (which the article, dated 23 February 2025, places 'ce vendredi'), as saying that FARDC soldiers and Maï-Maï militiamen had looted their cows, killed people, stolen from fields and houses and raped their women and girls; the residents gave no dates, places or numbers for these acts, and the article sets them in a context of insecurity it dates to 2017. It said it tried without success to reach a FARDC spokesperson.

place: Kamanyola / Ruzizi plain towards Uvira, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the rebels' advance, after their capture of Bukavu and Kamanyola, came as Burundian troops began to withdraw from Congolese soil, after having fought alongside the FARDC and the Wazalendo under bilateral cooperation between the Burundian and Congolese governments.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that at least a hundred Congolese police officers had fled to Burundi from Uvira, as announced on Wednesday in Bujumbura by the Burundian minister in charge of internal affairs.

BBC News Afrique reported that Wazalendo fighters reportedly wanted to seize the Congolese army's weapons and ammunition, accusing the soldiers of having deserted the front lines and fallen back south to Kalemie. An unnamed source told the BBC that the Wazalendo rose up to oppose the abuses of the regular army and asked the regular troops to give them their weapons, and that about 15 000 Congolese had crossed into Burundi. The BBC said it could not independently verify this information.

Human Rights Watch reported that military, humanitarian and other sources expressed concern about the lack of command and control by the Congolese army over the Wazalendo, who in some cases were said to have even disarmed or attacked soldiers.

place: Mulongwe (commercial centre), Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing several of its sources, that two groups of Wazalendo militiamen led by self-proclaimed generals René Makanaki and Itongwa (head of the Landa Bango group) fought each other on Saturday 5 April in the Mulongwe commercial centre and its surroundings in Uvira; a local civil society actor said some wounded were taken to the Uvira general referral hospital (HGR), and the sources said Néné Rubota, spokesperson of a synergy of Wazalendo armed groups led by General Gashumba, was shot and wounded.
Actualite.cd reported that, for several days, Wazalendo of different groups controlled the city of Uvira, which it described as the provisional capital of South Kivu.

place: Uvira city and surroundings, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC reported in its final report that from February, as DRC authorities and security actors largely withdrew from Uvira, Wazalendo armed groups took de facto control of Uvira city and its surroundings, used disproportionate force and committed widespread abuses, targeting Banyamulenge communities in particular.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, to restore security, the FARDC headquarters and the South Kivu governorate were relocated to Uvira in early March, and that in early April DRC Defence Minister Guy Kabombo and former RAD national coordinator General Padiri travelled from Bujumbura to Uvira to appease the Wazalendo groups.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, at a meeting, Wazalendo factions complained of lack of support, military logistics and funding, and that to calm them the Defence Minister announced that all Wazalendo leaders would be placed under the authority of the RAD.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil society, that DRC Defence Minister Guy Kabombo announced in Uvira on Monday 7 April that the local Wazalendo fighters supporting the army in defending the city depend exclusively from now on on the national coordinator of the Armed Defence Reserve (RAD), General Padiri Bulenda.

place: Uvira (arrival at Kavimvira border), South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that during his visit to Uvira on a Monday (dateline 7 April 2025), Defence Minister Guy Kabombo, accompanied by Lieutenant General Padiri Bulenda (national coordinator of the Wazalendo) and a Burundian army delegation, praised the commitment of the Burundian army, the Burundian National Defence Force (FDNB); SOS Médias Burundi stated in its own narration that the FDNB had deployed nearly 10.000 soldiers in the DRC.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that during the Defence Minister's visit to Uvira (dateline 7 April 2025), fighters complained that the Burundian army had reportedly forbidden them from attacking M23 positions at Kamanyola, and that Defence Minister Guy Kabombo replied that the restrictions aimed to avoid uncoordinated actions that could compromise joint operations, while reaffirming the Congolese government's confidence in the FDNB.

place: Kavimvira post, Kalundu port, Uvira, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that during the Defence Minister's visit to Uvira (dateline 7 April 2025), abuses were reported, notably illegal tax levies at the Kavimvira post, Kalundu port and along the road axes.

Radio Okapi reported that the new commander of the 33rd military region, General Dunia, began on Tuesday 8 April the identification of Wazalendo fighters in Uvira, to distinguish genuine from false Wazalendo and give the government a list of those deserving benefits.

place: Rugenge and the hills above Uvira, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that FARDC and Wazalendo exchanged fire from Thursday 24 April at Rugenge and in the heights of Uvira, over occupation of certain positions; sources quoted said the cause was a camp-management dispute.

Actualite.cd reported that the army described the gunfire as a redeployment of its forces: a communiqué signed by Lieutenant Elongo Kyondwa Marc, spokesperson of the Sukola 2 operational sector, said the shots heard in the hills overlooking Uvira were due to loyalist soldiers redeploying on different ridges to ensure maximum protection of the city.

place: Uvira hills; Katongo to Hauts Plateaux of Fizi, South Kivu
statement: MediaCongo, relaying Radio Okapi and MCP, reported that on Friday 25 April heavy gunfire between FARDC and Wazalendo shook Uvira again; Sukola 2 Sud-Sud spokesperson Lieutenant Marc Elongo said the fighting was linked to the redeployment of FARDC from Katongo to the Hauts Plateaux of Fizi, and that the Wazalendo, displeased, expressed opposition by firing, suspecting this regular army unit of collaborating with rebels in the Fizi Hauts Plateaux.

place: Kasenga and Kakombe, hills overlooking Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that FARDC and their wazalendo allies clashed again on the morning of Thursday 1 May in two neighbourhoods of Uvira: according to local sources fighting began about 5:00 a.m. at Kasenga and spread to the hills overlooking the city; shooting stopped in the city centre around 10:00 but continued in the surrounding hills. The reasons given by different sources were control and management of certain positions in and around the city.

place: Kasenga, Kavimvira and Mulongwe communes, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that calm returned on Friday 2 May in the communes of Kasenga, Kavimvira and Mulongwe in Uvira, 24 hours after fighting between the FARDC and Wazalendo; according to local sources the clash wounded civilians, but the number of victims was not specified.

Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Sud-Sud operations confirmed that the points of divergence had been smoothed out and that the FARDC were securing the city, upstream and downstream, describing a misunderstanding maintained by a small group of Wazalendo.

place: Kasenga and Kakombe hills, Kituntu, Uvira, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the South Kivu provincial administration continued to publicly deny any clash between FARDC and Wazalendo in the Uvira region, that it had received no official statement from the local FARDC command despite repeated attempts to contact it, and, citing several local testimonies, that the hostilities were triggered by an FARDC attempt to install new military positions at Kituntu, about ten kilometres from Uvira.

place: Katogota, Kamanyola, hills of Rutebe, Kayange and Luzinzi, Ruzizi plain (Uvira/Walungu border), South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that fighting broke out between Wazalendo and AFC/M23 rebels in the territories of Uvira and Walungu, with the agglomerations of Katogota and Kamanyola in a spiral of violence since Monday 5 May; according to local sources the Wazalendo launched a surprise attack first on forward M23 positions, the clashes lasted eight hours on the hills of Rutebe, Kayange and Luzinzi, civilians were wounded, and both sides suffered losses according to a human rights activist.

place: Uvira (Kavimvira crossing, Sokola 2 Sud operational sector), South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on the Wednesday before its publication the FARDC chief of staff, Lieutenant General Jules Banza Mwilambwe, and his Burundian counterpart, General Prime Niyongabo, head of the FDNB, crossed the border at Kavimvira escorted by a large Burundian military contingent and headed to the 'Sokola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu' operational sector, where they held a closed meeting; they left around 16:50 for Bujumbura without a statement to the press.

place: Katogota and Kamanyola areas, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that tensions between FARDC, Wazalendo militias and Burundian troops were worsening notably in the Katogota and Kamanyola areas, and that Wazalendo militiamen accuse certain Burundian units of slowing their offensives against the M23.

place: Ruzizi Plain, Uvira and Hauts Plateaux (near Minembwe), South Kivu
