statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 approximately 14 FDNB battalions under the 'Task Force Congo' (TAFOC) umbrella were still on DRC territory, of which 10 were reportedly in the Ruzizi Plain, two in and around Uvira and two in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that FARDC, FDNB and intelligence sources estimated at least 7,000 troops in South Kivu.

place: Kamanyola - Sange - Uvira road, Ruzizi plain, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its final report, the AFC/M23 controlled mining areas in Kalehe, Walungu and Mwenga territories as far as Kamanyola in the south, while the FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo kept control of the Ruzizi plain and held positions along the Kamanyola-Sange-Uvira road, blocking the AFC/M23 advance towards Uvira.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its report, relations between FARDC and Wazalendo had improved and some Wazalendo groups had left the centre of Uvira at the request of FARDC command.

Radio Okapi reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Pulusi returned to Uvira, the provisional capital of the province, on Tuesday 20 May after four months' absence, and, in an address to residents, said he carried a message from the head of state announcing the 'beginning of the end' of the M23 war; a local civil society actor said that for them the end of the war means the withdrawal of the rebels from occupied territories, among other things.

place: South Kivu (resident quoted is from Uvira)
statement: Human Rights Watch said that in April it received credible information of Wazalendo fighters beating and whipping men and women they accused of having acted inappropriately, and quoted an Uvira resident as saying that some Wazalendo act as if they were the police.

Human Rights Watch reported that South Kivu's interim governor, Jean-Jacques Elakano, told media on 23 April that the province could not collect taxes because of Wazalendo fighters, who should not 'substitute for the State'; HRW also reported that in March and April Wazalendo set up roadblocks on main roads linking several South Kivu towns, where they harassed residents and collected 500 to 1 000 Congolese francs per person.

place: Uvira city (Kalundu port, Kavimvira border post), South Kivu
statement: Imurenge.com, a Banyamulenge community website, reported that, since February 2025, reports indicate that over 40 Banyamulenge individuals in Uvira had been assaulted and robbed, one young man killed and a woman seriously injured, and that Wazalendo militias were preventing many Banyamulenge from returning to work at Kalundu port and the Kavimvira border post.

place: Road to Bijombo, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, that Banyamulenge police officers, teachers and women travelling towards Bijombo in Uvira territory were arrested, tortured and stripped of their belongings by Wazalendo elements on Wednesday 11 June 2025 (date per the photo caption), the victims including seven police officers, four teachers and two women; the victims said they were intercepted by men of the self-proclaimed generals Landabango and Alexis Dunia while on the road to Bijombo under escort of Burundian soldiers, and the Wazalendo reportedly then arrested them, accusing them of belonging to the M23. The outlet reported that police officers and teachers were freed through the intervention of the deputy mayor of the city of Uvira.

place: Kasenga, Kavimvira, Kilibula, Kawizi, Kiliba (Uvira territory); Mulongwe and Lusenda camps; Sange transit centre, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that more and more young Burundians were joining Wazalendo militias in Uvira territory, with testimonies in the neighbourhoods of Kasenga, Kavimvira, Kilibula, Kawizi and Kiliba, and that some refugees from the Mulongwe and Lusenda camps or the Sange transit centre had also been seen in Wazalendo ranks; it also cited regional security sources saying nearly 10,000 Burundian soldiers, supported by Imbonerakure, were officially in the DRC.

place: Uvira and Ruzizi health zones, South Kivu
statement: MSF said that since February, in collaboration with the health ministry, it had treated nearly 400 war-wounded and 800 cholera cases in three dedicated treatment centres in South Kivu, and that Uvira was hosting more than 250 000 displaced people since the start of the fighting.

place: Bukavu - Kamanyola - Uvira road, South Kivu
statement: MSF said that persistent insecurity had made the road between Bukavu, Kamanyola and Uvira almost impassable, making it impossible for humanitarian organisations to move between the two sides of the front line, and MSF reported adapting by crossing different countries to bring aid and provide care on each side.
MSF's medical lead in Uvira, Dr Aurora Revuelta, said MSF had intensified its response to strengthen capacity to care for war wounds, cholera cases and victims and survivors of sexual violence.

MSF said that Kamanyola, close to Katogota, was under M23/AFC control and had also seen its health system weakened by violence, and that while some stability had been restored in the town, most fighting continued in the surrounding hills, making access to fields impossible.

Actualite.cd reported that the UN Deputy Special Representative and Humanitarian Coordinator Bruno Lemarquis, in Uvira since 28 June, said the UN was there to assess security for the physical return of UN agencies to South Kivu, to study humanitarian access and the mechanisms for opening a humanitarian corridor, and to consider support to the provincial institutions provisionally installed in Uvira.

Actualite.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean Jacques Purusi, based in Uvira since the fall of Bukavu to the M23, said Lemarquis's visit proved that peace, stability and security were returning, and that the authorities would do everything to eradicate the multiple barriers erected in places to facilitate the opening of a humanitarian corridor so that the population, including in areas occupied by the 'aggressors', could receive medicines, food and other assistance.

place: Luvungi bridge on the Bukavu-Uvira route (Luvingi), Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, in a 17-minute audio message broadcast on 19 July, General Makanaki (Makanaki Kasimbira John, described by the outlet as an influential Wazalendo figure) said that any truck coming from Bukavu must be burned by the Wazalendo and would not pass the Luvingi bridge, saying 'These are the trucks that bring the M23'; the outlet described the convoy as 55 trucks of food and medicine for displaced people in Uvira, and South Kivu governor Jean Jacques Purusi had said an agreement had been reached between all parties concerned.

place: Hôpital général de référence d'Uvira, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Médecins sans frontières announced in a communiqué of Friday 25 July the end of its mission in Uvira from the end of July 2025, ending care for new war-wounded patients and cholera patients at the Hôpital général de référence d'Uvira; MSF cited the attainment of the medical objectives set when the project began in November 2024.

place: Uvira, Shabunda, Kalemie (as named in the communiqué)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on the previous Sunday, the M23-AFC coalition denounced the reinforcement of government troops on several axes, notably Shabunda, Uvira and Kalemie, and accused the Congolese authorities of violating the ceasefire.

place: Ruzizi plain beyond Uvira; Nyangezi–Kamanyola axis, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on the southern axis the FARDC and Wazalendo control a large portion of the Ruzizi plain beyond the city of Uvira, while the rebels keep their hold on the Nyangezi–Kamanyola axis and on certain localities of the Ruzizi plain chiefdom; according to concordant sources cited by Radio Okapi, the rebel coalition's troops were redeploying with heavy equipment towards the Walungu and Uvira axes to consolidate their positions.

Radio Okapi reported that a FARDC soldier was shot dead and several civilians were wounded after an altercation on Monday 25 August between the FARDC and Wazalendo fighters at Mulongwe, Uvira territory; according to local sources it was triggered by a dispute over the control of vehicles carrying people from Burundi who had come for the burial of a colonel, and the Sokola 2 South Kivu spokesperson said the soldier was hit by a stray bullet while protecting the convoy.

place: Kavimvira and Kasenga quarters, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Tuesday the border town of Uvira saw violent clashes between the FARDC and the local Wazalendo militias, concentrated in the Kavimvira and Kasenga quarters; bodies of both sides were lying along the road linking Kasenga to Kavimvira.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that the spokesperson of the South Kivu provincial government, Luganywa Bashizi Didier Kabi, relayed the position of governor Jean Jacques Purusi, who condemned the oral and physical violence of the previous two days in certain quarters of Uvira.

Radio Okapi reported that the Wazalendo and the army had clashed on 25 August over the arrival of a delegation from Burundi for the funeral of colonel Patrick, who had recently died, and that, according to the military authorities, these clashes caused the death of at least five Wazalendo fighters and the arrest of fourteen others.

Afrikarabia reported that President Félix Tshisekedi's appointment of General Olivier Gasita as deputy commander of the 33rd military region, and his taking up duty in Uvira on 1 September, were at the heart of the unrest, with civil society organisations and above all the Wazalendo militias leading the protest; SOS Médias Burundi reported that General Gasita was entrenched in an Uvira hotel under the joint protection of the FARDC and of 'militaires burundais'.
SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing local sources, that General Gasita arrived in Uvira escorted by Burundian soldiers of the FDNB as well as FARDC elements.

place: Axes towards the Burundi border and Kalundu port, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that since 2 September the local 'forces vives' and Wazalendo combatants had erected barricades on strategic axes, notably towards the Burundian border, paralysing cross-border trade and lake operations at Kalundu port, and that, according to several sources, the port was under the exclusive surveillance of the Wazalendo.

Radio Okapi reported that the Nouvelle société civile congolaise announced a partial suspension of the strike from Friday 5 September, after three days of a movement launched by Wazalendo combatants and citizen movements against the appointment of General Olivier Gasita as commander of operations and intelligence.

Radio Okapi reported that the Wazalendo accuse General Gasita of being a double agent serving the M23 rebellion and of having played a decisive role in the take of Bukavu by that armed group in February 2025.

Afrikarabia reported that the deputy Justin Bitakwira, who is also coordinator of the Wazalendo in South Kivu, accuses General Gasita of collusion with the M23 and of having delivered a speech calling on the Wazalendo to let the rebels pass, which would have facilitated the fall of Bukavu.

Radio Okapi reported, according to concordant sources, that on 2 September at Kalungwe two civilians, including a moto-taxi driver and his client, were wounded by a bullet fired by a Wazalendo fighter after refusing to take part in the demonstration that day.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local medical sources, that three civilians, including two moto-tricycle drivers, wounded during the Wazalendo demonstrations against General Gasita's appointment died on Thursday 4 September.

Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on Thursday, the deputy mayor of Uvira, Kifara Kapenda, deplored the disturbances to public order, called for the end of the demonstrations while saying the demonstrators' demands had been heard, and invited the organisers to an emergency meeting on Friday 5 September.

Radio Okapi reported that violent clashes between the FARDC and the Wazalendo had been reported, causing two new civilian deaths according to local civil society, and that a meeting between urban authorities, military leaders and demonstrators had produced no significant progress.
SOS Médias Burundi reported that a 5-year-old child died in an explosion during the night of 6 to 7 September in Uvira.

place: Kabindula quarter, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Mutualité des Banyamulenge denounced in a communiqué acts of discrimination, physical violence and intimidation, including women and girls beaten in Kabindula and denial of access to drinking water, some demonstrators saying 'Allez puiser au Rwanda'.
SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Mutualité des Banyamulenge denounced the abduction of a FARDC soldier and a policeman, both Banyamulenge.

Afrikarabia reported that a Wazalendo official issued a call giving '10 jours aux Tutsi d’Uvira pour quitter la ville', and that Kinshasa said it did not know the author of the message, which could be 'une manipulation'.

place: Uvira city (town hall, Sokola 2 headquarters), South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, according to local sources, at least 5 people were killed and about twenty wounded, several seriously, after FARDC fire to disperse demonstrators in Uvira on 8 September, while the FARDC's official version, per the same page, was one 12-year-old child killed by a stray bullet and 9 wounded (4 soldiers and 5 civilians).

Radio Okapi reported that, according to the spokesperson of operations Sokola 2, sub-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, the disturbances in Uvira left 1 dead (a 12-year-old child hit by a bullet) and 9 wounded (4 FARDC soldiers and 5 civilians); Radio Okapi reported that the incidents broke out when demonstrators deemed uncontrolled tried to force the entrance of a military base, and that one of them was reportedly caught with a grenade, according to the military authorities; civil society denounced a violent repression and called on the President of the Republic to intervene.

place: Kimanga quarter near the town hall, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that automatic-weapon fire was heard for at least twenty minutes, at around 10 o'clock local time, near the Uvira town hall in the Kimanga quarter on Monday 8 September 2025, that law enforcement elements were firing in the air to disperse demonstrators, and that several sources spoke of dead and wounded among civilians and the security forces.

Radio Okapi reported that the demonstrations, organised by civil society and supported by Wazalendo fighters, had been violently repressed by the FARDC; that at least eight people died during the successive demonstrations in Uvira and about ten were wounded, including soldiers; and that the bishop of Uvira, Mgr Sébastien Moyengo, had condemned the disproportionate use of force against civilians.

Radio Okapi reported, citing military sources, that General Olivier Gasita left Uvira at dawn on Tuesday 9 September at around 3 a.m., without other details on his real destination; Afrikarabia reported that he was exfiltrated from Uvira to Bujumbura and then Kinshasa.

Radio Okapi reported that social and economic activities resumed on Wednesday 10 September in Uvira, 24 hours after General Gasita's departure, with shops reopening and public transport resuming, while schools remained closed because parents feared new demonstrations.

Actualite.cd reported that after an inter-institutional meeting chaired on Monday 8 September in Kinshasa by President Félix Tshisekedi, National Assembly president Vital Kamerhe said the Head of State is preoccupied by the Uvira tensions and seeks solutions through a government mission sent to Uvira.

Radio Okapi reported that a government delegation led by Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani was in Uvira with the mission of reconciling local communities, easing tensions and restoring state authority; the delegation also included Aimé Boji (Industry), Floribert Anzuluni (Regional Cooperation), Eliezer Ntambwe (minister delegate for Defence in charge of veterans), FARDC chief of staff General Jules Banza and national police commissioner general Benjamin Alongaboni. SOS Médias Burundi reported that Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo arrived escorted by Burundian and Congolese soldiers.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that the FARDC spokesperson, Major General Sylvain Ekenge, firmly rejected the demonstrators' demands, saying the Wazalendo have no instruction to give within the Armed Forces of the DRC and calling on the 'real' Wazalendo not to fall into the enemy's trap.

Afrikarabia reported that the spokesperson of the Congolese army supported General Olivier Gasita, saying that a soldier does not belong to communities and that 'un militaire communautaire n’existe pas'.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Wazalendo militias criticise the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB), present in Uvira as part of bilateral military cooperation, for not conducting offensives against the M23.

The SOS Torture Burundi Justice Newsletter stated that Burundi reportedly deployed an additional contingent of 700 soldiers to Uvira on August 21, 2025, to reinforce more than 24 battalions of Burundian soldiers already deployed in eastern DRC to counter the advance of the M23.

place: Mulongwe camp, Kavimvira transit centre (Uvira), South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in recent weeks 332 Burundian refugees in 74 households, who had lived in the Mulongwe and Lusenda camps and the Kavimvira transit centre in South Kivu, were repatriated to Burundi via the Gatumba border post; refugees trying to farm at Kahwizi and Kiliba reported being attacked, and a refugee, Niyonkuru, said that Wazalendo militiamen attack them on the way to the fields.

A UN Peacebuilding Support Office briefing on the DRC (September 2025) stated that Uvira had been at the center of tensions, both in relation to a possible AFC/M23 advance and to growing strain between the FARDC and wazalendo factions.

Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué published from Goma, AFC/M23 communication head Lawrence Kanyuka warned that AFC/M23 'will no longer tolerate the barbaric surge of hate speech in Uvira, in Ituri and in the rest of the DRC'.

place: Runingu border crossing, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the movement (identified in the quoted passage as MRDP-Twirwaneho) affirms that Burundian troops and FDLR elements crossed the border at Runingu to reinforce the FARDC and Wazalendo in the area, and that it wrote that the presence of foreign troops worsens the security and humanitarian crisis.

Human Rights Watch reported that on 10 December 2025 M23 and Rwandan forces entered Uvira after several days of fighting in South Kivu, and that witnesses said hostilities in the city had largely ended when these forces took control.

Afrikarabia reported that AFC/M23 rebels had entered Uvira on Tuesday evening, and that testimonies on site spoke of the flight of civil and military authorities during that day while the rebellion was at Kiliba, some fifteen kilometres north of Uvira.
BBC reported that the M23 said it had 'liberated' the city of Uvira, while South Kivu Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told local media that the army and allied militia remained in control of the city.

Al Jazeera reported, citing its correspondent in Uvira, that government forces and allied militias known as Wazalendo, which had been using the city as a headquarters, began fleeing even before M23 fighters entered.

place: Between Bukavu and Uvira, South Kivu
statement: Al Jazeera reported that regional authorities said at least 400 civilians, including children, had been killed in violence between the cities of Bukavu and Uvira, both then under M23 control.

Human Rights Watch reported that it documented 62 cases of summary executions and unlawful killings in Uvira during the M23 and Rwandan-forces occupation, the victims being 54 men, 2 women, 5 boys and one girl.

place: Kasenga and Rugenge, Uvira (city), South Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch reported that residents said that during the occupation of Uvira, M23 and Rwandan forces carried out systematic searches in several areas, in particular the Kasenga and Rugenge neighbourhoods.

Human Rights Watch reported that it documented rapes and other sexual violence by M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers against women and girls, and that survivors described being raped under threat of being killed, with a firearm pointed at them, at home or in the fields.

Human Rights Watch reported that the lack of operational health services in Uvira during the occupation left survivors of sexual violence without access to essential care, including HIV post-exposure prophylaxis.

Human Rights Watch reported that M23 abducted a number of men and boys, often near military bases in Uvira, with no mention of a link to the Wazalendo, and that HRW considers they were probably forcibly recruited into M23.
The Union des femmes des médias pour la paix (UFMP), in a report cited by Deutsche Welle, recorded 183 cases of rape in December in the city of Uvira, followed by 220 in January and 626 in February.

place: Sange to Uvira, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: The ICRC reported that an ICRC and DRC Red Cross team evacuated 21 people wounded by weapons, seven of them children, over 40 km to Uvira, where they were being treated by medical teams of the ICRC-supported Uvira general referral hospital; the ICRC said the fighting of the past week in Uvira, Walungu, Mwenga and Fizi territories made rescue and transfer of the wounded extremely difficult.

place: Uvira, Bukavu and Fizi hospitals, South Kivu
statement: The ICRC reported that, between 2 and 16 December, more than 193 people wounded by weapons were treated in hospitals it supports, 110 of them at the Uvira general referral hospital (HGR), 63 at the Bukavu provincial general referral hospital and 20 at the Fizi general referral hospital.
UN News reported that the UN deputy spokesperson said humanitarian partners reported more than 200,000 people displaced across South Kivu and at least 70 civilians killed in the current escalation.

UN News reported that between 5 and 8 December nearly 25,000 people crossed the border into Burundi, including Congolese nationals, returning Burundians and third-country migrants, and that in Uvira at least 32 WFP-supported schools suspended classes to house displaced families, depriving more than 12,000 children of school meals, the UN Deputy Spokesperson said.

place: Uvira (city), South Kivu and Burundi border
statement: BBC Afrique reported that, according to the UN, the Uvira offensive caused dozens of deaths, at least 100 wounded and more than 200,000 displaced, and that at least 30,000 civilians fled to Burundi.

Anadolu reported that on Wednesday the Congolese government attributed the violence in Uvira to a 'widespread offensive launched in recent days by the Rwandan Defense Forces' along the Kamanyola-Uvira axis, calling it a 'blatant violation' of the ceasefire and of commitments under recent peace agreements; Kigali denied the accusations.
Anadolu reported that on Wednesday Rwanda accused the Congolese and Burundian armies of violating a ceasefire provided under the Washington peace deal.

Anadolu reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame said on Thursday that Burundian soldiers deployed in eastern DRC spend days shelling civilians, and Anadolu noted there was no immediate reaction from Burundi.
Anadolu reported that Burundi's Foreign Minister Edouard Bizimana warned on Monday that 'any attack targeting Burundian citizens or soldiers deployed in the DRC will never be tolerated'.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that captured Burundian soldiers would be handed over to their country's authorities, and that Uvira was totally under M23 control.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that a Burundian delegation was forced to go to Luvungi, in South Kivu, to demand the return of its captured soldiers and negotiate a secure corridor for its troops encircled in the Hauts-Plateaux.

Al Jazeera reported that AFC leader Corneille Nangaa posted a signed statement on X on Tuesday confirming that fighters would withdraw from Uvira 'as per United States mediation request', and that the coalition called the move a 'unilateral trust-building measure' and called for a neutral force to monitor the ceasefire.
BBC Afrique reported that M23 chief Bertrand Bisimwa said on Wednesday that the withdrawal from Uvira was 'underway', with spokesperson Willy Ngoma adding it was 'in the interest of peace'.

Kigali Today reported that the rebel coalition announced it was ready to leave Uvira, asking that soldiers and all other armed people be removed from the city and that neutral forces be deployed to protect civilians and infrastructure and help enforce the ceasefire.

Al Jazeera reported that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that Rwanda's actions in eastern DRC were a 'clear violation' of the peace deal, and said in a post on X that the United States would take action to ensure promises made to the president are kept.

The International Contact Group for the Great Lakes (United States, Belgium, Denmark, the EU, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland and the UK) urged M23 and the Rwanda Defence Force to immediately halt offensive operations in eastern DRC, in particular in South Kivu, and called on the RDF to withdraw from eastern DRC.

BBC Afrique reported that the DRC government spokesperson Me Didier Kabi called the rebels' announced withdrawal from Uvira a 'mise en scène' orchestrated by the rebels to reduce pressure from partners, and that the DRC authorities said they held credible information of a 'dissimulation teintée de retrait'; BBC Afrique noted that government forces had not returned to the city.

BBC Afrique reported that DRC government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya told the BBC Newsday programme that the M23 announcement aimed to 'divert the attention of the American mediation team', which he said was preparing to take measures against Rwanda, and that he called the decision to leave Uvira a 'positive sign' while saying the government needed to confirm the situation on the ground.

BBC Afrique reported that a local civil-society member, speaking anonymously, said some M23 troops had begun to withdraw from Uvira but that police belonging to the same group continued to arrive, while another inhabitant expressed doubts about the withdrawal.

SOS Médias Burundi reported (dated Uvira, 24 November 2025) that clashes between groups claiming allegiance to the Wazalendo and the FARDC had left about six people dead and more than fifteen wounded between Sunday and Monday, 24 November 2025.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that in a statement published on 23 November the FARDC denounced violence by what it called 'fake Wazalendo'; per the army, Sunday's clashes killed four people (one FARDC soldier, two Wazalendo fighters, a civilian motorcycle rider) and wounded 14.

place: Luvungi, Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Sunday 23 November, at Luvungi in the Ruzizi plain, a man known as Huruma, described as a 'fake Wazalendo' and as having been a guardian (mlezi) of the Holy Family Parish, fired live rounds during diocesan youth celebrations at the Holy Family Catholic Church, killing two people and wounding five; the Diocese of Uvira strongly condemned the act.
SOS Médias Burundi reported that in Sange on Saturday 22 November two Wazalendo were killed in clashes between two rival groups, those of Kamama and Ngomanzito, according to local sources.
SOS Médias Burundi reported that several Uvira members of parliament, including national deputy Justin Bitakwira Bihona-Hayi, condemned abuses and killings attributed to some Wazalendo elements.

Actualite.cd reported that during the disorder that night, FARDC soldiers and their wazalendo allies stripped and ransacked the Iàmba health centre in the Bangwe sub-village (Nundu health zone) at Makobola, and a member of the Iàmba health-area development committee said they broke the doors from the pharmacy, looted all the medicines and took all the equipment from the head nurse's office.

Actualite.cd reported that multiple cases of sexual assault of women were reported in the FARDC and wazalendo expedition into Makobola; a local civil-society actor said the women were forced to help carry looted goods and returned to their homes after being raped.

place: Makobola, Fizi territory, South Kivu (Kigongo front, Uvira)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to its sources in the region, the Makobola disorder broke out after a disagreement, for reasons not yet clarified, between soldiers of the Guépard unit returning from the Kigongo front at Uvira and soldiers of the Hiboux unit; some sources spoke of dissension between the commands of the two units.
BBC reported that Burundi had shut its border with DR Congo, a Burundian military source was quoted as saying by AFP.

place: Uvira city to Sange, South Kivu
statement: Ebuteli (Kivu Security Barometer) reported that on 16 January the AFC/M23 rebels withdrew from the city of Uvira and repositioned at Sange, about 30 km from Uvira, a crossroads to the middle and high plateaux of Uvira and Fizi, notably towards Mulenge and Lubarika.
SOS Médias Burundi reported that the last elements of the rebel movement began leaving the city of Uvira on Saturday evening and completed the operation on Sunday morning.

Ebuteli reported that the FARDC and the Wazalendo retook the city of Uvira on 18 January, and that several abuses, often linked to attempted extortion, followed; an army communiqué reported by Actualite.cd also dated the retaking to Sunday 18 January 2026.

place: Kabunambo and Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory
statement: Congo Indépendant reported, citing local sources, that M23/RDF/AFC elements remained on 19 January in the Ruzizi plain and close to the city, notably at Kabunambo, less than one kilometre from the centre.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that Wazalendo militias, taking advantage of the vacuum left by the M23, advanced towards Uvira and took control of the village of Kirungu, 15 km from the city, and fired on several mountains overlooking Uvira.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the locality of Kirungu, four hours' walk upstream of Uvira, fell on the evening of Monday 16 March under the control of the rebel coalition, a site linking Uvira to the middle and high plateaux of Minembwe.

place: Point zéro, high plateaux of Fizi and Uvira
statement: Ebuteli reported that the Twirwaneho occupied the zones around the 'point zéro', a strategic position controlling the high plateaux of Fizi and Uvira, and that the FARDC had thinned out the middle and high plateaux to position themselves in the city of Uvira.

place: North of Uvira, Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux
statement: Human Rights Watch said that the M23 withdrew from Uvira in January 2026 and maintains positions to its north, in the Ruzizi Plain, and in the Hauts Plateaux, the highlands southwest of the city, and that fighting continues between the M23 and Congolese forces and their Wazalendo allies.

Actualite.cd reported that an army communiqué signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay Mongba, acting FARDC spokesperson, deplored the systematic pillage of the city by soldiers of the AFC/M23-RDF coalition before their evacuation, and said some twenty civilians involved in looting were arrested and would be brought before the courts.

Congo Indépendant reported that the army deplored systematic pillage attributed to M23/RDF/AFC elements before their evacuation, and that the rebels rejected these accusations and blamed the abuses on the army and its Wazalendo allies.

Actualite.cd reported that Defence Minister Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita told the Council of Ministers that security forces had returned to Uvira to ensure public order and that the scenario of chaos foreseen by the rebellion after its withdrawal had been foiled.

Radio Okapi reported that the DRC government announced a plan for the progressive restoration of State authority in the city of Uvira and its surroundings, including coordinated security, judicial and humanitarian measures.

Radio Okapi reported that the government communiqué of Monday 19 January denounced the deportation of civilian populations, in particular members of the Banyamulenge community, alleging that some were forced to leave Uvira by the AFC/M23 to be used as justification for the movement's presence on Congolese soil.

Congo Indépendant reported that, after an emergency meeting chaired by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya gave a stocktake of 1,500 dead, 3,000 displaced and 12,000 children out of school and separated from their parents.
Congo Indépendant reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said the withdrawal of the Rwandan forces could not be interpreted as a gesture of appeasement nor as the end of the aggression.

Congo Indépendant reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, sceptical, spoke of a 'faux retrait' (false withdrawal) and called for vigilance, judging that the enemy remains active and cunning.

Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa, in a letter of Thursday 15 January 2026 to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, announced that he had placed the city of Uvira under the responsibility of the international community.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a message on X on Wednesday 14 January, accused Congolese authorities of repeated ceasefire violations and said drones of the Kinshasa coalition forces bombed the port of Kalundu around 2:20 p.m., causing significant material damage and loss of life.

Radio Okapi reported, citing a MONUSCO communiqué, that MONUSCO and the ICGLR (CIRGL) were on a mission in Uvira from 23 to 27 February to prepare deployment of the joint ceasefire monitoring mechanism, and quoted acting Special Representative Vivian Van de Perre as saying MONUSCO's mandate in South Kivu is focused on ceasefire monitoring and does not include protection of civilians.

place: Bujumbura (statement on Burundian forces in eastern DRC)
statement: Iwacu reported that on 2 January 2026 the secretary general of Burundi's ruling CNDD-FDD party, Révérien Ndikuriyo, said at a Bujumbura press conference: 'Nous avons un accord qui nous permet d’intervenir au Congo', a reply Iwacu described as radically different from the Burundian ambassador's earlier claim of withdrawal.

place: Brussels (statement on Burundian forces and Uvira)
statement: Iwacu reported that on 17 December 2025 Burundi's ambassador to the EU, Thérence Ntahiraja, told the European Parliament that the Burundian army had withdrawn its troops from eastern DRC after the peace accord, and that this is why the Rwandan army and the M23 advanced easily to Uvira.

SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing residents' testimony, that from Sunday to Tuesday several civilians were killed in Uvira, some for refusing to hand over their phones, others for an appearance likened to Tutsi, or accused of collaborating with the M23; some testimonies named Wazalendo elements as perpetrators, others unidentified armed bandits.
SOS Médias Burundi reported that shops, houses and stores were regularly pillaged by armed men in Uvira from Sunday to Tuesday.

SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing residents, cases of sexual violence in several quarters of Uvira between Sunday and Tuesday; it wrote that a woman was reportedly killed after giving food to Wazalendo fighters, who reportedly then assaulted her ('violentée'), and that young girls were targeted for their looks or for refusing to give up their phones.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that security sources within the FARDC said more than twenty Banyamulenge families remained under the protection of the regular forces, as some community leaders called on their own members and on the FARDC to stop the pillage and killings.

place: Kalundu, Kabindula and Sondo quarters, Uvira city
statement: Ebuteli reported that on 19 January the Mai-Mai Kuruninga killed a boy in Kalundu quarter and a man in Kabindula quarter, and the Mai-Mai Landa Bango killed a woman in Sondo quarter, in Uvira city.

place: Kilibuli and Kasenga quarters, Uvira city
statement: Ebuteli reported that on 19 January a group of ten unidentified armed men killed a man in Kilibuli quarter, accusing him of collaborating with the M23, and that on 24 January, during a robbery in Kasenga quarter, unidentified armed men killed a 22-year-old civilian.
Ebuteli counted at least 21 civilians killed in Uvira territory in January 2026, against at least 151 in December 2025, the month the M23 took Uvira.

place: Blue Cut bar, Kalundu public port, Uvira city
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several eyewitness accounts, that a drone attributed to the FARDC bombed a bar called Blue Cut near the Kalundu public port around 2:30 p.m. on Wednesday, reportedly causing deaths and numerous injuries among civilians as well as significant material damage.

Ebuteli reported that on 14 January a FARDC kamikaze drone air strike in Kalundu quarter, Uvira city, targeted and destroyed a hotel in which an M23 meeting was being held, and that the toll could be several dozen victims among civilians, fighters and M23 cadres.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that sources close to the AFC/M23 denied that M23 members were present at the Blue Cut bar in Kalundu when it was hit by a drone, asserting that no leaders or fighters from the movement were there.

Human Rights Watch said that the South Kivu governor and the Congolese army commander took steps to control Wazalendo groups in Uvira, that some Wazalendo had been arrested for threatening and shooting at civilians, and that HRW visited them in military detention cells.

Human Rights Watch said there had been a lot of damage to houses, government buildings and property of Banyamulenge, as well as destruction and looting of goods during the military withdrawal, although it was difficult to identify those responsible.

Congo Indépendant reported that destruction and pillage targeted essential public services in Uvira, including the customs (DGDA), tax (DGI), immigration (DGM) and administrative revenue (DGRAD) directorates and the OCC quality-control agency.

Congo Indépendant reported that more than 267,000 people were now refugees or displaced, nearly 250,000 of them in Burundi, and that Minister of State Ève Bazaiba, who stayed in Burundi, called it a 'human tragedy'.

Human Rights Watch said that M23 fighters committed sexual violence against women and girls, especially those who ventured out to find food on their farmlands where they were isolated and vulnerable, and that most of these women and girls had not received any medical care.

Radio Okapi reported that a Government report, presented in Kinshasa on a Tuesday by Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba, said about 14,400 women were raped in five weeks of occupation of Uvira by the Rwandan army and its proxies.
sources: Radio Okapi; Human Rights Watch; Actualite.cd

statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Government report presented by Human Rights Minister Samuel Mbemba on a Tuesday said more than 1,500 people died and more than 300,000 were forced to flee during the occupation of Uvira, with bombings, summary executions, abductions, sexual violence and pillage creating a climate of generalised terror.

Human Rights Watch said its research indicated that the M23 and Rwandan forces killed at least several dozen people when they took Uvira, adding that it is difficult to know who is buried in all reported mass graves.

place: Kavimvira road and Kilomoni, Uvira city
statement: The DRC Council of Ministers of 27 February heard, from Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani after his mission, that mass graves had been found in Uvira, one near the World Food Programme office on the road to Kavimvira reportedly containing about 35 bodies per local sources, and a second at Kilomoni; no official exhumation had yet taken place and the identity of perpetrators and victims remained unknown.

place: Kavinvira cemetery and Kilomoni quarter, Uvira city
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the South Kivu provincial government, in a communiqué of 28 February 2026, said preliminary findings were that 151 civilians were buried in the mass graves, 121 at the Kavinvira cemetery and 30 in an enclosure in Kilomoni quarter, and that 'these executions took place on the eve of the forced withdrawal, on 18 January 2026, of the AFC/M23 elements, supported by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF)'. The national government's account of the Council of Ministers meeting of Friday 27 February 2026 said no official exhumation had yet taken place and the identity of perpetrators and victims remained unknown.

place: Mayi ya Moto, Kilomoni, Kala, Rutembo, Kaponda, Uvira area
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Government report presented that Tuesday listed three mass graves at Mayi ya Moto containing 115 bodies, one at Kilomoni with 31 bodies, one at Kala, two at Rutembo and two tombs at Kaponda.
Radio Okapi reported that the Government report presented that Tuesday said the Government had identified more than 162 trucks from Rwanda involved in organised looting operations.

place: Kabimba and Kifuta, Kalungwe groupement, Bavira chiefdom
statement: Ebuteli reported that FARDC supported by the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and the Wazalendo attacked M23 fighters at Kabimba village on 7 January and at Kifuta village on 10 January, in Kalungwe groupement, Bavira chiefdom, in the middle plateaux of Uvira territory.

place: Abala and Mukoko, Basilocha groupement, high plateaux of Fizi
statement: Ebuteli reported that on 11 January Twirwaneho fighters allied with the M23 attacked FARDC and Wazalendo positions at Abala village in the high plateaux of Fizi, and that in reprisal the FARDC targeted Mukoko village with drones on 11 and 12 January and recovered arms and ammunition lost at Abala.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that residents said a FARDC drone was shot down in Fizi territory by Twirwaneho fighters after clashes in which the FARDC, supported by the Wazalendo and elements of the FDNB, fought Twirwaneho fighters, described as a military ally of the AFC/M23 in South Kivu.

Ebuteli reported that on 29 January the Twirwaneho/M23/Red Tabara coalition and the FNL attacked the Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo in the villages of Kilumbi and Abala in Fizi territory, killing three Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo.

place: Rutanga quarter, Sange commune, Ruzizi plain
statement: Ebuteli reported that on 29 January a grenade thrown by M23 fighters killed five civilians and wounded eleven in Rutanga quarter, Sange commune, in the Ruzizi plain.

Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant local sources, violent clashes on Tuesday 17 March between the FARDC and AFC-M23 rebels at Luvungi, near Kabunambo, with bombardments, driving civilians from Runingu towards Uvira, and described the clashes as ending the relative truce around Uvira observed since the AFC-M23 withdrawal.

Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the 33rd military region had announced the closure of road traffic from Runingu on the Bukavu-Uvira axis, leaving public transport vehicles and humanitarian convoys blocked there.

place: Kavimvira border post, Uvira / Gatumba, Burundi
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the authorities of the DRC and Burundi agreed to reopen on Monday 23 February 2026 the common border between Bujumbura and Uvira, through the Kavimvira and Gatumba border posts, with traffic resuming immediately, after the population of Uvira had been cut off from Bujumbura since the AFC-M23's temporary occupation of the city on 10 December 2025.

place: Kasambura, Ruzizi plain (Bukavu-Uvira road, RN5), Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: 7sur7.cd reported that Bukavu-Uvira road traffic resumed on Wednesday 1 April 2026, fifteen days after FARDC and Wazalendo elements had suspended it in the Ruzizi plain, and that since 15 March the traffic had been cut at Kasambura by FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo elements.

DW (Swahili) reported that Jean-Jacques Elakano, speaking to journalists in Uvira, said the government feared AFC/M23 rebels were using trade and family travel between Bukavu and Uvira to infiltrate areas controlled by the government army; a DW photo caption said the governor of South Kivu, based in Uvira, had said travel would stay suspended until the rebels left Bukavu.

place: Sange, Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: DW (Swahili) reported that since Saturday AFC/M23 fighters had been withdrawing from the Sange area and some hill villages towards the north of Uvira district, and that videos circulating online showed government soldiers and Wazalendo groups entering the village of Sange.

place: Nyakabere, Mutarule, Luberizi, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: DW (Swahili) reported that the Congolese army said the AFC/M23 rebels had left the villages of Nyakabere, Mutarule and Luberizi, a claim that DW said AFC/M23 had not confirmed so far.

place: Ruzizi plain (Kabunambo, Sange, Mutarule, Luberizi, Bwegera, Lemera, Luvungi), Uvira territory; Katogota, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that AFC/M23 rebels left several localities of the Ruzizi plain in Uvira territory on Monday; according to local sources they withdrew from Kabunambo, Sange, Mutarule, Luberizi, Bwegera, Lemera and Luvungi towards Katogota, and residents of Sange, Luberizi and Lemera took to the streets to celebrate their departure.

place: Kigoro, Kigurwe, Kabunambo, Ruzizi plain (RN5), c. 26 km north of Uvira, South Kivu
statement: MediaCongo reported that since dawn on Wednesday 6 May 2026 violent clashes opposed AFC/M23 rebels, supported according to several sources by the Rwandan defence forces, to FARDC and Wazalendo self-defence groups, concentrated in the Ruzizi plain at Kigoro, Kigurwe and Kabunambo about 26 kilometres north of Uvira; it said no official toll had been given and that the city remained under government-force control.

place: Uvira (city): Kimanga, Kabindula, Songo, Kilibula, Kalundu and Nyamianda quarters, South Kivu
statement: La Presse Africaine reported that, in a security assessment presented on Thursday 7 May 2026, the chiefs of six quarters of Uvira (Kimanga, Kabindula, Songo, Kilibula, Kalundu and Nyamianda) painted a dark picture of the security situation; according to this assessment, armed robbery, killings, abductions, death threats, torture and other abuses were reported almost daily, especially at night, and the outlet wrote that this violence was reportedly attributed ('seraient attribuées') largely to uncontrolled elements of the VDP Wazalendo and of the FARDC, and in part to unidentified armed men.

Kivutimes reported that Uvira had for more than three months faced a multiplication of arbitrary arrests without trial and that, according to several local sources, some arrests were reportedly carried out by certain Wazalendo, often to obtain ransoms from detainees' families; Mapenzi Manyebwa, coordinator of the Uvira civil society synergy, denounced arrests made without respect for legal procedures, with citizens paying fines outside any judicial logic.

place: Ruzizi near Kalundu port, Uvira (city); onward to Bijombo (Uvira territory) and Itombwe (Mwenga territory), South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on 15 May 2026 several boats carrying Burundian soldiers landed at Ruzizi, not far from the port of Kalundu in Uvira, before troops were deployed towards Bijombo (Uvira territory) and Itombwe (Mwenga territory); the article said the deployment was estimated (without saying by whom) at about two battalions, aimed at rebalancing the balance of forces in the Minembwe area and controlling movements between Rurambo, Bijombo and Minembwe.

place: Kinshasa (press conference); North Kivu localities and the Hauts Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that at a press conference in Kinshasa on Saturday 6 June the army's interim spokesperson, Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay, firmly denounced the continuation of attacks despite ongoing diplomatic initiatives, and that, according to the military authorities, several localities of North Kivu and the highlands of Fizi and Uvira in South Kivu continued to be the scene of attacks.

place: Uvira General Referral Hospital (with Bukavu and Fizi hospitals), South Kivu
statement: The ICRC reported that between 15 May and 15 June 2026 the five hospitals it supports in North and South Kivu recorded a total of 303 casualties, 30% more than for 15 April-14 May, and that, in a sign of intensifying hostilities in the Hauts Plateaux, the hospitals in Bukavu, Uvira and Fizi in South Kivu had admitted 170 casualties (56% of the 303 patients).

place: Busuma camp (Burundi) to Uvira (city), South Kivu
statement: DW reported that the repatriation of Congolese refugees who had fled to Burundi during the AFC-M23 occupation of Uvira in December began on Thursday, and that in Uvira the returnees were received at a transit centre where they were expected to receive resettlement kits.

place: South Kivu (Fizi, Mwenga, Uvira, Kalehe, Shabunda territories); returnees concentrated in Uvira territory
statement: OCHA's South Kivu situation report stated that armed clashes had intensified in the territories of Fizi, Mwenga, Uvira, Kalehe and Shabunda, and that rapid multisectoral assessments in March counted more than 542 200 returnees at provincial level, most of them concentrated in Uvira territory.

place: Kavimvira bridge, RN5, Uvira (city), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Kavimvira bridge on the RN5 in Uvira collapsed on Tuesday 16 June; according to local health sources one person died and two were injured, a medical source quoted saying three people were injured, of whom a young boy died in hospital after a blow to the head and the other two had light injuries, while the NSCC Sud-Sud civil society group said in a statement that its field investigations showed three deaths, including two minors aged 14 and 17 and an adult, plus an injured woman. Local authorities had not yet commented officially on the circumstances of the collapse or the final toll.

place: Uvira (city) and surroundings (incl. Katala, Uvira territory), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the Human Rights Watch report 'Nous sommes des civils !', HRW documented eight cases of rape committed by M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers against women in and around Uvira between December 2025 and January 2026, with survivors describing being raped in their fields or homes, often under threat of death or at gunpoint.

place: Kavimvira medical centre, Uvira (city); Katala, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd, relaying the Human Rights Watch report, reported that a woman assaulted while working in her field at Katala, Uvira territory, on 15 December, went to the Kavimvira medical centre in Uvira for care but could not be treated and left without essential medicines, receiving only a small number of tablets; HRW said survivors stressed the near-total lack of accessible health services during the M23 and Rwandan occupation, notably the absence of timely PEP treatment.

In the standfirst of an article, Jeune Afrique said that Uvira, the provisional capital, occupied for a month by AFC/M23 rebels, had remained a major fallback point for the wazalendo, militiamen who, seeking recognition and influence, had become as unavoidable as they were cumbersome; the summary of the series the article belongs to said the rebels had for now pulled back but that Uvira lived under permanent tension.

place: South Kivu (province-level statement; includes the Ruzizi plain north of Uvira)
statement: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC reported in its final report that in South Kivu no RDF or AFC/M23 troop withdrawals were documented and fighting continued, and that additional RDF reinforcements arrived from Rwanda in April, including sophisticated weaponry and anti-aerial man-portable air defence systems.

place: Hauts Plateaux of South Kivu (parts of Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories)
statement: Human Rights Watch said in a press release that Congolese armed forces and armed groups in the Hauts Plateaux of South Kivu were obstructing the delivery of humanitarian aid and preventing civilians from fleeing the fighting, and that the UN had described humanitarian access restrictions to the Hauts Plateaux, an area covering parts of the Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories, as 'severe'.

place: North Kivu (Masisi, Rutshuru, Walikale) and South Kivu (Uvira, Fizi, Mwenga)
statement: Radio Okapi reported, a year after the Washington peace accord, that the territories of Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale in North Kivu and those of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga in South Kivu remained the most affected by violence, with civilians displaced and material destruction.

place: Kimete, Wihene, Kashamata, highlands of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, spokesperson of operation Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu, said the positions of Kimete, Wihene and Kashamata had been retaken by the army, and that AFC/M23-Twirwaneho - RDF - Red Tabara elements had been forced to fall back towards Rugezi and Bigaragara, south of Minembwe.

place: Bidjaga, east of Point Zéro, highlands of Mwenga/Fizi
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC denounced drone bombings attributed to the AFC/M23 the previous weekend in the village of Bidjaga, east of Point Zéro, and other densely populated villages, killing about ten people according to the army communiqué.

place: Point Zero (Point Zéro), Itombwe sector, Mwenga
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, in a statement signed by Fidèle Rugabo, the military spokesperson for the armed group Twirwaneho, the fighters claimed to have launched an offensive on Saturday, July 4, against the Point Zero position, before taking control after several hours of fighting; the outlet said no official reaction had been recorded at the time of publication.

place: Point Zéro, border of Fizi and Mwenga
statement: Actualite.cd reported that clashes at Point Zéro, on the limit of Fizi and Mwenga territories, had multiplied since Friday 28 August, with heavy weapons and drones used by both belligerents, according to local sources.

Actualite.cd reported that a civil-society actor in the Fizi area said that from 4 a.m. on 31 August the government force FARDC, wazalendo and the Burundians launched a drone attack at Point zéro, causing massive displacement.

place: Malimba, Rubarati, Ruhuha, Uvira territory (also Fizi, Mwenga)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported from Uvira that fighting had been reported since Sunday in several areas of the territories of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga, between the FARDC supported by the FDNB and Wazalendo militias, and AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho fighters.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that a Wazalendo fighter present in the Malimba area said that the FARDC, the FDNB and the Wazalendo had retaken positions previously held by AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and Red Tabara fighters at Malimba, Ruhuha and Rubarati; SOS Médias Burundi noted this could not be independently verified.

place: Kabanju, Kipupu, Nyamabuguma, Point Zéro, Fizi and Mwenga
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Twirwaneho spokesperson Fidèle Rugabo said his fighters had repelled several attacks by the FARDC, the FDNB, the Wazalendo militias and the FDLR, citing in a post on X Kabanju, Kipupu, Nyamabuguma and Point Zéro in Fizi and Mwenga territories; SOS Médias Burundi said these claims could not be independently verified.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that two FDNB officers, Captain Félicien Kanjori and Major Jérémie Nitunga, were arrested after the drone strike attributed to the M23 on the Mwalu hotel in Fizi; they were reportedly arrested by mercenaries in the area and suspected of passing intelligence. The outlet said the Congolese and Burundian armies had not yet communicated on the arrests.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that on 19 August 2026 the Mwalu hotel in Fizi was struck by drones, seriously injuring two people including the manager, Mwando Lukaba, with significant material damage; an FARDC spokesperson in the region attributed the attack to the M23 and said two bombs were dropped, which the outlet said could not be independently verified.

Radio Okapi reported that the citizen platform MCLA-RDC said in a communiqué published Tuesday 4 August 2026 that at least four armed incidents were recorded between 1 and 4 August, causing the deaths of four people, several injuries and concern among residents.

Radio Okapi reported that, according to MCLA-RDC, on 1 August in the Kavimvira quarter of Uvira a woman identified as Aimée Vumilia, aged 31 and mother of five children, was reportedly hit by a bullet, and on 2 August the lifeless body of a man was found in the Murambia zone of the Mulongwe-Kasenga quarter.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that at least six people had been killed since the start of August in several quarters of Uvira, amid a recrudescence of night attacks attributed to armed men.

place: Uvira, South Kivu (vehicles handed over; earlier held in Burundi)
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing official local sources, that police vehicles received in Uvira had been kept hidden for nearly a year in Burundi after the capture of Uvira by the AFC/M23 rebels.

Radio Okapi reported that users of the Uvira-Luvungi, Mwenga-Uvira and Uvira-Fizi-Baraka roads denounced barriers erected by certain Wazalendo fighters, and that according to several testimonies it collected on Tuesday 4 August, taxes of 10 000 to 50 000 Congolese francs would be demanded of travellers.

Radio Okapi reported that the Vice-Governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, urged all Wazalendo components to act responsibly and respect the provisions set by the Provincial Security Council, and called for the dismantling of all unauthorised barriers.

Actualite.cd reported that six civil-society actors of Baraka, including their president Etunda Maisha Albert, were released on the afternoon of 27 August from Uvira central prison; they had been arrested on 13 August at Baraka-Centre in Fizi territory and transferred to Uvira days later.

place: Uvira city (Kavimvira, Kasenga, Kalundu, Mulongwe, Kimanga, Nyamianda)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that shots were heard in Uvira from early morning on Wednesday 16 September, at Kavimvira, Kasenga, Kalundu, Mulongwe, Kimanga, Nyamianda and elsewhere, and that a local civil-society source said a fourth-year primary pupil of EP Umoja de Kamongola was shot dead at Kalundu.

Actualite.cd reported that many sources described the 16 September shooting in Uvira as an expression of 'anger' by wazalendo after one of their members was arrested by the army on 5 September, the reasons for which were not known; residents said leaflets demanding his release had circulated the previous day.

Actualite.cd reported that on 15 September the Congolese National Police dispersed a C64 coalition demonstration in Uvira against changing the constitution, and that rapporteur François Igilima said four people were arrested and taken away by the police.

Actualite.cd reported that the Uvira garrison military tribunal sentenced 18 soldiers of the Simba battalion to death for cowardice at the front in a verdict delivered on 4 September, without extenuating circumstances; the trial had opened on 23 August.

MediaCongo reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi said that preliminary estimates counted up to 49 mass graves identified in the Uvira sector and that more than 241 bodies had already been counted in three of them alone. This entry is dated by the article reporting the statement: the graves relate to killings during the earlier rebel occupation of the city (see actor), not to events of this quarter.

place: Place du Monument, Mulongwe commune, Uvira
statement: Radio Okapi reported that at the GENOCOST day ceremony in Uvira on Sunday 2 August, survivors of the recent occupation of the city by the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition recounted violence they said they witnessed or suffered, notably executions of civilians, disappearances and other serious human rights violations.

place: Uvira health zone (zone de santé d'Uvira)
statement: Global Voices, republishing an article by IciCongo, reported that health actors recorded more than 1 100 cases of rape in only three months in the Uvira health zone. This entry is dated by the article's publication; the article does not attribute perpetrators or name the data holder, and it dates the three months inconsistently (see note).

place: Conflict-affected provinces; Uvira, Ruzizi plain and highlands mentioned
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) recorded 2 607 violations in conflict-affected provinces between January and June 2026, concerning 5 032 victims, and noted that despite the AFC/M23's withdrawal from Uvira and the Ruzizi plain, reprisals, displacement and an intensification of fighting continued to be reported in the highlands.

Radio Okapi reported that Uvira's national deputy Claude Misare, in a letter of Monday 17 August to the Minister of National Defence, asked for clarification on the destination of resources for the support of Wazalendo deployed in combat zones.

place: Uvira city, also Sange and Kawizi
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Uvira was largely paralysed on Wednesday 5 August by a ville morte day called by local forces vives to press the central government over the deteriorating security situation in the highlands of Uvira and in Fizi, with civil society asking for modern military equipment for the FARDC and Wazalendo.

place: Mugobe, Itara-Luvungi groupement, Ruzizi plain (Uvira territory)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that violent fighting between the FRN rebels (spelled RFN in the article's text) and the FARDC, all parties backed by their allies, was reported at Mugobe and other villages of the Itara-Luvungi groupement in the Ruzizi plain, and that according to its sources RFN elements attacked FARDC and wazalendo positions in the zone from 8h00 local time.

Actualite.cd reported, citing an actor of Uvira society ("un acteur de la société d'Uvira"), that some schools of the Itara-Luvungi groupement sent pupils home after weapons detonations at Mugobe, and reported that the clashes disrupted traffic between Bukavu and Uvira.
Actualite.cd reported that after the AFC/M23 withdrawal from Uvira city and the Ruzizi plain under US pressure in December 2025, the rebels had positioned themselves at Kamanyola.

Actualite.cd reported that the Uvira garrison military tribunal sentenced 27 soldiers to death for cowardice before the enemy on Friday, in a trial of 112 soldiers prosecuted after fleeing clashes; the verdict was given on 2 October, with five years for 54 soldiers.
Actualite.cd reported that six women soldiers were among those convicted of violating orders and cowardice, with the sentences passed against them not specified.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that 27 Garde républicaine soldiers were sentenced to death by a military court sitting in Uvira, with the verdict given on Saturday 3 October after about 2 weeks of hearings at the Uvira central prison.

place: Malimba and Masango, Bijombo groupement (Uvira territory)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the 112 soldiers of the 21st battalion 'Simba' were prosecuted notably for abandoning, on the night of 23 August, strategic positions in the mountainous zones of Malimba and Masango in the Bijombo groupement while engaged in the defence of Uvira.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that after the abandonment of the Malimba and Masango positions the Congolese authorities reinforced several positions, including Malimba, Ruhuha, Masango and Rubuga, and that drones were reportedly used, according to statements by Twirwaneho spokesperson Fidèle Rugabo.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that Uvira was taken by the AFC/M23 in December 2025 before the movement withdrew from it on 17 January 2026 under strong American pressure, and that the AFC/M23 kept positions north of the city and in the highlands.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the situation remained tense on Friday 2 October at Kabindula, seat of the Bavira chiefdom in Uvira territory, after the installation of a new groupement head, Kabale Ghislain, who replaces Romain Lenge, who had been acting.
Radio Okapi reported that protests were organised against the installation and that the police intervened to disperse the demonstrators.
Ouragan.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi said "Il n'y a aucun problème à Uvira", calling the rumours an enemy montage and use of a digital army to panic the population.

Ouragan.cd reported that Purusi said that Minova, Katana, Kabamba, Bukavu and lately Uvira had 'fallen' through panic created on social networks, and that the M23 backed by Rwanda, 'today FRN', was trying to create panic.
Ouragan.cd reported that Purusi said the provincial government was about to receive the UN fact-finding mission on the human-rights situation in South and North Kivu.

place: Kawihene, Rugezi, Point Zéro (Fizi highlands near Minembwe); Munanira, Mitimbili (Walungu)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that fighting between the FARDC and Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) fighters took place on Monday 26 October in several localities of Fizi and Walungu territories, and that, according to civil-society sources, the fighting was concentrated around Kawihene, Rugezi and Point Zéro in the Fizi highlands, where both sides reportedly used drones and heavy artillery.
Radio Okapi reported that military sources said the FARDC had retaken control of Mitimbili, which the outlet said could not yet be independently confirmed.

Radio Okapi reported that rumours of FRN fighters' presence at Kawizi, a locality about eight kilometres ("huit kilomètres") from Uvira city, were denied by local civil-society forces ("forces vives") and by the FARDC, who said the locality remained under their control.

Radio Okapi reported that Captain Sylvain Bijanu, spokesperson of the 33rd military region, rejected the information about an FRN advance towards Uvira, and that Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi denounced a 'media war' by FRN fighters and called Uvira a 'fortress' protected by the FARDC and their allies.

place: Kahwizi (Kawizi), less than 10 km from Uvira
statement: Taarifa Rwanda reported, citing frontline sources, that FRN fighters captured the Kahwizi (Kawizi) locality less than 10 kilometres from Uvira city.

place: Gitabo, Nyabigega, Mangwa, Kuwamabuye, Nyarurango, Rugomero; Runingu
statement: The Rio Times reported that Taarifa wrote on 27 October that FRN fighters had captured the villages of Gitabo, Nyabigega and Mangwa, and had taken Kuwamabuye, Nyarurango and Rugomero, heading toward Runingu.
The Rio Times reported that Congolese officials said the rebels had not advanced, and that Radio Okapi reported the army and the South Kivu governor call Uvira calm and secure.

place: middle plateaux of Uvira; Kaziba chiefdom; Munanira; Kigoma groupement
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that a precarious calm had been observed since the morning of Tuesday 27 October on the front lines in the middle plateaux of Uvira and in the Kaziba villages, while shooting was still heard on Monday on the Munanira axis and in the Kigoma groupement.

place: Kawizi; Uvira; Kiliba, Kabunambo, Sange, Luvungi
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that rumours spread on social networks of an FRN advance toward Kawizi, about 10 kilometres from Uvira, were denied by sources presented as reliable, and that activities took place normally in Uvira town and at Kiliba, Kabunambo, Sange and Luvungi, according to a human-rights activist.

place: Mitimbili hill; Nshoko hills (Kahungwe groupement), Kaziba chiefdom
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that FRN troops were said to have concentrated their positions on Mitimbili hill, between the Muhumba and Kabembe groupements, while Wazalendo fighters were said to be positioned on the Nshoko hills in the Kahungwe groupement.

Actualite.cd reported that thousands of inhabitants, among them women and children, fleeing clashes between the RFN and the army backed by the Wazalendo, had arrived in recent days at Rurambo in the Uvira highlands.

Actualite.cd reported that in the Uvira highlands Rurambo was still occupied by the FARDC backed by the Wazalendo, while the neighbouring village of Kahololo was considered the main bastion of "Twirwaheno" (as printed), currently allied to the RFN, which it described as backed by the Twirwaneho and Red Tabara.
Actualite.cd reported that at Kaziba local structures said they had recorded près de 12.000 (nearly 12.000) displaced households after 10 days of clashes between the RFN and the Congolese army.

place: Kaziba chiefdom (Walungu); middle plateaux of Uvira
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that most of the displaced persons were exposed to the weather and had received no humanitarian assistance to date, that those wounded by bullets remained without adequate care, and that women, children and the elderly were among the most exposed, notably to risks of sexual violence, family separation and trauma.

Radio Maendeleo reported that the Parlement citoyen pour la démocratie et la bonne gouvernance, in a note made public and consulted by Radio Maendeleo on Tuesday 27 October, took a position following alerts of arrests, assaults and presumed abductions of inhabitants in several areas of South Kivu, particularly on the Nyangezi-Kamanyola axis in Walungu territory, and that it cited in particular the 'interpellation' (stopping and holding for questioning) of about ten young people from the villages of Bujenjere and Nacirhongwe while they were along National Road 5, on the Bukavu-Uvira axis.

Agenzia Fides reported that fighting resumed on 26 October in South Kivu on the Fizi highlands, and that the city of Uvira, a bastion of government forces supported by elements of the Burundian army and by pro-government Wazalendo militiamen engaged in fighting against rebel forces led by former president Joseph Kabila, "remains the main target".

Agenzia Fides reported that some senior FARDC officers were joining the FRN, among them Brigadier General François Kamanzi, former commander of operations of the 12th military region in Kongo-Central province, who deserted the FARDC to join the new movement.

Agenzia Fides reported that the NGO ACMEJ, which had sent it a note on 23 October, said that during a speech at Kamanyola on 17 October a delegation of the FRN and of Rwanda reportedly told the civilian population of its intention to launch a new offensive against villages of the Ruzizi plain, highland areas and part of Mwenga territory, and that according to ACMEJ the objective would be to retake Uvira.

Agenzia Fides reported that ACMEJ's note said that from 20 October 2026 FRN soldiers and Rwandan allies stationed at Kamanyola and Katogota began attacking the villages of Katogota and Lubarika in the middle highlands, with a plan to reach Lubarika, descend to Luvungi and conquer Uvira.

BBC Gahuza reported a statement by FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka that Brigadier General François Kamanzi was head of operations in the 12th military region in Kongo-Central province and that two other senior soldiers also chose to join the FRN.

place: Bujumbura (statement); Burundi border incl. Uvira-Bujumbura crossings
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundi's Minister of the Interior, Public Security and Community Development, Léonidas Ndaruzaniye, announced on Thursday that people from, or who merely transited through, eastern DRC zones controlled by the AFC-M23 would not be allowed to enter Burundi, and that he said 'Nous sommes les alliés de Kinshasa'.

Actualite.cd reported that the public hearings of the Uvira trial opened on 15 September in flagrante procedure and concerned soldiers who fled clashes between the FARDC and fighters of the AFC/M23 coalition, RED Tabara and Twirhaneho.

Actualite.cd reported that other rebels had taken the direction of villages of the Itara-Luvungi groupement, notably Katogota, Bulinga and Kinyinya near Mugobe, and another part had settled in the Kigoma highlands (Kageregere and surroundings).

Radio Maendeleo reported, citing civil-society sources, that more than 2 500 households had left Kaziba-centre and Kafindjo and dispersed to neighbouring chiefdoms and territories, including the Bafuliru chiefdom in Uvira territory and Bukavu city.

UN experts said that, between November 2025 and February 2026, human rights defenders in North and South Kivu were reportedly targeted by M23 members and collaborators, and that two women human rights defenders protesting forced expulsions of civilians in Uvira, South Kivu, were reportedly abducted and tortured by M23 elements; their fate and whereabouts remain unknown.

UN experts said they were horrified by the abuse of human rights defenders and their families in North and South Kivu, and said there are allegations of attempted killings, repeated kidnappings, torture, sexual violence and death threats at the hands of M23, targeting those documenting abuses.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (not specified)
statement: UN experts said that a woman human rights defender working on LGBT rights was abducted multiple times and severely tortured and continues to be aggressively pursued, and that in another case armed men allegedly raided a defender's home and abducted and violently assaulted his spouse to force her to reveal his whereabouts.

According to the president of the UN-mandated Independent Commission of Inquiry on eastern DRC (Arnauld Akodjenou), the accounts it gathered describe conflict-related sexual violence, including sexual slavery, forced recruitment, unlawful killings, arbitrary arrests, and attacks on schools and health facilities in North and South Kivu; UN News reported that the commission's work is at a preliminary stage and that its members do not claim to establish responsibility.

According to the president of the UN-mandated Independent Commission of Inquiry on eastern DRC, accounts gathered by the commission describe attacks on schools and health facilities in North and South Kivu; UN News, summarising the commission, reported that the fighting had profoundly affected health systems and that the Ebola epidemic further complicates access to populations and the work of humanitarian organisations.

A UN News (ONU Info) article of 29 June 2026 on a UN commission of inquiry's alert carries, under the section heading 'Une société prise au piège', an item credited 'ONU Info' stating that experts affirm rapes, gang rapes, extremely violent assaults and killings of civilians are a recurring feature of M23's modus operandi; the experts are not identified there. The same article says the commission's members do not claim, at this stage, to establish responsibilities.

place: DRC (UN Security Council resolution; venue not stated by the source)
statement: UN News reported that the Security Council renewed on Monday, until 1 July 2027, the sanctions regime on armed groups active in the DRC and the mandate of its Group of Experts, and in its resolution reaffirmed its demand for an 'immediate and unconditional' withdrawal of Rwandan forces from Congolese territory, an end to Kigali's support for M23 and an end to Congolese army support for the FDLR.

MSF reported that the current frontline at Katogota in South Kivu bisects the road connecting Bukavu and Uvira, and that M23/AFC's position on Katogota was putting pressure on Uvira, which was under government control.
MSF reported that the area of Kamanyola, next to Katogota, was under M23/AFC control and that its healthcare system had been weakened by violence.

MSF reported that in February 2025 residents reported increased violence and clashes in Uvira between the Congolese army and its alleged allies, the Wazalendo fighters, and that medical facilities were not spared from gunfire, hampering patients' access to care.

place: Bukavu - Kamanyola - Uvira road, South Kivu
statement: MSF reported that persistent insecurity had rendered the road between Bukavu, Kamanyola and Uvira nearly impassable, making it impossible for humanitarian organisations to move between the two sides of the frontline, so MSF crossed various countries to deliver aid on each side.

place: North Kivu (AFC/M23-held areas), from Butembo, Beni and Ituri
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 authorities announced on Tuesday (23 June 2026 per the page) that drivers coming from Butembo, Beni and Ituri province would no longer be allowed to enter entities under AFC/M23 control, with the stated aim of limiting the spread of Ebola.
Actualite.cd reported that, since 23 May 2026, passenger transport between Goma and Butembo had been suspended until further notice by the North Kivu governorate under AFC/M23 administration.

The FARDC, in a communiqué reported by the news site, confirmed the defection of Kasereka Kabido, head of the FPP/AP/FCR movement and a member of the Wazalendo, and that according to FARDC spokesperson major-general Sylvain Ekenge, Kabido and his group had chosen to rally to Rwanda and its M23/AFC allies.

Mediacongo reported that the self-proclaimed general Kabido and his armed group FPP/AP had officially joined the AFC-M23, which it described as a politico-military movement backed by Rwanda according to several national and international reports, and that the self-proclaimed general Shimiray Guidon, described as the commander of the Wazalendo across North Kivu, condemned this act of treason in a communiqué.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 September (2025) 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye, commander of AFC/M23's 'First Defense Zone' covering the Goma–Rutshuru–Kanyabayonga–Kirumba axis, declared in Kirumba that AFC/M23 intended to resume hostilities aimed at capturing Butembo and Kisangani.

place: Kanyabayonga and Kirumba, Lubero, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that Bahati Erasto, North Kivu's AFC/M23-appointed governor, during visits to Kanyabayonga and Kirumba between 9–11 June (2025), claimed that Lubero, Butembo and Beni would soon fall under AFC/M23 control.

Human Rights Watch reported that several witnesses said that one M23 commander, 'Captain Gaston', executed a Colonel Amurabi in Rumangabo around June 2025, and that Amurabi was a legal defender (défenseur judiciaire) in the military justice system in Goma, according to a former detainee and judicial and Congolese military intelligence sources.

place: Rumangabo and Tshanzu (Tchanzu), Rutshuru, North Kivu
