statement: Human Rights Watch recommended that concerned governments sanction RDF and M23 commanders responsible for serious abuses in 'training centers' and military and unofficial detention sites, including RDF Special Force commander Brig. Gen. Stanislas Gashugi, and M23 camp commanders and instructors Léon Kanyamibwa and Bertin Mas0zera, identified in this report.

The US Treasury (OFAC), announcing sanctions, said that John Imani Nzenze is an M23 commander and M23's chief of intelligence, regarded as one of the closest collaborators and confidants of Sultani Makenga, the overall military commander of M23, and that Gustave Kubwayo, commonly known as 'Colonel Sirkoof', is an FDLR commander and the leader of the Commando de Recherche et d’Action en Profondeur, an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, who led an FDLR operational command structure in Nyiragongo territory, North Kivu, that formed in 2022.

Radio Okapi reported that on Monday 8 September 2025 civil society in Uvira marched to demand the departure of general Olivier Gasita, recently named FARDC commander in charge of operations and intelligence of the 33rd military region; the population accused him of having facilitated the capture of Bukavu by AFC/M23, and Wazalendo militiamen were at the front of the opposition, while the FARDC spokesperson had three days earlier reaffirmed that Gasita enjoyed the army's confidence.

place: Lushagala IDP camp, Goma, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that one man, reportedly accused of being an M23 member due to his ethnicity, was lynched on 25 January in the Lushagala internally displaced persons camp in Goma.
The UN Group of Experts (annex 43) quoted a WHO report of 7 February 2025 that since 26 January 3082 injured and 843 dead had been reported from 31 health facilities in and around Goma, North Kivu.
The UN Group of Experts reported that over 1,000 wounded were registered in Goma between 23 and 28 January, including civilians, many of them women and children.

place: Birere, Mapendo and Kahembe neighbourhoods, Goma, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 27 January 2025 heavy cross-border exchanges of artillery fire between the DRC and Rwandan forces caused civilian casualties on both sides of the border; in Goma the Birere neighbourhood near the airport was severely impacted, with at least 53 civilian fatalities documented, mainly women and children, after at least five shells struck homes in Mapendo and Kahembe neighbourhoods between 27 and 28 January 2025. The Group does not say which side fired those shells; it adds that residents reported FARDC heavy artillery positioned near residential areas.

The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 46 that, according to local sources verified by UN sources, the FARDC bombing of Nyabibwe (Kalehe territory) on 6 February 2025 caused three civilian injuries (a man and his two children) and impacted at least 35 civilian homes, with no fatalities.

The UN Group of Experts recorded that an AFC/M23 communiqué issued on 6 February 2025 claimed deliberate targeting of Nyabibwe by FARDC bombing, resulting in the massacre of civilians, notably four fatalities including an infant.

The UN Group of Experts reported that from 26 to 27 January, in Goma, retreating FARDC and Wazalendo systematically looted civilian homes and shops, engaging in theft, extortion and the shooting of civilians resisting extortion.

The UN Group of Experts reported, without stating where, that MONUSCO documented the rape of three girls aged 13 to 17 by FARDC soldiers between 31 January and 2 February, and that FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported the arrest of alleged perpetrators.

place: Bukavu (military court); offences in villages of Kabare and Kalehe territories, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 10 February at least 84 FARDC soldiers appeared before a military court in Bukavu, accused of desertion, the murder of at least 12 civilians, rape, looting and other crimes committed in several villages of Kabare and Kalehe territories.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in Bukavu at least six children who had dressed up in military uniforms and played with weapons discarded by fleeing FARDC soldiers were killed by AFC/M23 soldiers conducting security sweeps on 16 February.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 6 February the AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Bahati Erasto, justified AFC/M23 search operations as necessary to apprehend 'Wazalendo and FDLR, mercenaries and FARDC who are still hiding in the houses'.

place: AFC/M23-held areas of North and South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 imposed sentences, typically beatings or summary executions, arbitrarily, and that perceived disloyalty, theft or sexual violence were generally punished by death.

place: Goma and other AFC/M23-held areas, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 operated clandestine detention sites where detainees were held incommunicado, subjected to torture and in many cases either disappeared or later found dead, their bodies discarded in public or remote areas.

place: Stade de l’Unité, Goma, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 51 that multiple corroborated testimonies identified the Stade de l’Unité in Goma as a holding and detention site operated by AFC/M23 and RDF forces, notably used for detaining and forcibly recruiting individuals.

The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 51 that a video filmed on 17 February 2025, two days after AFC/M23 took control of Bukavu, shows the public beating of an individual by men in military uniforms.

place: Stade de l’Unité, Goma, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 51 that video footage provided to it on 18 March 2025 documents severe corporal punishment inflicted by several armed individuals in uniform at the Stade de l’Unité in Goma.

place: Katindo neighbourhood (near Katindo camp, Afia Bora), Karisimbi commune, Goma, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 22 February 2025 at least 17 civilian men were executed near Katindo camp, in Karisimbi commune, Goma, and verified the deaths of at least 17 male victims through photographic and video evidence corroborated by witness testimony; according to witnesses cited by the Group, the killings took place during ongoing AFC/M23 sweeping operations in the Katindo neighbourhood.

The UN Group of Experts reported that during door-to-door searches by AFC/M23 on 22 and 23 February in the Katindo area of Goma, at least 50 civilians were reported to have been killed or forcibly disappeared, with executions taking place on the streets and in civilian homes.

The UN Group of Experts reported that a source close to AFC/M23 confirmed the group's responsibility for the Katindo incident, stating that AFC/M23 acknowledged internally that it was a 'bad incident' involving the summary execution of men accused of taking 'drugs'.

The UN Group of Experts reported that after a France24 report on the Katindo killings, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka dismissed the report as 'fake news' and blatant misinformation aligned with Kinshasa's propaganda, and denied having spoken to France24.

The UN Group of Experts reported that Bertrand Bisimwa admitted the existence of regular daily and nocturnal patrols sweeping Goma but claimed they were carried out lawfully, in a statement published on X on 9 March 2025.

place: Kinshasa (communiqués on Goma and eastern DRC)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the DRC, through official communiqués regularly published by its Minister of Interior, Shabani Lukoo Bihango, denounced the scale and systematic nature of abuses perpetrated by AFC/M23 and the Rwandan army, including summary executions.

The UN Group of Experts reported that following the takeover of Minova on 21 January 2025, local sources and intelligence reports indicated AFC/M23 rounded up all the local youth and men and transported them in trucks to an undisclosed location.

place: Minova, Goma and Bukavu, North and South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that multiple sources said AFC/M23 systematically abducted men, adolescents and children in conquered territories, including in and around urban settings such as Minova, Goma and Bukavu.

place: Stade de l’Unité, Goma, to Rumangabo, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on the morning of 29 January 2025 social media footage showed hundreds of FARDC gathered at the Stade de l’Unité in Goma, and that images show hundreds loaded onto trucks and taken to Rumangabo for accelerated military training.

place: VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR areas of influence and IDP camps, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that in response to increasing AFC/M23 attacks starting January 2025, VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR intensified the recruitment of new combatants, including children, in their areas of influence and in internally displaced persons camps.

place: N’shanga IDP camp, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 January 2025 AFC/M23 dismantled the N’shanga IDP camp in Kalehe territory to repurpose the site for the reinforcement of its elements advancing towards Sake.
The UN Group of Experts reported that on 28 January 2025, in Minova, local sources reported that AFC/M23 elements destroyed IDP camps and forced IDPs to return home.

The UN Group of Experts reported that between 27 and 29 January widespread looting, mainly by the population, of humanitarian warehouses, including those of UNFPA, MSF and the ICRC, resulted in acute shortages of food, medicines and emergency relief supplies.

place: Goma, North Kivu (arrest); statement by Kinshasa
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 39 that the DRC Government stated that the arrest of FDLR 'Brigadier General' Ezechiel Gakwerere was staged by the Government of Rwanda to sustain the narrative of FARDC-FDLR cooperation, in order to justify Rwanda's act of aggression.

The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 39 that FDLR spokesperson Cure Ngoma denied Ezechiel Gakwerere's cooperation with the FARDC, acknowledging his FDLR membership but insisting he was no longer active as he was sick and under medical treatment in Goma.

place: North Kivu (location of announcement not stated)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 7 March 2025 'General' Kasereka Kasyano Kabidon announced the allegiance of the Front commun de la résistance (FCR), a Wazalendo coalition, to AFC/M23, but several FCR members disavowed the announcement and reiterated their loyalty to the Government.

The UN Group of Experts reported that Justin Ndayishimiye, a member of the national Parliament, convened a meeting on 19 March 2025 with VDP/Wazalendo commanders from Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale territories in Katoyi, Masisi territory, to restore VDP/Wazalendo-FARDC coordination and cohesion.

place: Kibati, north-east of Goma, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 20 that on 24 January 2025 RDF troops positioned in Kanyamahoro and Kibumba attacked FARDC Special Forces and PMC positions in Kibati, north-east of Goma, with ZU-23 MM anti-aircraft guns and Type 63 multiple rocket launchers.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 25 January 2025 a MONUSCO armoured personnel carrier at a blocking position in Sake was struck by hostile fire, killing one peacekeeper and injuring four others; military analysts indicated the damage was most likely caused by a missile strike, and analysis of the missile’s trajectory, eyewitness testimony and military analysis indicates that it was fired from the RDF position on the Bulenga peninsula.

place: Ndosho, Mugunga, Kyeshero and Lac Vert, Goma; clashes also in Rusayo, Rumoka and Lushaga, Nyiragongo territory
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 23 that during the night of 11-12 April 2025 a group of reportedly 200 Wazalendo and FDLR combatants attacked AFC/M23 positions in Goma, including the neighbourhoods of Ndosho, Mugunga, Kyeshero and Lac Vert.

The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 23 that sources said up to 52 individuals were killed in the 11-12 April attack on Goma, including at least 12 AFC/M23 combatants and/or RDF soldiers, a figure the Group could not independently verify; eyewitness, security, intelligence and MONUSCO sources reported RDF reinforcements crossed the border into Goma.

The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 23 that the SADC stated in an official communiqué that 'SAMIDRC has not participated in any joint operations' and refuted AFC/M23's allegations, which it qualified as 'inaccurate and misleading'.

The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 3 January 2025 the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo armed groups of the VDP coalition and the FDNB, clashed with the M23/AFC on the Kitchanga-Kayabayonga axis.

The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 19 January 2025 the FARDC, supported by FDLR combatants and the Coalition of Patriotic Movements for the Defense of the Nation (CMPDN), attacked AFC/M23 in Masisi centre.

place: Mabanga, Rutubogo and Karisimbi (as printed), North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 20 February the FARDC, with APCLS, CMC-FDP and NDC-R combatants, clashed with AFC/M23 and RDF in Mabanga, Rutubogo and Karisimbi.

place: Kalembe, border of Masisi and Lubero territories, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 23-24-25 February 2025 the FARDC, with ANCDH and APCLS combatants, clashed in Kalembe, at the border between Masisi and Lubero territories.

place: Kamandi Lac, Lake Edward shore, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 6 March 2025 AFC/M23 clashed with the FARDC and VDP in Kamandi Lac, along the shores of Lake Edward.
The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 10 April 2025 AFC/M23 attacked the FPP-AP stronghold in Bunyatenge, Lubero territory.

place: Katana and Nyamukubi (north of Bukavu); Kamanyola, Ruzizi Plain, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 72 that several hundred FDNB troops were deployed north of Bukavu, in Katana and Nyamukubi, to contain AFC/M23 and RDF, and that on 31 January an additional 2,000 Burundian troops were sent to Kamanyola in the Ruzizi Plain.

place: Lumbishi, Numbi and Nyabibwe, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early February 2025 AFC/M23 expanded its influence into South Kivu, establishing exclusive control over key mineral trading centres in Lumbishi, Numbi and Nyabibwe in Kalehe territory.

place: Kamanyola (South Kivu); Bisie, Walikale territory (North Kivu)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that further military advances towards Uvira resulted in the paralysis of mining activities in Kamanyola, and that the Alphamin Bisie tin mine in Walikale territory suspended operations from 13 March to mid-April 2025.

place: Nyabibwe and Mukwija port, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 looted 186 tons of untagged 3T minerals in Nyabibwe, South Kivu, smuggling them to Rwanda through Mukwija port in Kalehe territory.

place: Bukavu to Kamanyola, Uvira and Bujumbura (Burundi)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that after AFC/M23 and RDF took Bukavu on 16 February, Government authorities, FDNB and FARDC withdrew towards Kamanyola, Uvira and Bujumbura in Burundi.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 9 and 25 March an airplane operating for the benefit of RDF conducted three landings in Minembwe to evacuate at least 16 wounded Twirwaneho and provide pharmaceutical and military supplies.

place: Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu, and diaspora
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that, as previously reported, a significant portion of the Banyamulenge community rejected support for AFC/M23 and Rwanda, that these dissidents were systematically persecuted and intimidated by members of their own community, including abroad, and that some, including in the diaspora, were targeted for assassination, their names circulating on hit-lists called 'akagara'.

place: Bukuma chefferie office, Goma; underground cell north of Kanyaruchinya, North Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 17 that in March 2025 a prominent civil society member from the Bweza groupement, displaced in Goma, was kidnapped by Ephrem Kabasha, the AFC/M23 appointed territorial administrator of Nyiragongo, from the office of Bukuma chefferie and taken to an underground cell north of Kanyaruchinya and tortured, then released the same evening.

The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 17 that in mid-February 2025 Ephrem Kabasha, recently appointed by AFC/M23 as territorial administrator of Masisi, prohibited all associations, including civil society, during a speech in Kaseni.

The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 17 that on 7 January 2025 Ndayambaje Birahira, AFC/M23-appointed deputy provincial coordinator in charge of public finances and taxes in North Kivu, threatened the family of a prominent civil society actor from Rutshuru and obliged the family to leave their house, which AFC/M23 expropriated with all its contents.

The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 71 that Nicolas Kyalangalilwa Mulondani, Federal President of the party Leadership et Gouvernance pour le Développement (LGD) in South Kivu, officially announced his allegiance to AFC/M23 on 22 February, and that Samy Jean Takimbula, Vice-President of the Bureau de Coordination de la Société Civile of South Kivu, pledged support on 23 February and was disavowed by the BCSC/SK President.

place: Bukavu to Rumangabo camp, Rutshuru territory, via Goma
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 12 that on 22 February approximately 2,000 FARDC and PNC were brought from Bukavu to Rumangabo camp, via Goma.

place: Mangoli village, about 15 km north of Bandulu, Bapere sector, Lubero territory
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 15 August 2025 at about 05:00 ADF elements carried out an incursion into Mangoli village, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, killing at least 32 civilians with bladed weapons; an undetermined number of persons were abducted and at least 28 houses were looted and burned.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on the night of 15 to 16 August 2025 ADF elements carried out an incursion into the Mbimbi neighborhood of the town of Oicha, killing nine civilians and injuring two others; the assailants set fire to 19 houses and burned five motorcycles.

The UN Group of Experts reported that throughout 2025 attacks perpetrated under Abwakasi's command led to the killing of over 600 persons, making it the deadliest of all ADF units, and resulted in the displacement of an estimated 25,000 people and the destruction of at least 26 villages and 9 mining sites.

place: eastern DRC (provinces not broken down in this passage)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that one humanitarian actor stated that between January and June 2025 nearly 28,000 victims of sexual violence sought care at facilities it supported in eastern DRC, and that 75 percent of these attacks were committed by armed individuals.

place: Ituri and North Kivu (places not specified)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported (S/2026/466) that it received information about, but was not able to investigate, new cases of conflict-related sexual violence in Ituri and North Kivu, in particular sexual slavery and forced pregnancy by ADF-ISCAP elements leading to the birth of children; the sentence cites the Group's earlier report S/2023/990 (para. 21, annex 12) and gives no dates for the cases.
sources: United Nations Security Council; Amnesty International

place: eastern DRC, majority in North Kivu and South Kivu
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that OCHA DRC recorded 626 security incidents affecting humanitarian workers in 2025, including thirteen deaths, and that the majority of recorded incidents in 2025 and January-February 2026 occurred in North Kivu and South Kivu.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 2 January 2026 a drone strike hit the office of the INGO War Child in Masisi, killing seven people and injuring 42 and others, mainly women and children, and said it is continuing to investigate; in the main text it listed the strike, which it says hit the War Child sub-base in Masisi centre, among FARDC drone operations that affected civilian objects and populations.
The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF withdrew only to Sange, 35 kilometres north of Uvira in the Ruzizi Plain, where AFC/M23 established its headquarters.

place: Kabunambo, about 25 km north of Uvira, Ruzizi Plain
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that in mid-February 2026 the frontline stabilized north of Uvira: fighting ceased on the Ruzizi Plain but persisted in the highlands, and the line settled around Kabunambo with a 10-15 kilometre buffer between the warring parties.

place: Bugarama and Nyangezi (Rwanda) to Kamanyola, Luvungi and Sange along the RN5
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 2 February 2026 approximately 25 trucks carrying RDF troops departed from Bugarama and Nyangezi in Rwanda, arriving in Kamanyola before continuing toward Luvungi and Sange along the RN5.

place: Ruzizi Plain, Moyens Plateaux, Hauts Plateaux, Ngweshe-Mwenga axis, direction of Fizi
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that as of mid-February 2026 RDF deployments in South Kivu were approximately 1,800 troops along the Ruzizi Plain-Moyens Plateaux axis, 800 in the Hauts Plateaux, 1,800 along the Ngweshe-Mwenga axis, and an undetermined number elsewhere including in the direction of Fizi.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 16 December 2025 AFC coordinator Corneille Nangaa posted on his X account a statement announcing that AFC/M23 would unilaterally withdraw its forces from Uvira "as per the United States' mediation request".

The UN Group of Experts reported that Uvira remained effectively under AFC/M23 and RDF control until January, and that AFC/M23 and RDF maintained a covert presence within Uvira, including through combatants dressed in civilian attire or their integration into local "police" units.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in a letter to the UN Secretary-General three days before its withdrawal from Uvira, AFC/M23 justified the withdrawal by citing its "sincere commitment to the ceasefire" and its intention to pursue a peaceful and political resolution of the conflict, said it had requested MONUSCO to ensure civilian protection in Uvira, and called for the deployment of a "neutral force".

The UN Group of Experts reported that by mid-February 2026 RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux; the Group also noted that RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23.

The UN Group of Experts reported that RED Tabara had long-standing camps in Masango (Uvira territory), Magunda (Mwenga territory) and Kipupu (Mwenga territory), and that RED Tabara leadership had repeatedly denied links with AFC/M23 while its combatants took part in hostilities alongside AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and RDF.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 2 March 2026 the US Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned the Rwanda Defence Forces and four senior commanders for direct involvement in destabilizing eastern DRC.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the individuals designated by OFAC were Vincent Nyakarundi, Chief of Staff of the RDF; Major-General Ruki Karusisi, commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former Special Operations Force Commander; General Mubarakh Muganga, Chief of Defence Staff; and Stanislas Gashugi, Special Operations Force Commander since 15 March 2025.

The UN Group of Experts, in its own summary (not a transcript) of an interview President Paul Kagame gave to Jeune Afrique on 26 March 2026, reported that Kagame indicated no intention to withdraw or scale down Rwanda's military posture, stating that defensive measures would remain in place until the perceived threat was addressed, by any means necessary.

The UN Group of Experts, in its own summary (not a transcript) of an interview President Paul Kagame gave to Jeune Afrique on 26 March 2026, reported that Kagame described the fall of Uvira as "inevitable", a necessary consequence of the situation on the ground, claiming that it should not have come as a surprise to any of the parties, including the US, since they were informed on a daily basis of the "evolution of the situation".
The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 continued to privilege military expansion, escalating military operations with the objective of taking Walikale, Kisangani, Kalemie and Beni.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in South Kivu no RDF or AFC/M23 troop withdrawals were documented and fighting continued, and that additional RDF reinforcements arrived from Rwanda in April 2026, including sophisticated weaponry and anti-aerial man-portable air defence systems.

place: Bwito and Bwisha chefferies, Rutshuru territory
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF continued anti-FDLR operations in the Bwito and Bwisha chefferies, Rutshuru territory, also targeting civilians associated with FDLR or affiliated armed groups, including through systematic killings, destruction of livelihoods and burning of villages.

The UN Group of Experts reported that between January and March 2026 significant AFC/M23 and RDF troop reinforcements were documented at the Lubero frontline, raising concerns of an imminent offensive toward Butembo and Beni, which did not materialize.

The UN Group of Experts reported that throughout the reporting period AFC/M23 and RDF prioritized capturing Pinga and Walikale and, since March, also focused on the Bunyakiri (Kalehe)-Ntoto (Masisi)-Hombo (Walikale) axis, which would allow an alternative, southern approach to Walikale.

place: Uvira and Makobola (20 km south of Uvira)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that the capture of Uvira on 10 December 2025 and the rapid advancement of AFC/M23 and RDF forces southwards to Makobola, 20 km south of Uvira, represented a significant territorial expansion, with mutual allegations of cross-border shelling by Burundi and Rwanda.

The UN Group of Experts (final report S/2026/466, citing its earlier report S/2025/446, para. 176) reported that the strength of MRDP/Twirwaneho was estimated at 2,500 to 3,000 combatants, led by Charles Sematama.

The UN Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 elements consolidated around Banyamulenge population centres, including Minembwe, Mikenge and Muranvia, and that RDF presence in the Hauts Plateaux was limited to sporadic, platoon-sized specialized elements and air support.

The UN Group of Experts reported that since February 2026 access to Minembwe had been limited to air supply only, and that several rotations of planes airdropping supplies were documented in March and April 2026.

The UN Group of Experts reported that members of the Banyamulenge community denounced both parties for trapping civilians in an active combat zone, calling on FARDC to lift the siege and establish a humanitarian corridor and on MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 to allow civilians to leave safely.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (not specified)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that each M23 combat unit was supervised and supported by RDF, and that RDF personnel were integrated into mixed battalions alongside M23 elements, including commando units originating from Bigogwe, Rubavu and Cyangugu.
The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the DRC continued to provide funds, logistics and weapons to VDP/Wazalendo groups in North Kivu, in violation of the sanctions regime.

The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR combatants remained embedded within several VDP/Wazalendo groups, notably CMC/FDP, FDDP and APCLS, reinforcing their ranks while obscuring affiliation with FDLR.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in December 2025 Kinshasa-based authorities and FARDC proposed a "coalition nationale des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP/Wazalendo)" following a general assembly held on 13 December 2025, but that VDP/Wazalendo disavowed the initiative, including the proposed leadership.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the "Synergie Masisi-Walikale", comprising 17 armed groups, was led by APCLS leader Janvier Karahiri and sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwisa (CDi.033), and that FDLR-FOCA combatants were integrated into the Masisi-Walikale and Petit Nord synergies.

place: South Kivu, centred on Uvira by December 2025
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that between August and December 2025 Wazalendo relations with FARDC deteriorated significantly, with Wazalendo attacking some FARDC, accusing them of treason, and confiscating weapons and ammunition.

place: outside Uvira town; Fizi; Hauts and Moyens Plateaux
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that after AFC/M23 and RDF occupied Uvira, Wazalendo retreated outside Uvira town or to their bases in Fizi and the Hauts and Moyens Plateaux.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 political actors such as Justin Bitakwira, known for anti-Tutsi rhetoric, and Willy Mishiki mobilized political support and advocated for increased logistical and financial assistance for the Wazalendo in South Kivu.

place: Walungu, Kabare, Minembwe, Mwenga, outskirts of Uvira and Fizi
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that Wazalendo groups often mounted the first lines of defence against AFC/M23 and RDF, including around Uvira, and that between August and December 2025 they fought against AFC/M23 and RDF in Walungu, Kabare, Minembwe and Mwenga and on the outskirts of Uvira and Fizi.

place: Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories; Point Zero; Tuwe Tuwe
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that since reclaiming Uvira, Wazalendo factions supported joint ground operations by FARDC and FDNB in Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, and that in Fizi the FARDC-Wazalendo-FDNB coalition, supported by air strikes, fought to maintain control over Point Zero and Tuwe Tuwe.
The UN Group of Experts reported that in January 2026 CNPSC, through its "finance bureau", published a comprehensive list of taxes across multiple sectors.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in a letter addressed to the President of the United States in July 2025 the FDLR leadership presented its mission as protecting the Rwandese refugee community in the DRC.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 10 March 2026 FARDC elements shot down two kamikaze drones in Mikenge, South Kivu, and that the following day another kamikaze drone struck FARDC positions in the same area.

place: Kutundu axis, Kitundu groupement; Muranvya and Mugeti, Bijombo
statement: The UN Group of Experts listed, in an annex on kamikaze drone attacks, that on 10 April at approximately 23:00 a kamikaze drone struck positions of the FARDC 113th Infantry Regiment in the Kutundu axis within Kitundu groupement (Uvira area), causing multiple FARDC casualties, and that around 23:30 a drone strike targeted FARDC positions in Muranvya, Bijombo (Uvira Territory), affecting elements of the 22nd Simba Battalion. The annex entry does not name who operated the drones; separately, its main text states that between 1 and 14 April RDF and AFC/M23 carried out at least nine drone attacks on FARDC positions in the Hauts Plateaux.

The UN Group of Experts reported that it identified the aircraft destroyed by a FARDC airstrike on 27 March 2025 at the Kigoma airfield in Walikale, then under AFC/M23 control, as a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan operated by Ocean Heights Aviation Training Centre, a company based in Entebbe, Uganda.

The UN Group of Experts reported that talks between the Government of the DRC and AFC/M23 under the Doha process took place in Montreux, Switzerland, between 13 and 17 April 2026, with modest outcomes, leading to a memorandum of understanding on the operationalization of the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism.

The UN Group of Experts reported that Mr. Kabila, the former President (as the report's section heading identifies him), travelled frequently to AFC/M23-controlled territory from May 2025 and held meetings with senior AFC/M23 leadership.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in September 2025 the Military High Court of the DRC sentenced Mr. Kabila to death in absentia, including for treason and organizing an insurrection, accusing him of collaborating with AFC/M23.

The UN Group of Experts reported that Moïse Nyarugabo, a former Congolese senator and key member of Mr. Kabila's inner circle, rose to increasing prominence within the movement; the Group said, citing its earlier reports (S/2021/560 and S/2025/446), that he was a key figure in MRDP/Twirwaneho without holding a formal position, and that he represented MRDP/Twirwaneho interests in high-level meetings with Mr. Kabila and AFC/M23 leadership.

place: Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms, Rutshuru territory
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported, in a footnote, that United Nations and humanitarian actors reported the overall civilian death toll had surpassed 500 throughout Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms since April 2025, and that the Group could not independently establish verified casualty figures.

place: Nyanzalé, Bukombo, Tongo, Bambo (Bwito chiefdom), Rutshuru
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF and AFC/M23 launched coordinated operations in Bwito chiefdom, western Rutshuru, in late April and early May, targeting FDLR and allied forces of the CMC-FDP, including in and around Nyanzalé, Bukombo, Tongo and Bambo.

place: Farmlands between Kiwanja and Ishasha (Binza, Bwisha chiefdom), Rutshuru
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that since mid-July 2025 RDF and AFC/M23 resumed military operations after significant redeployments, and that RDF forces conducted large-scale cordon-and-search operations in farmlands along the main road between Kiwanja and Ishasha while AFC/M23 established a security cordon restricting civilian movement.

place: Marangara, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 27 May 2025 RDF and AFC/M23 attacked FDLR positions in Marangara, an FDLR stronghold, and that civilians were killed and houses set on fire during the clashes; and that on 28 May RDF and AFC/M23 accused inhabitants of Marangara, Lukara and Kirumba of hiding FDLR in their houses, after which, in retaliation, livestock and household items were looted and houses burnt, causing massive displacement.

place: Muliki and Kauma, Tongo groupement, Rutshuru
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 6 October 2025 fire was detected coinciding with attacks reported between Muliki and Kauma, Tongo groupement, with AFC/M23 attacks reported in both locations on 6 and 7 October 2025.
The UN Group of Experts reported that a fire detected on 19 October 2025 coincided with fires reported near Kamena, targeted by AFC/M23 attacks on the same day.

The UN Group of Experts reported that UNHCR in Uganda recorded the arrival of over 70,000 refugees between January and 21 September 2025, with a sharp increase in arrivals from Rutshuru territory since April, coinciding with the start of anti-FDLR operations.

The UN Group of Experts reported that humanitarian actors, civil society and local leaders denounced the AFC/M23 practice of expelling civilians and subsequently denying access to their lands in the areas of the operations it described, leading to loss of livelihoods and a looming famine.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 had vacated Walikale in April 2025 owing to logistical constraints and diplomatic pressure, and that from late May AFC/M23, supported by RDF, prepared renewed offensives from Masisi towards Walikale.

place: Masisi-Kashebere and Nyabiondo-Kashebere axes, Masisi/Walikale boundary
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that from late May 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF deployed reinforcements into Masisi territory along the Masisi-Kashebere and Nyabiondo-Kashebere axes, at the boundary with Walikale territory, with the objective of taking Walikale centre.

The UN Group of Experts reported that throughout June and July military activity intensified across Masisi and Walikale as AFC/M23 and RDF pushed westward and fortified key positions, while VDP/Wazalendo coalitions escalated harassment to delay advances, resulting in heavy clashes around Pinga and Mpeti and along the Masisi–Kashebere–Kibati axis.

The UN Group of Experts reported that by late September AFC/M23 and RDF operations had expanded on three fronts with the aim of encircling Pinga, and that clashes continued around Bibwe in October, with AFC/M23 and RDF capturing additional villages.

place: Nzibira, Luntukulu, Chulwe, Lubimbe, Walungu and Shabunda
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF progressively expanded and consolidated their presence in South Kivu, along various axes across Walungu, Mwenga, Uvira and Kalehe territories, and listed continued advances into Walungu and Shabunda in September and October, culminating in the capture of Nzibira, Luntukulu, Chulwe and Lubimbe.

The UN Group of Experts reported that since late April reinforcements had been documented in strategic locations such as Kamanyola, Katogota, Nyangezi, Luhwinja and Kaziba, including convoys that crossed the border with Rwanda, and that these deployments enabled AFC/M23 and RDF to maintain control over key transit hubs, including Kaziba, Katogota and the Tubimbi–Luhwinja corridor.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 advances towards Uvira were blocked by FDNB and FARDC positions defending the Ruzizi plain, and that the FARDC-Wazalendo-FDNB coalition continued to contest AFC/M23 and RDF advances on multiple fronts.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF continued to provide military support, including troop reinforcements, to besieged MRDP-Twirwaneho enclaves in the Hauts Plateaux despite heavy pressure from FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo forces, and that MRDP-Twirwaneho access routes and supply chains had collapsed.
The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 maintained control over the main 3T (tin, tantalum, tungsten) mining areas around Lumbishi, Numbi and Nyabibwe in Kalehe territory.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 established de facto control over mining operations in the Luhihi area (Kabare territory) following its takeover in mid-February, replacing official State services with a local 'mining office' under its authority, and that the de facto authorities imposed a production tax of 30 per cent on the sale price of ore at pit level.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 30 August AFC/M23 suspended mining activities in Lomera due to tensions with the mining community, and that local sources estimated well over 5,000 artisanal miners operated at Lomera during the first half of 2025.
The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 May 2025 AFC/M23 took over the industrial open-pit Twangiza gold mine, owned by Twangiza Mining SA, in Luhwindja chiefdom, Mwenga territory.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 15 October 2025 at approximately 04:00 a.m. FARDC carried out an aerial strike on the Twangiza site targeting power-generation facilities, with no civilian casualties reported.

The UN Group of Experts reported that a second series of FARDC strikes on Twangiza on 23 October 2025, at 01:03 am, destroyed two fuel-storage tanks and a portion of the processing plant, rendering industrial operations inoperable.

The UN Group of Experts reported that Twangiza Mining SA publicly denounced the systematic looting and destruction of industrial and environmental assets by AFC/M23, alleging active RDF support; the Group also wrote that Reuters had reported the company's allegation that AFC/M23 looted at least 500 kilograms of bullion since seizing the mine in May. The Group dates that Reuters article 21 September 2025, but the Reuters URL in its own footnote is dated 2025-10-21.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 23 October AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa publicly denied the allegations made by Twangiza Mining SA, claiming that the mine was inactive, with only artisanal miners present, and that AFC/M23 lacked the necessary expertise and resources to operate gold mines; and that AFC/M23 published a communiqué on 27 October 2025 denying the accusations.

The UN Group of Experts conservatively estimated that between 6,000 and 7,000 RDF personnel remained deployed across North and South Kivu at the time of drafting, comprising at least two brigades and two special forces battalions.
The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF had established a base on Idjwi island, often used for troop deployments and rotations via Lake Kivu.

place: North and South Kivu front lines
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 sources, including a senior commander participating in joint operations, confirmed that RDF elements, referred to as the 'Friendly Force', 'manage the front lines' and 'control M23 combatants'.

The UN Group of Experts reported that Guidon Shimiray Mwissa (CDi.033), leader of NDC-R and VDP commander, moved his headquarters from Pinga to Kibati, Walikale territory, to contain RDF and AFC/M23 advancement along the Walikale-Kibua-Kashebere-Masisi axis.

The UN Group of Experts reported that APCLS leader Janvier Karairi Boingo and his troops were based in Lukweti, Masisi territory, while CMC-FDP, led by Dominique Ndaruhutse, was in Virunga National Park fighting in areas including Katsiru, Rwindi, Bukombo, Bambo, Tongo and Kalengera in Rutshuru territory.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 30 September 2025 VDP/Wazalendo leaders and government authorities met in Kinshasa to redefine counter-offensive strategies and cooperation, that sources privy to the discussions reported the Government agreed to continue providing financial and logistical support to VDP/Wazalendo, and that the Government continued to provide $300,000 monthly to VDP/Wazalendo through the office of the governor of North Kivu.

The UN Group of Experts reported that FARDC Colonel Sekololo, based in Walikale, still acted as the liaison between FARDC and VDP, and that regular FARDC helicopter rotations to VDP/Wazalendo-held front lines in Walikale delivered uniforms, weapons, ammunition and food supplies.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the contract of Congo Aviation, formerly Agemira, was abruptly terminated at the end of July, following accusations of responsibility for the fall of Goma and Bukavu, and that the Congo Aviation CH-4 drone pilots, identified as Algerian nationals, have been contracted directly by the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The UN Group of Experts reproduced, in an annex, statistics on extrajudicial or summary executions by perpetrators in all DRC conflict-affected provinces showing AFC/M23 as the actor responsible for most of the violations in August 2025 (35,6%), surpassing ADF, CODECO and Wazalendo groups; a reduction in AFC/M23 violations in September 2025 (9,47%), surpassed by ADF (36,09%), CODECO (16,57%) and FARDC (10,65%); and an increase in M23-attributed killings in October 2025 (to 19,8%).

place: not specified in the source (para. 81 follows the North Kivu discussion)
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported, in a paragraph on abuses by VDP/Wazalendo groups, that Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains combatants have been implicated most frequently in serious abuses against civilians, such as abductions, lootings, rape, unlawful killings and arson.

The UN Group of Experts reported that VDP/Wazalendo groups also engaged in retaliatory attacks, including summary executions or targeted assassinations of individuals accused of collusion with AFC/M23, albeit on a much smaller scale than the recent systematic violations perpetrated by AFC/M23 and RDF.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in early September competition over the control of roadblocks in Mwenga sparked violence among Wazalendo groups, notably Mai Mai Corbeau and Mai Mai Malaika, which forced the FARDC to intervene to dismantle the growing number of barriers.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, according to witnesses it interviewed, Wazalendo groups established an ever-increasing number of roadblocks in and around Uvira, including along major and secondary roads; that Wazalendo imposed taxes ranging from 5,000 to 50,000 Congolese francs on road users, traders and citizens; and that between March and September at least 10 roadblocks were identified on the Misisi-Lulimba axis.

place: Locality in Walikale near the Rutshuru border; Rusamambo axis
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 26 May AFC/M23 carried out a cordon-and-search operation in a locality in Walikale, near the Rutshuru border, during which approximately 80 young men suspected of affiliation with Wazalendo factions were apprehended, and that they were reportedly transferred by force to the Rusamambo axis two days later, dressed in AFC/M23 uniforms, and deployed to the frontlines to serve as human shields.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 3 July the Congolese Minister for Human Rights, Chantal Chambu, denounced that more than 300 young men, including minors, had been captured in Rubaya without any valid legal justification and taken to an unknown destination, and that local sources, civil society and eyewitnesses confirmed the incident.

The UN Group of Experts reported that two individuals abducted by AFC/M23 with a group of 35 young men in April 2025 escaped and testified in June; they described hunger, untreated illnesses and physical abuse including torture among trainees at Rumangabo, and said 13 individuals in their group had been executed.

The UN Group of Experts reported that it interviewed victims of arrest who had witnessed torture, inhumane treatment, including detainees stripped naked and held without food and water, and summary executions in detention centres in Goma.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the newly established M23/PRC continued to conduct large-scale operations in Goma and Bukavu, resulting in arbitrary detentions and the forcible conscription of boys and men.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 continued the recruitment and training of its 'local defence' forces, tasked with maintaining security in towns and villages controlled by AFC/M23, and that these forces were frequently implicated in clashes with FDLR and Wazalendo combatants and in human rights abuses; it annexed an announcement on the graduation of 242 Local Defense Personnel in Nyiragongo, dated 23 September 2025.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 September FARDC's 3rd Defense Zone command reported that it received 30 alleged AFC/M23-ARC combatants, including two minors, who surrendered voluntarily to the FARDC, while 15 others were captured during clashes in North Kivu and South Kivu.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 February AFC/M23 forces issued an ultimatum to residents of Karenga, who had returned to Karenga after the dismantling of IDP camps around Goma in early February, to leave by the next day or be shot.

place: Sake and Stade de l’Unité, Goma
statement: The UN Group of Experts reported that in Sake, prior to transferring the refugees to Goma, AFC/M23 screened them, separating women and children from men, amid reports of physical violence, and that at least 180 men accused of FDLR affiliation were separated and brought to Stade de l’Unité in Goma, from where they were taken to an unknown location and their whereabouts remain unknown.

The UN Group of Experts reported that at least 72 Congolese nationals transferred to Rwanda were returned to the DRC after successfully demonstrating their Congolese citizenship, while other Congolese citizens were unlawfully deported to Rwanda without having been given the opportunity to prove their citizenship.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 17 May Rwanda's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe, stated that the transferred individuals were “previously held hostages by the FDLR genocidal force.”

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka echoed, shortly thereafter, the statement by Rwanda's foreign minister that the transferred individuals were “previously held hostages by the FDLR genocidal force.”

The UN Group of Experts reported that since January 2025 at least 5,798 individuals were repatriated to Rwanda, primarily from Masisi territory but also from Rutshuru territory, and that a confidential source with direct knowledge of repatriation operations referred to recent repatriations, including the repatriation of 227 Rwandan refugees on 23 October, primarily Hutu women and children from Masisi and Rutshuru territories.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in May and June 2025 the Congolese government accused AFC/M23 and Rwanda of ethnic cleansing by resettling “Rwandan families” with Rwandan identity cards in eastern DRC, and annexed an official communiqué by the DRC Minister of Interior of 14 May 2025 accusing Rwanda of orchestrating an ethnic cleansing and repopulation operation.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 16 June AFC/M23 appointed Jean-Damascène Mwigimba as provincial director for its own iteration of the Commission Nationale pour les Réfugiés (CNR), overseeing cross-border refugee movements.
The UN Group of Experts reported that local sources confirmed AFC/M23 began in July 2025 to build a centre in Karenga, Masisi territory, including a transit site, a school and a health centre.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 9 October AFC/M23 installed Bashali Luanda Jaques on the throne of the Bashali chefferie during a ceremony in Kitchanga, in contravention of traditional succession procedures and despite objections from the Bashali royal family representing the legitimate Mwami, Bashali N'siyi Minihire Roger.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 converted villages into towns or communes, including in Sake, Ngungu, Rubaya and Bweremana in Masisi territory, abolishing all customary rights, and that in August AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor Bahati Erasto announced plans to subdivide Goma into four communes instead of the existing two.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 19 June AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor Bahati Erasto authorized the resumption of operations within the land registry and property title divisions in North Kivu, and that on 25 July Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba, AFC/M23-appointed governor of South Kivu, issued land management laws, including new procedures for obtaining building permits and cadastral documents.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 29 May 2025 AFC/M23 announced an arbitration court for local conflicts in Goma, that on 12 August it created a 25-member Commission pour la Restauration de la Justice presided by Delion Kimbulungu Mutangala, and that on 3 November the commission announced 378 successful magistrate candidates.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government declared it would invalidate all judicial acts undertaken by AFC/M23 in violation of the country’s constitutional order, and annexed a statement of the DRC Conseil Supérieur de la Magistrature, dated 12 September 2025, declaring all judicial acts undertaken by AFC/M23 a violation of the constitutional order of the DRC.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the Peace Agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of Rwanda was signed in Washington, D.C. on 27 June 2025, brokered by the United States of America in consultation with Qatar and Togo (as African Union mediator).

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 3 July Benjamin Mbonimpa, head of the AFC/M23 delegation in Doha, and Freddy Rukema Kanyiki, AFC/M23's deputy coordinator, reiterated the need for the DRC Government to agree to several trust-building measures, and that the Doha Declaration of Principles, brokered by Qatar, was signed by the DRC Government and AFC/M23 on 19 July 2025 and welcomed by the Government of Rwanda.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the parties maintained active engagement in Doha and on 18 September signed a formal prisoner exchange agreement as part of confidence-building measures, and that on 14 October both sides concluded an agreement establishing a ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism.
The UN Group of Experts reported that in July 2025 Benjamin Mbonimpa, AFC/M23 permanent secretary and chief negotiator at Doha, stated that AFC/M23 was proposing federalism as a form of governance.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo expected AFC/M23 to withdraw and accept cantonment, while AFC/M23 leaders insisted on maintaining control of current positions and seeking integration into State structures.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in a letter addressed to the US President, as facilitator of the Washington peace process, the FDLR leadership alleged that the FDLR's assigned mission consisted of protecting the Rwandese refugee community in the DRC, and expressed concern that the neutralisation plan was being implemented in an indiscriminate manner, potentially targeting civilians.

The UN Group of Experts reported that VDP/Wazalendo spokesperson Jules Mulumba called for the recognition of the VDP/Wazalendo as legitimate stakeholders and requested their inclusion in peace negotiations, and stated that they rejected any agreements from Doha that did not consider their demands.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that M23 members committed retaliatory killings immediately after seizing localities, and that several civilians were summarily executed in Minova, South Kivu, in January immediately after M23 took control.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in June and July M23 summarily executed dozens of individuals following confrontations with Government forces in Walungu and Kabare territories (South Kivu), as apparent collective punishment.

place: Bishwa chefferie [as printed in para. 31; para. 19 prints Bwisha], Rutshuru territory
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that from 8 to 29 July M23 members, accompanied by civilians armed with machetes and alleged RDF soldiers, attacked several farms in Bishwa chefferie in Rutshuru and allegedly executed hundreds of civilians, mainly Hutu; the FFM said it could not fully investigate these incidents given time constraints.
The OHCHR fact-finding mission stated in a footnote that OHCHR reported M23 killed at least 319 civilians in Rutshuru from 9 to 21 July.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that at least 21 civilians, including adolescent boys below 18, were executed in M23 cordon-and-search operations in the Kasika neighborhood of Goma on 22 and 23 February; armed M23 members went door to door rounding up local youth, allegedly on accusations of criminality, and killed most victims at point blank range.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 16 February in Bukavu M23 members killed a man, allegedly for failing to present identification documents; on 22 February a man was executed for stealing a telephone, and the same day two men accused of filming an M23 convoy were publicly executed, the perpetrators reportedly stating to bystanders that 'no indiscipline will be tolerated'.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission recorded at least 11 children deliberately shot at and killed by M23 for no discernable reason; examples given were a 17-year-old boy shot in the head at a bar in Goma in February, and a woman and her two young children shot in April.
The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 13 February in Goma M23 members killed Delcat Idengo, a singer and activist known for songs critical of both M23 and the Congolese authorities.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in at least four incidents in Goma M23 entered hospitals to locate suspected FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR members being treated or hiding there, detaining hundreds of people, including patients, medical personnel and accompanying family members.

place: M23-controlled areas, North and South Kivu
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that M23 detained thousands of civilians, primarily during cordon-and-search operations conducted almost daily since January.

place: M23-controlled areas, North and South Kivu
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that many of those detained, mostly able-bodied men and boys around 15 and older, were loaded into trucks and taken away.
The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 17 February AFC/M23 issued instructions giving a one-week ultimatum for parents to retrieve their children.

place: Improvised detention sites, North and South Kivu
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported accounts indicating that some guards at improvised M23-run detention sites in North and South Kivu were Rwandans, and said it received credible information that senior M23 commanders, including M23's military leader, were present at some of these sites; their names were retained on file.

place: Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps, Rutshuru territory
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that individuals forcefully recruited or otherwise detained were transported to former FARDC camps in Rumangabo and Tshanzu (Rutshuru territory) for 're-education' and military 'training' for three to four months, before being reportedly deployed to the front line.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that guards from Tshanzu removed women from their enclosures at night, and that many women detainees, unable to endure the hunger, were subjected to sexual exploitation and forced to exchange sex for food.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that other incidents in M23 detention included so-called 'corrective rapes', forced nudity, non-consensual touching and sexual slurs, perpetrated either by M23 guards or by co-detainees with the instigation or acquiescence of de facto authorities.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that after capturing Goma, M23 members ordered tens of thousands of IDPs living in camps around the city to dismantle their shelters and return to their villages.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 25 February Hutu families who had returned to Karenga (Masisi territory, North Kivu) after the forced dismantlement of their camp were ordered to leave the town within a day and were threatened that if they did not comply, 'the Red Cross would come to collect [their] bodies'.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that between 10 and 13 May M23 forces detained hundreds of people, mostly men and adolescent boys, during cordon-and-search operations in Goma, Nyiragongo and Sake and took them to Goma stadium, where they were grouped by presumed affiliation.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 22 May UNHCR stated that more than 1,700 'Rwandan nationals' brought to a transit center after cordon-and-search operations had been returned to Rwanda after screening interviews conducted 'under pressure'.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in North Kivu women and adolescent girls were subjected to gang rapes by retreating FARDC and Wazalendo, and that one woman was held hostage, tied to a tree and raped daily for two weeks by multiple perpetrators until her family paid a ransom.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that during their retreat soldiers from the 'Satan II' and 'Guépard' units repeatedly entered homes, looted property and raped civilians, following a consistent pattern across multiple locations and over a wide geographic area.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported community mobilization campaigns with door-to-door visits and mass gatherings, particularly between February and April in Fizi territory, South Kivu, during which boys and girls were encouraged to enroll.

place: South Kivu: checkpoints, Uvira, Fizi territory
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported verified witness accounts of boys visibly under 18 carrying weapons at Wazalendo checkpoints in South Kivu, patrolling in Uvira, and bearing AK-47 rifles in Fizi territory.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission examined allegations of at least six children killed when M23 entered Bukavu, who had taken uniforms and weapons left behind by fleeing Wazalendo and FARDC members; it could not determine the precise circumstances of their deaths.

place: Uvira and parts of Fizi territory
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that after February Wazalendo groups capitalized on the security vacuum left by retreating Congolese forces to assert control over Uvira and parts of Fizi territory, establishing parallel administrative and judicial structures, conducting informal trials and carrying out illegal arrests.

place: Uvira and parts of Fizi territory
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission identified at least 13 detention sites under the direct authority of self-proclaimed Wazalendo 'generals', where detainees were routinely subjected to torture and other forms of ill-treatment.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that Wazalendo groups substantially restricted freedom of movement with numerous checkpoints in Uvira and along the Uvira-Kamanyola or Uvira-Fizi roads, where civilians were required to pay 'fees'.

place: not specified (para. 65, in the report's section on FARDC, Wazalendo and affiliated groups)
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission said it received multiple reports of members of the Tutsi community being killed, and of others being denied access to local markets on ethnic grounds.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that the escalation of violence in January led to a sharp rise in sexual violence reported by the United Nations and humanitarians, with cases involving children tripling in one month.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that sexual violence took place mainly in the form of gang rapes by up to seven perpetrators, during or after military operations, in the context of disruption of law and order or during the displacement of populations fleeing armed conflict.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in some instances victims were abducted and subjected to sexual slavery; for example, a 19-year-old woman was abducted, taken to an unknown location to become the 'wife' of an FDLR element who raped her for two days.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported cases of sexual violence against men and boys and LGBT individuals, including a verified case of a 13-year-old boy raped along with his mother, a 14-year-old boy beaten and forced to have sexual intercourse with a female relative in front of his siblings, and a documented case of forced nudity, beatings and public humiliation of an LGBT individual by Wazalendo members.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that it confirmed that, during the mass escape from Munzenze prison on 27 January, most of the 160 women inmates, along with numerous infants, died, and that an undetermined number were gang-raped, in some cases in front of their children, by male inmates who had forced their way into the women's ward.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission confirmed repeated rapes, other ill-treatment and death threats by an escapee previously convicted by national judicial authorities, against victims and human rights defenders who had testified against him in court.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that victims' access to appropriate healthcare remained severely constrained due to ongoing hostilities, limited financial resources, threats against healthcare personnel, non-payment of salaries to medical staff, insufficient post-exposure prophylaxis kits and a reduction in international funding to health and support providers.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that shells reportedly struck the maternity ward of Charité Maternelle Hospital in Goma on 28 January, killing and injuring several civilians, including newborns and pregnant women.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 24 January multiple projectiles, including a 122mm rocket, struck the Rusayo IDP camp, killing at least 14, mostly women and children, and injuring many others.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 27 February at least 13 individuals were killed when explosions occurred during an M23-organized gathering at Place de l'Indépendance in Bukavu; it could not identify the perpetrator of the explosions.
The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in June clashes between M23 and Wazalendo, including shelling by all parties in Kabare territory, resulted in dozens of civilians killed.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 23 January M23 and RDF launched a coordinated offensive on Sake, 25 km west of Goma, eventually overwhelming FARDC troops supported by MONUSCO and SAMIDRC as well as private military companies contracted by the Congolese Government.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that the spontaneous withdrawal of some FARDC troops from their positions, the killing of the Military Governor of North Kivu and the desertion of senior FARDC officers further accelerated the breakdown of Congolese defenses, and that by 29 January M23 and RDF had taken full control of Goma.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 14 February M23 seized Kavumu airport and two days later entered the provincial capital Bukavu without resistance, as Government forces had withdrawn toward the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira.

place: Uvira and parts of Fizi territory
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that after the Uvira and Kamanyola clashes most FARDC troops withdrew further, effectively ceding control of Uvira and parts of Fizi territory to Wazalendo.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that upon capturing Goma and Bukavu, AFC/M23 appointed 'administrators' to formalize its control as de facto authority and introduced its own 'tax collection system', and that civil servants and customary chiefs opposing M23 were replaced with individuals supportive of M23.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission described a '10 houses system' implemented in M23-held areas as an administrative structure for local chiefs appointed by M23 to monitor residents' movements and report daily on suspicious activities.
The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that the Government of Rwanda has consistently denied allegations of its direct involvement with M23, including in response to the report.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported in a footnote that Rwanda denied, in its response to the report, the finding of active and decisive involvement of the RDF alongside M23 during the capture of Goma.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported in a footnote that, in its response to the report, the Congolese Government noted that formal orders were issued by the President and the FARDC Chief of Staff to prohibit any collaboration with the FDLR.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission cited a May 2025 AFC Secretariat document titled 'AFC/M23's reaction to allegations human rights violations in the Goma and Bukavu' as the source for M23's 'stated objective' of restoring order, security and stability.
The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 27 June senior ministers of the DRC and Rwanda signed a Peace Agreement in Washington.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 19 July there followed a Declaration of Principles between the Government of the DRC and M23 in Doha, committing to reaching a comprehensive peace agreement by 18 August.

place: South Kivu near the Burundian border; Lubero, Rutshuru and Walikale territories
statement: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in July both M23 and FARDC reinforced their positions in South Kivu near the Burundian border, and that M23 maintained military pressure in North Kivu, targeting residual FARDC, FDLR and Wazalendo forces in Lubero, Rutshuru and Walikale territories.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that cross-border shelling between the FARDC and RDF allegedly resulted in civilian casualties, with Rwandan authorities reporting at least 16 deaths and 177 injured in Gisenyi, including women and children; the FFM said it was unable to corroborate civilian casualties.

The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that during the fighting for Goma three UN peacekeepers were killed, allegedly in a targeted attack by M23 and RDF (source: Spokesman for the Secretary-General).

Actualite.cd reported, citing medical sources it contacted, that the Mweso general referral hospital (Masisi) was overwhelmed by the high number of war-wounded arriving from combat zones, in the context of continuing clashes between AFC/M23 and the FARDC supported by local militias.

Actualite.cd reported that MSF announced the early end of its medical activities in Baraka, Fizi health zone, South Kivu, because of the deteriorating security situation, saying it had evacuated its teams after the M23 advance and the capture of Uvira, and that activities at Baraka general hospital and three health centres had ended.

Kivu Morning Post reported that four civilians of Bukumbirwa were missing since Monday 27 October 2025 after Wazalendo elements of the CMC group, led by a self-proclaimed general named Bigabo, passed through fields at Mahasha near Bukumbirwa (Muronga, Walikale), and that the group accuses them of complicity with the AFC-M23; an anonymous resident was quoted.

7sur7.cd reported that Congolese human rights minister Chantal Mwavita said that between 28 and 29 June more than 300 young people were arrested by the M23 at Rubaya and about twenty others at Rugendo (Kabare), were presented publicly at a meeting as volunteers, and that she denounced this as forced recruitment.

7sur7.cd reported that the Congolese Interior Ministry, in an official communiqué, denounced actions in AFC-M23-held areas of North Kivu including more than 272 assassinations and summary executions, more than 300 rapes and more than 300 acts of torture, which it said occurred mainly between 20 September and 2 October 2025 in Rutshuru, Walikale and Masisi territories.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (areas under rebel occupation)
statement: Radio Okapi/MCP, via Mediacongo, reported that the Congolese Interior Minister said he had recorded at least 123 assassinations and 223 rapes in North and South Kivu in October (2025), according to a communiqué received by Radio Okapi on Saturday 1 November; the page headline says 'more than 120' assassinations.

Radio Okapi/MCP, via Mediacongo, reported that the Congolese Interior Minister said more than 100 young people from Bukavu were kidnapped and forcibly enrolled between 14 and 28 October (2025) at camp Sayo, then taken to an unknown destination.

place: Cahoboka dispensary, Irambi Katana grouping (Katana), Kabare
statement: 7sur7.cd reported that, according to a communiqué of the South Kivu provincial government signed by its spokesperson Luganywa Bashizi Didier, six civilian men, including patients and health-care staff, were killed by AFC/M23 rebels in Irambi Katana grouping (Kabare) in an attack on the night of 23 to 24 November 2025 on the Cahoboka dispensary; the communiqué said the victims were forcibly taken from the facility and subjected to cruel treatment before being summarily executed.

Actualite.cd reported, citing an OCHA report it said was made public on Tuesday 18 November, that the looting of health structures on 16 October at Rwindi and Birambizo (Rutshuru territory) deprived nearly 92,500 people of access to care.

place: South Kivu (Walungu, Kabare, Kalehe, Fizi, Uvira, Mwenga)
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing an OCHA report, that protection actors documented 2,504 incidents in South Kivu, including 263 cases of gender-based violence, 137 cases of sexual violence and 366 cases of violations of children's rights; the headline says the sexual violence and child rights cases were recorded in July.
Actualite.cd reported, citing an OCHA report, that two health facilities were attacked in Kalehe and Uvira territories of South Kivu.

Radio Okapi reported that more than 74 civilians were killed and 83 wounded in South Kivu since 2 December 2025 in clashes between the FARDC and the M23 (the source adds 'appuyés par les combattants Wazalendo', supported by Wazalendo fighters); the report cites a communiqué of Bruno Lemarquis (humanitarian coordinator and acting head of MONUSCO) on the escalation of violence. The page does not say who produced the figures.

Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué seen on 10 December 2025, Bruno Lemarquis (humanitarian coordinator and acting head of MONUSCO) said the escalating violence in South Kivu notably hinders medical evacuations and affects schools and other civilian infrastructure.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that four people were killed and eleven wounded on Thursday 29 January 2026 around 18:30 in Sange, Uvira territory, by a grenade explosion; according to local sources an unidentified individual threw the device in the middle of the town, and MP Justin Bitakwira publicly accused the M23 of being behind it. The M23 held a meeting with residents of Sange on 30 January and called on anyone illegally holding arms or munitions to hand them in.

Actualite.cd reported, in an article on the Forum des ONGI en RDC condemning drone strikes in Goma, that in January 2026 the office of the international organisation War Child in Masisi, North Kivu, had already suffered significant damage following an air attack in the area.

place: eastern DRC (communiqué on Goma, North Kivu)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the Forum des ONGI en RDC, in a communiqué condemning drone strikes in Goma, recalled that in 2025, 13 humanitarians were killed in the region against 9 in 2024, and that 626 security incidents targeting them were recorded in 2025 against 428 the previous year, citing OCHA.

Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that about a hundred road users had been blocked at Kanyabayonga, in the south of Lubero, since 3 October 2026 (the page prints 'vendredi 3 octobre 2026') after the closure of the Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja, Kanyabayonga-Kibirizi, Kanyabayonga-Rwindi and Kanyabayonga-Vitshumbi axes, a measure it said followed the confirmation of six new Ebola cases in the Kayna and Alimbongo health zones and was confirmed in a communiqué of the AFC/M23 administration that controls the area. It said the AFC/M23 administration at Rutshuru announced the suspension of traffic on the Kanyabayonga–Kikuku, Kanyabayonga–Vitshumbi, Kanyabayonga–Kiwanja and Nyakakoma–Ishasha axes, with only goods vehicles and humanitarian vehicles with the governor's prior authorisation allowed. Users at Kiwanja asked for Ebola prevention measures to be reinforced while allowing traffic to resume.

Actualite.cd reported that after five days of occupation the M23 rebels backed by the Rwandan army withdrew from Kasugho, an agglomeration of 21 thousand ('21 milles') inhabitants at the foot of the Tayna gorilla reserve, 45 km west of Lubero-centre, and that a resident who requested anonymity said the rebels withdrew without fighting in the night to 7 March and headed for Bunyatenge.

BETO reported that M23 elements withdrew from Friday 7 March from three villages of Lubero territory, Kasugho, Katoyo and Kagheri, about 45 km west of Lubero centre, after intense clashes between the FARDC supported by VDP and the M23; it also said the Ugandan army (UPDF) had for some weeks occupied the neighbouring village since the M23 threatened Lubero-centre.

BETO, in a 7 March 2025 article whose byline reads 'AFP La Rédaction Kinshasa' and which is signed Merveilles Kiro, reported that during their withdrawal from Kasugho the M23 rebels were accused of looting, including equipment of the RTCT Kasugho radio and villagers' shops, and quoted a witness as saying they took the new mixer, the computer and the microphones from their base at the radio; Actualite.cd quoted an anonymous resident as saying that before leaving the rebels looted, notably at radio Tayna and in shops.

Actualite.cd reported that by the evening it still could not establish who controlled Kasugho: civil society sources spoke of Ugandan UPDF soldiers, a unit of which was deployed on the axis from Lubero centre to Kasugho, while the local authority said Kasugho was controlled by Wazalendo militiamen; Paluku Kuliumbwa said the UPDF soldiers were not yet at Kasugho but at Kagheri, 15 km away, and that the Wazalendo controlled Kasugho. The outlet also reported, per its sources on the spot and confirmed by Paluku Kuliumbwa, the state's delegated official at Kasugho, that Wazalendo who returned after the rebels' withdrawal came across an armed man in a drunken state, taken to be an M23 rebel, and shot him dead.

place: Lubero territory (Kitsombiro, Kipese, Kasugho), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Uganda's chief of defence staff, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, argued in an X post the previous week that the M23 rebels backed by the Rwandan army should fall back 20 km south of their positions in Lubero (Kitsombiro, Kipese, Kasugho); the outlet noted that some said the M23 was ceding place to the Ugandan army at Kasugho.

Actualite.cd reported that the rebels kept control of the stretch from Kanyabayonga to Kitsombiro, a distance of nearly 100 km towards Butembo, and were still positioned at Kitsombiro, about 30 km from Lubero-centre, described as their current target.

Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that the M23 also controlled gold-bearing zones such as Musigha, in the Bunyatenge area of Lubero, forcing the self-proclaimed general Kasereka Kasiyano Kabido, leader of the FPP-AP group, to rally them to 'keep his mining interests'.

place: Kamandi Gite, Kibanda, Luofu, Kirumba, Kayna (Lubero), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local and security sources, that clashes between the FARDC, backed by Wazalendo fighters, and the M23 rebels, supported by Rwanda, resumed at about 4 am on 14 January in the villages of Kamandi Gite and Kibanda, about 60 km from Lubero-Centre, with heavy and light weapons heard as far as Kayna and Kirumba; that other fighting was reported a little further east in the village of Luofu and around the rural area of Kirumba; and that, per security sources, the FARDC, keeping their initial positions, were replying to M23 attacks by shelling rebel positions with artillery and combat helicopters.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23, reinforced by the RDF, consolidated its positions in Lubero territory in anticipation of future operations and that in mid-October 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF redeployed additional troops from Tchanzu to the Lubero front line along the Kanyabayonga-Kirumba axis, reportedly including recruits who had graduated on 1 October.

The UN Group of Experts reported that sources reported on 16 September 2025 the deployment of at least 15 fully loaded trucks with AFC/M23 combatants coming from the AFC/M23-ARC training camp in Rumangabo in Kirumba, near Kanyabayonga, in Lubero territory, two days after a pass-out ceremony.
