The UN Group of Experts reported that Bahati Erasto, North Kivu's AFC/M23-appointed governor, during visits to Kanyabayonga and Kirumba between 9 and 11 June, claimed that Lubero, Butembo and Beni would soon fall under AFC/M23 control.

Actualite.cd, relaying MONUSCO, reported that ninety-two defendants were appearing before the Butembo garrison military tribunal sitting at Lubero-Centre, accused of several charges including sexual violence, in hearings launched on 26 June with MONUSCO support and expected to last about ten days; MONUSCO's public information section in Beni said the defendants, including 45 FARDC soldiers and 47 civilians, were prosecuted for rapes, sexual violence, abduction of children and extortion of funds, crimes committed between 2021 and 2024.

Actualite.cd reported that three displaced adults had died of hunger at Lubero-Centre in the previous month and that the displacement site in the territory office compound faced hunger, lack of access to medical care and a total lack of humanitarian assistance. Kathungu Thamweya Charline, president of the displaced in Lubero commune, told the outlet that five children had also died, that several other displaced people were bedridden in local health facilities without adequate care, and that no humanitarian aid had arrived for more than three months. The outlet said humanitarian organisations could no longer reach the area because of persistent insecurity, and that the displaced were fleeing violent clashes between the FARDC and AFC/M23 in several entities of south Lubero, some coming from areas regularly attacked by other armed groups.

place: Kayna health zone, Lubero, North Kivu
statement: 7sur7.cd reported that the Kayna health zone was affected by the Ebola epidemic with a confirmed case, a 21-year-old man from Butembo intercepted on 2 September at a checkpoint in the Itsu health area; it said this came two months after AFC-M23 had announced the end of the epidemic in the zones under its administration, and that, per the Lubero administrator Kiwewa Mitela, surveillance was reinforced in the Kayna and Kirumba health zones.

place: Vuvogho health centre, Kanyabayonga (Lubero), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that in the south of Lubero territory the Kayna health zone faced serious operating difficulties, and that at Kanyabayonga the Vuvogho health centre struggled to give adequate care for lack of funds; the head nurse Paluku Mupanda said its operation rested almost entirely on patients' contributions, a consequence of the absence of partners in the health sector, and the centre regularly ran out of medicines, notably for malaria.

Radio Okapi reported that the town of Nyabiondo in Masisi territory passed on Sunday 9 March under the occupation of the M23/AFC rebels, which it described as backed by Rwanda, after intense fighting between those rebels and the FARDC, supported by fighters of the APCLS of Janvier Kalahiri.

place: Nyabiondo, Kashebere, Kibua; Masisi and Walikale
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the occupation of Nyabiondo on Sunday 9 March caused a massive displacement of inhabitants of at least six villages, who according to local notables took refuge at the Kashebere health centre, while others went towards Kibua and the surrounding bush.
Radio Okapi reported that several local sources said the M23 rebels were aiming at Walikale-centre in order to reach the Bisiye deposits.

Radio Okapi reported that local actors lamented the absence of humanitarian aid in the area affected by the fighting around Nyabiondo, with the exception of Médecins sans frontières (MSF), which continued to support the Nyabiondo hospital.

Actualite.cd reported that the company Alphamin Bisie Mining (ABM) announced the immediate suspension of its mining operations from Friday 14 March because of growing risks to the safety of its staff.

Actualite.cd reported that clashes particularly shook the locality of Kibati, where the AFC/M23 and the FARDC-wazalendo coalition fought violently over control of the village, and that, according to its sources, at the end of Thursday 13 March the belligerents shared control of Kibati, the outcome remaining uncertain.

Actualite.cd reported, in a headline, that the Kibua general hospital in Walikale territory received medicines six months after its looting by AFC/M23 rebels, and quoted its medical director, Dr Isaac Bihango, as saying the aid would help relaunch medical activity and that medical prescriptions, which had become the system of care, would now be a thing of the past.

Actualite.cd reported that the Kibua general hospital released 13 people who had been blocked at the hospital for failure to pay their bills after treatment, thanks to the medicines aid received on 26 September.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil society, that displaced people and their host families in Walikale territory received no humanitarian assistance and that for nearly four months several health structures in the region had been deprived of supplies of medicines and other essential inputs, a crisis it attributed to instability caused by the M23's occupation of several North Kivu localities.

The ICRC reported, in a press release on access to health care in the Kivus, that a man identified as Shukuru said he was wounded at Pinga in July in Walikale territory and was evacuated to Beni for care, at the Beni general referral hospital about 300 km from where he was wounded.

Radio Okapi reported that the M23 rebellion was intensifying its campaign to recruit young people in North Kivu for what it calls the Congolese revolutionary army (ARC), through a recruitment and mobilisation committee, and that the campaign also took place in the town of Kitshanga, Bukoma groupement, which the article places in Rutshuru territory.

Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on Monday 28 April by an anonymous local human rights organisation, PARECO-FF Wazalendo fighters led by the militia chief Kigingi Jean de Dieu were accused of abuses against civilians in Katoyi sector, Masisi territory, including setting up a parallel fiscal and judicial administration and levying illegal taxes, with the organisation's remarks said to be corroborated by local administrative sources.

Radio Okapi reported that, according to the same anonymous local human rights organisation and administrative sources, the Katoyi sector office was reportedly vandalised and looted at the beginning of April by Kigingi's militiamen.

place: Ufamandu 1er (Bahunde chiefdom) and Nyamaboko 1er groupement, Osso-Banyungu sector, Masisi
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, in a memorandum addressed on Friday 17 October to the military and civil authorities of North Kivu, notables of the Bahunde chiefdom and Osso-Banyungu sector in Masisi territory accused three Wazalendo factions, the UPDC of Noah Maachano and PARECO-FF factions commanded by Kigingi Jean de Dieu and Mutayomba Jam's, of abuses against civilians, listing disrespect for customary authority, illegal taxes on goods and illegal exploitation of some mining sites.

place: Kalungu and Kinyana, Bashali Mokoto groupement, Masisi
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that men of Corneille Nangaa and Sultani Makenga (AFC/M23) attacked from the morning the positions of the Wazalendo of the ANCDH at Kalungu, after reinforcing their troops in men and equipment during the past week; the article places the fighting on the Tuesday and is dated Wednesday 9 July.
Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 rebels temporarily dislodged Nyatura fighters from Bupfuhi, a locality that was said to have been burned.

place: Kinyana, Nyabikeri, Rwankeri, Bibwe; Bashali Mokoto, Masisi
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local notables, that between 5 a.m. and 8 a.m. AFC-M23 fought the Wazalendo of the ANCDH of Jean-Marie Bonane on the hills overlooking the villages concerned, and that residents of Kinyana, Nyabikeri, Rwankeri and Bibwe were seen with their luggage moving towards Bulende, Kasopo and Lukweti.
Radio Okapi reported that the day before, attacks by Wazalendo on the town of Nyabiondo in Masisi caused the death of a child and injured four other people.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that hundreds of displaced families who had fled recent fighting between AFC-M23 and Wazalendo groups were living in alarming conditions at Mweso, in schools and churches, without humanitarian assistance.
Radio Okapi reported that in a communiqué made public on Monday the AFC-M23 accused the Congolese army of using heavy artillery and drones against its positions from 3 a.m. until late in the evening.

place: Kibati, Mikumbi, Miba; Luberike groupement, Walikale
statement: Radio Okapi reported that other sources indicated that, after the fighting at Kibati, the Wazalendo reportedly withdrew to Mikumbi and Miba, 3 km further west, leaving the area in the hands of the AFC/M23 rebels.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the shooting at Kibati had stopped after a day of fighting reported on Thursday in the area, and that the FARDC and wazalendo maintained their presence in the centre of Kibati while the AFC/M23 rebels controlled the hills overlooking the town.

place: Kaleta and Bitoyi, Ufamandu groupements, Masisi
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing civilian and military sources, that on the morning of Monday 28 September two positions held by wazalendo fighters at Kaleta and Bitoyi, in the Ufamandu groupements of Masisi territory, were targeted at about 7 a.m. by air strikes attributed to the AFC/M23 rebels.

Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that at Burungu, in the Bashali chiefdom, at least eight civilians were reportedly killed and six others wounded on Saturday evening, a toll that could not be independently confirmed at the time of publication.

Journal de Kinshasa reported, citing local and military sources, that for the first time since the start of fighting in the area the town of Pinga in Walikale territory was targeted on Monday 28 September 2026 by an attack attributed to the AFC/M23, drones targeting FARDC positions and causing panic and a temporary suspension of activities in the town.

place: Mindjendje area: Tchad, Kahongoboka, Kukibingu, Bubolwa, Luola; Walikale
statement: Journal de Kinshasa reported that the attack on Pinga came only 24 hours after the FARDC, supported by wazalendo, retook several positions around Mindjendje, notably Tchad, Kahongoboka, Kukibingu, Bubolwa and Luola.

place: Rushihe hill, Katobo, Banamulindwa locality, Kisimba groupement, Walikale
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting began on Saturday 24 October when the army and wazalendo attacked the positions of the FRN rebels on the Rushihe hill overlooking Katobo (Banamulindwa, Kisimba groupement, Walikale), and that the government coalition dislodged the rebels and took control of the position.

Actualite.cd reported that after the fighting at Rushihe a precarious calm was observed on Monday 26 October at Katobo, and that gunfire from heavy and light weapons caused displacement, with several Katobo inhabitants fleeing to Ihula and others taking refuge in the forest.

Actualite.cd reported that a new landslide on Tuesday 3 March 2026 at the Kasasa mining site in the Rubaya mining zone (Masisi) reportedly cost the lives of more than a hundred people, mostly artisanal diggers, and said it came about a month after a collapse on 28 January 2026 at the same site that had killed more than 400 people, not counting the missing.
Actualite.cd reported that the Rubaya mining zone, rich in coltan, cassiterite, gold and tourmaline, remained under the control of the M23 rebels.

KT Press (Rwanda) reported that Katoyi (Gatoyi) has changed hands repeatedly since late 2025: AFC-M23 captured it in November 2025, FARDC and PARECO-Wazalendo forces retook it in December, and further fighting returned control to AFC-M23 around February and March 2026.

KT Press (Rwanda) reported that by 24-25 August 2026 the AFC-M23-appointed administrator of Masisi had visited Remeka, taken part in community work and launched maintenance of the Ngungu-Remeka road, and had urged remaining Wazalendo fighters to join AFC-M23.

Kivu Morning Post, relaying MSF, reported that MSF had documented many cases of sexual violence against women, girls and children in eastern DRC since early January 2025, and had collected testimonies in Goma, Sake, Rutshuru and Masisi, in which victims said they were forced at gunpoint.
Amnesty International reported that one interviewee said he could hear the screams of detainees being tortured inside the shipping containers that M23 uses as detention cells near the Rubaya mine.

place: Rubaya (North Kivu) and Lomera (South Kivu) mining sites
statement: Amnesty International reported that seven miners recounted how M23 detained miners and threatened to send them to M23 military training centres if they failed to pay ransoms for their release.
Amnesty International reported that, in Rubaya, miners said Rwandans play a dual role as civilian miners or mineshaft managers but also take part in hostilities when needed alongside M23 fighters.

place: Makobola, Bangwi, Swima (Fizi/Uvira territories), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting broke out on Sunday after an attack on AFC/M23 rebels in the village of Bangwi, where intense clashes lasted all day, causing mass displacement of the population towards Swima and Mboko.

place: Makobola, Lake Tanganyika, Fizi/Uvira territories, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the AFC/M23 had deployed a marine unit on Lake Tanganyika that took part in the fighting at Makobola and its surroundings.
Actualite.cd reported that, despite FARDC reinforcements sent to the wazalendo from Kalemie, the town of Mboko, located 55 km north of Baraka, remained under the control of AFC-M23 fighters.

Kivutimes reported that violent fighting had opposed AFC-M23 rebels and the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo, around Makobola since 'samedi 21 décembre 2025', and that, per the outlet, military authorities had not yet communicated an official casualty toll while families fled explosive devices.
Kivutimes reported that the town of Mboko, about 55 km north of Baraka, remained under the direct threat of AFC-M23 fighters, who were maintaining pressure on that axis.

place: Minembwe; Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma, Kwasabuni (high plateaux), Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that violent fighting broke out on Friday around Minembwe between Twirwaneho fighters allied to AFC-M23 and Wazalendo militiamen integrated into the Congolese army, and that the Wazalendo Biloze Bishambuke (FABB) of General Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito said they were continuing to defend their positions.

place: Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma, Kwasabuni (south of Minembwe), Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: A Wazalendo spokesperson told Kivu Morning Post that the AFC Twirwaneho M23 attacked Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma and Kwasabuni, on the high plateaux south of Minembwe, on the morning of Friday 21 November 2025, in violation of the Doha framework agreement.

place: Kipupu (Mwenga territory); Makobola 2 (Fizi territory), South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, over the weekend, AFC/M23 rebels occupied the localities of Kipupu (Mwenga territory) and Makobola 2 (Fizi territory), a few days after the taking of Uvira.

Radio Okapi reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, called on the international community, in particular the United States, to compel Rwanda to withdraw the troops that, he said, support the AFC-M23 rebels, and said 'all batteries are being put in motion' to reconquer the territories already in rebel hands.
BBC News Gahuza reported, citing residents, that a Congolese government war plane carried out strikes on Monday in the Minembwe area, controlled by Twirwaneho fighters in South Kivu.

place: Kiziba hill, Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Twirwaneho group said these air strikes also targeted Kiziba hill, on which the main hospital in Minembwe stands, as well as the University Eben-Ezer Minembwe (UEMI), two secondary schools and the Methodist church.

BBC News Gahuza reported that some government supporters, heard in DR Congo media, said the strikes aimed only at destroying the Minembwe airstrip and a Twirwaneho weapons store, and that the BBC could not reach the government army side to respond to accusations of targeting civilians.

place: Hauts-Plateaux above Baraka, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: MSF said that, in the Hauts-Plateaux on the heights above Baraka, 57 000 people remained isolated, surrounded by armed groups, and that humanitarian access was impossible for the moment; MSF's medical project lead in Fizi said people were afraid to pass armed groups' checkpoints to reach its medical care.

place: Bukavu to Baraka route, South Kivu
statement: MSF said that, because it cannot move directly from M23-controlled areas to government-controlled ones, supplies cannot be transported directly from Bukavu to Baraka and must take a long detour via Rwanda, Tanzania and Burundi.

A humanitarian early-warning alert listing HEKS-EPER as its principal source, with the status 'preliminary diagnosis / awaiting assessment', reported that about 65 000 people (in 9.311 households) had arrived in the town of Baraka since 11 December 2025.

The same alert reported that the threat of a possible M23 advance towards Baraka caused a large part of this population, together with the host population, to flee towards Burundi, Tanzania and the Ubwari peninsula.

place: Rusanguku and Bilalombili, South Kivu (the article places them in Fizi territory in its lede and in the Mwenga high plateaux in the civil-society quote)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that fighting had opposed, since Friday 12 December 2025, the FARDC and the Burundian army to Twirwaneho fighters allied to AFC-M23 at Rusanguku and Bilalombili, which its lede places in Fizi territory; Fizi territory civil society said the FARDC 'Sokoi' and the Burundian army were shelling these villages to find a route for Burundian soldiers to cross Mutambala to reach Baraka with the aim of returning to Burundi, and its quoted statement places the villages in the high plateaux of another territory.

place: Mboko port, Bijombo, Rugezi, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, on a Thursday morning, several Burundian soldiers stationed at the Mboko port (Tanganyika sector) told residents they were heading to Bijombo to fight the rebels, and that, according to local sources, this new mobilisation followed bloody clashes the previous week at Kahololo (Uvira territory) and more recently at Rugezi (Fizi territory).
SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundian operations towards Bijombo and Minembwe came in the wake of a strategic meeting held on 14 May in Uvira between the Congolese and Burundian general staffs.

place: Minembwe, Mikalati, Kipupu, Point Zero (Fizi); Kitoga, Muhuzi, Itombwe forest, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dateline Bukavu, 16 October 2025) that, despite the signing of a ceasefire agreement on 14 October in Doha between the Congolese government and the M23, Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB) units continued a massive deployment in Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories; that for several days military convoys from Burundi had been reported at Kitoga, Muhuzi and the Itombwe forest; and that significant reinforcements had also been observed at Minembwe, Mikalati, Kipupu and Point Zero in Fizi territory.

SOS Médias Burundi quoted a resident contacted from Fizi as saying that 'Burundian soldiers want to attack Twirwaneho in Mikenge' and that sources among the Wazalendo told them an attack was imminent.

place: Fizi territory (Balala Nord grouping), South Kivu
statement: The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's August 2025 note on Fizi territory listed local armed groups, including Twirwaneho, led by deserter colonel Charles Sematama after the death of Michel Rukundo alias Makanika and active in Balala Nord grouping.

The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's note said that the most important Maï-Maï factions in Fizi territory were those of Yakutumba, Ebuela (also known as Kibukila) and Biloze Bishambuke, which now collaborate with the FARDC under the name Wazalendo against the AFC/M23 and its allies, and that a coordination of Wazalendo against the AFC/M23 in Fizi territory was set up under the direction of Willam Yakutumba.

The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's August 2025 note on Fizi territory said, citing an APADEC humanitarian note of 19 March 2025, that since Minembwe and its surroundings came under the control of Twirwaneho elements allied to AFC/M23, inhabitants no longer had access to essential goods coming from Uvira via Baraka and Fizi centre, and that Wazalendo groups allied to the FARDC on that route had banned itinerant traders from going to Minembwe, raising food prices.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (countrywide figures; not Kivu-only)
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office documented 1,359 human rights violations and abuses nationwide in the reporting period, and that AFC/M23 remained the largest single perpetrator, responsible for 489 human rights abuses affecting 1,279 victims (752 men, 391 women, 125 children and 11 persons), followed by Wazalendo groups (143 abuses), ADF (98), FDLR (44) and CODECO (23).

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (countrywide; the report stresses the Kivus)
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office documented 40 cases of conflict-related sexual violence countrywide against 46 women and 23 girls, 57 instances of which were attributed to armed groups.

The UN Secretary-General reported that on 17 June, in Masisi territory, at least 60 bodies were reportedly discovered following AFC/M23 operations against FDLR and Nyatura elements, as counter-FDLR operations continued to systematically target civilians, resulting in deaths and displacement.

place: Rutshuru, Masisi, Nyiragongo and Walikale territories, North Kivu
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that FDLR abuses of the civilian population remained concentrated in Rutshuru territory but also occurred in Masisi, Nyiragongo and Walikale, and that since 20 June the group had allegedly been involved in at least 44 human rights abuses and protection incidents affecting 89 victims, including 15 victims of summary executions.

place: Point Zero / Minembwe area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that in South Kivu, Twirwaneho and M23 pushed back FARDC outside of the general Minembwe area and regained control of Point Zero on 4 July, effectively restoring the frontline to its late January 2026 configuration.

place: Walikale and Masisi territories, North Kivu
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that from mid-August 2026 intensified clashes between M23 and various factions of armed self-defence forces in Walikale and Masisi territories resulted in widespread violence and drove the displacement of 70,800 civilians, according to humanitarian reports.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (transfer location not stated)
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that on 7 August the DRC Government facilitated, through the International Committee of the Red Cross, the release and transfer to AFC/M23 of 15 detainees under the prisoner exchange protocol of the Doha Framework, and that AFC/M23 subsequently claimed that only 9 of the 15 individuals appeared on the list of 768 prisoners it had submitted.

The UN Secretary-General reported that, with MONUSCO support, the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus conducted its first ceasefire monitoring and verification mission in Minembwe, South Kivu, on 24 and 25 August 2026 and a second mission to Masisi, North Kivu, from 10 to 12 September.

The UN Secretary-General reported that MONUSCO verified 366 grave violations affecting 276 children (80 girls and 196 boys), including 142 cases of recruitment and use, 111 of abduction and 69 of killing and maiming, with 269 cases in North Kivu and 97 in Ituri, and that MONUSCO with UNICEF secured the release of 47 children detained by FARDC, including 11 girls, associated with two Wazalendo-affiliated armed groups.

The UN Secretary-General reported that MONUSCO documented 518 protection incidents across North Kivu and Ituri resulting in 470 civilian deaths, including 61 women and 56 children, with ADF and M23 the two largest perpetrators, with 214 and 170 fatalities respectively.

place: Mines near Rubaya (North Kivu) and Lomera mine (Kabare territory, South Kivu)
statement: Amnesty International reported (21 September 2026) that it documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners at the Rubaya (North Kivu) and Lomera (South Kivu) mines, with witnesses and family members reporting that 10 were beaten to death, two were shot dead and six abducted miners were later found dead; it attributed the abuses to Rwanda-backed M23 fighters. The press release does not say when the killings took place. Neither M23 nor Rwandan government officials responded to Amnesty International's request for comment.

place: Near the Rubaya mine, North Kivu
statement: Amnesty International reported that M23 uses three shipping containers as detention cells near the Rubaya mine, and that more than 20 miners who worked at the Rubaya mine were kept in an underground cell known as a ndake and beaten three times a day by M23 fighters.

Amnesty International reported, in a briefing published on 21 September 2026 that gives no date for the detention, that in Lomera (Kabare territory, South Kivu) M23 detained four men, accused them of communicating with authorities in Kinshasa and suspected them of having links to the Wazalendo armed group.

Amnesty International reported that testimonies indicate Rwandans are present at Rubaya and Lomera and that, in both places, security guards, some of whom identified as Rwandan and spoke Kinyarwanda, collaborate with M23 and have beaten and ill-treated miners.

place: Walungu and Shabunda territories, South Kivu
statement: IPIS reported, citing an interviewee, that women in Wazalendo-controlled zones such as Walungu and Shabunda territories frequently report being extorted at arbitrary checkpoints, accompanied by invasive and intimate body searches typically justified by suspicion of mineral smuggling.

IPIS reported that a source mentioned that ten women were allegedly executed in Shabunda territory for resisting Wazalendo demands for forced payments at mining-site entrances, 'jeton corporel' (body tokens) and invasive searches.

place: Wazalendo-controlled mining areas in the Kivus (not specified further)
statement: IPIS reported that, according to reports, no post-rape kits are available in the mining areas under Wazalendo control and women attempting to engage local organisations risk being targeted; that its partners indicated local women's organisations have been prevented from operating in certain Wazalendo-controlled zones; and that, in the affected areas, where according to its sources the justice system is effectively absent, some health facilities exist but are severely under-resourced and many international and national NGOs have suspended their operations due to insecurity.

place: Bahunde and Osso chiefdoms, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: IPIS reported that by late February 2026 the pro-government Wazalendo coalition launched a large-scale offensive on AFC/M23 positions in the Osso and Bahunde chiefdoms south of Masisi town, and, supported by FARDC air strikes, temporarily recaptured several villages including Chugi, Kibabi and Kaniro, which AFC/M23 quickly regained while retaining control of the coltan mines around Rubaya.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (countrywide; North Kivu and South Kivu nearly 80 per cent of victims)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), in its 2025 report, documented 887 cases of sexual violence affecting 1,534 victims, including 854 women and 672 girls, in 2025, and that North Kivu and South Kivu account for nearly 80 per cent of victims recorded.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo; North Kivu and South Kivu named as epicentres
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report on November 2025 recorded 91 victims of conflict-related sexual violence in one month, mostly women and girls, an increase of 28 per cent in thirty days, with North Kivu and South Kivu remaining the epicentres.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (80 per cent of violations in Ituri and the two Kivus)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH monthly report for May 2026 counted 59 victims of conflict-related sexual violence, mostly women and girls, and that state actors, mainly FARDC soldiers, were designated as first responsible for nearly half of these abuses, ahead of armed groups.

UN News (Kiswahili), relaying Radio Okapi, reported that the DRC government announced a phased plan to restore State authority in Uvira after the departure of AFC/M23 fighters, and that a government spokesperson called the M23 departure a "short-lived event" and said the only acceptable outcome was full, effective and unconditional withdrawal of AFC/M23 and the Rwandan army from the whole DRC.

SOS Médias Burundi reported from Uvira, citing several consistent accounts, that elements believed to be affiliated with the Wazalendo militia, supported by some civilians, ransacked homes, businesses and places of worship belonging to the Banyamulenge community in various neighbourhoods of the city; it named among the victims a resident, Sifa, whose two-story house was reportedly completely looted before being destroyed.

place: Kilomoni and Mulongwe, Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dateline Bukavu) that the burial in Uvira of Colonel Patrick Gisore, of the Banyamulenge community, and his wife Yvonne Nyamahoro, who died in a military plane crash in Kisangani, turned violent on a Monday; according to several witnesses armed elements claiming to be Wazalendo interrupted the ceremony and intercepted the funeral procession in Kilomoni, while other members of the Banyamulenge community were arrested in Mulongwe or forcibly locked inside a church; local sources said some assailants fired live ammunition at people outside the church and looting took place. Human Rights Watch separately said that since August 25 Wazalendo fighters had prevented the funeral of an army colonel from the Banyamulenge community and his wife for several days and robbed people there.
sources: SOS Médias Burundi; Human Rights Watch

place: Uvira city and road to the Kavimvira/Gatumba border, South Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch reported that on 2 September 2025 Wazalendo militias set up roadblocks in Uvira, particularly along a major route to the Burundi border, and that for several days Wazalendo fighters intermittently prevented people from fleeing across the border, witnesses said; a border officer told HRW that the Wazalendo 'did not want to see people fleeing to Burundi'.

Human Rights Watch reported that on 6 September 2025 the Congolese army spokesperson, Gen. Sylvain Ekenge, said at a news conference: 'We don't control the Wazalendo, the Wazalendo are not part of the armed forces', and that it was not the army's job to 'manage' them.

place: Burundi (refugees from the Uvira area; place within Burundi not stated)
statement: Human Rights Watch reported that in Burundi on 8 September 2025 police and ruling-party youths detained hundreds of Congolese refugees and asylum seekers, according to several witnesses and media reports, giving them the 'choice' of going to an official camp or returning to Congo, which about 80 people did.
Human Rights Watch reported that on 5 September 2025 Wazalendo fighters fired small arms and artillery within Uvira, killing an 8-year-old boy when a shell struck his house.

place: Gatumba-Kavimvira border; Uvira city, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dateline Bujumbura, 23 January 2026) that a delegation of South Kivu provincial authorities led by the mayor of Uvira returned to Uvira from Bujumbura via the Gatumba–Kavimvira border crossing on a day the outlet gives as 'jeudi 23 janvier 2026'; that the Burundi-Congo border at Gatumba had remained closed since 10 December 2025, after the fall of Uvira to the M23; and that since the capture of Bukavu almost a year earlier a large part of the province's Congolese officials had resided in Bujumbura.

SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition, dateline Bujumbura) reported that at a session of Burundi's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Bujumbura, Foreign Minister Édouard Bizimana announced that the Burundi-Congo border would remain closed until further notice, insisted that the M23 was lying when it claimed to be withdrawing from the city of Uvira, and said this apparent withdrawal hid a strategy of regrouping its fighters.

SOS Médias Burundi (in Swahili) reported that the South Kivu governor, Jean-Jacques Purusi, had assured Uvira residents after crossing the border that the Burundi-Congo border would reopen within two to three days, by 30 January 2026 at the latest.

place: Gatumba-Kavimvira border and Bujumbura province, Burundi
statement: Iwacu reported that, according to UNHCR, more than 84,000 people from South Kivu had crossed into Burundi since the beginning of December 2025, bringing the total of Congolese refugees and asylum seekers in Burundi to more than 200,000, and that UNHCR declared a level 2 emergency for Burundi needing USD 33 million.

place: Bujumbura, Burundi (response to refugees from Uvira)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition, dateline Bujumbura) reported that at a meeting in Bujumbura the UNHCR representative in Burundi, Brigitte Mkanga-Eno, expressed concern at the humanitarian funding shortfall: of the USD 33 million needed for emergency needs only USD 6 million had been raised so far, an amount she said was insufficient, especially for health services, sanitation and access to clean water.

place: Uvira city (including Kalundu port), South Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch said it documented widespread looting, following the M23's withdrawal from Uvira, of homes, shops, churches and public buildings, including those belonging to the Banyamulenge, through witness accounts and verified photographs and videos, and that it geolocated videos showing unidentified people in civilian clothes looting the city courthouse, a Methodist church used by the Banyamulenge community, a restaurant, a government office building and the city's port of Kalundu.

Human Rights Watch reported that on 17 January 2026 Banyamulenge community leaders in Uvira held a meeting and said they had received instructions from the M23 that Banyamulenge people should leave with them or face reprisal attacks by Wazalendo groups, according to two community leaders and a community member.

Human Rights Watch reported that Congolese Defence Minister Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita told it in a meeting on 20 January 2026 that 'the Banyamulenge should not be forcibly displaced or deported, and should feel free to return to Uvira if they wish to do so'.

place: Uvira city and Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
statement: Human Rights Watch said it had reviewed credible information that Wazalendo militias prevented people from fleeing towards the Hauts Plateaux (highlands of Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories) after the M23 withdrawal from Uvira, and noted that these concerns were heightened by the continued closure of the border with Burundi.

place: Rugombo, Cibitoke (Burundi); Katogota, Lubarika, Luvungi, Kamanyola (Uvira/Walungu border area, South Kivu)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dateline Cibitoke) that on Friday morning, around 10:00, a 12-year-old boy was injured in Rugombo, Burundi, by shrapnel, and that residents of the Congolese towns of Katogota, Lubarika, Luvungi and Kamanyola, across the border from Burundi, were also living under fire, with several shells having killed civilians in their homes in recent days.

Actualite.cd reported that DRC Human Rights Minister Samuel Mbemba presented an official report on 7 April according to which more than 14 400 women were victims of rape during the period of occupation, sexual violence the report says was recorded in different localities of Uvira and its surroundings.

place: Uvira and surrounding health zones (Uvira, Fizi, Baraka)
statement: In a press release on the health crisis in the Uvira region, the WHO reported that forty health structures had been attacked or pillaged, causing the loss of equipment, the destruction of medicine stocks and the temporary flight of health workers, and that the general referral hospitals of Uvira, Fizi and Baraka were operating in permanent overload.

Actualite.cd, summarising an OCHA overview of the security and humanitarian situation in South Kivu for December 2025, reported that health sources said more than eight health structures had been pillaged in the Ruzizi and Uvira health zones, drastically or even totally reducing their operational capacity.

place: South of Uvira city, Fizi highlands; Uvira to Fizi route
statement: The ICRC reported that its teams and those of the Red Cross of the DRC had received many evacuation requests for dozens of wounded people stuck notably south of Uvira city and on the highlands of Fizi territory; François Moreillon, head of the ICRC delegation in the DRC, said its emergency surgical team that came to Fizi from Uvira had to travel six days by road when the trip could have taken three hours on the lake, and that the lack of access forced this detour.

place: Ruzizi health zone (Ndunda, Kigurwe, Rusabagi health areas)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that four people had died of cholera out of 182 cases recorded in recent days in the Ruzizi health zone, Uvira territory, that the zone's head nurse (infirmier titulaire) acknowledged the teams were limited in supplies to fight the disease, and that the resurgence came six months after the departure of Médecins sans frontières (MSF), which had announced the end of its mission in Uvira.

place: Sangé health zone (Ndunda, Nazareno, Sangé-État, CEPAC)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that at least 240 cholera cases were recorded in the Sangé health zone, Uvira territory, during the first week of January 2026, and that according to the zone's epidemiological bulletin the Ndunda health area was the epicentre of the outbreak.

Actualite.cd reported that Javid Abdelmoneim, international president of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), speaking before the UN Security Council on 12 December 2025, denounced the trivialisation of sexual violence by state and non-state armed groups in the armed conflicts in eastern DRC; the outlet identified these as AFC/M23, FDLR, ADF, Wazalendo and some FARDC elements.

The UN Secretary-General's annual report on conflict-related sexual violence (covering January to December 2025) stated that reports of sexual violence also surfaced after the capture of Uvira by M23 elements in December 2025; the passage does not say who the alleged perpetrators were. It also stated that mass prison escapes in Goma, Bukavu, Kabare, Uvira and Kalemie enabled perpetrators convicted of sexual violence crimes, including armed group commanders, to flee.

BBC Afrique reported that the Congolese government, in a communiqué of 22 January 2026, rejected the Human Rights Watch statement of 20 January 2026 on Uvira as a "partial or truncated" reading of events, and held the RDF/M23 primarily responsible for endangering civilians, notably through its illegal armed occupation of the city.

Actualite.cd reported that in a clarification by Lawrence Kanyuka, head of communication and spokesperson of AFC/M23, the movement said the latest Human Rights Watch report on Uvira raised serious questions about its credibility, impartiality and objectivity and was strongly influenced by the political narrative of the Kinshasa regime, and attributed the abuses committed in Uvira to a government coalition of FARDC, FNDB, FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries.

The BBC reported that Human Rights Watch said it wrote in April to both the Rwandan government and M23 leaders for a response to the allegations in its Uvira report and that neither replied; the BBC noted that Rwanda has consistently denied supporting the M23 or that its own soldiers have been deployed to eastern DR Congo.

Radio Okapi reported that the city of Uvira woke calm on Monday 19 January 2026 after a day marked the day before by pillaging and sporadic gunfire, and that the pillaging had targeted State services, economic operators and many individuals.

place: Kabunambo; Luvungi; Bwegera; Sange; Kiliba ONDS (Ruzizi plain)
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 troops, withdrawn from Uvira 'lundi' as the article puts it, had set up their headquarters at Kabunambo, less than a kilometre north of the city centre, and that residents reported large numbers of AFC-M23 troops in several localities of the Ruzizi plain, notably Luvungi, Bwegera, Sange and Kiliba ONDS.

The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), in its analysis for November 2025, stated that the Wazalendo also committed abuses in the context of internal clashes and interference in the administration of justice, notably in the city of Uvira.

The outlet reported that at least 4 civilians were killed on Monday 30 June 2025 in clashes between Wazalendo and M23 rebels at Muku, Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, South Kivu; it reported that residents said M23 rebels launched the assault on Wazalendo positions and that the toll among the belligerents was not yet known.

7sur7.cd reported that, the day before the clashes it was reporting at Muku (Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory), a hospital centre ('centre hospitalier') was vandalised and looted by armed men in the same village.

Beto.cd reported that, after two bombs fell on the Mwalu hotel in Fizi-Centre, South Kivu, in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 19 August 2026 around one o'clock in the morning, Colonel Michel Apoko Bangala, commander of the Sukola 2 South Kivu operational sector, reported two seriously wounded and major material damage, attributed the strike to Rwandan forces and spoke of TB2-type devices.

Radio Okapi reported that residents of Katana looted, on Monday 11 August, property belonging to senator Bahati Lukwebo at the SMAL site, a building under construction in the centre of Katana (South Kivu); it said the exact reasons for the act, in an area under M23 rebel control, remained unclear according to local sources.

Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to local civil society, at least two civilians were killed on Sunday 7 June 2026 in a drone attack by the Congolese army on the village of Ilundu, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, and that the victims were taken to Minembwe hospital; it reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the 7 June 2026 bombings by the 'coalition FARDC-FDNB' on Ilundu/Basita killed several civilians and wounded many, mainly women and children.

place: Bidegu, Gakenke and Mikenge, Hauts-Plateaux (Minembwe area), Fizi/Mwenga territories
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a communiqué the AFC/M23 accused the Congolese army and its allies of intensifying air strikes on civilian zones, saying that from 22 June 2026 at 23:30 to 23 June at 12:00 they struck Bidegu and surroundings with kamikaze drones and KT-6, and that, according to spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, on 23 June between 06:00 and 11:00 they intensified strikes on Gakenke and Mikenge.

place: Kongo-Central (former post); statement issued by the FRN, Goma dateline
statement: Chimp Reports reported that FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka confirmed on Tuesday, October 27, that Kamanzi, formerly operations commander of the FARDC 12th Military Region in Kongo Central, had joined the FRN's military wing; the outlet reported that Kinshasa had not publicly confirmed the reported defection.
CNN reported that DRC communications minister Patrick Muyaya confirmed the rape of the 165 women, telling CNN on Wednesday that "the government condemns with the greatest energy this barbaric crime."

DW, citing dpa, reported that local police investigator Robert Kayembe told Germany's DPA news agency that over 160 women in Munzenze prison were raped and a number yet to be established were burned when their wing was set on fire.

place: Goma and Bukavu (statement made at UN Security Council, New York)
statement: At a UN Security Council emergency meeting, DRC Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner said that in Goma more than 4,500 wounded people had rushed to overflowing hospitals and that 500 charred corpses were found in the Muzenze prison after mass executions, and said of Bukavu that the same scenario was playing out, including 'hospitals destroyed'.

The New Times (Kigali), a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that Bisimwa said in an earlier, undated post that the accusations against AFC-M23 regarding human rights violations are false and that the mass rapes of female prisoners occurred before AFC-M23's presence in Goma.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu (HRW report subject; places not named in the excerpt)
statement: The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda published a response to a Human Rights Watch report, stating that Rwanda rejects HRW's allegations of RDF involvement in forced recruitment, detention, torture, executions, forced labor, or child recruitment, and rejects HRW's attempt to collapse M23 and RDF into one actor.

Actualite.cd reported that, hours after EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib described the humanitarian situation as "catastrophique", AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa told the press in Goma on 20 February that the situation is catastrophic "non plus dans la zone contrôlée par l'AFC/M23", and asserted that humanitarian access in territories under his movement's control would be "garanti".

BBC Swahili reported that a Human Rights Watch investigation found that executions and rape were among the atrocities committed by M23 and Rwandan soldiers during their invasion of Uvira, that HRW said it wrote in April to the Rwandan government and M23 leaders for a response to the allegations and no one responded, and that M23 and the Rwandan government had not yet responded to BBC's request for comment.

place: CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that on the evening of Thursday 13 March CBCA Ndosho hospital in Goma was again the target of an incursion by AFC/M23 rebels, that according to witnesses the rebels fired shots inside the hospital, apparently while pursuing a young man presumed to be a thief, and that a humanitarian source reported that a bullet hit a patient in the thigh.

The SECO consolidated annex to the Swiss Congo sanctions ordinance lists Charles Sematama, title Colonel, born 1975 at Kalunyo Village, Kamombo Localities, South Kivu, address Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu, with the justification 'Commander and military leader of Twirwaneho (CDe.011)'; the Government of Jersey notice said the Committee approved the addition on 14 July 2026.
sources: Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs; Government of Jersey

statement: The SECO consolidated annex lists Twirwaneho, address Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu, stating that it 'has been involved in atrocities in the South-Kivu province of the DRC, including the killing of civilians, recruiting children, and activities that threaten the peace and security of the people of the DRC'.
sources: Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs

statement: The SECO consolidated annex (entries for him and for the AFC) lists Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo as 'the leader of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) (CDe.010), a politico-military movement allied with the United Nations-sanctioned March 23 Movement/Congolese Revolutionary Army (M23/ARC)', and lists the Alliance Fleuve Congo as an entity with address 'eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo' and the justification 'Established in 2023.'
sources: Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs; Government of Jersey

statement: The SECO consolidated annex lists Gustave Kubwayo, alias Sirkoof, as 'one of the main' FDLR-FOCA commanders and 'the new commander of the Commando de Recherche et d'Action en Profondeur (CRAP)', alleged to be 'involved in planning, promulgating and supporting the armed group's activities, such as targeting civilians, kidnapping for ransom and illegally exploiting natural resources'.
sources: Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs; Government of Jersey

statement: The SECO consolidated annex lists Sebastien Uwimbabazi, address Rutshuru, North Kivu, with the designation 'Brigadier General and Leader of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) (CDe.005)'.
sources: Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs; Government of Jersey

statement: The SECO consolidated annex lists Muhammed Lumisa (address 'Congo DR', nationality 'Uganda') as one of the commanders of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), alleged to be 'involved in planning, promulgating, and supporting the militia's activities' and to oversee the group's external logistics; the entry's designation describes him as 'Commander, doctor and head of external logistics' of the ADF.
sources: Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs; Government of Jersey

statement: The SECO consolidated annex lists John Imani Nzenze with the designation 'Colonel' and 'M23 intelligence chief', alleged to be 'involved in planning, promulgating and supporting the armed group's activities'.
sources: Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs; Government of Jersey

statement: Al Jazeera reported that Rwanda said international sanctions would reduce the likelihood of peace with M23, after the UK said it would pause some bilateral aid and impose other diplomatic measures on Kigali; Rwanda's Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the measures 'regrettable' and said the UK 'has now clearly chosen a side'.

place: Bukavu (hearing at the Cercle sportif de la Botte), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Times reported that on 14 February 2025 the Bukavu garrison military tribunal, presided by magistrate major Amsini Lazare, sentenced 212 of 282 prosecuted FARDC soldiers to death for offences including murder, rape, attempted murder, dissipation of munitions and flight before the enemy, and acquitted 70.

place: Uvira (trial at Uvira central prison); positions at Malimba and Masangu, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on Friday 2 October the Uvira garrison military tribunal sentenced to death twenty-seven soldiers of the Republican Guard for cowardice before the enemy, after a flagrancy trial of 112 soldiers of the FARDC 21st battalion 'Simba' accused of abandoning or poorly securing positions on the heights of Malimba and Masangu on the night of 22 to 23 August 2026; fifty-four others received five years, ten received six months, and twenty-one defendants, including five women, were acquitted.

place: Masisi, Walikale, Kalehe, Walungu, Mwenga, Uvira and Fizi territories
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that the use of drone warfare and indiscriminate strikes by State and non-State actors had increased notably in Masisi, Walikale, Kalehe, Walungu, Mwenga, Uvira and Fizi territories of North and South Kivu, significantly escalating the risk to civilians.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (nationwide count; 86 per cent of all violations in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu)
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that, among State agents, FARDC had committed most of the human rights violations registered (198 violations) and that Congolese National Police agents had been responsible for 107 human rights violations, in the Joint Human Rights Office's nationwide count for the reporting period.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (location not specified)
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that MONUSCO, in close collaboration with UNICEF, secured the release of 47 children detained by FARDC, including 11 girls, associated with two Wazalendo-affiliated armed groups.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (location not specified)
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that the security incidents affecting United Nations personnel and premises in the reporting period included the unlawful detention of United Nations personnel by AFC/M23.

The UN Secretary-General reported that the rapid expansion of the Ebola outbreak significantly increased humanitarian needs, with a gradually increasing proportion of cases in North Kivu, and that two factors, the spread of Ebola across seven provinces and certain continued restrictions on MONUSCO's freedom of movement in areas controlled by AFC/M23 (including prior notification and authorization requirements), intersect in North Kivu and limit access to vulnerable populations.

The UN Secretary-General reported that on 26 August MONUSCO transported by helicopter from Goma to Beni 16 civilians who had sought protection at its Goma facilities since January 2025, where they were received by Government authorities, and that the Mission continued to provide protection in Goma to 13 unarmed security actors.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo / Rwanda (statements)
statement: The UN Secretary-General reported that on 28 July the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo announced that a faction of FDLR elements had signed a protocol on disarmament, demobilization and cantonment through sensitization, and that the Government of Rwanda rejected the plan, arguing that the Washington Accords require the verifiable neutralization of FDLR and claiming it was a delaying tactic by the DRC Government.

place: Security Council, New York (statement); Ntoto; "Warungu" territory as printed
statement: Rwanda's representative told the Security Council that, according to 'information available', on 8 March 2026 an FARDC helicopter airlifted 12 tonnes of ammunition and food rations to Ntoto, which were subsequently distributed among FARDC, FDLR, Pareco and APCSS elements, and that as recently as 15 August 2026 'information available indicated' FARDC operating alongside CNRND, FLN, FDLR and an armed group the auto-generated transcript renders as "Wazalandonyatwa" in what it renders as "Warungu" territory.

place: South Kivu highlands (statement at Security Council, New York)
statement: Rwanda's representative told the Security Council that, according to 'information available in the public domain', since 2017 more than 650 villages had been destroyed or burned in the South Kivu highlands, more than 700,000 cattle looted and sold in public markets, and at least 147 schools and 57 health facilities destroyed.

The representative of the DRC told the Security Council that on the 20th September a TB2 drone strike attributed to the Rwandan Defense Forces targeted a Congolese position in Pinga, killing five people and seriously injuring eight others.

place: Security Council, New York (statement); areas under RDF/AFC/M23 occupation
statement: The representative of the DRC told the Security Council that the DRC was particularly concerned by consistent reports of the displacement and transplantation of Rwandan populations in Congolese localities emptied of their inhabitants, followed by repeated massacres which the speaker said were perpetrated by the RDF and the AFC/M23.

The representative of Burundi told the Security Council that Burundi called for the cessation of all support to armed groups and for the implementation of commitments undertaken to address security concerns in the region, in full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, and wished future Secretary-General reports to continue to provide a precise and balanced account of the contribution of regional actors to peace efforts, mediation, ceasefire verification and civilian protection.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (88% in the east)
statement: The head of MONUSCO told the Security Council that since his last briefing to the Council the UN Joint Human Rights Office had documented 1,537 human rights violations and abuses across the country, 88% of which occurred in the east, including conflict-related sexual violence perpetrated both by armed groups and by members of the defence and security forces, which affected 382 victims including 257 women and 122 girls.

The head of MONUSCO told the Security Council that, while Ituri remained the epicenter of the Ebola outbreak, the number of cases was also increasing in North Kivu, where insecurity continued to hamper response efforts.

place: Kanyola, Luntukulu, Kabare, Walungu, Kale, Bukavu, Goma (as listed by the speaker)
statement: The President of the Coordination Bureau of Civil Society in South Kivu told the Security Council that in areas of North and South Kivu controlled by AFC M23 a parallel administration illegally taxes and (as the auto-generated transcript prints it) 'exhorts' compatriots at gunpoint and commits targeted abuses, and said that what is happening in Kanyola, Luntukulu, Kabare, Walungu, Kale, Bukavu and Goma is methodical: 'assassinations, arson, collective punishment and death-trap detention centers where prisoners are denied family visits'.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (reporting covers North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema and Tanganyika)
statement: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on conflict-related sexual violence reported that in 2025 MONUSCO verified 1,534 cases of conflict-related sexual violence in the DRC, an 86 per cent increase from 2024, affecting 854 women, 672 girls, 4 men and 4 boys, with survivors as young as 1 year old.

place: eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu areas under M23, per report context)
statement: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on conflict-related sexual violence reported that documented cases implicating M23, including rape, gang rape and sexual slavery, rose from 152 in 2024 to 439 in 2025, that M23 elements perpetrated sexual violence against civilians perceived to be affiliated with the Armed Forces and Wazalendo-labelled armed groups, and that violations implicating M23 occurred in detention and during cordon-and-search operations, affecting women, girls, men and boys, as well as LGBT individuals.

The UN Secretary-General's annual report on conflict-related sexual violence reported that in North Kivu and South Kivu cases of sexual violence affecting 60 women and 17 girls were attributed to armed groups operating under the Wazalendo label, and that in South Kivu Twirwaneho elements were implicated in 64 cases, RED Tabara elements in 60 cases and the Forces nationales de libération in 15 cases.

place: South Kivu (looting during withdrawal from the frontline); other locations not specified
statement: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on conflict-related sexual violence reported that, of the cases documented in 2025 that were attributed to State actors, 285 implicated the Armed Forces (a 60 per cent increase from 2024) and 4 implicated other State actors; Armed Forces personnel were implicated in cases including rape in the context of looting during their withdrawal from the frontline in South Kivu; the Uganda Peoples’ Defence Forces were implicated in seven cases and the Burundi National Defence Force in two, and there were seven documented cases committed by the Congolese National Police in 2025.

place: Goma and Kavumu airport (Bukavu area); medical facilities in eastern DRC (not itemised)
statement: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on conflict-related sexual violence reported that targeted attacks and looting of medical facilities and prolonged closures of Goma and Kavumu airports caused critical supply shortages, including of post-rape kits.

The UN Secretary-General's annual report on conflict-related sexual violence reported that attacks on judicial and correctional facilities destroyed case files related to conflict-related sexual violence, and that mass prison escapes in Goma, Bukavu, Kabare, Uvira and Kalemie enabled perpetrators convicted of sexual violence crimes, including armed group commanders, to flee.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (country-wide figures; most violations in North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri per other UN sources, not this report)
statement: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on children and armed conflict reported that the killing (519) and maiming (399) of 918 children (661 boys, 257 girls) in the DRC in 2025 were attributed to M23 (404), CODECO (109), the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (100), Nyatura (66), unidentified perpetrators (69), Wazalendo (13), the Congolese National Police (14), among others, with most casualties occurring during military operations (766).

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (country-wide figures; most violations in North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri per other UN sources, not this report)
statement: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on children and armed conflict reported that sexual violence was perpetrated against 592 children (3 boys, 589 girls) in the DRC in 2025, attributed to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (147), M23 (124), CODECO (69), Nyatura (38), Mai-Mai Mazembe (25), Mai-Mai Yakotumba (23), unidentified perpetrators (46) and others, and that perpetrators from the Armed Forces (27), the National Intelligence Agency (2) and armed groups (1) were arrested or prosecuted.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (country-wide figures; most violations in North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri per other UN sources, not this report)
statement: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on children and armed conflict reported that attacks on 121 schools (81) and hospitals (40) in the DRC in 2025, including against protected persons (19), were attributed to M23 (45), the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (25), unidentified perpetrators (11), Twirwaneho (7), CODECO (6), ADF (3), Raia Mutomboki (3) and 11 other parties (21).

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (country-wide figures; most violations in North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri per other UN sources, not this report)
statement: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on children and armed conflict reported that 1,067 children (910 boys, 157 girls) were abducted in the DRC in 2025, by M23 (570), ADF (102), Nyatura (97), CODECO (61), Mai-Mai Mazembe (37), Wazalendo (37) and others, most for the purpose of recruitment and use (508).

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (country-wide figures; most violations in North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri per other UN sources, not this report)
statement: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on children and armed conflict reported that in the DRC in 2025 some 1,397 children (1,109 boys, 288 girls) were recruited and used by parties including Mouvement national congolais (173), Mai-Mai Mazembe (158), M23 (142), CODECO (119), ADF (85), Nyatura (84) and Raia Mutomboki (79), and that some 114 children (107 boys, 7 girls) were detained for alleged association with armed groups by the Armed Forces (108), the National Intelligence Agency (4) and the Congolese National Police (2), all of whom were released following UN advocacy.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo (country-wide figures; most violations in North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri per other UN sources, not this report)
statement: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on children and armed conflict reported that 19 incidents of denial of humanitarian access were verified in the DRC in 2025, including the killing of one humanitarian worker, by M23 (3), Twirwaneho (3), Wazalendo (3), unidentified perpetrators (5), the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (1), Raia Mutomboki (1) and two other parties (3).

The UN Secretary-General wrote in his annual report on children and armed conflict that he condemned the 2025 offensive in North Kivu and South Kivu by M23 with the direct support and participation of the Rwanda Defence Forces, leading to a significant increase in child casualties and abductions; that ongoing military operations by all parties, together with the increased use of drone strikes, were deeply concerning; and that the scale of sexual violence by the defence and security forces and by armed groups was appalling.

place: Security Council, New York (statement about eastern DRC)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, chairing the Security Council's 10190th meeting on 8 July 2026 in New York, denounced sexual violence in eastern DRC, which she attributed to armed groups and foreign forces including Rwanda, saying that in zones affected by armed groups and under occupation by foreign forces, including Rwanda, these violences were linked to forced displacement, illicit economies and predation.

place: Security Council, New York (statement about DRC)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that DRC deputy permanent representative to the UN Ambassador Jocelyne Kabengele Lukundulu said at the Security Council's 10,251st meeting, on the theme of children and conflicts, on 26 October that the situation on the ground remained worrying and that child protection must be integrated into the design of ceasefires, peace agreements and transitional justice mechanisms.

place: Ufamandu 1er groupement, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing an anonymous medical source in the Katoyi health zone, that four health structures (CS Ufamandu, CS Miano, CSR Katuunda and CS Nyandeki) in Ufamandu groupement, Masisi territory, had been destroyed in the context of fighting between the FRN rebels and the FARDC supported by Wazalendo, damaged by bombardments after medicines stored in them were looted by unidentified persons.

place: Masisi centre, Bahunde chiefdom, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that a nurse of the Masisi general referral hospital, identified as Montaigne Byanikiro, was shot dead in the night of Wednesday to Thursday 19 February 2026 in Masisi centre, Bahunde chiefdom; according to local sources, unidentified armed men burst into his home at around 23 hours and reportedly opened fire several times before fleeing. The Masisi nurses condemned what they called a new murder targeting a member of the health staff.

Insecurity Insight reported, as of 24 April 2025 and citing MSF, that in Goma city, North Kivu, an unspecified number of MSF staff were shot and wounded by an unidentified perpetrator over the past few months, and at least one was hospitalised.

place: North Kivu (facilities not named in the report text)
statement: The Safeguarding Health in Conflict Coalition's 2025 annual report (data by Insecurity Insight) reported that M23 militia in North Kivu set ablaze two health centers on the pretext that they were treating members of opposition parties.
sources: Insecurity Insight / Safeguarding Health in Conflict Coalition

place: North Kivu (place not named in the report text)
statement: The Safeguarding Health in Conflict Coalition's 2025 annual report reported that at least two health workers were killed with bladed weapons in eastern DRC in 2025, including a nurse who was beheaded by M23 after being accused of providing medical care to opposition parties; the body was later found in the bush in North Kivu.
sources: Insecurity Insight / Safeguarding Health in Conflict Coalition

place: a commune in North Kivu (not named in the report text)
statement: The Safeguarding Health in Conflict Coalition's 2025 annual report reported that in one incident during their withdrawal from a commune in North Kivu, M23 rebels looted a health center, taking all the medical equipment and medications, then destroyed the solar power system that sustained its cold chain and broke all doors and windows, while health center staff hid in the surrounding bush.
sources: Insecurity Insight / Safeguarding Health in Conflict Coalition

statement: Radio Okapi reported that on 11 June the Katwa Ebola treatment centre had already been the target of an attempted attack, in an article on resistance to Ebola response teams in Butembo and Beni.

place: Centre hospitalier adventiste de Wanamahika, Mutiri, Butembo, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the North Kivu provincial health division issued a search notice after the disappearance of two Ebola patients from the Wanamahika adventist hospital centre at Mutiri, Butembo, following an attack by men carrying bladed weapons who burst into the facility to forcibly remove a woman and her child who had recently tested positive for Ebola; it identified them as Zawadi Manacée and her daughter Christelle Kavugho, aged six and a half. The same article, citing an official notice, also said the two patients reportedly left the hospital centre before the child's planned transfer to an Ebola treatment centre.

place: Cité Belge neighbourhood, Bungulu commune, Beni city, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that on Saturday 1 August residents of the Cité Belge neighbourhood in Beni opposed the transfer of a patient suspected of Ebola to a treatment centre and that the ambulance carrying out her evacuation was stoned, requiring the intervention of law enforcement. Insecurity Insight, citing Congo Quotidien, MSN and Reuters, reported that on 01 August 2026 in Cité Belge neighbourhood, Bungulu commune, Beni city, an ambulance sent to evacuate an Ebola patient was stoned by demonstrators, who broke its windshield, and that police fired warning shots to disperse them.

place: Mangothe health area and Ndindi health centre, Beni health zone, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing a situation report it consulted, that in the Beni health zone, North Kivu, people tried to set fire to the homes of two community relays in the Mangothe health area and that the Ndindi health centre was also threatened with arson before an intervention restored order.

place: Kanyabayonga, Kayina, Kirumba, Kipese (Lubero territory), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the towns of Kanyabayonga, Kayina, Kirumba and Kipese, in Lubero territory, were under M23 occupation, and that Lubero territory was also hit by ADF attacks.

place: Kirumba-Katondi axis, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that vehicles carrying men and equipment had been seen shuttling for about two weeks on the Kirumba-Katondi axis in southern Lubero, a movement it said had intensified since a recent AFC/M23 meeting at Kirumba at which the rebellion expressed its intention to take Butembo and Beni.

place: Mashango, Bukombo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (patients admitted at Mweso, Masisi), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that an AFC-M23 patrol was ambushed by CMC fighters at Mashango village (Bukombo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru) the day before its report, and, citing several local sources, that dozens of civilians, notably residents of Katsiru who had come to Mashango for community work, were trapped in the exchange of fire; at least 18 wounded civilians were admitted to Mwesso referral hospital in neighbouring Masisi territory, according to medical sources.

place: Musimba / Vweyera, near Butembo, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the Representation of Students of Congo (REC) Butembo-Lubero announced on Wednesday 12 November the immediate suspension of classes in all institutions of Butembo city and Lubero territory after the death of Rosette Kavira Vyahula, a student at ISTM Butembo, shot dead by a muzalendo militiaman. The outlet says the shot reportedly occurred during a dispute between wazalendo groups at Vweyera, and elsewhere that she was killed by a muzalendo militiaman named Nzingene at Musimba as she returned from lectures; she was taken to hospital at Musimba and died of her wounds.

place: Butembo (city); attacks at Ntoyo (Lubero) and Fotodu (Beni-Mbau), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that socio-economic activities were partially paralysed on the morning of Thursday 11 September in Butembo, where urban civil society and LUCHA held a 'day of mourning without activities' in solidarity with communities bereaved by recent ADF attacks, which it said had killed more than 70 civilians at Ntoyo (Lubero territory) and 18 at Fotodu (Beni-Mbau sector, Beni territory); around 10:45 demonstrators and police clashed, the police using live ammunition and demonstrators throwing stones, and the outlet said no serious incident had been reported so far.

Actualite.cd reported a 'ville morte' day in Butembo called by the citizen-movements synergy and pressure groups; LUCHA activist Jean-Pierre Kasma told the outlet its main aim was to demand the departure of the mayor of Butembo, the removal of the urban police commander, the relocation of 'wazalendo' group positions inside and around the city, and the opening of independent investigations.

Radio Okapi reported that, according to protesters at a day without activities in Beni, at least eight murders had been recorded in less than a month in Beni city, involving armed men including soldiers already arrested.

place: Babila-Bakaiko farming zones, west of Oicha, Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that an attack attributed to ADF rebels in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 6 May killed at least 26, many of them farmers; according to local civil society it took place in the Babila-Bakaiko farming zones about 40 km west of the rural commune of Oicha (Beni), in the farming blocks of Katere, Manzumbu, Musangwa, Wasafi and Mangambo.

place: Ngadi and Vemba, Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Denis Mukwege strongly condemned on Monday 1 June the attacks attributed to ADF rebels that killed at least 16 in the localities of Ngadi and Vemba, Beni territory, in the night of 'samedi 31 mai', and that he was particularly alarmed by violence against members of the indigenous pygmy community.

Radio Okapi reported that Amnesty International, in a report published on Tuesday 5 May, denounced massive abuses by ADF rebels against civilians in North Kivu and Ituri, citing violations including killings, abductions and torture, forced marriages and pregnancies, and repeated sexual violence.
Radio Okapi reported that Amnesty International, in its report on the ADF, said the attacks target mainly populations but also fields, health centres and homes, often looted and then burned.

place: Rubaya (Masisi, North Kivu) and Lomera (Kabare, South Kivu)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Amnesty International said it had documented serious human rights abuses in mining zones controlled by the M23 in North Kivu and South Kivu, based on testimony from 26 people, with research on a coltan mine near Rubaya (Masisi, North Kivu) and the Lomera gold site (Kabare, South Kivu); Amnesty said it had documented the summary execution of 18 artisanal miners at Rubaya and Lomera, of whom, according to testimony, ten were reportedly beaten to death, two shot dead and six abducted before being found dead.

place: Masisi centre, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post wrote, without naming a source, that on 2 January an FARDC drone missed its target at Masisi centre, exploding on homes and causing more than 40 civilian wounded and at least 6 dead.

place: Buhimba and Mahanga, Walikale and Masisi territories, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 rebels had taken control of Buhimba and Mahanga (Walikale and Masisi territories) over the weekend after dislodging the Congolese army and the Wazalendo; Kipande Mungo, head of Osso Banyungu sector, told the outlet the rebels had been at Mahanga in Osso since Saturday at 12:00 and the population was dispersed.
Kivu Morning Post reported that the Congolese army accused the rebels of carrying out several attacks on its positions in Rutshuru, Masisi and Kalehe and said it would not let this happen.
Kivu Morning Post reported that, for its part, the AFC-M23 accused the FARDC of violating the agreement signed in Doha by breaking the ceasefire.

place: Buhimba, Walikale territory (M23 withdrew to Mahanga and Kasopo, Masisi), North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that relative calm was reported at Buhimba (Waloa Yungu grouping) after two days of violent fighting between FARDC and M23, that M23 fighters had withdrawn to Mahanga and Kasopo in neighbouring Masisi territory, and, citing a local source, that Buhimba remained under government forces' control.

place: Kibati, Luberike grouping, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing a local civil-society source, that Wazalendo launched their first attack on AFC-M23 positions on Saturday 28 February 2026 and that intense fighting pitted AFC-M23 fighters against the Wazalendo from early Monday in Kibati village (Luberike grouping, Walikale). It also reported that the fighting intensified until Sunday 1 March but that AFC-M23 repelled the assaults and held its positions in central Kibati.

place: Masisi territory (Ngungu, Rubaya, Nyabiondo, Pinga axis), North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that fighting continued, notably around Ngungu, Rubaya, Nyabiondo and on the axis toward Pinga, despite ceasefire appeals, and that control of Rubaya, one of the country's main coltan and cassiterite sites, had remained in AFC/M23 hands for nearly two years.

place: Katana groupement, Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani said summary executions of civilians were multiplying, notably in Katana groupement, Kabare territory, and that in the night of 23 to 24 November at least 12 people were arrested and then summarily executed by AFC/M23 rebels, who accused them of collaborating with or belonging to the Wazalendo.

place: Katana groupement, Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani said that, among at least 12 people arrested then summarily executed in the night of 23 to 24 November (in a report on executions notably in Katana groupement, Kabare territory), was a patient removed from a health centre before his execution; the victims were aged 20 to 40.

Radio Okapi reported that the Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani also denounced the summary execution of two young men of the same family at Kaniola, Walungu territory, on 21 November, killed and then buried in a mass grave by AFC/M23 elements.

place: South Kivu (Nyamarongo, Boavo chefferie; Lumbichi, as printed)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC 3rd defence zone, based in Kisangani, published a communiqué on Friday 8 August in which its spokesperson, Major Mavudisa Kamba, condemned targeted killings of civilians and forced recruitment of minors by the RDF/M23/AFC coalition in South Kivu, and cited the killing of more than 80 civilians on 4 August 2025 at Nyamarongo village, Boavo chefferie, and of six civilians, two of them minors, at Lumbichi on 24 July.

place: Kimbili and Nyalubemba, Bamuguba Sud groupement, Bakisi chefferie, Shabunda territory, South Kivu
