statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that AFC-M23 rebels extended their progression in Shabunda territory, South Kivu, by occupying the villages Kimbili and Nyalubemba after an offensive on 20 November against forward positions of the FARDC and Wazalendo fighters, and that, according to local civil society, the Nyalubemba health centre at Kimbili was overwhelmed by civilian and military wounded.

Radio Okapi reported that the ICRC said an assessment carried out between 2 and 10 September 2025 of 240 health facilities in the two Kivus found 85% out of stock of essential medicines and supplies, that transfer of the wounded was hindered by fighting and patients travelled long distances on foot at risk to their lives, and that more than 70% of the 240 structures had received people wounded by weapons.

place: Mikenge, Hauts Plateaux, Fizi territory, South Kivu (page says Fizi; other sources place it in Mwenga)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC announced they had retaken the cité of Mikenge, Fizi territory, South Kivu, on Sunday '1er mard' (read as 1 March), after violent clashes with rebels in the Hauts Plateaux, and that the spokesperson of operations Sukola 2 Sud South Kivu, Sub-Lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan, said several rebels were neutralised, 5 captured and 17 surrendered, and that among 11 bodies found were an AFC-M23 brigade commander and a logistics officer.

place: Bilalombili, near Mikenge, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that on 1 March (2025) fighting resumed in Bilalombili village near Mikenge, Mwenga territory, where, according to several local sources, Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and Android elements allied to M23 attacked Wazalendo positions, and that local civil societies denounced the burning of the houses of Bilalombili, which had hosted people displaced from Mikenge, without giving a toll.

place: Ilundu and Alengei, Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that clashes took place on Wednesday 24 June in the villages of Ilundu and Alengei, Minembwe zone, Fizi territory, between the FARDC and fighters of the Twirwaneho armed coalition and their allies, described as backed by Rwanda, and that the militia accused the FARDC of drone bombardments of its positions.

place: London (meeting); Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu (subject)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, at the sixth meeting of the Comité mixte de surveillance (CMS) on the security situation in the DRC, held on Wednesday 24 June 2026 in London, Kinshasa and Kigali reaffirmed their commitment to de-escalate tensions linked to the situation of Minembwe.

place: Tchambombo, Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that fighting between Wazalendo fighters and AFC/M23 troops was reported throughout Thursday 2 April 2026 in Tchambombo village, Ziralo groupement, on the Kalehe highlands, and, citing local sources, that many residents fled into the bush and to villages deemed safer.

place: Kaniola and Mugogo, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that fighting between AFC/M23 troops and Wazalendo fighters was reported on Wednesday 19 November 2025 in Kaniola groupement and at the Mugogo trading centre, Walungu territory, and that several families fled to nearby villages of Kaniola groupement.

Deutsche Welle (Swahili) reported that Amnesty International said M23 fighters backed by Rwanda and Wazalendo groups allied to the Congolese army committed serious atrocities in eastern DRC, including gang rapes of women, and that women from North Kivu and South Kivu gave testimony, 14 of whom recounted being gang-raped; the outlet reported that Beatrice from Bukavu said she was attacked by five M23 soldiers.

place: Goma and Bukavu hospitals (North and South Kivu)
statement: Deutsche Welle (Swahili) reported that Amnesty International said M23 attacks included hospitals, where patients and staff were abducted or detained, and that this happened between February and May 2025 when the group controlled much of Goma and Bukavu.

place: Kaburantwa and Rugano hills, Bukinanyana, Bujumbura province, Burundi (fighters from South Kivu)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several testimonies collected on site, that armed men who fled fighting in South Kivu in December and crossed the Rusizi river into Bukinanyana commune, Bujumbura province, were accused by residents of looting and, according to several testimonies, of sexual violence, with women and girls said to be victims of rape under threat of reprisals if they reported.

BBC News Swahili reported that the military police department of the DRC army said it was holding rebel FARDC soldiers and pro-government Wazalendo fighters linked to indiscriminate shooting in the city of Uvira. A resident told BBC that rebel soldiers were being arrested by the military police and that those looting or firing indiscriminately were being arrested.

BBC News Swahili reported that a resident of Uvira told BBC that the disturbances seen since Wednesday continued into Thursday night with gunfire in several areas, and that during the night FARDC soldiers broke into several houses demanding money, phones and food.
SOS Médias Burundi reported on 10 December 2025 that the city of Uvira fell to the M23 rebel movement on the night of 9 December, and that the fighters entered without encountering resistance.

place: Mulongwe, Kasenga, Kavimvira and the Burundi border post, Uvira city
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, according to several witnesses, that M23 columns simultaneously entered several neighbourhoods of Uvira including the Mulongwe commercial centre, the Kasenga neighbourhood, the Kavimvira area and the border post with Burundi.

place: Uvira city (port of Kalundu), South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, shortly before the M23 assault, almost all loyalist forces (FARDC and Wazalendo) had abandoned their positions in Uvira, with retreat routes observed towards Kalemie via the port of Kalundu, towards Fizi and, for some soldiers, towards Burundi.

place: Kasenga and Kavimvira neighbourhoods, Uvira city
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing a Kasenga resident, that in some streets of Kasenga and Kavimvira the bodies of Wazalendo fighters were still visible in the morning, and that Red Cross teams were seen collecting them.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Sunday 14 December Burundian day labourers crossed the border via the Kavimvira-Gatumba crossing and that on Monday 15 December approximately 500 Burundian refugees still in Uvira were also repatriated.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that an M23 spokesperson said the movement had "no problem with African people, much less with Burundians", could not be held responsible for the prolonged blockade of Burundians in Uvira, and that the border on the Congolese side had remained open under a policy of free movement in areas under its control.
Deutsche Welle (Swahili) reported that thousands of civilians had been forced to flee to Burundi after M23 rebels entered the city of Uvira.

BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 announced on Saturday that it was withdrawing the observer contingent that had remained in Uvira and asked MONUSCO to deploy troops to protect the city; on Sunday morning Wazalendo fighters returned to Uvira and that evening FARDC troops began entering.
BBC News Gahuza reported that the Congolese army (FARDC) announced it had taken the city of Uvira and that its soldiers had been controlling it since Sunday 18 January 2026.
BBC News Gahuza reported that FARDC accused M23 fighters, which it said were working with Rwandan forces, of destroying and looting before leaving Uvira; M23 spokesperson Balinda denied this.

BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 spokesperson Balinda, in an interview with BBC, denied FARDC's accusation of destruction and looting in Uvira, calling it a lie and saying that the items it was accused of looting had been shown to be still there.
BBC News Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that since Wazalendo and FARDC re-entered Uvira, the city had become a hotbed of fighting, violence, looting and hate speech.
BBC News Gahuza reported that the Congolese state army said about 20 residents seen taking part in looting and disturbing security in Uvira had been arrested and would be brought before justice.

BBC News Gahuza reported that a resident of Uvira, who asked not to be named, told BBC that looting took place at government houses, city offices, the military court, a hotel called Suzanna belonging to a person known as Muchepe, and elsewhere, and that it happened in two phases: first AFC/M23 looted almost everything in the city, including vehicles and other valuables, and the second phase was carried out by Wazalendo and residents.

place: Uvira city, South Kivu (statement made at AU PSC meeting)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe, in a statement posted on his X account after an African Union Peace and Security Council meeting, said Rwanda welcomed the unilateral withdrawal of AFC/M23 from Uvira as a goodwill gesture towards the mediators and a strong signal of readiness to return to the negotiating table.

place: Eastern DRC (statement tied to Uvira withdrawal)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that Rwanda also reiterated its concerns about what it called daily ceasefire violations by the Kinshasa-backed armed coalition, saying that a ceasefire binds both parties to a conflict equally and cannot be imposed on only one.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundian Foreign Minister Édouard Bizimana declared at a Bujumbura meeting with representatives of partner countries and international organisations that the Burundi-Congo border would remain closed until further notice, and asserted that the M23 was lying when it claimed to have withdrawn from Uvira, saying the apparent withdrawal masked a regrouping and repositioning of its fighters.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that the governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, after crossing the border, had assured the population in Uvira that the Burundi-Congo border would be reopened within two to three days, by 30 January 2026 at the latest; the same report says the border's continued closure was later announced.
SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Gatumba-Kavimvira border crossing was closed on 10 December 2025, after Uvira fell to the M23.

place: Uvira city (Kavimvira to Kalundu), South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Uvira largely observed a 'ghost town' day on Wednesday, called for by the Provincial Coordination of the New Congolese Civil Society (NSCC), with traffic virtually nonexistent from Kavimvira to Kalundu and markets, shops and warehouses closed.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that, according to testimonies gathered on site in Uvira, two people were killed the day before a day of mobilization, and that over the past month around ten people had reportedly lost their lives and more than twenty others had been injured in various security incidents.

place: Uvira general hospital (Hôpital général d'Uvira), Uvira city
statement: Congo Rassure reported that on 26 February gunfire and explosions heard inside the Uvira general hospital caused patients and health staff to flee.

place: Walikale-centre (tribunal seat); Lukole village (facts), Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit hearing at Walikale-centre, sentenced ten FARDC soldiers of the 3415th regiment on Tuesday 1 September 2026, two of them to death for the murder of their company commander, Captain Musanga Bebeto, together with criminal participation and dissipation of war munitions. According to the prosecution, as reported by the outlet, the soldiers opened fire on their commander during operations against AFC/M23 at Lukole village, Masisi territory, on 30 October 2025. The outlet also reported that, in addition to the sentences, soldiers Seleko Mbele Jubilet, Kongo Byemba, Bwana Bisele and Guy Bashomba were jointly ordered to pay 50,000 US dollars to the civil party in damages.

place: Mubi Centre (facts), Walikale territory, North Kivu; tribunal sitting at Walikale
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit chamber at Walikale, sentenced to death on Monday 9 February (2026) Sergeant Maleso Buka Pierre, a judicial police officer attached to the Mubi judicial inspectorate, convicted of murder for facts of Saturday 31 January at Mubi Centre. According to the case file as reported, while a wanted man named in the article, presented as a member of an armed group, tried to evade arrest, one of two officers sent to execute an arrest warrant fired without orders and the man died minutes later.

Actualite.cd reported that on Wednesday 10 December (2025) the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit hearing at Walikale, sentenced six people (three soldiers, two VDP fighters and one civilian): two of the three soldiers accused of losing weapons and war munitions were sentenced to death and the third to 15 years for desertion, and a VDP fighter prosecuted for rape received 20 years of servitude pénale principale.

place: Manyama-Beu, Beni-Mbau sector, Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: 7sur7.cd reported that the Beni garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit chamber at Manyama-Beu (Beni-Mbau sector, Beni territory), delivered its verdict on Tuesday 28 July 2026 in a case of two soldiers prosecuted notably for breach of orders during operations against the ADF and for the murder of three civilians the previous weekend: Ahundu Likamba Ruffin was sentenced to 20 years of servitude pénale principale, and Irakunda Bindibikwira to death for breach of orders, murder of three civilians and attempted murder.

place: Manyama-Beu / Oicha, Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: 7sur7.cd reported, in its article on the Beni garrison military tribunal's Manyama-Beu verdicts, that hearings concerning a third soldier prosecuted for the alleged rape of a 19-month-old girl had been suspended, the case file being examined at Oicha, where the victim was receiving medical care.

Actualite.cd reported that on Monday 3 November 2025 the AFC/M23, through a justice-revival commission (CRJ) it had set up some months earlier, announced the integration of 378 new magistrates into its judicial system, described by the outlet as now parallel to the government's, following a test held in Goma on 14 September 2025.

place: Kinshasa (statement); Goma and Bukavu (AFC/M23-held areas concerned)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the president of the Constitutional Court and of the Conseil supérieur de la magistrature, Dieudonné Kamuleta, had recalled in a communiqué published on 12 September 2025 that the country's Constitution and organic laws give the Conseil supérieur de la magistrature exclusive power to recruit and manage magistrates nationwide, and that any parallel attempt is therefore, according to him, 'nulle et de nul effet'; the Justice Minister Guillaume Ngefa had announced the forthcoming signature of an ordinance annulling all judicial decisions taken by AFC/M23 leaders.

place: Rubaya mine, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: BBC News Afrique reported that, according to the government, more than 200 people, including 70 children, were killed when a landslide caused a mining area to collapse in eastern DRC; it quoted the Ministry of Mines communiqué giving a provisional toll of more than 200 dead and many injured, and said it could not independently verify the toll. It also reported that the ministry blamed the M23 rebels, that the M23 had not yet commented, that a source at Rubaya told the BBC the collapse was caused by attacks by government forces and that only six people had died, and that the government had not responded to that claim.

MSF said in a communiqué that on 1 May a team travelling between Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu in South Kivu was stopped at a checkpoint held by Wazalendo elements, and that armed men opened fire among themselves while the team was in the middle.

RFI reported that the newly built Mwalu hotel in Fizi-centre was hit by a drone strike at one in the morning in the night of 18 to 19 August, that two civilians were seriously injured, and that the Congolese army accuses the AFC/M23 of being behind the attack, citing two explosive devices dropped by drones.

place: Ilundu/Basita, Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that two people were killed and six wounded in bombardments in the night of Saturday 6 to Sunday 7 June in Ilundu/Basita village, Minembwe, Fizi territory, and that the Réseau local de protection des civils dans les Hauts Plateaux, a citizens' collective based in Minembwe, said in a communiqué that the shots, attributed to the FARDC and the Burundian FDNB, targeted an inhabited area of the village; the reported toll names Prince Runezerwa Mahiyaho, aged 19, who died on arrival at the general hospital, and Résor Kigeri Mazuru, who reportedly died at the scene; the outlet said that at publication no official reaction from the FARDC or the FDNB had been obtained.

place: Maiba village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that more than 70 bodies, including those of women, children and elderly people, were found on Saturday 15 February in a church building in Maiba village, Lubero territory; civil society believed they were people reported missing who had been abducted on 12 February by unidentified armed men, and said they were found bound and beheaded, probably killed with bladed weapons. Radio Okapi added that concordant sources in the region suspected local armed groups and ADF rebels of being the perpetrators.

place: Maiba, Manzya groupement, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that at least 70 civilians died in Lubero territory in an act attributed to ADF rebels near Maiba in the Manzya groupement, and that their bodies were found 'vendredi dernier' (the previous Friday) two days after the abduction, according to the local community protection committee. It quoted the committee's coordinator Vitwamba Vianney as saying the victims were taken hostage in the night of 11 to 12 February and that the victims, of all ages, were finished off in a local church.

place: Luofu, Kamandi Gite and Kibanda (west of Kayna), Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that fighting between the FARDC and M23 rebels continued on Wednesday 15 January at Luofu, in Lubero territory, North Kivu, and that clashes were also reported in several villages south of Lubero, notably Kamandi Gite and Kibanda, west of the rural commune of Kayna.

place: Mighende village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that new fighting broke out on Monday 26 January between Wazalendo fighters and AFC/M23 rebels in Mighende village, about thirty kilometres from Lubero-Centre, Lubero territory; according to local sources, AFC/M23 elements attacked a Wazalendo position and burned its camp.

place: Kalonge and Lubango villages, southern Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting had opposed AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo self-defence groups since Monday 30 March in several localities of southern Lubero territory; according to local and security sources, the first clashes broke out on Monday around 5 am in the villages of Kalonge and Lubango, about thirty kilometres from the territorial capital, where AFC/M23 forces reportedly attacked Wazalendo elements of the Mouvement des résistants des patriotes congolais (MRPC) recently deployed after a partial rebel withdrawal. The fighting displaced civilians, and several sources said AFC/M23 had reportedly retaken control of the villages concerned.

place: Lunyasenge, North Kivu (territory not stated by the source)
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Lunyasenge, which it described as about fifty kilometres west of Lake Edward, was taken on 2 May by AFC/M23 rebels supported by the Rwandan army, according to Kinshasa and several international reports, and that violent fighting opposed the rebels and Congolese soldiers; the toll remained unclear, but several local sources spoke of heavy human losses.

Actualite.cd reported that in a communiqué published on 4 May the Congolese army confirmed the loss of Lunyasenge, denouncing a flagrant violation of the ceasefire in force, and that Colonel Mak Hazukay, FARDC spokesperson in the Grand-Nord, reaffirmed the army's will to 'riposter sur tous les fronts' if the threats persisted.

place: Kasindi, Beni territory (displaced from Lunyasenge), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the border town of Kasindi, in Beni territory, received on the evening of Monday 5 May the first wave of displaced people fleeing Lunyasenge, taken recently by AFC/M23 rebels.

place: ADF camp in Lubero territory (exact place not stated), North Kivu
statement: ACLED reported that by the end of the first quarter of 2025 the M23-RDF offensive had reached an ADF camp in Lubero territory under the leadership of Ahmad Mahmood Hassan, commonly called Abwakasi.

place: Ngadi neighbourhood, Ruwenzori commune, Beni city, North Kivu
statement: Radio Moto Beni-Butembo (RMBB) reported that suspected ADF rebels attacked Ngadi neighbourhood, Ruwenzori commune, in the city of Beni, in the night of Saturday to Sunday 31 May 2026, targeting among other places the Ngadi pygmy camp; the provisional toll was at least 7 killed, mostly pygmies including the comedian Shukurani Nzanzu Mangese, six bodies being found early on Sunday and the seventh victim dying of wounds in a health facility, and sources on site said several other civilians were missing.

place: Masisi and Lubero territories; Lake Edward, North Kivu
statement: OCHA reported in a weekly regional 'latest events at a glance' infographic that fighting in Masisi and Lubero had displaced over 100,000 people, disrupted health services and affected food supplies to Lubero, and that a boat carrying people fleeing the fighting on Lake Edward sank, leaving 22 people missing.

place: Bapere sector and Manzia and Mwenye groupements, Lubero territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Muhindo Tafuteni, president of the local civil society, said ADF activism was continuing in the Bapere sector and the Manzia and Mwenye groupements, and that 'for the month of January alone, we deplore more than 52 people killed'; he also said schools and health structures were no longer functioning in that part of the country.

place: Kahwela, Kivumu, Luhemba (Fizi territory), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that fighting broke out on a Thursday morning in the villages of Kahwela, Kivumu and Luhemba in Fizi territory between Wazalendo forces and Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC-M23; it said the Wazalendo accused the Twirwaneho of launching attacks targeting cultivators in those localities.

Kivu Morning Post reported that Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC-M23 accused the Congolese army, in coalition with the Burundian army, of a targeted attack on the village of Mikenge near Minembwe, and that according to their statements the attack took place on 10 September with the support of Wazalendo forces.

place: Itombwe sector (Mwenga territory), South Kivu; fighting also extended to the hauts plateaux of Fizi and the moyens plateaux of Uvira
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that from 10 to 27 August 2026 at least 23 people were killed, 17 seriously wounded and at least six villages burned in fighting between AFC-M23-Twirwaneho troops and the DRC armed forces and their allies in the Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory; it said the figures were given by the Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d'Itombwe after monitoring.

place: Itombwe sector (Mwenga); Point Zéro (Fizi territory), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that the Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d'Itombwe counted at least 1100 households, more than six thousand people, displaced in the bush or in host villages in that part of South Kivu, and that sources reported continued drone and mortar bombardments at Point Zéro in Fizi territory, causing panic and new displacement.

place: Kipupu-Mikenge axis, up to 'Filon 14' (Itombwe massif), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that over the weekend and until Monday morning 31 August 2026 the Kipupu-Mikenge axis was the scene of violent clashes between the two sides as far as the area known as Filon 14 in the Itombwe massif.

place: Nakiele, Kilumbi, Kanguli health areas (Fizi territory), South Kivu; 17 villages listed incl. Point zéro, Kitasha, Mikenge 1 and 2, Kakenge, Abala
statement: Actualite.cd reported that nearly 41.900 people displaced by clashes between AFC/M23 elements and FARDC/Wazalendo were living in precarious conditions in villages including Nakiele, Kilumbi and Kanguli in Fizi territory; it quoted civil society as saying its assessments counted 41.952 displaced persons in 8618 households, living without sufficient access to food, drinking water, health care or shelter.
Radio Maendeleo reported that new fighting at the start of the week led to the AFC/M23-Twirwaneho troops taking the centre of the village of Kanguli since Wednesday 22 July.

place: Point Zéro, Kipupu, Mulima, Mukera, Fizi-Centre (Fizi / Mwenga), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 troops still controlled the village of Point Zéro and its surroundings, while the FARDC kept their positions at Kipupu, Mulima, Mukera and as far as Fizi-Centre.

place: Baraka, Fizi territory and part of Itombwe sector (Mwenga), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that telecommunication network services remained suspended in the town of Baraka, across Fizi territory and part of the Itombwe sector, a measure in force for more than a month and taken by the authorities for security reasons, notably after the taking of several villages including Point Zéro by AFC/M23; local civil society said even private Starlink connections were blocked.

place: Kipupu (Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 seized Kipupu centre on Friday 10 July before withdrawing, that clashes over control were reported at Kipupu on 12-13 July, and that the chef-lieu of the Itombwe sector then returned to the control of the army and its allies.

Radio Okapi reported that the vice-governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, at a security council meeting held on Monday in Uvira, denied rumours of the fall of Baraka to the rebels and urged the population to stay calm and carry on with their activities.

place: Point Zéro; Kashamata, Wihene, Kimete (Fizi territory), South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the army announced its 'repli stratégique' from Point Zéro for tactical reasons, and that the spokesperson of operation Sokola 2 South Kivu, sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, said the villages retaken by the FARDC were Kashamata, Wihene and Kimete, with the rebels forced to fall back towards Rugezi and Bigaragara, south of Minembwe.

place: Mikenge and surroundings (Minembwe highlands), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local sources, violent clashes on Wednesday 1 July 2026 at Mikenge and its surroundings in the Minembwe highlands; it said that for a month Twirwaneho allied to the AFC/M23 had been fighting the Congolese army backed by the Burundian army and Wazalendo, and that civil-society sources said the fighting reportedly caused several victims.

Kivu Morning Post reported that on Tuesday 30 June 2026 hundreds of residents of the Banyamulenge community demonstrated in Minembwe to protest against Congolese army drone attacks, which it said had intensified, and called for the withdrawal of Burundian troops present in the highlands of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga.

place: Mikenge, Gakenke, Kalingi, Bidegu (Minembwe highlands), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué, the association Mahoro Peace Association (MPA) said 32 civilians were wounded during offensives by the Burundian and Congolese armies in the villages of Mikenge, Gakenke, Kalingi and Bidegu between 8 and 11 June 2026.

place: Ilundu and Minembwe (Fizi territory), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that violent clashes took place on Sunday 14 June 2026 at Ilundu, a few kilometres from the centre of Minembwe, between the Twirwaneho and the FARDC, and that over the weekend aerial bombardments by FARDC Sukhoï-25 aircraft were recorded at Minembwe, causing many victims.

place: Rugezi (hauts plateaux); Nundu health zone, Tanganyika sector (Fizi territory), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that more than 31 mille (31 thousand) people displaced from the hauts plateaux of Fizi, particularly Itombwe and neighbouring villages, were in the moyens plateaux, notably the Nundu health zone, Tanganyika sector, Fizi territory; its source said the latest clashes took place 'last Sunday' in the village of Rugezi, causing new waves of displacement.

place: Fizi and Nundu health zones (Fizi territory), South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that more than 53 000 people fled to localities in the Fizi and Nundu health zones between August and October 2026 after intensified clashes in the hauts plateaux of Fizi; it reported OCHA as adding that fighting in early September and from 20 to 25 September reportedly caused civilian casualties and damaged essential infrastructure.

place: Point Zéro; Biziba Irumba (Minembwe periphery); Natulonge; Kabindo, Fizi / Mwenga, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that violent clashes continued at Point Zéro, which it placed in Mwenga territory, from the morning of 'ce 20 Septembre 2026', while several local sources said the fighting resumed there from the morning of 19 September; sources said a coalition of the FARDC, Wazalendo and 'les burundais' faced an AFC/Red Tabara Twirwaneho coalition; it said fighting had spilled over 'since yesterday' into the villages of Biziba Irumba on the periphery of Minembwe in Fizi territory, and that on 18 September fighting was concentrated in Natulonge and Kabindo in Fizi territory.

Kivu Morning Post reported that FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from 01:00 on Friday 16 October 2026 the coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime were intensely bombarding Rugezi and its surroundings in the Minembwe region with heavy artillery and kamikaze drones.

place: Rugezi and Gipimo (Minembwe region), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the FRN accused government forces on Monday 19 October 2026 of having bombarded Rugezi and its surroundings in the Minembwe region between the evening of Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 October 2026; it also reported that Colonel Fidèle Rugabo, described as spokesperson of FRN fighters in the Minembwe area, said the populations of Rugezi and Gipimo were attacked during the night.

place: Kashaka, Kigogo, Ngenga road and Kasika, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local civil society, clashes between AFC/M23 and FARDC supported by Wazalendo lasted all day Sunday at Kashaka toward Kigogo and on the national road toward Ngenga, which, in the words of the Mwenga civil society president Samuel Itebo, created insecurity at Kasika; State exam papers started late in several villages of Lwindi chiefdom as a result.

place: Kiseke, Muhabo, Natulinge, Nabindi, Kisemu, Kalulu and Senge, Mwenga-Kipupu axis, Mwenga
statement: Enquete.cd reported that, according to residents and civil-society actors, several houses were burned at Kiseke (Mwenga territory) after fighting between FARDC and the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition spread to Kiseke and Nabindi, that civilian victims including women and children 'would have died in the flames', and that house fires were also reported at Muhabo, Natulinge, Nabindi, Kisemu, Kalulu and Senge; the page said no official toll had been communicated and did not say who set the fires.

place: Cidasa-Kasika zone and Kaulile, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga
statement: Enquete.cd reported that fighting was reported from the morning of 'this Sunday' in the Cidasa-Kasika zone, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga, reportedly opposing FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters and Burundian forces to AFC-M23 elements, and that the fighting had already displaced several residents; new clashes were also reported around the village of Kaulile.

MSF said that in Shabunda territory more than 260,000 people faced measles and cholera epidemics, due to limited access to drinking water and sanitation facilities, coupled with the displacement of people who fled violence; it said 1,002 cholera cases with 39 deaths had been recorded since 3 July 2026, according to local authorities, and that 7,620 measles cases had been reported, with 467 deaths notified.

place: Kahumiro, Bambo groupement, Bwito chiefdom (near Virunga park), Rutshuru
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources in the region, that at least ten civilians, mostly farmers, were killed on Wednesday 22 January at Kahumiro, near Virunga National Park in Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory), and that they were executed by M23/RDF coalition elements.

place: Lubwe Sud, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting was reported on Tuesday in the Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory), with M23 initiating the attack, in the agglomeration of Lubwe Sud.

place: Kiseguro and Ngwenda, Binza groupement, Rutshuru
statement: Actualite.cd reported that at least five M23/RDF coalition elements were killed in an ambush by wazalendo fighters near Kiseguro in the Binza groupement (Rutshuru), and, citing its sources, that the M23 rebels had been surprised taking agricultural produce from farmers.

Kivu Morning Post reported that violent clashes broke out from the morning of Wednesday 12 November 2025 in the Bukombo groupement (Rutshuru), particularly in the villages of Maruho, Machazo, Manyoni and Mudugugudu, and that further AFC-M23 attacks on Wazalendo positions were reported at Kibunanwa and Busukura in Mutanda groupement, with displaced people heading to Bambo, Lusogha, Kashalira and Kishishe.

place: Manyoni, Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local sources, that at least three bodies were found on the morning of Tuesday 11 November at Manyoni, Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru), the day after violent clashes between Wazalendo and AFC-M23, and that the victims were said to be three men killed with a bladed weapon.

Kivu Morning Post reported that at least five people were killed and nine wounded on the night of Friday to Saturday 6 December 2025 during an incursion of armed bandits it described as assimilated to the Wazalendo in the Katsiru agglomeration, Bukombo groupement (Rutshuru). A former presenter and journalist of Radio Communautaire de Mweso, Rachid Kazadi, was among the dead.

place: Nyabanira, Kasave, Makoka, Binza groupement, Rutshuru
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local testimony, that the evacuation order affecting villages of the Binza groupement (Rutshuru), mainly Nyabanira, Kasave and Makoka, was imposed by the M23. A Binza notable said the flight began on 12 July and intensified on Friday 25 July.

place: Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru (villages not named)
statement: Opinion Info reported a provisional toll of five dead, nearly twenty seriously wounded and about ten women raped, according to local sources contacted on 4 November 2025, in fighting since the start of that week between M23-AFC rebels and CMC-FDP Wazalendo fighters in Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru; an anonymous community source also mentioned the rape of fifteen women during the fighting. The outlet does not say who committed the rapes.

place: Kinyankuku (and neighbouring Kyahemba), Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the situation remained tense on the morning of Monday 10 November in the village of Kinyankuku, Bukombo groupement (Rutshuru), after fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and CMC-FDP wazalendo; citing its sources, it said hostilities began in the night from Sunday to Monday after an attack by AFC/M23 rebels on wazalendo positions. It said access to the fields on the outskirts of Kitshanga, notably on the Bukombo axis, was impossible and that farming was paralysed in the area, including at Kyahemba, a neighbouring locality also affected by the fighting.

place: Muko, Karambi, Mashango and other villages of Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that about ten houses were burned between Sunday and Monday 15 December 2025 during fighting between AFC-M23 and CMC-FDP Wazalendo in Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru, and said the fires occurred during AFC-M23 military operations against CMC-FDP in villages including Muko, Karambi and Mashango.

Actualite.cd reported that 30 women, accused by AFC/M23 rebels of being informants of the wazalendo on their movements, were abducted by AFC/M23 rebels on 28 December 2025 at Bukombo (Rutshuru) and taken to the Rubona camp, one of the garrisons held by the rebels; it said the Congolese army had accused the rebels of torturing the women, that 27 women were gradually released according to its sources at Bukombo, and that three remained in captivity.

place: Miti-Murhesa health zone (Mudaka, Bushumba and Miti groupings receiving displaced), Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: An early-alert entry on the ehtools humanitarian platform reported more than 18174 people (about 3029 households) displaced in the Miti-Murhesa health zone, Kabare territory, after armed clashes, which the alert dates between 25 July and 2 August 2026, in villages of the Bugobe grouping and around the Kahuzi-Biega National Park; the alert names the CHB de Katana as the structure raising the alarm. It listed the displaced as lacking, among other things, essential medicines.

place: Cimpwiji, Nyamyera village, Mudusa grouping, Kabare territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that a large fire killed two people and affected more than a hundred households in the night of Friday 14 to Saturday 15 August 2026 at Cimpwiji, in the village of Nyamyera, Mudusa grouping, Kabare territory; it said the fire started around 1 a.m. while most inhabitants were asleep. The article gives no cause and attributes it to no armed actor.

place: Bundje (Bunje in 7sur7.cd), Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that at least three people, including a woman and her two children, were killed and several others wounded on Friday 7 August 2026 during clashes between Wazalendo and AFC/M23 at Bundje, Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory, and that, according to local sources, a bomb was dropped from the front line on the Mpanama-Chabikere-Katale axis in the village of Bundje. 7sur7.cd quoted an army spokesperson as saying that three civilians, a woman and her two children, died when the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition threw several bombs at populated areas.

place: Bundje, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji attributed the 7 August 2026 fire at Bundje to the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition, saying it had launched 82 mm mortar bombs blindly into densely populated areas, killing three people including a woman and her two children.

place: Bunje (Bundje), Zirhalo (Ziralo) grouping, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: 7sur7.cd quoted the army spokesperson in the Sukola 2 Nord Sud-Kivu operational sector, named by the outlet as Sous-lieutenant Jérémie Meya, as saying that the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition tried unsuccessfully to make an incursion into Bunje on Friday 7 August and threw bombs blindly at populated areas, killing three civilians including a woman and her two children, and that the FARDC condemn these violations and reserve the right to respond.

place: Bundje, Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that the lower part of Bundje (Kalehe territory) was occupied by the Wazalendo while the upper part was controlled by AFC/M23 elements.

place: Katale, Mpanama (Kalehe territory) and Kabulungu (Kabare territory), South Kivu
statement: Ouragan.cd reported that the army said it had foiled attacks attributed to the M23 on Tuesday 11 and Wednesday 12 August 2026, and that, according to Major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region and spokesperson of the Task Force, the assaults concerned several sectors, notably Katale and Mpanama in Kalehe territory and Kabulungu in Kabare territory; the FARDC said they had reacted to contain the attacks and prevent an advance by M23 fighters.

place: Kalehe and Kabare territories (Katale, Mpanama, Kabulungu), South Kivu
statement: In an article on the fighting of 11 and 12 August 2026 in Kalehe and Kabare territories, Ouragan.cd reported that the shelling had reportedly already caused several deaths, that a woman and her two children were killed in the bombardments according to information given by the military spokesperson, and that other local sources put the toll at at least six civilians killed since the start of the week, a figure the outlet said remained to be confirmed. The article does not date the deaths.

place: localities of Buhavu chiefdom (Katale named for drone strikes), Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: ReelActu reported that, according to the Sukola 2 Nord Sud-Kivu operational sector command, at least three civilians were killed and 18 seriously wounded in bombardments on Saturday 15 August 2026 in several localities of the Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory; it said the FARDC attributed the drone and heavy-artillery bombardments to the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition and that a first unconsolidated toll of more than ten civilians killed had not been confirmed by military authorities or an independent medical source.

place: Lumbishi, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: ReelActu reported that local sources said the rebels had retaken control of Lumbishi after several hours of fighting, while clashes in Ziralo grouping opposed AFC-M23 fighters and Wazalendo.

place: Kusisa (Igali axis), Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that fighting between the FARDC supported by Wazalendo and AFC/M23 at Kusisa, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, which had intensified for three days on the Igali axis, left at least four dead including a mother and her two children, and that four Congolese soldiers were reportedly wounded.

place: Chambombo, Shanje, Lumbishi, Kavumu-Luzirantaka, Numbi, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the Congolese army said it had retaken control of several localities, notably Chambombo, Shanje, Lumbishi, Kavumu-Luzirantaka and Numbi, and that a precarious calm was reported there.

place: Ramba, Mubuku grouping (displaced from Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom), Kalehe territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that more than 815 households had fled violence in the Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory, to take refuge at Ramba in the Mubuku grouping, and were living in very difficult conditions without adequate shelter, food, drinking water or access to health care; it quoted Joseph Safari Enakesha, territorial inspector of MSCO-Kalehe, as saying the displaced had lost everything and that children, women and the elderly were sleeping without shelter, food, water or health care.

place: Hauts Plateaux of Kalehe territory (Ziralo grouping), South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that fighting reported over the previous seven days in a large part of the Hauts Plateaux of Kalehe territory compromised the resumption of classes after the Easter holidays, with schools closed, pupils displaced and teachers fleeing in several localities of the Ziralo grouping.

place: Rubarati, Ruhuha, Malimba, Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that clashes were reported on Sunday in the Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, between fighters presented by local sources as affiliated to Twirwaneho and the M23 and FARDC elements and Wazalendo militiamen; according to local sources the fighting reportedly led to the capture of several positions held until then by the FARDC and Wazalendo in the areas of Rubarati, Ruhuha and Malimba, information the outlet said could not be independently verified.

place: Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that representatives of civil society of Uvira territory said Burundian fighters of the Red Tabara group had reportedly taken part in the Bijombo fighting alongside the elements presented as Twirwaneho/M23, an alleged involvement the outlet said had not, at that stage, been independently confirmed.

place: Malimba, Rubarati, Masango-centre, Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that a member of local civil society said Malimba and Rubarati, in the Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, passed under the control of AFC/M23-Twirwaneho on Sunday 23/08/2026 after clashes against the FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundians, while the same source denied reports that Masango-centre had been taken, saying it remained under Wazalendo and Congolese army control.

place: Malimba, Rubarati, Uvira mountains, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: Kglnews, writing in Kinyarwanda, reported that, according to information from local structures, heavy fighting was reported on the morning of Sunday in the Uvira mountains, South Kivu, between Wazalendo rebels, which it described as allied with the FDLR, and fighters of the Twirwaneho group within AFC/M23, and that these rebels, mostly Banyamulenge, were said to have taken the areas of Malimba and Rubarati.

place: Masango, Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: Bwiza.com, writing in Kinyarwanda, reported that on Wednesday 26 August 2026 the village of Masango, in the Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu, was taken by Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 fighters, as shown by videos posted on social media.

place: Hauts-Plateaux d'Uvira and Fizi, South Kivu
statement: MediaCongo, relaying ACP/MCP, reported that the spokesperson of operations Sukola 2 Sud-Sud-Kivu, Sub-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, said that after the FARDC's riposte against the RDF coalition and its M23-Twirwaneho and Red Tabara allies in the Uvira and Fizi highlands, the FARDC had neutralised 23 rebels, 11 had surrendered and several weapons had been recovered.

place: Malimba, Masango, Ruhua (Ruhuha), Rubarati; Kashongo and Magunda, Uvira highlands, South Kivu
statement: MediaCongo, relaying ACP/MCP, reported that, according to a military spokesperson, the agglomerations of Malimba, Masango, Ruhua and Rubarati were now under the control of the loyalist army, and that the M23, Twirwaneho and allied fighters were forced to retreat towards Kashongo and Magunda.

date: 2026-09-01 (statement reported 2026-09-02; dates of the killings and of the discovery not given)
place: Masango, Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: MediaCongo, relaying ACP/MCP, reported that the spokesperson of operations Sukola 2 Sud-Sud-Kivu said the FARDC had discovered a mass grave at Masango where civilians killed during the occupation of that agglomeration by what he called 'the forces of evil', including Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and M23, which he said were supported by Rwanda, were said to be buried.

place: Nzibira, Lutunkulu, Luhago, Walungu territory, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that local leaders said that since 20 August the inhabitants of Nzibira and surrounding localities, in Walungu territory, had been leaving their homes after violent fighting between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo, with mass displacements also reported at Lutunkulu and Luhago, and that each camp accuses the other of being behind the clashes.

AfriquActu reported that in the locality of Luntukulu, about 75 km from Bukavu, the Congolese army supported by Wazalendo repelled on Thursday an assault by the M23 supported by the Rwandan army, and that according to local sources the fighting caused significant material damage.

The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Baudoin Ngaruye Wa Myamuro with the title 'Military Leader of the movement du Mars (M23)' and the position 'Brigadier General' (UN ref CDi.019).

The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Sultani Makenga (a.k.a. 'MAKENGA, Colonel, Sultani') with the position 'Military leader of the Mouvement du 23 Mars (M23) group operating in the Democratic Republic of the Congo'.

The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Bernard Maheshe Byamungu (a.k.a. TIGER ONE) with the positions 'Brigadier General' and 'Deputy Commander of operations and intelligence for M23', and its narrative says he was promoted in January 2023 to Brigadier for the Congolese Revolutionary Army and then appointed chief of staff and deputy to Sultani Makenga.

The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Willy Ngoma with the positions 'Major' and 'Military spokesperson for M23'.

place: North Kivu (as described in the draft)
statement: A Council of the European Union draft implementing regulation (document 6582/25, 11 March 2025, marked LIMITE) proposed a statement of reasons describing Major-General Eugène Nkubito as Commander of the 3rd Division of the Rwanda Defence Force, deployed in eastern DRC and more specifically in North Kivu province, in that position since August 2022.

place: Eastern DRC (as described in the draft)
statement: A Council of the European Union draft implementing regulation (document 6582/25, 11 March 2025, marked LIMITE) proposed a statement of reasons describing Pascal Muhizi as Brigadier-General of the Rwanda Defence Force since June 2021 and Commander of the 2nd Division of the RDF, deployed in Eastern DRC since August 2023.

place: Eastern DRC (as described in the draft)
statement: A Council of the European Union draft implementing regulation (document 6582/25, 11 March 2025, marked LIMITE) proposed a statement of reasons describing Major-General Ruki Karusisi as the commander of the Special forces of the Rwanda Defence Force, deployed in eastern DRC.

place: Chambombo, Nyalugusha village, Ziralo groupement, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local civil society, that Wazalendo of the MCDPIN group of 'Monsieur Haguma Kanyengwenye Maik Maik' and of 'Monsieur Grevisse Nsimparinga' systematically looted civilians' property at Chambombo, a village of Nyalugusha in Ziralo groupement, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe, on Monday 13 April 2026.

Amnesty International described Dominique 'Domi' Kamanzi Ndaruhutse as CMC-FDP's top commander and said he has fought with various Nyatura groups for more than 10 years and has, according to the UN Group of Experts on DRC, collaborated with the FDLR, particularly in Rutshuru's Bwito area.

place: M23-controlled zones of North Kivu and South Kivu (ceremony venue not stated in the excerpts)
statement: Deutsche Welle reported that the special session of the State examinations for self-taught secondary candidates was held on Tuesday 25 March in the zones controlled by the M23 rebels in North and South Kivu, and described Chantal Murekatete as an M23 cadre and principal adviser to the provincial governor.

The Sentry reported that Ahmad Mahmood Hassan (also known as Abwakasi) leads operations along the Lubero-Bapere-Manguredjipa axis, with headquarters in Lohoa and positions across Batike, Baredje and Bapukara.
The Sentry reported that Abwakasi reportedly commands around 600 individuals, including roughly 250 combatants since June 2024.

place: Madina camp (Mambasa territory, Ituri per The Sentry)
statement: The Sentry listed Meya Sebagala (Mzee Mayor) among key ADF leaders present along Baluku at Madina camp, citing its interviews with military intelligence, civil society representatives and local researchers in eastern DRC in January 2026.
Actualite.cd reported that since June 2024 Bapere (Lubero) has hosted two ADF groups, including the one led by Abwakasi, which it described as known for its harsh and deadly methods.

place: Asangwa, near the Lindi river, boundary of Lubero and Mambasa territories
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC announced on Tuesday 24 March that Difenda Kasibandi, one of the leaders of the ADF, had been killed in a joint FARDC-UPDF operation at Asangwa, on the outskirts of the Lindi river, on the boundary between Lubero and Mambasa territories. In its own narration, the outlet said the operation targeted a group of Islamists led by ADF chief Abouakas.

place: Uvira and the hills above it
statement: RFI said that the Wazalendo groups at Uvira are led by known and feared militia chiefs, citing among them the former FARDC member René Itongwa, the former soldier and CNPSC leader William Amuri Yakutumba, sanctioned by the UN, and John Makanaki Kasimbira, whom it described as long installed in the hills overlooking Uvira and very hostile to General Olivier Gasita, deputy commander of the 33rd military region.

In an analysis of the cohabitation of FARDC and Wazalendo at Uvira, RFI said that Wazalendo and FARDC do not always obey the same hierarchy and that the Wazalendo are groups organised in quasi-autonomous entities, each answering directly to its chief.

Kivu Morning Post reported that general 'Muzalendo' Makanaki Kasimbira, in a viral video, denounced General Gasita, saying: 'Here in Uvira, we refuse this disorder of sending us foreign faces, people who do not look like Congolese. If they have their Rwandan commanders, we will not accept them here in Uvira.'

Tumaini Africa News reported that the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, accompanied by representatives of the VDP Wazalendo, expressed gratitude to President Tshisekedi and the central government for a 325 US dollar incentive payment called 'effort de guerre', in a press briefing held in Kalundu commune, Uvira city.

Tumaini Africa News reported that the 'self-proclaimed lieutenant general' Makanaki said, in the same press briefing at Uvira, that the incentive payment was a pleasant surprise and a real comfort for the Wazalendo.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the RAD provincial coordinator, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, announced on Thursday 22 January 2026 security measures for Uvira: at a press conference he formally banned carrying firearms and bladed weapons in urban areas and the erection of illegal roadblocks by self-defence groups, demanded the immediate withdrawal of the Wazalendo from the city centre, and said that urban security now fell exclusively under the PNC and the Military Police; the outlet added that the RAD was setting up a special unit to secure the city.

Radio Okapi reported that in April 2025 the national defence minister had announced at Uvira that the local Wazalendo fighters supporting the army in defending the city now depended exclusively on the national coordinator of the Réserve armée de défense (RAD), General Padiri Bulenda.

Bunia Actualité reported that the military governor of North Kivu, Major General Évariste Kakule Somo, called on the VDP, known as Wazalendo, to show more discipline in a meeting on Friday in his liaison office in Butembo, and that John Maangayiko, spokesperson of the Wazalendo of Grand Nord-Kivu, spoke in the presence of the FARDC operations commander in the area, Brigadier General Joseph Mugisa.

The Agence Congolaise de Presse (ACP), the state news agency, reported from a Ministry of the Interior workshop at Uvira that Willian Amuri Yakutumba, whom ACP described as coordinator of the 'Wazalendo' in South Kivu province, said that not all armed persons are Wazalendo and that the Wazalendo must be distinguished from other armed groups or individuals in South Kivu; ACP also described Alexis Dunia as 'also coordinator of wazalendo'.

place: Rutshuru territory (CMC-FDP operates primarily in the Bukombo area)
statement: Amnesty International said that the top commander of the CMC-FDP is Dominique “Domi” Kamanzi Ndaruhutse, whom the European Union sanctioned in July 2024, and that he has fought with various Nyatura groups for more than 10 years and, according to the UN group of experts on DRC, collaborated with the FDLR, particularly in Rutshuru’s Bwito area.

place: Kinshasa (National Assembly Defence and Security Committee)
statement: Amnesty International said that the FARDC supports the armed groups financially and with weapons and ammunition, and that the DRC's finance minister told the National Assembly's Defence and Security Committee in December 2025 that the state pays Wazalendo groups US$4 million per month.

place: Point-Zero, Fizi territory (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported, citing residents, that the Twirwaneho armed group took the Point-Zero area in Fizi territory after heavy fighting on Wednesday and Thursday.

place: Point-Zéro, Fizi territory (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that some Congolese media confirmed government forces with Wazalendo had pushed Twirwaneho fighters out of Point-Zéro on Thursday, an area they had held for nearly two weeks; BBC said it asked the FARDC and Twirwaneho sides and neither had replied.

place: Minembwe area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: DW Swahili reported that the FARDC spokesperson for the Sokola 2 operations in South Kivu, Luteni (Lieutenant) Reagan Mbuyi, said the aircraft brought down came from Rwanda, that 'one of those helicopters from Rwanda, we shot it down', and that 13 rebel fighters of the group DW prints as Tugwaného and of M23 AFC had surrendered to the FARDC.

place: Mikenge and surroundings, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory / Minembwe highlands, South Kivu
statement: DW Swahili reported that, despite the army saying the situation had calmed, local sources in the war zone said fighting began again that day in the early morning at Mikenge and neighbouring areas.

place: Minembwe, Fizi territory (Hauts Plateaux), South Kivu
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that Mufashi, a civil-society leader in the Minembwe area, said that besides essential goods no longer reaching residents, international aid organisations that used to take medicines to the area were now not allowed to get there.

place: Minembwe, Fizi territory (Hauts Plateaux), South Kivu
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Tuesday residents of Minembwe protested against what they called the closure of all roads linking them to Uvira, which they attributed to government and Burundian forces.

place: Roads from Minembwe toward Uvira, South Kivu
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Burundian army admitted it had closed the roads, aiming to 'protect Uvira and the Burundian border', and asked residents in Minembwe to 'separate themselves from the enemies' there.

place: Minembwe and surroundings, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Twirwaneho group announced it controlled Minembwe and its surroundings and, for the first time, confirmed it had allied itself with AFC/M23, according to a person in Minembwe.

place: Point-Zéro, Baruta hill and Isumo, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Umuryango.rw reported that Twirwaneho took Point-Zéro on the morning of 16 January 2026, a day after taking other key points in Fizi territory including Baruta hill and shooting down a drone, and that Twirwaneho's leadership said the DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo and FDLR forces fled toward Mulima and Mutambala.

place: Mikenke (Mikenge) camp, Minembwe area, South Kivu
statement: BTN Rwanda reported that FARDC launched an air strike in Minembwe, and that politician Moïse Nyarugabo said the attack was launched on a camp in the Mikenke area on the morning of 12 December 2025.

place: Minembwe area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: BTN Rwanda reported that the MRDP-Twirwaneho group said that closing the paths residents of Minembwe use to reach markets and clinics was meant to kill them because of their Banyamulenge ethnicity.

Kigali Shows reported that Colonel Joseph Nganzo Olikwa Tipi, deputy commander of the 12th Brigade of the FARDC at Minembwe, was killed at Mikenke on Tuesday 3 March 2026 in fighting between government forces with allied groups and Twirwaneho with AFC/M23; it said FARDC leadership had not publicly commented.

Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that Burundian army non-commissioned officer Ferdinand Nyabenda, nicknamed Bikorwa, fell three months earlier at Rugezi in Fizi territory and that his family was not informed.

place: Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories (highlands), South Kivu
statement: UN News (Swahili) reported that OCHA, in a statement quoting its humanitarian partners, said that since the middle of July fighting in the Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga areas had caused more than 48,000 people to leave their homes.

place: Highland areas of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
statement: UN News (Swahili), citing OCHA, reported that the health sector in the affected areas was badly affected by the destruction of health facilities and the departure of health workers, and that since January more than 80 people wounded by fighting and explosive remnants of war had been unable to get the treatment they needed.

place: Point Zero, Rusanguku, Tuwetuwe, Mikenge, Minembwe and surroundings, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: DW Swahili reported that Jacques Alimasi, described as the supervisor (Msimamizi) of the Fizi territory civil-society organisation, said fighting continued in Fizi, citing the previous day in Point zero village and also the villages of Rusanguku, Tuwetuwe, Mikenge, Minembwe and villages around Minembwe, and that killings were increasing.

place: Mikenke (Mikenge) general hospital, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, moved to Gipupu (Kipupu), South Kivu
statement: Minembwe Capital News (a Banyamulenge community outlet) reported that on Thursday 22 May 2025 the headquarters of the Mikenke hospitals was moved to Gipupu; it said the reason was not clearly known but that the administration described it as security reasons.

place: Lusenda refugee camp, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that, according to sources at Lusenda camp, the police commissioner in charge of the camp, Masumbuko Lutombo, personally directs recruitment operations aimed mainly at young Burundian refugees, to integrate them into the Wazalendo armed groups.

place: Lusenda refugee camp, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that at Lusenda in South Kivu the sick had had no access to medicines for six months; it said IDAV, a partner of the UN refugee agency (HCR), indicated that stocks of medicines were at Kalemie and being forwarded.

place: Lusenda refugee camp, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that, according to a source among the refugees at Lusenda camp, some women were engaging in prostitution to feed their children amid famine in the camp.

place: Irumba and Rugezi, south of Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Umuryango.rw reported that Twirwaneho spokesperson Kamasa Ndakize Welcome announced on 5 August 2025 that attacks by FDLR, FARDC and another group, Mai Mai Ngomanzito, began at Irumba and Rugezi in the south of Minembwe, and that Twirwaneho confirmed Burundian forces took no part in that day's attacks.

Bwiza reported, citing 'various reports' coming from Goma, that the drone attack launched on Goma by the forces of the DRC government was aimed at, among others, former president Joseph Kabila Kabange; it said the attack of 11 March struck the mainly residential Himbi area near Lake Kivu, where residents said they heard two explosions at dawn.

Umuryango.rw reported that on Thursday 7 May Congolese government forces launched a drone attack at Muja in Nyiragongo territory, where AFC/M23 soldiers were, that the explosion was heard in Goma city, and that, in the outlet's words, no one was killed or injured.

place: Nyanzale and Kiyeye, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: BBC Gahuza reported, citing members of Rutshuru civil society, that heavy fighting on Saturday and Sunday between M23 and Wazalendo fighters at Nyanzale (Rutshuru territory) left civilians dead and others fleeing; civil society member Kambele said he had learned of at least three civilians dead near Nyanzale, and BBC wrote that Congolese media reported that a child was among those who died in the Sunday evening fighting.

BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 said the new Human Rights Watch report accusing it of killing at least 140 civilians, mostly Hutu, is 'a lie' with 'no foundation'; in a statement by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka it said the HRW and UN allegations are politically motivated, and that HRW deliberately avoided mentioning armed groups it says work with Kinshasa, including FDLR, Nyatura, PARECO and Wazalendo.

place: Goma, North Kivu (and attacks on schools and hospitals, place not specified)
statement: UN News Kiswahili reported that a report prepared by the Fact-Finding Mission (FFM) of the UN human rights office said all parties failed to protect civilians adequately during the fighting, in particular when M23 and RDF took the city of Goma at the end of January 2025, and during attacks on schools and hospitals.

place: M23-controlled areas of North Kivu and South Kivu
statement: UN News Kiswahili reported that the UN human rights office Fact-Finding Mission (FFM) report said M23 members committed sexual violence, mainly gang rape, and other forms of sexual violence including sexual slavery; women and girls were mainly targeted, but men, boys and people UN News Kiswahili calls 'watu wa jinsia moja' (literally 'people of the same sex') were also victims, including in detention.

place: North Kivu and South Kivu front-line withdrawal areas (not specified in the excerpt)
statement: UN News Kiswahili reported that the OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission found a pattern of widespread sexual violence, especially rape and gang rape of women and girls, and looting by FARDC and Wazalendo members as they withdrew from the front line in January and February.

place: Mugunga and Rusayo groupement, west of Goma, North Kivu
statement: Umuryango.rw reported that in the night of 21 to 22 July 2025 Wazalendo fighters, suspected to have come from Virunga Park, attacked the Mugunga area and Rusayo groupement, that gunfire was heard for about three hours, and that AFC/M23 pushed the Wazalendo fighters back.

Umuryango.rw reported that Manzi Willy, whom it described as the governor of North Kivu appointed by AFC/M23, said on 22 July that their fighters continue to destroy everything that could disturb the security of Goma, and that when AFC/M23 took Goma the opposing forces had hidden guns, ammunition and bombs among the population, which the alliance uncovers day by day.

place: Buramba (Binza groupement, Bwisha chiefdom) and Kiwanja-Ishasha road (Katoro, near Katwiguru; Cabafu), Rutshuru territory
statement: Bwiza reported that residents of Buramba village (Binza groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory) continue to complain of insecurity caused by Wazalendo and FDLR rebels who harass them, and that, it is said, those often harassed are accused of working with AFC/M23; citing Kivu Morning Post, it said these armed rebels also attack users of the Kiwanja-Ishasha road at places such as Katoro, near Katwiguru, and Cabafu, where the latest attack took place on Sunday 8 March 2026.

place: Bumbasha, Karambi, Chahemba (Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru), near Mweso
statement: Bwiza, relaying Radio Okapi, reported that heavy fighting took place all morning on Monday 12 January between AFC/M23 fighters and CMC Wazalendo in many villages of Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru territory, that no toll had been announced, and that the fighting started at Bumbasha, a few kilometres from Mweso, before spreading to Karambi and Chahemba, sending hundreds of residents fleeing to nearby villages and to Mweso centre.

place: Munguli (Kihondo groupement) and Kikuro (Tongo groupement), Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Umunota reported that heavy fighting between AFC/M23 fighters and Wazalendo fighters of the Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC) took place from dawn on Monday, mainly at Munguli in Kihondo groupement and at Kikuro in Tongo groupement, according to information from the area.

place: Birambizo and Karambi (Bukombo groupement) and Kihondo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
statement: Umunota reported that on Saturday and Sunday heavy fighting took place at Birambizo and Karambi in Bukombo groupement and in Kihondo groupement, that according to information from the area it made hundreds of residents flee their homes, and that on Sunday at least six houses were burned in Karambi town and its surroundings.

Umuryango.rw reported that an announcement of 9 April 2026 by the AFC/M23-appointed governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto, named Kisuba Ngabo Désiré mayor of Goma in place of Julien Katembo Ndalieni, who was made head of Lubero territory, and named Nshimiyimana Juvénal, formerly in charge of mobilisation and recruitment of new fighters in AFC/M23, deputy mayor of Goma.

Umuryango.rw reported that on 11 May CADECO, a bank opened by AFC/M23 after the Congolese government closed banks in the areas the group controls, opened two counters in Goma at a ceremony led by the AFC/M23 deputy governor of North Kivu for economy and finance, Shadrack Amani.

place: At least two hospitals in Goma, North Kivu
statement: UN News Kiswahili reported that OCHA had reported that armed men raided at least two hospitals in Goma, the capital of North Kivu, and abducted several patients.

place: Tchanzu training centre, Rutshuru, North Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Sunday 8 February 2026 AFC-M23 presented 7,532 new commandos who had finished military training at Tchanzu (Rutshuru, North Kivu), a ceremony it described as marking a new stage in the structure of the ARC (Jeshi la Mapinduzi la Kongo), the armed wing of the movement led by General Sultani Makenga.

SOS Médias Burundi quoted Major General Sultani Makenga, AFC-M23 military coordinator, as saying to the new troops: 'From today you have become soldiers of the ARC, an army that emerged to liberate the people, our country is run by incompetent people living in Kinshasa'.

place: Murambi (north of Goma) and a sports ground used as an open prison, Goma
statement: DW Kiswahili reported that by the end of May hundreds of men were sitting on black volcanic gravel in the streets of Murambi, north of Goma, guarded by M23 fighters; that some Goma residents said people were arrested for minor reasons such as wearing dirty clothes or not shaving, many being gathered in a sports ground then turned into an open prison; and that those not cleared by evidence considered credible were taken to private places of detention.
DW Kiswahili reported that Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said residents of Goma continue to face suffering.
DW Kiswahili reported that civilians and former government fighters were forcibly registered, and that M23 announced it had gained 7,000 new members by September.
DW Kiswahili reported that in October the group began appointing its own magistrates, but that observers said the rebels' court system was not fair.

BBC Gahuza reported that M23 said the more than 2,500 people who died in the recent fighting in Goma were government soldiers (FARDC) and Wazalendo; that Bertrand Bisimwa, one of the leaders of M23, said no family in Goma was in mourning because of those dead; and that he said the bodies removed from the streets and buried were those of FARDC soldiers and their collaborators, including Wazalendo, FDLR, European mercenaries and Burundian forces, who died in battle.

BBC Gahuza reported that the UN humanitarian office OCHA-RDC said at least 2,000 bodies had already been buried and about 900 others were in the morgues of various hospitals in Goma, and that the UN said on Monday that at least 900 people had been killed and more than 2,800 wounded in the fighting, with hospitals still struggling to treat all the wounded.

BBC Gahuza reported that M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, replying on X to the Human Rights Watch report, said that report and the recent Amnesty International report are 'propaganda tools working for the Kinshasa authorities', and cited a report published by M23 the previous week saying that only 874 fighters died in the fighting to take Goma.

BBC Gahuza reported that Patrick Muyaya, spokesperson of the Kinshasa government, had recently said that more than 2,000 bodies were still in the streets of Goma needing burial, and that he accused Rwandan forces and M23 of killing civilians in the recent fighting in Goma and its surroundings.

place: Katindo and other Goma neighbourhoods (Camp Katindo, Avenue du Commandant Belge, Avenue Kasika, Avenue Mulongwe)
statement: BBC Gahuza reported that a Human Rights Watch report said M23 killed at least 21 civilians in Goma in February whose deaths it could confirm, with evidence of many more; that on 22 February at least three pickup trucks carrying M23 fighters went to different parts of Goma and the fighters killed seven people in Katindo, with 11 more bodies including a boy found later near a construction site; that the next day the fighters rounded people up to force them into M23 and killed three who tried to escape; and that three health workers told HRW more than 50 bodies were removed from the Kasika area between 22 and 23 February.

place: Kanyaruchinya and Lushagara displacement camps, outskirts of Goma
statement: BBC Gahuza reported that displacement camps on the outskirts of Goma, which had held hundreds of thousands of people, were bare ground after M23 fighters took the city; an independent journalist in Goma who visited the Kanyaruchinya and Lushagara camps said almost all the tents were down; it was not clearly known whether the remaining displaced people had gone home voluntarily or by force; and Dany Kalume of Goma civil society said many had returned to areas of Rutshuru and Masisi controlled by M23 and that M23 had provided vehicles the previous week to take back those remaining in some of the camps.

UN News Kiswahili reported that the UN Special Rapporteur on human rights defenders, Mary Lawlor, said she had received credible reports of human rights defenders held incommunicado, forcibly disappeared and tortured in Rutshuru and Masisi, North Kivu, and that about six defenders were reported to have disappeared after trying to flee Goma after the city was taken by M23.

UN News Kiswahili reported that Mary Lawlor, UN Special Rapporteur on human rights defenders, said a defender had recently told her that M23 rebels had drawn up a list of human rights defenders to be arrested in the areas they controlled.

Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa told residents of Goma that, a year after the city's administration was installed, everything was now in order, that the war in the city was completely over, and that what remained was to continue development and to liberate all of Congo.

Umuryango.rw reported that in the early morning of 11 March drones of the DRC army fired on residents' homes in the Himbi area, killing three civilians including the Frenchwoman Karine Buisset, who worked for UNICEF.

Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 condemned the attack and said it was not right for the international community to keep silent while the DRC government deliberately violates the ceasefire agreement signed in Doha, Qatar.

Umuryango.rw reported that on the morning of 12 March 2026 many Goma residents gathered in a protest against the drone attack launched on the city by the forces of the DRC, asking AFC/M23 to liberate the whole country, after an invitation from civil society, and that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the protesters asked AFC/M23 to remove Félix Tshisekedi's government throughout the DRC.

Umuryango.rw reported that on the morning of 22 December 2025 residents of Goma and neighbouring areas took part in a protest against AFC/M23's withdrawal from the city of Uvira, and that AFC/M23 fighters had left Uvira on 17 and 18 December after about a week there.

place: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
statement: Rwandan Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo said, in reaction to a Human Rights Watch report, that 'the RDF is not AFC/M23' and that any proper investigation requires impartiality, access to where events happen, solid evidence, respect for the law and not announcing conclusions in advance or putting calls for sanctions first, according to Igihe.

place: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
statement: Igihe reported that Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo, in a post on X, dismissed the Human Rights Watch report as part of a 30-year pattern of anonymous claims, no site visits or forensics, and 'sanctions first and investigation later'.

place: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
statement: According to Igihe, Makolo said that HRW itself had stated that Kinshasa arms, supports and works closely with the FDLR, Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army, which she said made HRW unable to take on an impartial investigation.

Igihe reported that the Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda said that no HRW investigator set foot at the places named in the report, and that there were no visits, no exhumations for investigation and no laboratory tests.
According to Kigali, as reported by Igihe, HRW's own report acknowledges that the Congolese army has supported armed groups opposed to M23, including the FDLR.

Igihe reported that the Rwandan statement cited passages in the HRW report saying that Congolese authorities armed, financed and coordinated operations with Wazalendo militias and that government support for such groups contributed to human rights violations.
Igihe wrote that the HRW report also states that the Congolese army and those allied with it carried out acts of abuse, killing, rape and unlawful detention in the outskirts of Goma.

According to Igihe, the Rwandan government said HRW claims to have satellite images showing killings 'carried out by Rwandan forces and M23', with features resembling graves, but that HRW cannot confirm whether they are graves or other objects.
