Rwanda's Office of the Government Spokesperson said, according to Igihe, that 'alleged M23 conduct cannot be treated as RDF conduct' and accused HRW of 'selective accountability', saying it focused primarily on Rwanda and M23 and paid insufficient attention to abuses by Congolese government forces and their allies.

Igihe reported that a 78-page HRW report published on 10 June alleges that Rwandan military forces and the M23 rebel movement carried out large-scale forced recruitment and abusive detention of captured combatants and civilians in North and South Kivu between mid-2024 and December 2025.

Makolo said, according to Igihe, that the sustainable solution to the conflict is to implement the Washington agreement and impartial mediation aimed at ending the war and promoting regional cooperation; the English edition quotes her as saying the Washington peace accords remain 'the path forward'.
Igihe reported that Rwanda's statement highlighted the FDLR as a key security threat and accused HRW of failing to adequately examine its role and its links to Congolese government forces.

Igihe reported that the Rwandan Office of the Government Spokesperson said HRW had not named the Congolese or Wazalendo individuals for whom it was calling for sanctions, and quoted it as saying 'HRW strongly condemns Rwanda and M23, while the support Kinshasa gives to violent armed groups is described in a deceptive/vague way'.

Igihe reported that in May 2026 AFC/M23 accused Human Rights Watch of defaming it, publishing falsehoods and ignoring the truth, in response to an HRW report released on 14 May that accuses its fighters of killing civilians in Uvira city, raping women and abducting people between December 2025 and January 2026.
Igihe reported that AFC/M23 said the DRC army continues to work with the FDLR, which HRW does not want to address in its reports, and that HRW's bias makes the organisation lose credibility.

place: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
statement: Igihe reported that Rwandan Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo said on X on 14 May 2026 that 'HRW has a way of working and Rwanda is always its yardstick showing it has worked well'.

Igihe reported that Makolo was criticising an HRW report released on 13 May that accuses Rwandan forces and M23 fighters of killing civilians, abducting them and raping women in Uvira city from 10 December 2025 to 17 January 2026.
Igihe reported that the Rwandan government has often told the international community that none of its troops are in eastern DRC and that it only put defensive measures on the border.
Igihe wrote that in January 2025 armed units including the FDLR fired into Rubavu town while fighting M23 in Goma, and that many of the shells fired were neutralised by Rwandan forces.

Igihe wrote that HRW explained that those it interviewed included Burundian and DRC officials including soldiers, and argued that this makes the report highly doubtful because they are the ones fighting M23 in areas including Uvira.

Igihe reported that the DRC army coalition was accused of shooting at a civilian plane carrying medicines and food to Minembwe commune on the morning of 27 August 2026; MRDP-Twirwaneho officer Colonel Fidèle Rugabo said the plane was hit by a shell from a gun on the ground as it reached the Bikuba area.
Colonel Fidèle Rugabo of MRDP-Twirwaneho said, according to Igihe: 'MRDP strongly condemned the shooting down of a civilian plane that was carrying medicines and food'.

ReelActu reported that a plane was shot down on Thursday near the Minembwe aerodrome in the Fizi highlands, during the mission of the expanded Joint Verification Mechanism (MCVE+), and that the circumstances of its destruction and the nature of its cargo were the subject of opposing versions.

ReelActu reported that Rugabo Fidèle, a member of the Twirwaneho-M23 coalition, publicly confirmed the destruction of the plane and accused the FARDC of shooting down 'a civil aircraft carrying medicines and food', calling the incident a 'provocation' that came two days after the MCVE+ team left Minembwe.
ReelActu reported that Congolese security sources maintain the plane was carrying out a resupply mission for rebel positions in the highlands.

ReelActu reported that no independent source had confirmed whether the plane was civil or military, or its exact cargo, and that the Congolese authorities had not yet published a communiqué detailing the circumstances of the operation.

LSi Africa reported that Fizi territory administrator Sammy Kalonji Badibanga said the plane came from Rwanda and was carrying soldiers, equipment and food, while sources linked to Twirwaneho-AFC/M23 described it as a civil aircraft linking Bukavu to Minembwe with medicines and equipment on board and two crew members.

Kivu Morning Post wrote that a civil plane carrying medicines was shot down near Minembwe on Thursday, and that the Fizi territory administrator 'under the Kinshasa regime' claimed the attack, saying the plane had been shot down by the FARDC.
Igihe reported that the plane was shot down after the international body in charge of ceasefire monitoring (EJVM+) visited Minembwe on 25 August and assessed the effects of the attacks.

According to Igihe, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, FDLR and foreign mercenary forces began attacking Point-Zero, Nyaruhinga and Mukoko in Minembwe at about seven in the morning and that the DRC coalition was using combat drones and heavy weapons.
Igihe reported that AFC/M23 also accused the DRC government forces of attacks in areas of Walungu territory in South Kivu, including Nzibira, Kishadu and Chulwe, and in Katoyi in Masisi territory.
Igihe, citing the SOS Médias website of the Burundians, reported that the Kamenge military hospital alone was housing 87 wounded Burundian soldiers.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that, in recent days, more than a hundred wounded had been reported, 87 of them admitted to the Kamenge military hospital, north of Bujumbura, and that Burundian authorities were keeping silent about the real losses.

SOS Médias Burundi reported, quoting a journalist at the Kamenge military hospital, that lack of beds forced some patients to share the same bed and that 'a single bed can accommodate up to three patients' because the two emergency wards were full.

Igihe reported that other wounded had been sent to other hospitals including Tanganyika Care Polyclinic, and that many Bujumbura hospitals were severely overcrowded, with up to three patients on one bed.

Igihe reported, on the basis of unspecified information ('hari amakuru avuga'), that because of defeat the Burundian army leadership had asked its soldiers to return home quickly to avoid losing more lives in the war in the DRC.

Igihe reported that from the morning of 8 December 2025 many Burundian troops, Imbonerakure and Wazalendo were fleeing from Uvira city to Bujumbura, and that residents who saw them said they looked exhausted.

Igihe reported that the Burundian army sent many soldiers to the border to receive those fleeing, to keep calm, and that those coming from the DRC were being disarmed before continuing to where they were lodged.

Igihe reported that Burundian, DRC and Wazalendo forces were being overpowered because they had lost many areas, and that AFC/M23 fighters who left Kamanyola the previous week had reached Sange, about 30 kilometres towards Uvira city.

place: Minembwe area (Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories)
statement: Igihe reported that Burundi had sent nearly 20 thousand soldiers ('ibihumbi 20') to South Kivu, many of whom went to areas around Minembwe in Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, closing the routes by which Banyamulenge went to markets and clinics.

Igihe reported that it is said ('biravugwa') that Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani, commander of the eighth battalion of the Burundian forces fighting in eastern DRC, was shot dead by AFC/M23; the news began circulating on the evening of 5 December 2025, with reports that he fell in fighting at Luvungi that killed many other Burundian soldiers fighting beside the FARDC.

Igihe reported that Pacifique Nininahazwe, head of FOCODE, said on X that Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani (SS1564), commander of the eighth battalion of Burundian forces in the DRC (TAFOC), was shot dead the previous night with his three guards, and that he was the highest-ranking FDNB soldier killed in this war.
Igihe reported that Lt Col Minani was formerly of the old Burundian army (Ex FAB) and had been promoted to the rank of Lieutenant Colonel in July of the year of writing.

place: Lubarika, Mitambili, Katogota, Luvungi, Sange (Uvira territory)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that among the Burundian soldiers killed since 1 December in the localities of Lubarika, Mitambili, Katogota, Luvungi and Sange was Lieutenant-Colonel Athanase Minani, the highest-ranking Burundian officer killed since the start of the official intervention in the DRC.
Igihe reported that neither the Burundian army nor AFC/M23 had confirmed the death of the senior Burundian soldier (Lt Col Minani).

Igihe wrote that information reaching it said AFC/M23 had learned that DRC, Burundian and Wazalendo forces were about to attack it at Kamanyola and decided to fire first; a person close to AFC/M23's top leadership told it that the explosions heard on the morning of 2 December were fired by AFC/M23 fighters and had seriously shaken the DRC government coalition.

Igihe reported that, on the same day as the explosions it dates to the morning of 2 December, DRC and Burundian forces fired on Kamanyola centre, held by AFC/M23 for nearly 10 months, with shells destroying civilian homes and infrastructure; three civilians died and others were injured.

Igihe reported that since the morning of 5 December 2025 DRC, Burundian and Wazalendo forces were attacking areas of Uvira territory including Katogota, Kamanyola and Luvungi groupement, and that shells falling on Luvungi made many residents flee to areas such as Sange, Runingu, Ndolera and Uvira city.

place: Kamanyola, Katogota, Luvungi (Uvira territory); shelling alleged from Burundian territory
statement: Bertrand Bisimwa, Deputy Leader of AFC/M23 in charge of political activities, said, according to Igihe, that Burundian forces inside Burundi were shelling heavily populated areas of Kamanyola, Katogota and Luvungi, causing the deaths of innocent people including children and destroying houses, schools, churches and markets.
Igihe reported that the fighting continued after Rwanda and the DRC signed a peace agreement on 4 December 2025, which AFC/M23 said does not concern it.

place: Lubero territory: Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi, Kipese; Alimbongo, Kirumba, Kanyabayonga
statement: Igihe reported that earlier in the week of the article, DRC media outlets reported that AFC/M23 was withdrawing fighters from areas it listed as Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese and relocating them to Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga, and that the move was prompted by pressure from the United States government.

According to Igihe, North Kivu Governor Erasto Bahati (AFC/M23 administration) dismissed the reports of withdrawal in a statement, saying the activities along the front were regular troop rotations within AFC/M23 and that the rumours were fuelled by social media and the Kinshasa government.

Igihe reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye said in an interview with Jeune Afrique published on 10 May 2026 that the closure of the Gatumba and Vugizo border crossings with the DRC was linked to the proximity of M23 fighters near Burundi's borders, alleging that M23 operates with Rwanda's backing.

According to Igihe, Ndayishimiye said that Burundi considers the presence of M23 fighters near its borders a security concern and expressed hope that the Washington peace agreement would increase pressure to end the tensions.

Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye maintained that Burundian troops were sent to the DRC to assist Congolese forces against their enemies rather than to defend Burundi itself, under regional arrangements that assigned South Kivu as Burundi's operational zone.

Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye argued that fighting continued despite regional efforts because some countries failed to contain the conflict, and that only Uganda and Burundi remained actively engaged, with Burundian troops operating under the directives of the Congolese army.

Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye repeated accusations that Rwanda supports RED Tabara, a group Burundi describes as terrorist, and that Rwanda has consistently denied this, insisting it does not support any group seeking to destabilize Burundi.

Igihe reported that, asked about Rwanda's accusation that Burundi collaborates with the FDLR, Ndayishimiye said he had asked President Paul Kagame for intelligence on FDLR positions and that Burundi would attack the group if given such information.

Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye acknowledged that Congolese forces work with the FDLR, but argued that Burundian troops operate separately under Congolese command structures and do not mix with those groups.

Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye proposed coordinated military action by Rwanda, the DRC, Burundi and Uganda against armed groups in the region, saying this could reassure Rwanda about its security concerns.

Igihe reported that Burundi had deployed more than 20,000 troops to South Kivu under bilateral agreements with the DRC, and that the deployment was reduced in early December 2025 after M23 fighters captured several areas in the Ruzizi Plain and the city of Uvira.

Igihe described TAFOC as the Burundian bilateral contingent in the DRC, which began operations in South Kivu in 2022 alongside Congolese forces against armed groups including RED Tabara, FOREBU, FNL and Twirwaneho.

Igihe, relaying an AFC/M23 communiqué, reported that seven people died, three were seriously injured and one lightly injured on Saturday 12 September 2026 when an explosive device, which the communiqué describes as planted by those AFC/M23 called enemies, went off at Jomba, Gikoro, Rugunga village in Rutshuru, after a child found it in a field and began handling it.

Igihe reported that AFC/M23 expressed deep sorrow, condoled with the families, and asked residents of liberated areas to follow instructions on avoiding explosives still in the ground, not to touch, move or try to dismantle anything they suspect may be a bomb.

Igihe reported that DRC soldiers and fighters of the Wazalendo alliance exchanged fire in Uvira city overnight, with heavy gunfire (AK-47 and machine guns) heard from eight in the evening on 5 September 2025, because of a disagreement.

Igihe reported, on unspecified information ('amakuru avuga'), that the Wazalendo fighters who exchanged fire with the DRC army belonged to the armed group led by 'Général' John Makanaki, which has operated in South Kivu for a long time.

Igihe reported that since 2 September 2025 Wazalendo had been in a major protest in Uvira demanding that DRC Brig Gen Gasita Olivier leave the city because, they claimed, he is Rwandan, doubting his nationality because he is a Munyamulenge; Wazalendo closed the main road, halting all economic activity.

Igihe reported that on 5 September 2025 the acting mayor of Uvira, Kifara Kapenda Kik'v, led a meeting to calm tensions attended by Wazalendo leaders including Makanaki and 'Général' William Amur Yakutumba, but it achieved nothing as the protest continued.
Wazalendo leader William Yakutumba said at the meeting held in Uvira, according to Igihe: 'That leader who was sent here, called Gen Gasita, we do not want him here in Uvira'.

Igihe reported that Yakutumba insisted Brig Gen Gasita must leave Uvira, and that Makanaki said that if the soldier had not left by 8 September his fighters would close the DRC-Burundi border and the Uvira port on Lake Tanganyika.

FARDC spokesperson Maj Gen Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa, according to Igihe, had asked Wazalendo to accept Brig Gen Gasita, explaining that he had not betrayed the country and had been appointed by the Head of State; the fighters refused and asked for his replacement.

place: Kipese, Katondi, Munyakandomi, Vulera, Kirumba (Lubero territory)
statement: Igihe reported that on the morning of 25 September 2025 various media reported that M23 had deployed additional troops and weapons in Lubero territory to strengthen control over Kipese, Katondi, Munyakandomi, Vulera and Kirumba.
Igihe reported that in February 2025 M23 captured the Kitsombiro area in Lubero after intense clashes with the FARDC.

Igihe reported that M23 had also reinforced its forces in the localities of Rusamambu and Bukumbirwa, which it read as signalling plans to extend control to other parts of what it called South Kivu Province.

Igihe reported that the group had recruited 7,437 new fighters who had undergone six months of military training at the Rumangabo base in North Kivu, including former FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo members who joined M23 after the capture of Goma and Bukavu.

AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a statement on Thursday 3 April 2025, according to Igihe, that the group had repositioned its forces in Walikale and surroundings, and warned that if Kinshasa regime forces persisted in provocations or attacked civilians in liberated areas or AFC/M23 positions, the goodwill gesture would be cancelled and 'we will eliminate the threat at its source'.

place: Walikale; Kigoma airstrip; Ngora, Kisima, Mubanda
statement: Igihe reported that M23 took control of Walikale on 19 March 2025, notably seizing the Kigoma airstrip, after conquering several surrounding localities including Ngora, Kisima and Mubanda.

Igihe reported that after taking Walikale the rebel group announced its withdrawal, describing it as 'a choice aimed at creating a climate conducive to political dialogue', and called on local authorities and residents to guarantee security in the region.

Igihe reported that the Congolese government and the M23 were to begin direct talks on 9 April 2025 in Doha, Qatar, the first direct negotiation between the two parties since the rebels took two provincial capitals.

Igihe reported that a meeting initially planned in Angola on 18 March was abruptly cancelled after M23 withdrew in protest against European Union sanctions on its leaders, and that diplomatic efforts resumed after an unexpected mid-March meeting between Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame in Doha.

Igihe reported that the AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto, changed the leadership of Goma city, and that a notice of 9 April 2026 named Kisuba Ngabo Désiré, until then deputy mayor, mayor of Goma, replacing Julien Katembo Ndalieni, who became head of Lubero territory.
Igihe reported that Nshimiyimana Juvénal, who had been in charge of mobilisation and recruiting new fighters in AFC/M23, was named deputy mayor of Goma.

Igihe reported that, in the same reshuffle, Katembo Isevisya, who had been in the Lubero territory leadership, and Radjabu Kwizera Elie were given deputy burgomaster posts, Radjabu Kwizera Elie as deputy burgomaster of Karisimbi commune.
Katembo said in an interview with Igihe in January 2026 that Goma was now safe and that all activities, including trade, were going better than before.
Igihe reported that AFC/M23 took the city of Goma on 27 January 2025 and then installed new officials to bring it back on track in security, welfare and infrastructure projects.

place: Mikenke, Point-Zéro, Makombo, Mikalati, Gipupu, Murambya, Mwenga (around Minembwe)
statement: Igihe reported that MDRP-Twirwaneho had for days been saying that many Burundian troops were deployed around Minembwe, including Mikenke, Point-Zéro, Makombo, Mikalati, Gipupu, Murambya and Mwenga, to starve the Banyamulenge by closing the roads they use to go to buy supplies.

Igihe reported that during heavy fighting in the Ruzizi Plain since the start of the previous week many Burundian troops left areas they controlled such as Sange, Runingo, Kiliba and Uvira town, fleeing along with the DRC forces, Wazalendo and the FDLR.

Igihe reported ('bivugwa') that the Burundian troops left these areas on an order from their top command because they had lost many soldiers in the war, including one of their leaders, Lt Col Athanase Minani, and that many were taken prisoner.
Igihe reported that Wazalendo groups affirm that some Burundian soldiers fled with them into the Itombwe forest, where they were going to regroup to attack various areas controlled by AFC/M23.

Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis, Vice-President of MRDP-Twirwaneho, told Igihe on 11 December 2025 that Burundian troops were still numerous in the high areas around Minembwe and said: 'The Burundian troops are still where they were. Even now Burundians are fighting the self-defending residents there at Irango, at Ndondo'.

place: areas bordering Minembwe; Mikalati military camp
statement: Igihe reported that on 6 December Burundian troops took hostage nearly 100 civilians who had gone shopping in areas bordering Minembwe, and that Twirwaneho explained that some were taken to the Mikalati military camp and others to an unknown place; Nkurunziza said the troops had since released these civilians.

Nkurunziza of MRDP-Twirwaneho said, according to Igihe, that the Burundian troops had disgraced their country in this war, that their best option was to go home, and that otherwise they would be removed by force from the high hills around Minembwe.

Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu, AFC/M23 deputy chief of staff, arrived in Uvira city on 10 December 2025 and asked the Burundian troops still in the high hills of South Kivu to come down and go home in peace, saying 'We have no problem with the Burundians because we are neighbours'.

Igihe reported that FARDC's military spokesperson in South Kivu, Lt Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said in a communiqué that FARDC had been controlling Minembwe since the night of 17 June 2026, that Twirwaneho fighters were fleeing towards Walungu territory, and that FARDC had captured many MRDP-Twirwaneho and M23 fighters, weapons, ammunition and other military equipment.

Igihe reported that MRDP-Twirwaneho Vice-President Alexis Mugisha Nkurunziza said the claim that DRC forces had taken Minembwe was false, and that Col Fidèle Rugabo affirmed that the group still controls Minembwe, saying 'The lies are many. Up to now we are still in Minembwe... Long live M23'.

Igihe reported that MRDP-Twirwaneho President Dr Freddy Kaniki Rukema told journalists at a press conference in Goma on 18 June that DRC government forces had intensified attacks in Minembwe, that attacks on civilians there had increased and that the international community knew but was doing nothing; asked whether Minembwe had been taken, he said they had not done it and would not.

Igihe reported, citing reliable information from South Kivu, that despite the difficult mountainous terrain M23 fighters had reached Minembwe to join Twirwaneho in protecting the security of residents.

Igihe reported that Burundian troops had also reached the front to help the DRC forces take Minembwe commune, but that available information says they had recently lost many soldiers, some of whose bodies were loaded onto a truck and taken to Bujumbura.

Igihe reported that on 25 December 2025 Wazalendo fighters appeared in Makobola centre (Fizi territory) saying they had driven AFC/M23 out, and that their spokesperson, named Winston Makufuli, said 'People should remain calm, we have taken Makobola back. We thank President Félix Tshisekedi who sent FARDC troops to protect our country's security'.

Igihe reported, on 'reliable information' and a resident's account, that AFC/M23 left Makobola without fighting, as 25 December was calm and residents were celebrating Christmas; a Makobola resident said that in the afternoon ("saa munani z'amanywa") they saw the fighters heading towards Uvira with their luggage and that FARDC and Wazalendo arrived a few minutes later.

Igihe reported that on 24 December there was heavy fighting in various parts of Makobola centre, caused by drone and heavy-weapon attacks launched by DRC forces and Wazalendo, at Makobola 1, Makobola 2, Kiringi, Kirambi and elsewhere, causing many residents to flee to safer areas including Uvira city.
Igihe reported that on the morning of 26 December DRC forces and Wazalendo fired on Kalundu port on Lake Tanganyika, by Uvira city, using war drones.
Igihe reported that AFC/M23 affirms that by 18 December all its fighters had left Uvira city, to build confidence in the Doha talks with the DRC government.

Igihe reported that AFC/M23 delegates returned to the Doha talks on 12 December, but the DRC government refused to send its delegates there, complaining that the alliance's fighters had taken Uvira city on 9 December.

Igihe reported that Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, President of the Council of Ministers of Togo and the mediator appointed by the African Union, made a visit of a few hours to Kinshasa on 22 December to discuss the war in eastern DRC.

Igihe reported that Point-Zéro was captured by AFC/M23 and MRDP-Twirwaneho fighters in the middle of the night of 4 July 2026, after heavy fighting against DRC forces allied with Burundian forces, Wazalendo and the FDLR.

Igihe reported that in January 2026 Twirwaneho fighters had captured Point-Zéro and used it to block attacks that had long been launched on Minembwe, but were dislodged by DRC government forces using drones and warplanes.

Azarias Ruberwa said, according to Igihe, that there is a serious humanitarian problem around Point-Zéro and Minembwe because attacks are launched as if the area were uninhabited, adding that he feared people might be displaced permanently.

Igihe reported that AFC/M23 said that as long as DRC government forces continue to fire blindly at areas it controls, including Point-Zéro, without regard for civilians living there, it will continue to fight for them and protect its positions.

Igihe reported that in recent days the alliance of forces supporting the DRC government launched drone and heavy-weapon attacks on Point Zéro, trying to retake it and continuing into the centre of Minembwe, but that Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 fighters held firm.

According to Igihe, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on 10 October 2026 that forces including those of the DRC, FDLR, Maï-Maï groups, foreign mercenaries and Burundian soldiers launched drone attacks on the night of 9 October 2026 ("saa yine z'ijoro", about 10 p.m.) on Point Zéro village and surroundings, and similar attacks later that night ("saa saba z'ijoro" of 9 into 10 October) at Rugezi and surroundings in Minembwe; he said the attacks on inhabited areas caused deaths and mass flight.

AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that from the early hours of 20 April 2026 the coalition of DRC government forces launched a suicide-drone attack on the Mikenke area in Minembwe commune.

AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that at 5:30 government coalition forces also attacked the densely populated area of Mitimingi in Masisi territory, causing much damage and making many families flee; Igihe places this in its account of attacks on 20 April 2026.

place: Kalingi, Bidegu (Minembwe commune, South Kivu); Mitimingi (Masisi, North Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that in the night of 18 to 19 April 2026 the DRC government forces coalition launched heavy-weapon and suicide-drone attacks on areas including Kalingi and Bidegu in Minembwe and on Mitimingi and neighbouring areas.

place: Minembwe and Masisi (South and North Kivu)
statement: AFC/M23 spokesperson Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that AFC/M23 continues to point to repeated, deliberate breaches of the ceasefire by the Kinshasa government and that it is fully ready to defend civilians and to set up a proper security space to protect the population.

place: Switzerland (talks); body covers North Kivu and South Kivu
statement: Igihe reported that the DRC government and AFC/M23 had agreed that the work of an international body to monitor compliance with the ceasefire in North Kivu and South Kivu would start soon, and that the agreement launching the body's activities was signed in Switzerland on 14 April.

AFC/M23 told Congolese and the international community, according to Igihe, that the Kinshasa government was putting war first, while Igihe reported that DRC forces were still launching drone and heavy-weapon attacks on Minembwe and Masisi while the talks that began on 13 April were under way.

AFC/M23 said, according to Igihe, that no residents of Minembwe commune would be killed again by the government forces coalition because the war there was over; AFC/M23 deputy leader for political affairs, diplomacy and governance Bertand Bisimwa (as Igihe spells the name) delivered the message to Minembwe residents.

place: Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu, Rwitsankuku (Minembwe area, South Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that the DRC, Burundian, FDLR and Wazalendo forces were dispossessed of areas including Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu and Rwitsankuku, and that once these areas were taken senior AFC/M23 leaders visited them.

Igihe reported that once the Minembwe-area positions were taken, senior AFC/M23 leaders visited them, including Bisimwa, Dr. Freddy Kaniki (in charge of economy and finance in the alliance and President of MRDP Twirwaneho) and Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu (Deputy Commander-in-Chief of M23); it also states that 8 July was a day of songs of thanks for the residents of Minembwe.

AFC/M23 deputy leader Bertand Bisimwa said, according to Igihe, that AFC/M23 fighters from many parts of the country and MRDP Twirwaneho had united to stop what he described as a plan by the DRC government forces to wipe out Congolese because of their ethnic origin.

place: Binza groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
statement: The AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Col Bahati Musanga Erasto, asked residents of the Binza groupement (Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, near the Ugandan border) to distance themselves from the FDLR, telling them its founders had shed innocent blood in Rwanda, according to Igihe.

place: Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu), general allegation
statement: Igihe quoted Governor Bahati as saying FDLR members are thieves who spend their days deceiving residents, robbing them and raping women and girls. No date, place, victim or incident is given.
Igihe quoted governor Bahati as saying, of the FDLR ('those bandits'), that what they can do is ambush vehicles, loot, and kill those inside; the passage gives no date, place or incident.

Col Bahati Musanga Erasto, the provincial governor appointed by AFC/M23, said, according to Igihe, of the FDLR, that 'we know well that they are still in the forests, and we will not cease to fight them until we defeat them.'

Igihe reported that Governor Bahati indicated that if FDLR fighters were not supported by some of the residents who take them food in the forests, they would leave it and hand themselves over to AFC/M23, which would hand them to Rwanda.

place: Rwanda (receiving FDLR fighters from eastern DRC)
statement: Igihe reported that in November 2025 the vice-president of Rwanda's national demobilisation and reintegration commission (RDRC), Maj Gen (Rtd) Jacques Nziza, explained that in 10 months Rwanda had received more than 200 FDLR fighters.

place: Areas under AFC/M23 control in North Kivu; Rwanda
statement: Igihe reported, citing a UN report it does not name, that FDLR fighters captured and repatriated to Rwanda since AFC/M23 took Goma in January 2025 are far more numerous than those who returned while the DRC government controlled the area.

AFC/M23 deputy leader Bertrand Bisimwa criticised the United Nations on X, according to Igihe, after the UN sanctioned several AFC/M23 leaders, saying it had been misled and was driven by emotion, and that sanctioning only the side that respects its peace commitments showed the UN had lost its way.
Bisimwa said, according to Igihe, that putting pressure on people affected by ethnic discrimination to leave their land is a grave mistake that will have consequences.

place: UN Security Council (listing); persons active in North and South Kivu
statement: Igihe reported that the UN had recently imposed sanctions on AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa, on Col Nzenze Imani, described as in charge of intelligence and military operations in the alliance, and on Brig Gen Charles Sematama, who leads Twirwaneho in Minembwe commune; Igihe wrote that Sematama was sanctioned for leading a group accused of "killing civilians, recruiting children into the army and engaging in activities that disturb the peace and security of the population."
AFC/M23 deputy leader and MRDP-Twirwaneho President Freddy Kaniki said, according to Igihe, that forces supporting the DRC government had again besieged Minembwe commune in South Kivu.

Kaniki said, according to Igihe, that Minembwe was in a serious security situation and that the DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, FDLR and foreign mercenary forces had chosen to breach the ceasefire agreement adopted at the Doha talks.

Kaniki said, according to Igihe, that residents of Minembwe had their routes closed to them for going to seek health care, for bringing food and for going to markets, contrary to the Doha resolutions.

Kaniki called on the international community, according to Igihe, to act before a serious humanitarian problem arises, saying AFC/M23 continues to support the political path but will not keep watching Minembwe residents being put in danger.

place: Point-Zéro and areas around Minembwe (South Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that in early July 2026 AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho fighters had restored security in Minembwe by driving the DRC government forces coalition out of surrounding areas including Point-Zéro, and that the government forces were now launching strong attacks around Minembwe, including Point-Zéro, intending to retake them.

place: Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that five people were killed in an attack in the night of 25 to 26 October 2026 at Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory; Euphrem Kabasha, Rutshuru territory administrator appointed by the FRN, said it was carried out by the FDLR together with the Nyatura CMC FDP of Gashegu Héritier and Mbitezi.

place: Kabizo and Katovu, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that the fighting in Rutshuru territory had stopped farming activity in the areas of Kabizo and Katovu.

Twirwaneho officer Col Fidèle Rugabo said, according to Igihe, that at 'saa cyenda z’urukerera' on 18 September 2026 DRC, Burundian, FDLR, P5 and Wazalendo forces attacked residents at Mukoko and Nyaruhinga, and that 'the enemy is being beaten like a drum'.
Col Rugabo said, according to Igihe, that at 'saa kumi n’ebyiri z’igitondo' pro-government armed forces attacked the Gipimo area in the direction of Kabanju.

place: Minembwe, Kalehe, Masisi (South and North Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that these attacks followed ones that the DRC government forces coalition had been launching for days on areas controlled by Twirwaneho and AFC/M23, including Minembwe, Kalehe and Masisi; Col Rugabo said, according to Igihe, that Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 strongly condemned these attacks.
Igihe reported that on 16 February 2025 M23 confirmed it had captured the city of Bukavu after dislodging soldiers of the DRC government forces coalition.
Igihe reported that from 16 February 2025 M23 fighters began searching for armed people still hiding in Bukavu and confronting soldiers who had fled to the south-east of the city.

place: Kamanyola border crossing (Walungu territory, South Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that M23 had controlled the DRC side of the Kamanyola border crossing with Rwanda since the evening of 18 February 2025, after driving out Wazalendo fighters.

Igihe reported that it was said ('biravugwa') that Burundian troops, described as a strong arm of the DRC government, had started leaving the war and returning to Bujumbura, and that Reuters had reported that four people, including a soldier, UN staff and a diplomat, confirmed this.

Igihe reported that M23 had taken Mumosho and Nya-Ngezi in Walungu territory and appeared to be heading towards Uvira territory, and that M23 had entered three territories of South Kivu: Kalehe, Kabare and Walungu.

AFC/M23 called, in a communiqué released on the evening of 17 February 2025 by political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka and reported by Igihe, on political and armed groups in the DRC that aim to protect civilians to join it in a struggle to liberate the country and remove the Kinshasa government.

Igihe wrote that AFC/M23 indicates it is committed to talking with the DRC to resolve the country's security problems and, failing that, will only settle once it reaches Kinshasa and liberates the population.

place: Areas held by AFC/M23 in North and South Kivu
statement: Igihe reported that in most of the areas AFC/M23 had already 'liberated' it had put its new leaders, who it said were committed to security and development of residents.

Rwandan President Paul Kagame said, in an interview with Jeune Afrique as published by Igihe, that he was satisfied with the outcome of the Dar es Salaam regional summit and that what matters now is how its resolutions are implemented, especially by the Congolese side.

Kagame said, according to Igihe's rendering of his Jeune Afrique interview, that nothing explained President Tshisekedi's non-attendance in person at the summit, and that the night before he had chosen to go to Chad to ask for military assistance.
Kagame said, per Igihe, that Rwanda had signed more than five agreements with the DRC government since 2007 that the DRC never implemented, and that a group with a genocide ideology still exists.
Kagame said, per Igihe, that the DRC government had hired mercenaries who came from Europe.

Kagame said, per Igihe, that what Rwanda took from the statements of the presidents of Burundi and the DRC was a plan to destabilise Rwanda, and that they fuelled the war and said they would remove the Rwandan government.
Kagame said, per Igihe, that he has sympathy for M23 'based on evidence and proof' and that the group defends many people who have long been persecuted, killed and chased out as refugees.

Kagame said, in rhetorical questions rendered by Igihe, that the Wazalendo were set up by the Congolese government to carry out ethnically based killings and that Burundi's leadership entered the conflict to support its Congolese counterparts in their plan to kill and wipe out those people.

place: Goma to Bukavu (North and South Kivu)
statement: Kagame said, per Igihe, that 'they' (the FDLR, by context) are still there, that some had fled and others had gone south to regroup, and that they followed the Burundian troops from Goma to Bukavu.

Asked, in a question stating that M23's attacks on Goma killed more than 3000, whether Rwanda had a role, Kagame answered 'None' and said the measures Rwanda put in place are only defensive, according to Igihe.

Kagame said, per Igihe, that most of those killed in the fighting were FARDC soldiers, FDLR fighters and Wazalendo armed groups fighting alongside them, and that the number of civilians killed is reckoned at about 500.

Kagame replied, per Igihe, 'Yes, it is taken as though there is no doubt that Rwandan troops are there, but the FDLR is a threat to Rwanda's security', adding that mercenaries and provocations by Félix Tshisekedi and Burundi also threaten Rwanda.
Kagame said, per Igihe, that rather than choose between threats to security and sanctions he would take up arms against what aims to harm Rwanda, regardless of sanctions.

Kagame said, per Igihe, that he does not go to greet people and be photographed; that they were to meet in Luanda to sign an agreement prepared by their ministers and technicians, not to hold talks; and that the agreement was not agreed because Kinshasa refused to include key issues.

Asked whether he supported the aim of M23 and AFC to remove Felix Tshisekedi from power, Kagame said, per Igihe, that he could understand what they were expressing, and that Rwanda has a problem with a Congolese government that he said was not elected, either the first or second time, and that he said aims only to persecute the population, sow more chaos and enrich itself.

place: Lubero territory and other AFC/M23-held areas (North Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 denied reports that it had begun withdrawing fighters from some areas it controls in the east of the country; in a communiqué, Erasto Bahati, whom Igihe calls the provincial governor, said what was happening on the front lines was a routine replacement of troops in the AFC/M23 military and that the reports were rumours fuelled by the Kinshasa authorities' social media.

place: Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi, Kipese; Alimbongo, Kirumba, Kanyabayonga (Lubero territory, North Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that at the end of the week Congolese newspapers had begun writing that AFC/M23 was withdrawing fighters from areas of Lubero territory (Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese) and relocating them to Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga; AFC/M23 denied this.

Igihe reported that Twirwaneho, a group it describes as defending Banyamulenge who are persecuted and killed by the DRC government, announced it had joined AFC/M23 in the struggle to remove the Kinshasa government.
Igihe reported that Twirwaneho had announced its leader, Col Rukunda Michel known as Makanika, died in a drone strike by the DRC forces coalition on 19 February 2025.

Igihe reported that the new Commander-in-Chief of Twirwaneho, Brig Gen Charles Sematama, told Voice of America that Col Rukunda left them strong and that they must finish the struggle he started whatever happens.

Brig Gen Sentama (as Igihe prints the name in this passage; Sematama elsewhere in the article) said, according to Igihe, that they had been fighting a war of self-defence for seven years, had tried to alert foreign countries and to persuade Kinshasa to drop discrimination and protect people equally, that this kept failing, and that they were now determined to do it openly themselves.

Brig Gen Sentama (as Igihe prints the name) alleged, according to Igihe, that all the Mai Mai groups were united with the FDLR and had begun attacking and destroying the homes of Banyamulenge, that foreign countries were shown this but stayed silent, that the killings continue to this day and that they had killed the leader.

Brig Gen Sematama said, according to Igihe, that in the fight to remove the Kinshasa government they had taken areas of Minembwe in Fizi territory and others, that they had driven FARDC out of where it had been, and that they had entered Mikenke and would continue.

Brig Gen Sematama said, according to Igihe, in reply to international calls to lay down arms and join talks: 'We are being killed. Should we lay down our guns and then they kill us?', adding that they had appealed to the world for a long time and nothing had been done.

Brig Gen Sematama, the new Twirwaneho leader, called, according to Igihe, on all young Banyamulenge men to come to the rescue and unite to remove 'this government of killers', which he said was committing 'genocide' and wiping out their parents.

M23's military spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma said, according to Igihe, in a message on 21 February 2025 accompanied by a photo of Col Rukunda, that those who think they will wipe out the Banyamulenge in the DRC are mistaken and that these Congolese will soon be liberated to move freely in their country.
Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe warned the United States, according to Igihe, that its biased sanctions cannot resolve the conflict between Rwanda and the DRC and instead inflame it.

Nduhungirehe said, in a France 24 interview with Marc Perelman reported by Igihe, that the Washington agreement had not produced results because the DRC government kept breaching the ceasefire, kept helping the FDLR, and was hosting opponents of the Rwandan government, including Juvénal Habyarimana's son Jean Luc Habyarimana.

Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that on 5 June 2026 US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told legislators that Rwanda was complying with the Washington agreement while the DRC government had done nothing, which he said showed weak political will.

Nduhungirehe reminded Perelman, per Igihe, that Massad Boulos, an adviser to Trump, had told the UN security council that the government of RDC (as Igihe writes it) had not dismantled the FDLR, at least in the areas it controls; the sentence goes on that this showed the reason Rwanda is the one still being punished is not understandable.

place: areas held by AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho (South and North Kivu)
statement: Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that DRC forces had also launched attacks on various areas controlled by AFC/M23 and MRDP Twirwaneho, killing many civilians, and asked how many civilians must die before it is understood that the DRC should respect the ceasefire.

Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that the US sanctions on Gasabo Refinery, its head and other mining companies on 25 June could bring no solution between Rwanda and the DRC and were biased, adding that sanctions are not a mediator's role.

Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that the effects of bias had begun to show because DRC forces had stepped up attacks on the Banyamulenge in Minembwe commune and on AFC/M23 positions, since President Tshisekedi saw that the US would not penalise him.

Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that the US had set no deadline for Rwanda to lift its defensive measures and that Rwanda itself had offered an idea of how both sides could speed up implementation of the Washington agreement; Igihe adds that Rubio told legislators he was confident Rwanda would lift them by mid-July 2026.
Igihe reported that on 2 March 2026 the United States imposed sanctions on the Rwandan army and its officials, accusing them of violating the Washington peace agreement.

place: Point-Zéro, Baruta, Kalonge, Bicumbi, Rubemba (Fizi/Mwenga highlands, South Kivu)
statement: Twirwaneho officer Col Fidele Rugabo announced, according to Igihe, that Twirwaneho had taken Point-Zéro, Baruta, Kalonge, Bicumbi and Rubemba at 'saa munani y’igicuku' on 4 July 2026, ending military operations at Point-Zéro at 'saa munani n’iminota 35'.
Igihe reported that before taking Point-Zéro, Twirwaneho had taken other key areas around Minembwe commune, including Mikenke and Bilalombili, on 1 July 2026.
Igihe reported that on 17 January 2026 Twirwaneho had taken Point-Zéro but lost it shortly afterwards when it was attacked with drones and by soldiers of a DRC special-forces unit known as Hiboux.

Col Fidele Rugabo said, according to Igihe, that the DRC, Burundian, FDLR and Wazalendo forces had been shamed by Twirwaneho and M23 fighters, and he greeted residents of Fizi and Baraka, hinting that Twirwaneho might take those places too.

Igihe reported that Twirwaneho and M23 had accused the DRC government forces coalition of using Point-Zéro to prepare major attacks on Minembwe centre and other key Banyamulenge areas including Mikenke.

place: Uvira and Luvungi (South Kivu); briefing in Bujumbura
statement: Burundi's Foreign Minister Dr. Edouard Bizimana said at a briefing with diplomats on 8 December 2025, according to Igihe, that AFC/M23 had aimed to take the city of Uvira before the Washington peace agreement was signed on 4 December but, he said, was held back by Burundian forces.

Bizimana said, according to Igihe ('uyu muyobozi', this official, read as the minister from the preceding paragraph), that Burundian troops went to the DRC to protect Burundi's borders, Burundians and their property, that they cannot leave while the problems that took them there remain unsolved, and that they went there with the agreement of the Congolese government.

place: n/a (statement); Burundian forces in South Kivu
statement: AFC/M23 military spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma said on 6 December, according to Igihe, 'Those who crossed over have learned a lesson', that 'Congo is not Cibitoke, nor Ngozi or their Bujumbura', and that they come to AFC/M23's home where it is fighting for the truth.

place: Katogota, Rurambo, Luberizi, Luvungi, Mutalule, Bwegera, Nyakabere, Sange (Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that within a week the Burundian army, working with DRC forces, Wazalendo and FDLR, had been dispossessed of many areas of South Kivu including Katogota, Rurambo, Luberizi, Luvungi, Mutalule, Bwegera, Nyakabere and Sange; a photo caption says AFC/M23 fighters coming from Kamanyola were now approaching the city of Uvira.

Igihe reported that 4 December 2025 was a very bad day for Burundian forces, as many were killed in an AFC/M23 attack and more than 100 were taken prisoner, and that Lt Col Athanase Minani was killed then.

place: Bujumbura (Burundi): Kamenge military hospital; Tanganyika Care Polyclinic
statement: Igihe reported that many Bujumbura hospitals received bodies and wounded Burundian soldiers, and, citing 'the SOS website', that the military hospital at Kamenge alone received 87 wounded, with others taken to other clinics including Tanganyika Care Polyclinic.

Igihe reported ('Amakuru avuga' = reports say) that after losing Sange on 8 December 2025 Burundian soldiers were ordered to leave Uvira city quickly, though it was not known whether to regroup or not to return; DRC soldiers, Wazalendo, Imbonerakure and many civilians followed them.
Igihe reported that Bizimana asserted AFC/M23's aim was to take Uvira before Christmas, and that as of 8 December 2025 AFC/M23 fighters were within 30 kilometres of Uvira city.

place: Around Minembwe: Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories (South Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that most of the Burundians who remained in the DRC were concentrated in areas around Minembwe in Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories.

Igihe reported that M23 had taken the Kitsombiro centre in Lubero territory after heavy fighting against DRC forces on the morning of 19 February 2025, and that Kitsombiro is 25 kilometres from the Lubero centre.

Igihe reported ('amakuru avuga', 'haravugwa') that, according to news from Lubero, DRC forces tried to use heavy guns and helicopters to stop M23 fighters without success, and that soldiers who fled the fighting were reportedly arrested by the army's military-conduct branch.

place: Alimbongo, Kanyabayonga, Kayna, Kirumba, Matembe (Lubero territory, North Kivu)
statement: Igihe reported that M23 already controlled other areas of Lubero territory, including Alimbongo, Kanyabayonga, Kayna, Kirumba and Matembe, which it said it had taken at the end of 2024.

A FARDC captain shot dead Lungele Mbiso, coordinator of the communication cell of South Kivu governor Jean Jacques Purusi, on the afternoon of 5 July 2025, according to Actualite.cd (citing local civil society); Igihe reports the same killing in Uvira territory.

Uvira youth leader Kiza Tiniko said, according to Actualite.cd and Igihe, that angry residents lynched (beat to death) the captain who had killed the governor's communication coordinator; Actualite.cd adds, citing several other sources, that the soldier threw away his weapon before being chased by the population, and Igihe adds, citing news from Uvira, that he threw away the gun he had used to shoot Lungele out of fear of being prosecuted.
Igihe reported that the office of the government-appointed South Kivu governor, Jean-Jacques Purusi, relocated to Uvira in February 2025 once AFC/M23 had taken Bukavu.

DW Swahili reported, according to Samuel Kagheni, described as one of the civil-society leaders in the village, that on Saturday the ADF attacked the village of Ngohi Vuyinga in Lubero territory (North Kivu); 9 people were killed and many others lost their homes after their houses were burned.

place: Butembo (Kimemi neighbourhood, Mont Tabor and Mavina area), Butembo city
statement: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that about ten militiamen were killed in violent clashes between the night of Monday 3 March and the morning of Tuesday 4 March in Butembo, and that, according to civil society in Kimemi, the fighting pitted two Wazalendo militia groups against each other. It said an interim report indicated ten militiamen killed and several wounded, treated in health structures in the area.

place: near the Université Catholique du Graben (UCG) campus, Butembo
statement: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) quoted a resident on social media as saying that four dead bodies were discovered 'this morning', that they 'would be' young militiamen from the Mavina group, and that they had been tied up before being hanged (the verb used, kunyongwa, can also mean strangled).

BBC Gahuza (Kirundi), relaying RFI, reported that news from Butembo said about ten people died in clashes between two groups of Wazalendo fighters, which broke out on 3 March and lasted several hours in the Kimemi hills of the city; it added that an army spokesman in the area said in a video that six dead were known, while non-political associations said up to ten died on both sides.

Vatican News (Swahili), citing local sources of the pontifical charity Aid to the Church in Need (given as ACS), reported that more than 70 bodies were found in a Protestant church at Maiba, North Kivu; it said the killings took place between 12 and 15 February 2025 at the hands of ADF fighters who entered the village and abducted about 100 people.

UN News Kiswahili, relaying a MONUSCO statement released in Kinshasa, reported that ADF attacks between 13 and 19 November 2025 in parts of Lubero (Bapere and Baswagha areas) killed 89 civilians, including 20 women, with the number of children not yet known.

place: Byambwe, 60 km west of Lubero, Lubero territory
statement: UN News Kiswahili, relaying MONUSCO, reported that in the village of Byambwe, 60 km west of Lubero, at least 17 civilians, including women who were receiving care in the maternity ward, were killed inside a health centre run by the Catholic Church, and that four wards with patients caught fire during the attack.

UN News Kiswahili reported that MONUSCO strongly condemned recent attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Beni and Lubero, North Kivu, between 9 and 16 August 2025, which caused the deaths of about 52 civilians including women and children.

DW Swahili reported that a government official in the area, Macaire Sivikunula, said the attack happened 'last night' in the village of Ntoyo in Lubero territory, and that Lubero military administrator Colonel Alain Kiwewa told Reuters the number killed was about 60 and might rise because some people had not yet been found.

TRT Afrika Swahili reported that suspected ADF rebels killed 19 civilians in a night attack in eastern DRC, according to two local officials. Alain Kiwewa, military administrator of Lubero, said the attack, believed to have been carried out by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), took place in the village of Mukondo in North Kivu and that the toll could rise; a local pastor who declined to be named said the attackers wore uniforms resembling those of the Congolese army and attacked people with guns, knives and clubs.

DW Swahili reported that 10 people were killed in eastern DRC by extremist rebels linked to the group calling itself the Islamic State (IS), and that these ADF rebels attacked the village of Makoko in Lubero territory, North Kivu, 'yesterday'; it said, as stated by David Sikuli, a member of parliament for the province, that at the time there were no Congolese soldiers in the village, only fighters known as Wazalendo.

place: clinic near Butembo, Butembo / Lubero area
statement: BBC Swahili reported that a six-year-old girl who was being treated for Ebola was abducted from a health facility in eastern DRC: armed people stormed a clinic near the town of Butembo in North Kivu and took the child with her mother. Dr. Lubambo Maboko Gaston, the province's Ebola response manager, told Reuters that the two had not yet been found and made an urgent call to the abductors.

place: Vemba-Katota and Vemba-Masulukwede axes, east of Ngadi, near Beni
statement: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that a new series of attacks attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) caused mourning in the Beni area of North Kivu, and that between the night of Saturday 30 May and Sunday 31 May 2026, about 17 civilians were killed in several coordinated attacks on the Vemba-Katota and Vemba-Masulukwede axes in the Beni area, according to local sources and civil-society actors.

SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that in the Butembo and Beni health zones, as well as Kisangani, doctors, nurses, laboratory technicians and community health workers were refusing to return to work, demanding payment of their salaries and hazard allowances.

place: Musienene (Butembo military tribunal); offences alleged in Lubero-Centre, Kimbulu and Musienene
statement: BBC Swahili reported that the trial of about sixty FARDC deserter soldiers and two female accomplices opened on the day of the entry before the Butembo military tribunal sitting at Musienene; local journalist Seros Muyisa, present at the hearing, told the BBC the accused were charged with fleeing the enemy, theft, rape, extortion and other offences in the areas of Lubero-Centre, Kimbulu and Musienene.

BBC Gahuza (Kirundi) reported in an update that 55 of the soldiers accused of offences including fleeing the battlefield and looting were convicted and sentenced to death, and that the trial of about 60 FARDC soldiers began on Monday in the city of Butembo.

place: North Kivu (Lubero territory, per record REC-0981)
statement: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported, citing DRC media and a statement signed by the Wazalendo leader Shukuru Bulenda, that the defecting groups were Mai-Mai Kabidon (FPP-AP), part of Mai-Mai Kifuafua and the Nduma Defense of Congo-Renovated (NDC-R/M) group, who were said to have joined AFC/M23 on 9 March 2025.
Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported that M23 captured the town of Kasugho on 2 March 2025 and left on 7 March, heading for Bunyatenge, a gold-mining area six hours from Kasugho.
UN News Kiswahili reported, citing OCHA, that violence increased on 2 May in the Lubero area, forcing about 30,000 people to flee their homes.

DW (French) reported that the Butembo human-rights network Redho said it recorded 280 sexual-violence cases brought to justice in the city of Butembo in 2025, in a report made public in mid-March; Redho coordinator Muhindo Wasingya said the slowness of judicial procedures favours out-of-court settlements between families.

Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that M23 had continued its attacks in eastern Congo and entered the town of Walikale, two days after Presidents Tshisekedi of Congo and Kagame of Rwanda called for a ceasefire following their meeting in Qatar.
Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that the AFC/M23 alliance said, in a statement published on X, that it had decided to withdraw its forces from Walikale town and from the neighbouring areas.

Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that the Congolese Foreign Minister Therese Kayikwamba Wagner told journalists that the government was waiting eagerly to see whether M23 would really withdraw from the town of Walikale.

Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that M23 rebels had withdrawn from the strategic town of Walikale, describing the move as a gesture of goodwill before peace talks; confirming the departure, Congolese army spokesperson Sylvain Ekenge said on Friday that his soldiers had witnessed it.

place: Kaleta-Bitoyi (Ufamandu II) and Burungu (Bashali), Masisi territory
statement: Taarifa Rwanda (Kinyarwanda edition) said that, in a communique issued on Monday 28 September, the organisation Forces vives de Masisi said many residents had been killed or wounded and others had fled their villages, some of them killed by drone strikes; it quoted civil society member Télesphore Mithondeke as saying that a drone attack at Kaleta-Bitoyi, in Ufamandu II, killed a woman and a child, and that fighting at Burungu in Bashali killed eight residents.

BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that AFC/M23 denied Amnesty International's allegations that it killed and abused small-scale miners and took gold and coltan to Rwanda; in a statement it issued in Goma on Tuesday, AFC/M23 said Amnesty had not provided solid evidence that could be examined.

place: Rubaya (Masisi, North Kivu) and Lomera (South Kivu)
statement: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that, in a report published on Monday, Amnesty had accused the movement of killings, ill-treatment of people ('ugukubagura abantu'), detention without legal procedure, forced labour and forcible recruitment into armed groups, and said these happened at the Rubaya coltan site in North Kivu and at the Lomera gold mines in South Kivu.
BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 authorities in eastern DRC said more than 200 people had died after a mine collapsed in the mineral-rich town of Rubaya.

BBC News Gahuza reported that Lumumba Kambere Muyisa, spokesperson of the governor of North Kivu province, told the media that the upper parts of the mine had fallen into the mine on Wednesday because of heavy rain.

BBC News Gahuza reported that the DRC government, in a statement on the Rubaya mine collapse, said that in June 2025 more than 300 civilians had died at Rubaya in a similar way, and that a ministerial order of February 2025 had banned mining in the Rubaya zone.

Bwiza (Rwanda), relaying information reaching Actualite.cd, reported that on Tuesday 20 October, at Ntoto, capital of the Waloa Uroba groupement in Walikale territory, a soldier and a civilian were killed by bullets when two units of the FARDC turned on each other, and that another soldier and a civilian were seriously wounded; it said the head of the Waloa Uroba groupement, Barthélemy Mulengezi Luc, explained that the incident occurred when a group of soldiers coming from the front tried to cross Ntoto.

Bwiza (Rwanda) reported that 54 soldiers of the 3415th regiment of the FARDC began to be tried before the Goma Military Court, sitting specially in Walikale, from Monday 26 October, and that they are accused of offences including murder, abandoning their duties, wasting ammunition and military equipment, and refusing to obey orders; according to Major Dieudonné Kasereka, in charge of communications in the 34th military region, the soldiers were arrested on 20 October after the events at Ntoto, in the Waloa Loanda area.

Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that around 'saa saba' in the night of 19 to 20 October (the seventh hour of the night, about one in the morning), Wazalendo groups attacked AFC/M23 at Nyabiondo and heavy fighting began; it placed the Nyabiondo centre in Masisi territory, North Kivu.

Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that on the evening of 18 October aircraft of the DRC army fired on AFC/M23 positions at Mpeti and Buhaya in Walikale, and that AFC/M23 deputy leader Bertrand Bisimwa condemned the attack, recalling that the DRC government was violating the agreement the two sides made in Doha, Qatar.

Ijambo.net (Rwanda) reported that M23 took the trading centre of Mubi in Walikale territory on Friday 21 March, with reports saying it took it without fighting because the government forces had already fled it; it said the centre lies about 36 kilometres from Walikale-Centre on the road to Kisangani.

BBC Swahili reported that, in a statement issued on Sunday 23 March 2025, Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said the government welcomed the news that FARDC and Wazalendo military activities would also be suspended.

BBC News Swahili reported that the Congolese army had stepped up its campaign to get FDLR rebels to surrender to Congolese authorities or to MONUSCO peacekeepers, and that police and army officers had been using loudspeakers in the Walikale area of North Kivu to urge them to surrender; it said the operation was also in the Pinga area, on the Masisi border, where some FDLR groups are said to be camped.

place: Nyabiondo and neighbouring villages, Masisi territory
statement: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported that M23 launched surprise attacks that broke through government forces' strongholds near the capital of the Masisi district and ended up capturing the Nyabiondo area and several neighbouring villages, from 'the day before yesterday, March 9, 2025'.

place: North Kivu (location not stated in the excerpt)
statement: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported that, according to media in the DRC and a statement signed by the Wazalendo leader Shukuru Bulenda, the groups that defected included Mai-Mai Kabidon (FPP-AP), part of Mai-Mai Kifuafua and the Nduma Defense of Congo-Renovated (NDC-R/M), and that these groups were alleged to have joined AFC/M23 on March 9, 2025.

BBC News Gahuza reported that on Thursday the areas of the Nyamaboko 1 groupements in Masisi 'became the hotbed of terrifying fighting', according to Voltaire Batundi, head of Masisi civil society, and that the fighting, which began in the morning and lasted almost all day, made thousands of people leave their homes and flee.
BBC News Gahuza reported that some Congolese media said that on Thursday the M23 took the Kazinga area in Masisi, but that this information had not been confirmed by any of the warring sides.

place: JTN tea estate, Mweso, Masisi territory
statement: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that on Thursday 26 February 2026, at about 16:15, combined forces, especially those of the FDLR, entered the JTN tea area at Mweso and shot 19 cows, of which 15 died immediately and 4 were seriously wounded.

place: JTN tea estate, Mweso, Masisi territory
statement: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the fighters fired bursts of bullets at a 19-year-old girl called Wamahoro, from Kitchanga, who died immediately.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that women it interviewed on September 21, 2025 in MPATI, in the Bashali chiefdom of Masisi territory, recounted brutal acts committed by NYATURA and CMC-FDP militiamen; a resident identified as M. N. said 'almost all the women here were raped during the war' and that she herself had suffered brutal acts at the hands of the men of Jenerali Guidon. The excerpts do not date the acts.

Kigali Today (Rwanda) reported that Rwandan President Kagame said that in the areas M23 controls, it does well in combating FDLR and other criminal groups, but that in Masisi, Walikale and other areas controlled by FARDC, FDLR is still found there, cooperating with government forces.

SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that an air strike attributed to the Congolese armed forces (FARDC) killed about seven civilians and wounded more than 40 others on Friday, January 2, 2026, at Masisi-Center.

SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that, according to Doctors Without Borders (MSF), 42 people, most of them wounded in the attack, were currently admitted to the Masisi General Referral Hospital.
SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that MONUSCO condemned on Saturday 3 January 2026 the drone strike of the previous day at Masisi-Center.

SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported, in a dispatch datelined Goma 27 November 2025, that heavy fighting broke out at dawn on Thursday between M23 rebels and local Wazalendo militiamen at the village of Kibati, in the Luberike grouping of Walikale territory.

SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that the FARDC used their air force to strike AFC/M23 positions at Kibati (Walikale) and Kasopo (Masisi), and that no official casualty figures were available.

BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge said M23 rebels had retaken the town of Masisi on the afternoon of Thursday, after he had announced in the morning of the same day that government forces had retaken it on Wednesday.

BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge said government forces were doing well there and were the ones controlling the whole town of Ngungu and its surroundings.

BBC News Swahili reported that the M23 rebellion, backed by Rwanda, took control of the town of Masisi, an important town in eastern DRC, on Saturday, and that the DRC army had pulled back, saying it was avoiding losing more lives in the town of Masisi.

BBC News Swahili reported that Alexis Bahunga, a member of parliament of North Kivu province, told AFP that it was with great sadness that he learned of the capture of the Masisi centre by M23, and that he asked the government to take steps to restore government authority across the whole area.

Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 said FDLR fighters, together with Wazalendo, killed 10 residents in Masisi and Walikale territories; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the attack was launched in the Malemo and Kalembe area, on the Masisi-Walikale border, in the night of 24 May 2026, and that in Malemo they killed three civilians, wounded six and abducted the local leader, whose fate was still unknown.
Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 said that after leaving those areas, FDLR and Wazalendo heavily looted the Bweru area, taking 11 cows belonging to residents and many pigs.

place: Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje and Kibati and surroundings (Masisi and Walikale)
statement: UMUSEKE (Rwanda) reported on 10 September 2026 that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said government forces launched attacks at dawn on Thursday 10 September 2026 in areas including Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje and Kibati and their surroundings, and that, posting on X, he said the fighting was continuing and many residents had fled.

UMUSEKE (Rwanda) reported that the AFC/M23 spokesperson said the escalation of fighting affected residents' security and could hinder aid work, and that aid organisations and their staff could not reach residents affected by the attacks.

place: Mindjendje hill, Banakindi, Kisimba groupement (Walikale-Masisi border)
statement: Rwanda Tribune (Rwanda) reported that information from the area said AFC/M23 had taken Mindjendje hill, in the Banakindi area of the Kisimba groupement; it said fighting on Thursday 10 September 2026 began in the morning and continued in areas near the border of Walikale and Masisi, and that residents said the fighting was heavy and drones were used.

place: Mishipo, Makungurano area, Waloa Loanda groupement, Walikale territory
statement: Bwiza (Rwanda, English edition), relaying Actualite.cd, reported that various reports from the Waloa Loanda groupement in Walikale territory indicated that a large number of armed individuals, believed to be FDLR rebels, were disturbing security in Mishipo, in the Makungurano area; that, according to several sources, a man claiming to be a general, known as Mutayonga and said to be from Masisi territory, had been in Mishipo for several days with around 100 armed men; that reports suggested the group's leader told residents to vacate the area, claiming he had bought the land; and that, according to information received by Actualite.cd, the alleged FDLR fighters had been firing shots to intimidate the population.

place: Chinono, between Ziralo and Mubuku groupements, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe
statement: Bwiza, citing Kivu Morning Post, reported that heavy fighting with heavy weapons between AFC/M23 fighters and the Wazalendo and FARDC coalition began, from 'saa saba z'amanywa' (the Kinyarwanda daytime hour count), on Thursday 3 September 2026 at Chinono, an area linking Ziralo and Mubuku in Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory; it cited local civil society as saying the fighting made many residents flee.

Bwiza, citing Kivu Morning Post, reported that other fighting in the same area took place on Wednesday 2 September 2026 when the coalition attacked the village of Lomera in Kabare territory, and that an AFC/M23 communiqué said the attack killed people and made many residents flee.

Bwiza (byline Bénjamin BABOU) reported that AFC/M23 had taken Tushunguti, in Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory, after heavy fighting with FARDC and armed groups supporting it, and that information from the area said AFC/M23 fighters had driven out Wazalendo and others on the Kinshasa side.

Bwiza reported, citing information from the area, that FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters retook the centre of Numbi in Kalehe territory on Tuesday 6 October 2026 after it had been controlled by M23 rebels for several months; it added that, according to some information, M23 fighters had fallen back to Numbi on Monday after losing positions at Shanje, Gasenda and the hills of Bukumba.

Bwiza reported that, according to information announced by the AFC/M23 alliance, forces fighting for Kinshasa, chiefly FDLR members, began destruction at Shanje and its surroundings (Kalehe territory) on Wednesday 7 October 2026 from 'saa yine n'igice za mu gitondo', burning many civilian houses and the market; the AFC/M23 communiqué said further information on damage and casualties would be published later.

Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a message on 7 October 2026 that attacks by forces supporting the Kinshasa government, including FDLR fighters, in the Shanje area of Kalehe territory had destroyed civilian houses and the market, and that details of the damage and of any dead or wounded would be published later.

place: Kavumu village, about 30 km from Bukavu, Kabare
statement: DW Kiswahili (Iddi Ssessanga) reported that a woman, whose name DW said had been changed for her safety, told DW that three soldiers broke into her home and one of them tried to rape her; DW said the incident took place in February in Kavumu village, 30 km from Bukavu.

place: Villages in northern South Kivu along Lake Kivu (Kalehe and Kabare area, as the article frames the M23 advance on Bukavu)
statement: DW Kiswahili reported that, in villages of northern South Kivu that it describes as having become war zones during the fighting of January and February, women and children suffered rape and sexual violence by armed men, and that community groups and activists blamed the Congolese army and Wazalendo fighters (from North Kivu) for taking part.

DW Kiswahili reported that in areas taken by M23, such as Bukavu and Goma, witnesses had reported a rise in rape, mostly of married women and girls, and that some women were forced to have sex to obtain certain services; it said many survivors do not report out of fear or shame.
DW Kiswahili, citing MSF, reported that in the north of South Kivu MSF had attended to nearly 700 victims since the start of the year.

DW Kiswahili (Mitima DeLachance) reported that hundreds of Catholic women marched in South Kivu on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, representing 44 parishes of the Bukavu archdiocese, and that the march was held at the Olame centre because public demonstrations had been banned by the new authorities of Bukavu city.

place: Villages of Kabare and Kalehe territories; Bukavu
statement: DW Kiswahili reported that before AFC/M23 took Bukavu in February, soldiers of the Congolese army had already been convicted of sexual violence against women in several villages of Kabare and Kalehe, and that when AFC-M23 arrived in Bukavu the accused fled, together with judges and lawyers.

DW Kiswahili reported that, after AFC/M23 reached Bukavu, rape cases were later witnessed although they were dismissed by AFC/M23; it quoted women's rights defender Nono Mwavita as saying women's security has not improved.

place: Mitimbili and Munanira, Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu
statement: Bwiza reported a communiqué of Lawrence Kanyuka, whom it called FRN spokesperson, saying that on Monday 26 October 2026 at about 4:00 a.m. the Kinshasa-backed forces attacked Mitimbili and Munanira in Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu territory, after attacks on Kuwihene, Rugezi and Point Zéro in the Minembwe area the previous night using kamikaze drones and 120mm and 82mm mortars.

place: Mitimbili hills, Muhumba groupement, Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu; Mwera, Butuzi groupement
statement: Bwiza reported that on Monday 12 October 2026 fighting between AFC/M23 fighters and FARDC supported by Wazalendo was reported in Kaziba chiefdom, and that, according to information from the area reaching Bwiza, it restarted at 'saa kumi n'ebyiri za mu gitondo' on the Mitimbili hills in Muhumba groupement, east of Kaziba near the border with Bafulero chiefdom; it added that a second battle at Mwera in Butuzi groupement was reported on social network X.

place: Schools in Kabare and Walungu territories
statement: Umuryango.rw reported that the Wazalendo alliance, backed by the DRC government, expelled students and teachers from schools in Kabare and Walungu territories of South Kivu, that the expulsions began on 9 September 2025, and that videos on social media showed people fleeing while Wazalendo fighters told them studying or teaching meant nothing to them.

place: Schools in Kabare and Walungu territories
statement: Umuryango.rw reported that, in videos circulating on social media, one Wazalendo fighter was heard speaking Swahili and saying that students found studying would be killed, and another told students everyone should go home and that whoever went to school would die.

Umuryango.rw reported that the AFC/M23 alliance condemned the silence of the international community, aid organisations and human rights defenders while Wazalendo continued actions depriving residents of their rights, and that spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said, citing the Wazalendo statements, that 'these words push people into killings and war crimes'.

DW Kiswahili reported that local civil society organisations spoke of the deaths of at least seven people, including five civilians, and of wounded people being treated at Kavumu health facilities, after Wazalendo tried for a few minutes to take Kavumu airport before M23 forces drove them out.

DW Kiswahili reported that further heavy fighting between M23 and Wazalendo took place 'yesterday, Sunday' at Burhale in Walungu district, where vehicles and houses suspected of sheltering M23 were burned by Wazalendo in an area called Mashango.

place: Kasheke, Lemera, Bushaku and other villages, Kalehe and Kabare
statement: DW Kiswahili (Tatu Karema) reported that witnesses said heavy fighting had taken place since early morning at Kasheke village after other heavy fighting there and in the villages of Lemera and Bushaku and in some villages of Kabare and Kalehe, and that civil society sources estimated that nearly 12 villages were under Wazalendo control, which M23 had not confirmed.

place: Nzibira, Walungu; surrounding villages Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza, Kalongo
statement: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that M23 rebels took the town of Nzibira in Walungu territory on the evening of 'yesterday, Sunday' after first shelling army positions, according to witnesses, and it cited Radio Okapi for fighting in surrounding villages including Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza and Kalongo.
