Umuryango.rw reported that fighting between AFC/M23 and FARDC and allied groups intensified on Sunday 21 September 2025 in Walungu territory and ended with M23 defeating the government army and Wazalendo fighters and taking Nzibira, with the heaviest fighting at Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza and Kalongo, as Radio Okapi reported.

BBC News Gahuza reported that the AFC/M23 group accused the DRC government army of 'excessively severe' drone attacks 'in areas inhabited by civilians' at Lumbishi, Kalehe territory, on Monday, and that Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that the CH-4 drone attacks 'destroyed many things and caused many civilians to flee'.

BBC News Gahuza reported that Jacques Kongolo, adviser to President Félix Tshisekedi, told BBC on Monday that the government side was not the one violating the ceasefire agreements, and quoted him as saying that the other side uses Rwandan drones to shoot at them and then lies that it was the government side that fired.

Bwiza reported that the Lumbishi, Shanje, Kavumu and Numbi areas of Kalehe territory were retaken by AFC/M23 fighters a few hours after Wazalendo had taken them, and that on Tuesday 6 October 2026 the Kinshasa-aligned coalition, chiefly Wazalendo and FDLR, had taken Shanje town, the Gasenda area and the Bukumba hills.

Bwiza reported, citing unnamed 'new information', that about 60 houses, including kiosks, were burned in Shanje centre and cattle were looted, including two herds said to belong to Gen. Gabriel Amisi Kumba, known as Tango Four.

place: Chambombo, Cyangugu, Kaziba ya Rumbishi, Kwisimbi and Gafufura, Kalehe
statement: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X on Tuesday 11 August 2026 that the Kinshasa government's forces, including FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo groups, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army (FDNB), had launched general attacks from 05:00 with heavy weapons on densely populated parts of Kalehe territory, including Chambombo, Cyangugu, Kaziba ya Rumbishi, Kwisimbi and Gafufura, with some residents killed and injured.

Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 announced that on 17 August 2026 FARDC, FDLR and other armed groups working with the Kinshasa government launched simultaneous attacks (the spokesperson listing also FDLR, Wazalendo groups, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army FDNB among the attackers) in places including Kalehe territory (Katare, Tushunguti, Nyamugari and Kivoka) and on the Minembwe line, with AFC-M23 saying 120mm mortars and KT-6 drones were used and that the attacks killed civilians and destroyed homes and schools.

place: Avenue Kasheke 3, Buholo-Kasha, Bagira commune, Bukavu
statement: Umuseke, crediting Radio Maendeleo, reported that a large fire broke out on the morning of Thursday 10 September 2026 on Avenue Kasheke 3 in the Buholo-Kasha area of Bagira commune, Bukavu, damaging two schools (Mogo primary school and a school called Furaha), with at least 27 bodies counted by 15:00 on provisional figures; the page quotes the Buholo-Kasha area head Patrice Mugaruka Buduge as saying the fire started at about 8:00 a.m.

Bwiza reported that the AFC-M23 alliance announced that 24 children and students, 19 girls and five boys, died in a fire that struck houses in the Tshimpunda area of Kadutu commune, Bukavu, and that spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué of Thursday 10 September 2026 that the fire happened in the first hours after noon.

Umuseke (byline Ndekezi Johnson) reported that AFC/M23 fighters took Idjwi island, in Lake Kivu, South Kivu, and that since the evening of 12 March 2025 the island had been controlled by M23; it quoted one journalist on the island as saying government soldiers fled before M23 fighters set foot there.

Umuseke reported that on arriving at Idjwi AFC/M23 first gave a broadcast on the island's radio, Obuguma, before meeting residents, and that Mustapha Maomboleo, head of Idjwi territory, said the broadcast was meant to reassure the island's residents.

BBC News Swahili reported that, according to the United Nations, at least 42,000 people were living in temporary camps on Idjwi island, while locals estimated there might be as many as 60,000 displaced people living on the island.

BBC News Swahili reported that Idjwi island had only one main hospital and few vehicles, that it was often impossible for people in remote areas to get treatment, and quoted local radio director Yves Minani as saying that sometimes they must walk 10 km with a patient on a stretcher and that patients sometimes die on the way.

Ijambo (Chief editor Yves Iyaremye) reported that M23 said the FARDC used a Sukhoï 25 warplane to bomb inhabited areas of Kalehe territory, killing 10 people and wounding 25, and that M23 political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a communiqué, put the attack on Thursday 13 February 2025.

place: Kalehe General Hospital (Ibitaro Bikuru bya Kalehe), Kalehe
statement: Ijambo reported that M23 said the bombing destroyed Kalehe General Hospital, which usually received many patients in the area, and many houses of residents.

place: Kalehe-Centre (taken Wednesday 12 February 2025, per the page); Bukavu (alleged violence)
statement: Ijambo reported that M23 said it took Kalehe-Centre to stop the violence reported in Bukavu city, where it accused FARDC and its helpers, including FDLR, Burundian soldiers and Wazalendo, of killing residents, looting their property and committing serious violence against women.

BBC News Gahuza reported on the capture of Kalehe centre by M23, quoting an unnamed Kalehe civil-society leader who said that since the evening of Wednesday M23 fighters were in Kalehe centre, the main town of Kalehe territory.

BBC News Gahuza reported that on Wednesday the provincial army command said that M23 attacked army positions at Kalehe Centre and Ihusi, quoting it as saying 'these attacks caused the loss of many civilian lives', and that the army says Rwandan troops fight alongside M23, which both sides deny; M23 had said nothing yet on the army's statement.

place: Kalehe territory (to Idjwi, lake islands and Bukavu)
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that fighting that began on Tuesday and grew on Wednesday made residents flee in various directions, including to islands in Lake Kivu and the large island of Idjwi, and others south towards Bukavu, according to a Kalehe civil-society member who told BBC.

Umuryango.rw reported that Wazalendo fighters attacked Kavumu in Kabare territory on the morning of Sunday 13 April, that videos on social media showed fighters with DRC flags in Kavumu centre heading for the airport that M23 had taken two months earlier, and that, according to information, after a short fight M23 retook all of Kavumu; it added that information reaching BWIZA said many Wazalendo were killed, including the leader of the attack.

place: Kavumu airport, Kabare (about 25 km from Bukavu, per the page)
statement: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 fighters denied information spreading on social media from Burundians that they had been dispossessed of Kavumu airport in South Kivu, and that AFC/M23-Twirwaneho said the circulating information was false and urged people to beware of rumours, saying 'Wazalendo and FARDC have no strength'.

Bwiza reported that on the morning of Sunday 22 February [2026] security kept deteriorating in Kavumu, Kabare territory, after fighting the previous Saturday, and that a local resident said the fighting began after a Wazalendo fighter was taken to a health centre and could be heard from Katana to Kavumu.

place: Kamakombe and Mbayo villages, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare
statement: Bwiza reported that on Wednesday 30 July heavy fighting took place in Kamakombe village, Kabare territory, between M23 and a Wazalendo group, that it reportedly began on Tuesday at Mbayo village in Bugorhe groupement after M23 was reportedly reinforced at Kavumu airport, and that civil-society representatives said AFC/M23 rebels set out to drive the group out of Kamakombe on Wednesday morning.

place: Bukavu; Kavumu and Katana, Kabare territory
statement: Umuryango.rw reported that, according to residents, armed men suspected to include government soldiers and Wazalendo caused fear over the weekend in Bukavu and its outskirts and in Kavumu and Katana in Kabare territory, where they were accused of looting and killing civilians, and that Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi confirmed that about seven civilians were killed at Kavumu.

Umuryango.rw reported that Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi of South Kivu, speaking about the violence at Kavumu and nearby, said that it was not possible to confirm that those responsible were government soldiers and that they could be bandits who take advantage of the situation to buy weapons and frighten the population; he said it happened as troops at the front were being replaced by new teams.

Umuryango.rw reported that civil-society members issued a statement saying more than nine people were killed in these acts, that people were looted and others wounded, and that they blamed government forces and Wazalendo; it quoted Maitre Pascal Mupenda, a Kabare official, via RFI, as saying nine dead were being counted and that the soldiers should leave.
Umuryango.rw reported that on Saturday armed men fired into the air in Bukavu city before entering shops and small markets and looting, as Bukavu residents showed on social media.

Umuryango.rw reported that Kinshasa government spokesman Patrick Muyaya told Top Congo FM on Sunday that M23, which he called the Rwandan army, had approached and taken Nyabibwe and that all further attacks launched from Nyabibwe had been thwarted, and that rumours reaching Bukavu of M23 being 10 or 15 km away were false as they were in fact more than 100 km away.

Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on 28 August 2025 that since the night of Wednesday 27 August 2025 an alliance of Kinshasa's forces, which he listed as FARDC, FDLR, Mai Mai Wazalendo, mercenaries, Imbonerakure and the Burundian army, had been shelling densely populated areas of Minembwe (Mikenke) and Kalehe (Katana, Kavumu, Katasomwa, Nyabibwe) with CH-4 drones and heavy weapons.

Umuryango.rw reported that fighting at Nyangezi and Lurhala in Walungu territory began on 17 June 2025 and that, according to information from Nyangezi, about 45 km from Bukavu, many residents fled the trading centre on the morning of 18 June; it quoted a resident as saying the fighting started the day before and reached Weza.

Umuryango.rw reported that Wazalendo fighters attacked AFC/M23 positions at Katana, Mumosho and Chirunga in Kabare territory on the morning of 18 June, with residents explaining that Wazalendo tried to dislodge AFC/M23 from these areas.

Bwiza (English edition, byline Fred Karege) reported that on 20 May 2025 the DRC National Commission for Monitoring the Implementation of the Addis Ababa Agreement released a report detailing serious crimes against civilians in Goma and Bukavu between January and April 2025 during the occupation by AFC-M23, presented at the National Museum in Kinshasa by the commission's coordinator Alphonse Ntumba Lwaba.

UN News Kiswahili reported that, in Uvira city, local civil society organisations were reporting that about 12 civilians had been killed by armed groups since 18 January, and quoted UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric saying about 2,400 people had fled Uvira towards Kamanyola.

BBC News Gahuza reported that, according to Radio Okapi, calm returned to Uvira on Monday after clashes on Sunday between FARDC and Wazalendo in which 12 people, civilians and soldiers, died; Serge Kigwati, who heads civil society there, confirmed that the clashes arose because Wazalendo tried to disarm FARDC soldiers who had fled Bukavu and the FARDC refused.

place: Warehouses near Kalundu port, government offices and homes, Uvira city
statement: Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that, as Wazalendo and some FARDC soldiers returned to Uvira on Sunday, several incidents of looting occurred in warehouses near Kalundu port, in several government offices and in some people's homes, especially those of members of the Banyamulenge community.
Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that in the evening FARDC soldiers removed several Banyamulenge families who feared for their safety in Uvira and took them to a safe place.

Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, in a press release, warned that some AFC/M23 fighters were allegedly hiding in Uvira to cause chaos and blame the Wazalendo and the Congolese army, and confirmed that AFC/M23 had withdrawn to the Sange area although they were supposed to withdraw to Kamanyola.

Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that Corneille Nangaa, AFC/M23 coordinator, said on X that AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira in good faith and that he was appalled by acts of reprisal, looting of public property, targeted killings and the forced displacement of the Tutsi Banyamulenge community.

Umuseke (a Rwandan online outlet) reported that the FARDC and the Wazalendo, usual partners in fighting the M23, shot at each other openly on Thursday 1 May, with fighting starting at about saa kumi n'imwe in the morning at Kasenga and spreading quickly to surrounding areas, and that residents of Kakombe said gunfire continued on Friday and that they had no choice but to flee.

Umuseke reported that Burundian soldiers deployed to protect the town of Uvira refused to get involved in the FARDC-Wazalendo fighting, and that the Wazalendo said some FARDC soldiers had prepared a boat to take them to Kalemie if M23 fighters attacked Uvira.

Kigali Today (Rwanda) reported that residents of Uvira said that since AFC/M23 left, groups of young criminals backed by the Wazalendo broke into and looted the homes and churches of Banyamulenge and other Kinyarwanda speakers, and that the Impuzamashyirahamwe Iharanira Uburenganzira bwa Muntu (DPC) issued a letter on 18 January 2026 raising concern for the safety of Uvira residents, especially Banyamulenge.

place: Lemera, Uvira territory, South Kivu (travelling towards Mulenge)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that Colonel Fureko, a Banyamulenge and a recently integrated Wazalendo officer, was arrested on Saturday 8 November at Lemera, Uvira territory, while travelling to Mulenge, that former colleagues accused him of links to M23 and Twirwaneho, and that according to several sources Fureko and eight young Banyamulenge with him were beaten, wounded and stripped of their weapons and uniforms.

Mwananchi reported, without naming a source for this passage, that Wazalendo fighters had had to stand firm to defend the town of Uvira against M23 fighters after FARDC soldiers were alleged to have fled the fighting, with others taking canoes to escape to Kalemie.

BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi edition) reported that on the third day nobody could move around the town because of looting by armed people, including of the stores of charitable organisations, and quoted a statement posted on X by MSF saying that, unable to move around the town, medical teams and other aid workers were in danger, and that hospitals in the area kept receiving wounded people every day, including ordinary civilians.

Bwiza (a Rwandan outlet) reported that on Wednesday 31 December 2025 the DRC government, through its Communications Minister and spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, accused the Rwandan forces in a statement of attacks in the Kamanyola-Uvira areas 'with bombs and kamikaze drones' that, it said, killed more than 1,500 people and displaced about 500,000.

place: Highlands of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga, South Kivu
statement: Bwiza reported that Patrick Muyaya also accused the Rwandan forces of sending three battalions of soldiers into the highlands of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga, saying they were disguised as Twirwaneho fighters.

place: Uvira territory and Kamanyola axis, South Kivu
statement: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23, through its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, replied that what the Kinshasa government said was propaganda and lies intended to mislead the public.

place: Kamanyola, Luvungi, Sange and surroundings, Ruzizi plain
statement: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 said the killings of civilians in South Kivu during the previous month's fighting came from air attacks and shells fired by Kinshasa's forces including FARDC, FDLR, Mai-Mai Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and Burundi's national army, in areas including Kamanyola, Luvungi and Sange, with 8 killed and 55 wounded in Kamanyola alone.
Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 said that, in areas that government forces had tried to retake including Uvira and Makobola, those forces carried out 'acts of rape and organised looting'.

place: not stated in the cited passage
statement: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 accused government forces of having fired heavy and light weapons on residents who were holding a peaceful demonstration on 22 December.

place: Kadezi hills (between the Kaziba and Lubarika hills), about 70 km from Uvira city
statement: Umuseke (a Rwandan outlet), in a correction, reported that fighters of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), led by Joseph Kabila, had taken the Kadezi area, which it said is distinct from Kawezi as had continued to be reported, and that the Kadezi hills lie 70 kilometres from the town of Uvira; it said news of the capture had circulated on social media from the morning of Monday 26 October 2026.

place: Kiliba Haut, Kagando groupement, Uvira territory (Bijombo front)
statement: Analysons Kongo reported (dateline Uvira, 17 September 2026), citing The Great Lakes Eye, which cited an anonymous Burundian colonel, that twelve Burundian soldiers were allegedly killed by their own comrades after trying to leave their positions on the Bijombo front, in the night of 10 September at Kiliba Haut, Kagando groupement, Uvira territory; it said the FDNB had issued no communiqué confirming or denying the information.

place: Bijombo and Masango hills, Magunda direction, Uvira territory
statement: Rwanda Tribune reported that fighting began in the early hours of Saturday 10 October 2026 and that, according to residents, at around 'saa yine' in the morning fighters said to belong to the AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and Red-Tabara alliance attacked positions of the Wazalendo groups Binjigi and Masango, which repelled the attack, with fighting continuing towards Magunda; it said that as of writing no official statement had explained how the fighting ended or whether there were dead or wounded.

Umuryango (a Rwandan outlet) reported that the head of Kamanyola, Hassan Shabani, said that from 2 to 4 December about 150 shells fired from Burundi hit Kamanyola, killing eight residents; that a doctor at Saint-Joseph Hospital in Kamanyola said that while Burundian forces were firing on the town they received 55 wounded, including 27 seriously wounded who were sent to Bukavu general hospital; and that a resident whose wife and two children were killed told CTGL that a shell fell on their house and four people died.
Umuryango reported that Kamanyola head Hassan Shabani said that in the shelling of 2-4 December schools, civilians' houses and the hospital were hit, with eight people dead.

place: Uvira city (main military headquarters), South Kivu
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that a 12-year-old boy died of gunfire and at least nine other people were wounded during a protest in Uvira on Monday, and that the FARDC spokesperson in the area, Lt. Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said the child was killed when the army tried to stop protesters entering the main military office in the town.
BBC News Gahuza reported that the Associated Press, repeating South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, said the dead in the Uvira protest were three people, with five wounded.

place: Uvira city and surroundings, South Kivu
statement: Bwiza (a Rwandan outlet) reported that the DRC government had cut internet in the town of Uvira a few days after its forces returned, and that the DRC government had said nothing on the matter, while reports said President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi gave the order.

Bwiza reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, president of M23 and deputy coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo, said on X that the Kinshasa government's decision to cut internet in Uvira aimed to hide the bad acts its forces were committing there.

Bwiza reported that the UN Group of Experts on Congo report said the assault on Uvira was led directly by AFC/M23 military leaders Gen. Sultani Makenga and Bernard Byamungu, and that Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe, former Rwandan army chief of staff, 'played a major role in coordinating' the operation.

Bwiza reported that houses of Tutsi in Uvira were attacked by residents led by Wazalendo fighters who had returned to the town and looted everything, particularly in Tutsi homes, and that other reports said a church considered to be mostly Tutsi was looted that Sunday morning.
Bwiza reported that it was said five civilians had died in Uvira after the Wazalendo and FARDC returned, though the outlet said it could not confirm this.

Bwiza reported that the Banyamulenge organisation Amohoro Peace Association issued a statement saying Banyamulenge were in danger, that Uvira was heading into a humanitarian emergency, and that after AFC/M23's withdrawal under United States pressure Banyamulenge civilians were being hunted while Wazalendo groups were targeting, killing and looting the homes of people called 'Banyarwanda'.

BBC News Gahuza reported that the DRC government said it had ordered its troops not to confront the M23 as it advanced in Uvira, and explained that it wanted to avoid civilians losing their lives there.

BBC News Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a statement on X that for more than three months AFC/M23 had denounced hate speech, attacks on citizens because of their appearance, and killings 'in the liberated areas' of M23 carried out by fighters allied with the Kinshasa government and its accomplice Burundi, and that the town of Uvira was now 'liberated'.

place: Kavimvira and Kagenge quarters, Uvira city
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that Olivier Muhasha, one of the journalists in Uvira, told it that morning that the fighters had reportedly entered only two quarters, Kavimvira and Kagenge, while the others were in the hands of the government army and the Wazalendo, and that Uvira has 14 quarters.
BBC News Gahuza reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told Radio Okapi on Tuesday that Uvira was controlled by government troops, denying rumours that M23 rebels had entered the town.

Umuryango (a Rwandan outlet) reported that AFC/M23 shot down a FARDC Sukhoi-25 combat aircraft that had been used to attack it; according to information from South Kivu, the aircraft was hit in the air over Kalundu port, Uvira territory, at about saa saba in the afternoon of 26 December 2025 and fell into Lake Tanganyika, and two people aboard were said to have died.

place: Kalundu port and Kala, Uvira territory
statement: Umuryango reported that DRC forces attacked Kalundu port on Lake Tanganyika, where two AFC/M23 boats were said to have been hit and the fighters aboard died, and that DRC army combat drones hit AFC/M23 bases including one at Kala, Uvira territory, at the former MONUSCO base.

Umuryango reported that AFC/M23 fighters left Makobola in the afternoon of 25 December 2025 and were then attacked, and that DRC forces and Wazalendo went to take control of Makobola, as residents there confirmed.

place: Uvira city, including Kavimvira near the Burundi border
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that fighting on Tuesday between Wazalendo and FARDC in Uvira left people dead and created tension according to the town's authorities, that DRC media said about eight people had died, that part of the fighting took place in the Kavimvira area near the Burundi border, and that Radio RFI said it began over a disagreement between Wazalendo and FARDC on the entry of people coming from Burundi.

BBC News Gahuza reported that, in an official statement on the events, the provincial governor asked the Wazalendo and the government army to 'take measures to avoid falling into the enemy's trap', saying the enemy was spreading false information that he had surrounded the town of Uvira, and that Governor Jean Jacques Purusi, on the government side, convened an 'extraordinary meeting' with representatives of the army, religious leaders, youth and women, customary authorities and the leaders of the "Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie" or Wazalendo.

BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that Human Rights Watch said its researchers found evidence that 53 civilians (46 men, one woman and five boys) were summarily killed in attacks on residents' homes in different parts of Uvira after the Rwanda-backed fighters took the town in December, and that HRW visited three sites said to hold mass graves, one of them in a place permanently guarded by UN peacekeepers.

BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that Human Rights Watch said it investigated and documented eight cases of rape alleged against the M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers during their occupation of Uvira, and quoted a woman who said they stripped her, tied her hands behind her back with her clothes and raped her, and that her husband was shot dead when he tried to help her.

BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda had continued to deny backing M23 or deploying its soldiers in eastern DRC, and that M23 and the Rwandan government did not respond to the BBC's request for comment on HRW's findings on Uvira.

place: eastern DRC (statement about the Uvira-period conflict)
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Saturday night Burundi's foreign minister Edouard Bizimana wrote on X that it was important to stress Qatar's bad role in using its word and money to stop the United States from acting, and in the same post accused Rwanda of continuing to seize areas in eastern DR Congo contrary to the Washington agreement without the United States doing anything.

BBC News Gahuza reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, in what it described as correcting his foreign minister, said on X that Burundi had always praised Qatar's 'important role' in mediation on the DRC and that it was necessary to clarify 'whatever was not clearly understood and the wrong words' about Qatar's role.

place: Uvira, Kalehe and Mwenga areas, South Kivu
statement: UN News Kiswahili reported that, in South Kivu, about 20 civilians had been killed and 10 wounded since 23 March in fighting in the Uvira, Kalehe and Mwenga areas, and quoted the UN spokesperson saying that destruction of homes and livestock had forced many families to flee while access to food and health services remained limited.

Radio Okapi reported that, in reaction to Amnesty International's June 2026 report accusing the CMC-FDP armed group of serious abuses in Rutshuru, the CMC-FDP spokesperson categorically rejected the accusations and said that no official complaint had been filed before the movement's internal disciplinary or judicial bodies.

DW Swahili reported that Minister of Information and government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya accused the M23 of continuing the war and called their announcement of leaving Uvira 'upotoshaji' (a distortion/misinformation), saying it was a ploy to disrupt the mediator, the United States.

place: Goma, North Kivu (Ndosho and CBCA Virunga hospitals)
statement: Ouragan.cd reported a communiqué published on 6 March by Deputy Prime Minister for the Interior Jacquemain Shabani. In the article's account, Kigali deployed its troops on 28 February and on 3 and 4 March in the Ndosho and CBCA Virunga hospitals to take away patients, most of them Congolese soldiers, and their carers, and some of them were executed. The article then attributes to the Interior Ministry communiqué the statement that the Rwandan army and its M23 auxiliaries carried out incursions into Goma hospitals, taking about a hundred patients and carers, among them Congolese soldiers, and that they were summarily executed.

Actualite.cd reported that DRC Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba presented on 7 April a report on violations allegedly committed by AFC/M23 during the occupation of Uvira and its surroundings with Rwandan support; the government said it had counted more than 14 400 women raped, and the page gives two different figures for people killed, which it does not reconcile (see note).

place: Mayi Moto, Kilomani, Kala, Rutembo (Uvira area), South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the Congolese government said it had found several mass graves after the AFC/M23 left Uvira: three graves at Mayi Moto holding 115 bodies according to the government, one at Kilomani with 31 bodies, one at Kala and two at Rutembo.

Radio Okapi reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, speaking on Radio Okapi's Dialogue entre Congolais on Tuesday 20 January, confirmed that life had resumed in Uvira after the AFC/M23 withdrawal and that loyalist forces now controlled the city; he announced the imminent restoration of State authority.

UNE.CD reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi returned on Friday 23 January 2026 to Uvira, the provisional seat of provincial institutions, after the withdrawal of the AFC-M23; it said he, his provincial government and other officials had fallen back to Fizi-Baraka after the fall of Uvira on 10 December 2025. Kivutimes, reporting the same arrival, said instead that the provincial authority had been forced to flee to Bujumbura, in Burundi.

JamboRDC reported that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge, speaking to the press on Saturday 6 September, called on the residents of Uvira to stay calm and not to give in to enemy manipulation, after protests by Wazalendo and citizen movements demanding the departure of General Olivier Gasita.

MediaCongo Press reported that National Assembly president Vital Kamerhe announced on Monday 8 September 2025, after an inter-institutional meeting chaired by the head of state, that President Tshisekedi had decided to send a government mission to Uvira after protests against the appointment of General Gasita as head of military intelligence in the area.

Actualite.cd reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, reacting at a press briefing to recent Human Rights Watch and Global Witness reports on the security, humanitarian and natural-resources situation in AFC/M23-held areas, said the publications were not a surprise to the Congolese authorities and that Kinshasa was acting on a judicial front and an economic front.

place: Kinshasa (national statement on the FRN), other
statement: Radio Okapi reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, after the creation of the FRN, said that the former head of state's choice to take up arms was an attack on the Republic and the constitutional order.

Radio Okapi reported that, according to parliamentary sources, head of state Félix Tshisekedi told members of parliament and senators of the presidential majority that the emergence of the FRN was in no way a surprise to him.

place: Kabizo (Butare locality), Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the wife of local notable Rugamba and their five children (one boy and four girls) were killed by armed men who attacked their home at Kabizo, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, on the night of Thursday to Friday 3 July [2026], and that the Congolese army and the AFC/M23 each blamed the other.

place: Kabizo, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the 34th military region, Major Dieudonné Kasereka, rejected the AFC/M23's version of the Kabizo killings and denounced a disinformation campaign meant, in his words, to conceal abuses committed by RDF/AFC-M23 elements.

place: Kabizo, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that, on its X account, the AFC/M23 attributed the Kabizo attack to FDLR rebels, whom it accused of acting in collaboration with the FARDC.

Radio Okapi reported that Lieutenant-colonel Mutimura, spokesperson of the FDLR-FOCA, categorically rejected disarmament, justified armed struggle by the protection of Rwandan refugees and set as conditions an inter-Rwandan dialogue and a return in full dignity.

Radio Okapi reported that the Congolese army had issued an ultimatum to the FDLR a month earlier: surrender and lay down arms for repatriation to Rwanda, or face force; the army said the decision was taken within the implementation of the Washington accord of 27 June.

place: Eastern DRC, South Kivu / North Kivu
statement: DW Swahili reported that the Congolese army said M23's claims were not true and that a video showing fighters captured in Congo being handed over to Rwanda was 'forged'.

place: Kisangani, Tshopo (announcement); operations in eastern DRC
statement: DW Swahili reported that the Congolese army had started operations to hunt FDLR rebels, announced officially at Kisangani (Tshopo) by the deputy army commander, General Ychaligonza Jacques, who called on FDLR fighters to surrender.

Radio Okapi reported that the Minister of National Defence said at the Council of Ministers of Friday 6 February [2026] that the FARDC had defeated attacks by 'la coalition RDF-M23-AFC' in South Kivu by retaking several localities including Minembwe-centre.

place: Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory (Nyamilima, Kiseguru, Kasave, Rubare named), North Kivu
statement: Kigali Today reported that a statement issued by AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that the allegations of HRW and the UN were based on political motives, and accused these organisations of bias toward the DRC government; AFC/M23 also said that this could not replace HRW going there in person and that those it spoke to were known extremists and DRC government employees. The statement replied to an HRW report, published on 20 August 2025, saying that residents of areas near Virunga National Park, mostly Hutu, were killed in 14 villages between 10 and 30 July.

Kigali Today reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrance Kanyuka, standing in the city centre, spoke about the AFC/M23 departure from Uvira; Kanyuka said that Uvira had been a key stronghold of forces allied with the Kinshasa government, including Wazalendo, FDLR, Mai-Mai, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army. The outlet, in reported speech ('ngo'), added that since Uvira was 'liberated' things had reportedly been good and people lived in peace, with no obstruction, no theft and no abuse.

place: Goma, North Kivu (ceremony at Stade de l'Unité; burial at Mubambiro)
statement: Under a headline saying that the bodies of people killed by FARDC drones were buried in Goma, Kigali Today reported that at the ceremony the bodies were placed at the Stade de l’Unité, where bereaved families gathered; AFC/M23 political spokesperson Laurence Kanyuka said on X that they had met to honour the civilians killed, shot by the 'bloodthirsty' coalition forces working with the Kinshasa government.

Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on his X account that, besides Banyamulenge Congolese being killed, the DRC government was also forcibly removing people from their homes in Minembwe; the outlet wrote that among those known so far to have been killed in that area was the elder Rudaga Adriyani, aged 95, killed in drone attacks that the coalition of Kinshasa government forces carried out in the Minembwe areas on Monday 23 March 2026.

Umunota reported that Kimbulungu, secretary of AFC/M23, said that although the Congolese government and those close to it blamed AFC/M23 for the escape of Munzenze prison inmates and the deaths of the women there, these events happened before AFC/M23 fighters arrived; he also said that from 2 to 13 February AFC/M23 found 874 bodies in the city of Goma, although the Congolese government says about 3000 died.

place: Minembwe general hospital, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: MediaCongo, relaying ACP/MCP and citing the same military sources as its report on FARDC advances around Minembwe, reported that bombardments attributed to drones from Rwanda, which it called the aggressor country, targeted the Minembwe general hospital and some civilian homes on Wednesday morning.

place: Rubaya area, Masisi territory, North Kivu (strike location per BBC: near Rubaya)
statement: BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 confirmed the death of its military spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma, saying he was killed on the 24th of February in a 'full-scale war' it accuses Kinshasa of resuming; in a statement issued on Saturday, M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that the Kinshasa regime deliberately violated the ceasefire, mainly targeting AFC/M23 soldiers and civilians with its drones outside the front lines. The BBC reported that the DRC government had made no official announcement on the M23 statement or on Ngoma's death.

Reporter.cd reported that the DRC government, in an official 'mise au point' reframing a Human Rights Watch communiqué on Uvira, said that the RDF/M23 withdrawal from the city of Uvira on 17 January 2026 came after a period of systematic looting, large-scale theft, threats, intimidation and acts of community stigmatisation, and that at that stage no death or injury had been reported within the Banyamulenge community since the RDF/M23 withdrawal.

place: Kibuwa (Kibua) general referral hospital, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Okapinews reported that the Kibuwa general referral hospital, in the health zone of the same name in Walikale territory, North Kivu, was looted on Friday by M23 rebels during their withdrawal from the town, and that Dr Yves Tshongo, chief medical officer of the Kibuwa zone, confirmed this without giving details, saying the hospital had indeed been attacked by M23 elements.

place: Minembwe, Mikenge and Karingi, South Kivu highlands (Fizi/Mwenga)
statement: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 said it was saddened to see the international community remaining silent on killings being carried out by the Kinshasa government against residents of areas including Minembwe, Mikenge and Karingi in South Kivu; Kanyuka said these acts against innocent and defenceless civilians were being carried out by FARDC, FNDB, Wazalendo, FDLR and foreign mercenaries.

DW Kiswahili, in a piece one year after the fall of Goma, quoted humanitarian worker Mwende Kanane as saying there were even reports of rape in the prison before the prisoners escaped, and wrote that the security situation became more fragile after inmates escaped from Munzenze prison, which contributed to an increase in crime and cases of rape, especially against women; DW also wrote that, according to the United Nations, the number of people who died reached about 3,000.

place: Kiseguru, Binza groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Presse Actu reported that AFC-M23 rejected, on Thursday 4 June 2026, FARDC accusations implicating it in the summary execution of ten civilians in the locality of Kiseguru, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu; in a 'mise au point' the rebel movement called them 'allégations mensongères, infondées et politiquement motivées' (false, unfounded and politically motivated allegations).

place: Burundi (statement on deployment in eastern DRC)
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundi's Minister of National Defence and Veterans, Alain Tribert Mutabazi, defended the deployment of Burundian troops in the DRC, saying that this presence falls within a security cooperation agreement concluded between Bujumbura and Kinshasa.

BBC News Gahuza reported that, after M23 took Uvira, Burundi's foreign minister Édouard Bizimana told the news agency AFP that signing agreements and then not implementing them is contempt for everyone, first of all for President Trump.

BBC News Gahuza reported that Burundi's foreign minister Édouard Bizimana had told Radio RFI, before the capture of Uvira, that 'those troops' would leave only if the Kinshasa government asked for it, because it was with Kinshasa that they had made the agreement.

place: UN Security Council (statement on Burundi-Rwanda tension over Uvira)
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda's ambassador to the UN, Martin Ngoga, said that Rwanda has no plan to attack Burundi, and that M23 had also said earlier that it has no such plan.
BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 had said earlier that it has no plan to attack Burundi.

place: Muramvya (Burundi), statement on forces deployed in eastern DRC
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye on Friday praised the commitment of his country's defence and security forces deployed in the DRC, at a public broadcast held at the Royal stadium in Muramvya, Gitega province, and congratulated them for their courage and commitment.

place: Bujumbura (Burundi), statement on the war in eastern DRC
statement: Actualite.cd reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, as future president of the African Union, called on the United States, as guarantor of the Washington accords, to increase pressure on the parties so that they respect their commitments.

place: South Kivu (Banyamulenge communities), statement on Burundi
statement: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23, through its coordinator Corneille Nangaa, said it was concerned by the attitude of the Burundian president and incoming African Union chair, an attitude it said contributes to the persistence of targeted violence against Banyamulenge communities, and that it called on the international community and continental institutions to exercise sustained vigilance.

place: Mikalati, Bijombo groupement (Fizi territory), South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, according to concordant testimonies, Burundian soldiers posted at Mikalati intercepted several groups of women, men and young people from Minembwe who were trying to reach the Bijombo market to buy basic goods such as salt, sugar or soap. The outlet also wrote that an FDNB spokesperson was not available to answer these allegations and that in most cases the Burundian authorities have denied accusations of mistreating Banyamulenge.

La Libre reported that Kinshasa's troops, supported notably by Wazalendo militias and by Burundian army personnel, were forced to turn back when they were less than two kilometres from Minembwe airport; it wrote that several accounts from Congolese rebel circles and from Burundian ranks mention a large number killed in these clashes near Minembwe, with all figures between 100 and 150 Burundians in one morning, and that since the start of the Burundian intervention Bujumbura has published no 'credible' official figure.

place: Uvira, Minembwe and other places in the DRC, as listed by Kagame
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to Kagame, a contingent of more than twenty thousand Burundian soldiers was said to be operating in several provinces, notably Uvira, Minembwe, Kalemie, Kindu, Walikale and Kisangani, and that he accused Burundi of regular strikes against civilians, notably at Minembwe; the outlet wrote that at the time of publication the Burundian authorities had not reacted.

Radio Isanganiro, in a 'vrai ou faux' item on an online claim about Congolese officials moving their families from Uvira to Bujumbura and about Burundian soldiers in camps in Burundi, wrote that the Burundian army has never published such information and that reliable international media have never published information on the number of troops Burundi has, abroad or at home.

Ijambo.net reported that the Government of Rwanda, in a statement issued on Monday 2 March 2026, rejected the sanctions the United States had imposed on some senior RDF officers, saying they were biased and aimed at presenting a picture contrary to the truth about the long-running insecurity in eastern DRC. The outlet reported that the US named Maj Gen Vincent Nyakarundi, Maj. Gen Ruki Karusisi, Gen Mubarakh Muganga and Brig Gen Stanislas Gashugi, and that Rwanda said the US had ignored drone and ground attacks by DRC forces that it said continued despite the agreement to stop fighting and killed many civilians.

place: Uvira (the HRW report's subject); statement made online
statement: Umuryango.rw (Rwandan outlet) reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo, in a post on X on 14 May 2026, criticised Human Rights Watch, writing (in the outlet's Kinyarwanda rendering) that HRW has its way of working and Rwanda is always its measure showing that it has worked well. The outlet described the HRW report of 13 May as accusing Rwandan soldiers and fighters of the armed group M23 of killing civilians, abducting them and raping women in the city of Uvira from 10 December 2025 to 17 January 2026.

place: Kigali (statement); sanctions concern the eastern DRC conflict
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe, in a France 24 interview broadcast on Monday, wondered why Rwanda 'alone' is being sanctioned although the US-led peace agreement signed in December 2025 concerns both sides, and said of the sanctions: 'Those sanctions first of all are unfair to us, they concern one side and are not productive.'

A Rwandan broadcaster's website reported that Rwanda's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Olivier Nduhungirehe, writing on X, disputed remarks by US adviser Massad Boulos by saying AFC/M23 had completed its withdrawal from Uvira weeks before the US imposed sanctions on the RDF; the outlet reported him saying AFC/M23 began leaving Uvira on 16 December 2025 and completed its withdrawal on 17 January 2026, and that the Congolese army later returned to the city alongside Burundian forces, the FDLR and Wazalendo armed groups.

Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that Paul Kagame, asked about the capture of Uvira on 10 December (six days after the Washington agreement) and US pressure, said that 'they' wanted to convince people there was a link between the capture of Uvira and the Washington agreement and that it was a way of rejecting the agreement, 'That is not true at all', and added that whether or not the Washington agreement was signed, 'the capture of Uvira was necessary'.

Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that Paul Kagame, asked whether he agreed with the reading that Rwandan troops are on eastern DRC soil after Rwanda's ambassador in Washington said on 22 January that Rwanda has 'security cooperation with AFC/M23', answered 'Yes, of course', and said that defensive measures mean protecting Rwanda and its borders from threats, including using military equipment and sending troops on the ground, and that if guarding the border requires dealing with the problem 5, 10 or 20 kilometres back, it is a defensive measure.

Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that, asked about repeated reports that M23 has violated human rights and forcibly put people into the army since taking Goma in January 2025, Paul Kagame answered that he would accept that allegation if told that Goma has more peace than before M23 went there, and said things are now better than before and that Goma and Bukavu are doing well.

Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that Paul Kagame said that M23 is not a Rwandan group but a Congolese group that came to be called AFC/M23, which also includes former president Joseph Kabila.

Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that Paul Kagame said that in areas M23 holds it works well in confronting 'these criminals', but in the territories of Masisi, Walikale and elsewhere where FARDC operate, the FDLR are still present in cooperation with the government.

Umunota.com (Rwandan outlet) reported that Rwanda's Foreign Minister, Amb Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe, said in an RBA interview on the evening of 10 December 2025 that Rwanda is not the one to answer for ceasefire violations, but the FDLR and Burundian troops, who he said have a plan to destabilise Rwanda's security.

Umunota.com reported that Foreign Minister Nduhungirehe, in the same RBA interview, said that Burundian soldiers in South Kivu had now reached twenty thousand, a problem he said Rwanda has raised repeatedly, and alleged that they prevent the Banyamulenge from leaving their areas so as to starve them.

place: Burundian troop positions in the DRC (location not specified)
statement: Umunota.com reported that, on the Monday of the week of publication, Burundi's Foreign Minister Bizimana Edouard, speaking with representatives of countries in Burundi, said that Rwanda had attacked the positions of Burundian troops in the DRC and allegedly had a plan to attack them, and that they would therefore defend themselves.
Umunota.com reported that Muyaya, in a message posted on X, said that all the attacks launched on the Banyamulenge in Minembwe were launched by M23 together with Rwanda.

Umunota.com reported that Makolo, replying to Muyaya, said his words were a ploy to shift the crimes of FARDC onto M23, and wrote: 'Accusing others of what you do, where the one who committed crimes pins them on the one they were committed against. It is usually used to encourage people to violence or genocide.'

BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda's President Paul Kagame, at a gathering with some Kigali residents on Sunday, asked Rwandans to prepare to face sanctions, which he called 'gufunga umukandara' (tightening the belt).

place: Kigali (statements); sanctions concern the eastern DRC conflict
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Rwandan government had not yet said anything publicly about the new EU sanctions (on Generals Ruki Karusisi, Eugène Nkubito and Pascal Muhizi), but that regarding the earlier sanctions by the United Kingdom, America and Canada, Rwandan officials say those sanctions do not help resolve the war in DR Congo and undermine Africa's effort to seek a peaceful solution.

BBC News Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Oscar Balinda said that gold and coltan mined in the east of the DRC pass through Rwanda but only in transit to foreign markets; that he said the Amnesty report was the same as others published by organisations he said are paid by the Kinshasa government to tarnish the name of AFC/M23, and the outlet wrote that he gave no evidence for this; and that Amnesty said AFC/M23 had not answered its questions, while AFC/M23 denies that Amnesty ever approached it.

A Rwandan broadcaster's website reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe, speaking to AFP in Moscow on 28 October 2026, defended Rwanda against accusations over the conflict in eastern DRC, saying the country should not be blamed for political and security problems that require Congolese solutions; he said Rwanda must not be held as a scapegoat for what is happening in Congo forever, and rejected Kinshasa's description of former Congolese president Joseph Kabila as a Rwandan proxy.

BBC Gahuza reported, citing its Kinshasa correspondent, that the Congolese army (FARDC) confirmed it had carried out strikes on Rubaya centre on Tuesday that 'killed' AFC/M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma.

BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka wrote on X at about 5 a.m. on Tuesday that the drone attacks 'fired blindly' at the Rubaya area 'killing innocent civilians', calling it a 'crime against humanity and a war crime'.

Umusare News reported that, in a statement, AFC/M23 said that 'such cruelty against a civilian aircraft carrying aid is exceptional inhumanity' and that it ended the chance of delivering to residents what they needed while they 'have been besieged for years, without access to the market'.

Umusare News reported that, on state radio-television, the DR Congo army spokesperson Gen. Maj. Sylvain Ekenge said appropriate measures were taken against an aircraft that 'flew into Congolese airspace without authorisation'.

place: Lumbishi/Rumbishi, Chambombo, Cyamatare, Gasovu, Kalehe highlands, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué, the AFC-M23 accused the 'coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime' of launching simultaneous heavy-artillery attacks on densely populated areas of Kalehe territory (Rumbishi, Chambombo, Cyamatare and Gasovu), which spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said caused several deaths and forced many civilians to flee. The outlet added that the Congolese army had not yet reacted.

place: Minembwe axis (Rugezi, Kalingi, Gakenke, Bidegu), South Kivu; Lubero axis (Kabesebese, Mutondi), North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 accused the Congolese army of launching several attacks on its positions on 31 March 2026 and said the coalition of the Kinshasa regime (FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo militias, mercenaries and the Burundian National Defence Force) launched generalised attacks on all front lines and that, according to spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, fighting was recorded on the Minembwe axis (Rugezi, Kalingi, Gakenke, Bidegu); the AFC-M23 communication also listed the villages of Kabesebese and Mutondi on the Lubero axis as under attack.

Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23, in a message on X by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, accused the FARDC and allied Wazalendo of looting, targeted violence and hate speech in Uvira after the AFC/M23 withdrawal, and said that loyalist forces had also multiplied attacks on its positions in the Fizi highlands and that there had been recent clashes at Kipese (Lubero) and Kasoko (Masisi).

place: Minjenje and Kibati, Walikale, North Kivu; Minembwe area (Mukoko, Rugezi, Point Zéro), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué, AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka accused coalition forces of Kinshasa, the FDLR, Wazalendo militias, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian National Defence Force of intensifying operations on several fronts on Sunday 13 September 2026, and said attacks on Walikale territory began around 14:00 against Minjenje and Kibati, with ground and air operations including drones and heavy artillery.

Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué, AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the whole of May 2026 was marked by intensified land and air offensives by the 'coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime' against densely populated areas and its positions, notably at Minembwe, Masisi, Numbi and Walikale, and that any attack would now receive a proportionate response; the outlet added that other fighting was reported on the Kibati axis, on the border of Walikale and Masisi territories, with AFC-M23 accusing the army of attacking its areas with heavy artillery.

Ijambo reported that AFC/M23 appointed new authorities for North Kivu and Goma city in a statement posted on X by Laurence Kanyuka, AFC/M23 political spokesperson, naming Bahati Musanga Joseph governor of North Kivu, with Manzi Ngarambe Willy as vice-governor for politics, administration and legal affairs.

place: villages near Virunga National Park, Rutshuru, North Kivu
statement: BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 said a Human Rights Watch report accusing it of killing at least 140 civilians, mostly Hutu, in the previous month was 'a lie and distortion of the truth', that it had already rejected the allegations as 'unfounded' in a document of 7 August, and that a statement issued by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the HRW and UN allegations were politically motivated and biased towards the 'incapable' Kinshasa government.

place: villages near Virunga National Park, Rutshuru, North Kivu
statement: BBC Gahuza reported that the Rwandan government said, in a statement given to BBC Newshour, that the RDF has 'nothing to do with' the killings alleged in Human Rights Watch's report, that 'M23 is not controlled by Rwanda' and that M23 should be asked about these matters.

Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a communiqué on his X account, accused the FARDC of attacks on its positions and said that at least three civilians were killed and five others injured in a FARDC strike at Kamanyola.

place: Katogota-Luvungi axis (Uvira); Rugezi and Ngungu (Minembwe, Fizi); Kaziba (Walungu); Kasika (Mwenga); Civanga-Hombo (Kalehe)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that the 33rd military region of the FARDC, based at Uvira, said it had stopped attacks by AFC-M23 fighters, and that the region's spokesperson Captain Sylvain Bijanu said these 'enemies of peace' had also attacked its positions at Rugezi and Ngungu (Minembwe), Kaziba (Walungu), Kasika (Mwenga) and Civanga-Hombo (Kalehe).

place: Lumbishi, Katale, Tushunguti (Kalehe); Mikenge (Minembwe highlands), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a statement on X, the AFC/M23 spokesperson said the 'Kinshasa regime, through its coalition forces' launched generalised attacks on several axes targeting civilian populations on Tuesday 7 April 2026, with attacks, per the movement, spreading from 06:50 to Lumbishi, Katale and Tushunguti in Kalehe territory where civilian areas were also hit.

Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X on Monday 24 March 2025 that, contrary to the communiqué of Sunday 23 March 2025, the FARDC and their coalition forces had not withdrawn their attack drones from Walikale; he said this delayed the repositioning of AFC/M23 forces in the area and was a major obstacle to respect for the ceasefire.

place: Nzimbira, Mwenga, Bunyakiri, Kibuwa, Pinga and Uvira (South Kivu / Walikale area)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23, in a communiqué signed by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, accused the Congolese authorities of continuing 'offensive military manoeuvres', citing troop and materiel movements at Nzimbira, Mwenga, Bunyakiri, Kibuwa, Pinga and Uvira, and said two military ships carrying more than 1 125 fighters of the 'coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime' docked at Uvira on Sunday 10 August from Kalemie.

place: Malemo and Kalembe (and Bweru), between Masisi and Walikale, North Kivu
statement: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23, in a statement issued by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, said that around 22:00 on the night of Sunday 24 May 2026 FDLR fighters supported by Wazalendo attacked the villages of Malemo and Kalembe between Masisi and Walikale; Kanyuka said seven civilians were killed and three seriously injured at Malemo, and three killed, nine injured and a village chief abducted at Kalembe, and that the fighters looted 11 cows and many pigs at Bweru.

place: Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje, Kibati, Buhimba, Masisi and Walikale, North Kivu
statement: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X on Thursday 10 September 2026 that, from 05:00, forces of the Kinshasa government and the groups supporting them intensified attacks on populated areas on the edges of Masisi and Walikale (Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje, Kibati and surroundings), that at about 07:00 they attacked Buhimba (Masisi) with ground forces using 82 mm mortars and 12.7 mm machine guns, and that aid organisations and their staff had difficulty reaching affected residents.

Bwiza reported, citing reliable information reaching it, that AFC/M23 fighters regained control of Remeka in Masisi territory after a commando operation on the night of Wednesday 23 September 2026, and that the capture was also confirmed by Ngarambe Manzi Willy, whom the outlet calls the Deputy Governor of North Kivu Province, in a message on X.

Bwiza reported that AFC/M23, through spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, said that an attack at 18:30 on Sunday 29 March, when the coalition of DRC government forces entered the densely populated centre of Shanji, killed people it named as Shadai Ndagije, Bisengi Mpenze, Gitinywa Etienne, Gashimye Hitimana, Daniel Hategeka, Ndayambaje Muhire and Iradukunda Nsanzumuhire, and injured more than 20 others.

place: Kipese, Munyakondomi, Ivatama, Ilambula, Luseke, Musimba (Lubero), North Kivu
statement: Bwiza reported that, since Monday 23 March, AFC/M23 had started withdrawing troops from areas it controlled in Lubero territory, including Kipese, Munyakondomi, Ivatama, Ilambula, Luseke and Musimba, and that information from inside AFC/M23 said the group took the decision to pull out of areas it had controlled for more than a year as a confidence-building measure toward resolving the conflict peacefully.

Bwiza reported that AFC/M23, in a statement by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, said that on Sunday 28 June 2026 at around 01:00 the coalition of forces of the Kinshasa government burned many civilian houses at Lumbishi (Kalehe) after organised looting, and that entire families perished in the fire.

place: Irundu and Nyarujoka (Minembwe highlands); Uvira (city), South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué published on Tuesday 25 February 2025, AFC/M23 said that several villages of Minembwe, notably Irundu and Nyarujoka, were bombed that day, and alerted to a rise in persecution of the Banyamulenge community in Uvira city, which it said took the form of arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances and other repression; the outlet added that the Congolese authorities had not officially reacted to the accusations.

place: Kuwihene, Rugezi axis, Minembwe region (South Kivu); Kacyayi, Kumungoti and Marangara (Masisi, North Kivu)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 said on Sunday 11 October 2026 that the Congolese armed forces and their allies had intensified offensives against civilians in North and South Kivu, and that, according to spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, at 06:15 those forces intensified ground offensives towards Kuwihene on the Rugezi axis in the Minembwe region, with FDLR elements on the front line alongside foreign mercenaries, causing deaths and mass displacement of civilians.

Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on 26 July 2025, FARDC spokesperson Maj. Gen. Sylvain Ekenge called 'unfounded' the MRDP-Twirwaneho claims that FDLR elements trained in Burundi had infiltrated to commit targeted massacres of Banyamulenge, described them as an attempt at manipulation, and said the FARDC held verified information on a planned massacre at Minembwe involving Twirwaneho in collaboration with Red Tabara.

Bwiza reported that M23 rebels took control of Katogota, about 80 km north of Uvira, on the Thursday before publication, and that M23 had so far neither confirmed nor denied its presence there, while videos circulating on social media showed armed men claiming to belong to M23 in the area.

place: Masisi territory (Masisi), North Kivu; symbolic burial held at the Unity Stadium, Goma
statement: The Associated Press reported that M23 claimed that the attack of 2 January in the Masisi territory, which it said targeted its military positions, was carried out by the FARDC and their allies, and that the rebel group said all the victims are civilians, a claim questioned by at least one expert.

place: Goma (Unity Stadium), North Kivu; strikes in Masisi territory
statement: The Associated Press reported that the administrator of the Masisi territory, Emmanuel Ndizeye, said at the ceremony that the area had been hit by 'a series of bombings', and that the bodies transferred to Goma came only from areas accessible by road.

The Associated Press reported that Erasto Musanga, named as the governor of North Kivu by the M23 administration, accused President Félix Tshisekedi of being responsible for the violence, saying 'Even as we speak, Tshisekedi is killing more people', and threatened legal action through the M23's own justice system.

place: Goma, North Kivu (statement made in Kinshasa)
statement: The Associated Press reported that Patrick Muyaya, the spokesperson for the Congolese government, said in a post on X that the funeral held on Thursday was 'the height of indecency and inhumanity'.

place: Rugezi, Minembwe region, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a post on his X account that in the night of 21 to 22 October 2026 the coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime intensified their bombardments of the densely populated zone of Rugezi, in the Minembwe region, using kamikaze drones and heavy artillery fire, and that the bombardments were continuing.

place: Luvungi, Lubarika and the Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a post on his X account that the Kinshasa regime had entered a decisive phase of its military preparations and was preparing a large-scale offensive mobilising land forces, air assets and heavy artillery simultaneously, reinforcing troops and military equipment at Luvungi and Lubarika.

place: Luvungi, Lubarika and the Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
statement: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a post on his X account that there were movements of Burundian troops crossing the Ruzizi river towards the Ruzizi plain, joining other elements gathered at the established headquarters, and that foreign mercenaries were also part of the military set-up.

place: 12th military region, Kongo-Central (statement issued by FRN in eastern DRC)
statement: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a post on his X account that Brigadier General François Kamanzi, commander of operations of the 12th military region in Kongo-Central, had joined the 'Lions de Sarambwe' within the Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC), having chosen to break with the Kinshasa regime whose daily attacks, the post says, deliberately target civilian populations.

place: statement issued by FRN in eastern DRC
statement: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in the same post that two other officers had also joined the FRN's ranks, that their identities would be made public in the coming days, and encouraged other FARDC members and all Congolese to join the FRN.

place: eastern DRC (HRW report covering Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps); statement published via X
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X that the movement strongly rejects the Human Rights Watch report as 'very biased' (ibogamye cyane), selective, containing untruths and not matching realities on the ground.

place: eastern DRC (HRW report covering Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps); statement published via X
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that Kanyuka added that the HRW report again focuses almost entirely on AFC/M23 while greatly downplaying or ignoring the very serious abuses committed by the combined forces of the Kinshasa regime, and that this approach raises serious questions about the neutrality and credibility of its conclusions.

place: eastern DRC (HRW report covering Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps); statement published via X
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 firmly denies 'these allegations', which in the article refer to the abduction of young men and boys and their military training, and that Kanyuka said its mobilisation activities are carried out openly, without hiding them, and 'voluntarily'.

place: eastern DRC (HRW report covering Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps); statement published via X
statement: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda's foreign minister Olivier Nduhungirehe replied to BBC Gahuzamiryango by WhatsApp that the Rwandan government does not respond to HRW reports of this kind, saying 'Ntacyo. Ntitujya dusubiza HRW.' (Nothing. We never respond to HRW.)

place: Point-Zéro and Nyamabuguma, Minembwe region, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from 14:00 on Thursday 10 September 2026 until late at night the coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime continued indiscriminate bombardments with kamikaze drones against Point-Zéro and Nyamabuguma in the Minembwe region.

place: Rurambo and Bijombo axes (Kirungwa, Munanira, Gataka, Zikambitse-Marimba, Rubarati, Kajoka), Uvira/Fizi highlands, South Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to Twirwaneho spokesperson colonel Fidèle Rugabo, two battalions, 'dont celui des Hiboux et des forces burundaises' (the wording is ambiguous: including that of the Hiboux and of Burundian forces), had been deployed on the Rurambo axis, and that on the Bijombo axis four battalions of the FARDC and of the Burundian army, with elements of the P5 and Wazalendo, were visible towards Kirungwa, Munanira, Gataka, Zikambitse-Marimba, Rubarati and Kajoka.

place: Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese areas; Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga, North Kivu
statement: Into Rwanda reported that a statement released by Erasto Bahati, whom it calls the Governor of North Kivu Province, dismissed reports of an AFC/M23 pull-back, saying that what is happening is a routine rotation of troops, and quoted the statement as saying the activities along the battlefront are part of the regular military troop rotations within AFC/M23.

place: Kigali (statement on the eastern DRC conflict)
statement: A pro-government Rwandan outlet reported that on Wednesday, 2 July 2025, the Rwandan government spokesperson Makolo Yolande set out Rwanda's position on the report of the group of UN experts (whom the outlet calls 'so-called' experts), and that she criticised the group for what the outlet calls lies in the report aimed at distorting the truth.

place: Kigali (statement on the eastern DRC conflict)
statement: The outlet (pro-government) reported that Makolo Yolande said the UN experts' report confirms that the FDLR is helped by the Congolese government, but that the experts deliberately discount the concerns of Rwanda that led to the putting in place of defensive measures.

place: Rubaya mining site (Masisi territory, North Kivu) and Lomera (Kabare territory, South Kivu)
statement: JamboRDC reported that in a mise au point published on Tuesday, signed by Bertrand Bisimwa, deputy coordinator of the AFC/M23, the movement said it rejects 'formally and as a whole' the accusations in Amnesty International's report on the Rubaya and Lomera mining sites, which it judges 'not established and insufficiently substantiated'.

place: Rubaya mining site (Masisi territory, North Kivu) and Lomera (Kabare territory, South Kivu)
statement: JamboRDC reported that the AFC/M23 said each case alleged by Amnesty should establish the reality of the alleged facts, their date and place, the identity of the alleged perpetrators and any link with the AFC/M23 and its chain of command, and that 'an accusation does not in itself constitute proof'.

place: Bujumbura (Burundi); the armed groups named operate in eastern DRC
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundian authorities presented 13 people to journalists on 9 October, a majority of them Banyamulenge refugees, whom the authorities accused of espionage for Rwanda and for armed groups active in eastern RDC; Pierre Nkurikiye said the suspects collaborated with armed groups active in the region, including the AFC/M23, Red-Tabara and Twirwaneho.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that, on the occasion of the presentation of the suspects, the spokesperson of the ministry in charge of security, Pierre Nkurikiye, called on Burundians to monitor the Banyamulenge and to stop renting houses to them.

Actualite.cd reported that Burundi's permanent representative to the UN, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, in his presentation on Friday 12 December 2025, accused Rwanda of having favoured the taking of Uvira in violation of the Washington accords and resolution 2773, and quoted him as saying Burundi was particularly concerned by cross-border attacks, including artillery and drones, some of which reached localities of Burundian territory.

UMUSEKE reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said the RDC government cannot pursue the process of halting the fighting while it is itself the one starting the war; she was replying to Patrick Muyaya, minister of information, who had explained that President Tshisekedi said Rwanda was violating the agreements by launching attacks in South Kivu. UMUSEKE also reported that Makolo stressed that Rwanda has nothing to do with the fighting continuing in South Kivu.

place: Beni, Ituri, Kwamouth, Goma, Minembwe, Uvira (as listed by the speaker)
statement: Umuryango.rw reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said Kayikwamba's message was meant to mislead and that the DRC government should not hide its failure to protect Congolese from its own army and armed groups, and quoted her saying that it is not Rwandans who are killing in Beni, Ituri, Kwamouth, Goma, Minembwe or Uvira.
Umuryango.rw reported that the Government of Rwanda said that reports of the UN human rights office (OHCHR) in the DRC show that armed groups, the FARDC and the FDLR are the ones raping civilians.

The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda published a "response" to the Human Rights Watch report of 14 May 2026, saying that the 14 May report claimed that the M23 and Rwandan forces, and no longer the Wazalendo, were the principal threat to the civilians covered in HRW's January 2026 statement, and that the conduct of the FARDC and Wazalendo in Uvira and the surrounding territory had not been the subject of a comparable 23-page investigative report.

The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda published a response to a post by Muyaya and to an HRW report, saying that nowhere in the HRW document is Rwanda attributed responsibility for the mass graves, and that the same report documents summary executions and sexual violence by the FARDC and Wazalendo against South Kivu populations before and during their withdrawal from Uvira.

The Rwandan Ministry of Defence website published a "fact-checking" stating that Jean-Jacques Purusi accused Rwanda and the AFC/M23 of being responsible for the massacres in Uvira, pointing to mass graves, and responding that since the AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira the city has been in chaos, with killings, looting and sexual violence in several neighbourhoods.

place: High Plateaus of South Kivu (Hauts Plateaux), incl. Minembwe area
statement: The Rwandan Ministry of Defence website published a "fact-checking" stating that in the High Plateaus of South Kivu the Banyamulenge have faced systematic attacks by a coalition of Maï-Maï groups operating in collaboration with the FARDC, involving killings, rape, the burning of villages, mass theft of cattle and "even drone strikes by the Congolese government".

Bwiza reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo, on X, accused Muyaya of continuing to turn the day of remembrance for the victims of the Gatumba killings into a platform for spreading messages against Rwanda; Bwiza reported that Muyaya had also accused Rwanda of having links with M23 and with the Twirwaneho and Red-Tabara groups.

The Rwandan Ministry of Defence website published a "fact-checking" responding to Jean-Jacques Purusi's accusation that the AFC/M23 slaughtered Banyamulenge cattle to frame the FARDC, stating that multiple recent reports describe drone strikes affecting the Minembwe area in South Kivu that hit civilians and property, including injuries and deaths.

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/509 of 17 March 2025 states that on 25 January 2025 the EU High Representative expressed deep concern at the escalation of the conflict in eastern DRC, aggravated by the renewed offensive of the M23 armed group supported by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), and that the RDF's unauthorised presence in the DRC violates its territorial integrity.
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/509 of 17 March 2025 states that revenues from the illegal extraction and trafficking of natural resources from eastern DRC are used to fund, among others, the M23, and adds nine persons and one entity to the EU's DRC sanctions list (Annex Ia to Regulation (EC) No 1183/2005).
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: The EU listed Bertrand Bisimwa on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), describing him as leader (president) of the political branch of the M23, born 8 September 1972 in Bukavu, Congolese, and stating that he holds a leading position as President of the M23.
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: The EU listed Major-General Ruki Karusisi, also known as Rocky, on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), describing him as Commander of the Special Force Command of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), Rwandan, born 6 May 1974, and stating that he is the commander of the RDF Special forces deployed in eastern DRC.
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: The EU listed Désiré Rukomera on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), describing him as head of recruitment and propaganda of the M23, Rwandan, holding that position since January 2024.
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: The EU listed John Imani Nzenze, also known as Mike Bravo, on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), describing him as 'Colonel' and 'G2' intelligence chief of the M23, Congolese, born 6 August 1978 in Kakwende (South Kivu).
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: The EU listed Major-General Eugène Nkubito on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), describing him as Commander of the 3rd Division of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), deployed in eastern DRC and more specifically in North Kivu, a position held since August 2022.
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: The EU listed Brigadier-General Pascal Muhizi on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), describing him as Brigadier-General of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) since June 2021 and Commander of the RDF 2nd Division, deployed in eastern DRC since August 2023.
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: The EU listed Jean-Bosco Nzabonimpa Mupenzi on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), describing him as Deputy Chief of Finances and Production of the M23/ARC, born in Rubaya, Masisi, North Kivu, Congolese, operating in North Kivu since January 2024.
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: The EU listed Francis Kamanzi on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), describing him as Chief Executive Officer of the Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board (RMB) since February 2024, and stating that minerals exploited in M23-controlled mining areas are trafficked to Rwanda and mixed with Rwandan production.
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
