statement: The EU listed Joseph Musanga Bahati, also known as Erasto, Bahati Erasto, Colonel Erasto and Colonel Bahati Musanga, on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), describing him as Governor of North Kivu, born 18 August 1978 in Bashali-Mokoto (Busumba), Congolese, Chief of Finance of the M23 for several years and appointed governor of North Kivu in January 2024 within the M23 'administration'.
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

place: Eastern DRC (as stated in the act)
statement: The EU listed Gasabo Gold Refinery, established in Kigali, Rwanda, on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), stating that it began refining on 1 June 2022 after the closure of Aldango Gold Refinery and that gold transiting through it contributes to the illicit export via Rwanda of illegally extracted gold.
sources: Official Journal of the European Union

statement: The New Humanitarian reported that a civil society activist in Uvira said that for three months the state was completely absent in the city, that there were abuses, and that people were whipped, arrested and some died in detention; the article ties this to a militia-led policing force that residents said carried out arbitrary arrests.

The New Humanitarian reported that a Banyamulenge woman who has lived in Uvira all her life said she was attacked by six Wazalendo fighters, three in plain clothes and three in uniform, while fetching water at a tap; that the attackers called them 'Rwandans'; and that she was beaten with sticks 'until I couldn't even scream anymore'. The article does not date the attack.

The New Humanitarian reported that demonstrations organised against Gasita in Uvira turned violent when Congolese military forces fired on unarmed protesters, killing at least one person and wounding several others, including children.

The New Humanitarian reported that the self-proclaimed Wazalendo police chief for South Kivu, General Kimanuka Musasa Nyambwe Nungisa, denied that the militias have implemented a taxation system and said they came to defend Uvira when authorities and security services fled.

The New Humanitarian reported that the Congolese army carried out raids in search of alleged M23 collaborators, mainly in hotels across Uvira, and that these operations led to arbitrary arrests and contributed to a climate of fear, particularly among Banyamulenge.

The New Humanitarian, in an article about Uvira, reported that in September Wazalendo fighters disrupted the funeral of an army colonel, a Tutsi officer from the region, and his wife (both had died in a plane crash), accusing the relatives of collaborating with Rwanda, and that witnesses reported Wazalendo militants declaring that no 'Rwandan' should be buried on Congolese soil. The article does not state where the funeral took place or name the colonel.

date: 2026 (page undated; '2 mois ago' on a copy saved about 2026-10-29)
statement: Foxtime.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi officially announced the discovery of at least 344 bodies in three mass graves in the city of Uvira and its outskirts, brought to light after the withdrawal of the AFC/M23.

date: 2026 (page undated; '2 mois ago' on a copy saved about 2026-10-29)
statement: Foxtime.cd reported that the military judiciary has already opened investigations directly targeting the commanders and leaders of the AFC/M23 coalition to formally establish responsibility for what the outlet called 'this barbarity', in its article on the Uvira mass graves.
Afrique Diplo reported that the FARDC stated that a Burundian was arrested in Uvira for propaganda in favour of the M23/Red-Tabara, while another person is accused of espionage activities.

place: Kinshasa (presentation); North Kivu and South Kivu (arrests)
statement: Afrique Diplo reported that on Saturday 3 January 2026 in Kinshasa the Congolese army presented to the press seven soldiers it identified as members of the Rwanda Defence Force and eight foreign civilians, arrested during recent fighting against the AFC/M23 in North Kivu and South Kivu.

place: Rumangabo (Rutshuru, North Kivu), where IGIHE says the soldiers are held; Kinshasa
statement: IGIHE, a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that RFI had announced on 8 April 2026 that the ICRC was ready to take 'these soldiers' to Kinshasa but that the DRC government had not yet agreed to receive them for fear that they might include 'enemies'.

Xtrafrica published a transcript-style account of an RFI interview in which DRC government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said that, according to Kinshasa, the invasion of Uvira was organised under Kigali's direct command and that bombs and kamikaze drones were used indiscriminately against peaceful civilians.

place: Murambya, Minembwe area (Fizi / Mwenga / Uvira highlands), South Kivu
statement: IGIHE, a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, published an opinion piece alleging that, with Minembwe, Bijombo and Rurambo encircled, the Banyamulenge live in separate ghettos, with their freedom of movement denied and their activities subject to roadblocks, permanent police checks, extortion and regular abuses 'up to murder', citing that of 'the young Singaye Marebo at Murambya'. The passage does not say who killed him, when, or where Murambya is.

IGIHE, a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that Burundian army spokesperson General Gaspard Baratuza, in a radio interview with BBC Gahuza, mentioned the presence of FNL and Red Tabara fighters at Minembwe.

place: Sake Afya referral health centre (Centre de Santé de Référence Sake Afya), Sake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to the communication cell of the North Kivu governorate, the operating theatre of the Sake Afya referral health centre (CSR) in Masisi territory had been ransacked and vandalised during the latest clashes in the area, making surgical interventions almost impossible; the article does not say who damaged it. It reported that the vice-governor of North Kivu, Schadrack Amani, of the Front pour la refondation de la Nation (FRN), handed over medical equipment for the centre's maternity and operating theatre on Tuesday 27 October 2026.

place: Sake Afia health centre, Bikali neighbourhood, Sake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Insecurity Insight's October 2025 DRC incident-monitoring brief listed, as a publicly reported and unverified incident, that on 27 October 2025 the Sake Afia health centre in Bikali neighbourhood, Sake town, Masisi territory, was stormed by armed men dressed in military uniforms who took everything before fleeing during a night attack on the area.

place: Lake Kivu shore, Goma (Étoile du Kivu boat port), North Kivu
statement: Kinpressactu reported that the human rights organisation Dynamique Génération Consciente (DYGENEC-RDC) raised an alert on Monday 12 October 2026 that four young fishermen had reportedly been found dead in Lake Kivu at Goma and a fifth was missing, and denounced alleged executions involving armed elements of the AFC/M23. According to DYGENEC-RDC, the four were Ombeni Dunia Patrick, Chrispin Cuma, Ishara Bunaza and Emmanuel Cikuru, and their bodies were taken to the morgue of the Goma general hospital; the fifth, Adili Banza Julien, had not been found. DYGENEC-RDC said colleagues of the victims told it the five men had reportedly been tied up and thrown into Lake Kivu on the night of Saturday 10 to Sunday 11 October 2026, and that two more bodies had reportedly been found on Monday morning at the Étoile du Kivu boat port. Kinpressactu said these elements, the alleged circumstances of the deaths and the alleged involvement of armed elements required independent verification.

place: Goma port, Lake Kivu, Goma, North Kivu
statement: CongoRassure reported that the body of a young man in his thirties, identified as Crispin Chuma, resident of the Les Volcans quarter in Goma commune, was pulled from Lake Kivu at the Goma port on the morning of Sunday 11 October, with, according to local sources, his feet and hands tied and marks of strangulation and torture. According to testimony gathered on the spot, he had been returning home on Saturday evening around 20:30 with two friends, singing a song deemed hostile to the M23/AFC rebellion; pursued by armed men assimilated to the M23, his two friends reportedly fled, while Crispin Chuma was reportedly arrested and taken to an unknown destination, and his body was found floating the next morning.

place: Goma, North Kivu (AFC/M23 intelligence office; Munzenze central prison)
statement: The Committee to Protect Journalists reported that on 19 September 2025, intelligence agents with the M23 and AFC rebel groups detained Ricardo Olenga, a reporter with the privately owned Radio Kako FM, at their Goma office, according to local media and two journalists who spoke to CPJ anonymously; it said the groups detained him for sharing a video that discussed alleged abuses by the two groups, that he is accused of spreading false news, and, according to those sources, that he was transferred on 23 October to Goma's Munzenze central prison. CPJ said its request for comment to M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma received no response.

Reporters Without Borders (RSF), in a March 2026 report on journalists in the Great Lakes region, said Ricardo Olenga, a Kako FM radio contributor, was arrested by the M23 in Goma on 19 September 2025 and detained until 17 November in unsanitary conditions, after the station's YouTube channel and TikTok account broadcast a video in which a member of the public deplored conditions since the M23 takeover.

place: Lac Vert quarter, Goma, North Kivu (son released at Mugunga)
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that Bulenda Siliro, 74, an avenue chief in the Lac Vert quarter of Goma, was killed on Tuesday 16 September after being kidnapped with his son; the Lac Vert quarter chief, Dedesi Mitima, told the outlet the kidnapping took place between 12 and 13 September, that the family paid the full ransom but only the son was released (reaching Mugunga on the morning of 17 September), and that Bulenda Siliro was shot dead anyway.

place: Kalinda quarter, Mulekera commune, Beni city, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that a group of at least ten men escaped mob justice on Wednesday 17 September 2025 in the Kalinda quarter of Mulekera commune, Beni city, after residents suspected and apprehended them; according to its sources the men, all from Ituri, were assimilated to M23-AFC rebels. It said the Congolese National Police intervened to save them and that the Mulekera mayor, Commissaire supérieur principal Ngongo Mayanga Dieudonné, said the competent services were questioning the suspects. Challenge Info quoted Ngongo Mayanga as saying it could not yet be confirmed whether they were rebels and that investigations were under way.

place: Kiziba 2 village, Mudja groupement, Nyiragongo territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Prosper Kimanuka Musekura, chief of Kiziba 2 village in Nyiragongo territory, was killed in the night from Monday to Tuesday 11 February with all the members of his family: armed bandits entered his home and opened fire, killing the chief, his wife and his three children, a boy and two girls. It said the perpetrators were not known and that civil society actors in Nyiragongo suspected a settling of scores resembling a targeted assassination. A second outlet, whose Kiziba II article is the second source cited here, reported that Kimanuka Musekura Prosper, chief of Kiziba II village in Mudja groupement, was killed in the night of Monday 10 to Tuesday 11 February 2025 with his wife and three children by heavily armed unknown persons, named the children as his son Benjamin and his daughters Sifa and Iragi, and said the five bodies were taken to a local morgue.

place: Kiziba 2 village, Mudja groupement, Nyiragongo territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the chief of Kiziba 2 village in Mudja groupement, Nyiragongo territory, was killed with his three children in the night of Monday to Tuesday 11 February 2025; according to its sources unidentified armed bandits entered the victims' home around 1:00 and fired on them. A relative speaking anonymously said four people had been killed for reasons not yet elucidated, that no one could say who committed the act, and that Prosper Kimanuka Musekura was among the dead.

place: Makengele avenue, Katoyi quarter, near Katindo mosque (Maranatha avenue), Goma, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that four people were killed and several wounded in an armed attack on a pharmacy in the Katoyi quarter of Goma on the evening of Friday 16 May 2025, around 19:00 on Makengele avenue near the Katindo mosque; it said men in uniform, not yet identified, burst in and opened fire, killing the pharmacist and three of his customers, and took an unspecified sum of money and telephones. A resident of Maranatha avenue told the outlet the shooting was around 19:27.

Enquete.cd reported that a 25-year-old man, missing since his arrest on 4 September 2025 in Goma, had been found dead and buried, according to information given to his relatives on 8 August. According to the testimony relayed by civil society actor and human rights defender Jules Ngeleza, Chubaka Buhendwa Josué Maroy had been arrested on alleged accusations of collaborating with the FDLR, and his arrest was reportedly carried out on the order of Sultani Makenga, military head of the M23. The outlet said the family said it learned of his death and burial from a security officer of the movement.

place: Kasanga-Tuha neighbourhood (Kasanga Tuha), Beni city, North Kivu
statement: Challenge Info reported that an agent in charge of dignified and safe burials in the Ebola response was violently assaulted on Wednesday 19 August 2026 in the city of Beni while recovering the body of a person presumed to have died of Ebola; Enquête News (enquetenews.info) reported that the agent of the response team against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola was assaulted at Kasanga-Tuha, Beni, and, according to testimonies, would have been confronted by youths present at the place of death; DW summarised that a response agent had been violently assaulted in Beni.
sources: Challenge Info; Enquête News; Deutsche Welle

place: Kasanga Tuha, Mulekera commune, Beni city, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that on 19 August 2026 at about 09:00 a Red Cross team deployed for awareness and intervention activities in the Kasanga Tuha neighbourhood, Mulekera commune, Beni, was confronted by the population, who according to witnesses accused the humanitarian team amid a high number of reported deaths; a Red Cross agent identified as Querrin was assaulted but reportedly came out "sain et sauf", and the toll also lists three other victims receiving care at the Beni General Referral Hospital.

place: Centre médical Ruwenzori, Beni city, North Kivu
statement: Enquête.cd reported that youths attacked and stoned on Monday 24 August a morgue of a health facility in Beni, North Kivu, before forcibly extracting a body, at a time when the DRC faces an Ebola epidemic; RTEE Kivu reported that a group of youths forced their way on Monday 24 August 2026 into the morgue of the Centre médical Ruwenzori in Beni and took away a body, and that according to first information they reportedly removed it without respecting the planned sanitary formalities.

place: Centre médical Ruwenzori, Beni city, North Kivu
statement: ACP (Agence Congolaise de Presse) reported that Dr Katembo Ngalika, medical director of the Centre médical Ruwenzori in Beni, said that youths came with brutality, broke doors and windows, and that the two people in the morgue were intimidated and beaten, and that the youths took the body in violation of the response norms; he said it was the third attack on this morgue since the start of the Ebola epidemic in the region and that no particular security arrangement had been put around the clinic despite alerts.

Enquête.cd reported that the military governor of North Kivu, Major General Evariste Somo Kakule, had recently warned that anyone who obstructed Ebola response operations or attacked the agents mobilised would be severely punished.
Radio Okapi reported that a viral video shows Beni youths armed with bladed weapons manhandling Ebola response agents, one victim being a woman seen receiving blows from sticks.

place: Luofu, Muhangi, Alimbongo (Lubero territory) and Butembo, North Kivu
statement: La Voix de l'UCG (lavoixdelucg.cd) reported that, according to Dr Kalima Nzanzu, president of the cell of doctors of the Grand Nord, pillaging in some hospitals, displacement of health staff and abandonment of patients, notably those with mental disorders, made an alarming picture; he said many doctors who worked in referral health centres and hospitals were now displaced in Butembo without work, that these centres were closed and, though deserted, had been pillaged, and he named the centres of Luofu and Muhangi and said the situation at Alimbongo was even more critical.

place: Kibirizi–Rwindi axis (Butindiri) and Kibirizi–Kibingu axis, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported, citing local humanitarian organisations, that at least ten people were abducted, two others killed and several goods pillaged between Tuesday and Wednesday 24 June in Rutshuru territory, in at least six localities; on Wednesday morning at least seven people were abducted between 9h and 10h on the Kibirizi–Rwindi (at Butindiri) and Kibirizi–Kibingu road axes, among them three motorcycle-taxi drivers and their clients, and the attackers also took at least eighteen packages of fish from Vitshumbi; the perpetrators of these abductions remained unknown.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that the mining town of Rubaya (Masisi territory) was hit on the night of Saturday 23 to Sunday 24 May 2026 by several explosions attributed by residents to military aircraft; a first strike allegedly targeted a hotel facility known as Rubaya's Guest House, causing several injuries and significant property damage according to local sources, and a second strike allegedly hit an outlying grazing area, destroying several homes and causing livestock losses; local civil society denounced shelling affecting inhabited areas far from the front lines.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that in a statement issued on 24 May the AFC/M23 accused the DRC Armed Forces and their allies of conducting air strikes in North Kivu and South Kivu, claiming that Rumangabo (Rutshuru) and the Virunga National Park eco-guards camp were targeted by CH-4 drones, and recalling bombings in Minembwe and Kalehe causing civilian casualties; the AFC/M23 described the operations as "war crimes". SOS Médias added that at the time of publication no official response from the Congolese authorities had been made public and that the information could not be independently verified.

place: Manzungu, Musangwa, Wasafi, Mangambo (Babila-Bakaiku, Batangi-Mbau), Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: Radio Elimu UOR (Butembo) reported that presumed ADF carried out a deadly incursion in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 6 May 2026 in Beni territory and that local civil society spoke of 24 people killed in the villages Manzungu, Musangwa, Wasafi and Mangambo (Babila-Bakaiku locality, Batangi-Mbau groupement, Beni-Mbau sector), according to KINOS KATUO; the vice-president of civil society in Oïcha commune, Samuel MAHAMBA, said 19 bodies had been counted at the morgue and feared the toll would rise; Enquête.cd reported at least 24 civilians killed in an attack attributed to the ADF, with bodies taken to the Oïcha morgue and others missing.

place: Matete, Kitoho, Mamuli neighbourhoods, Mbau, Batangi-Mbau, Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: 24News Agency reported that an attack attributed to ADF fighters in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 3 June 2026 simultaneously targeted the Matete, Kitoho and Mamuli neighbourhoods of Mbau (Beni territory), killing at least sixteen civilians, burning houses and motorcycles and carrying off an undetermined number of people; at Matete the victims were surprised while taking part in a wake (veillée mortuaire), the attackers burned a hut and three motorcycles before killing people, and the toll in that neighbourhood reached nine; at least seven were killed at Kitoho.

place: Mbau (Kingeste, Ngite), Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to details given by local civil society on Thursday 4 June, the toll of the Mbau attack had risen from 16 to 21 dead after four bodies were found towards Kingeste and a fifth near Ngite, with several other civilians still missing; the page adds that in three days the ADF had killed more than 40 people in attacks on the city and territory of Beni and had taken several civilians hostage.

place: Matété, Mamuli, Kitoho (Mbau), Batangi-Mbau groupement, Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: Congo Quotidien reported that an attack attributed to ADF rebels in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 3 June 2026 hit the localities of Matété, Mamuli and Kitoho (Batangi-Mbau groupement, Beni territory), causing the death of about ten people according to a provisional toll from local civil society; The Guardian wrote that at least 10 people were massacred in raids on those three villages and that the ADF has been blamed.

date: 2026-05-30 (date computed from weekday and publication date)
statement: The Guardian reported that just before midnight on Saturday the militia entered Beni, where people were beheaded and others shot, causing widespread panic and sending hundreds of people running into the bush; more than 20 men, women and children were reported killed and dozens missing, according to witnesses.

date: 2026-06-02 (date computed from weekday and publication date)
statement: The Guardian reported that the military governor of North Kivu said in a statement on Tuesday that three patients confirmed to have Ebola had fled treatment centres in Beni after the Saturday attacks.

place: Walo Uruba (Kiraku locality) and Shempunu, Walikale territory, North Kivu
statement: Labeur (labeur.info) reported that the Consortium International pour les Droits de l’Homme au Congo (CIDHC), in a report made public on Monday 4 May 2026, said it had documented civilians killed without investigation, citizens beaten to humiliation, and men and women arrested without warrant, detained without trial and released on payment; according to the CIDHC, at Walo Uruba (in the Kiraku locality) and at Shempunu, populations were allegedly beaten, locked up and forced to pay money on the pretext of not having shown a "salongo" token.
Labeur (labeur.info) reported that the CIDHC also deplored "un jeune brûlé vif à Byungu" (a youth burned alive at Byungu), without response, investigation or justice.
Labeur (labeur.info) reported that, according to the CIDHC, on the Goma–Masisi–Walikale road barriers erected by the FARDC, militiamen and Mai-Mai Wazalendo groups harass the population.

Labeur (labeur.info) reported that the CIDHC condemned the case of Amani Bitahi Lucien, a civil society actor, arrested and deprived of his liberty 26 times for having denounced injustice and the poor conditions suffered by the inhabitants; the report as quoted gives no dates for the arrests and does not name who made them.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the CIDHC, in a report covering January to April 2026, described Walikale detention conditions as critical and said detainees are often forced to pay to access basic rights such as food, health care or even space in detention.

place: Rumangabo military training centre, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Grands Lacs News reported that, on a visit to the Rumangabo training centre in Rutshuru territory at the weekend, General Sultani Makenga, head of the M23 armed branch, spoke with prisoners of war including former FARDC soldiers captured at the fall of Goma, and told them that anyone wishing to join the rebellion voluntarily was free to do so and that those wishing to return to Kinshasa could register under the prisoner-release process of the Doha process, to be facilitated with the ICRC. The page embeds an AFC/M23 post stating that the visit took place on Friday 2 January 2026.

Mediacongo reported that human rights activist Jacques Sinzahera said soldiers who answered a call by Sultani Makenga at a meeting on 4 January 2026 live in extremely difficult conditions at Rumangabo, and alleged that at least two soldiers die every week for lack of medicine and food; he called on MONUSCO and the ICRC to start repatriating them.

place: Bosco Lac, Lake Kivu shore, Goma (Ndosho arrests), North Kivu
statement: Enquête.cd reported that an inhabitant, in a testimony sent to journalist Daniel Michombero, denounced presumed summary executions attributed to the rebels and their Rwandan allies after two bodies were seen floating in Lake Kivu at the site known as "Bosco Lac" in Goma; according to the inhabitant, the victims were reportedly young men who had been arrested a few days earlier at their homes in the Ndosho neighbourhood by M23 elements. Enquête.cd added that the allegations could not be independently confirmed at the time of publication and that no official reaction from the M23/AFC had been recorded.

place: Goma, North Kivu (provincial assembly grounds, Himbi; near Mont Goma)
statement: Radio Okapi reported that Reporters sans frontières (RSF), in an investigation report published on Tuesday 24 March 2026, revealed inhuman detention places run by the rebel movement AFC-M23 in Goma, where at least two journalists were detained and tortured in ventilation-less metal containers; the page lists sites at the North Kivu provincial assembly (Himbi) and near Mont Goma by the RTNC, and a former detainee reportedly said up to 80 people could be packed into the containers.

Radio Okapi reported that, contacted by RSF, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka rejected the allegations about detention containers in Goma, calling them "informations totalement infondées" and "propagande", and said the movement makes no arrests of journalists.

place: Rumangabo camp, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 announced in a communiqué that it had once again handed over to the International Committee of the Red Cross more than 5 000 FARDC elements captured on different fronts, to be repatriated to Kinshasa under ICRC supervision, at a ceremony held on Monday 2 March 2026 at Rumangabo camp; Actualite.cd added that the rebels deplored Kinshasa's refusal to release their arrested comrades.

Actualite.cd reported that François Moreillon, head of the ICRC delegation in Kinshasa, reacted to the AFC/M23 communiqué by saying the ICRC had taken note of it and, as a neutral intermediary, stood ready to accompany such an operation with the agreement of all parties.

Journal de Kinshasa reported that on Thursday 12 March the Deputy Prime Minister for Defence, Guy Kabombo, received François Moreillon, head of the ICRC delegation in the DRC, to discuss the release of war detainees, which the page links to the AFC/M23 announcement from Rumangabo of the release of more than five thousand FARDC.

Umuseke (Rwanda) wrote that AFC/M23 had said it returned to Congo some 5000 soldiers and members of their families who had been stranded in the city of Goma, and that Congo "ntacyo yabivuzeho" (had said nothing about it).

place: Matete, Kitoho, Mamuli (Mbau sector), Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least 16 civilians were killed and five others reported missing on Wednesday 3 June 2026 in simultaneous attacks attributed to ADF-MTM rebels in Mbau sector (Kitoho, Matete and Mamuli localities), according to a provisional toll from Omar Kalisya, president of the Beni territory civil society; according to civil society the assailants split into three groups, the first attacking a wake (veillée mortuaire) in the Matete neighbourhood, the second striking Kitoho, and the third targeting wives of LENI police officers engaged in security operations at Matete, where according to first information two soldiers' wives and a baby were killed.

place: Bapakombe-Bakondo, Ngadi neighbourhood, Beni, North Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that several farming entities of the village of Bapakombe-Bakondo in Beni (North Kivu) were attacked in the night of Saturday to Sunday 31 May by ADF rebels, that about twenty civilians, pygmies and Bantu, were victims, and that the Association nationale des victimes du Congo (ANVC) condemned the massacre of the Ngadi neighbourhood and demanded an independent international investigation.

place: Munzambayi cell, Boikene district, Ruwenzori commune, Beni city (Beni), North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that an attack by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters at dawn on Thursday 11 June left, as a provisional toll, at least three civilians killed and two houses burned in the Munzambayi cell, Boikene district, Ruwenzori commune, Beni; La Presse Africaine reported a provisional toll of three dead, said the attackers also burned houses and three motorbikes before withdrawing to the forest, and, citing several local sources, said motorbike-taxi drivers took to the streets to denounce the deterioration of security after the attack attributed to the ADF.

place: Munzambayi cell, Boikene district, Beni city, North Kivu
statement: Dépêche.cd reported that the provisional toll communicated by the army for the ADF-attributed attack on the morning of Thursday 11 June in Boikene district, Ruwenzori commune, Beni (the Munzambayi cell) was three civilians dead, one of them burned alive, and three homes burned; Lieutenant Marc Elongo, spokesperson of the Sukola 1 Grand Nord operations, said the assailants had bypassed 'the positions held strongly in depth by the FARDC-UPDF coalition'.

place: Muzambayi, Boikene district, Beni city, North Kivu
statement: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO) reported that on 11 June, in Muzambayi in the Boikene district of the city of Beni, at least three civilians were executed and several homes were destroyed by fire, prompting a protest by the local population.

place: Matiba, Mbau, Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO) reported that on the night of 5-6 June, in Matiba, five civilians were summarily executed and a house was set on fire.

place: Kelekele, Mbau-Kamango axis, Beni territory, North Kivu
statement: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO) reported that on 6 June two civilians were killed in an ambush on the Mbau-Kamango axis in Kelekele, while at least two motorcycles were set on fire.

The UN Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO) reported that on the night of 2-3 June in Mbau, in Beni territory, ADF combatants summarily executed at least 18 civilians, including women and children, and injured at least nine others.

Imvahonshya (Rwanda) reported that Willy Manzi, the North Kivu deputy governor appointed by AFC/M23, confirmed on social media that an FDLR fighter known as Yoweri, nicknamed Tokyo, had been captured in fighting in Masisi; the outlet said news of his capture began circulating on social media on Friday 24 October 2025, when he was said to have been captured by AFC/M23 fighters.

place: Masisi, North Kivu (place of alleged crimes not stated in the quote)
statement: Imvahonshya reported that Willy Manzi, the North Kivu deputy governor appointed by AFC/M23, said on social media that Yoweri, alias Tokyo, together with others including Jean-Marie of the Nyatura group, Tiger and Ignace Dunia, had committed terrible crimes including rape, killings and the burning of countless houses; this is an allegation by an AFC/M23 official.

Umuseke (Rwanda) reported that an AFC/M23 fighter, Col. Samuel Nsabimana Mwendangabo, said Tokyo had been shot in the leg and then captured, and that he would first be treated; the colonel said he was captured 'aho bita i Muzimu'.

Dépêche.cd reported that FARDC military intelligence services announced in Beni the interception of a truck carrying several sacks of hemp and that, according to the Congolese army, the cargo allegedly belonged to an AFC-M23 commander identified as Zimurinda Innocent, based in Rutshuru territory.

Dépêche.cd reported that the FARDC presented in Beni, on Tuesday, 'plusieurs personnes accusées de collaborer avec les rebelles de l'AFC-M23', among them Byamungu Zembezembe Jean-Pierre, from South Kivu, arrested in the Matongé district in central Beni; Matofali Bushu Arsène, described by the army as a member of the armed group FFPP/AP of Kabido; and a young woman, Kavira Léa, whom the military authorities say was recruited by Katembo Ndalieni, former mayor of Goma under the rebel administration.

place: Renga and Kashenda districts, Bweremana, Masisi territory, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that at least two civilians died on Friday 3 January 2025 in bombardments that hit homes in the Renga district of the Bweremana agglomeration, Masisi, and three others were wounded by shrapnel in Kashenda district; according to local civil society, the bombs were launched by the M23 from the lines of fighting against local 'wazalendo' fighters.

place: Ndumba, Kashingamutwe, Kabase hills, Bweremana-Minova axis, Masisi, North Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported, citing the president of Bweremana civil society, that the M23 launched simultaneous attacks from 5 a.m. on wazalendo positions on several hills overlooking the Bweremana-Minova axis, including Ndumba, Kashingamutwe and Kabase.

Ouragan.cd reported that, on the margins of the 61st session of the UN Human Rights Council, DRC Human Rights Minister Samuel Mbemba said at the rostrum that he counted more than 17 000 documented serious human rights violations, nearly 15 000 deaths and about eight million displaced.

ChimpReports reported that the Tanzania People's Defence Forces (TPDF) said, in a statement by Col. Ilonda, that following consecutive attacks in the Sake and Goma areas on 24 and 28 January 2025 it had lost two of its soldiers while four others sustained injuries and were receiving treatment in Goma, and that all TPDF troops deployed in the DRC remain safe.

place: Musigiko cemetery, Kabare territory, and Bukavu, South Kivu
statement: 7sur7.cd reported that on 20 February the cemetery of Musigiko, in Kabare territory, South Kivu, was the burial place of 18 people who died in the fighting during the M23's capture of Bukavu, their bodies placed in body bags and laid in a mass grave in Bukavu; it said John Kashinzwe, Red Cross provincial secretary in South Kivu, specified the remains had been recovered from various places in the city, and that the Red Cross with the ICRC had earlier announced collecting 26 bodies.

CongoRassure reported that several FARDC soldiers captured at the fall of Goma had escaped from the military camp of Rumangabo, Rutshuru territory, where the M23 held them; according to testimonies it gathered, many of them reportedly died through summary executions, torture or forced labour, and one escapee said they were captured on 26 and 27 January 2025 in Goma and that 'beaucoup de nos frères d'armes ont été tués'.

place: Ilundu health centre, near Minembwe airfield (Minembwe), Fizi
statement: Deutsche Welle reported that a resident of Minembwe, speaking of drone bombardments, said that even the Minembwe general referral hospital and some health centres had been targeted, and quoted him as saying that the paediatric block had been bombed 'yesterday' and that the Ilundu health centre, next to the airfield, had been bombed too.

Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said in an RFI interview that he could share images in which Rwanda uses ambulances to transport drones and carry out attacks using the medical equipment of an ambulance; he called it a serious and substantiated accusation and said: "It is a war crime."

Mediacongo reported that, speaking to the press, the Congolese government spokesperson said Rwanda uses ambulances to transport drones intended to carry out attacks on civilians in South Kivu, and that he described these practices as war crimes.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that Colonel Alexis Rugabisha, commander of the FARDC 12th rapid-intervention brigade, was killed on Saturday 1 February 2025 in fighting with the M23 at Nyabibwe in Kalehe territory; military sources told the outlet he was shot by snipers after his men fled.

Radio Okapi reported that Colonel Alexis Rugabisha, commander of the FARDC 12th brigade, was killed in clashes between the FARDC and the M23 at Mukwija in Kalehe territory, and that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge, in a communiqué published on Sunday 2 February 2025, praised his bravery and called his death an inestimable loss for the army and the nation.

Actualite.cd reported that the Congolese army announced in a communiqué that Colonel Rugabisha Alexis, commander of the FARDC 12th brigade, was killed in combat against the Rwandan army and the M23 in Kalehe territory; according to spokesperson Major General Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, he fell 'armes à la main' after leading a counter-offensive that pushed the M23 back from Nyabibwe towards the surroundings of Minova.

place: Kavumu commercial centre, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare, South Kivu
statement: Radio Maendeleo reported that notables of northern Kabare territory denounced cases of abductions and intimidation at the Kavumu commercial centre that were pushing many young people and heads of families to leave their homes; the same report said gunfire had been heard for over a month and that deaths by bullets and injuries had been reported.

place: Buliriko quarter, Kavumu, Kabare, South Kivu
statement: Enquete.cd reported that, according to testimonies gathered on site, several residents of the Buliriko quarter of Kavumu, in Kabare territory, left their homes for Buhandahanda and Nzinzi, and that families said they feared a worsening situation after the installation on Saturday of a military camp attributed to AFC/M23 fighters.

Bwiza reported that FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza told journalists on Tuesday 29 September 2026 that Maj. Nitunga Jérémie and Capt Kanjori Félicien were arrested by the DRC state on 21 August 2026 and are held at the FARDC headquarters in Baraka, where they were arrested after being found with telephones, and that it is suspected they may have been used 'in improper activities or in giving certain information'.

PoliScoop reported, according to accounts shared by Burundian sources, that two Burundian army officers held in eastern DRC since August had been repatriated to Burundi; it also reported that Major Jeremie Nitunga and Captain Felicien Kanjori had been arrested on 21 August in Baraka and detained by the FARDC and allied groups operating in the area.

place: Rugezi and Kabanju, Fizi territory, South Kivu
statement: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, according to an anonymous Twirwaneho fighter it contacted, at least 17 Burundian soldiers were killed in the fighting at Rugezi and Kabanju, Fizi territory, and the fighter said: 'We captured one, along with their radios and their rifles.'

place: Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Fizi (spokesperson's words); the article places the recaptured Masango, Ruhua and Rubarati in the Mwenga highlands, Itombwe sector, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that the spokesperson of operation Sukola 2 Sud South Kivu, Lieutenant-Colonel Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said that following the FARDC response against what he called the 'terrorist coalition RDF and its allies M23, Twirwaneho and Red Tabara' in the Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Fizi, the FARDC had neutralised 23 rebels, 11 others had surrendered and several weapons were recovered.

place: Masango, Hauts Plateaux of Mwenga, Itombwe sector, South Kivu
statement: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the army, a mass grave was discovered at Masango, where civilians killed during the occupation of the town by the M23/Twirwaneho/Red Tabara rebel forces, supported by Rwanda, are said to be buried.

place: Kinshasa (presentation of the captives); capture sites in North and South Kivu, not specified
statement: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC presented to the press in Kinshasa on Saturday 3 January seven people it described as Rwandan soldiers and eight civilians, nationals of countries of the sub-region, and that Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay said these suspects had been apprehended far from the borders during military operations in North and South Kivu.

place: Uvira (city), South Kivu (capture, per Liberal Info); Kinshasa (presentation)
statement: Liberal Info reported that on Saturday the FARDC presented at the Collège des Hautes Études de Stratégie et de Défense (CHESD) in Kinshasa seven people described as soldiers of the Rwandan defence forces (RDF) and eight civilians, including Burundian and Tanzanian nationals, whom Liberal Info described as 'captured in the city of Uvira'; the identification of the seven as RDF soldiers is the FARDC's account.

place: Kinshasa (press conference) concerning Uvira, South Kivu
statement: Radio Okapi reported that FARDC Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay said, at the press presentation in Kinshasa, that the occupation of Uvira, far from Rwanda's borders, proves that the defensive-measures reason advanced by Kigali is 'un pire mensonge'.

Opinion Info and Actualite.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, at a press briefing with Patrick Muyaya on Thursday 2 April 2026, said about 210 bodies had been found in three mass graves (Actualite.cd: at least 210); Opinion Info quotes him as saying Human Rights Watch had just detected more than 61 mass graves and that 31 mass graves had been found in only three municipalities, and names the three graves as Kamvivira, Kilomoni and Kimanga.

African Facts reported that the group of James Bitolo, with other Biloze Bishamuke militiamen and Maï maï fighters, then attacked and pillaged the evangelical church where the funeral of Colonel Gisore took place, and quoted Muyoboke Ntabaye, president of the Banyamulenge mutuality of Uvira, as saying he was among those arrested in the church, that they shot at them, and that they stole crates of drinks, vehicles, medical equipment and telephones; African Facts wrote that videos and other testimonies it consulted corroborate the attack.

African Facts reported that, in a communiqué issued 'le jour même', the South Kivu government spokesperson summed up the events as a 'petite paralysie des activités dans Mulongwe' that would have caused no damage (conditional, as the article words it), and 'condamne les organisateurs des cérémonies funéraires'; the article adds that he also condemned messages aimed at tearing the social fabric between communities and spoke of a media war waged by the rebels.

place: Nyabianda / Namyanda quarter, Uvira (city), South Kivu (both spellings as printed)
statement: African Facts reported that soldiers and militiamen had reportedly acted together 'hier matin' in the Nyabianda quarter, and quoted Muyoboke Ntabaye, president of the Banyamulenge mutuality of Uvira, as saying that soldiers, maï maï and persons in police uniform began the cordon at 5:00 and it lasted until 13:00, that more than fifteen members of his community were arrested without valid reason, and that some were taken to the cells of the Wazalendo militias instead of government buildings; the article also quotes him describing waking up in a cordon in the quarter 'deNamyanda' where many Banyamulenge live.
